name: cookbook/build_on_github.shale
html: -- This recipe runs a build on GitHub instead of on the box. It dispatches a -- `workflow_dispatch` workflow (shale's .github/workflows/test.yml, which runs -- `zig build test`) for `ref`, and says the run's URL and id at once. Given -- that id, it checks the run: its status, or once the run is done, PASS or -- FAIL with its wall time, and for a failure the last 40 log lines (`gh run -- view --log-failed`), failing the launch. The workflow never runs on a push -- or a PR, only when this recipe asks. -- -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:build_on_github.shale ref=my-branch -- shale cookbook:build_on_github.shale run=40518919602 -- shale cookbook:build_on_github.shale ref=master wait=yes -- -- `repo` is showell/<repo> (default shale), `ref` the branch, tag or -- commit the workflow checks out (default the branch checked out here), -- `workflow` its file (default test.yml). A dispatch is 3 or 4 programs -- and a few seconds; `run=<id>` is one look, no waiting. `wait=yes` -- dispatches and polls every `every` seconds (default 15) until the run -- is done: it is for a background task, whose exit says the verdict. Each -- look is one program, so a wait is at most the run's `programs` budget of -- looks (1,000 unset, about four hours at 15 s). -- -- budget: steps=50000000 const REPO = arg("repo", "shale") const REF = arg("ref", "") const WORKFLOW = arg("workflow", "test.yml") const WAIT = arg("wait", "no") const RUN = arg("run", "") const EVERY = arg("every", 15) not_option("build_on_github", "repo", REPO) not_option("build_on_github", "ref", REF) not_option("build_on_github", "workflow", WORKFLOW) not_option("build_on_github", "run", RUN) if WAIT ~= "yes" and WAIT ~= "no" then fail("build_on_github: `wait` is yes or no, not " .. WAIT) end const SLUG = "showell/" .. REPO -- A `gh` program's output, trimmed; its failure fails the launch. `USED.n` -- counts them, for the summary. const USED = {n = 0} function gh(argv) USED.n = USED.n + 1 local r = run(argv, {tail = 40, timeout_ms = 60000}) if not has_key(r, "code") or r.code ~= 0 then fail("build_on_github: `" .. join(argv, " ") .. "` failed:\n" .. r.out) end return trim(r.out) end -- These calls use GitHub's REST API. `gh workflow run` and `gh run list` -- ask GraphQL, which a Claude Code session is refused; `gh api` on -- the REST paths works wherever `gh` does. -- The newest dispatched run's id, or "" when there is none. function newest() return gh({"gh", "api", "repos/" .. SLUG .. "/actions/workflows/" .. WORKFLOW .. "/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&per_page=1", "-q", ".workflow_runs[0].id // \"\""}) end -- The workflow dispatched on `ref`, and its run's id once listed. function dispatch(ref) local before = newest() -- The workflow's own file is the default branch's; `ref` is its input, -- the commit it checks out. local home = gh({"gh", "api", "repos/" .. SLUG, "-q", ".default_branch"}) gh({"gh", "api", "-X", "POST", "repos/" .. SLUG .. "/actions/workflows/" .. WORKFLOW .. "/dispatches", "-f", "ref=" .. home, "-f", "inputs[ref]=" .. ref}) -- The dispatch answers before the run is listed: a new id is this one. local id = before local looks = 0 while id == before do looks = looks + 1 if looks > 10 then fail("build_on_github: no new " .. WORKFLOW .. " run listed for " .. SLUG .. " after 10 looks") end sleep(2000) id = newest() end return id end -- "status conclusion seconds url", conclusion "-" while it runs; -- the seconds from its start to its end, or to now while it runs -- (`updatedAt` stands still then). const SAY = "\"\\(.status) \\(.conclusion // \"-\") \\((if .status == \"completed\" then (.updated_at | fromdate) else now end) - (.run_started_at | fromdate) | floor) \\(.html_url)\"" function look(id) local w = {} for x in words(gh({"gh", "api", "repos/" .. SLUG .. "/actions/runs/" .. id, "-q", SAY})) do push(w, x) end return {id = id, status = w[1], conclusion = w[2], secs = w[3], url = w[4]} end -- A run's verdict: its status while it runs, PASS, or FAIL with its log's -- tail, failing the launch. function verdict(v) if v.status ~= "completed" then print(v.status .. " after " .. v.secs .. " s: " .. v.url .. " (run " .. v.id .. ")") elseif v.conclusion == "success" then print("PASS in " .. v.secs .. " s: " .. v.url) else local r = run({"gh", "run", "view", v.id, "--repo", SLUG, "--log-failed"}, {tail = 40, timeout_ms = 60000}) for l in lines(r.out) do print(" " .. sub(l, 1, 240)) end print("FAIL (" .. v.conclusion .. ") in " .. v.secs .. " s: " .. v.url) fail("build_on_github: run " .. v.id .. " " .. v.conclusion) end end if RUN ~= "" then verdict(look(RUN)) else local ref = REF if ref == "" then ref = gh({"git", "branch", "--show-current"}) if ref == "" then fail("build_on_github: no branch checked out here: say `ref=`") end end local id = dispatch(ref) if WAIT == "no" then print("dispatched: https://github.com/" .. SLUG .. "/actions/runs/" .. id .. " (run " .. id .. ", " .. WORKFLOW .. " on " .. ref .. ")") else local v = look(id) print("waiting on " .. v.url .. " (" .. ref .. ")") while v.status ~= "completed" do -- One program is kept for a failure's log. if budget().programs < 2 then fail("build_on_github: still " .. v.status .. " after " .. v.secs .. " s, and this run's `programs` budget is spent (`--budget programs=N` raises it): " .. v.url) end sleep(EVERY * 1000) v = look(id) end verdict(v) end end

name: cookbook/check_conflict_markers.shale
html: -- Checks that files hold no conflict markers, the last step of a merge -- resolved by hand or with the conflicts library: -- -- shale <cookbook>/check_conflict_markers.shale files=a.zig,docs/b.md -- -- It prints PASS, or each file's markers and FAIL. `self_test=1` tests the -- library on the canned conflicts below instead. use("cookbook:merge_conflicts.shale") const DIFF3 = [=[ top <<<<<<< HEAD ours one ||||||| base base one ======= theirs one >>>>>>> topic middle <<<<<<< HEAD ours two ||||||| base ======= theirs two theirs two, more >>>>>>> topic end ]=] const TWO_WAY = [=[ a <<<<<<< HEAD ours ======= theirs >>>>>>> topic b ]=] function hunks_of(text) return conflict_hunks(text, "case") end function keep_of(text, side) return keep_side(text, side, "case") end function resolve_of(text, sides) return resolve_hunks(text, sides, "case") end function once_of(text, old, new) return replace_once(text, old, new) end function resolved_of(text) return assert_resolved(text, "case") end function assert_file_of(path) return assert_file_resolved(path) end -- Each failing call must stop with a message holding `want`. function expect_stop(wrong, name, r, want) if r.ok then push(wrong, name .. ": did not stop") elseif r.class ~= "fail" or not contains(r.error, want) then push(wrong, name .. ": stopped with " .. r.class .. ": " .. r.error) end end function expect_same(wrong, name, got, want) if got ~= want then push(wrong, name .. ": got [" .. got .. "], wanted [" .. want .. "]") end end function self_test() local wrong = {} local h = conflict_hunks(DIFF3) expect_same(wrong, "diff3 count", tostring(#h), "2") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 line 1", tostring(h[1].line), "2") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 line 2", tostring(h[2].line), "10") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 style", h[1].style, "diff3") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 ours", h[1].ours, "ours one\n") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 base", h[1].base, "base one\n") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 theirs", h[1].theirs, "theirs one\n") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 empty base", h[2].base, "") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 two lines", h[2].theirs, "theirs two\ntheirs two, more\n") expect_same(wrong, "diff3 labels", h[1].ours_label .. "/" .. h[1].theirs_label, "HEAD/topic") local t = conflict_hunks(TWO_WAY) expect_same(wrong, "two-way count", tostring(#t), "1") expect_same(wrong, "two-way style", t[1].style, "two-way") expect_same(wrong, "two-way ours", t[1].ours, "ours\n") expect_same(wrong, "two-way theirs", t[1].theirs, "theirs\n") expect_same(wrong, "no conflicts", tostring(#conflict_hunks("plain\n")), "0") expect_same(wrong, "keep ours", keep_side(DIFF3, "ours"), "top\nours one\nmiddle\nours two\nend\n") expect_same(wrong, "keep theirs", keep_side(DIFF3, "theirs"), "top\ntheirs one\nmiddle\ntheirs two\ntheirs two, more\nend\n") expect_same(wrong, "keep base", keep_side(DIFF3, "base"), "top\nbase one\nmiddle\nend\n") expect_same(wrong, "keep two-way", keep_side(TWO_WAY, "theirs"), "a\ntheirs\nb\n") expect_same(wrong, "hunk by hunk", resolve_hunks(DIFF3, {"theirs", "both"}), "top\ntheirs one\nmiddle\nours two\ntheirs two\ntheirs two, more\nend\n") expect_same(wrong, "rewrite", rewrite_hunks(TWO_WAY, {"mine\n"}), "a\nmine\nb\n") expect_same(wrong, "CRLF", keep_side("x\r\n<<<<<<< HEAD\r\no\r\n=======\r\nt\r\n>>>>>>> b\r\n", "theirs"), "x\r\nt\r\n") expect_same(wrong, "no final newline", keep_side("<<<<<<< HEAD\no\n=======\nt\n>>>>>>> b", "ours"), "o\n") expect_stop(wrong, "unclosed", attempt(hunks_of, "<<<<<<< HEAD\no\n=======\nt\n"), "case:1: the conflict that opens here never closes") expect_stop(wrong, "close before split", attempt(hunks_of, "<<<<<<< HEAD\no\n>>>>>>> b\n"), "case:3: a `>>>>>>>` before the `=======`") expect_stop(wrong, "nested open", attempt(hunks_of, "<<<<<<< HEAD\n<<<<<<< HEAD\n"), "case:2: a `<<<<<<<` inside") expect_stop(wrong, "second split", attempt(hunks_of, "<<<<<<< HEAD\n=======\n=======\n>>>>>>> b\n"), "case:3: a second `=======`") expect_stop(wrong, "base after split", attempt(hunks_of, "<<<<<<< HEAD\n=======\n||||||| base\n>>>>>>> b\n"), "case:3: a `|||||||` after the theirs section") expect_stop(wrong, "stray close", attempt(hunks_of, "a\n>>>>>>> b\n"), "case:2: a `>>>>>>>` marker outside") expect_stop(wrong, "base of two-way", attempt(keep_of, TWO_WAY, "base"), "is two-way and has no base") expect_stop(wrong, "no such side", attempt(keep_of, TWO_WAY, "mine"), "no side `mine`") expect_stop(wrong, "nothing to keep", attempt(keep_of, "plain\n", "ours"), "no conflict to resolve") expect_stop(wrong, "too few sides", attempt(resolve_of, DIFF3, {"ours"}), "has 2 conflicts, and 1 sides") expect_same(wrong, "replace once", replace_once("a b c", "b", "B"), "a B c") expect_same(wrong, "replace at the ends", replace_once("ab", "a", "") .. replace_once("ab", "b", "c"), "bac") expect_stop(wrong, "replace absent", attempt(once_of, "a b c", "d", "D"), "not found: d") expect_stop(wrong, "replace twice", attempt(once_of, "a b a", "a", "A"), "found more than once: a") expect_stop(wrong, "replace empty", attempt(once_of, "a", "", "A"), "the old text is empty") expect_same(wrong, "markers in diff3", tostring(#conflict_markers(DIFF3)), "8") expect_same(wrong, "markers in plain", tostring(#conflict_markers("<<<<<<<< eight\n=== \n")), "0") local ok = attempt(resolved_of, keep_side(DIFF3, "ours")) if not ok.ok then push(wrong, "resolved text: stopped: " .. ok.error) end expect_stop(wrong, "left markers", attempt(resolved_of, TWO_WAY), "case:2: 3 conflict markers left, the first `<<<<<<< HEAD`") local dir = fresh_dir("scratch:", "conflicts") local f = path_under(dir, "f.txt") create(f, DIFF3) expect_stop(wrong, "file markers left", attempt(assert_file_of, f), "f.txt:2: 8 conflict markers left") keep_side_file(f, "theirs") expect_same(wrong, "file kept", read(f), keep_side(DIFF3, "theirs")) assert_file_resolved(f) remove_tree(dir) for w in wrong do print("wrong: " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("conflicts self-test: " .. #wrong .. " wrong") end print("conflicts self-test: all cases right") end if arg("self_test", "") ~= "" then self_test() else local files = arg("files", "") if files == "" then fail("check_conflict_markers: give files=a,b (or self_test=1)") end local bad = 0 for p in split(files, ",") do for m in conflict_markers(read(p)) do print(p .. ":" .. m.line .. ": " .. m.text) bad = bad + 1 end end if bad > 0 then fail("FAIL: " .. bad .. " conflict markers left") end print("PASS") end

name: cookbook/check_disk_space.shale
html: -- This recipe checks the free space on the filesystem that holds the working -- directory, by `df`, and stops a run before the disk fills. -- -- shale cookbook:check_disk_space.shale disk: 52 GB free -- shale cookbook:check_disk_space.shale floor=60 stops: disk: 52 GB free, under the floor of 60 GB; the biggest: ... -- shale cookbook:check_disk_space.shale report=1 the growth spots' sizes, biggest first -- shale cookbook:check_disk_space.shale self_test=1 -- -- By default it guards: under `floor=` GB free (20) it stops, exit -- nonzero, with one line naming the three biggest growth spots; otherwise -- it prints `disk: N GB free`. A verify runs it as its first check, so a -- full disk fails at the start and never mid-run. Fail, never warn: there -- is no warning band. -- -- With `report=1` it prints the sizes of the spots that grow, each by -- `du -sk`, biggest first, those under 0.1 GB counted on one line; sizes -- only, never a file's name or contents below a spot: -- - each folder of `build:lanes/` (a lane's Roc and Zig caches); -- - `~/.cache/roc` and `~/.cache/zig` (`$HOME`'s, as `printenv` says); -- - each top folder of `scratch:`. -- A spot that is not there is passed by, and so is a mount this box's -- mounts file lacks: the recipe runs anywhere Shale does. -- -- GB here is 2^30 bytes, `df`'s and `du`'s kibibytes over 1,048,576. -- -- budget: steps=20000000 const FLOOR = tonumber(arg("floor", "20")) const REPORT = arg("report", "0") == "1" const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "0") == "1" const KIB_PER_GB = 1048576 -- Free kibibytes on the working directory's filesystem: `df -Pk .`'s -- second line, its fourth field (Available). `.`, never an absolute path, -- so a working directory that holds the `keys:` mount is not refused. function free_kib() local r = must(run({"df", "-Pk", "."}, {cwd = ".", timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 4000})) local rows = split(trim(r.out), "\n") if #rows < 2 then fail("disk: `df -Pk .` gave no filesystem line: " .. trim(r.out)) end local cols = words(rows[#rows]) if #cols < 4 then fail("disk: `df -Pk .` gave a short line: " .. rows[#rows]) end return tonumber(cols[4]) end -- The verdict, kept apart from the stop so the self-test asserts both -- sides: `{ok, line}`. A failing line ends `the biggest: `, for the caller -- to finish, so the spots' `du`s (seconds) run only on a failure. function guard(free_gb, floor) if free_gb < floor then return {ok = false, line = "disk: " .. free_gb .. " GB free, under the floor of " .. floor .. " GB; the biggest: "} end return {ok = true, line = "disk: " .. free_gb .. " GB free"} end function gb_text(kib) local tenths = kib * 10 // KIB_PER_GB return (tenths // 10) .. "." .. (tenths % 10) .. " GB" end -- Each path's kibibytes by one `du -sk` of them all (a run has 64 -- programs; a box has more lanes): a map, a path that is not there left -- out. A file `du` could not read (exit 1) still leaves the total it could. function du_kib(paths) local argv = {"du", "-sk"} for p in paths do argv[#argv + 1] = p end local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = 600000, whole = 1000000}) local out = {} for line in split(r.out, "\n") do local m = re_find(line, "^(\\d+)\t(.*)$") if m ~= nil then out[m.groups[2]] = tonumber(m.groups[1]) end end return out end function is_dir_at(p) return is_dir(p) end -- The folders below a mount's folder, as `{path, label}`: the OS path and -- `prefix` and the name, the mount's spelling; none when the mount is not -- in this box's mounts file or the folder is not there. function folders_under(mounted, prefix) local here = attempt(is_dir_at, mounted) if not here.ok or not here.value then return {} end local out = {} for name in ls(mounted) do local p = path_under(mounted, name) -- The store refuses a symbolic link; a link is no growth spot of its own. local folder = attempt(is_dir_at, p) if folder.ok and folder.value then out[#out + 1] = {path = real(p), label = prefix .. name} end end return out end -- The spots `du` sized, biggest first: one it left out (a cache never -- made, or deleted) is no spot, never a stop. function sized(found, sizes) local out = {} for f in found do if has_key(sizes, f.path) then out[#out + 1] = {path = f.path, label = f.label, kib = sizes[f.path]} end end return sort(out, {{key = "kib", desc = true}, "label"}) end -- Every growth spot with its size, biggest first: `{path, label, kib}`. function spots() local home = trim(must(run({"printenv", "HOME"}, {timeout_ms = 10000, whole = 4000})).out) local found = folders_under("build:lanes", "build:lanes/") found[#found + 1] = {path = home .. "/.cache/roc", label = "~/.cache/roc"} found[#found + 1] = {path = home .. "/.cache/zig", label = "~/.cache/zig"} for f in folders_under("scratch:.", "scratch:") do found[#found + 1] = f end local paths = {} for f in found do paths[#paths + 1] = f.path end return sized(found, du_kib(paths)) end function biggest_three() local parts = {} for s in spots() do if #parts < 3 then parts[#parts + 1] = s.label .. " " .. gb_text(s.kib) end end if #parts == 0 then return "no growth spot found" end return join(parts, ", ") end if SELF_TEST then -- The floors chosen from the real free space, so the box's own disk -- never decides the outcome: one above it fails, it and one below pass. local free = free_kib() // KIB_PER_GB local under = guard(free, free + 1) if under.ok then fail("disk self_test: " .. free .. " GB free passed a floor of " .. (free + 1)) end local want = "disk: " .. free .. " GB free, under the floor of " .. (free + 1) .. " GB; the biggest: " if under.line ~= want then fail("disk self_test: the failing line is `" .. under.line .. "`, want `" .. want .. "`") end local at = guard(free, free) if not at.ok or at.line ~= "disk: " .. free .. " GB free" then fail("disk self_test: a floor equal to the free space (" .. free .. ") did not pass: " .. at.line) end if free > 0 then local over = guard(free, free - 1) if not over.ok then fail("disk self_test: " .. free .. " GB free failed a floor of " .. (free - 1)) end end if gb_text(0) ~= "0.0 GB" or gb_text(KIB_PER_GB * 3 // 2) ~= "1.5 GB" or gb_text(KIB_PER_GB - 1) ~= "0.9 GB" then fail("disk self_test: gb_text is " .. gb_text(0) .. ", " .. gb_text(KIB_PER_GB * 3 // 2) .. ", " .. gb_text(KIB_PER_GB - 1)) end local some = sized({{path = "/a", label = "a"}, {path = "/gone", label = "gone"}, {path = "/b", label = "b"}}, {["/a"] = 5, ["/b"] = 9}) if #some ~= 2 or some[1].label ~= "b" or some[2].label ~= "a" then fail("disk self_test: a spot du left out (deleted) is not skipped, or the rest are out of order") end print("disk self_test: PASS (" .. free .. " GB free: a floor of " .. (free + 1) .. " fails with the line, " .. free .. " and " .. (free - 1) .. " pass; a spot du left out is skipped)") elseif REPORT then print("disk: " .. (free_kib() // KIB_PER_GB) .. " GB free") -- A spot under a tenth of a GB is counted, not listed. local small = 0 for s in spots() do if s.kib * 10 < KIB_PER_GB then small = small + 1 else print(gb_text(s.kib) .. "\t" .. s.label) end end if small > 0 then print("and " .. small .. " spots under 0.1 GB each") end else local v = guard(free_kib() // KIB_PER_GB, FLOOR) if not v.ok then fail(v.line .. biggest_three()) end print(v.line) end

name: cookbook/check_page_links.shale
html: -- This recipe checks every link and image on a web page: each `href` and -- `src` the page holds, a relative one resolved against the page's own URL, -- asked for with a HEAD (a GET when a server refuses HEAD), so a big page -- costs its headers only, and followed through up to five redirects. It -- prints each one whose last answer isn't 200, then each that landed well -- only after a redirect (`moved:`, a link worth updating), then the counts. A page -- the check can't fetch stops it. `outside=0` checks only the page's own -- site; `most=N` stops after N links. -- -- shale cookbook:check_page_links.shale url=http://127.0.0.1:9210/ -- shale cookbook:check_page_links.shale url=https://roc.lynrummy.com/ outside=0 -- -- Each link is one program, so a page of more links than the run's -- `programs` budget (1,000 unset) wants `--budget programs=N`. -- -- budget: steps=200000000 const URL = arg("url", "") const OUTSIDE = arg("outside", 1) const MOST = arg("most", 500) if URL == "" then fail("check_page_links: say `url=`, the page to check") end not_option("check_page_links", "url", URL) -- The page's origin (`https://host`) and its folder (`https://host/a/`). function origin_of(url) local m = re_find(url, "^(https?://[^/]+)") if m == nil then fail("check_page_links: " .. url .. " is not an http:// or https:// address") end return m.groups[1] end function folder_of(url) local after = sub(url, #origin_of(url) + 1) local m = re_find(after, "^(.*/)") if m == nil then return origin_of(url) .. "/" end return origin_of(url) .. m.groups[1] end -- A link as an absolute URL, or nil for one this check passes by: a fragment, -- mailto: and javascript: links, and data: images. function resolved(link, page) if link == "" or starts_with(link, "#") or starts_with(link, "mailto:") or starts_with(link, "javascript:") or starts_with(link, "data:") then return nil end if starts_with(link, "http://") or starts_with(link, "https://") then return link end if starts_with(link, "//") then return sub(origin_of(page), 1, find(origin_of(page), "//") - 1) .. link end if starts_with(link, "/") then return origin_of(page) .. link end return folder_of(page) .. link end -- One request's answer: a HEAD, or a GET when the server refuses HEAD. function asked(url) local r = attempt(http, "HEAD", url, {timeout_ms = 20000}) if r.ok and r.value.status ~= 405 and r.value.status ~= 403 then return r.value end local g = attempt(http_get, url, {timeout_ms = 20000}) if g.ok then return g.value end return {status = 0, headers = {}, error = g.error} end -- Where a link ends, following up to five redirects: `{status, url, error}`, -- `url` the last one asked for. function landing_of(url) local at = url for hop = 1, 6 do local r = asked(at) local where = get(r.headers, "location", "") local moved = r.status == 301 or r.status == 302 or r.status == 303 or r.status == 307 or r.status == 308 if not moved or where == "" or hop == 6 then return {status = r.status, url = at, error = get(r, "error", "")} end at = resolved(where, at) end end local page = http_get(URL, {timeout_ms = 20000}) if page.status ~= 200 then fail("check_page_links: " .. URL .. " answered " .. page.status) end local seen = {} local links = {} for m in re_find_all(page.body, "(?:href|src)=\"([^\"]*)\"") do local u = resolved(m.groups[1], URL) if u ~= nil and not has_key(seen, u) then seen[u] = true if OUTSIDE == 1 or starts_with(u, origin_of(URL)) then push(links, u) end end end local bad = 0 local checked = 0 local moved = {} for u in links do if checked >= MOST then break end checked = checked + 1 local r = landing_of(u) local note = "" if r.url ~= u then note = " (moved to " .. r.url .. ")" end if r.status == 0 then note = " (" .. sub(r.error, 1, 80) .. ")" end if r.status ~= 200 then bad = bad + 1 print(r.status .. " " .. u .. note) elseif r.url ~= u then push(moved, u .. " -> " .. r.url) end end -- A link that lands well after a redirect works, but is worth updating. for m in moved do print("moved: " .. m) end local cut = "" if checked < #links then cut = " (most=" .. MOST .. ": " .. (#links - checked) .. " not checked)" end print(checked .. " links checked on " .. URL .. ", " .. bad .. " not 200, " .. #moved .. " moved" .. cut)

name: cookbook/check_recipe_names.shale
html: -- budget: steps=50000000 reads=20000 read_bytes=50000000 output_bytes=1000000 -- Checks that every cookbook recipe is named for what it does, in the words a -- newcomer expects. From Shale's root: -- -- shale cookbook/check_recipe_names.shale the gate: fails on any break -- shale cookbook/check_recipe_names.shale report=1 the same list, passing -- shale cookbook/check_recipe_names.shale self_test=1 its plants, then the cookbook -- -- `dir=` names another tree of recipes (`cookbook` by default) and `verbs=` -- another verb table (`cookbook/recipe_verbs.txt`). A `plants` folder is -- skipped: its files are a self-test's, named to break the rules. -- -- A recipe is one of two kinds, told from its code. A library is a file whose -- top level holds only `const` and `function` declarations, the language's -- own rule for what `use` loads (SHALE.md, "Libraries: `use`"); every other -- file runs. The rules: -- -- not_snake_case the name is lower-case words joined by `_`; -- runnable_without_verb a recipe that runs starts with a verb of the table; -- library_named_like_command a library starts with no verb of the table. -- -- Each break is printed as `path kind rules suggested`, then the counts. -- A suggestion is a start for the rename, never a verdict: a verb later in the -- name moves to the front (`name_hunt` to `hunt_name`), else the first verb of -- the header's opening sentence goes in front (`Finds ...` gives `find_`), -- else it says `<verb>_`. A library's leading verb moves to the end. -- -- `self_test=1` judges the plants, then the cookbook itself, so `zig build -- test` (its `cookbook-test`) fails on any break. COOKBOOK_ENFORCED false -- would only count the cookbook's breaks, on the last line. use("cookbook:findings.shale") const COOKBOOK_ENFORCED = true const PLANTS = "cookbook/plants/check_recipe_names" -- Each plant's name, its kind, the rules it breaks and the name suggested. const PLANT_VERDICTS = { {"find_negatives.shale", "runnable", "", ""}, {"merge_conflicts.shale", "library", "", ""}, {"report_rows.shale", "runnable", "", ""}, {"check_findings.shale", "library", "library_named_like_command", "findings_check.shale"}, {"disk_space.shale", "runnable", "runnable_without_verb", "find_disk_space.shale"}, {"name_hunt.shale", "runnable", "runnable_without_verb", "hunt_name.shale"}, {"totals.shale", "runnable", "runnable_without_verb", "<verb>_totals.shale"}, {"checkDisk.shale", "runnable", "not_snake_case", "check_disk.shale"}, {"Disk-Space.shale", "runnable", "not_snake_case,runnable_without_verb", "find_disk_space.shale"}, {"negatives.shale", "runnable", "runnable_without_verb", "find_negatives.shale (taken)"}, } -- The verbs of the table at `path`, as a set: one a line, `#` lines and blank -- ones skipped. function verb_table(path) if not exists(path) then fail("check_recipe_names: no verb table " .. path) end local verbs = {} for raw in lines(read(path)) do local l = trim(raw) if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then if re_find(l, "^[a-z]+$") == nil then fail("check_recipe_names: " .. path .. ": `" .. l .. "` is no plain lower-case verb") end if has_key(verbs, l) then fail("check_recipe_names: " .. path .. ": `" .. l .. "` is listed twice") end verbs[l] = true end end if #keys(verbs) == 0 then fail("check_recipe_names: " .. path .. " lists no verbs") end return verbs end -- `library` when every line that starts a statement at the top level starts -- with `const` or `function`, else `runnable`. A token opens a level when it -- is `function`, `if` or `do` (closed by `end`) or a bracket. function recipe_kind(path) local opens = set_of({"kw_function", "kw_if", "kw_do", "lbrace", "lparen", "lbracket"}) local closes = set_of({"kw_end", "rbrace", "rparen", "rbracket"}) local depth = 0 local last_line = 0 local starts = 0 local declarations = 0 for t in shale_tokens(path) do if t.tag ~= "comment" then if depth == 0 and t.line ~= last_line then starts = starts + 1 if t.tag == "kw_const" or t.tag == "kw_function" then declarations = declarations + 1 end end last_line = t.line if has_key(opens, t.tag) then depth = depth + 1 end if has_key(closes, t.tag) then depth = depth - 1 end end end if depth ~= 0 then fail("check_recipe_names: " .. path .. ": its blocks don't balance (" .. depth .. " left open)") end if starts > 0 and starts == declarations then return "library" end return "runnable" end -- `name` in snake_case: a capital starts a word, and `-` and spaces are `_`. function snake(name) local s = re_replace(name, "([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", "\\1_\\2") s = lower(re_replace(s, "[- ]+", "_")) return re_replace(s, "_+", "_") end -- The verb of the table that `word` is a form of (`finds`, `fetches`, -- `tidies`), or "". function verb_form(verbs, word) local w = lower(word) local stems = {w} if ends_with(w, "ies") then push(stems, sub(w, 1, #w - 3) .. "y") end if ends_with(w, "es") then push(stems, sub(w, 1, #w - 2)) end if ends_with(w, "s") then push(stems, sub(w, 1, #w - 1)) end for s in stems do if s ~= "" and has_key(verbs, s) then return s end end return "" end -- The first sentence of the comment that opens the file at `path`, a -- `-- budget:` line skipped. function header_sentence(path) local text = "" for l in lines(read(path)) do if not starts_with(l, "--") then break end if not starts_with(l, "-- budget:") then local body = trim(sub(l, 3)) if body == "" and text ~= "" then break end text = text .. " " .. body end end local m = re_find(text, "^([^.]*)") if m == nil then return "" end return m.group end -- The first verb of the table in `path`'s opening sentence, or "". A word -- right after a determiner is a noun (`This lint finds`, `A run stopped`). function header_verb(verbs, path) local determiners = set_of({"a", "an", "the", "this", "that", "each", "every", "its", "one"}) local after_determiner = false for w in words(header_sentence(path)) do local plain = re_replace(w, "[^A-Za-z]", "") if not after_determiner then local v = verb_form(verbs, plain) if v ~= "" then return v end end after_determiner = has_key(determiners, lower(plain)) end return "" end -- The numbers from `first` to `last`, a list (none when `last` < `first`). function range_list(first, last) local l = {} local i = first while i <= last do push(l, i) i = i + 1 end return l end -- The name suggested for a recipe of `kind` whose snake_case stem is `stem`. function suggested_stem(verbs, kind, stem, path) local parts = split(stem, "_") if kind == "library" then if has_key(verbs, parts[1]) and #parts > 1 then return join(drop(parts, 1), "_") .. "_" .. parts[1] end return stem end if has_key(verbs, parts[1]) then return stem end for i in range_list(2, #parts) do if has_key(verbs, parts[i]) then local rest = {} for j in range_list(1, #parts) do if j ~= i then push(rest, parts[j]) end end return parts[i] .. "_" .. join(rest, "_") end end local v = header_verb(verbs, path) if v == "" then v = "<verb>" end return v .. "_" .. stem end -- The verdict on one recipe: `{path, kind, rules, suggested}`, `rules` the -- names of the rules it breaks joined by `,` ("" when it passes). function judged_recipe(verbs, path) local kind = recipe_kind(path) local name = basename(path) if not ends_with(name, ".shale") then fail("check_recipe_names: " .. path .. " is no .shale file") end local stem = sub(name, 1, #name - 6) local broken = {} if re_find(stem, "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$") == nil then push(broken, "not_snake_case") end local fixed = snake(stem) local first = split(fixed, "_")[1] if kind == "runnable" and not has_key(verbs, first) then push(broken, "runnable_without_verb") end if kind == "library" and has_key(verbs, first) then push(broken, "library_named_like_command") end local suggested = "" if #broken > 0 then suggested = suggested_stem(verbs, kind, fixed, path) .. ".shale" if not starts_with(suggested, "<verb>") and exists(path_under(dirname(path), suggested)) then suggested = suggested .. " (taken)" end end return {path = path, kind = kind, rules = join(broken, ","), suggested = suggested} end -- The recipes under `dir`, every `.shale` file outside a `plants` folder. function recipes_in(dir) local found = {} for p in glob(dir .. "/**/*.shale") do local rel = sub(p, #dir + 2) if not starts_with(rel, "plants/") and find(rel, "/plants/") == nil then push(found, p) end end return found end -- The verdict on the tree at `dir`: `{rows, breaks, summary}`, `rows` every -- recipe's verdict and `breaks` those that break a rule. function judged_tree(verbs, dir) local rows = {} local breaks = {} local by_kind = {} local by_rule = {} local paths = recipes_in(dir) if #paths == 0 then fail("check_recipe_names: no recipes under " .. dir) end for p in paths do local v = judged_recipe(verbs, p) push(rows, v) incr(by_kind, v.kind) if v.rules ~= "" then push(breaks, v) for r in split(v.rules, ",") do incr(by_rule, r) end end yield() end local rule_counts = {} for r in {"not_snake_case", "runnable_without_verb", "library_named_like_command"} do push(rule_counts, r .. " " .. get(by_rule, r, 0)) end local summary = "check_recipe_names: " .. dir .. ": " .. #breaks .. " of " .. #rows .. " recipes break the naming standard (" .. get(by_kind, "runnable", 0) .. " runnable, " .. get(by_kind, "library", 0) .. " libraries); " .. join(rule_counts, ", ") return {rows = rows, breaks = breaks, summary = summary} end -- The breaks as a table's lines, for print_findings. function break_lines(breaks) if #breaks == 0 then return {} end return split(table(breaks, {"path", "kind", "rules", "suggested"}), "\n") end if arg("self_test", "") ~= "" then local verbs = verb_table(arg("verbs", "cookbook/recipe_verbs.txt")) local wrong = {} for c in PLANT_VERDICTS do local path = PLANTS .. "/" .. c[1] if not exists(path) then push(wrong, c[1] .. ": no such plant") else local v = judged_recipe(verbs, path) local got = v.kind .. " [" .. v.rules .. "] " .. v.suggested local want = c[2] .. " [" .. c[3] .. "] " .. c[4] if got ~= want then push(wrong, c[1] .. ": want " .. want .. ", got " .. got) end end end -- Every plant is in the table above, so a new one can't pass unjudged. local tree = judged_tree(verbs, PLANTS) if #tree.rows ~= #PLANT_VERDICTS then push(wrong, PLANTS .. " holds " .. #tree.rows .. " plants, the table " .. #PLANT_VERDICTS) end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail(tostring(#wrong) .. " check_recipe_names plants wrong") end local cookbook = judged_tree(verbs, "cookbook") if COOKBOOK_ENFORCED and #cookbook.breaks > 0 then print_findings(cookbook.summary, break_lines(cookbook.breaks)) fail(cookbook.summary) end local mode = "enforced" if not COOKBOOK_ENFORCED then mode = "report mode, COOKBOOK_ENFORCED false" end print("check_recipe_names: " .. #PLANT_VERDICTS .. " plants as they say; the cookbook: " .. #cookbook.breaks .. " of " .. #cookbook.rows .. " recipes break the standard (" .. mode .. ")") else local verbs = verb_table(arg("verbs", "cookbook/recipe_verbs.txt")) local tree = judged_tree(verbs, arg("dir", "cookbook")) print_findings(tree.summary, break_lines(tree.breaks)) if #tree.breaks > 0 and arg("report", "") == "" then fail(tree.summary) end end

name: cookbook/check_seals.shale
html: -- budget: steps=500000000 -- This recipe checks that a sealed value is made by its check alone. A sealed -- value is checked once and passed on as a type only its check can make, so a -- caller that skips the check does not compile. Zig has no private fields, so -- such a type carries a seal, a field of size zero that only its own file -- sets: -- -- pub const Id = struct { text: []const u8, id_seal: Seal = undefined }; -- -- is wrong (a default makes the seal anyone's); it is -- -- const Seal = struct {}; -- pub const Id = struct { -- text: []const u8, -- id_seal: Seal, -- pub fn of(s: []const u8) ?Id { ...; return .{ .text = s, .id_seal = .{} }; } -- }; -- -- A literal without the seal does not compile; this refuses one that sets -- it, `.id_seal =` read from Zig's tokens (a string or a comment is never -- code), anywhere but the seal's own file, its tests too. A payload is -- sealed the same way: name it as only its file does -- (`player_id`, not `text`), read it by a method, and list it as a seal, -- so a change to a value already made (`id.player_id = raw`) is refused too. -- -- shale cookbook:check_seals.shale dir=zig-server/src seals=id_seal:zig-server/src/player.zig -- shale cookbook:check_seals.shale dir=zig-webbox/src,dog-park/src seals=target_path:zig-webbox/src/http.zig headers=location:zig-webbox/src/http.zig -- -- `dir` is one tree or several (a consumer's beside its library's), and a -- seal's file is named from the root. With `headers=name:file`, a header of -- that name may be set (`.name = "location"`, any case) in that file only, so a -- response cannot carry one its checked helper did not make. -- -- One line a finding, then PASS or a FAIL that stops the run. What it cannot -- see: `@bitCast`, `@field`, `std.mem.zeroes` or `undefined` for a whole -- value, and a header named through a variable; each is a review's to -- refuse. const DIR = arg("dir", "") const SEALS = arg("seals", "") const HEADERS = arg("headers", "") if DIR == "" or (SEALS == "" and HEADERS == "") then fail("sealed: say `dir=<tree>[,<tree>...]` and `seals=field:file,...` or `headers=name:file,...`") end -- `field:file` pairs, each file there. function pairs_of(spec, what) local out = {} if spec == "" then return out end for s in split(spec, ",") do local parts = split(trim(s), ":") if #parts ~= 2 or parts[1] == "" or parts[2] == "" then fail("sealed: `" .. s .. "` is not `" .. what .. ":file`") end if not exists(parts[2]) then fail("sealed: " .. parts[1] .. "'s file " .. parts[2] .. " is not there") end out[parts[1]] = parts[2] end return out end local owner = pairs_of(SEALS, "field") local header_owner = {} for name in keys(pairs_of(HEADERS, "name")) do header_owner["\"" .. lower(name) .. "\""] = pairs_of(HEADERS, "name")[name] end -- The seals and headers `path` sets outside their own file, a line each; how many. function scan(path, owner, header_owner) -- Zig's tokens only for a file that names one at all. local text = read(path) local low = lower(text) local named = false for field in keys(owner) do if find(text, field) ~= nil then named = true end end for h in keys(header_owner) do if find(low, h) ~= nil then named = true end end if not named then return 0 end local found = 0 local p3 = nil local p2 = nil local p1 = nil for t in zig_tokens(path) do if p2 ~= nil and p2.tag == "period" and p1.tag == "identifier" and t.tag == "equal" and has_key(owner, p1.text) and owner[p1.text] ~= path then print("FAIL " .. path .. ":" .. t.line .. ": sets `" .. p1.text .. "`, which only " .. owner[p1.text] .. " may") found = found + 1 end if p3 ~= nil and p3.tag == "period" and p2.text == "name" and p1.tag == "equal" and t.tag == "string_literal" and has_key(header_owner, lower(t.text)) and header_owner[lower(t.text)] ~= path then print("FAIL " .. path .. ":" .. t.line .. ": sets a " .. t.text .. " header, which only " .. header_owner[lower(t.text)] .. " may") found = found + 1 end p3 = p2 p2 = p1 p1 = t end return found end local found = 0 local files = 0 for d in split(DIR, ",") do for e in walk_all(trim(d), {like = "*.zig"}) do if e.kind == "file" then files = files + 1 found = found + scan(e.path, owner, header_owner) -- A file's tokens are done with: a tree of any size fits. yield() end end end if found > 0 then fail("sealed: FAIL: " .. found .. " set outside their file: make the value with its check, and a header with its helper") end print("sealed: PASS (" .. files .. " files)")

name: cookbook/check_syntax.shale
html: -- This recipe checks that each file's syntax survived an edit, with the -- check that fits the file's kind. It prints one line a file, `ok` or the -- first error, then PASS, or a FAIL that stops the run, so no one has to -- remember each language's own command. -- -- shale cookbook:check_syntax.shale files=src/a.zig,roc/Walk.roc,tools/x.mjs -- shale cookbook:check_syntax.shale rev=HEAD~1..HEAD repo=repos:dog-park -- -- By kind: -- - `.zig`: `zig ast-check`, and `zig fmt --check` said apart (`fmt:`); -- - `.zon`: `zig fmt --check`; -- - `.roc`: `roc check` (an app or a module alike: a module's imports -- resolve from its folder); its warnings are no failure; -- - `.js`, `.mjs`: `node --check`; -- - `.shale`: `shale --check` (`shale=` names the binary, default `shale`); -- - `.py`: Python's own parser (`ast.parse`, which writes no `.pyc` as -- `py_compile` would), every file in one run, as a tool exception -- (`want`); -- - `.sh`: `bash -n`, as a tool exception; -- - `.md` and any other kind: nothing to check, said. -- -- It takes one program a file, one for every Python file, and one `zig fmt` -- for every Zig file; more than the run's `programs` budget is refused before -- the first. -- -- The tools are values (`zig=`, `roc=`, `node=`, each its name on PATH by -- default, or a path): a machine's PATH is not the build's. When the -- machine lacks a tool, the recipe says so instead of passing or failing: its files -- are `skip`, a line says `no <tool>: .<kind> files not checked`, and the -- PASS counts them apart. const FILES = arg("files", "") const REV = arg("rev", "") const REPO = arg("repo", ".") const SHALE = arg("shale", "shale") const ZIG = arg("zig", "zig") const ROC = arg("roc", "roc") const NODE = arg("node", "node") const MINUTES = arg("minutes", 5) not_option("syntax", "rev", REV) if FILES == "" and REV == "" then fail("syntax: say `files=a,b` or `rev=<range>`") end local paths = {} if FILES ~= "" then for p in split(FILES, ",") do if trim(p) ~= "" then push(paths, trim(p)) end end end if REV ~= "" then for p in lines(git_call(REPO, {"diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=d", REV, "--"}, nil, true, nil).out) do if p ~= "" then push(paths, path_under(REPO, p)) end end end for p in paths do not_option("syntax", "file", p) end function kind_of(p) local m = re_find(p, "\\.([A-Za-z0-9]+)$") if m == nil then return "" end return lower(m.group) end -- The line a tool's output says first went wrong: its own marker when it -- has one, else the first that says error, else the first at all. function first_error(out) local first = "" for l in lines(out) do if first == "" and trim(l) ~= "" then first = trim(l) end if starts_with(l, "── ✗") or starts_with(l, "── stopped") or re_match(l, "[Ee]rror") then return trim(l) end end return first end local by = {zig = {}, zon = {}, roc = {}, js = {}, shale = {}, py = {}, sh = {}, other = {}} for p in paths do local k = kind_of(p) if k == "mjs" then k = "js" end if not has_key(by, k) then k = "other" end push(by[k], p) end local programs = #by.zig + #by.roc + #by.js + #by.shale + #by.sh if #by.py > 0 then programs = programs + 1 end if #by.zig + #by.zon > 0 then programs = programs + 1 end if programs > budget().programs then fail("syntax: " .. #paths .. " files need " .. programs .. " programs, and this run's `programs` budget has " .. budget().programs .. ": check them in parts, or launch with `--budget programs=N`") end local verdict = {} -- Whether this machine has a tool: one not found is false, any other -- failure stops the run. function probe(argv) return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 2, want = "tool: whether this machine has it"}) end function has_tool(argv) local r = attempt(probe, argv) if r.ok then return true end if contains(r.error, "not found") then return false end fail("syntax: " .. argv[1] .. ": " .. r.error) end -- Each kind whose tool is missing: its files skipped, the line that says so. local missing = {} local skipped = 0 for k in {{kinds = {"zig", "zon"}, argv = {ZIG, "version"}, ext = ".zig and .zon"}, {kinds = {"roc"}, argv = {ROC, "version"}, ext = ".roc"}, {kinds = {"js"}, argv = {NODE, "--version"}, ext = ".js and .mjs"}} do local n = 0 for kind in k.kinds do n = n + #by[kind] end if n > 0 and not has_tool(k.argv) then push(missing, "no " .. k.argv[1] .. ": " .. k.ext .. " files not checked") for kind in k.kinds do for p in by[kind] do verdict[p] = "skip " .. p .. ": no " .. k.argv[1] skipped = skipped + 1 end by[kind] = {} end end end function say(verdict, p, bad, why) if bad then verdict[p] = "FAIL " .. p .. ": " .. why else verdict[p] = "ok " .. p .. why end return nil end -- A file's program, by its kind. function argv_of(kind, f) if kind == "zig" then return {ZIG, "ast-check", f} end if kind == "js" then return {NODE, "--check", f} end if kind == "shale" then return {SHALE, "--check", f} end return {"bash", "-n", f} end -- One program a file, its verdict by its exit. function each(verdict, kind, files) for p in files do local opts = {timeout_ms = MINUTES * 60000, tail = 60} if kind == "sh" then opts.want = "tool: a shell script's syntax, by bash's own parser" end if kind == "shale" and contains(SHALE, "/") then opts.want = "tool: the shale binary named by `shale=`" end if kind == "js" then opts.want = "tool: JavaScript's syntax, by node's own parser" end if kind == "zig" and contains(ZIG, "/") then opts.want = "tool: the zig named by `zig=`" end local r = run(argv_of(kind, real(p)), opts) if r.ended ~= "exit" then say(verdict, p, true, "did not finish (" .. r.ended .. ")") elseif r.code == 0 then say(verdict, p, false, "") else say(verdict, p, true, first_error(r.out)) end end return nil end local o = {timeout_ms = MINUTES * 60000, tail = 60} each(verdict, "zig", by.zig) each(verdict, "js", by.js) each(verdict, "shale", by.shale) each(verdict, "sh", by.sh) -- `roc check` exits 2 on warnings alone: its count of errors decides. for p in by.roc do local ro = {timeout_ms = o.timeout_ms, tail = o.tail} if contains(ROC, "/") then ro.want = "tool: the roc named by `roc=`" end local r = run({ROC, "check", real(p)}, ro) local clean = contains(r.out, "No errors found") or re_match(r.out, "── 0 errors") if r.ended ~= "exit" then say(verdict, p, true, "did not finish (" .. r.ended .. ")") elseif clean then say(verdict, p, false, "") else say(verdict, p, true, first_error(r.out)) end end -- Every Python file in one run; each failure on a line of its own. if #by.py > 0 then local argv = {"python3", "-c", "import ast,sys\nbad=0\nfor p in sys.argv[1:]:\n try: ast.parse(open(p,'rb').read(), p)\n except SyntaxError as e:\n print(p + ':' + str(e.lineno) + ': ' + str(e.msg)); bad=1\nsys.exit(bad)"} local real_of = {} for p in by.py do push(argv, real(p)) real_of[real(p)] = p end local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = o.timeout_ms, tail = o.tail, want = "tool: Python's syntax, by Python's own parser"}) for p in by.py do say(verdict, p, false, "") end for l in lines(r.out) do local m = re_find(l, "^([^:]+):") if m ~= nil and has_key(real_of, m.group) then local p = real_of[m.group] verdict[p] = "FAIL " .. p .. ": " .. l end end end -- `zig fmt --check` once for every Zig and ZON file: it names each it would change. local fmt = {} for p in by.zig do push(fmt, p) end for p in by.zon do push(fmt, p) end if #fmt > 0 then local argv = {ZIG, "fmt", "--check"} local real_of = {} for p in fmt do push(argv, real(p)) real_of[real(p)] = p end local fo = {timeout_ms = o.timeout_ms, tail = o.tail} if contains(ZIG, "/") then fo.want = "tool: the zig named by `zig=`" end local r = run(argv, fo) for p in by.zon do say(verdict, p, false, "") end for l in lines(r.out) do local f = trim(l) if has_key(real_of, f) then local p = real_of[f] verdict[p] = "FAIL " .. p .. ": fmt: zig fmt would change it" elseif contains(f, ": error:") then for p in by.zon do if contains(f, real(p)) then verdict[p] = "FAIL " .. p .. ": " .. f end end end end end for p in by.other do verdict[p] = "ok " .. p .. " (no check for this kind)" end local failed = 0 for p in paths do print(verdict[p]) if starts_with(verdict[p], "FAIL") then failed = failed + 1 end end for m in missing do print(m) end if failed > 0 then fail("syntax: FAIL, " .. failed .. " of " .. #paths .. " files") end if skipped > 0 then print("PASS: " .. (#paths - skipped) .. " files, " .. skipped .. " not checked") else print("PASS: " .. #paths .. " files") end

name: cookbook/color_shale.shale
html: -- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 reads=2000 changes=2000 change_bytes=64000000 -- This colors Shale with Shale. Each file comes out as a page holding one -- <pre><code class="language-shale"> with spans around its comments, strings, -- numbers, keywords and the names `function` declares. The class names are the -- Roc coloring's, so the Safari book's book.css serves unchanged. Shale has no -- types, so `syn-type` never appears. -- -- shale cookbook:color_shale.shale files=cookbook/look.shale out=colored -- -- `files=` is a comma list, and `a/b.shale` comes out as `<out>/a/b.shale.html`. -- A page links the stylesheet `css=` names, `book.css` unless told. -- -- The tokens are `shale_tokens`', the language's own lexer, comments among them. -- This recipe adds only the class of each. A file must also pass `shale --check`, -- so a file that lexes but doesn't compile gets no page either. Every byte must -- be in a token or be space between tokens, or the file is refused: nothing is -- guessed. -- -- A refused file gets no page, and the run says why and fails at its end. The -- text of a page with its spans taken away must equal the source's escaped text -- byte for byte, or the run stops there. Each file costs one program, and a run -- holds 64, so a bigger tree goes in parts. -- -- `self_test=1` proves both sides of each rule on sources written here. const FILES = arg("files", "") const OUT = arg("out", "") const CSS = arg("css", "book.css") const SHALE = arg("shale", "shale") const OPEN = "<pre><code class=\"language-shale\">" const CLOSE = "</code></pre>" const OUR_SPANS = "<span class=\"syn-[a-z]+\">|</span>" const CLASSES = {"syn-comment", "syn-string", "syn-number", "syn-keyword", "syn-name"} const CLASS_OF_TAG = {comment = "syn-comment", string = "syn-string", int = "syn-number"} function escaped(text) local s = join(split(text, "&"), "&") s = join(split(s, "<"), "<") s = join(split(s, ">"), ">") s = join(split(s, "\""), """) return join(split(s, "'"), "'") end function refuse(text, at, why) fail("line " .. #split(sub(text, 1, at), "\n") .. ": " .. why) end -- A name is `syn-name` right after `function`, and a comment between them -- doesn't end the wait for it. function class_of(tag, previous_tag) if tag == "name" and previous_tag == "kw_function" then return "syn-name" end if starts_with(tag, "kw_") then return "syn-keyword" end return get(CLASS_OF_TAG, tag, "") end -- Sets each token's `class`, "" for a name or a symbol. function classify(tokens) local previous_tag = "" for token in tokens do token.class = class_of(token.tag, previous_tag) if token.tag ~= "comment" then previous_tag = token.tag end end return tokens end -- Refuses unless the tokens hold `text`: each one's bytes are where it says, in -- order, with only space around them. function check_placed(text, tokens) local at = 0 for token in tokens do if token.start < at then refuse(text, token.start + 1, "a token overlaps the one before it") end if trim(sub(text, at + 1, token.start)) ~= "" then refuse(text, at + 1, "bytes no token holds") end if sub(text, token.start + 1, token.stop) ~= token.text then refuse(text, token.start + 1, "a token that isn't where it says") end at = token.stop end if trim(sub(text, at + 1, #text)) ~= "" then refuse(text, at + 1, "bytes no token holds") end return nil end -- The classed tokens of the file at `path`, whose text is `text`. function placed_tokens(path, text) local tokens = shale_tokens(path) check_placed(text, tokens) return classify(tokens) end function span(class, text) return "<span class=\"" .. class .. "\">" .. text .. "</span>" end -- `text` in HTML, each classed token in a span. A span can cross lines, which a -- <pre> takes as it comes. function colored(text, tokens) local pieces = {} local at = 1 for token in tokens do if token.class ~= "" then push(pieces, escaped(sub(text, at, token.start))) push(pieces, span(token.class, escaped(sub(text, token.start + 1, token.stop)))) at = token.stop + 1 end end push(pieces, escaped(sub(text, at, #text))) return join(pieces, "") end function without_our_spans(html) return re_replace(html, OUR_SPANS, "") end function check_text(path, text, html) if without_our_spans(html) ~= escaped(text) then fail("color_shale: coloring changed the text of " .. path) end return nil end function page(path, html) return "<!doctype html>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<title>" .. escaped(path) .. "</title>\n<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"" .. escaped(CSS) .. "\">\n" .. OPEN .. html .. CLOSE .. "\n" end function first_line(out) for l in lines(out) do if trim(l) ~= "" then return trim(l) end end return "no output" end -- A mount's name makes a folder, as `cookbook:a.shale` has no place under `out` -- otherwise. function page_path(path, out) return out .. "/" .. substitute(path, ":", "/", {missing_ok = true}) .. ".html" end -- Writes the file's page, or says why not in `tally.refused`. function color_file(path, out, tally) local checked = run({SHALE, "--check", real(path)}, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 4}) if checked.code ~= 0 then push(tally.refused, path .. ": " .. first_line(checked.out)) return nil end local text = read(path) local got = attempt(placed_tokens, path, text) if not got.ok then push(tally.refused, path .. ": " .. got.error) return nil end local html = colored(text, got.value) check_text(path, text, html) for token in got.value do if token.class ~= "" then incr(tally.counts, token.class) end end local target = page_path(path, out) mkdir(dirname(target)) replace(target, page(path, html)) tally.colored = tally.colored + 1 return nil end function color_files(paths, out, programs_left) if #paths > programs_left then fail("color_shale: " .. #paths .. " files need " .. #paths .. " programs, and this run's `programs` budget has " .. programs_left .. ": color them in parts, or launch with `--budget programs=N`") end local tally = {colored = 0, refused = {}, counts = {}} for class in CLASSES do tally.counts[class] = 0 end for path in paths do color_file(path, out, tally) end return tally end -- `shale_tokens` reads a file, so a source goes through one in the test's folder. function source_tokens(checks, source) local path = checks.folder .. "/source.shale" replace(path, source) return placed_tokens(path, source) end -- `expect_html` holds a source to its exact HTML, and the guard to it too. function expect_html(checks, what, source, want) local html = colored(source, source_tokens(checks, source)) if html ~= want then fail("self_test: " .. what .. " gave [" .. html .. "], not [" .. want .. "]") end check_text(what, source, html) push(checks.passed, what) return nil end function expect_refused(checks, source, why) local got = attempt(source_tokens, checks, source) if got.ok or not contains(got.error, why) then fail("self_test: [" .. source .. "] gave " .. json_write(got)) end push(checks.passed, "refused: " .. source) return nil end function expect_misplaced(checks, what, text, tokens, why) local got = attempt(check_placed, text, tokens) if got.ok or not contains(got.error, why) then fail("self_test: " .. what .. " gave " .. json_write(got)) end push(checks.passed, what) return nil end function c(text) return span("syn-comment", text) end function s(text) return span("syn-string", text) end function n(text) return span("syn-number", text) end function k(text) return span("syn-keyword", text) end function f(text) return span("syn-name", text) end function test_comments_and_strings(checks) expect_html(checks, "a `--` in each kind of string, then a comment at the line's end", "x = \"a -- b\" -- c\ny = 'd -- e'\nz = [=[f -- g]=] -- h\n", "x = " .. s(""a -- b"") .. " " .. c("-- c") .. "\ny = " .. s("'d -- e'") .. "\nz = " .. s("[=[f -- g]=]") .. " " .. c("-- h") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a comment's quote opens no string", "-- it's \"so\n1\n", c("-- it's "so") .. "\n" .. n("1") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "an escaped quote stays in, and an escaped backslash doesn't hide the end", "\"a\\\"b\" \"c\\\\\" -- d\n", s(""a\\"b"") .. " " .. s(""c\\\\"") .. " " .. c("-- d") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "the other quote inside a string", "\"it's\" 'a \"b\"'\n", s(""it's"") .. " " .. s("'a "b"'") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a long string over lines, holding what would start or end others", "x = [=[\n-- no \"comment\n]] end\n]=] -- yes\n", "x = " .. s("[=[\n-- no "comment\n]] end\n]=]") .. " " .. c("-- yes") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a higher level holds a lower closer", "[==[a ]=] b]==] 1\n", s("[==[a ]=] b]==]") .. " " .. n("1") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a block comment over lines, with code after its closer", "--[=[ it's\nend \"x ]=] y = 1\n", c("--[=[ it's\nend "x ]=]") .. " y = " .. n("1") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "`--[=x` is a line comment", "--[=x\n1 --[==y ]==]\n2\n", c("--[=x") .. "\n" .. n("1") .. " " .. c("--[==y ]==]") .. "\n" .. n("2") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "`--` needs no space and takes an expression with it", "a--1\nb - -1\n", "a" .. c("--1") .. "\nb - -" .. n("1") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a comment at the end of a file, with no newline", "1 -- a", n("1") .. " " .. c("-- a")) expect_html(checks, "a bare `--` at the end", "--", c("--")) expect_html(checks, "a CR stays in the comment it ends", "-- a\r\n1\r\n", c("-- a\r") .. "\n" .. n("1") .. "\r\n") expect_html(checks, "bytes past ASCII in a comment and a string", "-- é\n\"ñ\" 'ü' [=[ö]=]\n", c("-- é") .. "\n" .. s(""ñ"") .. " " .. s("'ü'") .. " " .. s("[=[ö]=]") .. "\n") return nil end function test_words_and_numbers(checks) expect_html(checks, "keywords inside names, on both sides", "end_col iffy do_it _end end1 Function nil_ok format\nend if do\n", "end_col iffy do_it _end end1 Function nil_ok format\n" .. k("end") .. " " .. k("if") .. " " .. k("do") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "every keyword", "and break const continue do else elseif end false for function if in local nil not or return then true while\n", k("and") .. " " .. k("break") .. " " .. k("const") .. " " .. k("continue") .. " " .. k("do") .. " " .. k("else") .. " " .. k("elseif") .. " " .. k("end") .. " " .. k("false") .. " " .. k("for") .. " " .. k("function") .. " " .. k("if") .. " " .. k("in") .. " " .. k("local") .. " " .. k("nil") .. " " .. k("not") .. " " .. k("or") .. " " .. k("return") .. " " .. k("then") .. " " .. k("true") .. " " .. k("while") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "`use` and `attempt` are names, as the lexer has them", "use attempt\n", "use attempt\n") expect_html(checks, "digits in a name, and a number beside a symbol", "a1 x2y 1..2 t[3]\n", "a1 x2y " .. n("1") .. ".." .. n("2") .. " t[" .. n("3") .. "]\n") expect_html(checks, "a function's name, and a call that is none", "function iffy(x)\n return iffy(x)\nend\n", k("function") .. " " .. f("iffy") .. "(x)\n " .. k("return") .. " iffy(x)\n" .. k("end") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "a comment between `function` and its name", "function --[=[ a ]=] b()\n", k("function") .. " " .. c("--[=[ a ]=]") .. " " .. f("b") .. "()\n") expect_html(checks, "a local named like the keyword declares no function", "local function_name = 1\nfunction_name2()\n", k("local") .. " function_name = " .. n("1") .. "\nfunction_name2()\n") expect_html(checks, "every symbol, in a row", "+ - * // % .. == ~= < <= > >= = ( ) { } [ ] , . # ? ;\n", "+ - * // % .. == ~= < <= > >= = ( ) { } [ ] , . # ? ;\n") expect_html(checks, "`]=` closes an index before an assignment", "t[1]=2\n", "t[" .. n("1") .. "]=" .. n("2") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "an empty file", "", "") return nil end function test_html(checks) expect_html(checks, "text that looks like our own span", "x = '<span class=\"syn-comment\">' -- </span>\n", "x = " .. s("'<span class="syn-comment">'") .. " " .. c("-- </span>") .. "\n") expect_html(checks, "an escape already in the source", "-- & <\n", c("-- &amp; &lt;") .. "\n") if not attempt(check_text, "p", "a < b", "a < " .. span("syn-name", "b")).ok then fail("self_test: added spans changed the text") end local changed = attempt(check_text, "p", "a b", "a " .. span("syn-name", "c")) if changed.ok or changed.error ~= "color_shale: coloring changed the text of p" then fail("self_test: changed text gave " .. json_write(changed)) end if attempt(check_text, "p", "<", span("syn-name", "<")).ok then fail("self_test: a lost escape passed") end if attempt(check_text, "p", "ab", span("syn-name", "a") .. "bb").ok then fail("self_test: a repeated byte passed") end local overlap = {{start = 0, stop = 2, class = "syn-name"}, {start = 1, stop = 2, class = "syn-name"}} if attempt(check_text, "p", "ab", colored("ab", overlap)).ok then fail("self_test: overlapping tokens passed") end push(checks.passed, "the text check, both sides") return nil end -- What the lexer refuses reaches a caller as its own words, with the line. function test_refusals(checks) expect_refused(checks, "\"abc", "no closing quote") expect_refused(checks, "\"a\nb\"", "past the end of its line") expect_refused(checks, "'a\"", "no closing quote") expect_refused(checks, "\"a\\", "no closing quote") expect_refused(checks, "\"a\\\nb\"", "an escape this language does not have") expect_refused(checks, "x\ny\n[=[ a", "line 3: a long string with no `]=]`") expect_refused(checks, "[==[ a ]=]", "with no `]==]`") expect_refused(checks, "--[=[ a", "a long comment with no `]=]`") expect_refused(checks, "[[a]]", "a long string needs a level") expect_refused(checks, "--[[a]]", "a long comment needs a level") expect_refused(checks, "[=a", "`[=` opens a long string") expect_refused(checks, "a @ b", "no token starts with") expect_refused(checks, "a / b", "use `//`") expect_refused(checks, "a ~ b", "bitwise") expect_refused(checks, "s:upper()", "method calls") expect_refused(checks, "local é = 1", "no token starts with") expect_refused(checks, "x = 1.5", "float") return nil end -- A token list that doesn't hold its text is refused, whichever way it fails. function test_placing(checks) local a = {text = "a", start = 0, stop = 1} local b = {text = "b", start = 2, stop = 3} check_placed(" a\tb\n", {{text = "a", start = 1, stop = 2}, {text = "b", start = 3, stop = 4}}) push(checks.passed, "tokens with only space around them") expect_misplaced(checks, "a byte between tokens", "a?b", {a, b}, "line 1: bytes no token holds") expect_misplaced(checks, "a byte before the first token", "\n?a", {{text = "a", start = 2, stop = 3}}, "line 2: bytes no token holds") expect_misplaced(checks, "a byte after the last token", "a b", {a}, "bytes no token holds") expect_misplaced(checks, "a token whose bytes are elsewhere", "a c", {a, b}, "isn't where it says") expect_misplaced(checks, "a token over the one before it", "ab", {{text = "ab", start = 0, stop = 2}, {text = "b", start = 1, stop = 2}}, "overlaps") return nil end -- A file `shale --check` refuses gets no page and fails the run's count, though -- `shale_tokens` would take an undeclared name, and a good file beside it still -- comes out. function test_files(checks) local folder = checks.folder replace(folder .. "/good.shale", "print(1) -- a\n") replace(folder .. "/undeclared.shale", "print(nobody)\n") replace(folder .. "/floats.shale", "print(1.5)\n") local tally = color_files({folder .. "/good.shale", folder .. "/undeclared.shale", folder .. "/floats.shale"}, folder .. "/out", budget().programs) if tally.colored ~= 1 or #tally.refused ~= 2 then fail("self_test: the file run gave " .. json_write(tally)) end if not contains(tally.refused[2], "float") then fail("self_test: the refusal said " .. tally.refused[2]) end if tally.counts["syn-comment"] ~= 1 or tally.counts["syn-number"] ~= 1 or tally.counts["syn-keyword"] ~= 0 then fail("self_test: the counts gave " .. json_write(tally.counts)) end local good = read(page_path(folder .. "/good.shale", folder .. "/out")) if not contains(good, OPEN .. "print(" .. n("1") .. ") " .. c("-- a") .. "\n" .. CLOSE) then fail("self_test: the page was [" .. good .. "]") end if #glob(folder .. "/out/**/*.html") ~= 1 then fail("self_test: a refused file left a page") end push(checks.passed, "a file run, with what the real lexer refuses") local too_many = {} for i = 1, 65 do push(too_many, "x.shale") end local over = attempt(color_files, too_many, folder .. "/out", 64) if over.ok or not contains(over.error, "`programs` budget has 64") then fail("self_test: 65 files gave " .. json_write(over)) end push(checks.passed, "more files than a run's programs") return nil end function self_test() local checks = {folder = fresh_dir("scratch:", "color-shale"), passed = {}} test_comments_and_strings(checks) test_words_and_numbers(checks) test_html(checks) test_refusals(checks) test_placing(checks) test_files(checks) remove_tree(checks.folder) print("color_shale self_test: PASS, " .. #checks.passed .. " checks") return nil end if arg("self_test", "") == "1" then self_test() else if FILES == "" or OUT == "" then fail("color_shale: files=a.shale,b.shale names the files, and out=DIR where their pages go") end local tally = color_files(split(FILES, ","), OUT, budget().programs) for why in tally.refused do print("color_shale: refused " .. why) end local counts = {} for class in CLASSES do push(counts, sub(class, 5, #class) .. "=" .. tally.counts[class]) end print("color_shale: " .. tally.colored .. " colored, " .. #tally.refused .. " refused, " .. join(counts, " ")) if #tally.refused > 0 then fail("color_shale: " .. #tally.refused .. " refused") end end

name: cookbook/count_shale_stops.shale
html: -- This recipe counts how an agent's Shale launches went, from a Claude Code -- transcript: each Bash call's command and the answer it got, paired by the -- call's id. A launch is a heredoc (`shale <<'TAG'`) or a script (`shale -- path.shale`). Each ends one of four ways: it ran, Shale stopped it (`── -- stopped at`), the gate refused the call before Shale saw it, or the -- harness denied it. A stop by the script's own `fail` is a check's verdict, -- counted apart; Shale's other stops are grouped by kind and by message, -- with quoted values blanked so that one mistake made twice counts as one -- line. The calls the heredocs make and the programs they `run` are counted -- too: where the agent works, and where it trips. -- -- With no `transcript=`, it reads the newest transcript under the -- `projects:` mount. `since=` is an ISO time; only the calls from then on -- count. `most=N` sets how many lines each list shows (20). -- -- shale cookbook:count_shale_stops.shale -- shale cookbook:count_shale_stops.shale since=2026-11-14T19:50 -- -- budget: steps=2000000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=4000000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const TRANSCRIPT = arg("transcript", "") const SINCE = arg("since", "") const MOST = arg("most", 20) const PART = 8 * 1024 * 1024 function newest_transcript() local best = nil local best_at = -1 for p in glob("projects:*/*.jsonl") do local s = stat(p) if s.modified > best_at then best = p best_at = s.modified end end if best == nil then fail("count_shale_stops: no transcript under projects:") end return best end -- Whether a JSON value read back is a list: Shale has no `type`, so by the -- first byte of its JSON. function is_list(v) return starts_with(json_write(v), "[") end -- A tool result's text: a string, or a list of parts with `text`. function result_text(content) if not is_list(content) then return content end local parts = {} for c in content do if has_key(c, "text") then push(parts, c.text) end end return join(parts, "\n") end function launch_kind(command) if find(command, "shale") == nil then return "" end if re_find(command, "shale[^\\n]*<<'[A-Za-z]+'") ~= nil then return "heredoc" end if re_find(command, "shale[^\\n]*\\.shale") ~= nil then return "script" end return "" end -- One stop's line, with quoted values blanked, for grouping. function stop_key(text) local m = re_find(text, "── stopped at [^:]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+[^:]*: ([^\\n]*)") if m == nil then return nil end local said = m.groups[1] local cut = find(said, " (") if cut ~= nil then said = sub(said, 1, cut - 1) end said = re_replace(said, "\"[^\"]*\"", "\"…\"") if #said > 110 then said = sub(said, 1, 110) .. "…" end return said end function bump(counts, key) counts[key] = get(counts, key, 0) + 1 end function ranked(counts) local rows = {} for k in keys(counts) do push(rows, {n = counts[k], what = k}) end sort(rows, "n", "desc") local top = {} for r in rows do if #top < MOST then push(top, r) end end return top end local path = TRANSCRIPT if path == "" then path = newest_transcript() end local calls = {} local tally = {heredoc = 0, script = 0} local ends = {} local stop_kinds = {} local stop_lines = {} local builtins = {} local programs = {} local at = 0 local done = false while not done do local part = read_lines(path, at, PART) for l in part.lines do local is_call = find(l, "\"tool_use\"") ~= nil and find(l, "\"Bash\"") ~= nil local is_answer = find(l, "\"tool_result\"") ~= nil if is_call or is_answer then local v = json_read(l) local recent = SINCE == "" or get(v, "timestamp", "") >= SINCE local content = v.message.content if recent and is_list(content) then for c in content do if c.type == "tool_use" and c.name == "Bash" then local kind = launch_kind(c.input.command) if kind ~= "" then calls[c.id] = kind tally[kind] = tally[kind] + 1 if kind == "heredoc" then for b in re_find_all(c.input.command, "([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)\\(") do bump(builtins, b.groups[1]) end for p in re_find_all(c.input.command, "run\\(\\{\"([^\"]+)\"") do bump(programs, p.groups[1]) end end end elseif c.type == "tool_result" and has_key(calls, c.tool_use_id) then local text = result_text(c.content) local kind = calls[c.tool_use_id] local key = stop_key(text) if key ~= nil and starts_with(key, "fail:") then bump(ends, kind .. ", stopped by its own `fail` (a check's verdict)") elseif key ~= nil then bump(ends, kind .. ", stopped by Shale") bump(stop_kinds, split(key, ":")[1]) bump(stop_lines, key) elseif find(text, "shale-gate:") ~= nil then bump(ends, kind .. ", refused by the gate") elseif find(text, "denied") ~= nil and get(c, "is_error", false) then bump(ends, kind .. ", denied by the harness") elseif get(c, "is_error", false) then bump(ends, kind .. ", nonzero exit, no stop line") else bump(ends, kind .. ", ran") end end end end end end at = part.next done = part.done end print(path) print(tally.heredoc .. " heredocs, " .. tally.script .. " script launches" .. (SINCE == "" and "" or ", since " .. SINCE)) print("") print(table(ranked(ends), {"n", "what"})) print("") print("Shale's stops, by kind (a script's own `fail` left out):") print(table(ranked(stop_kinds), {"n", "what"})) print("") print("Shale's stops, by message:") print(table(ranked(stop_lines), {"n", "what"})) print("") print("calls in heredocs (builtins and the script's own functions):") print(table(ranked(builtins), {"n", "what"})) print("") print("programs heredocs run:") print(table(ranked(programs), {"n", "what"}))

name: cookbook/fetch_page.shale
html: -- This recipe fetches a page from a launch line, by the Linux prelude's -- `http_get` (which runs `curl`), and prints the status, how long the fetch -- took, and the body's first `head` lines, or its lines holding `grep`'s -- literals. A status other than `status` (default 200) fails the launch. It -- suits a release's checks: a `/version`, a page's text, a wait for a new -- commit to serve. -- -- shale cookbook:fetch_page.shale url=https://dogpark.lynrummy.com/version -- shale cookbook:fetch_page.shale url=https://dogpark.lynrummy.com/ grep=Begin,Game -- shale cookbook:fetch_page.shale url=https://dogpark.lynrummy.com/version wait=5419352 minutes=10 -- shale cookbook:fetch_page.shale url=https://chat.example/api/v1/messages json=messages.1.id -- -- `json` reads the body as JSON (`json_read`) and prints the value at a -- dotted path, a list's items by number from 1 (`messages.1.id`); `json=.` -- is the whole body, compact. A path that is not there fails, naming the -- part that was not. -- -- `bearer` is a Shale path (through a mount) whose file holds a token, -- sent as `Authorization: Bearer` and never shown. `wait` fetches every -- `every` seconds (default 10) until the body holds that literal, for at -- most `minutes` (default 10); a failed fetch meanwhile (the server -- restarting) is said and tried again. Each try is one program (the -- fetch; the wait between is `sleep`, none), so a wait is at most the run's -- `programs` budget of fetches (1,000 unset): `minutes * 60 / every` under it. -- -- budget: steps=50000000 const URL = arg("url", "") const GREP = arg("grep", "") const HEAD = arg("head", 20) const STATUS = arg("status", 200) const BEARER = arg("bearer", "") const WAIT = arg("wait", "") const MINUTES = arg("minutes", 10) const EVERY = arg("every", 10) const JSON = arg("json", "") -- What `json` walks: a table, or a scalar (whose `tostring` is itself), -- and a table a map when `keys` takes it. function text_of(v) return tostring(v) end function keys_of(v) return keys(v) end if URL == "" then fail("http: say `url=`") end local opts = {} if BEARER ~= "" then opts.bearer = BEARER end local r = nil if WAIT == "" then r = http_get(URL, opts) else local tries = 0 local most = MINUTES * 60 // EVERY + 1 -- A fetch a try: said here, not by the programs budget halfway. local left = budget().programs if most > left then fail("http: a wait of " .. most .. " fetches, and this run's `programs` budget has " .. left .. " left: raise `every`, lower `minutes`, or launch with `--budget programs=N`") end while true do tries = tries + 1 local got = attempt(http_get, URL, opts) if got.ok and contains(got.value.body, WAIT) then r = got.value break end local said = "status " .. (got.ok and got.value.status or "none: " .. tostring(got.error)) if tries >= most then fail("http: " .. URL .. " never held `" .. WAIT .. "` in " .. MINUTES .. " minutes (" .. tries .. " fetches; the last: " .. said .. ")") end print("waiting (" .. tries .. "): " .. sub(said, 1, 160)) sleep(EVERY * 1000) end end local body = lines(r.body) if JSON ~= "" then local v = json_read(r.body) local walked = "" if JSON ~= "." then for part in split(JSON, ".") do local n = parse_int(part) local next = nil local table = not attempt(text_of, v).ok local map = table and attempt(keys_of, v).ok if table and not map and n ~= nil then if n >= 1 and n <= #v then next = v[n] end elseif map and has_key(v, part) then next = v[part] end if next == nil then fail("http: the body has no `" .. part .. "`" .. (walked == "" and "" or " in `" .. walked .. "`")) end v = next walked = walked == "" and part or walked .. "." .. part end end local shown = v if not attempt(text_of, v).ok then shown = json_write(v) end print("json: " .. JSON .. " = " .. sub(tostring(shown), 1, 2000)) elseif GREP ~= "" then local held = 0 for l in body do for w in split(GREP, ",") do if w ~= "" and contains(l, w) then held = held + 1 print("grep: " .. sub(l, 1, 240)) break end end end if held == 0 then print("grep: no line holds " .. GREP) end else for i = 1, #body do if i > HEAD then print(" ... " .. (#body - HEAD) .. " more lines (head=" .. HEAD .. ")") break end print(" " .. sub(body[i], 1, 240)) end end print("── " .. r.status .. " in " .. r.ms .. " ms: " .. URL) if r.status ~= STATUS then fail("http: " .. URL .. " answered " .. r.status .. ", not " .. STATUS) end

name: cookbook/find_phrase.shale
html: -- This recipe finds a phrase in wrapped prose, even where a line break splits -- it. A line-by-line search never sees `*(not yet` at the end of one line and -- `settled)*` at the start of the next. This reads prose the way a reader -- does, a paragraph at a time, and finds the phrase in it: -- -- shale <cookbook>/find_phrase.shale find="(not yet settled)" in=docs -- shale <cookbook>/find_phrase.shale find="*(not yet settled)*" new="" in=docs/roc-style.md -- shale <cookbook>/find_phrase.shale find="*(not yet settled)*" new="" in=docs write=1 -- shale <cookbook>/find_phrase.shale self_test=1 -- -- Prose, in a Markdown file (`.md`), is its paragraphs, list items -- (a continuation line belongs to its item), block quotes and headings, -- each its own; a blank line ends one, and a fenced code block (``` or -- ~~~), a table row (`|`) and an HTML line (`<`) are never prose. In a -- code file, its comment blocks: consecutive whole-line comments with one -- marker (`//`, `///`, `//!` in Zig; `##`, `#` in Roc; `--` in Shale; `#` -- in a shell script), an empty comment line ending one. -- -- To match, it joins each paragraph's words with one space, and the -- phrase's too, so a line break, indentation or a run of spaces inside the -- phrase is one space. A hit is said as `path:line`, the line it starts on, -- with `(N lines)` when it crosses breaks. A phrase -- that matches only with `*` and a backtick taken out of both (`**a -- phrase\nsplit**`) is said as a hit `(markup inside)`, and never edited: -- which `*` goes with the edit is the reader's call (find it again with the -- markup in the phrase, `*(not yet settled)*`, and that hit is plain). -- -- An edit (`new=`, shown, written with `write=1`) replaces each plain -- hit and rewraps its paragraph from the hit's line only until the line -- breaks fall back into step: lines before it are kept, and once a line -- would start at a word that started a line before, the rest are kept as -- they were, so the diff is the lines the edit moved. The width is the -- paragraph's widest line; a continuation line takes the paragraph's -- second line's prefix (a list item's hanging indent, a comment's marker). -- A rewrap moves words, so a paragraph whose breaks -- mean something (a poem, a hand-aligned table in prose) is the reader's to -- edit by hand; a phrase inside an inline code span is prose here. -- -- `in` is a comma-separated list of files and folders (folders walked for -- `.md` and the code files above, their .git, .zig-cache, zig-out and -- node_modules passed by); `nocase=1` matches without case. -- -- budget: steps=2000000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const markup = "*`" -- Whether `c` (one character) is a space or a tab. function is_blank_char(c) return c == " " or c == "\t" end -- How many leading spaces and tabs `l` has. function indent_of(l) local i = 1 while i <= #l and is_blank_char(sub(l, i, i)) do i = i + 1 end return i - 1 end -- A Markdown list item's prefix length (its indent, marker and the spaces -- after), or 0 for a line that starts none: `- `, `* `, `+ `, `1. `, `2) `. function item_prefix(l) local i = indent_of(l) + 1 local c = sub(l, i, i) local j = i if c == "-" or c == "*" or c == "+" then j = i + 1 else while j <= #l and sub(l, j, j) >= "0" and sub(l, j, j) <= "9" do j = j + 1 end if j == i or (sub(l, j, j) ~= "." and sub(l, j, j) ~= ")") then return 0 end j = j + 1 end if not is_blank_char(sub(l, j, j)) then return 0 end while j <= #l and is_blank_char(sub(l, j, j)) do j = j + 1 end return j - 1 end -- The comment markers of a code file, by its extension, longest first; nil -- for a file this does not read. function markers_of(path) if ends_with(path, ".zig") then return {"///", "//!", "//"} end if ends_with(path, ".roc") then return {"##", "#"} end if ends_with(path, ".shale") then return {"--"} end if ends_with(path, ".sh") or ends_with(path, ".py") or ends_with(path, ".toml") then return {"#"} end return nil end -- A new block whose first line is `n`, with its prefix and content. function block(n, prefix, content) return {first = n, prefixes = {prefix}, contents = {content}, quote = false, marker = "", indent = -1} end function add_line(b, prefix, content) push(b.prefixes, prefix) push(b.contents, content) end -- A Markdown text's prose blocks. function md_blocks(text) local out = {} local cur = nil local fence = false local n = 0 for l in lines(text) do n = n + 1 local t = trim(l) local ip = item_prefix(l) if starts_with(t, "```") or starts_with(t, "~~~") then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = nil fence = not fence elseif fence then -- code, never prose elseif t == "" or starts_with(t, "|") or starts_with(t, "<") then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = nil elseif starts_with(t, "#") then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end local h = indent_of(l) + 1 while sub(l, h, h) == "#" do h = h + 1 end while is_blank_char(sub(l, h, h)) do h = h + 1 end push(out, block(n, sub(l, 1, h -
