1), sub(l, h, #l))) cur = nil elseif ip > 0 then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = block(n, sub(l, 1, ip), sub(l, ip + 1, #l)) elseif starts_with(t, ">") then local q = find(l, ">") local e = q + 1 if is_blank_char(sub(l, e, e)) then e = e + 1 end if cur ~= nil and cur.quote then add_line(cur, sub(l, 1, e - 1), sub(l, e, #l)) else if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = block(n, sub(l, 1, e - 1), sub(l, e, #l)) cur.quote = true end else local d = indent_of(l) if cur ~= nil and not cur.quote then add_line(cur, sub(l, 1, d), sub(l, d + 1, #l)) else if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = block(n, sub(l, 1, d), sub(l, d + 1, #l)) end end end if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end return out end -- A code file's comment blocks: whole-line comments with one marker at one -- indent, an empty one ending a block. function comment_blocks(text, markers) local out = {} local cur = nil local n = 0 for l in lines(text) do n = n + 1 local d = indent_of(l) local rest = sub(l, d + 1, #l) local m = nil for mk in markers do if m == nil and starts_with(rest, mk) then m = mk end end if m == nil then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = nil else local e = d + #m + 1 if sub(l, e, e) == " " then e = e + 1 end local prefix = sub(l, 1, e - 1) local content = sub(l, e, #l) if trim(content) == "" then if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = nil elseif cur ~= nil and cur.marker == m and cur.indent == d then add_line(cur, prefix, content) else if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end cur = block(n, prefix, content) cur.marker = m cur.indent = d end end end if cur ~= nil then push(out, cur) end return out end -- `path`'s prose blocks, or nil for a file this does not read. function blocks_of(path, text) if ends_with(path, ".md") then return md_blocks(text) end local markers = markers_of(path) if markers == nil then return nil end return comment_blocks(text, markers) end -- A block's words, each with its line (1 for the block's first) and its -- offset in `raw`, the words joined by one space. function words_of(b) local ws = {} local raw = "" local k = 1 while k <= #b.contents do for w in words(b.contents[k]) do if raw ~= "" then raw = raw .. " " end push(ws, {text = w, k = k, at = #raw + 1}) raw = raw .. w end k = k + 1 end return {list = ws, raw = raw} end -- `s` without markup: {key, from}, `from[i]` the place in `s` of `key`'s i-th. function stripped(s) local key = "" local from = {} local i = 1 while i <= #s do local c = sub(s, i, i) if not contains(markup, c) then key = key .. c push(from, i) end i = i + 1 end return {key = key, from = from} end -- The index of the word holding offset `at` of the block's raw text. function word_at(ws, at) local i = #ws while i > 1 and ws[i].at > at do i = i - 1 end return i end -- Every start of `needle` in `hay`, 1-based. function starts_of(hay, needle) local out = {} if needle == "" then return out end local at = find(hay, needle) while at ~= nil do push(out, at) at = find(hay, needle, at + 1) end return out end -- Every hit of `phrase` in `text` (a file at `path`): {line, lines, at, -- stop, block, plain}: plain hits as written, then the hits only markup -- hides, each said once. function hits_in(path, text, phrase, nocase) local out = {} local bs = blocks_of(path, text) if bs == nil then return out end local p = join(words(phrase), " ") if nocase then p = lower(p) end local pk = stripped(p).key local bi = 1 while bi <= #bs do local b = bs[bi] local w = words_of(b) local raw = w.raw if nocase then raw = lower(raw) end local taken = {} for at in starts_of(raw, p) do local s = word_at(w.list, at) local e = word_at(w.list, at + #p - 1) push(out, {line = b.first + w.list[s].k - 1, lines = w.list[e].k - w.list[s].k + 1, at = at, stop = at + #p - 1, block = bi, plain = true}) push(taken, at) end local st = stripped(raw) for at in starts_of(st.key, pk) do local ra = st.from[at] local seen = false for t in taken do if ra >= t and ra <= t + #p then seen = true end end if not seen and pk ~= "" then local re = st.from[at + #pk - 1] local s = word_at(w.list, ra) local e = word_at(w.list, re) push(out, {line = b.first + w.list[s].k - 1, lines = w.list[e].k - w.list[s].k + 1, at = ra, stop = re, block = bi, plain = false}) end end bi = bi + 1 end return out end -- `ws` laid on lines no wider than `width`, the first after `first` and -- the rest after `cont`: the lines' words, each line a list. function laid(ws, width, first, cont) local out = {} local cur = {} local len = 0 local prefix = first for x in ws do if #cur > 0 and #prefix + len + 1 + #x > width then push(out, cur) cur = {} len = 0 prefix = cont end if #cur > 0 then len = len + 1 end push(cur, x) len = len + #x end if #cur > 0 then push(out, cur) end return out end -- `contents` (each line's text after its prefix) laid again from line -- `a`, onto `out`: a line too wide gives its last words to the head of -- the next, and once past line `upto` (the last the edit touched) a line -- with nothing carried into it is kept as it was, and so is the rest. function relaid(prefixes, contents, a, upto, width, cont, out) local carry = {} local k = a while k <= #contents do if #carry == 0 and k > upto then push(out, prefixes[k] .. contents[k]) else local cur = carry for x in words(contents[k]) do push(cur, x) end local ls = laid(cur, width, prefixes[k], cont) local j = 1 while j < #ls do if j == 1 then push(out, prefixes[k] .. join(ls[j], " ")) else push(out, cont .. join(ls[j], " ")) end j = j + 1 end carry = {} if #ls == 1 then push(out, prefixes[k] .. join(ls[1], " ")) elseif #ls > 1 then if k == #contents then push(out, cont .. join(ls[#ls], " ")) else carry = ls[#ls] end end end k = k + 1 end return out end -- Block `b`'s lines (its words `w`) with raw[at..stop] replaced by `new`, -- the block's new lines, whole, prefixes and all. Only the lines the edit -- moves change: a replacement of as many words as the hit takes their -- places, line by line; any other is the hit's line's text, the hit's -- later lines folded into it. Either way a line too wide gives its last -- words to the next, and the first line that fits past the edit ends it. -- A line an edit made shorter stays short: nothing is pulled up. function rewrapped(b, w, at, stop, new) local ws = w.list local s = word_at(ws, at) local e = word_at(ws, stop) local a = ws[s].k local z = ws[e].k local width = 0 local k = 1 while k <= #b.contents do local len = #b.prefixes[k] + #b.contents[k] if len > width then width = len end k = k + 1 end local cont = b.prefixes[1] if #b.prefixes >= 2 then cont = b.prefixes[2] elseif item_prefix(b.prefixes[1] .. "x") > 0 then cont = rep(" ", #b.prefixes[1]) end local head = sub(ws[s].text, 1, at - ws[s].at) local tail = sub(ws[e].text, stop - ws[e].at + 2, #ws[e].text) local texts = {} for x in ws do push(texts, x.text) end -- A removal that leaves only what followed the hit in its last word -- (`settled)*.` less the hit is `.`) gives that to the word before. if trim(head .. new) == "" and tail ~= "" and s > 1 then texts[s - 1] = texts[s - 1] .. tail tail = "" end local nw = words(head .. new .. tail) -- Each line's words, the hit's replaced. local per = {} k = 1 while k <= #b.contents do push(per, {}) k = k + 1 end local prefixes = {} local contents = {} local out = {} if #nw == e - s + 1 then local i = 1 while i <= #ws do local x = texts[i] if i >= s and i <= e then x = nw[i - s + 1] end push(per[ws[i].k], x) i = i + 1 end k = 1 while k <= #b.contents do push(prefixes, b.prefixes[k]) if k >= a and k <= z then push(contents, join(per[k], " ")) else push(contents, b.contents[k]) end k = k + 1 end else local i = 1 while i <= #ws do if i < s or i > e then push(per[ws[i].k], texts[i]) end if i == s then for x in nw do push(per[a], x) end end i = i + 1 end -- The hit's later lines fold into its first. k = a + 1 while k <= z do for x in per[k] do push(per[a], x) end k = k + 1 end k = 1 while k <= #b.contents do if k <= a or k > z then push(prefixes, b.prefixes[k]) if k == a then push(contents, join(per[k], " ")) else push(contents, b.contents[k]) end end k = k + 1 end z = a end k = 1 while k < a do push(out, prefixes[k] .. contents[k]) k = k + 1 end return relaid(prefixes, contents, a, z, width, cont, out) end -- `text` (at `path`) with every plain hit of `phrase` replaced by `new`: -- {text, edited, skipped}, the hits markup hides skipped and counted. function edited(path, text, phrase, new, nocase) local hs = hits_in(path, text, phrase, nocase) local skipped = 0 local plain = {} for h in hs do if h.plain then push(plain, h) else skipped = skipped + 1 end end -- From the last hit back: an edit moves only the lines after it. local ls = lines(text) local i = #plain while i >= 1 do local h = plain[i] local bs = blocks_of(path, join(ls, "\n")) local b = bs[h.block] local w = words_of(b) local now = rewrapped(b, w, h.at, h.stop, new) local first = b.first local last = b.first + #b.contents - 1 local rebuilt = {} local k = 1 while k < first do push(rebuilt, ls[k]) k = k + 1 end for l in now do push(rebuilt, l) end k = last + 1 while k <= #ls do push(rebuilt, ls[k]) k = k + 1 end ls = rebuilt i = i - 1 end local out = join(ls, "\n") if ends_with(text, "\n") and not ends_with(out, "\n") then out = out .. "\n" end return {text = out, edited = #plain, skipped = skipped} end -- A hit as a reader sees it: `path:line: ...the phrase...` and its notes. function said(path, h, text) local b = blocks_of(path, text)[h.block] local raw = words_of(b).raw local from = h.at - 20 if from < 1 then from = 1 end local to = h.stop + 20 if to > #raw then to = #raw end local notes = "" if h.lines > 1 then notes = notes .. " (" .. tostring(h.lines) .. " lines)" end if not h.plain then notes = notes .. " (markup inside)" end return path .. ":" .. tostring(h.line) .. ": " .. sub(raw, from, to) .. notes end -- The files of `in`: each named file, and each folder's prose files. function files_of(spec) local out = {} for p in split(spec, ",") do local q = trim(p) if ends_with(q, ".md") or markers_of(q) ~= nil then push(out, q) else for e in walk(q, {skip = ".git,.zig-cache,zig-out,node_modules"}) do if e.kind == "file" and (ends_with(e.path, ".md") or markers_of(e.path) ~= nil) then push(out, e.path) end end end end return out end if arg("self_test", "") ~= "" then local P = "cookbook/plants/find_phrase/" local wrong = {} local cases = { {"notyet.md", "(not yet settled)", "4 2 plain"}, {"notyet.md", "*(not yet settled)*", "4 2 plain"}, {"notyet.md", "(not yet settled) by", "4 2 markup"}, {"bold.md", "a phrase split", "1 2 markup"}, {"item.md", "the first part of the phrase", "2 2 plain"}, {"fence.md", "phrase in a fence", ""}, {"blank.md", "one paragraph", ""}, {"comment.zig", "that wraps here", "1 2 plain"}, {"comment.zig", "in a string", ""}, } for c in cases do local text = read(P .. c[1]) local got = {} for h in hits_in(P .. c[1], text, c[2], false) do local kind = "markup" if h.plain then kind = "plain" end push(got, tostring(h.line) .. " " .. tostring(h.lines) .. " " .. kind) end if join(got, "; ") ~= c[3] then push(wrong, c[1] .. " \"" .. c[2] .. "\": want [" .. c[3] .. "], got [" .. join(got, "; ") .. "]") end end local edits = { {"notyet.md", "*(not yet settled)*", "", "notyet.edited.md"}, {"punct.md", "*(not yet settled)*", "", "punct.edited.md"}, {"item.md", "first part", "very first and longest part", "item.edited.md"}, {"comment.zig", "that wraps here", "that bends here", "comment.edited.zig"}, } for e in edits do local r = edited(P .. e[1], read(P .. e[1]), e[2], e[3], false) local want = read(P .. e[4]) if r.text ~= want then push(wrong, e[1] .. " edited: want\n" .. want .. "got\n" .. r.text) end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail(tostring(#wrong) .. " prose plants wrong") end print("prose: " .. tostring(#cases) .. " finds and " .. tostring(#edits) .. " edits as their plants say") else local phrase = arg("find", "") if phrase == "" then fail("prose: find= the phrase (see the header)") end local new = arg("new", nil) local write = arg("write", false) local nocase = arg("nocase", false) local total = 0 local hidden = 0 for f in files_of(arg("in", ".")) do local text = read(f) for h in hits_in(f, text, phrase, nocase) do print(said(f, h, text)) total = total + 1 if not h.plain then hidden = hidden + 1 end end if new ~= nil then local r = edited(f, text, phrase, new, nocase) if r.edited > 0 then if write then replace(f, r.text) else local before = lines(text) local after = lines(r.text) print("-- " .. f .. ": " .. tostring(r.edited) .. " edited (write=1 writes it); its lines now:") local k = 1 while k <= #after do if before[k] ~= after[k] then print(" " .. tostring(k) .. ": " .. after[k]) end k = k + 1 end end end end end print("prose: " .. tostring(total) .. " hits of \"" .. phrase .. "\", " .. tostring(hidden) .. " with markup inside") end

name: cookbook/findings.shale
html: -- This library prints a recipe's findings between two copies of its -- summary. `print_findings(summary, lines)` prints the summary, then each -- line, then the summary again (just once when there are no lines). -- -- use("cookbook:findings.shale") -- print_findings("check_errors (Roc): 12 files; 3 errors", lines) -- -- The summary is printed twice because Shale stops printing at a script's output budget (64 KiB by -- default, a few hundred lines), so the first copy survives a long list; -- and roc-chat's verify checks only the last line. A script whose list -- can be long raises its budget to 4 MB with this line at its top: -- -- -- budget: output_bytes=4000000 function print_findings(summary, lines) print(summary) if #lines == 0 then return nil end for line in lines do print(line) end print(summary) return nil end

name: cookbook/folder_names.shale
html: -- This library holds the rule for when a text names a folder: the name must -- stand alone. A folder's name is a whole run of letters, digits, `_` and -- `-`, so `dog-park` is not found inside `dog-park-page` or `dog-park_x`, -- and the case must match, so `Shale` never names `shale`. -- -- Some names that stand alone are file names, not folders, and -- `in_file_name` tells them: a name followed by a dot and a letter -- (`docs/observatory.adoc` links a file, not the observatory repo), except -- `.git` (`showell/shale.git` names the repo), and a name right after a dot -- that follows a letter or digit (`Main.roc`, a file's extension). -- -- `survey_repos.shale` and `map_repos.shale` find the READMEs' mentions by -- it, and `retire_checkout.shale` finds the paths that name a checkout. -- -- use("cookbook:folder_names.shale") -- for t in re_find_all(src, NAME_RUN) do ... end -- if stands_alone(src, at, #name) and not in_file_name(src, at, #name) then ... end const NAME_RUN = "[A-Za-z0-9_-]+" function is_namey(ch) return ch ~= "" and re_find(ch, "^[A-Za-z0-9_]$") ~= nil end function is_letter(ch) return ch ~= "" and re_find(ch, "^[A-Za-z]$") ~= nil end -- Whether the `len` bytes at `at` are a whole run of NAME_RUN's characters: -- the byte before and the byte after are neither a letter, a digit, `_` nor -- `-`. function stands_alone(src, at, len) local before = "" if at > 1 then before = sub(src, at - 1, at - 1) end local after = sub(src, at + len, at + len) for ch in {before, after} do if ch == "-" or is_namey(ch) then return false end end return true end -- Whether the name at `at` is part of a file name: `name.ext` (but not -- `name.git`) or `base.name`. function in_file_name(src, at, len) local after = at + len if sub(src, after, after) == "." and is_letter(sub(src, after + 1, after + 1)) then local is_git = sub(src, after + 1, after + 3) == "git" and not is_namey(sub(src, after + 4, after + 4)) if not is_git then return true end end if at > 2 and sub(src, at - 1, at - 1) == "." and is_namey(sub(src, at - 2, at - 2)) then return true end return false end

name: cookbook/go/find_deep_calls.shale
html: -- Calls nested three or more deep, like `f(g(h(x)))`, in a Go tree, read -- from Go's own parser (go_tree, cookbook/go/parsed.shale). Such a call is -- read from the inside out; a named middle step reads left to right. The -- Roc recipe's rule (cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls.shale), in Go's terms. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/go/find_deep_calls.shale min=4 -- shale cookbook:go/find_deep_calls.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: `glob=` the files (`**/*.go`), `tests=0` to leave out the -- `_test.go` files, `min=` the least depth to report (3), and `loose=1`, -- under which a composite literal argument (`T{...}`, `[]T{...}`) does not -- start the count again. -- -- A call's depth is one more than the deepest call among its arguments. -- What reads left to right passes its parts' depth through without adding -- a level: a method's receiver (`a.f().g()`), a selector, an index or a -- slice, `*`, `&` and the other operators, parentheses, and a type -- assertion. A conversion to a type the syntax shows (`string(b)`, -- `[]byte(s)`, `(*T)(p)`) is no level either; one to a named type -- (`Note(x)`) looks like any call, since the tree has no types. A function -- literal starts again at zero, since its body is read on its own, and so -- does a composite literal, whose parts have names or places, unless -- `loose=1`. So `f(g(h(x) + 1))`, `f(*g(h(x)))` and `f(g(h(x).a))` are -- each three deep. -- -- Each finding is the outermost call of one nest: -- path:line:col: nested: depth N, <outermost> to <deepest>: <source line> -- between two copies of the counts; the run exits 0 on findings and fails -- on a file go-ast refuses. `self_test=1` reads -- `cookbook/go/plants/find_deep_calls/` at min 3, each line ending `// want: -- nested N, ...` giving exactly those nests. -- budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:go/plants/find_deep_calls/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.go") or arg("glob", "**/*.go") const TESTS = arg("tests", 1) == 1 const LOOSE = arg("loose", "") == "1" const MIN = SELF_TEST and 3 or arg("min", 3) use("cookbook:go/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") const PASS_THROUGH = {SelectorExpr = true, IndexExpr = true, IndexListExpr = true, SliceExpr = true, StarExpr = true, UnaryExpr = true, BinaryExpr = true, ParenExpr = true, TypeAssertExpr = true} const LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH = {CompositeLit = true, KeyValueExpr = true} const TYPE_NAMES = {string = true, bool = true, byte = true, rune = true, int = true, int8 = true, int16 = true, int32 = true, int64 = true, uint = true, uint8 = true, uint16 = true, uint32 = true, uint64 = true, uintptr = true, float32 = true, float64 = true, complex64 = true, complex128 = true, any = true, error = true} const TYPE_KINDS = {ArrayType = true, MapType = true, ChanType = true, FuncType = true, InterfaceType = true, StructType = true} function passes_depth_through(kind, loose) return has_key(PASS_THROUGH, kind) or (loose and has_key(LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH, kind)) end -- Whether the call at `i` converts to a type the syntax shows. function is_conversion(nodes, i) local fun = nodes[kid_in(nodes, i, "Fun")] if fun.kind == "Ident" then return has_key(TYPE_NAMES, fun.name) end if has_key(TYPE_KINDS, fun.kind) then return true end if fun.kind == "ParenExpr" then local inner = nodes[fun.kids[1]] return inner.kind == "StarExpr" or has_key(TYPE_KINDS, inner.kind) end return false end function is_call(nodes, i) return nodes[i].kind == "CallExpr" and not is_conversion(nodes, i) end -- The call depth of node `i`, cached in `memo`, -1 not yet known. function call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose) if memo[i] >= 0 then return memo[i] end local node = nodes[i] local depth = 0 if node.kind == "CallExpr" then local deepest_argument = 0 for a in kids_in(nodes, i, "Args") do deepest_argument = max(deepest_argument, call_depth(nodes, memo, a, loose)) end -- The function called passes its receiver's depth through. local fun_depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, kid_in(nodes, i, "Fun"), loose) if is_conversion(nodes, i) then depth = deepest_argument else depth = max(1 + deepest_argument, fun_depth) end elseif passes_depth_through(node.kind, loose) then for k in node.kids do depth = max(depth, call_depth(nodes, memo, k, loose)) end end memo[i] = depth return depth end function continues_nest(nodes, i, loose) return nodes[i].kind == "CallExpr" or passes_depth_through(nodes[i].kind, loose) end -- Whether the call at `i` is its nest's outermost: the first call above it, -- through nodes that continue the nest, is not as deep. function is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, loose) local p = nodes[i].parent while p > 0 do if is_call(nodes, p) then return call_depth(nodes, memo, p, loose) < call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose) end if not continues_nest(nodes, p, loose) then return true end p = nodes[p].parent end return true end -- A call's name: `f`, `strings.Trim`, or `.Trim` for a method on a value -- the syntax does not name. function call_name(nodes, i) local fun_at = kid_in(nodes, i, "Fun") local fun = nodes[fun_at] if fun.kind == "Ident" then return fun.name end if fun.kind == "SelectorExpr" then local x = nodes[kid_in(nodes, fun_at, "X")] local sel = nodes[kid_in(nodes, fun_at, "Sel")].name if x.kind == "Ident" then return x.name .. "." .. sel end return "." .. sel end return fun.kind end function is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose) local p = nodes[j].parent while p > 0 and p ~= top do if not continues_nest(nodes, p, loose) then return false end p = nodes[p].parent end return p == top end -- The nest's deepest call: the first call of depth 1 inside it. function deepest_call(nodes, memo, top, loose) local j = top + 1 while j <= #nodes and nodes[j].depth > nodes[top].depth do if is_call(nodes, j) and call_depth(nodes, memo, j, loose) == 1 and is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose) then return j end j = j + 1 end return top end const paths = go_paths(GLOB, TESTS) local parsed = parse_go_files(paths) local finding_lines = {} local count_by_depth = {} const found_at = {} for f in parsed.files do local nodes = f.nodes local memo = {} for n in nodes do push(memo, -1) end local source_lines = {} for i = 1, #nodes do if is_call(nodes, i) and call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) >= MIN and is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) then if #source_lines == 0 then source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") end local line = nodes[i].line local depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) local span = call_name(nodes, i) .. " to " .. call_name(nodes, deepest_call(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE)) push(finding_lines, f.path .. ":" .. line .. ":" .. nodes[i].col .. ": nested: depth " .. depth .. ", " .. span .. ": " .. trim(source_lines[line])) incr(count_by_depth, tostring(depth)) push_at(found_at, f.path .. ":" .. line, "nested " .. depth) end end end local counts = {} for depth in sort(keys(count_by_depth)) do push(counts, "depth " .. depth .. " " .. count_by_depth[depth]) end print_findings("find_deep_calls (Go): " .. #paths .. " files; nested " .. #finding_lines .. " (min " .. MIN .. ", " .. (LOOSE and "loose" or "strict") .. ")" .. (#counts > 0 and ("; " .. join(counts, ", ")) or ""), finding_lines) fail_if_go_refused("find_deep_calls", parsed.refused) if SELF_TEST then check_want_marks("find_deep_calls", paths, found_at, {"nested"}) end

name: cookbook/go/find_smells.shale
html: -- Functions in a Go tree that may want a second look, read from Go's own -- parser (go_tree, cookbook/go/parsed.shale). The Zig smells that translate -- to Go, and the block nesting a reader has to hold in their head: -- -- long_func a function or method of `long=` lines or more (80), its -- signature to its `}`: a seam to look for. -- deep_block a function whose statements nest `deep=` blocks deep (4): -- each `if`, `for`, `switch` or `select` is a level, an -- `else if` is not, and a function literal starts again at -- zero, judged on its own. The finding is at the first -- statement that deep. -- many_params a function of `params=` parameters or more (6): a struct -- waiting to be named. -- bool_param a function with a `bool` parameter: a call site's bare -- `true` says nothing, where a named type would. -- -- One line a finding, `path:line: <check>: <what>`, between two copies of -- the counts; the run exits 0 on findings, which are for a reader, and fails -- on a file go-ast refuses. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/go/find_smells.shale long=60 tests=0 -- shale cookbook:go/find_smells.shale self_test=1 -- -- `glob=` names the files (`**/*.go`), and `tests=0` leaves out the -- `_test.go` files. `self_test=1` reads `cookbook/go/plants/find_smells/` at -- `long=19`, so a plant stays small, and the other defaults; each line -- ending `// want: <check>, ...` gives exactly those findings. -- budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:go/plants/find_smells/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.go") or arg("glob", "**/*.go") const TESTS = arg("tests", 1) == 1 const LONG = SELF_TEST and 19 or arg("long", 80) const DEEP = SELF_TEST and 4 or arg("deep", 4) const PARAMS = SELF_TEST and 6 or arg("params", 6) const CHECKS = {"long_func", "deep_block", "many_params", "bool_param"} use("cookbook:go/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") const LEVELS = {IfStmt = true, ForStmt = true, RangeStmt = true, SwitchStmt = true, TypeSwitchStmt = true, SelectStmt = true} const FUNCTIONS = {FuncDecl = true, FuncLit = true} function say(report, path, line, check, what) push(report, {path = path, line = line, check = check, what = what}) return nil end -- A function's name, or `a func literal in f` for a literal. function function_name(nodes, i) if nodes[i].kind == "FuncDecl" then return nodes[kid_in(nodes, i, "Name")].name end local p = nodes[i].parent while p > 0 and nodes[p].kind ~= "FuncDecl" do p = nodes[p].parent end if p == 0 then return "a func literal" end return "a func literal in " .. nodes[kid_in(nodes, p, "Name")].name end -- Each parameter `{name, type}`, one a name (`a, b int` is two). function params_of(nodes, source_lines, func) local got = {} local list = kid_in(nodes, kid_in(nodes, func, "Type"), "Params") for field in kids_in(nodes, list, "List") do local t = source_of(source_lines, nodes[kid_in(nodes, field, "Type")]) local names = kids_in(nodes, field, "Names") if #names == 0 then push(got, {name = "_", type = t}) end for k in names do push(got, {name = nodes[k].name, type = t}) end end return got end function signatures(f, nodes, source_lines, report) for i = 1, #nodes do if nodes[i].kind == "FuncDecl" then local name = function_name(nodes, i) local n = nodes[i] local length = n.end_line - n.line + 1 if length >= LONG then say(report, f.path, n.line, "long_func", "`" .. name .. "` is " .. length .. " lines") end local params = params_of(nodes, source_lines, i) if #params >= PARAMS then say(report, f.path, n.line, "many_params", "`" .. name .. "` takes " .. #params .. " parameters") end local flags = {} for q in params do if q.type == "bool" then push(flags, q.name) end end if #flags > 0 then say(report, f.path, n.line, "bool_param", "`" .. name .. "` takes `bool` " .. join(flags, ", ") .. ": a caller's bare `true` says nothing") end end end return nil end -- The block depth of each statement, counted from its function: a level -- for each `if` (not an `else if`), `for`, `switch` and `select` around it -- and its own; one finding a function, at its first statement `DEEP` deep. function nesting(f, nodes, report) local level = {} local deepest = {} local first_deep = {} -- Each node's function, its nearest FuncDecl or FuncLit. local owner = {} for i = 1, #nodes do local n = nodes[i] local p = n.parent local inherited = 0 local func = 0 if p > 0 then inherited = level[p] func = owner[p] end if has_key(FUNCTIONS, n.kind) then inherited = 0 func = i end local own = 0 if has_key(LEVELS, n.kind) and not (n.kind == "IfStmt" and get(n, "role", "") == "Else") then own = 1 end push(level, inherited + own) push(owner, func) if own == 1 and func > 0 and level[i] > get(deepest, tostring(func), 0) then deepest[tostring(func)] = level[i] if level[i] == DEEP then first_deep[tostring(func)] = i end end end for key in keys(first_deep) do local func = parse_int(key) local at = nodes[first_deep[key]] say(report, f.path, at.line, "deep_block", "`" .. function_name(nodes, func) .. "` nests " .. deepest[key] .. " blocks deep, the first " .. DEEP .. " here") end return nil end const paths = go_paths(GLOB, TESTS) local parsed = parse_go_files(paths) local report = {} for f in parsed.files do local source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") signatures(f, f.nodes, source_lines, report) nesting(f, f.nodes, report) end sort(report, {"path", "line", "check", "what"}) local count_by_check = {} local finding_lines = {} const found_at = {} for r in report do incr(count_by_check, r.check) push(finding_lines, r.path .. ":" .. r.line .. ": " .. r.check .. ": " .. r.what) push_at(found_at, r.path .. ":" .. r.line, r.check) end local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. get(count_by_check, c, 0)) end print_findings("smells (Go): " .. #paths .. " files; " .. join(counts, ", ") .. " (long " .. LONG .. ", deep " .. DEEP .. ", params " .. PARAMS .. ")", finding_lines) fail_if_go_refused("smells", parsed.refused) if SELF_TEST then check_want_marks("smells", paths, found_at, CHECKS) end

name: cookbook/go/hunt_names.shale
html: -- Awkward names in a Go tree, a question each, read from Go's own parser -- (go_tree, cookbook/go/parsed.shale). The Zig and Roc name hunts' checks -- that translate to Go, judged by the same word tables in cookbook/words/: -- -- vague a name of nothing but vague words (`data`, `handleData`, -- `processStuff`, `info`): a function, a method, a type, a -- var or const, a `:=` or a range variable, a parameter or -- a struct field. A lone `handle` or `run` function is an -- entry point's convention and passes. -- question a function named `is*`, `has*`, `can*` or `should*` that -- gives no bool, or one that gives a bool named as a state -- (`loaded() bool`): ask it, `isLoaded`. -- negative a bool parameter, field or var named `no*` or `not*`, or -- a function `isNot*`: `noCache = false` reads twice. -- name_type a parameter or field named `*Count` that is no integer, -- or `*Path` that is no string or path type. -- phrase_name a function whose first word is a preposition and which -- gives no bool (`inView`, `byName`, `forUser`): bare, it -- hides what it gives. Name the thing (`treesInView`). A -- conversion (`to*`, `into*`) passes, and so does a -- constructor: `at`, `between`, `by`, `for`, `from`, `of` or -- `with` first, giving a type its own folder declares. -- -- Go's compiler and gofmt already settle unused names and layout, so -- nothing here repeats them. One line a finding, `path:line: <check>: -- <why>`, between two copies of the counts; the run exits 0 on findings, -- which are for a reader, and fails on a file go-ast refuses. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/go/hunt_names.shale -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/go/hunt_names.shale tests=0 -- shale cookbook:go/hunt_names.shale self_test=1 -- -- `glob=` names the files (`**/*.go`; one with `*` goes on stdin with -- `--args-stdin`), and `tests=0` leaves out the `_test.go` files. -- `self_test=1` reads `cookbook/go/plants/hunt_names/`, each line ending -- `// want: <check>, ...` giving exactly those findings (parsed.shale's -- `check_want_marks`). -- budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:go/plants/hunt_names/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.go") or arg("glob", "**/*.go") const TESTS = arg("tests", 1) == 1 const CHECKS = {"vague", "question", "negative", "name_type", "phrase_name"} use("cookbook:go/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") const VAGUE = go_word_table("vague.txt") const PARTICIPLES = go_word_table("participles.txt") const ED_VERBS = go_word_table("ed_verbs.txt") const PREPOSITIONS = go_word_table("prepositions.txt") const ENTRY = {handle = true, run = true} const ASKING = {is = true, has = true, can = true, should = true} const CONVERSION_WORDS = {to = true, into = true} const CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS = {at = true, between = true, by = true, ["for"] = true, from = true, of = true, with = true} function is_participle(w) if has_key(PARTICIPLES, w) then return true end return #w > 3 and ends_with(w, "ed") and not has_key(ED_VERBS, w) end function is_int_type(t) return re_match(t, "^u?int(8|16|32|64)?$") or t == "uintptr" end function is_all_vague(ws) if #ws == 0 then return false end for w in ws do if not has_key(VAGUE, w) then return false end end return true end -- A type's last name, `*store.Note` as `Note`, `[]Note` as `Note`. function type_base(t) local m = re_find(t, "([A-Za-z0-9_]+)$") if m == nil then return "" end return m.group end -- The types each folder declares, `dir|Name`, so a constructor's result -- can be its own package's. function folder_types(files) local got = {} for f in files do local nodes = f.nodes for i = 1, #nodes do if nodes[i].kind == "TypeSpec" then local name = kid_in(nodes, i, "Name") if name > 0 then got[dirname(f.path) .. "|" .. nodes[name].name] = true end end end end return got end -- The type text of each value a field list gives, one a name (`a, b int` -- is two ints). function field_types(nodes, source_lines, list) local got = {} if list == 0 then return got end for field in kids_in(nodes, list, "List") do local t = source_of(source_lines, nodes[kid_in(nodes, field, "Type")]) local names = kids_in(nodes, field, "Names") if #names == 0 then push(got, t) end for k in names do push(got, t) end end return got end function say(report, path, line, check, what) push(report, {path = path, line = line, check = check, what = what}) return nil end function function_names(f, nodes, source_lines, types, report) for i = 1, #nodes do if nodes[i].kind == "FuncDecl" then local name = nodes[kid_in(nodes, i, "Name")].name local line = nodes[i].line local ftype = kid_in(nodes, i, "Type") local results = field_types(nodes, source_lines, kid_in(nodes, ftype, "Results")) local gives_bool = #results == 1 and results[1] == "bool" local ws = go_words(name) local first = ws[1] if is_all_vague(ws) and not (#ws == 1 and has_key(ENTRY, first)) then say(report, f.path, line, "vague", "`" .. name .. "` is only vague words: what does it handle, and how?") end if #ws > 1 and has_key(ASKING, first) and not has_item(results, "bool") then local gives = #results == 0 and "nothing" or ("`" .. join(results, ", ") .. "`") say(report, f.path, line, "question", "`" .. name .. "` asks a question but gives " .. gives) end if gives_bool and is_participle(first) then say(report, f.path, line, "question", "`" .. name .. "` gives a bool but is named as a state, `" .. first .. "`: ask it (`is" .. upper(sub(first, 1, 1)) .. sub(first, 2) .. "`)") end if #ws > 2 and first == "is" and ws[2] == "not" then say(report, f.path, line, "negative", "`" .. name .. "` asks a negative: `!" .. name .. "()` reads twice") end if has_key(PREPOSITIONS, first) and not gives_bool and not has_key(CONVERSION_WORDS, first) then local own = #results > 0 and has_key(types, dirname(f.path) .. "|" .. type_base(results[1])) if not (has_key(CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS, first) and own) then say(report, f.path, line, "phrase_name", "`" .. name .. "` starts with a preposition, `" .. first .. "`, and gives " .. (#results == 0 and "nothing" or ("`" .. join(results, ", ") .. "`")) .. ": bare, it hides what it gives; name the thing (`treesInView`, not `inView`)") end end end end return nil end -- Whether field `i` is a parameter or a struct's field, as `name_type` and -- `negative` judge them; a result's name is neither. function is_param_or_member(nodes, i) local list = nodes[i].parent local role = get(nodes[list], "role", "") return role == "Params" or role == "Fields" end function value_names(f, nodes, source_lines, report) for i = 1, #nodes do local n = nodes[i] local named = {} local type_text = "" if n.kind == "Field" and is_param_or_member(nodes, i) then named = kids_in(nodes, i, "Names") type_text = source_of(source_lines, nodes[kid_in(nodes, i, "Type")]) elseif n.kind == "ValueSpec" then named = kids_in(nodes, i, "Names") local t = kid_in(nodes, i, "Type") if t > 0 then type_text = source_of(source_lines, nodes[t]) end elseif n.kind == "TypeSpec" then named = kids_in(nodes, i, "Name") elseif n.kind == "AssignStmt" and get(n, "tok", "") == ":=" then named = kids_in(nodes, i, "Lhs") elseif n.kind == "RangeStmt" and get(n, "tok", "") == ":=" then named = kids_in(nodes, i, "Key") for k in kids_in(nodes, i, "Value") do push(named, k) end end for k in named do local id = nodes[k] if id.kind == "Ident" and id.name ~= "_" then local ws = go_words(id.name) if is_all_vague(ws) then say(report, f.path, id.line, "vague", "`" .. id.name .. "` is only vague words: what does it hold?") end if n.kind == "Field" or n.kind == "ValueSpec" then if type_text == "bool" and #ws > 1 and (ws[1] == "no" or ws[1] == "not") then say(report, f.path, id.line, "negative", "`" .. id.name .. "` is a negative flag: `" .. id.name .. " = false` reads twice") end end if n.kind == "Field" and type_text ~= "" then local last = ws[#ws] if last == "count" and not is_int_type(type_text) then say(report, f.path, id.line, "name_type", "`" .. id.name .. "` is a count of type `" .. type_text .. "`") end if last == "path" and type_text ~= "string" and not contains(type_text, "Path") and not contains(type_text, "path") then say(report, f.path, id.line, "name_type", "`" .. id.name .. "` is a path of type `" .. type_text .. "`") end end end end end return nil end -- The findings for one file, each `{path, line, check, what}`. function hunt(f, types, report) local nodes = f.nodes local source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") function_names(f, nodes, source_lines, types, report) value_names(f, nodes, source_lines, report) return nil end const paths = go_paths(GLOB, TESTS) local parsed = parse_go_files(paths) local types = folder_types(parsed.files) local report = {} for f in parsed.files do hunt(f, types, report) end sort(report, {"path", "line", "check", "what"}) local count_by_check = {} local finding_lines = {} const found_at = {} for r in report do incr(count_by_check, r.check) push(finding_lines, r.path .. ":" .. r.line .. ": " .. r.check .. ": " .. r.what) push_at(found_at, r.path .. ":" .. r.line, r.check) end local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. get(count_by_check, c, 0)) end print_findings("hunt_names (Go): " .. #paths .. " files; " .. join(counts, ", "), finding_lines) fail_if_go_refused("hunt_names", parsed.refused) if SELF_TEST then check_want_marks("hunt_names", paths, found_at, CHECKS) end

name: cookbook/go/parsed.shale
html: -- What the Go recipes share: the files' trees from go_tree (go-ast, Go's -- own go/parser), the files it refused, a few ways to read a node, a Go -- name's words, and the self-test that holds a recipe to its plants' -- `// want:` marks. -- -- use("cookbook:go/parsed.shale") -- local parsed = parse_go_files(paths) {files, refused} -- ...the recipe's findings... -- fail_if_go_refused("hunt_names", parsed.refused) -- check_want_marks("hunt_names", paths, found_at, CHECKS) -- -- A node is go_tree's: `{kind, depth, parent, kids, line, col, end_line, -- end_col}`, `role` (the parent's field that holds it, `Fun`, `Args`, -- `Body`) and its scalars (`name`, `value`, `op`, `tok`). -- The files that parse, and a `path: reason` line for each that doesn't. function parse_go_files(paths) local files = {} local refused = {} for f in go_tree(paths) do if f.err == "" then push(files, f) elseif starts_with(f.err, f.path) then push(refused, f.err) else push(refused, f.path .. ": " .. f.err) end end return {files = files, refused = refused} end -- After the findings: the files go-ast refused, then a failure. function fail_if_go_refused(who, refused) if #refused == 0 then return nil end for r in refused do print("refused: " .. r) end fail(who .. ": go-ast refused " .. #refused .. " files (named above), which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged") end -- The paths a glob names, less the `_test.go` files when `tests` is false. function go_paths(pattern, tests) local kept = {} for p in glob(pattern) do if tests or not ends_with(p, "_test.go") then push(kept, p) end end return kept end -- The kids of node `i` that its field `role` holds, in order. function kids_in(nodes, i, role) local got = {} for k in nodes[i].kids do if get(nodes[k], "role", "") == role then push(got, k) end end return got end -- The one kid of node `i` in field `role`, or 0 when it has none. function kid_in(nodes, i, role) for k in nodes[i].kids do if get(nodes[k], "role", "") == role then return k end end return 0 end -- A node's source text when it sits on one line, else its first line's -- part and `...`. function source_of(source_lines, n) if n.line == 0 then return "" end local l = source_lines[n.line] if n.end_line == n.line then return sub(l, n.col, n.end_col - 1) end return sub(l, n.col, #l) .. "..." end -- A Go name's words, lower case: `serveHTTP` is {serve, http}, -- `parseURLPath` {parse, url, path}, `no_cache` {no, cache}. function go_words(name) local s = re_replace(name, "([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", "\\1_\\2") s = re_replace(s, "([A-Z])([A-Z][a-z])", "\\1_\\2") local got = {} for w in split(lower(s), "_") do if w ~= "" then push(got, w) end end return got end -- A word table of cookbook/words/: a word a line, `--` starting a note. function go_word_table(file) local t = {} for l in lines(read("cookbook:words/" .. file)) do local w = trim(split(l, "--")[1]) if w ~= "" then t[w] = true end end return t end -- The self-test. A plant line ending `// want: a, b` must give exactly -- those findings, as `found_at` (`path:line` to a list of tags) holds -- them, in any order; an unmarked line none; a `quiet_*.go` plant no mark; -- and each of `checks` must fire on some plant, since a check no plant -- fires could be blind. A tag is a check's name, or what the recipe says -- its finding is (`nested 3`). function check_want_marks(who, paths, found_at, checks) local wrong = {} local fired = {} local marks = 0 for p in paths do local n = 0 for l in lines(read(p)) do n = n + 1 local key = p .. ":" .. n local got = sort(get(found_at, key, {})) for g in got do fired[split(g, " ")[1]] = true end local mark = re_find(l, "// want: ([^/]+)$") if mark ~= nil then marks = marks + 1 if starts_with(basename(p), "quiet_") then push(wrong, key .. ": a quiet plant holds a `// want:` mark") end local want = {} for w in split(mark.group, ",") do push(want, trim(w)) end sort(want) if join(got, ", ") ~= join(want, ", ") then push(wrong, key .. ": found [" .. join(got, ", ") .. "], want [" .. join(want, ", ") .. "]") end elseif #got > 0 then push(wrong, key .. ": found [" .. join(got, ", ") .. "] on a line not marked for it") end end end if marks == 0 then push(wrong, "no plant holds a `// want:` mark") end for c in checks do if not has_key(fired, c) then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on no plant") end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail(who .. " self_test: " .. #wrong .. " wrong") end print(who .. " (Go) self_test: PASS (" .. #paths .. " plants, " .. marks .. " marked lines: each gives exactly its marks, no other line a finding, every check fires)") return nil end

name: cookbook/listen.shale
html: -- This recipe listens to a roc-chat conversation for one agent. It reads the -- conversation's stream (`GET /conversations/<conv>/stream`) and prints one -- line for each post meant for the agent, `#<id> by <principal>: <its first -- line>`. The key stays in a secrets mount: `run`'s `secrets` gives it to -- curl alone, which reads it from its environment (`--variable`), so no -- script sees it. -- -- shale cookbook:listen.shale site=https://chat.lynrummy.com conv=3 me=agent:2 key=keys:roc_chat_cc_key once=1 -- shale cookbook:listen.shale site=... conv=3 me=agent:2 key=keys:... log=listen.log after=12 -- shale cookbook:listen.shale site=... conv=all me=agent:2 key=keys:... log=listen.log -- -- With `conv=all` it listens to every conversation the agent is in, on -- roc-chat's one stream per agent (`GET /stream`, its app/AgentStream.roc), each message -- naming its conversation. A post is heard as -- `#<id> in conversation <c> by <principal>: <its first line>`, or for a -- channel topic that names the agent `#<id> in topic <channel>/<topic> by -- ...`. `after=` is then an event's place, `<at>.<spot>.<message>`, as the stream -- writes its ids (the stop names the one to go on from); none, or `0`, is -- live only, nothing before the run. The server's resume may send another -- conversation's post of the last second again; a run drops a repeat by -- conversation and id, so only a start from `after=` may print one twice. -- The budget warning is per conversation, as the server's limit is. -- -- A post is for the agent when both of these hold (`for_me`, pure): -- 1. it is not the agent's own (`by` is not `me`); -- 2. it names the agent: the server's `mentions` holds `me`. The rule -- of who a post names has one home, roc-chat's app/Mentions.roc -- (words, skipping quoted and fenced text), so every listener agrees; -- a message without `mentions` stops the run, named, never a guess. -- There is no rule for agents answering agents: the roc-chat server -- bounds agent-to-agent traffic, the one home of that limit, so an -- agent's every mention is heard. -- The server's limit on agent-to-agent posts is mirrored here (its numbers -- below), so at 12 of 15 of the agent's own agent-to-agent posts this hour -- one line, `budget: ...`, says so once a crossing, before any post heard -- with it; it never ends a run, and goes to `log=` too. -- `after=` is the last id already handled: nothing at or before it is -- printed. -- -- A run's output reaches the terminal only when it -- ends, so the stream is held in windows: one curl a window (`window=` seconds, 20 by default, under -- curl's `--max-time`), the first with no `Last-Event-ID` (the newest page), -- each after it resuming at the last whole frame. A post is heard at most -- a window late. -- The windows run in batches (`after_batch`, pure), each a -- child run of this script (`batch=1`, every value passed on) of 63 curls, -- about 21 minutes of quiet at 20 s windows. It -- ends one of three ways: a post heard with `once=1`, which the caller -- prints and exits 0 on; a stop (a refusal, a gap), which stops the caller -- with the batch's own line; or its curls spent, which it ends with -- `listen batch spent: after=<id>`, and the caller starts the next batch -- from that id. Any other end stops the caller, named, never a quiet loop. -- A batch is one of the caller's programs, so a run listens through 63 -- batches, about 22 hours of quiet; then it stops, naming the `after=` to -- start it again with. The batch's lines (posts, `budget:`, reconnects) -- reach the caller's output when the batch ends, and `log=` as heard. -- - `once=1` prints the first post for the agent and exits 0: a detached -- command that ends is what wakes a session on the box. -- - Otherwise each line is appended to `log=` as it is heard (required), -- for `tail -F` under a watcher, until the run's batches are spent; the -- stop names the `after=` to go on from. -- The recipe reconnects by itself (`after_window`, pure). A deploy restarts -- roc-chat and ends every stream, so the stream ended by the server, no -- connection, curl failing mid-stream, or any status but 200, 401, 403 -- and 404 (a 502 from the proxy while the server is down) is a reconnect, -- never a stop. Each prints one line, `reconnecting after <reason>, from -- after=<id>, in <n> s`, (to `log=` too), waits (`backoff_s`: 2, 5, 15, -- 30, then 60 s between attempts, back to 2 after a window that ran its -- length) and resumes from the last id seen, so nothing is missed or -- heard twice. A reconnect is a curl, one of its batch's 63, and each -- batch begins its waits again at 2 s. -- A listener that can no longer hear stops loudly: a refusal, 401 or 403 (the key -- revoked or wrong) or 404 (no such conversation, or not the agent's), -- a `gap` (more missed than the backlog holds), a message without -- `mentions` (a server older than them), or the run's batches spent -- (start it again with the `after=` the stop names) each stop the run -- nonzero, named. -- -- `self_test=1` feeds the recorded frames in `cookbook/plants/listen/` -- through the same `consume` the live path uses, and a batch's every end -- through `after_batch`: no roc-chat, no network. Two hidden knobs serve a -- live test against a local server: `curls=` (1 to 63) a batch's curls, -- to roll batches over quickly, and `self=` the script a batch runs -- (`cookbook:listen.shale`, as no builtin names a script's own path). -- -- budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=400000000 const SELF = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const SITE = arg("site", "") const CONV = arg("conv", "") const ME = arg("me", "") const KEY = arg("key", "") -- `conv=all`: the agent's one stream, every conversation it is in. const ALL = CONV == "all" -- Where a run starts: a message id, or with `conv=all` an event's place -- (empty: live only). const AFTER_TEXT = arg("after", "0") const AFTER = parse_int(AFTER_TEXT) or 0 const ONCE = arg("once", "") == "1" const LOG = arg("log", "") const WINDOW_S = tonumber(arg("window", "20")) -- A batch, the child run that holds the windows (see HOW IT LISTENS). const BATCH = arg("batch", "") == "1" -- How the parent runs itself: no builtin names a script's own path, so -- it is said here, and `self=` (a hidden test knob) runs a lane's copy. const SELF_PATH = arg("self", "cookbook:listen.shale") -- A batch's windows: 63 curls, so its lines reach the caller every 21 -- minutes or so; `curls=` (a hidden test knob) takes fewer, to roll batches over. const WINDOWS_MOST = tonumber(arg("curls", "63")) -- The parent's programs: one a batch, all but one, left spare. const BATCHES_MOST = 63 -- The line a batch ends with when its curls are spent: the parent goes -- on from its id. Never a post's line, which starts with `#`. const SPENT = "listen batch spent: after=" const LINE_MOST = 200 -- **roc-chat's agent-to-agent limit, mirrored**: an agent makes at most -- AGENT_POSTS_MOST posts naming another agent in WINDOW_SECS, counting -- only those since the last human post (a human post resets it). The -- server enforces it; the listener warns at WARN_AT, before a refusal. const AGENT_POSTS_MOST = 15 const WINDOW_SECS = 3600 const WARN_AT = 12 -- ── the decision, pure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── function contains_item(list, x) for v in list do if v == x then return true end end return false end -- The agents a post names, from the server's `mentions` (roc-chat's -- app/Mentions.roc, the one home of the rule); `consume` has refused a -- message without them. function names(msg, id) return contains_item(msg.mentions, id) end -- Rules 1 and 2. function for_me(msg, me) if msg.by == me then return false end return names(msg, me) end -- Whether `by` is an agent and the post names an agent not itself: one -- of the agent-to-agent posts the server's limit counts. function agent_to_agent(msg) if not starts_with(msg.by, "agent:") then return false end for m in msg.mentions do if m ~= msg.by and starts_with(m, "agent:") then return true end end return false end -- The agent's agent-to-agent posts within the hour before `newest`. -- `at` is roc-chat's message time in seconds, and "now" is the newest -- `at` seen, never the box's clock, so a replay counts as the live run -- did. function budget_used(ats, newest) local n = 0 for t in ats do if t > newest - WINDOW_SECS then n = n + 1 end end return n end -- The post's first line with text, trimmed and cut. function first_line(md) for l in lines(md) do local t = trim(l) if t ~= "" then if #t > LINE_MOST then return sub(t, 1, LINE_MOST) .. "..." end return t end end return "" end -- An event's place on the one stream, `<at>.<spot>.<message>` -- (roc-chat's AgentStream), the spot a conversation's number or a channel -- topic's `<channel key>/<topic key>`: `{at, conv, id}`, or nil for text -- that is none. function place_of(text) local m = re_find(text, "^([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+|[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9-]+)\\.([0-9]+)$") if m == nil then return nil end return {at = tonumber(m.groups[1]), conv = m.groups[2], id = tonumber(m.groups[3])} end -- ── the reconnect, pure ────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- What a window's answer means, `{act, reason}`: `go` (it ran its -- length, curl's `--max-time`, code 28: listen on), `stop` (a refusal, -- which no retry mends) or `reconnect` (anything else, an outage). -- `status` is curl's `%{http_code}`, "000" when nothing answered. function after_window(status, code) if status == "401" or status == "403" then return {act = "stop", reason = "the stream answered " .. status .. ": the key refused (revoked or wrong)"} end if status == "404" then return {act = "stop", reason = "the stream answered 404: no such conversation, or not the agent's (with conv=all, a server without /stream)"} end if status == "200" then if code == 28 then return {act = "go", reason = ""} end if code == 0 then return {act = "reconnect", reason = "the server ended the stream"} end return {act = "reconnect", reason = "curl exited " .. code .. " mid-stream"} end if status == "000" or status == "" then return {act = "reconnect", reason = "no connection (curl exited " .. code .. ")"} end return {act = "reconnect", reason = "the stream answered " .. status} end -- Seconds to wait before the `n`th reconnect in a row. function backoff_s(n) if n <= 1 then return 2 end if n == 2 then return 5 end if n == 3 then return 15 end if n == 4 then return 30 end return 60 end -- The `after=` a caller goes on from: the last id seen, or the one it -- gave if nothing newer came; with `conv=all`, the last event's place, or -- the one it gave. function resume_id(state) if state.all then if state.last_place ~= "" then return state.last_place end return state.after_place end if state.last > state.after then return state.last end return state.after end -- ── the batches, pure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- What a batch's end means, `{act, lines, after, reason}`, from `run`'s -- answer (`code`, `ended`, `out`): `lines` are the batch's own (posts, -- `budget:` and reconnect lines), to pass through; `act` is `done` (a -- post heard with `once`), `next` (its curls spent: go on from `after`) -- or `stop` (its own stop, a refusal or a gap, or an end that is none of -- these, so a broken batch never loops quietly). function after_batch(r, once) local out = {} local after = "" local spent = false local stopped = "" local post = false -- Shale's footers (`── time:`, `── used:`, a stop's `called from`) -- end a run, and a footer can run over lines; only `── budgets` comes -- first. local footer = false for l in lines(r.out) do if starts_with(l, "──") and not starts_with(l, "── budgets") then footer = true local at = find(l, ": fail: ") if starts_with(l, "── stopped at ") then if at ~= nil then stopped = sub(l, at + 8) else stopped = l end end elseif footer or starts_with(l, "──") then -- not the batch's elseif starts_with(l, SPENT) then spent = true after = sub(l, #SPENT + 1) elseif l ~= "" then push(out, l) if starts_with(l, "#") then post = true end end end if stopped ~= "" then -- The stop's own step count is the child's, not the line's. local m = re_find(stopped, " \\([0-9]+ steps\\)$") if m ~= nil then stopped = sub(stopped, 1, m.at - 1) end end if r.ended ~= "exit" then return {act = "stop", lines = out, after = "", reason = "listen: a batch ended by " .. r.ended .. ", not by itself"} end if r.code ~= 0 then if stopped == "" then stopped = "listen: a batch exited " .. r.code .. " naming no stop" end return {act = "stop", lines = out, after = "", reason = stopped} end if once and post then return {act = "done", lines = out, after = "", reason = ""} end -- An empty id is the one stream before its first event: still live only. if spent and (after == "" or re_find(after, "^[0-9]+$") ~= nil or place_of(after) ~= nil) then return {act = "next", lines = out, after = after, reason = ""} end return {act = "stop", lines = out, after = "", reason = "listen: a batch exited 0 with no post and no `" .. SPENT .. "<id>` line"} end -- ── the frames, pure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- `after` is a message id; with `conv` "all", `after_place` an event's -- place (or empty, for live only). The budget's count is kept a -- conversation each (`budgets`). function new_state(me, after, conv) return {me = me, after = after, conv = conv, all = conv == "all", after_place = "", last_place = "", last = 0, seen = {}, budgets = {}} end -- The state for `conv=all`, resuming after `place` (empty: live only). function new_all_state(me, place) local s = new_state(me, 0, "all") s.after_place = place return s end -- Conversation `conv`'s budget count, made at its first post. function budget_of(state, conv) if not has_key(state.budgets, conv) then state.budgets[conv] = {mine_ats = {}, newest = 0, warned = false} end return state.budgets[conv] end -- Whether a post at `p` comes after the run's start: always for a live -- run; past the start's id in its conversation; another conversation's -- of that second or later (AgentStream.is_after, the server's own rule). function after_start(state, p) local start = place_of(state.after_place) if start == nil then return true end if p.conv == start.conv then return p.id > start.id end return p.at >= start.at end -- The whole frames of a stretch of the stream, each `{event, id, data}`: -- a frame ends at a blank line, so the last piece, cut by the window or -- empty, is left for the next window to bring again; `: ping` and other -- comment lines are none. function frames(text) local got = {} local pieces = split(text, "\n\n") for k = 1, #pieces - 1 do local f = {event = "message", id = "", data = {}} local any = false for l in lines(pieces[k]) do if starts_with(l, "event: ") then f.event = sub(l, 8) any = true elseif starts_with(l, "id: ") then f.id = sub(l, 5) any = true elseif starts_with(l, "data: ") then push(f.data, sub(l, 7)) any = true end end if any then push(got, {event = f.event, id = f.id, data = join(f.data, "\n")}) end end return got end -- A stretch of the stream into `state`: `{lines, warns, err}`, each line a -- post for the agent past `after`, each warn a budget crossing, `err` a gap's account or a message's without -- `mentions`, each ending where `after=` goes on. A post seen before -- (a window that brings one again) is not printed twice. function consume(state, text) local out = {} local warns = {} for f in frames(text) do if f.event == "gap" then local g = json_read(f.data) local where = "<id>" if has_key(g, "conversation") then where = tostring(g.conversation) end return {lines = out, warns = warns, err = "a gap: posts before " .. get(g, "before", "?") .. " are past the backlog; read them with GET /conversations/" .. where .. "?before= and start again with after="} end if f.event == "message" then local msg = json_read(f.data) if not has_key(msg, "mentions") then return {lines = out, warns = warns, err = "the server sent no mentions with #" .. msg.id .. ": is it a roc-chat older than 2026-10-30, when every message began to carry them? Who a post names is the server's to say, never guessed here; with a server that sends them, go on with after="} end -- Where the post is: its spot (a conversation's number, or a -- channel topic's keys, as a place writes them) and its label. local conv = state.conv local label = "conversation " .. state.conv if state.all then if has_key(msg, "conversation") then conv = tostring(msg.conversation) label = "conversation " .. conv elseif has_key(msg, "channel") and has_key(msg, "topic") then conv = lower(msg.channel) .. "/" .. lower(msg.topic) label = "topic " .. msg.channel .. "/" .. msg.topic else return {lines = out, warns = warns, err = "the one stream sent #" .. msg.id .. " naming no conversation or topic: is it a roc-chat without GET /stream? Go on with after="} end end local key = conv .. "#" .. tostring(msg.id) if not has_key(state.seen, key) then state.seen[key] = true local mine = for_me(msg, state.me) local b = budget_of(state, conv) if msg.at > b.newest then b.newest = msg.at end if starts_with(msg.by, "human:") then b.mine_ats = {} elseif msg.by == state.me and agent_to_agent(msg) then push(b.mine_ats, msg.at) end local used = budget_used(b.mine_ats, b.newest) if used >= WARN_AT and not b.warned then push(warns, "budget: " .. used .. " of " .. AGENT_POSTS_MOST .. " agent-to-agent posts this hour; ask a human to post in " .. label .. " to reset it") end b.warned = used >= WARN_AT if state.all then if f.id ~= "" then state.last_place = f.id end local p = {at = msg.at, conv = conv, id = msg.id} if mine and after_start(state, p) then push(out, "#" .. msg.id .. " in " .. label .. " by " .. msg.by .. ": " .. first_line(msg.markdown)) end else if msg.id > state.last then state.last = msg.id end if mine and msg.id > state.after then push(out, "#" .. msg.id .. " by " .. msg.by .. ": " .. first_line(msg.markdown)) end end end end end return {lines = out, warns = warns, err = ""} end -- ── the self-test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const PLANTS = "cookbook:plants/listen" function expect(tally, cond, what) if cond then print("ok " .. what) else print("FAIL " .. what); tally.bad = tally.bad + 1 end return nil end -- The windows in order, each a plant file, through one state. function replay(files, after) local state = new_state("agent:2", after, "3") local all = {} local warns = {} for f in files do local r = consume(state, read(PLANTS .. "/" .. f)) for l in r.lines do push(all, l) end for w in r.warns do push(warns, w) end if r.err ~= "" then return {lines = all, warns = warns, err = r.err, state = state} end end return {lines = all, warns = warns, err = "", state = state} end -- The same, on the one stream (`conv=all`), from `place`. function replay_all(files, place) local state = new_all_state("agent:2", place) local all = {} local warns = {} for f in files do local r = consume(state, read(PLANTS .. "/" .. f)) for l in r.lines do push(all, l) end for w in r.warns do push(warns, w) end if r.err ~= "" then return {lines = all, warns = warns, err = r.err, state = state} end end return {lines = all, warns = warns, err = "", state = state} end function self_test() local tally = {bad = 0} local two = replay({"backlog.sse", "live.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, two.err == "" and two.state.last == 9, "after two windows the last whole frame is #9, the cut #10 left for the next") local three = replay({"backlog.sse", "live.sse", "again.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, join(three.lines, " | ") == "#1 by human:7: @CC hi | #2 by agent:1: @CC can you look? | #4 by agent:1: @CC thanks | #5 by human:7: CC, one more thing | #8 by agent:1: @CC and a second | #10 by agent:1: @CC a third agent post in a row", "the three windows give #1, #2, #4, #5, #8 and #10, each once: " .. join(three.lines, " | ")) expect(tally, three.err == "" and three.state.last == 10, "the third window brings #5 and #9 again and #10 whole") local resumed = replay({"backlog.sse", "live.sse", "again.sse"}, 5) expect(tally, join(resumed.lines, " | ") == "#8 by agent:1: @CC and a second | #10 by agent:1: @CC a third agent post in a row", "after=5 gives #8 and #10: " .. join(resumed.lines, " | ")) local gap = replay({"gap.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, gap.err ~= "" and contains(gap.err, "posts before 40") and #gap.lines == 0, "a gap is an error, named") local served = replay({"served.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, join(served.lines, " | ") == "#2 by human:7: the server says this one names CC", "the server's mentions decide, over the markdown: " .. join(served.lines, " | ")) local status = replay({"status.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, join(status.lines, " | ") == "#4 by agent:1: @CC a question, after two status posts", "the agent's own posts are not heard, even naming it; the question after them is: " .. join(status.lines, " | ")) local unserved = replay({"unserved.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, contains(unserved.err, "the server sent no mentions with #2") and join(unserved.lines, " | ") == "#1 by human:7: @CC first" and unserved.state.last == 1, "a message without mentions stops the run, named, after the posts before it: " .. unserved.err) local tenth = replay({"tenth.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, #tenth.lines == 10 and tenth.lines[10] == "#19 by agent:1: @CC tenth", "an agent's tenth mention in a row, answered by the agent each time, is still heard: " .. join(tenth.lines, " | ")) local warn = replay({"budget_warn.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, join(warn.warns, " | ") == "budget: 12 of 15 agent-to-agent posts this hour; ask a human to post in conversation 3 to reset it", "twelve of the agent's agent-to-agent posts in the hour warn once, the thirteenth not again: " .. join(warn.warns, " | ")) local reset = replay({"budget_reset.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, #reset.warns == 0, "a human post after eleven starts the count again, so eleven more warn nothing: " .. join(reset.warns, " | ")) local old = replay({"budget_old.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, #old.warns == 0, "posts older than the hour count for nothing: " .. join(old.warns, " | ")) local quiet = replay({"pings.sse"}, 0) expect(tally, #quiet.lines == 0 and quiet.state.last == 0, "pings alone are nothing") for s in {"401", "403", "404"} do local d = after_window(s, 0) expect(tally, d.act == "stop" and contains(d.reason, s), "a " .. s .. " stops the run, naming it: " .. d.reason) end local full = after_window("200", 28) expect(tally, full.act == "go", "a window that ran its length (200, curl 28) listens on") local ended = after_window("200", 0) expect(tally, ended.act == "reconnect" and ended.reason == "the server ended the stream", "a stream the server ended (200, curl 0) reconnects: " .. ended.reason) local cut = after_window("200", 56) expect(tally, cut.act == "reconnect" and contains(cut.reason, "56"), "curl failing mid-stream reconnects: " .. cut.reason) local down = after_window("000", 7) expect(tally, down.act == "reconnect" and contains(down.reason, "no connection"), "no connection (000, curl 7) reconnects: " .. down.reason) local slow = after_window("000", 28) expect(tally, slow.act == "reconnect", "nothing answering within the window (000, curl 28) reconnects, never a go") for s in {"500", "502", "503", "504", "429", "400", "410"} do expect(tally, after_window(s, 0).act == "reconnect", "a " .. s .. " is no refusal: it reconnects") end local waits = {} for n = 1, 7 do push(waits, tostring(backoff_s(n))) end expect(tally, join(waits, " ") == "2 5 15 30 60 60 60", "the waits back off 2, 5, 15, 30, then 60 s: " .. join(waits, " ")) expect(tally, resume_id(new_state("agent:2", 12, "3")) == 12 and resume_id(three.state) == 10, "a reconnect goes on from the after= given until a newer id is seen") local heard_once = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "reconnecting after the server ended the stream, from after=7, in 2 s\nbudget: 12 of 15 agent-to-agent posts this hour; ask a human\n#9 by human:7: @CC hi\n── time: 4 s\n"}, true) expect(tally, heard_once.act == "done" and join(heard_once.lines, " | ") == "reconnecting after the server ended the stream, from after=7, in 2 s | budget: 12 of 15 agent-to-agent posts this hour; ask a human | #9 by human:7: @CC hi", "a batch that heard a post with once=1 is done, its lines passed through, the footer not: " .. join(heard_once.lines, " | ")) local refused = after_batch({code = 1, ended = "exit", out = "reconnecting after no connection (curl exited 7), from after=7, in 2 s\n── stopped at cookbook:listen.shale:470:43: fail: listen: the stream answered 401: the key refused (revoked or wrong); nothing to retry (812 steps)\n── used: 812 of 200000000 steps\n"}, true) expect(tally, refused.act == "stop" and refused.reason == "listen: the stream answered 401: the key refused (revoked or wrong); nothing to retry" and #refused.lines == 1, "a batch's refusal stops the parent with the batch's own line: " .. refused.reason) local spent = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "reconnecting after the stream answered 502, from after=12, in 2 s\n" .. SPENT .. "12\n── time: 1260 s\n"}, true) expect(tally, spent.act == "next" and spent.after == "12" and join(spent.lines, " | ") == "reconnecting after the stream answered 502, from after=12, in 2 s", "a batch with its curls spent starts the next from its id, the spent line not passed through: " .. spent.after) local logged = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "#9 by human:7: @CC hi\n" .. SPENT .. "9\n"}, false) expect(tally, logged.act == "next" and logged.after == "9" and logged.lines[1] == "#9 by human:7: @CC hi", "without once=1 a post heard is passed through and the next batch goes on from its id") local wrapped = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "── budgets from the script's header: steps=200000000\n#9 by human:7: @CC hi\n── time: 5 programs, 10.1 s in all; the slowest 2.0 s: curl -sN -w\n%{http_code} --variable; slept 2.0 s\n called from x\n"}, true) expect(tally, wrapped.act == "done" and join(wrapped.lines, " | ") == "#9 by human:7: @CC hi", "the budgets header and a footer running over lines are not the batch's: " .. join(wrapped.lines, " | ")) local silent = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "reconnecting after the server ended the stream, from after=3, in 2 s\n"}, true) expect(tally, silent.act == "stop" and contains(silent.reason, "no post and no"), "a batch that exits 0 with neither a post nor a spent line stops, never loops: " .. silent.reason) local bare = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = ""}, false) expect(tally, bare.act == "stop", "a batch with no output at all stops") local crashed = after_batch({code = 2, ended = "exit", out = "shale: cookbook:nope.shale: not found\n"}, true) expect(tally, crashed.act == "stop" and contains(crashed.reason, "exited 2") and crashed.lines[1] == "shale: cookbook:nope.shale: not found", "a batch that dies naming no stop stops the parent with its code, its output passed through: " .. crashed.reason) local killed = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "timeout", out = SPENT .. "4\n"}, true) expect(tally, killed.act == "stop" and contains(killed.reason, "timeout"), "a batch ended by its timeout stops, even with a spent line: " .. killed.reason) local junk = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = SPENT .. "x\n"}, true) expect(tally, junk.act == "stop", "a spent line whose id is no number stops") -- ── conv=all: the one stream ── local all2 = replay_all({"all.sse", "all_again.sse"}, "") expect(tally, join(all2.lines, " | ") == "#1 in conversation 3 by human:7: @Cloud hi | #1 in conversation 5 by human:8: back at you | #3 in conversation 3 by agent:1: @Cloud a question | #3 in conversation 5 by human:8: one more", "the one stream gives each conversation's posts for the agent, each naming its conversation, a repeat (5/1, sent again on resume) once, its own and others' not: " .. join(all2.lines, " | ")) expect(tally, all2.state.last_place == "1793400005.5.3" and resume_id(all2.state) == "1793400005.5.3", "the last whole frame's place is where it goes on from: " .. resume_id(all2.state)) local cut_first = replay_all({"all.sse"}, "") expect(tally, cut_first.state.last_place == "1793400003.5.2", "a frame the window cut is left for the next: " .. cut_first.state.last_place) local from = replay_all({"all.sse", "all_again.sse"}, "1793400003.3.2") expect(tally, join(from.lines, " | ") == "#3 in conversation 3 by agent:1: @Cloud a question | #3 in conversation 5 by human:8: one more", "after=<place> drops its conversation's earlier posts and others' of earlier seconds: " .. join(from.lines, " | ")) expect(tally, resume_id(new_all_state("agent:2", "1.2.3")) == "1.2.3" and resume_id(new_all_state("agent:2", "")) == "", "with nothing newer seen, it goes on from the place it was given, or live") local all_gap = replay_all({"all_gap.sse"}, "") expect(tally, contains(all_gap.err, "posts before 40") and contains(all_gap.err, "/conversations/5?before="), "a gap on the one stream names its conversation: " .. all_gap.err) local unnamed = replay_all({"all_unnamed.sse"}, "") expect(tally, contains(unnamed.err, "naming no conversation") and #unnamed.lines == 0, "a message on the one stream naming no conversation stops the run, named: " .. unnamed.err) local all_budget = replay_all({"all_budget.sse"}, "") expect(tally, join(all_budget.warns, " | ") == "budget: 12 of 15 agent-to-agent posts this hour; ask a human to post in conversation 5 to reset it", "the budget is counted per conversation, its warning naming it, another's post not counted: " .. join(all_budget.warns, " | ")) expect(tally, place_of("1793400003.5.2").conv == "5" and place_of("1.2") == nil and place_of("1.2.3.4") == nil and place_of("a.2.3") == nil, "a place is three counts, dots between") local topics = replay_all({"all_topic.sse"}, "") expect(tally, join(topics.lines, " | ") == "#1 in topic Workshop/Desk by human:7: a job for you | #4 in conversation 3 by human:7: @Cloud hi | #3 in topic Workshop/Desk by human:7: and another", "a channel topic's posts are heard as the topic's, beside a conversation's, a repeat once, the agent's own not: " .. join(topics.lines, " | ")) expect(tally, topics.state.last_place == "1793400013.workshop/desk.3", "a topic's place is where it goes on from: " .. topics.state.last_place) local from_topic = replay_all({"all_topic.sse"}, "1793400012.workshop/desk.2") expect(tally, join(from_topic.lines, " | ") == "#3 in topic Workshop/Desk by human:7: and another", "after=<a topic's place> drops its topic's earlier posts and others' of earlier seconds: " .. join(from_topic.lines, " | ")) expect(tally, place_of("1.workshop/desk.2").conv == "workshop/desk" and place_of("1.Workshop/Desk.2") == nil and place_of("1.a/b/c.2") == nil and place_of("1.desk.2") == nil, "a topic's spot is two lowercase keys, a slash between") local place_spent = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = SPENT .. "1793400005.5.3\n"}, false) expect(tally, place_spent.act == "next" and place_spent.after == "1793400005.5.3", "a batch on the one stream starts the next from its place") local quiet_all = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = SPENT .. "\n── time: 1260 s\n"}, true) expect(tally, quiet_all.act == "next" and quiet_all.after == "", "a quiet batch on the one stream, nothing heard yet, starts the next live only") local no_spent = after_batch({code = 0, ended = "exit", out = "── time: 1260 s\n"}, true) expect(tally, no_spent.act == "stop", "a batch with no spent line at all still stops, an empty id or not") if tally.bad > 0 then fail("listen: self-test: " .. tally.bad .. " failed") end print("listen self_test: PASS (own posts and pings give none, an agent's every mention is heard, the server's mentions decide, a message without them stops the run, after= and a repeated window print nothing twice, a gap is named, the budget warns once at 12 in the hour since a human spoke, 401, 403 and 404 stop, an ended stream, no connection and every other status reconnect, backing off 2 to 60 s, and a batch heard, refused, spent or broken each decides the caller: done, stop, the next batch, stop; and conv=all hears every conversation's, each named, a repeat once, from a place, its gaps and budgets per conversation)") end -- ── the live path ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function heard(l) print(l) if LOG ~= "" then append(LOG, l .. "\n") end return nil end function needed() if SITE == "" or CONV == "" or ME == "" or KEY == "" then fail("listen: site=, conv= (an id, or all), me= and key=keys:<file> are each needed") end if not ONCE and LOG == "" then fail("listen: without once=1, log= is needed: a run's output shows only when it ends, and the lines are appended there as they are heard") end return nil end -- One batch: its windows, until a post with `once`, a stop, or its curls -- spent, which it ends with the `SPENT` line. function listen() needed() local state = new_state(ME, AFTER, CONV) if ALL then local start = AFTER_TEXT if start == "0" then start = "" end if start ~= "" and place_of(start) == nil then fail("listen: with conv=all, after= is an event's place, <at>.<conversation>.<message>, or 0 for live only: " .. start) end state = new_all_state(ME, start) end -- Reconnects in a row, since the last window that ran its length. local tries = 0 for w = 1, WINDOWS_MOST do local argv = {"curl", "-sN", "--max-time", tostring(WINDOW_S), "-w", "\\n%{http_code}", "--variable", "%LISTEN_KEY", "--expand-header", "Authorization: Bearer {{LISTEN_KEY:trim}}"} local resume = "" if state.all then resume = resume_id(state) elseif state.last > 0 then resume = tostring(state.last) end if resume ~= "" then push(argv, "-H") push(argv, "Last-Event-ID: " .. resume) end if state.all then push(argv, SITE .. "/stream") else push(argv, SITE .. "/conversations/" .. CONV .. "/stream") end local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = (WINDOW_S + 30) * 1000, whole = 16777216, secrets = {LISTEN_KEY = KEY}}) local cut = #r.out while cut > 0 and sub(r.out, cut, cut) ~= "\n" do cut = cut - 1 end local status = sub(r.out, cut + 1) local next = after_window(status, r.code) if next.act == "stop" then fail("listen: " .. next.reason .. "; nothing to retry") end if status == "200" then local got = consume(state, sub(r.out, 1, cut - 1)) for w in got.warns do heard(w) end for l in got.lines do heard(l) if ONCE then return nil end end if got.err ~= "" then fail("listen: " .. got.err .. resume_id(state)) end end if next.act == "go" then tries = 0 elseif w < WINDOWS_MOST then tries = tries + 1 heard("reconnecting after " .. next.reason .. ", from after=" .. resume_id(state) .. ", in " .. backoff_s(tries) .. " s") sleep(backoff_s(tries) * 1000) end end print(SPENT .. resume_id(state)) return nil end -- The listener a caller starts: batches, each a child run of this script, -- one of the parent's programs each. function listen_batches() needed() if WINDOWS_MOST < 1 or WINDOWS_MOST > 63 then fail("listen: curls= is 1 to 63, a batch's programs") end local after = tostring(AFTER) if ALL then after = AFTER_TEXT end for b = 1, BATCHES_MOST do local argv = {"shale", "--root", ".", SELF_PATH, "batch=1", "site=" .. SITE, "conv=" .. CONV, "me=" .. ME, "key=" .. KEY, "after=" .. after, "window=" .. WINDOW_S, "curls=" .. WINDOWS_MOST} if ONCE then push(argv, "once=1") end if LOG ~= "" then push(argv, "log=" .. LOG) end -- The longest a batch can take: each curl its window and slack, and -- the longest wait after it. local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = WINDOWS_MOST * (WINDOW_S + 90) * 1000 + 60000, tail = 2000, width = 4096}) local d = after_batch(r, ONCE) -- The batch wrote its lines to `log=` as it heard them. for l in d.lines do print(l) end if d.act == "done" then return nil end if d.act == "stop" then fail(d.reason) end after = d.after end fail("listen: " .. BATCHES_MOST .. " batches of " .. WINDOWS_MOST .. " curls, a run's programs spent; start it again with after=" .. after) end if SELF then self_test() elseif BATCH then listen() else listen_batches() end

name: cookbook/look.shale
html: -- This recipe shows lines of files by number, and finds a literal's lines -- across files, folders, mounts or a git revision.
