These are the two reads -- most shell escapes were for (`sed -n a,bp` and `grep -n`, often over -- several files or repos at once), in one launch with no script to write: -- -- shale <cookbook>/look.shale at=src/io.zig:690-730,build.zig:16-29 -- shale <cookbook>/look.shale find=pathFromRoot( in=src,build.zig ext=zig -- shale <cookbook>/look.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' (a value with spaces) -- find=pub fn findProgram -- in=zig:lib/std/Build.zig -- ARGS -- shale <cookbook>/look.shale rev=origin/master at=QUEUE.md:10-40 -- shale <cookbook>/look.shale rev=HEAD~3 find=fuzz_runs in=src,build.zig ext=zig -- -- `at` is a comma-separated list of `path:first-last` (or `path:n` for one -- line); a mount path (`zig:lib/std/Build.zig:100-120`) works, the range -- after the last colon. `find` is a literal (not a pattern), looked for in -- each file or folder of `in` (comma-separated; folders searched by the -- prelude's `grep_tree`: hidden folders, zig-out, zig-pkg and node_modules -- left out, and a link, a binary file or a name the store can't hold -- listed at the end as passed by), files -- matching `like` (`*` for all; a glob is no plain word, so it goes on -- stdin with `--args-stdin`) and ending in one of `ext`'s extensions -- (`ext=zig`, `ext=ts,tsx`: plain words, for the launch line). At most `most` lines are printed, and a -- run that finds more says so: never a silent cut. A found line longer than -- `wide` characters is cut there, ending ` ...`. -- -- With `rev=`, the files are read at a git revision, in place of `git show -- origin/master:QUEUE.md | awk`: every path of `at` and `in` is read as `rev` holds it, in the git checkout `repo` (default the -- root), through the git prelude; a folder of `in` is the files `git -- ls-tree` lists under it there, `like` as before. Its own argument, not a -- `rev:path`, because a path's colon is already a mount's. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 const AT = arg("at", "") const FIND = arg("find", "") const IN = arg("in", ".") const LIKE = arg("like", "*") const EXT = arg("ext", "") -- Whether a walked file ends in one of `ext`'s extensions (any, unset). function wanted(path) if EXT == "" then return true end for e in split(EXT, ",") do if ends_with(path, "." .. trim(e)) then return true end end return false end const MOST = arg("most", 300) const WIDE = arg("wide", 200) const REV = arg("rev", "") const REPO = arg("repo", ".") not_option("look", "rev", REV) -- A file's text: as the disk holds it, or as `rev` does. function text_of(path) if REV == "" then return read(path) end return git_show(REPO, REV .. ":" .. path) end -- The files under `place` at `rev` (`place` itself when it is a file there). function files_at_rev(place) local args = {"ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", REV, "--"} if place ~= "." then push(args, place) end local got = {} for p in lines(git_call(REPO, args, nil, true, nil).out) do if p ~= "" and (LIKE == "*" or like(basename(p), LIKE)) and wanted(p) then push(got, p) end end return got end -- Each line holding FIND under `place` at `rev`, by path: `{path: -- {{line, text}, ...}}`, from one `git grep` (a `git show` a file would -- spend a program on each file). It exits 1 when nothing is found. function grep_at_rev(place) local argv = {"git", "-c", "color.ui=never", "--no-optional-locks", "grep", "-n", "-I", "-F", "-e", FIND, REV, "--"} if place ~= "." then push(argv, place) end local r = run(argv, {cwd = REPO, timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 16777216}) if r.code ~= 0 and r.code ~= 1 then fail("look: `git grep` at " .. REV .. " exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. sub(r.out, 1, 200)) end local by_path = {} local skip = #REV + 2 for l in lines(r.out) do local rest = sub(l, skip) local m = re_find(rest, ":\\d+:") if m ~= nil then local p = sub(rest, 1, m.at - 1) if not has_key(by_path, p) then by_path[p] = {} end push(by_path[p], {line = parse_int(sub(m.text, 2, #m.text - 1)), text = sub(rest, m.at + #m.text)}) end end return by_path end if AT == "" and FIND == "" then fail("look: give at=path:first-last[,...] or find=TEXT [in=dirs] [ext=zig]") end -- `path:first-last` or `path:n`, split at the last colon. function range_of(spec) local parts = split(spec, ":") if #parts < 2 then fail("look: " .. spec .. " is not path:first-last") end local span = parts[#parts] local path = join(take(parts, #parts - 1), ":") local ends = split(span, "-") local first = parse_int(ends[1]) local last = first if #ends == 2 then last = parse_int(ends[2]) end if first == nil or last == nil or last < first then fail("look: " .. spec .. ": the range is not first-last") end return {path = path, first = first, last = last} end if AT ~= "" then for spec in split(AT, ",") do local r = range_of(trim(spec)) if REV ~= "" then print("== " .. REV .. ":" .. r.path .. ":" .. r.first .. "-" .. r.last) else print("== " .. r.path .. ":" .. r.first .. "-" .. r.last) end local i = 0 for l in lines(text_of(r.path)) do i = i + 1 if i > r.last then break end if i >= r.first then print(i .. "\t" .. l) end end if i < r.first then print("(the file has " .. i .. " lines)") end end end if FIND ~= "" then local exts = {} for e in split(EXT, ",") do if trim(e) ~= "" then push(exts, trim(e)) end end local name_like = LIKE if name_like == "*" then name_like = "" end local shown = 0 local found = 0 local files = 0 local passed = {} local cut = false for given in split(IN, ",") do local place = trim(given) local hits = {} if REV ~= "" then local paths = files_at_rev(place) local at_rev = grep_at_rev(place) if #paths == 0 then print("(not at " .. REV .. ": " .. place .. ")") end for path in paths do files = files + 1 for m in get(at_rev, path, {}) do push(hits, {path = path, line = m.line, text = m.text}) end end -- `.` is the root, a folder `is_dir` will not be asked about. elseif place ~= "." and not exists(place) then print("(not there: " .. place .. ")") else -- A file named alone is searched whatever `ext` and `like` say. local opts = {} if place == "." or is_dir(place) then opts = {ext = exts, like = name_like} end local r = grep_tree(place, FIND, opts) files = files + r.files hits = r.hits for x in r.passed do push(passed, x) end if r.cut then cut = true end end for m in hits do found = found + 1 if shown < MOST then local text = trim(m.text) if #text > WIDE then text = sub(text, 1, WIDE) .. " ..." end print(m.path .. ":" .. m.line .. ": " .. text) shown = shown + 1 end end end if found > shown then print("... " .. (found - shown) .. " more (most=" .. MOST .. " shown; raise most= or narrow in=)") end for x in passed do print("(passed by, " .. x.why .. ": " .. x.path .. ")") end if cut then print("(a folder's search stopped at grep_tree's 10,000 hits: narrow in=)") end print(found .. " lines in " .. files .. " files") end

name: cookbook/map_repos.shale
html: -- This recipe maps the repos in one folder: for each, its branch, its last -- commit and how long ago, its commits in the last 30 days, its uncommitted -- files, how far it is from its upstream, the repo it is a worktree of, its -- README's title, and the other repos its README names. A README names a -- repo when the repo's folder name appears in it as a whole word, case and -- all, so `roc-apps` never counts as `roc` (`folder_names.shale`'s -- `NAME_RUN`, the rule's one home). That is a map of what the READMEs -- say, not of what the builds use. `survey_repos.shale` is its sibling for -- each repo's history (first commit, age, commit count), its README's -- opening and the sentences that name the others. For an essay on the -- repos, start with `plan_repo_essay.shale`, the playbook. -- -- Run it from the folder that holds the repos. `in=lanes` maps a folder -- inside it instead (its worktrees, say), with the README links still to the -- repos at the top. A folder with no .git is listed at the end, not mapped. -- `dot=1` prints the README links as a Graphviz graph instead of the table, -- and `json=1` prints every row as JSON, for a page to draw from. -- -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/map_repos.shale -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/map_repos.shale in=lanes -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/map_repos.shale dot=1 -- -- budget: steps=200000000 reads=20000 arena_bytes=1000000000 use("cookbook:folder_names.shale") const IN = arg("in", ".") const DOT = arg("dot", 0) const JSON = arg("json", 0) const RECENT_DAYS = 30 const LOG_CAP = 1000 const TODAY = now() // 86400 -- Each repo takes three programs (its log, its upstream, its status), so a -- folder of more than about 300 repos wants `--budget programs=N`. -- Days since 1970-01-01 for a civil date (Howard Hinnant's algorithm). function days_from_civil(y, m, d) if m <= 2 then y = y - 1 end local era = y // 400 local yoe = y - era * 400 local mp = (m + 9) % 12 local doy = (153 * mp + 2) // 5 + d - 1 local doe = yoe * 365 + yoe // 4 - yoe // 100 + doy return era * 146097 + doe - 719468 end -- The day number of a git ISO date, `2026-11-14T17:34:50+00:00`. function day_of(iso) local parts = split(sub(iso, 1, 10), "-") return days_from_civil(tonumber(parts[1]), tonumber(parts[2]), tonumber(parts[3])) end function path_of(name) if IN == "." then return name end return IN .. "/" .. name end -- Where a repo's HEAD file is. A worktree's .git is a file naming its git -- folder absolutely, `gitdir: /.../dog-park/.git/worktrees/dog-park-page`, -- and a path here is relative, so that is read as its main repo's folder at -- the top of the run's root. function head_path_of(path) if exists(path .. "/.git/HEAD") then return path .. "/.git/HEAD" end local gitdir = trim(read_or(path .. "/.git", "")) local at = find(gitdir, "/.git/worktrees/") if at == nil then return "" end local main_parts = split(sub(gitdir, 1, at - 1), "/") return main_parts[#main_parts] .. sub(gitdir, at, #gitdir) .. "/HEAD" end -- The main repo a worktree belongs to, or "" for a repo of its own. function worktree_of(path) local head = head_path_of(path) if head == "" or starts_with(head, path .. "/.git/") then return "" end return split(head, "/")[1] end function branch_of(path) local head_path = head_path_of(path) local head = "" if head_path ~= "" then head = read_or(head_path, "") end if head == "" then return "?" end local name = trim(join(split(head, "ref: refs/heads/"), "")) if #name == 40 then return "(detached)" end return name end function readme_of(path) for name in {"README.md", "README", "readme.md"} do if exists(path .. "/" .. name) then return read(path .. "/" .. name) end end return "" end function title_of(text) for l in lines(text) do if starts_with(l, "# ") then return trim(sub(l, 3, #l)) end end return "" end function map_repo(repo, names, edges) local path = path_of(repo) local log = git_log(path, {n = LOG_CAP}) local last_date = "" local last_subject = "(no commits)" local days = -1 if #log > 0 then last_date = sub(log[1].date, 1, 10) last_subject = sub(log[1].subject, 1, 60) days = TODAY - day_of(log[1].date) end local recent = 0 for c in log do if TODAY - day_of(c.date) <= RECENT_DAYS then recent = recent + 1 end end local recent_text = "" .. recent if recent == LOG_CAP then recent_text = LOG_CAP .. "+" end local up = git_upstream(path) local sync = "no upstream" if up ~= nil then sync = "+" .. up.ahead .. " -" .. up.behind end local text = readme_of(path) local seen = {} local links = {} for t in re_find_all(text, NAME_RUN) do if get(names, t.text, false) and t.text ~= repo and not get(seen, t.text, false) then seen[t.text] = true push(links, t.text) push(edges, {from = repo, to = t.text}) end end sort(links) return { repo = repo, of = worktree_of(path), branch = branch_of(path), last = last_date, days = days, recent = recent_text, dirty = #git_status(path), sync = sync, subject = last_subject, title = sub(title_of(text), 1, 50), links = join(links, ","), } end -- The folders in `folder`, by name, and its symbolic links, which the store -- follows none of (a lane can be a link to a checkout elsewhere). function entries_of(folder) local dirs = {} local links = {} for e in walk_all(folder, {depth = 1}) do local parts = split(e.path, "/") local name = parts[#parts] if e.kind == "directory" then push(dirs, name) elseif e.kind == "other" then push(links, name) end end sort(dirs) sort(links) return {dirs = dirs, links = links} end local listed = entries_of(IN) local repos = {} local strays = {} for e in listed.dirs do if exists(path_of(e) .. "/.git") then push(repos, e) else push(strays, e) end end -- The names a README can link to: the repos at the top of the root. local names = {} for e in entries_of(".").dirs do if exists(e .. "/.git") then names[e] = true end end local rows = {} local edges = {} for repo in repos do push(rows, map_repo(repo, names, edges)) end sort(rows, "days") if JSON == 1 then print(json_write({rows = rows, edges = edges, strays = strays, links = listed.links, today = TODAY})) elseif DOT == 1 then print("digraph repos {") print(" rankdir=LR;") for e in edges do print(" \"" .. e.from .. "\" -> \"" .. e.to .. "\";") end print("}") else print(table(rows, {"repo", "of", "branch", "last", "days", "recent", "dirty", "sync", "links"})) print(#repos .. " repos, " .. #edges .. " README links; recent = commits in the last " .. RECENT_DAYS .. " days (at most " .. LOG_CAP .. " read)") if #strays > 0 then print("not repos: " .. join(strays, ", ")) end if #listed.links > 0 then print("symbolic links, not followed: " .. join(listed.links, ", ")) end end

name: cookbook/merge_conflicts.shale
html: -- A library for resolving git merge conflicts: it parses the markers git -- leaves in a file, so a resolution is a few lines saying which side each -- hunk keeps. `use("cookbook:merge_conflicts.shale")`; check_conflict_markers.shale tests it. -- -- It reads git's default markers, seven characters wide, in both styles: -- diff3 (`<<<<<<<`, `|||||||`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) and the two-way one -- with no base section. A marker out of order, or a hunk never closed, -- stops the run, naming its line. -- The kind of marker a line is: "open", "base", "split", "close", or "" for -- none. A CR before the newline is ignored, so CRLF files read the same. function conflict_marker_kind(line) local l = line if ends_with(l, "\r") then l = sub(l, 1, #l - 1) end if l == "=======" then return "split" end local heads = {{"<<<<<<<", "open"}, {"|||||||", "base"}, {">>>>>>>", "close"}} for h in heads do if starts_with(l, h[1]) and (#l == 7 or sub(l, 8, 8) == " ") then return h[2] end end return "" end -- The text after a marker, which git fills with the side's name. function conflict_marker_label(line) return trim(sub(line, 8)) end -- The text cut into segments, in order: `{kind = "text", text}` for what is -- outside every hunk, and `{kind = "hunk", ...}` as conflict_hunks gives one. -- Each segment's text keeps its newlines, so joining them gives the text back. function conflict_segments(text, where?) local at = "conflicts" if where ~= nil then at = where end local pieces = split(text, "\n") local segments = {} local plain = {} local hunk = nil local part = "" local i = 0 for piece in pieces do i = i + 1 local whole = piece if i < #pieces then whole = piece .. "\n" end local kind = conflict_marker_kind(piece) if hunk == nil then if kind == "open" then if #plain > 0 then push(segments, {kind = "text", text = join(plain, "")}) end plain = {} hunk = {kind = "hunk", line = i, style = "two-way", ours_label = conflict_marker_label(piece), theirs_label = "", ours = {}, base = {}, theirs = {}} part = "ours" elseif kind == "base" or kind == "close" then fail(at .. ":" .. i .. ": a `" .. sub(piece, 1, 7) .. "` marker outside any conflict") else push(plain, whole) end elseif kind == "open" then fail(at .. ":" .. i .. ": a `<<<<<<<` inside the conflict that opens at line " .. hunk.line) elseif kind == "base" then if part ~= "ours" then fail(at .. ":" .. i .. ": a `|||||||` after the " .. part .. " section of the conflict at line " .. hunk.line) end hunk.style = "diff3" part = "base" elseif kind == "split" then if part == "theirs" then fail(at .. ":" .. i .. ": a second `=======` in the conflict at line " .. hunk.line) end part = "theirs" elseif kind == "close" then if part ~= "theirs" then fail(at .. ":" .. i .. ": a `>>>>>>>` before the `=======` of the conflict at line " .. hunk.line) end hunk.theirs_label = conflict_marker_label(piece) hunk.ours = join(hunk.ours, "") hunk.base = join(hunk.base, "") hunk.theirs = join(hunk.theirs, "") push(segments, hunk) hunk = nil else push(hunk[part], whole) end end if hunk ~= nil then fail(at .. ":" .. hunk.line .. ": the conflict that opens here never closes with `>>>>>>>`") end if #plain > 0 then push(segments, {kind = "text", text = join(plain, "")}) end return segments end -- Each hunk in the text, in order: `{line, style, ours, base, theirs, -- ours_label, theirs_label}`. `line` is its `<<<<<<<` line's number, `style` -- is "diff3" or "two-way", and a two-way hunk's `base` is "". Each side's -- text is its lines whole, newlines and all. function conflict_hunks(text, where?) local hunks = {} for s in conflict_segments(text, where) do if s.kind == "hunk" then push(hunks, s) end end return hunks end -- The text with its hunks replaced, in order, by the strings in `texts`, -- one a hunk. A count that differs from the hunks' stops the run. function rewrite_hunks(text, texts, where?) local out = {} local n = 0 local segments = conflict_segments(text, where) for s in segments do if s.kind == "hunk" then n = n + 1 end end if n ~= #texts then fail("rewrite_hunks: the text has " .. n .. " conflicts, and " .. #texts .. " texts were given") end local k = 0 for s in segments do if s.kind == "text" then push(out, s.text) else k = k + 1 push(out, texts[k]) end end return join(out, "") end -- One hunk's text for a side: "ours", "theirs", "base", or "both" (ours, -- then theirs). A two-way hunk has no base to keep, which stops the run. function hunk_side_text(h, side) if side == "ours" then return h.ours end if side == "theirs" then return h.theirs end if side == "both" then return h.ours .. h.theirs end if side == "base" then if h.style ~= "diff3" then fail("conflicts: the conflict at line " .. h.line .. " is two-way and has no base") end return h.base end fail("conflicts: no side `" .. side .. "`: ours, theirs, base or both") end -- The text with each hunk resolved to the side `sides` names for it, one a -- hunk, in order: `resolve_hunks(t, {"ours", "theirs"})`. function resolve_hunks(text, sides, where?) local hunks = conflict_hunks(text, where) if #hunks ~= #sides then fail("resolve_hunks: the text has " .. #hunks .. " conflicts, and " .. #sides .. " sides were given") end local texts = {} local k = 0 for h in hunks do k = k + 1 push(texts, hunk_side_text(h, sides[k])) end return rewrite_hunks(text, texts, where) end -- The text with every hunk resolved to one side. A text with no conflict -- stops the run, since resolving it is surely a mistake. function keep_side(text, side, where?) local hunks = conflict_hunks(text, where) if #hunks == 0 then fail("keep_side: no conflict to resolve") end local sides = {} for h in hunks do push(sides, side) end return resolve_hunks(text, sides, where) end -- The text with `old`, which must be there exactly once, replaced by `new`. -- Absent or found twice, it stops the run rather than change nothing. function replace_once(text, old, new) if old == "" then fail("replace_once: the old text is empty") end local at = find(text, old) if at == nil then fail("replace_once: not found: " .. old) end if find(text, old, at + 1) ~= nil then fail("replace_once: found more than once: " .. old) end return sub(text, 1, at - 1) .. new .. sub(text, at + #old) end -- Every marker line left in the text, `{line, text}`. A lone `=======` is -- counted though it can be a Markdown heading's underline. function conflict_markers(text) local found = {} local i = 0 for l in lines(text) do i = i + 1 if conflict_marker_kind(l) ~= "" then push(found, {line = i, text = l}) end end return found end -- Stops the run if any marker is left in the text, naming the first. -- `where` names the text in the message, a path for a file. function assert_resolved(text, where) local found = conflict_markers(text) if #found > 0 then fail(where .. ":" .. found[1].line .. ": " .. #found .. " conflict markers left, the first `" .. found[1].text .. "`") end end -- Stops the run if any marker is left in the file. function assert_file_resolved(path) assert_resolved(read(path), path) end -- A file's every hunk resolved to one side, written back, then checked. function keep_side_file(path, side) local text = keep_side(read(path), side, path) assert_resolved(text, path) replace(path, text) end

name: cookbook/plan_repo_essay.shale
html: -- This recipe is the playbook for one ask of Steve's: "give me an essay on -- our local repos" (a repo map, how the repos fit together). It gathers what -- the essay is written from, checks first that the world still looks the way -- this playbook expects, and prints the steps left. Choosing what the -- diagrams show and writing the prose stay the writer's job. -- -- It stops, before printing anything to write from, when the world has moved -- too far for a sensible update. Each stop says what changed and what to do: -- -- * survey_repos.shale's JSON lost a field this playbook reads (the survey -- changed under it: update this recipe in the same change); -- * a folder's kind is none of `clone`, `worktree of <main>` and `not git`, -- or a worktree's main checkout is gone; -- * the READMEs name no other folder at all (the mention scan broke); -- * the essay surface's notes folder, or its gate or prune script, is gone -- (the essay has nowhere to go, or no gate to pass); -- * more than half of the folders came or went since the last map, so an -- update of it would be a new essay: write one from the survey alone and -- rerun with `fresh=1`, which skips this check. -- -- When it passes, it prints, in this order: what changed since the last map -- (folders added and removed, folders with new commits, titles that changed), -- the older repo notes still on the surface (their diagrams are the place to -- start), the age table as a pipe table to paste, the README mentions to draw -- from, and the steps left: write the note, pass the gate, prune, hand Steve -- the link. Then it saves today's survey as the baseline for the next map, in -- `<data>/state/repo_survey-<today>.json`; the last map is the newest saved -- before today. -- -- cd /home/steve && shale cookbook:plan_repo_essay.shale -- cd /home/steve && shale cookbook:plan_repo_essay.shale fresh=1 -- cd /home/steve && shale cookbook:plan_repo_essay.shale self_test=1 -- -- `repos=` is the folder of checkouts (default `showell_repos`) and `data=` -- the essay surface's data folder (default `essays`), both relative to -- the folder it runs from. -- -- budget: steps=50000000 arena_bytes=400000000 const REPOS = arg("repos", "showell_repos") const DATA = arg("data", "essays") const FRESH = arg("fresh", 0) const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", 0) -- The fields of survey_repos.shale's JSON this playbook reads. A field gone -- from it is a stop, never a blank column. const SURVEY_KEYS = {"today", "rows", "mentions", "links"} const ROW_KEYS = {"folder", "kind", "main", "branch", "remote", "first", "last", "days", "commits", "title", "readme"} const MENTION_KEYS = {"from", "to", "count"} function cell(s) return join(split("" .. s, "|"), "\\|") end function survey_now(repos) local r = run({"shale", real("cookbook:survey_repos.shale"), "json=1"}, {timeout_ms = 100000, whole = 8000000, cwd = repos}) if r.code ~= 0 then fail("plan_repo_essay: survey_repos.shale stopped:\n" .. r.out) end -- Shale prints its budget and time lines around the one JSON line. for l in lines(r.out) do if starts_with(l, "{") then return json_read(l) end end fail("plan_repo_essay: survey_repos.shale printed no JSON line:\n" .. r.out) end function missing_keys(m, wanted) local gone = {} for k in wanted do if not has_key(m, k) then push(gone, k) end end return gone end -- What changed from `base` to `s`: {added, removed, active, retitled}. function changes(s, base) local before = {} for row in base.rows do before[row.folder] = row end local now_rows = {} for row in s.rows do now_rows[row.folder] = row end local d = {added = {}, removed = {}, active = {}, retitled = {}} for row in s.rows do if not has_key(before, row.folder) then push(d.added, row.folder) else local b = before[row.folder] if row.last ~= b.last or row.commits ~= b.commits then push(d.active, row.folder .. " (" .. b.commits .. " to " .. row.commits .. " commits)") end if row.title ~= b.title then push(d.retitled, row.folder .. ": \"" .. b.title .. "\" to \"" .. row.title .. "\"") end end end for row in base.rows do if not has_key(now_rows, row.folder) then push(d.removed, row.folder) end end return d end -- The stops for a survey `s` against the last map's survey `base` (nil when -- there is none) and `fresh`. Pure, so the self-test can feed it worlds. function assess(s, base, fresh) local stops = {} local gone = missing_keys(s, SURVEY_KEYS) if #gone > 0 then push(stops, "survey_repos.shale's JSON has no " .. join(gone, ", ") .. ": the survey changed; update plan_repo_essay.shale with it") return stops end local folders = {} for row in s.rows do local g = missing_keys(row, ROW_KEYS) if #g > 0 then push(stops, "survey_repos.shale's rows have no " .. join(g, ", ") .. ": the survey changed; update plan_repo_essay.shale with it") return stops end folders[row.folder] = true end for row in s.rows do if row.kind ~= "clone" and row.kind ~= "not git" and not starts_with(row.kind, "worktree of ") then push(stops, row.folder .. " is a `" .. row.kind .. "`, a kind this playbook has no words for: say what it is, then teach the survey and this recipe") end if starts_with(row.kind, "worktree of ") and not has_key(folders, row.main) then push(stops, row.folder .. " is a worktree of " .. row.main .. ", which is no folder here: retire it or find its main") end end if #s.mentions == 0 then push(stops, "no README names another folder: the mention scan broke (run survey_repos.shale self_test=1)") end for m in s.mentions do local g = missing_keys(m, MENTION_KEYS) if #g > 0 then push(stops, "survey_repos.shale's mentions have no " .. join(g, ", ") .. ": update plan_repo_essay.shale with it") return stops end end if base ~= nil and fresh ~= 1 then local d = changes(s, base) local moved = #d.added + #d.removed if moved * 2 > #s.rows then push(stops, moved .. " of " .. #s.rows .. " folders came or went since the map of " .. base.today .. ": write a new essay from the survey, not an update, and rerun with fresh=1") end end return stops end function state_dir(data) return data .. "/state" end -- The newest saved survey from before `today`, or nil. function last_map(data, today) local dir = state_dir(data) if not exists(dir) then return nil end local names = {} for e in walk_all(dir, {depth = 1}) do local name = basename(e.path) if starts_with(name, "repo_survey-") and ends_with(name, ".json") and sub(name, 13, 22) < today then push(names, name) end end if #names == 0 then return nil end sort(names) return json_read(read(dir .. "/" .. names[#names])) end function save_map(data, s) local dir = state_dir(data) if not exists(dir) then mkdir(dir) end local path = dir .. "/repo_survey-" .. s.today .. ".json" if exists(path) then remove(path) end create(path, json_write(s)) return path end function print_list(label, items) if #items == 0 then print(label .. ": none") else print(label .. " (" .. #items .. "): " .. join(items, ", ")) end end function print_plan(s, base, data) print("== since the last map") if base == nil then print("no earlier map is saved: this is the first, so the essay is the whole picture") else local d = changes(s, base) print("the last map: " .. base.today) print_list("added", d.added) print_list("removed", d.removed) print_list("with new commits", d.active) print_list("retitled", d.retitled) end print("") print("== older repo notes on the surface (start from their diagrams; read Steve's replies in comments/)") local olds = {} for e in walk_all(data .. "/notes", {depth = 1}) do local name = basename(e.path) if find(name, "repo") ~= nil and (ends_with(name, ".note") or ends_with(name, ".md")) then push(olds, data .. "/notes/" .. name) end end sort(olds) if #olds == 0 then print("none: the surface keeps 20 notes, and the last map rolled off") end for o in olds do print(o) end print("") print("== the age table, oldest first (a pipe table sorts on the surface)") print("| folder | what it is | kind | first commit | last commit | age (days) | commits |") print("|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|") for r in s.rows do print("| " .. join({cell(r.folder), cell(r.title), cell(r.kind), r.first, r.last, "" .. r.days, "" .. r.commits}, " | ") .. " |") end if #s.links > 0 then print("symbolic links, not surveyed: " .. join(s.links, ", ")) end print("") print("== README mentions (from -> to: count), what the diagrams' arrows come from") local from = "" local parts = {} for m in s.mentions do if m.from ~= from then if from ~= "" then print(from .. " -> " .. join(parts, ", ")) end from = m.from parts = {} end push(parts, m.to .. ": " .. m.count) end if from ~= "" then print(from .. " -> " .. join(parts, ", ")) end print("") print("== the steps left") print("1. For what each README says about the others, in sentences: cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:survey_repos.shale contexts=1") print("2. Group the folders into five or six areas. Draw one diagram of the areas and one per area, each small (```dot fences).") print("3. Write " .. data .. "/notes/repos-" .. s.today .. ".note: what changed, the diagrams, the age table above, and anything that looks stale.") print("4. Pass the gate: cd /home/steve && shale repos:essay-surface/scripts/check_note.shale data=" .. data .. " note=repos-" .. s.today .. ".note") print("5. Prune: cd /home/steve && shale repos:essay-surface/scripts/prune_notes.shale data=" .. data) print("6. Hand Steve http://localhost:9301/notes/repos-" .. s.today .. ".note") end function expect(what, got, want) if got ~= want then fail("plan_repo_essay self_test: " .. what .. " is " .. tostring(got) .. ", should be " .. tostring(want)) end end function plant_row(folder, kind, main, last, commits, title) return {folder = folder, kind = kind, main = main, branch = "main", remote = "", first = "2026-01-01", last = last, days = 10, commits = commits, title = title, readme = "README.md"} end function plant_world(rows) return {today = "2026-02-01", rows = rows, mentions = {{from = "a", to = "b", count = 1}}, links = {}} end function self_test() local base = plant_world({plant_row("a", "clone", "", "2026-01-05", "3", "A"), plant_row("b", "clone", "", "2026-01-05", "2", "B"), plant_row("c", "clone", "", "2026-01-05", "1", "C"), plant_row("d", "not git", "", "", "", "")}) base.today = "2026-01-20" local same = plant_world({plant_row("a", "clone", "", "2026-01-30", "4", "A"), plant_row("b", "clone", "", "2026-01-05", "2", "Bee"), plant_row("c", "clone", "", "2026-01-05", "1", "C"), plant_row("e", "worktree of a", "a", "2026-01-30", "5", "A")}) expect("a sound world's stops", #assess(same, base, 0), 0) local d = changes(same, base) expect("added", join(d.added, ","), "e") expect("removed", join(d.removed, ","), "d") expect("active", join(d.active, ","), "a (3 to 4 commits)") expect("retitled", #d.retitled, 1) expect("no baseline's stops", #assess(same, nil, 0), 0) local far = plant_world({plant_row("x", "clone", "", "2026-01-30", "1", "X"), plant_row("y", "clone", "", "2026-01-30", "1", "Y"), plant_row("a", "clone", "", "2026-01-30", "1", "A")}) expect("a world moved too far", #assess(far, base, 0), 1) expect("the same, with fresh=1", #assess(far, base, 1), 0) local odd = plant_world({plant_row("a", "git file", "", "2026-01-30", "1", "A"), plant_row("w", "worktree of gone", "gone", "2026-01-30", "1", "W")}) expect("an odd kind and a dangling worktree", #assess(odd, nil, 0), 2) local quiet = plant_world({plant_row("a", "clone", "", "2026-01-30", "1", "A")}) quiet.mentions = {} expect("no mentions", #assess(quiet, nil, 0), 1) local shrunk = plant_world({{folder = "a", kind = "clone", main = "", branch = "main", remote = "", first = "2026-01-01", last = "2026-01-30", days = 10, commits = "1", readme = "README.md"}}) expect("a row field gone", #assess(shrunk, nil, 0), 1) local nofield = {rows = {}, mentions = {}, links = {}} expect("a survey field gone", #assess(nofield, nil, 0), 1) print("plan_repo_essay self_test: PASS (a sound world, too far, odd kinds, no mentions, a survey that changed)") end if SELF_TEST == 1 then self_test() else for p in {DATA .. "/notes", "repos:essay-surface/scripts/check_note.shale", "repos:essay-surface/scripts/prune_notes.shale"} do if not exists(p) then fail("plan_repo_essay: " .. p .. " is gone: the essay surface moved; find where notes live now and update this recipe") end end local s = survey_now(REPOS) local base = nil if has_key(s, "today") then base = last_map(DATA, s.today) end local stops = assess(s, base, FRESH) if #stops > 0 then for st in stops do print("STOP: " .. st) end fail("plan_repo_essay: the world changed too much for this playbook (" .. #stops .. " stops above)") end print_plan(s, base, DATA) print("") print("plan_repo_essay: " .. #s.rows .. " folders, " .. #s.mentions .. " mentions; baseline saved at " .. save_map(DATA, s)) end

name: cookbook/plants/check_recipe_names/merge_conflicts.shale
html: -- The conflict markers: a good library name, its const a map over lines. const MARKERS = { open = "<<<<<<<", close = ">>>>>>>", } function is_marker(l) if starts_with(l, "<<<<<<<") then return true end for m in {"=======", ">>>>>>>"} do if starts_with(l, m) then return true end end return false end
