name: cookbook/prose/build_term_index.shale
html: -- budget: steps=2000000000 reads=100 read_bytes=20000000 output_bytes=400000 -- This builds a book's index from its prose, and reports what the index says -- about the book's order: a term used long before the chapter that teaches it, -- a term with no home, and a chapter that brings in too many terms at once. -- -- cd <a book's checkout> && shale <cookbook>/prose/build_term_index.shale book=book/book.md terms=book/index_terms.txt -- shale <cookbook>/prose/build_term_index.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- book the markdown document, each `## ` heading a chapter; -- terms the terms and their categories (the format is below); -- stop_at the heading, after `## `, of the first chapter left out, -- such as the first appendix; the whole book by default; -- early_gap a first mention this many chapters or more before the -- early_mentions busiest chapter, with this many mentions or fewer, is a -- possible forward use (3 and 2 by default); -- spread a term in this many chapters or more has no home (15); -- new_terms a chapter that first mentions this many terms or more -- carries too many new ideas (6). -- -- A term is found in a chapter when one of its patterns matches a line of that -- chapter's prose: every line outside a ``` fence, headings and table cells -- included, read in lower case. The text above the first chapter is left out. -- -- The terms file has a `## Category` line above each group of terms. A term is -- a line `Name`, or `Name | pattern | pattern ...`, the patterns regular -- expressions over the lower-cased line, `\bname\b` when none is given. A part -- `main: Chapter title` names the chapter that teaches it, in place of the one -- that mentions it most. A blank line, or one that starts `#` but not `## `, -- is skipped. -- -- The output is markdown: the index, one table per category, with each term's -- busiest chapter, its first, and every chapter that mentions it; then the -- smells. It judges nothing and exits 0; a smell is a question for the writer. const DEFAULT_LIMITS = {early_gap = 3, early_mentions = 2, spread = 15, new_terms = 6} -- The terms as `{category, name, patterns, main}`, in the file's order. -- `where` names the file in a stop. function terms_of(text, where) local found = {} local category = "" local number = 0 for raw in split(text, "\n") do number = number + 1 local l = trim(raw) if starts_with(l, "## ") then category = trim(sub(l, 4)) elseif l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then if category == "" then fail("build_term_index: " .. where .. ":" .. number .. ": a term before any `## Category`") end local parts = split(l, " | ") local name = trim(parts[1]) local patterns = {} local main = "" for part in drop(parts, 1) do local p = trim(part) if starts_with(p, "main: ") then main = trim(sub(p, 7)) else push(patterns, p) end end if #patterns == 0 then push(patterns, "\\b" .. lower(name) .. "\\b") end push(found, {category = category, name = name, patterns = patterns, main = main}) end end return found end -- The chapters above `stop_at` ("" for none) as `{number, title, lines}`, -- each holding its prose in lower case. function chapters_of(text, stop_at) local found = {} local now = nil local fenced = false for l in split(text, "\n") do if starts_with(l, "```") then fenced = not fenced elseif not fenced then if starts_with(l, "## ") then local title = trim(sub(l, 4)) if stop_at ~= "" and title == stop_at then break end now = {number = #found + 1, title = title, lines = {}} push(found, now) elseif now ~= nil then push(now.lines, lower(l)) end end end return found end -- How many lines of `chapter` match any of `patterns`. function mentions(chapter, patterns) local n = 0 for l in chapter.lines do local hit = false for p in patterns do if not hit and re_find(l, p) ~= nil then hit = true end end if hit then n = n + 1 end end return n end -- One term's entry: `{term, counts, chapters, first, most}`, `counts` holding -- the lines that mention it in each chapter it's in. A term found nowhere has -- no `first` or `most`. function entry_of(term, chapters) local counts = {} local present = {} local first = nil local most = nil for c in chapters do local n = mentions(c, term.patterns) if n > 0 then counts["" .. c.number] = n push(present, c.number) if first == nil then first = c end if most == nil or n > counts["" .. most.number] then most = c end end end if first == nil then return {term = term, counts = counts, chapters = present} end if term.main ~= "" then most = nil for c in chapters do if c.title == term.main then most = c end end if most == nil then fail("build_term_index: " .. term.name .. "'s main chapter, " .. term.main .. ", is no chapter of the book") end if not has_key(counts, "" .. most.number) then fail("build_term_index: " .. term.name .. "'s main chapter, " .. term.main .. ", never mentions it") end end return {term = term, counts = counts, chapters = present, first = first, most = most} end function entries_of(book_text, terms_text, terms_where, stop_at) local chapters = chapters_of(book_text, stop_at) if #chapters == 0 then fail("build_term_index: the book has no `## ` chapters") end local entries = {} for t in terms_of(terms_text, terms_where) do push(entries, entry_of(t, chapters)) end return {chapters = chapters, entries = entries} end function is_found(e) return has_key(e, "first") end -- The smells, as `{early, spread, nowhere, crowded}`: the entries of the -- first three, and each crowded chapter as `{chapter, names}`. function smells_of(index, limits) local early = {} local spread = {} local nowhere = {} for e in index.entries do if not is_found(e) then push(nowhere, e) else if e.most.number - e.first.number >= limits.early_gap and e.counts["" .. e.first.number] <= limits.early_mentions then push(early, e) end if #e.chapters >= limits.spread then push(spread, e) end end end local crowded = {} for c in index.chapters do local fresh = {} for e in index.entries do if is_found(e) and e.first.number == c.number then push(fresh, e.term.name) end end if #fresh >= limits.new_terms then push(crowded, {chapter = c, names = fresh}) end end return {early = early, spread = spread, nowhere = nowhere, crowded = crowded} end function chapter_name(c) return c.number .. ". " .. c.title end function print_index(index) print("# The index") local category = "" for e in index.entries do if e.term.category ~= category then category = e.term.category print("") print("## " .. category) print("") print("| Term | Most in | First in | Every chapter |") print("|---|---|---|---|") end if not is_found(e) then print("| " .. e.term.name .. " | (nowhere) | | |") else local numbers = {} for n in e.chapters do push(numbers, "" .. n) end print("| " .. e.term.name .. " | " .. chapter_name(e.most) .. " | " .. chapter_name(e.first) .. " | " .. join(numbers, ", ") .. " |") end end return nil end function print_smells(smells, limits) print("") print("# The smells") print("") print("## Mentioned early, dwelt on later") print("") print("| Term | First in | Mentions there | Most in | Mentions there |") print("|---|---|---|---|---|") for e in smells.early do print("| " .. e.term.name .. " | " .. chapter_name(e.first) .. " | " .. e.counts["" .. e.first.number] .. " | " .. chapter_name(e.most) .. " | " .. e.counts["" .. e.most.number] .. " |") end print("") print("## Spread across " .. limits.spread .. " chapters or more") print("") print("| Term | Chapters | Most in |") print("|---|---|---|") for e in smells.spread do print("| " .. e.term.name .. " | " .. #e.chapters .. " | " .. chapter_name(e.most) .. " |") end print("") print("## Found nowhere") print("") for e in smells.nowhere do print("- " .. e.term.name) end print("") print("## Chapters that first mention " .. limits.new_terms .. " terms or more") print("") print("| Chapter | New terms |") print("|---|---|") for c in smells.crowded do print("| " .. chapter_name(c.chapter) .. " | " .. join(c.names, ", ") .. " |") end return nil end -- The names of `entries`, joined by `, `. function names_of(entries) local names = {} for e in entries do push(names, e.term.name) end return join(names, ", ") end function stop_message(r) if r.ok then return "" end return r.error end if arg("self_test", "") ~= "" then local P = "cookbook/prose/plants/build_term_index/" local wrong = {} local limits = {early_gap = 2, early_mentions = 1, spread = 4, new_terms = 3} local index = entries_of(read(P .. "book.md"), read(P .. "terms.txt"), P .. "terms.txt", "Appendix") if #index.chapters ~= 4 then push(wrong, "want 4 chapters above the appendix, got " .. #index.chapters) end -- Each term as `name first most chapters`. local got = {} for e in index.entries do if is_found(e) then local numbers = {} for n in e.chapters do push(numbers, "" .. n) end push(got, e.term.name .. " " .. e.first.number .. " " .. e.most.number .. " " .. join(numbers, ",")) else push(got, e.term.name .. " nowhere") end end local want = "budget 1 3 1,3; mount 1 2 1,2; stop 1 4 1,2,3,4; heredoc 1 1 1,4; script 1 3 1,3; gate 2 2 2; fence nowhere; appendix nowhere" if join(got, "; ") ~= want then push(wrong, "the entries: want [" .. want .. "], got [" .. join(got, "; ") .. "]") end local s = smells_of(index, limits) local smell_cases = { {"early", names_of(s.early), "budget, stop"}, {"spread", names_of(s.spread), "stop"}, {"nowhere", names_of(s.nowhere), "fence, appendix"}, } for c in smell_cases do if c[2] ~= c[3] then push(wrong, c[1] .. ": want [" .. c[3] .. "], got [" .. c[2] .. "]") end end if #s.crowded ~= 1 or s.crowded[1].chapter.number ~= 1 or join(s.crowded[1].names, ", ") ~= "budget, mount, stop, heredoc, script" then push(wrong, "crowded: want chapter 1 with budget, mount, stop, heredoc, script") end -- The whole book reads the appendix too, where `appendix` is found. local whole = entries_of(read(P .. "book.md"), read(P .. "terms.txt"), P .. "terms.txt", "") if #whole.chapters ~= 5 or not is_found(whole.entries[8]) then push(wrong, "the whole book: want 5 chapters and `appendix` found") end local stops = { {"no_category.txt", "a term before any `## Category`"}, {"bad_main.txt", "is no chapter of the book"}, {"unmentioned_main.txt", "never mentions it"}, } for c in stops do local why = stop_message(attempt(entries_of, read(P .. "book.md"), read(P .. c[1]), P .. c[1], "Appendix")) if not contains(why, c[2]) then push(wrong, c[1] .. ": want a stop holding `" .. c[2] .. "`, got `" .. why .. "`") end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail(tostring(#wrong) .. " build_term_index plants wrong") end print("build_term_index: " .. #index.entries .. " terms, " .. #smell_cases + 1 .. " smells and " .. #stops .. " stops as their plants say") else local book = arg("book", "") local terms = arg("terms", "") if book == "" or terms == "" then fail("build_term_index: book= and terms= name the document and its terms (see the header)") end local limits = { early_gap = arg("early_gap", DEFAULT_LIMITS.early_gap), early_mentions = arg("early_mentions", DEFAULT_LIMITS.early_mentions), spread = arg("spread", DEFAULT_LIMITS.spread), new_terms = arg("new_terms", DEFAULT_LIMITS.new_terms), } local index = entries_of(read(book), read(terms), terms, arg("stop_at", "")) print_index(index) print_smells(smells_of(index, limits), limits) end

name: cookbook/prose/find_negatives.shale
html: -- budget: steps=200000000 reads=100 read_bytes=10000000 output_bytes=1000000 -- This lint finds the negative sentences in a book's prose. A book whose rule -- is "say what happens, not what something isn't" rewrites each negative, or -- keeps it and lists it in a table with its kind. -- -- cd <a book's checkout> && shale <cookbook>/prose/find_negatives.shale manuscript=book/book.md table=book/negatives.txt -- shale <cookbook>/prose/find_negatives.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- manuscript the markdown document; -- table the sentences the book keeps (the format is below); -- stop_at the heading, after `## `, of the first chapter it doesn't -- read; the whole manuscript when it's not given. A book being -- rewritten a chapter at a time moves it down as it goes; -- words `negatives` by default, or `voice` for the disguised -- negatives and the verbs that give code a will; -- held how many unlisted negative sentences to expect, so a book -- with many today can hold the count and bring it down. -- -- The prose is every line above `stop_at` outside a ``` fence, except a line -- that starts `{{`, a book's include. Inline code, between backticks, is taken -- out before the words are read, so `doesn't` in a quoted name is never a hit, -- and so is a link to a chapter, `{{chapter Title}}`. A table row's cells are -- read one by one. A sentence ends at `.`, `!` or `?` followed by a space or -- the line's end, so `4.5` and `Distance.metres` stay in one. A curly -- apostrophe reads as a straight one. -- -- A negative is a sentence holding one of the words, matched as a whole word -- with any case. A sentence counts once, however many it holds. -- -- The table opens with the kinds, each a line `# keep name: what it is` or -- `# fix name: what it is`. Every other line that isn't blank or a `#` comment -- is `kind: the sentence`, the sentence exactly as this prints it, and its kind -- must be a `keep` kind. A sentence listed twice, a kind the table doesn't -- define, a `fix` kind on a sentence, or a table with no kinds stops the run. -- -- The checks: -- -- negative A negative sentence the table doesn't list. -- unused_exception A line of the table whose sentence the prose doesn't -- hold, or holds with no negative in it. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there is a finding. Given -- `held`, it passes with that many negatives, printing only the counts, and -- fails with any other number, more or fewer, or with an unused exception. -- The summary starts with the word set's name, `negatives:` or `voice:`. use("cookbook:findings.shale") -- The plain negatives, and their near friends: `unless`, `rather than`, -- `lacks`, `hardly` and `barely` each say a thing by what it isn't, too. const NEGATIVE_WORDS = { "not", "no", "none", "nothing", "nobody", "nowhere", "never", "neither", "nor", "without", "isn't", "aren't", "wasn't", "weren't", "don't", "doesn't", "didn't", "can't", "cannot", "won't", "wouldn't", "shouldn't", "couldn't", "hasn't", "haven't", "hadn't", "mustn't", "needn't", "ain't", "unless", "rather than", "lacks", "lack", "hardly", "barely", } -- Negatives in disguise, and verbs that give code a will. Only the -- third-person forms are listed, so "you know" is never a hit. const VOICE_WORDS = { "refuses", "refused", "leaves out", "left out", "stays out", "stay out", "spares", "skips", "omits", "free of", "knows", "decides", "wants", "trusts", "remembers", "forgets", "insists", } const WORD_SETS = {negatives = NEGATIVE_WORDS, voice = VOICE_WORDS} -- A sentence: code spans whole, and a `.`, `!` or `?` that a space doesn't -- follow inside it. const SENTENCE = "((?:`[^`]*`|[^`.!?]|[.!?][^ .!?`])+[.!?]*)" -- The pattern that finds the words of `word_set`, one of WORD_SETS' names. function word_pattern(word_set) if not has_key(WORD_SETS, word_set) then fail("negatives: words= is negatives or voice, not `" .. word_set .. "`") end return "\\b(" .. join(WORD_SETS[word_set], "|") .. ")\\b" end -- The texts of one line of prose: a table row's cells, or the line itself. function line_texts(l) if not starts_with(trim(l), "|") then return {l} end local cells = {} for c in split(l, "|") do if trim(c) ~= "" and re_find(c, "^ *:?-+:? *$") == nil then push(cells, c) end end return cells end -- The words of `pattern` in `sentence`, its code taken out, in the order they -- come. function words_in(sentence, pattern) local no_code = re_replace(substitute(sentence, "’", "'", {missing_ok = true}), "`[^`]*`", " ") local plain = lower(re_replace(no_code, "\\{\\{chapter [^}]*\\}\\}", " ")) local found = {} for m in re_find_all(plain, pattern) do push(found, m.group) end return found end -- Every sentence of `text` above the chapter `stop_at` ("" for none) that -- holds a word of `pattern`, as `{line, chapter, words, sentence}`, and how -- many sentences were read. `where` names the manuscript in a stop. function prose_hits(text, pattern, stop_at, where) local found = {} local read_count = 0 local is_fenced = false local chapter = "(before the first chapter)" local number = 0 local is_stopped = false for l in split(text, "\n") do number = number + 1 if not is_stopped then if starts_with(l, "```") then is_fenced = not is_fenced elseif not is_fenced and not starts_with(l, "{{") then if starts_with(l, "## ") then chapter = trim(sub(l, 4)) if stop_at ~= "" and chapter == stop_at then is_stopped = true end end if not is_stopped then for t in line_texts(l) do for m in re_find_all(t, SENTENCE) do local sentence = trim(m.group) if sentence ~= "" then read_count = read_count + 1 local words = words_in(sentence, pattern) if #words > 0 then push(found, {line = number, chapter = chapter, words = join(unique(words), ","), sentence = sentence}) end end end end end end end end if stop_at ~= "" and not is_stopped then fail("negatives: no heading `## " .. stop_at .. "` in " .. where) end return {found = found, read_count = read_count} end -- The table at `path` as `{kinds, rows, by_sentence}`: `kinds` from each -- kind's name to `keep` or `fix`, and each row `{kind, sentence, line}`. function exception_table(path) if not exists(path) then fail("negatives: no table " .. path) end local kinds = {} local rows = {} local by_sentence = {} local number = 0 for raw in lines(read(path)) do number = number + 1 local l = trim(raw) local at = "negatives: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": " local kind = re_find(l, "^# (keep|fix) ([a-z-]+): +[^ ]") if kind ~= nil then if has_key(kinds, kind.groups[2]) then fail(at .. "the kind `" .. kind.groups[2] .. "` is defined twice") end kinds[kind.groups[2]] = kind.groups[1] elseif l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then local m = re_find(l, "^([a-z-]+): +([^ ].*)$") if m == nil then fail(at .. "expected `kind: the sentence`") end local name = m.groups[1] local sentence = m.groups[2] if not has_key(kinds, name) then fail(at .. "`" .. name .. "` is no kind the table defines") end if kinds[name] ~= "keep" then fail(at .. "`" .. name .. "` is a kind to fix, not to keep") end if has_key(by_sentence, sentence) then fail(at .. "the sentence is listed twice") end push(rows, {kind = name, sentence = sentence, line = number}) by_sentence[sentence] = true end end if #keys(kinds) == 0 then fail("negatives: " .. path .. " defines no kinds") end return {kinds = kinds, rows = rows, by_sentence = by_sentence} end -- The verdict on the manuscript at `manuscript` against the table at `table_path`, -- as `{negatives, unused, summary}`: `negatives` the hits the table doesn't -- keep, `{line, chapter, words, sentence}`, and `unused` the finding lines of -- the table's unused rows. function judged(manuscript, table_path, word_set, stop_at) local pattern = word_pattern(word_set) local exceptions = exception_table(table_path) local prose = prose_hits(read(manuscript), pattern, stop_at, manuscript) if prose.read_count == 0 then fail("negatives: no prose in " .. manuscript) end local negatives = {} local kept = {} for f in prose.found do if has_key(exceptions.by_sentence, f.sentence) then kept[f.sentence] = true else push(negatives, f) end end local unused = {} for row in exceptions.rows do if not has_key(kept, row.sentence) then push(unused, table_path .. ":" .. row.line .. ": unused_exception: no negative sentence of the prose is `" .. row.sentence .. "`") end end local read_where = "" if stop_at ~= "" then read_where = " above `" .. stop_at .. "`" end local summary = word_set .. ": negative " .. #negatives .. ", unused_exception " .. #unused .. ", " .. #prose.found .. " negative sentences of " .. prose.read_count .. " read" .. read_where .. ", " .. #exceptions.rows .. " kept in the table" return {negatives = negatives, unused = unused, summary = summary} end function finding_line(manuscript, f) return manuscript .. ":" .. f.line .. ": negative [" .. f.chapter .. "] " .. f.words .. ": " .. f.sentence end -- Whether the verdict passes: no finding, or with `held` given (not ""), -- exactly that many negatives and no unused exception. function is_passing(verdict, held) if #verdict.unused > 0 then return false end if held == "" then return #verdict.negatives == 0 end return #verdict.negatives == tonumber(held) end -- The plants' findings as `line words` each, joined by `; `. function compact(verdict) local got = {} for f in verdict.negatives do push(got, f.line .. " " .. f.words) end return join(got, "; ") end -- A stop's message, or "" when `attempt` gave a value. function stop_message(r) if r.ok then return "" end return r.error end if arg("self_test", "") ~= "" then local P = "cookbook/prose/plants/find_negatives/" local BOOK = P .. "book.md" local wrong = {} local cases = { {"negatives", "", "table.txt", "3 isn't; 7 doesn't,never; 8 nothing; 11 doesn't; 15 not; 23 nothing", 1}, {"negatives", "Second", "table.txt", "3 isn't; 7 doesn't,never; 8 nothing; 11 doesn't; 15 not", 1}, {"voice", "", "voice.txt", "9 refuses,knows", 0}, } for c in cases do local v = judged(BOOK, P .. c[3], c[1], c[2]) if compact(v) ~= c[4] or #v.unused ~= c[5] then push(wrong, c[1] .. " stop_at=`" .. c[2] .. "`: want [" .. c[4] .. "] and " .. c[5] .. " unused, got [" .. compact(v) .. "] and " .. #v.unused .. " unused") end end -- The sentences whole: a `4.5` and a table cell, as a finding prints them. local v = judged(BOOK, P .. "table.txt", "negatives", "") local want_lines = { BOOK .. ":8: negative [First] nothing: The value 4.5 stays in one sentence with nothing in it.", BOOK .. ":15: negative [First] not: not a sentence", } for w in want_lines do local seen = false for f in v.negatives do if finding_line(BOOK, f) == w then seen = true end end if not seen then push(wrong, "no finding `" .. w .. "`") end end if #v.unused ~= 1 or not contains(v.unused[1], "table.txt:5: unused_exception") then push(wrong, "the unused row: got [" .. join(v.unused, "; ") .. "]") end -- `held` passes at the count alone, and an unused row fails it. local voice = judged(BOOK, P .. "voice.txt", "voice", "") local holds = {{voice, "1", true}, {voice, "0", false}, {voice, "2", false}, {voice, "", false}, {v, "6", false}} for h in holds do if is_passing(h[1], h[2]) ~= h[3] then push(wrong, "held=`" .. h[2] .. "` with " .. #h[1].negatives .. " negatives: want " .. tostring(h[3])) end end -- The stops, each with the words its message holds. local stops = { {"negatives", "Missing", "table.txt", "no heading `## Missing`"}, {"loud", "", "table.txt", "words= is negatives or voice"}, {"negatives", "", "twice.txt", "listed twice"}, {"negatives", "", "undefined.txt", "is no kind the table defines"}, {"negatives", "", "fix.txt", "a kind to fix, not to keep"}, {"negatives", "", "nokinds.txt", "defines no kinds"}, {"negatives", "", "gone.txt", "no table"}, } for s in stops do local why = stop_message(attempt(judged, BOOK, P .. s[3], s[1], s[2])) if not contains(why, s[4]) then push(wrong, s[3] .. " words=" .. s[1] .. " stop_at=`" .. s[2] .. "`: want a stop holding `" .. s[4] .. "`, got `" .. why .. "`") end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail(tostring(#wrong) .. " negatives plants wrong") end print("negatives: " .. #cases .. " readings, " .. #holds .. " holds and " .. #stops .. " stops as their plants say") else local manuscript = arg("manuscript", "") local table_path = arg("table", "") if manuscript == "" or table_path == "" then fail("negatives: manuscript= and table= name the document and its table (see the header)") end local held = arg("held", "") local verdict = judged(manuscript, table_path, arg("words", "negatives"), arg("stop_at", "")) if held ~= "" and is_passing(verdict, held) then print(verdict.summary .. ", as held") else local all = {} for f in verdict.negatives do push(all, finding_line(manuscript, f)) end for l in verdict.unused do push(all, l) end print_findings(verdict.summary, all) -- A stop inside a function prints the calls after it, so these stand at -- the top level, and the summary is the last line a caller reads. if held ~= "" then fail("negatives: held at negative " .. held .. " and unused_exception 0") end if #all > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end end

name: cookbook/prune_merged_branches.shale
html: -- This recipe finds the work branches that are merged, and deletes them when -- asked. In each repo it judges every branch on `origin` whose name starts -- with one of `prefixes` (`claude/` and `box/`: CC's and the box's) against -- `origin`'s default branch, one line each: -- -- delete roc-chat claude/roc-chat merged into main -- keep shale claude/x 3 commits not in master -- keep roc-chat box/auth origin's default branch -- -- A branch counts as merged only when its tip is an ancestor of the default -- branch's (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), never by its name, so a branch -- with even one commit the default lacks is kept, with the count. The -- default branch is always kept. Only `delete=1` deletes: the plain run is -- a report, and with `delete=1` each `delete` line is a `git push origin -- --delete`, said as it is done. Run it yourself (Steve), or let an agent -- run the report and hand you the `delete=1` line. -- -- shale cookbook:prune_merged_branches.shale -- shale cookbook:prune_merged_branches.shale delete=1 -- shale cookbook:prune_merged_branches.shale repos=roc-chat,shale prefixes=claude/ -- shale cookbook:prune_merged_branches.shale self_test=1 -- -- `repos` are folders under `repos:` (comma-separated; the default the -- repos CC and the box branch in). Each is fetched with `--prune` first, so -- a branch already gone is not reported. -- -- budget: steps=200000000 const DEFAULT_REPOS = "roc-chat,roc-markdown,chat-client,chat-markdown,roc-webbox,roc-apps,shale,metal-vmm,angry-gopher,zig-metal-unikernel,zig-webbox,zig-coverage-sdk,dog-park" const REPOS = arg("repos", DEFAULT_REPOS) const PREFIXES = arg("prefixes", "claude/,box/") const DELETE = arg("delete", "0") == "1" const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "0") == "1" function git(dir, args) local argv = {"git", "-C", dir} for a in args do argv[#argv + 1] = a end return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 1000000}) end -- As `git`, for a call whose nonzero exit is an answer, not a failure. function git_may_fail(dir, args, why) local argv = {"git", "-C", dir} for a in args do argv[#argv + 1] = a end return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 1000000, want = why}) end -- The default branch's name on origin, asked of origin itself (`remote -- set-head --auto`), never a checkout's old note of it, which outlives a -- default changed or a branch deleted. The name is read from the ref it -- set (`symbolic-ref`), never from what it prints, whose words changed in -- git 2.48 ("origin/HEAD set to main" before, "'origin/HEAD' is now -- created and points to 'main'" after). function default_branch(dir) local r = git_may_fail(dir, {"remote", "set-head", "origin", "--auto"}, "nonzero: said by the caller") if r.code ~= 0 then return nil end local ref = git_may_fail(dir, {"symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"}, "nonzero: no origin/HEAD, said by the caller") local said = trim(ref.out) if ref.code ~= 0 or not starts_with(said, "origin/") then return nil end return sub(said, #"origin/" + 1, #said) end function prefixed(name, prefixes) for p in prefixes do if starts_with(name, p) then return true end end return false end -- One repo's verdicts, a list of {act, repo, branch, why}: four programs -- (fetch, set-head, symbolic-ref, one for-each-ref with each branch's -- commits ahead of the default), whatever the branches. function judge(dir, label, prefixes) local out = {} git(dir, {"fetch", "-q", "--prune", "origin"}) local main = default_branch(dir) if main == nil then out[#out + 1] = {act = "skip", repo = label, branch = "", why = "origin's default branch is not known here"} return out end local refs = git(dir, {"for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short) %(ahead-behind:origin/" .. main .. ")", "refs/remotes/origin"}) for line in lines(refs.out) do local parts = split(trim(line), " ") if #parts == 3 and starts_with(parts[1], "origin/") then local name = sub(parts[1], #"origin/" + 1, #parts[1]) if name ~= "HEAD" and prefixed(name, prefixes) then if name == main then out[#out + 1] = {act = "keep", repo = label, branch = name, why = "origin's default branch"} elseif parts[2] == "0" then out[#out + 1] = {act = "delete", repo = label, branch = name, why = "merged into " .. main} else out[#out + 1] = {act = "keep", repo = label, branch = name, why = parts[2] .. " commits not in " .. main} end end end end return out end function say(v) print(v.act .. "\t" .. v.repo .. "\t" .. v.branch .. "\t" .. v.why) end if SELF_TEST then -- A bare origin with main; `merged` (merged), `ahead` (one commit more), -- and `box/default` made origin's default; the judge must keep and -- delete exactly as planted. local T = fresh_dir("scratch:", "branch_prune_self_test") local root = real(T) run({"git", "init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", root .. "/origin.git"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000}) run({"git", "clone", "-q", root .. "/origin.git", root .. "/work"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000}) local w = root .. "/work" git(w, {"-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "base"}) git(w, {"push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main"}) git(w, {"push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/claude/merged"}) git(w, {"-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "more"}) git(w, {"push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/claude/ahead"}) git(w, {"push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/other/ignored"}) git(w, {"remote", "set-head", "origin", "main"}) local got = {} for v in judge(w, "t", {"claude/", "box/"}) do got[v.branch] = v.act; say(v) end if got["claude/merged"] ~= "delete" then fail("self_test: claude/merged should be delete, is " .. tostring(got["claude/merged"])) end if got["claude/ahead"] ~= "keep" then fail("self_test: claude/ahead (one commit more) should be keep") end if has_key(got, "other/ignored") then fail("self_test: a branch outside the prefixes was judged") end -- The default branch itself, under a work prefix, is kept. git(w, {"push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/box/default"}) run({"git", "--git-dir", root .. "/origin.git", "symbolic-ref", "HEAD", "refs/heads/box/default"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000}) git(w, {"remote", "set-head", "origin", "--auto"}) got = {} for v in judge(w, "t", {"claude/", "box/"}) do got[v.branch] = v.why end if got["box/default"] ~= "origin's default branch" then fail("self_test: the default branch box/default was not kept as the default") end remove_tree(T) print("prune_merged_branches self_test: PASS (merged deleted, one commit ahead kept, the default kept, other prefixes untouched)") else local prefixes = split(PREFIXES, ",") local deleted = 0 local kept = 0 for name in split(REPOS, ",") do local label = trim(name) if not exists("repos:" .. label .. "/.git") then print("skip\t" .. label .. "\t\tno checkout at repos:" .. label) else local dir = real("repos:" .. label) local doomed = {} for v in judge(dir, label, prefixes) do say(v) if v.act == "delete" then doomed[#doomed + 1] = v.branch elseif v.act == "keep" then kept = kept + 1 end end if DELETE and #doomed > 0 then local argv = {"push", "origin", "--delete"} for d in doomed do argv[#argv + 1] = d end local pushed = git_may_fail(dir, argv, "nonzero: said below") if pushed.code == 0 then print(" deleted on origin: " .. join(doomed, ", ")) else print(" NOT deleted (" .. label .. "): " .. trim(pushed.out)) doomed = {} end end deleted = deleted + #doomed end end if DELETE then print("prune_merged_branches: " .. deleted .. " deleted, " .. kept .. " kept") else print("prune_merged_branches: " .. deleted .. " to delete, " .. kept .. " kept; nothing deleted (delete=1 deletes them)") end end

name: cookbook/read_wants.shale
html: -- This script reads back the log of escapes, the commands that went past -- shale-gate because Shale could not do them yet, or never will. It lists the -- newest escapes and counts them by kind, by tag and by session. -- -- shale cookbook:read_wants.shale (today, UTC) -- shale cookbook:read_wants.shale since=2026-10-23T22:24 -- shale cookbook:read_wants.shale since=2026-10-17 rows=0 top=30 -- shale cookbook:read_wants.shale tag=roc-check session=ba149522 -- -- `since` and `until` are times or their prefixes: `2026-10-23` is that day's -- start, and `until` itself is left out. `kind`, `tag` and `session` (or the -- start of one) keep only those escapes. `rows` is how many of the newest to -- list, where 0 gives the counts alone, and `top` is how many tags to count. -- -- `log` is the file, by default `state:wants.tsv`, through a `state` mount over -- ~/.local/state/shale. Each line of it holds the time, the session, `want` or -- `out-of-scope`, the tag, the text and the command, separated by tabs. -- -- budget: steps=200000000 const LOG = arg("log", "state:wants.tsv") const SINCE = arg("since", sub(date(now()), 1, 10)) const UNTIL = arg("until", "") const KIND = arg("kind", "") const TAG = arg("tag", "") const SESSION = arg("session", "") const ROWS = arg("rows", 40) const TOP_TAGS = arg("top", 20) function is_wanted(fields) return #fields >= 5 and fields[1] >= SINCE and (UNTIL == "" or fields[1] < UNTIL) and (KIND == "" or fields[3] == KIND) and (TAG == "" or fields[4] == TAG) and (SESSION == "" or starts_with(fields[2], SESSION)) end function read_escapes() local escapes = {} local offset = 0 while true do local part = read_lines(LOG, offset) for line in part.lines do local fields = split(line, "\t") if is_wanted(fields) then push(escapes, {time = fields[1], session = fields[2], kind = fields[3], tag = fields[4], text = fields[5]}) end end if part.done then return escapes end offset = part.next end end -- Gives each value of `field` among `escapes` with its count, most first. function counts_of(escapes, field) local count_by_value = {} for escape in escapes do incr(count_by_value, escape[field]) end local counts = {} for value in keys(count_by_value) do push(counts, {name = value, n = count_by_value[value]}) end sort(counts, "n", "desc") return counts end function print_newest(escapes) local first_listed = #escapes - ROWS + 1 if first_listed < 1 then first_listed = 1 end for i = first_listed, #escapes do local escape = escapes[i] local kind_note = escape.kind == "want" and "" or " (" .. escape.kind .. ")" print(sub(escape.time, 12, 16) .. " " .. escape.tag .. kind_note .. ": " .. sub(escape.text, 1, 160)) end if first_listed > 1 and ROWS > 0 then print("... " .. (first_listed - 1) .. " earlier (rows=" .. ROWS .. ")") end end function print_counts(escapes) local period = "since " .. SINCE if UNTIL ~= "" then period = period .. ", until " .. UNTIL end print("── " .. #escapes .. " escapes " .. period) local kinds = {} for kind in counts_of(escapes, "kind") do push(kinds, kind.n .. " " .. kind.name) end if #kinds > 0 then print("by kind: " .. join(kinds, ", ")) end local tag_counts = counts_of(escapes, "tag") local tags = {} for tag in take(tag_counts, TOP_TAGS) do push(tags, tag.n .. " " .. tag.name) end if #tags > 0 then print("by tag: " .. join(tags, ", ") .. (#tag_counts > TOP_TAGS and ", ... " .. (#tag_counts - TOP_TAGS) .. " more" or "")) end local sessions = {} for session in counts_of(escapes, "session") do push(sessions, session.n .. " " .. sub(session.name, 1, 8)) end if #sessions > 0 then print("by session: " .. join(sessions, ", ")) end end local escapes = read_escapes() print_newest(escapes) print_counts(escapes)

name: cookbook/read_zulip_topic.shale
html: -- This script prints the newest messages of a Zulip topic, oldest first, each -- with its sender and its markdown as written. -- -- shale cookbook:read_zulip_topic.shale site=roc.zulipchat.com email=you@example.com key=keys:roc_zulip_api_key stream=beginners topic=style num=20 -- -- `site` is the Zulip server's host, `email` the account the key belongs to, -- and `num` how many messages to read, 100 unless given. A value with a space -- needs `--args-stdin`, with one `NAME=VALUE` a line. -- -- `key` is a path in a secrets mount to a file holding only the API key. `run` -- hands the key to curl alone, which reads it from its environment -- (`--variable`), so no script sees it and it never reaches the output. -- -- Any status other than 200, or a `result` other than `success`, fails the -- launch with Zulip's own message. -- -- budget: steps=50000000 arena_bytes=500000000 const SITE = arg("site", "") const EMAIL = arg("email", "") const KEY = arg("key", "") const STREAM = arg("stream", "") const TOPIC = arg("topic", "") const NUM = arg("num", 100) if SITE == "" or EMAIL == "" or KEY == "" or STREAM == "" or TOPIC == "" then fail("zulip: site=, email=, key=keys:<file>, stream= and topic= are each needed") end function json_string(text) return "\"" .. substitute(substitute(text, "\\", "\\\\", {missing_ok = true}), "\"", "\\\"", {missing_ok = true}) .. "\"" end local scratch = fresh_dir("scratch:", "zulip") local body_path = scratch .. "/topic.json" local narrow = "[{\"operator\":\"channel\",\"operand\":" .. json_string(STREAM) .. "},{\"operator\":\"topic\",\"operand\":" .. json_string(TOPIC) .. "}]" local curl = run({"curl", "-sS", "-G", "https://" .. SITE .. "/api/v1/messages", "--variable", "%ZULIP_KEY", "--expand-user", EMAIL .. ":{{ZULIP_KEY}}", "--data-urlencode", "narrow=" .. narrow, "--data-urlencode", "anchor=newest", "--data-urlencode", "num_before=" .. NUM, "--data-urlencode", "num_after=0", "--data-urlencode", "apply_markdown=false", "-o", real(body_path), "-w", "%{http_code}"}, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 2000, secrets = {ZULIP_KEY = KEY}}) if curl.code ~= 0 then remove_tree(scratch) fail("zulip: curl exited " .. curl.code .. ": " .. curl.out) end local answer = json_read(read(body_path)) remove_tree(scratch) local http_status = curl.out if http_status ~= "200" or answer.result ~= "success" then fail("zulip: " .. SITE .. " answered " .. http_status .. ": " .. get(answer, "msg", "(no message)")) end local how_far_back = ", the newest " .. NUM if answer.found_oldest then how_far_back = ", from the first" end print("#" .. STREAM .. " > " .. TOPIC .. ": " .. #answer.messages .. " messages" .. how_far_back) for message in answer.messages do print("---- " .. message.sender_full_name .. " (message " .. message.id .. ")") print(message.content) end

name: cookbook/rename_words.shale
html: -- A word renamed across a project, any language: every whole-word `from` in -- the files matching `like` under `in` becomes `to`, one write a file, a -- one-line summary each. Whole words only (`fetchUserName` is left when -- `from` is `fetchUser`), but strings and comments are words too: read the -- summaries, then `git diff`. For Zig, `zig_rename` reads tokens instead -- (SHALE-AGENTS.md, "A symbol renamed across a tree"). -- -- shale cookbook:rename_words.shale from=fetchUser to=loadUser in=src ext=ts,tsx -- -- `ext` is the extensions to change (plain words for the launch line; a -- glob, `like=`, goes on stdin with `--args-stdin`). `in` is -- comma-separated files or folders (default the root); folders are -- walked past hidden ones (.git, .venv) and node_modules, zig-out and -- .zig-cache. A file that holds `from` only inside longer words is listed, -- not changed. -- -- budget: steps=500000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 const FROM = arg("from", "") const TO = arg("to", "") const IN = arg("in", ".") const LIKE = arg("like", "*") const EXT = arg("ext", "") -- Whether a walked file ends in one of `ext`'s extensions (any, unset). function wanted(path) if EXT == "" then return true end for e in split(EXT, ",") do if ends_with(path, "." .. trim(e)) then return true end end return false end if FROM == "" or TO == "" then fail("rename_words: give from=NAME to=NAME [in=dirs] [ext=ts,tsx]") end function passed_by(path) for part in {"/node_modules/", "/zig-out/", "/.zig-cache/"} do if contains("/" .. path .. "/", part) then return true end end return false end -- One file's whole-word edit; its own function, as `attempt` takes one. function rename_in(p) return edit(p, FROM, TO, {all = true, word = true}) end local renamed = 0 local files = 0 local only_inside = {} for given in split(IN, ",") do local place = trim(given) local paths = {} if place == "." or is_dir(place) then local opts = {kind = "file", skip = ".*"} if LIKE ~= "*" then opts = {kind = "file", skip = ".*", like = LIKE} end for e in walk_all(place, opts) do if not passed_by(e.path) and wanted(e.path) then push(paths, e.path) end end else push(paths, place) end for p in paths do if #grep_all(p, FROM) > 0 then local r = attempt(rename_in, p) if r.ok then renamed = renamed + r.value files = files + 1 elseif r.class == "argument" then -- `edit` found no whole word: `from` is only inside longer ones. push(only_inside, p) else fail(p .. ": " .. r.error) end end end end print(FROM .. " to " .. TO .. ": " .. renamed .. " in " .. files .. " files") if #only_inside > 0 then print("only inside longer words, left: " .. join(only_inside, ", ")) end

name: cookbook/retire_checkout.shale
html: -- This recipe says whether a checkout can be deleted. It only checks and -- never deletes: it ends with one verdict line, `CLEAR: <dir> can be -- deleted`, or `BLOCKED: <dir>` followed by every reason, one a line (and -- then stops, so the run exits nonzero). -- -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:retire_checkout.shale dir=roc -- shale cookbook:retire_checkout.shale self_test=1 -- -- Why it exists: a box cleanup once deleted an upstream clone that looked -- disposable. It had no uncommitted work and no unpushed branch, which was -- checked, and it was load-bearing all the same: build files in two sibling -- repos defaulted to it by a relative path, a build script named it through -- the `repos:` mount, a symbolic link in a lanes folder pointed at it, and a -- memory note said so. Nothing checked those, so the mistake was the -- system's, not the agent's. This recipe makes the check one launch, and its -- verdict the thing to quote before any `rm -rf`. -- -- `dir` is a folder in the root, the folder that holds the repos (run it -- from there). It is BLOCKED for each of these, and each says how to clear: -- -- 1. **Uncommitted or untracked changes** (`git status`), **and stashes** -- (`git stash list`). Commit and push them, or drop them on purpose. -- Ignored files are not counted. -- 2. **A local branch with commits on no remote**, named with its count -- (`git rev-list --count <branch> --not --remotes`), and a detached HEAD -- the same. Push it, or delete it with `git branch -D` once it is truly -- unwanted. The remotes are as the last fetch saw them: fetch first when -- a remote may have changed since. -- 3. **Worktrees**: a linked worktree registered in it (deleting the main -- checkout strands it), or, when it is itself a linked worktree, its -- branch with commits on no remote. Remove a worktree with `git -C <main> -- worktree remove <path>`, which is also the way to delete a worktree -- that comes out CLEAR. A linked worktree's branches and stashes are its -- main checkout's, so checks 1's stashes and 2 are its main's business -- and are not run on it. -- 4. **A symbolic link that resolves into it** (`readlink -m`), under the -- root, `build:` and `tools:` (`~/showell_repos`, `~/build` and `~/tools` -- on the box), walked 4 folders deep, hidden folders passed by (`.git`, -- `.zig-cache`): about 20,000 entries and a few seconds on the box. A -- link inside the folder itself does not count. Repoint or remove the -- link. A place that is not there here (no such mount) is SKIPPED, said. -- 5. **A tracked file of a sibling checkout that names it by a path**: -- `../<name>` (and so `../../<name>`, `../../../<name>`), `repos:<dir>`, -- `showell_repos/<dir>` (and so `~/showell_repos/<dir>`). A `.zon` path -- dependency is one of these (`.path = "../<name>"`) and is said as one. -- A `../` chain is left out only on evidence that it means another -- folder: taken from the file's own folder, it lands on a path that is -- there in the file's repo, as a repo's `"../../roc/Walk.roc"` from its -- `src/play/` lands on its own `roc/`. One that lands nowhere counts, -- since a build file also runs from worktrees at other depths. Each sibling is one `git grep`, which reads only tracked files and is -- cheap; a whole-tree `grep_tree` would run out of the store's read -- budget. Change the file to stop naming it (another path, a `-D` -- option), or retire that sibling first. -- 6. **A memory file that names its path** (the `memory:` mount, read -- whole, the forms of 5). Rewrite the note. Off the box there may be no -- such mount: the check is then SKIPPED, said in its line and in the -- verdict, never passed quietly. -- -- A name counts only where it stands alone, so `dog-park` is never found in -- `dog-park-page`, and `../roc.md` is a file, not the folder: -- `folder_names.shale` is that rule's one home. A folder that is not a git -- checkout is BLOCKED as such: nothing in it is in any history. -- -- `self_test=1` plants fake repos made by git in a scratch root, one for -- each reason, and shows each blocks for its own reason alone; a clean one -- and a worktree with its branch pushed come out CLEAR, a sibling named -- with a longer name (`clean-page` beside `clean`), a file name -- (`../clean.md`), a `../` chain into the sibling's own `clean/` and an -- untracked file do not block, and a missing memory folder and link place -- are SKIPPED, said. It checks that every plant is still there after. -- -- budget: steps=300000000 reads=300000 arena_bytes=600000000 programs=3000 use("cookbook:folder_names.shale") const DIR = arg("dir", "") const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", 0) const LINK_DEPTH = 4 const TEXT_WIDTH = 160 function git(dir_os, args) local argv = {"git", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "-C", dir_os} for a in args do push(argv, a) end return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 4000000}) end -- As `git`, stopping the run when git exits nonzero. function git_ok(dir_os, args) local r = git(dir_os, args) if r.code ~= 0 then fail("retire_checkout: `git -C " .. dir_os .. " " .. join(args, " ") .. "` exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. trim(r.out)) end return r end function there(p) return exists(p) end function short(s) local t = trim(s) if #t > TEXT_WIDTH then t = sub(t, 1, TEXT_WIDTH) .. "…" end return t end function plural(n, one, many) if n == 1 then return n .. " " .. one end return n .. " " .. many end -- A store path's OS path, for one whose last part may be a symbolic link, -- which `real` refuses: its folder's OS path and its name. function os_path(p) local d = dirname(p) if d == "" then local colon = find(p, ":") if colon ~= nil then d = sub(p, 1, colon) else d = "." end end return real(d) .. "/" .. basename(p) end -- An absolute OS path with its `.` and `..` parts taken out (the prelude's -- `path_normal` takes store paths only). function os_normal(p) local kept = {} for part in split(p, "/") do if part == ".." then if #kept > 0 then kept = take(kept, #kept - 1) end elseif part ~= "" and part ~= "." then push(kept, part) end end return "/" .. join(kept, "/") end function is_under(p, folder) return p == folder or starts_with(p, folder .. "/") end -- Whether a `../` chain that ends in the name, at `at`, names the folder. -- It counts unless there is evidence it means another folder: a chain that -- starts a word (after a quote, a space, `=`, `(`), taken from the file's -- own folder, lands outside the folder on a path that is there in the -- file's repo, as `"../../roc/Walk.roc"` from a repo's `src/play/` lands on -- its own `roc/`. A chain that lands nowhere still counts, since a build -- file is also run from worktrees at other depths, and so does one after -- anything else (`$ROOT/../roc`), or with no place to take it from (a -- memory note, `place` nil). `place` is {file_dir, repo_os, repo}, the -- file's folder and its repo's top as OS paths, and the repo's store path. function chain_names(text, at, tail_len, target_os, place) if place == nil then return true end local s = at while s > 3 and sub(text, s - 3, s - 1) == "../" do s = s - 3 end local before = "" if s > 1 then before = sub(text, s - 1, s - 1) end if before == "/" or before == "." or before == "$" or before == "}" or before == "-" or is_namey(before) then return true end local landed = os_normal(place.file_dir .. "/" .. sub(text, s, at + 3 + tail_len - 1)) if is_under(landed, target_os) or not starts_with(landed, place.repo_os .. "/") then return true end local a = attempt(there, place.repo .. sub(landed, #place.repo_os + 1, #landed)) return not (a.ok and a.value) end -- Whether a line names the checkout by a path: one of the forms, the name -- standing alone after it and not part of a file name. `place` is where a -- `../` chain is taken from (`chain_names`), nil for a text with none. function names_by_path(text, dir, name, target_os, place) local forms = {{lead = "../", tail = name}, {lead = "repos:", tail = dir}, {lead = "showell_repos/", tail = dir}} for f in forms do local whole = f.lead .. f.tail local at = find(text, whole) while at ~= nil do local tail_at = at + #f.lead if stands_alone(text, tail_at, #f.tail) and not in_file_name(text, tail_at, #f.tail) then if f.lead ~= "../" or chain_names(text, at, #f.tail, target_os, place) then return true end end at = find(text, whole, at + 1) end end return false end function add_reason(v, kind, text) push(v.reasons, {kind = kind, text = kind .. ": " .. text}) end -- 1: uncommitted and untracked changes; stashes, for a main checkout. function check_changes(v, os, is_worktree) local modified = 0 local untracked = 0 local shown = {} for l in lines(git_ok(os, {"-c", "core.quotepath=off", "status", "--porcelain"}).out) do if l ~= "" then if starts_with(l, "??") then untracked = untracked + 1 else modified = modified + 1 end if #shown < 5 then push(shown, sub(l, 4, #l)) end end end local n = modified + untracked if n > 0 then local more = "" if n > #shown then more = " and " .. (n - #shown) .. " more" end add_reason(v, "uncommitted", modified .. " modified, " .. untracked .. " untracked: " .. join(shown, ", ") .. more) end local said = "changes: " .. plural(n, "uncommitted or untracked path", "uncommitted or untracked paths") if is_worktree then push(v.checks, said .. "; stashes are the main checkout's, not checked") return nil end local stashes = {} for l in lines(git_ok(os, {"stash", "list"}).out) do if l ~= "" then push(stashes, l) end end if #stashes > 0 then add_reason(v, "stash", plural(#stashes, "stash", "stashes") .. ", the newest " .. short(stashes[1])) end push(v.checks, said .. ", " .. plural(#stashes, "stash", "stashes")) return nil end -- 2: local branches, and a detached HEAD, with commits on no remote. function check_branches(v, os) local remotes = {} for l in lines(git_ok(os, {"remote"}).out) do if l ~= "" then push(remotes, l) end end local refs = {} for l in lines(git_ok(os, {"for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)", "refs/heads"}).out) do if l ~= "" then push(refs, l) end end local branches = plural(#refs, "local branch", "local branches") if git(os, {"symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD"}).code ~= 0 then push(refs, "HEAD") branches = branches .. " and a detached HEAD" end local unpushed = 0 for ref in refs do local count = parse_int(trim(git_ok(os, {"rev-list", "--count", ref, "--not", "--remotes"}).out)) if count > 0 then local label = ref if starts_with(ref, "refs/heads/") then label = sub(ref, #"refs/heads/" + 1, #ref) else label = "HEAD (detached)" end local where = "on no remote" if #remotes == 0 then where = "on no remote (it has none)" end add_reason(v, "branch", label .. " has " .. plural(count, "commit", "commits") .. " " .. where) unpushed = unpushed + 1 end end push(v.checks, "branches: " .. branches .. ", " .. unpushed .. " with commits on no remote, against " .. plural(#remotes, "remote", "remotes") .. " as the last fetch saw them") return nil end -- 3, for a main checkout: the linked worktrees registered in it. function check_worktrees_of(v, os) local blocks = split(git_ok(os, {"worktree", "list", "--porcelain"}).out, "\n\n") local linked = 0 local i = 2 while i <= #blocks do local path = "" local branch = "detached" local prunable = "" for l in lines(blocks[i]) do if starts_with(l, "worktree ") then path = sub(l, 10, #l) end if starts_with(l, "branch refs/heads/") then branch = "branch " .. sub(l, 19, #l) end if starts_with(l, "prunable") then prunable = ", its folder gone (`git worktree prune`)" end end if path ~= "" then linked = linked + 1 add_reason(v, "worktree", "a linked worktree at " .. path .. " (" .. branch .. ")" .. prunable) end i = i + 1 end push(v.checks, "worktrees: " .. plural(linked, "linked worktree", "linked worktrees") .. " registered") return nil end -- 3, for a linked worktree: its branch, with commits on no remote. function check_worktree_branch(v, os) local common = trim(git_ok(os, {"rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"}).out) local main = common if ends_with(main, "/.git") then main = sub(main, 1, #main - 5) end local branch = trim(git_ok(os, {"branch", "--show-current"}).out) if branch == "" then branch = "HEAD (detached)" end local count = parse_int(trim(git_ok(os, {"rev-list", "--count", "HEAD", "--not", "--remotes"}).out)) if count > 0 then add_reason(v, "worktree", "a worktree of " .. main .. ", its " .. branch .. " with " .. plural(count, "commit", "commits") .. " on no remote") end push(v.checks, "worktree: a linked worktree of " .. main .. " on " .. branch .. ", " .. plural(count, "commit", "commits") .. " on no remote; its main's branches are not this folder's") push(v.notes, "it is a worktree: delete it with `git -C " .. main .. " worktree remove " .. os .. "`, never rm") return nil end -- 4: the symbolic links under the places that resolve into the folder. function check_links(v, os, places, depth) local walked = {} local entries = 0 local link_paths = {} for place in places do local a = attempt(there, place) if not a.ok or not a.value then local why = "not there" if not a.ok then why = a.error end push(v.skipped, "links under " .. place) push(v.checks, "SKIPPED: links under " .. place .. ": " .. why .. "; no link there was looked for") else push(walked, place) for e in walk_all(place, {depth = depth, skip = ".*"}) do entries = entries + 1 if e.kind == "other" then push(link_paths, os_path(e.path)) end end yield() end end local into = 0 if #link_paths > 0 then local argv = {"readlink", "-m", "--", os} for p in link_paths do push(argv, p) end local outs = lines(must(run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 4000000})).out) local target = outs[1] local i = 1 while i <= #link_paths do local link = link_paths[i] local to = outs[i + 1] local inside = starts_with(link, target .. "/") if not inside and (to == target or starts_with(to, target .. "/")) then add_reason(v, "link", link .. " -> " .. to) into = into + 1 end i = i + 1 end end push(v.checks, "links: " .. entries .. " entries under " .. join(walked, ", ") .. ", " .. depth .. " deep, hidden folders passed by; " .. plural(#link_paths, "link", "links") .. ", " .. into .. " into it") return nil end -- 5: each sibling checkout's tracked files that name the folder by a path. function check_names(v, root, os, dir, name) local checked = 0 local named = 0 for e in walk_all(root, {depth = 1, kind = "directory", skip = ".*"}) do if exists(e.path .. "/.git") then local sib_os = real(e.path) if sib_os ~= os then checked = checked + 1 local r = git(sib_os, {"grep", "-n", "-I", "--null", "-F", "-e", "../" .. name, "-e", "repos:" .. dir, "-e", "showell_repos/" .. dir}) if r.code ~= 0 and r.code ~= 1 then fail("retire_checkout: git grep in " .. sib_os .. " exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. trim(r.out)) end for l in lines(r.out) do local parts = split(l, "\0") if #parts >= 3 then local text = join(drop(parts, 2), " ") local place = {file_dir = sib_os .. "/" .. dirname(parts[1]), repo_os = sib_os, repo = e.path} if names_by_path(text, dir, name, os, place) then local what = "" if ends_with(parts[1], ".zon") and contains(text, ".path") then what = " (a .zon path dependency)" end add_reason(v, "named", basename(e.path) .. "/" .. parts[1] .. ":" .. parts[2] .. what .. ": " .. short(text)) named = named + 1 end end end yield() end end end push(v.checks, "names: " .. plural(checked, "sibling checkout's", "sibling checkouts'") .. " tracked files by git grep; " .. plural(named, "line names", "lines name") .. " it by a path") return nil end -- 6: the memory files that name the folder by a path. function check_memory(v, memory, dir, name) local a = attempt(there, memory) if not a.ok or not a.value then local why = "not there" if not a.ok then why = a.error end push(v.skipped, "memory") push(v.checks, "SKIPPED: memory: " .. why .. "; no memory note was read, so none is known not to name it") return nil end local found = grep_tree(memory, name, {}) local named = 0 for h in found.hits do if names_by_path(h.text, dir, name, "", nil) then add_reason(v, "memory", h.path .. ":" .. h.line .. ": " .. short(h.text)) named = named + 1 end end push(v.checks, "memory: " .. plural(found.files, "file", "files") .. " under " .. memory .. "; " .. plural(named, "line names", "lines name") .. " it by a path") return nil end -- The verdict on one folder: {dir, os, reasons, checks, skipped, notes}, -- each reason {kind, text}. `cfg` is {root, places, memory, depth}. function judge(dir_arg, cfg) local dir = dir_arg while ends_with(dir, "/") do dir = sub(dir, 1, #dir - 1) end if dir == "" then fail("retire_checkout: name the folder, `dir=<folder>`, a folder in the root (run from the folder that holds the repos)") end if starts_with(dir, "/") or starts_with(dir, "~") or contains(dir, ":") or contains(dir, "..") then fail("retire_checkout: `dir=" .. dir .. "` must be a folder in the root, by its name (`dir=roc`): run from the folder that holds it") end local path = path_under(cfg.root, dir) if not exists(path) then fail("retire_checkout: there is no folder " .. path) end local os = real(path) local v = {dir = dir, os = os, reasons = {}, checks = {}, skipped = {}, notes = {}} local name = basename(dir) if exists(path .. "/.git/HEAD") then v.kind = "a checkout" check_changes(v, os, false) check_branches(v, os) check_worktrees_of(v, os) elseif exists(path .. "/.git") then v.kind = "a linked worktree" check_changes(v, os, true) check_worktree_branch(v, os) else v.kind = "not a git checkout" add_reason(v, "not-git", "it is not a git checkout, so nothing in it is in any history") end check_links(v, os, cfg.places, cfg.depth) check_names(v, cfg.root, os, dir, name) check_memory(v, cfg.memory, dir, name) return v end function verdict_line(v) if #v.reasons > 0 then return "BLOCKED: " .. v.dir end if #v.skipped > 0 then return "CLEAR: " .. v.dir .. " can be deleted, with " .. plural(#v.skipped, "check", "checks") .. " SKIPPED: " .. join(v.skipped, ", ") end return "CLEAR: " .. v.dir .. " can be deleted" end function print_verdict(v) print("retire_checkout: " .. v.dir .. ", " .. v.os .. " (" .. v.kind .. "); this checks and deletes nothing") for c in v.checks do print(" " .. c) end for n in v.notes do print(" note: " .. n) end print(verdict_line(v)) for r in v.reasons do print(" " .. r.text) end return nil end -- The self-test's plants, under a fresh scratch folder T: `repos/` (the -- root), `origins/` (a bare origin for each repo that has one), -- `elsewhere/` (checkouts outside the root), `links/` (a link place) and -- `memory/`. const USER_BUILD = [=[const named = b.option([]const u8, "named", "") orelse b.pathFromRoot("../../../named"); const page = "../clean-page"; // a longer name: never `clean` const doc = "../clean.md"; // a file name: never `clean` ]=] const USER_ZON = [=[.{ .dependencies = .{ .zoned = .{ .path = "../zoned" }, }, } ]=] const USER_LIST = [=[.{ "../../clean/Walk.roc", // the user repo's own clean/ folder, from src/play/ } ]=] const USER_SCRIPT = [=[## scripts/run.roc -- --repo ../rooted (run from the repo's top) ]=] const USER_DOCS = [=[The spelled checkout lives at `~/showell_repos/spelled`. The script reaches it as `real("repos:spelled")`. ]=] const MEMORY_NOTE = [=[The checkout at `~/showell_repos/remembered` is load-bearing. So is `repos:clean-page`, a longer name. ]=] function plant(T, name, at) local path = T .. "/" .. at .. "/" .. name mkdir(path) local os = real(path) git_ok(os, {"init", "-q", "-b", "main"}) create(path .. "/README.md", "# " .. name .. "\n") git_ok(os, {"add", "-A"}) git_ok(os, {"commit", "-q", "-m", "first"}) return os end function give_origin(T, os, name) local bare = real(T) .. "/origins/" .. name .. ".git" must(run({"git", "clone", "-q", "--bare", os, bare}, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 100000})) git_ok(os, {"remote", "add", "origin", bare}) git_ok(os, {"fetch", "-q", "origin"}) return nil end function commit_file(os, path, file, text) create(path .. "/" .. file, text) git_ok(os, {"add", "-A"}) git_ok(os, {"commit", "-q", "-m", "add " .. file}) return nil end function link(from_os, to_os) must(run({"ln", "-s", to_os, from_os}, {timeout_ms = 10000, whole = 10000})) return nil end function kinds_of(v) local ks = {} for r in v.reasons do push(ks, r.kind) end ks = unique(ks) sort(ks) return join(ks, ",") end function expect(what, got, want) if got ~= want then fail("retire_checkout self_test: " .. what .. " is `" .. tostring(got) .. "`, should be `" .. tostring(want) .. "`") end return nil end function expect_text(what, v, needle) for r in v.reasons do if contains(r.text, needle) then return nil end end print_verdict(v) fail("retire_checkout self_test: " .. what .. ": no reason says `" .. needle .. "`") end function self_test() local T = fresh_dir("scratch:", "retire_checkout_self_test") local R = T .. "/repos" for d in {"repos", "origins", "elsewhere", "links/a/b", "links/c", "memory"} do mkdir(T .. "/" .. d) end local Ros = real(R) local pushed = {"dirty", "untracked", "stashed", "unpushed", "has-wt", "linked", "named", "zoned", "spelled", "rooted", "remembered", "clean", "clean-page"} local os = {} for name in pushed do os[name] = plant(T, name, "repos") if name == "clean" then -- A link inside the folder, into itself, never counts. link(os[name] .. "/self-link", os[name] .. "/README.md") git_ok(os[name], {"add", "-A"}) git_ok(os[name], {"commit", "-q", "-m", "a link"}) end give_origin(T, os[name], name) end -- 1: a modified file; an untracked file; a stash. replace(R .. "/dirty/README.md", "# dirty, changed\n") create(R .. "/untracked/notes.txt", "new\n") replace(R .. "/stashed/README.md", "# stashed, changed\n") git_ok(os["stashed"], {"stash", "-q"}) -- 2: a branch two commits past every remote. git_ok(os["unpushed"], {"checkout", "-q", "-b", "side"}) commit_file(os["unpushed"], R .. "/unpushed", "a.txt", "a\n") commit_file(os["unpushed"], R .. "/unpushed", "b.txt", "b\n") -- 3: a linked worktree of has-wt, outside the root; worktrees of a main -- outside the root, one with its branch a commit past every remote. git_ok(os["has-wt"], {"worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", real(T) .. "/elsewhere/has-wt-side"}) local main_os = plant(T, "wt-main", "elsewhere") give_origin(T, main_os, "wt-main") git_ok(main_os, {"worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "wt-side", Ros .. "/wt-unpushed"}) commit_file(Ros .. "/wt-unpushed", R .. "/wt-unpushed", "c.txt", "c\n") git_ok(main_os, {"worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", Ros .. "/wt-pushed"}) -- 4: a link two folders deep into linked, and one to the longer name. link(real(T) .. "/links/a/b/to-linked", os["linked"] .. "/README.md") link(real(T) .. "/links/c/to-clean-page", os["clean-page"]) -- 5: a sibling whose tracked files name three checkouts, two longer -- names and a file name, and whose untracked file names clean. local user_os = plant(T, "user", "repos") mkdir(R .. "/user/a/b") mkdir(R .. "/user/src/play") mkdir(R .. "/user/scripts") mkdir(R .. "/user/clean") create(R .. "/user/clean/Walk.roc", "module []\n") create(R .. "/user/a/b/build.zig", USER_BUILD) create(R .. "/user/build.zig.zon", USER_ZON) create(R .. "/user/src/play/list.zon", USER_LIST) create(R .. "/user/scripts/run.roc", USER_SCRIPT) create(R .. "/user/docs.md", USER_DOCS) git_ok(user_os, {"add", "-A"}) git_ok(user_os, {"commit", "-q", "-m", "names"}) create(R .. "/user/notes.txt", "see ../clean, untracked\n") -- 6: a memory note. create(T .. "/memory/note.md", MEMORY_NOTE) -- Not git at all. mkdir(R .. "/plain") create(R .. "/plain/notes.txt", "loose\n") local cfg = {root = R, places = {R, T .. "/links"}, memory = T .. "/memory", depth = LINK_DEPTH} local cases = { {dir = "dirty", kinds = "uncommitted", says = "1 modified, 0 untracked: README.md"}, {dir = "untracked", kinds = "uncommitted", says = "0 modified, 1 untracked: notes.txt"}, {dir = "stashed", kinds = "stash", says = "1 stash"}, {dir = "unpushed", kinds = "branch", says = "side has 2 commits on no remote"}, {dir = "has-wt", kinds = "worktree", says = "elsewhere/has-wt-side (detached)"}, {dir = "wt-unpushed", kinds = "worktree", says = "its wt-side with 1 commit on no remote"}, {dir = "wt-pushed", kinds = "", says = ""}, {dir = "linked", kinds = "link", says = "links/a/b/to-linked -> " .. os["linked"] .. "/README.md"}, {dir = "named", kinds = "named", says = "user/a/b/build.zig:1: const named"}, {dir = "zoned", kinds = "named", says = "user/build.zig.zon:3 (a .zon path dependency)"}, {dir = "rooted", kinds = "named", says = "user/scripts/run.roc:1:"}, {dir = "spelled", kinds = "named", says = "user/docs.md:2: The script reaches it"}, {dir = "remembered", kinds = "memory", says = "note.md:1: The checkout at"}, {dir = "plain", kinds = "not-git", says = "not a git checkout"}, {dir = "clean", kinds = "", says = ""}, } local rows = {} for c in cases do local v = judge(c.dir, cfg) if kinds_of(v) ~= c.kinds then print_verdict(v) end expect(c.dir .. "'s reasons", kinds_of(v), c.kinds) if c.says ~= "" then expect_text(c.dir, v, c.says) end push(rows, {case = c.dir, reasons = #v.reasons, verdict = verdict_line(v)}) yield() end local spelled = judge("spelled", cfg) expect("spelled's reasons, `~/showell_repos/` and `repos:`", #spelled.reasons, 2) local wt = judge("wt-pushed", cfg) expect("wt-pushed's note", contains(wt.notes[1], "worktree remove"), true) -- A memory folder and a link place that are not there: SKIPPED, said. local bare_cfg = {root = R, places = {R, T .. "/no-links"}, memory = T .. "/no-memory", depth = LINK_DEPTH} local v = judge("clean", bare_cfg) expect("clean without memory: its reasons", kinds_of(v), "") expect("clean without memory: skipped", join(v.skipped, ","), "links under " .. T .. "/no-links,memory") expect("clean without memory: its verdict", verdict_line(v), "CLEAR: clean can be deleted, with 2 checks SKIPPED: links under " .. T .. "/no-links, memory") push(rows, {case = "clean, no memory", reasons = 0, verdict = verdict_line(v)}) local blocked = judge("remembered", bare_cfg) expect("remembered without memory: its reasons", kinds_of(blocked), "") -- Nothing was deleted. for c in cases do expect(c.dir .. " still there", exists(R .. "/" .. c.dir), true) end print(table(rows, {"case", "reasons", "verdict"})) print("") print_verdict(judge("named", cfg)) remove_tree(T) print("retire_checkout self_test: PASS (" .. #cases .. " cases each blocked for its own reason alone or CLEAR; longer names, a file name and untracked files never block; missing places SKIPPED, said; nothing deleted)") return nil end if SELF_TEST == 1 then self_test() else local cfg = {root = ".", places = {".", "build:", "tools:"}, memory = "memory:", depth = LINK_DEPTH} local v = judge(DIR, cfg) print_verdict(v) if #v.reasons > 0 then fail("retire_checkout: BLOCKED: " .. v.dir .. ", " .. plural(#v.reasons, "reason", "reasons") .. " above") end end

name: cookbook/roc/check_boundaries.shale
html: -- This recipe asks of every function in a tree of .roc files whether its -- boundary earns its keep, and whether each of its parameters is really a -- parameter. It reads each file's syntax tree from Roc's own parser -- (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale), and it checks the functions defined at the -- top level of a file or as members of a module type, not those inside -- another function. A finding is a question for a reader, not a verdict. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_boundaries.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc -- shale cookbook:roc/check_boundaries.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to read, `**/*.roc` by default. Read the whole tree, -- tests too, because a test that reaches a function keeps it -- quiet, and calls are counted only in the files read; -- ways the most ways through a body that `single` still calls a -- wrapper, 2 by default; -- nodes the most syntax-tree nodes in such a body, 24 by default; -- house with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style -- (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code; -- types with `types=1`, Roc's checker gives the types -- (cookbook/roc/types.shale), which `bool_param` needs. It is off -- by default, and needs the tree's `roc-version` file; -- root with `types=1`, the app that imports the files read, or several -- apps separated by commas (`root=a.roc,b.roc`); -- clients globs separated by commas, of files read only for the calls -- they make into the files checked, as apps that import a game. -- Their own functions and `if`s are not checked, even where `glob` -- matches them too; -- tests globs separated by commas, of checked files that are tests of -- the rest, as a tree's gate apps. A reference from one of them to -- a function outside them counts as a test's; -- test_reach `keeps` by default, so an `expect` or a test that reaches a -- function keeps it out of `dead` and `unused_api`. With -- `test_reach=dead`, only a production call or reference keeps a -- module type's member out of `dead`. A file's own top-level -- function is private to it, so its tests may still be all that -- reach it, and a test of a library's API is a user of it. -- -- The checks, most from the Roc style guide (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md): -- -- single A small function with exactly one production call, and no -- `expect`, test file or `##` doc comment that reaches or -- explains it, would read better inline at that call ("A -- function earns its boundary"; the guide calls it a rule of -- thumb). Its body must be one statement of at most `nodes` -- nodes and `ways` ways through: an `if` adds a way, and a -- `match` adds one for each arm past its first. A function -- passed as a value (`map_ok(Uid.to_str)`), a question named -- `is_*` or `has_*`, a recursive function and an entry into -- one (see `entry`) are quiet. -- fixed Every production call, two or more, passes the same -- literal for one parameter, or for one field of a record -- argument. A literal is a number, a string, a character, a -- tag (`Begin`, `Bool.True`) or a module's constant -- (`Limits.max`). "A parameter every caller passes the same -- value is no parameter": drop it, or add an entry function -- that takes only what varies. A recursive function's calls -- to itself must pass the same literal too. The same variable -- or call at every call site (`me`, `req.me`, -- `Host.list_srcs!({})`) is the caller's own value handed on, -- and is not a literal. A library's API keeps its parameters -- whatever this tree's callers pass, so `fixed` skips a -- module type's member in a file under a `lib/` folder, or in -- a module exposed by a `package` or `platform` header in the -- `main.roc` beside it. A file's own top-level functions there -- are checked. -- entry Every production call, two or more, passes the same literal -- for a parameter that the recursive function's own calls -- vary (`at: 0` outside, `at + 1` inside). The recursion -- needs the parameter, so the fix is an entry function that -- takes only what varies and passes the literal itself -- (`count = |xs| count_from(xs, 0)`). That entry function -- makes the one outside call, so it does not fire again. -- constant A function whose one argument is `{}`, by its annotation or -- its lambda's pattern, and whose name has no `!`, gives the -- same value at every call, so it can be a constant -- (`board = ...`, not `board = |{}| ...`). A function with an -- effect needs a `!` in its name. Roc refuses a generic -- constant, so a function whose annotated return type holds a -- type variable (`{} -> Viewer(id)`) is quiet. An unannotated -- function's type is unknown, so it is checked. -- dead A top-level or member function that nothing reaches in the -- files read: no production call, no `expect`, no test file, and -- no reference to it as a value, a record's shorthand -- (`{ helper }`) included. Its calls to itself don't count. A -- top-level function is private to its file, even in a package, -- and a member of a module no package exposes has no caller to -- come. Left alone are the names something else calls: what an -- app's header provides, what a platform requires and provides, -- and a method Roc calls by name (`is_eq`, `to_hash`). -- unused_api The same, for a member of a module its package or platform -- exposes, a member under a `lib/` folder, or a name a `module` -- header exposes. The callers of a public name are mostly -- outside the tree, so this is a question and not a verdict, and -- it has its own count. A member only an `expect` reaches is in -- neither, unless `test_reach=dead`. -- same_branches An `if` whose two branches are the same text, braces aside -- (`if m.over { m } else m`). The condition decides nothing, so -- a rule was lost, or the `if` should go. -- bool_param With `types=1` only: a parameter whose type is `Bool` is -- passed `Bool.True`, `Bool.False`, `True` or `False` by some -- call. "A flag a caller passes is a tag", named for what it -- means (`Loud`, not `Bool.True`). Every call counts, from an -- `expect`, a test file or the function itself too. A -- function with one parameter is quiet, as that parameter is -- the value it converts (`bool : Bool -> JsonOut`), and so is -- a field of a record argument. -- -- A reference to a function is its bare name in the file that defines it, -- `Type.name` anywhere, the type read through the file's `import ... as`, or -- a method call `.name(...)`. The receiver of a method call or of an arrow call (`x->f(a)`) is its first argument. A -- method call counts for every module type with a member of that name, so -- a member whose name another type's member shares is ambiguous, and only -- `constant` checks it. A test file is a file whose name ends in -- `twin.roc`, a file under a `twin/` or `test/` folder, or a spec app, -- named for its module followed by `Spec.roc` (`BlitSpec.roc`). Its -- references count as an `expect`'s do, never as production calls, and -- its own functions are not checked. -- -- Each finding is one line, `path:line: <check>: <why>`, where the line is -- the function's definition, and the findings are followed by a summary -- line of the counts. "` itself, its one outside call") end end end end if func.takes_empty_record_alone and not contains(func.name, "!") and not is_test_file(func.path) then report(func.path, func.line, "constant", "`" .. name .. "` takes `{}` alone and names no effect, so it gives the same value every call: a constant (`" .. func.name .. " = ...`), or a `!` if it has an effect") end if judged and #func.params > 1 and has_key(checker_types.real, func.path) then local every = concatenated({func.prod_calls, func.self_calls, func.test_calls}) for i = 1, #func.params do local param = func.params[i] local ty = kind(param) == "p-ident" and roc_type_at(checker_types, "pat", func.path, NODES[param]) or nil if ty == "Bool" then local literal_calls = {} for c in every do local v = get(argument_texts(c), tostring(i), "") if has_key(BOOL_LITERALS, v) then push(literal_calls, c.path .. ":" .. c.line .. " `" .. v .. "`") end end if #literal_calls > 0 then report(func.path, func.line, "bool_param", "`" .. name .. "`'s parameter " .. i .. ", `" .. raw_text(param) .. "`, is a `Bool` (the checker's type) passed as a literal at " .. #literal_calls .. " of its " .. #every .. " calls (" .. join(take(literal_calls, 3), ", ") .. (#literal_calls > 3 and ", ..." or "") .. "): a flag a caller passes is a tag, named for what it means (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)") end end end end end for g = 1, #NODES do if kind(g) == "e-if-then-else" and not is_test_file(NODE_PATH[g]) and has_key(CHECKED, NODE_PATH[g]) then local kids = children(g) local shown = #kids == 3 and branch_text(NODE_PATH[g], kids[2]) or "?" if shown ~= "?" and shown == branch_text(NODE_PATH[g], kids[3]) then report(NODE_PATH[g], NODES[g].line, "same_branches", "both branches of this `if` are `" .. sub(shown, 1, 40) .. "`: the condition decides nothing") end end end local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. finding_counts[c]) end print("check_boundaries (Roc): " .. #ROC_FILES .. " files" .. CLIENTS_READ .. ", " .. #keys(FUNCTIONS) .. " functions; " .. join(counts, ", ") .. house_note("check_boundaries")) fail_if_refused("check_boundaries", parsed.refused, checker_types.unreached) -- A plant's file name as the self-test reads it. A typed plant is a type -- module, so `typed/BoolParam.roc` reads as `bool_param.roc`, and so does a -- plant under `dead/`, as a package's header names its modules. function plant_check_name(p) if starts_with(p, TYPED_PLANTS) or starts_with(p, DEAD_PLANTS) then return snake_case_plant_name(basename(p)) end return basename(p) end if SELF_TEST then local wrong = {} for c in CHECKS do local planted = 0 for p in ROC_FILES do local base = plant_check_name(p) local planted_here = base == c .. ".roc" or starts_with(base, c .. "_") if planted_here then planted = planted + 1 end local fired_here = has_key(fired, p .. "|" .. c) if planted_here and not fired_here then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. p) end if fired_here and not planted_here then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on " .. p .. ", another check's plant") end end if planted == 0 then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` has no plant") end for p in CLIENT_FILES do if has_key(fired, p .. "|" .. c) then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on the client " .. p .. ", which is read only for its calls") end end end if #CLIENT_FILES == 0 or #keys(TEST_PATHS) == 0 then push(wrong, "no client or no gate plant read") end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("check_boundaries self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end print("check_boundaries (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none)") end

name: cookbook/roc/check_errors.shale
html: -- This recipe checks how Roc code reports failure, against the rules in -- roc-apps docs/roc-style.md ("Errors and failure"). It reads each .roc -- file's parse tree from Roc's own parser, so text in a comment or a string -- never matches. A finding is a question for the reader, not a verdict. -- There are five checks: -- -- error_alias A function's result is a `Try` whose error is an alias of -- tags (`ReadError : [Missing, Failed]`, or a module's -- `Accounts.Unreadable`) instead of the tags written in -- place. A shared alias makes every caller handle tags its -- function can't return. The alias is looked up in the files -- checked, through an alias of an alias.
