An error that is not -- a tag union (a record, a `Str`), an alias in an argument, -- an inferred error (`_`) and a type variable are all fine. -- An error declared outside the files checked can't be -- judged, so the summary line names it. -- optional_tag A tag named like an optional (`Some`, `None`, `Nothing`; -- the full list is cookbook/words/optionals.txt). A value -- that may be absent should be tagged by what it is, and its -- absence by why (`[Latest(Message), NoMessage]`). A type -- that names such a tag beside a tag with a payload is a -- finding at the tag's line. With no payload there, the union -- is a mode with two ways (`[Words, None]`), and `None` is one -- of them. A tag in an expression or a pattern is a finding, -- once per file, only when no type in the files checked names -- it, so read the whole tree. A tag matches by its whole name: -- `NoneChosen` is not `None`. -- set_fallback `List.set(l, i, v) ?? l`, or `l.set(i, v) ?? l`, where the -- fallback is the list being stored into. Naming `l` there -- makes every store copy the list (roc-apps CLAUDE.md, "Six -- shapes copy"). -- placeholder A `??` whose fallback is a string literal with nothing -- interpolated (`?? "bogus"`, `?? ""`). The style guide asks -- for a `crash` with a reason when the lookup can't fail, and -- a tag for the case when it can. -- number_fallback A `??` that falls back to a number after a lookup by -- index, `List.get(l, i) ?? 0.0` or `l.get(i) ?? 0.0`. An index -- past the end is a bug, not a zero. Without types `.get` is -- taken for a `List`'s, so a `Dict`'s may read here; `Dict.get` -- and any other lookup are left alone. -- -- `error_alias` reads only top-level and module-member annotations. The -- `??` checks read every expression. -- -- With `types=1 root=app/main.roc` (or `root=a.roc,b.roc` for several apps) -- the recipe also asks Roc's type checker (cookbook/roc/types.shale). A -- placeholder finding then names the fallback's type and the tags the lookup -- fails with, and `number_fallback` goes by the lookup's type instead of its -- name: any lookup that fails only with `[OutOfBounds]`. A lookup that can -- fail with `KeyNotFound` or `ListWasEmpty` may fall back to a number, since -- zero is often the right answer for a count or a total. A file that no root -- reaches is checked without types, listed after the findings, and fails the -- run. -- -- The recipe prints a summary line of counts, one line per finding -- (`path:line: check: why`), and the summary again. A file that does not -- parse is listed after the findings and fails the run, once every other -- file has been checked. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_errors.shale glob='app/**/*.roc' -- shale cookbook:roc/check_errors.shale self_test=1 -- -- `self_test=1` runs the checks over the plants in cookbook/roc/plants/check_errors/ -- (and its typed/ folder, with the types and root typed/QuietApp.roc). Each -- plant is named for the check it holds, and that check must fire on it and -- on no other check's plant. A `quiet_*.roc` plant must draw no finding, and -- a plant named for no check is a failure. Every `optional_tag` finding must -- point at a line that names its tag. -- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_errors/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const CHECKS = {"error_alias", "optional_tag", "set_fallback", "placeholder", "number_fallback"} use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") use("cookbook:roc/types.shale") const TYPES_ARG = arg("types", "0") if TYPES_ARG ~= "0" and TYPES_ARG ~= "1" then fail("check_errors: types=" .. TYPES_ARG .. " must be 0 (the default) or 1") end -- The self-test checks its typed plants with the types, and the rest without. const USE_TYPES = SELF_TEST or TYPES_ARG == "1" const ROOT = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "typed/QuietApp.roc") or arg("root", "") -- The words listed in cookbook/words/<file>, one per line, with `--` -- starting a note. function read_word_set(file) local words = {} for l in lines(read("cookbook:words/" .. file)) do local w = trim(split(l, "--")[1]) if contains(w, " ") or has_key(words, w) then fail("check_errors: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. w .. "` is not a single word, or is listed twice") end if w ~= "" then words[w] = true end end return words end const OPTIONALS = read_word_set("optionals.txt") const finding_counts = {} for c in CHECKS do finding_counts[c] = 0 end const fired = {} const finding_lines = {} function record_finding(path, line, check, why) push(finding_lines, path .. ":" .. line .. ": " .. check .. ": " .. why) finding_counts[check] = finding_counts[check] + 1 fired[path .. "|" .. check] = true return nil end const paths = glob(GLOB) if SELF_TEST then for q in glob(PLANTS .. "typed/*.roc") do push(paths, q) end end -- The self-test's untyped plants are exempt from being reached by its root. const TYPES = USE_TYPES and roc_types_for_files("check_errors", ROOT, roc_bin("check_errors", SELF_TEST), paths, SELF_TEST and set_of(glob(PLANTS .. "*.roc")) or {}) or {real = {}, pats = {}, exprs = {}, unreached = {}} const PARSED = parse_roc_files(paths) -- Every parsed file's nodes, in one list. Each node's `parent` and `kids` -- are indexes into this list, and a root's `parent` is 0. NODE_PATH holds -- each node's file. const NODES = {} const NODE_PATH = {} for f in PARSED.files do local offset = #NODES for n in f.nodes do local ks = {} for k in n.kids do push(ks, k + offset) end n.kids = ks if n.parent > 0 then n.parent = n.parent + offset end push(NODES, n) push(NODE_PATH, f.path) end end function kids(at) return NODES[at].kids end -- Nodes are in source order, each before its kids, so a subtree runs from -- its root to this node. function last_descendant(at) local i = at while #NODES[i].kids > 0 do i = NODES[i].kids[#NODES[i].kids] end return i end function kind(at) return NODES[at].kind end function node_name(at) return get(NODES[at], "name", "") end function node_raw(at) return get(NODES[at], "raw", "") end -- A node with no line of its own takes the line of the next node that has -- one. function node_line(at) local i = at while i <= #NODES and NODES[i].line == 0 do i = i + 1 end return i <= #NODES and NODES[i].line or "?" end -- Each tag of the tag union at `at`, as a whole node (`Some(U64)`). function union_tag_nodes(at) local out = {} for t in kids(at) do if kind(t) == "tags" then for g in kids(t) do push(out, g) end end end return out end -- The name of a tag node: `Some` for `Some(U64)`. function tag_name(g) if kind(g) == "ty-apply" then return node_name(kids(g)[1]) end return node_name(g) end function union_tag_names(at) local out = {} for g in union_tag_nodes(at) do push(out, tag_name(g)) end return out end -- ── error_alias ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const TOP_LEVEL_KINDS = {file = true, statements = true, ["s-type-decl"] = true, associated = true} -- Whether the annotation at `at` is top-level or a module member: every -- node above it is a file, its statements, a type declaration, or a type's -- associated block. function is_top_level(at) local p = NODES[at].parent while p > 0 do if not has_key(TOP_LEVEL_KINDS, kind(p)) then return false end p = NODES[p].parent end return true end -- The name the type declaration at `at` declares, or "" if `at` is not one. function declared_name(at) local ks = kids(at) if kind(at) ~= "s-type-decl" or #ks < 2 then return "" end return node_name(ks[1]) end -- The type declaration at `at`'s name, qualified by the declarations -- around it (`Stored.Problem`). function nested_name(at) local inner_first = {declared_name(at)} local p = NODES[at].parent while p > 0 do if declared_name(p) ~= "" then push(inner_first, declared_name(p)) end p = NODES[p].parent end local outer_first = {} for k = #inner_first, 1, -1 do push(outer_first, inner_first[k]) end return join(outer_first, ".") end -- Every type declared in the files checked, mapped to the node of what it -- is declared as. DECLARED_QUALIFIED is keyed by the qualified name, and a -- file's top-level types also by the file's module name (`Access.Answer` -- for `Answer` in Access.roc). DECLARED_IN_FILE is keyed by path and bare -- name. const DECLARED_QUALIFIED = {} const DECLARED_IN_FILE = {} for i = 1, #NODES do local name = declared_name(i) if name ~= "" then local definition = kids(i)[2] local qualified = nested_name(i) DECLARED_QUALIFIED[qualified] = definition if qualified == name then local file_name = split(NODE_PATH[i], "/") file_name = file_name[#file_name] DECLARED_QUALIFIED[sub(file_name, 1, #file_name - 4) .. "." .. name] = definition end DECLARED_IN_FILE[NODE_PATH[i] .. "|" .. name] = definition end end const BUILTIN_TYPES = {Str = true, Bool = true, U8 = true, U16 = true, U32 = true, U64 = true, U128 = true, I8 = true, I16 = true, I32 = true, I64 = true, I128 = true, F32 = true, F64 = true, Dec = true, List = true, Dict = true, Set = true, Box = true} -- What the error type named `name` in `path` is: "union" for an alias of -- tags (followed through up to 8 aliases of aliases), "unknown" for a type -- declared outside the files checked, or "other" for anything else (a -- record, a builtin, an empty module type). function error_kind(path, name, hops) if has_key(BUILTIN_TYPES, name) then return "other" end local at = get(DECLARED_IN_FILE, path .. "|" .. name) or get(DECLARED_QUALIFIED, name) if at == nil then return "unknown" end if kind(at) == "ty-tag-union" then return #union_tag_names(at) > 0 and "union" or "other" end if kind(at) == "ty" and node_name(at) ~= "" and hops < 8 then return error_kind(path, node_name(at), hops + 1) end return "other" end -- The error node of a `Try(ok, error)` type at `at`, or 0 for any other node. function try_error_node(at) local ks = kids(at) if kind(at) == "ty-apply" and #ks == 3 and node_name(ks[1]) == "Try" then return ks[3] end return 0 end -- How many times each error declared outside the files checked is named. const unjudged_errors = {} for i = 1, #NODES do if kind(i) == "s-type-anno" and is_top_level(i) then local ks = kids(i) if #ks > 0 and kind(ks[1]) == "ty-fn" then local parts = kids(ks[1]) local result = parts[#parts] for j = result, last_descendant(result) do local err = try_error_node(j) if err > 0 and node_name(err) ~= "" and kind(err) == "ty" then local name = node_name(err) local ek = error_kind(NODE_PATH[i], name, 0) if ek == "union" then record_finding(NODE_PATH[i], node_line(i), "error_alias", "`" .. node_name(i) .. "` fails with `" .. name .. "`, a shared alias of tags: list the tags it can return in place, or leave the error to inference (`_`)") end if ek == "unknown" then unjudged_errors[name] = get(unjudged_errors, name, 0) + 1 end end end end end end -- ── optional_tag ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The optional tags some type names, and the first use of each optional -- tag in an expression or pattern, keyed by path and tag. const optionals_in_types = {} const first_optional_uses = {} -- Each `optional_tag` finding as `{path, line, tag}`, for the self-test. const optional_findings = {} for i = 1, #NODES do local k = kind(i) if k == "ty-tag-union" then local has_payload = false for g in union_tag_nodes(i) do if kind(g) == "ty-apply" then has_payload = true end end for g in union_tag_nodes(i) do local t = tag_name(g) if has_key(OPTIONALS, t) then optionals_in_types[t] = true if has_payload then push(optional_findings, {path = NODE_PATH[i], line = node_line(g), tag = t}) record_finding(NODE_PATH[i], node_line(g), "optional_tag", "`" .. t .. "` names an optional: tag what the value is, and its absence by why (`[Latest(Message), NoMessage]`)") end end end elseif k == "e-tag" or k == "p-tag" then local t = node_raw(i) local key = NODE_PATH[i] .. "|" .. t if has_key(OPTIONALS, t) and not has_key(first_optional_uses, key) then first_optional_uses[key] = {path = NODE_PATH[i], line = node_line(i), tag = t} end end end for key in sort(keys(first_optional_uses)) do local first_use = first_optional_uses[key] if not has_key(optionals_in_types, first_use.tag) then push(optional_findings, first_use) record_finding(first_use.path, first_use.line, "optional_tag", "`" .. first_use.tag .. "` names an optional, and no type in the files read says what it is: tag the value by what it is, and its absence by why") end end -- ── set_fallback and placeholder: what a `??` falls back to ────────────── -- Whether the expressions at `a` and `b` are the same value written twice -- (`board`, `r.b`): the same kinds, names and fields, all the way down. function same_expr(a, b) if kind(a) ~= kind(b) or node_raw(a) ~= node_raw(b) or get(NODES[a], "field", "") ~= get(NODES[b], "field", "") then return false end local ka = kids(a) local kb = kids(b) if #ka ~= #kb then return false end for k = 1, #ka do if not same_expr(ka[k], kb[k]) then return false end end return true end -- The list that the `List.set(l, i, v)` or `l.set(i, v)` call at `at` -- stores into, or 0 for any other expression. function set_target(at) local ks = kids(at) if kind(at) == "e-apply" and #ks == 4 and kind(ks[1]) == "e-ident" and node_raw(ks[1]) == "List.set" then return ks[2] end if kind(at) == "e-method-call" and get(NODES[at], "method", "") == ".set" then for k in ks do if kind(k) == "receiver" and #kids(k) == 1 then return kids(k)[1] end end end return 0 end -- Whether `at` is a string literal with nothing interpolated. function is_literal_str(at) if kind(at) ~= "e-string" then return false end for k in kids(at) do if kind(k) ~= "e-string-part" then return false end end return true end -- Whether `at` is a lookup by index: `List.get(l, i)` or `l.get(i)`. function is_index_lookup(at) local ks = kids(at) if kind(at) == "e-apply" and kind(ks[1]) == "e-ident" then return node_raw(ks[1]) == "List.get" end return kind(at) == "e-method-call" and get(NODES[at], "method", "") == ".get" end function is_number(at) return kind(at) == "e-int" or kind(at) == "e-frac" end for i = 1, #NODES do local ks = kids(i) if kind(i) == "e-binop" and get(NODES[i], "op", "") == "??" and #ks == 2 then local lookup = ks[1] local fallback = ks[2] local path = NODE_PATH[i] local target = set_target(lookup) if target > 0 and same_expr(target, fallback) then record_finding(path, node_line(fallback), "set_fallback", "`List.set(l, i, v) ?? l`: the fallback names `l`, so every store copies; write `?? crash \"...\"` instead (roc-apps CLAUDE.md, \"Six shapes copy\")") end -- With types, the tag union the lookup's `Try` fails with, such as -- `[OutOfBounds]`, or "" when it is unknown. local has_types = USE_TYPES and has_key(TYPES.real, path) local lookup_error = "" if has_types then local lookup_type = roc_type_at(TYPES, "expr", path, NODES[lookup]) local m = lookup_type ~= nil and re_find(lookup_type, "^Try\\((.*), (\\[[^\\[\\]]*\\])\\)$") or nil if m ~= nil then lookup_error = m.groups[2] end end local lookup_said = lookup_error ~= "" and (", for a lookup that fails with `" .. lookup_error .. "`") or "" if is_literal_str(fallback) then local text = "" for k in kids(fallback) do text = text .. node_raw(k) end record_finding(path, node_line(fallback), "placeholder", "falls back to the literal `\"" .. text .. "\"`" .. (has_types and (", a Str" .. lookup_said) or "") .. ": if the lookup can't fail, `crash` with a reason, \"never a silent `?? default`\"; if it can, keep that case as a tag (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md, \"Errors and failure\")") end if is_number(fallback) and (lookup_error == "[OutOfBounds]" or (not has_types and is_index_lookup(lookup))) then local fallback_type = has_types and (", a " .. (roc_type_at(TYPES, "expr", path, NODES[fallback]) or "?")) or "" record_finding(path, node_line(fallback), "number_fallback", "falls back to `" .. node_raw(fallback) .. "`" .. fallback_type .. lookup_said .. ": an index past the end is a bug, not a " .. node_raw(fallback) .. "; `crash` with a reason, or keep the case as a tag (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md, \"Errors and failure\")") end end end local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. finding_counts[c]) end local unjudged = {} for n in sort(keys(unjudged_errors)) do push(unjudged, n .. " (" .. unjudged_errors[n] .. ")") end local unjudged_said = #unjudged > 0 and ("; error_alias not judged, declared outside the files hunted: " .. join(unjudged, ", ")) or "" print_findings("check_errors (Roc): " .. #paths .. " files; " .. join(counts, ", ") .. unjudged_said, finding_lines) fail_if_refused("check_errors", PARSED.refused, TYPES.unreached) -- A plant's name relative to PLANTS. A typed plant's module name is read -- in snake case: `typed/PlaceholderIndex.roc` is `placeholder_index.roc`. function plant_name(path) local name = sub(path, #PLANTS + 1) if starts_with(name, "typed/") then return snake_case_plant_name(sub(name, 7)) end return name end function is_plant_for(name, check) return name == check .. ".roc" or starts_with(name, check .. "_") end if SELF_TEST then local failures = {} for c in CHECKS do local planted = 0 for p in paths do local mine = is_plant_for(plant_name(p), c) if mine then planted = planted + 1 end local did_fire = has_key(fired, p .. "|" .. c) if mine and not did_fire then push(failures, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. p) end if did_fire and not mine then push(failures, "`" .. c .. "` fires on " .. p .. ", another check's plant") end end if planted == 0 then push(failures, "`" .. c .. "` has no plant") end end -- No check would ever fail on a plant named for none of them. for p in paths do local name = plant_name(p) local named = starts_with(name, "quiet_") for c in CHECKS do if is_plant_for(name, c) then named = true end end if not named then push(failures, p .. ": a plant the table does not judge") end end -- Every error a plant names is declared in a plant; otherwise a quiet -- plant could pass without `error_alias` judging it. for n in sort(keys(unjudged_errors)) do push(failures, "`error_alias` cannot judge `" .. n .. "`, declared in no plant") end for f in optional_findings do local source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") if f.line == "?" or not contains(source_lines[f.line], f.tag) then push(failures, "`optional_tag` says " .. f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ", a line that does not name `" .. f.tag .. "`") end end for w in failures do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #failures > 0 then fail("check_errors self_test: " .. #failures .. " plants wrong") end print("check_errors (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none, each optional at its tag's line)") end

name: cookbook/roc/check_families.shale
html: -- This recipe checks that modules which look alike are spelled alike, and -- that one type name means one thing. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_families.shale -- shale cookbook:roc/check_families.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- roles a project's file of type names, one a line, that each module -- may declare for itself, as `Id` in `Message.Id`: read with its -- module it is a two-part name, so `twin_name` leaves it alone; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/check_families/`. -- -- The checks: -- -- family Modules whose names end in the same word form a family when -- there are three or more (`CatSighting`, `TreeSighting`, -- `RailSighting`). A public name that more than half of a -- family's members have is the family's, and each member -- without it is a finding. A member that differs for a good -- reason says so by naming the missing name in the `##` doc -- above its type, or in the file's opening comment. -- twin_name One public type name declared in two modules with different -- shapes, such as `Cat.Pose` and `Geom.Pose`: one word, two -- meanings. It is reported once, at its first declaration, with -- the others listed. Twins of one shape are copies, as when a -- package can't import its platform's type, so they are no -- finding. A shape ignores what a name is qualified by, and the -- order of fields and tags. A namespace module -- (`Collider := [].{ ... }`) builds a type and declares none, and -- so does an alias of the twin (`Pose : Geom.Pose`). App files are -- left out, because every app declares what its platform asks for. -- -- `twin_name` sees only the files read, so give it the whole tree: run by -- folder, it misses twins in two folders. -- -- A module is a file that declares a type named for itself, and its public -- names are that type's members. The output is the counts, one line per -- finding, and the counts again (cookbook/findings.shale). -- The run fails if there are findings, or if any file doesn't parse, and the -- files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const ROLES_FILE = arg("roles", "") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") use("cookbook:roc/headers.shale") const CHECKS = {"family", "twin_name"} const SMALLEST_FAMILY = 3 -- The file's opening comment and the doc above line `line`, as one text. function module_doc_text(path, line) local src = split(read(path), "\n") return join(opening_comment(src), " ") .. " " .. doc_above(src, line) end -- Each module in the files read, as `{name, path, line, members}`, where -- `members` is the set of its type's member names. function modules_of(declared_by_file) local out = {} for one in declared_by_file do local name = module_name(one.path) local module = {name = name, path = one.path, line = 0, members = {}} for d in one.declared do if d.kind == "type" and d.name == name and d.owner == "" then module.line = d.line end if d.kind == "value" and d.owner == name and not has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, d.name) then module.members[d.name] = true end end if module.line ~= 0 and #keys(module.members) > 0 then push(out, module) end end return out end function judge_families(modules, report) local family_of = {} for m in modules do local ws = name_words(m.name) if #ws > 1 then push_at(family_of, ws[#ws], m) end end for word in sort(keys(family_of)) do local members = family_of[word] if #members >= SMALLEST_FAMILY then local holders = {} for m in members do for name in keys(m.members) do incr(holders, name) end end for name in sort(keys(holders)) do if holders[name] * 2 > #members then for m in members do if not has_key(m.members, name) and not contains(module_doc_text(m.path, m.line), "`" .. name .. "`") then push(report, {path = m.path, line = m.line, check = "family", what = "`" .. m.name .. "` has no `" .. name .. "`, which " .. holders[name] .. " of the " .. #members .. " `*" .. word .. "` modules have: spell it alike, or name it in the module's doc to say why not"}) end end end end end end return nil end -- Whether the type `d` declares nothing of its own: a namespace module, or an -- alias of a type of its own name. function is_type_elsewhere(d) return d.shape == "" or d.shape == "[]" or d.shape == d.name end function has_two_shapes(places) for p in drop(places, 1) do if p.shape ~= places[1].shape then return true end end return false end function judge_twins(declared_by_file, roles, report) local places_of = {} for one in declared_by_file do if not one.is_app then local seen = {} for d in one.declared do if d.kind == "type" and not has_key(seen, d.name) and not is_type_elsewhere(d) then seen[d.name] = true push_at(places_of, d.name, d) end end end end for name in sort(keys(places_of)) do local places = places_of[name] if #places > 1 and not has_key(roles, name) and has_two_shapes(places) then local others = {} for p in drop(places, 1) do push(others, p.path .. ":" .. p.line) end push(report, {path = places[1].path, line = places[1].line, check = "twin_name", what = "`" .. name .. "` is also declared at " .. join(others, ", ") .. ", in another shape"}) end end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_families/" check_plants("check_families", "cookbook:roc/check_families.shale", CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "family/*.roc", counts = {family = 1}, says = {"RailSighting.roc:4: family: `RailSighting` has no `in_view`, which 3 of the 4 `*sighting` modules have"}}, {glob = at .. "family_answered/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "family_small/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "family_half/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"Bird.roc:4: twin_name: `Pose` is also declared at", "Cat.roc:4"}}, {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "roles.txt"}}, {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "other_roles.txt"}, counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"`Pose` is also declared at"}}, {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}}, {glob = at .. "twin_app/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "twin_copy/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "twin_namespace/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "twin_namespace_clash/*.roc", counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"`Lamp` is also declared at"}}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}}, }) return nil end function run_check() local paths = glob(GLOB) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local declared_by_file = {} for f in parsed.files do push(declared_by_file, {path = f.path, is_app = is_app(f), declared = declarations_of(f)}) end local report = {} judge_families(modules_of(declared_by_file), report) judge_twins(declared_by_file, ROLES_FILE == "" and {} or word_set(ROLES_FILE), report) local verdict = verdict_of("check_families", CHECKS, report, #paths) print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("check_families", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/check_foreign_code.shale
html: -- This recipe reads another project's Roc code with every check that can matter -- to it. It runs each recipe once over the whole tree, because `check_families` -- and `check_boundaries` judge across folders, and with `house=0`, because our house -- style is no fault in someone else's code. It only parses: it starts no Roc -- compiler and runs nothing from the tree. -- -- cd <their repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_foreign_code.shale -- shale cookbook:roc/check_foreign_code.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments, each optional: -- glob the files to read, `**/*.roc` by default; -- out the folder for each recipe's whole output, `scratch:foreign` -- by default; -- roles for `check_families`, the project's file of type names each module -- declares for itself; -- terms for `find_unclear_names`, its file of fixed terms; -- abbreviations for `find_unclear_names`, its own file of abbreviations; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/check_foreign_code/`. -- -- It prints each recipe's summary, then the findings to read first, and names -- any guide the tree has of its own, whose rules outrank ours. It fails if a -- recipe stops before its summary, or if a file doesn't parse. -- budget: output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const OUT = arg("out", "scratch:foreign") const ROLES = arg("roles", "") const TERMS = arg("terms", "") const ABBREVIATIONS = arg("abbreviations", "") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") const RECIPES = {"check_boundaries", "check_errors", "check_families", "hunt_names", "find_deep_calls", "find_extra_parens", "find_unclear_names", "check_stacking"} const READ_FIRST = {"dead", "same_branches", "number_fallback", "placeholder", "set_fallback", "twin_name", "family", "unused_api"} const GUIDES = {"docs/roc-style.md", "AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md"} const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_foreign_code" function recipe_argv(recipe, glob, more) local argv = {"shale", real("cookbook:roc/" .. recipe .. ".shale"), "glob=" .. glob} for a in more do push(argv, a) end return argv end -- A project's own data, for the recipes that take it, and `house=0` for those -- with house checks. function foreign_args(recipe) local out = {} if has_key(HOUSE_CHECKS, recipe) then push(out, "house=0") end if recipe == "check_families" and ROLES ~= "" then push(out, "roles=" .. ROLES) end if recipe == "find_unclear_names" and TERMS ~= "" then push(out, "terms=" .. TERMS) end if recipe == "find_unclear_names" and ABBREVIATIONS ~= "" then push(out, "abbreviations=" .. ABBREVIATIONS) end return out end function lines_of_check(out, check) local found = {} for l in lines(out) do if contains(l, ": " .. check .. ": ") then push(found, l) end end return found end function sweep() mkdir(OUT) local refused = {} local first = {} for c in READ_FIRST do first[c] = {} end for recipe in RECIPES do local r = run(recipe_argv(recipe, GLOB, foreign_args(recipe)), {timeout_ms = 600000, whole = 16000000, want = "any"}) replace(OUT .. "/" .. recipe .. ".txt", r.out) local summary = last_said(r.out) if not contains(summary, " files") then fail("check_foreign_code: " .. recipe .. " stopped before its summary: " .. trim(r.out)) end print(summary) for l in lines(r.out) do if starts_with(l, "refused: ") then push(refused, l) end end for c in READ_FIRST do for l in lines_of_check(r.out, c) do push(first[c], l) end end end print("") print("Read these first. Every recipe's whole output is in " .. OUT .. "/.") for c in READ_FIRST do for l in first[c] do print(l) end end for guide in GUIDES do if exists(guide) then print("This tree has its own guide, " .. guide .. ": a rule of ours left out above may be one of theirs, and theirs decide.") end end for l in unique(refused) do print(l) end if #refused > 0 then fail("check_foreign_code: roc-ast refused files, named above, which were judged by nothing") end return nil end function faults_of_house_run(recipe, glob) local faults = {} local on = run(recipe_argv(recipe, glob, {}), {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000, want = "any"}) local off = run(recipe_argv(recipe, glob, {"house=0"}), {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000, want = "any"}) for check in HOUSE_CHECKS[recipe] do if #lines_of_check(on.out, check) == 0 then push(faults, recipe .. ": `" .. check .. "` is silent by default") end if #lines_of_check(off.out, check) > 0 then push(faults, recipe .. ": `" .. check .. "` fires under house=0") end end if not contains(last_said(off.out), "left out as house style") then push(faults, recipe .. ": its summary under house=0 doesn't say so") end return faults end function faults_of_sweep() local faults = {} local r = run({"shale", real("cookbook:roc/check_foreign_code.shale"), "out=scratch:foreign_test"}, {cwd = PLANTS, timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000, want = "any"}) if r.code ~= 0 then push(faults, "the sweep exited " .. r.code) end for word in {": dead: `Style.leftover`", ": number_fallback: ", ": unused_api: `Shown.alone`", "its own guide, docs/roc-style.md"} do if not contains(r.out, word) then push(faults, "the sweep doesn't say `" .. word .. "`") end end if contains(r.out, ": paren_if: ") then push(faults, "the sweep prints a house check") end if contains(read("scratch:foreign_test/find_extra_parens.txt"), ": paren_if: ") then push(faults, "the sweep's own output holds a house check") end return faults end -- A platform's stacked `requires` is its own to choose, and an annotation it -- doesn't dictate is not. function faults_of_platform_names() local r = run(recipe_argv("check_stacking", PLANTS .. "/platform/main.roc", {}), {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000, want = "any"}) local bare = lines_of_check(r.out, "stack") if #bare ~= 1 or not contains(bare[1], "main.roc:17:") then return {"check_stacking on the platform plant gives: " .. join(bare, " | ")} end return {} end function faults_of_rewrite_refusal() local faults = {} for recipe in {"check_stacking", "find_extra_parens"} do local r = run(recipe_argv(recipe, PLANTS .. "/Style.roc", {"house=0", "write=1"}), {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000, want = "any"}) if r.code == 0 or not contains(r.out, "refuses house=0") then push(faults, recipe .. " accepts write=1 house=0") end end return faults end function self_test() local faults = {} for recipe in keys(HOUSE_CHECKS) do for f in faults_of_house_run(recipe, PLANTS .. "/*.roc") do push(faults, f) end end for f in faults_of_sweep() do push(faults, f) end for f in faults_of_platform_names() do push(faults, f) end for f in faults_of_rewrite_refusal() do push(faults, f) end for f in faults do print("FAIL " .. f) end if #faults > 0 then fail("check_foreign_code self_test: " .. #faults .. " wrong") end print("check_foreign_code self_test: PASS (each house check fires by default and not under house=0, and the sweep keeps what is real)") return nil end if SELF_TEST then self_test() else sweep() end

name: cookbook/roc/check_name_types.shale
html: -- This recipe finds names that disagree with their types: a number left bare -- beside a typed one, a constant that means "none" but has an ordinary type, -- and, given a project's table, a word whose names must hold one type. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_name_types.shale table=name_types.txt -- shale cookbook:roc/check_name_types.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- table the project's table of words and types, without which -- `name_type` has nothing to judge; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/check_name_types/`. -- -- Each line of the table is `word: Type, Type`, `word: none` or `word: any`, -- such as `dist: Distance`. A blank line or one starting with `#` is skipped, -- and a malformed line or a word listed twice stops the run. The table belongs -- to the project, because what `dist` must be depends on the project's types. -- -- The checks read top-level names, module members and the record fields of -- types and annotations, never locals: -- -- name_type A name whose last word is in the table has a type the -- table doesn't allow. A function is judged by what it -- returns, and a type by its last part, so -- `Geom.Distance` is `Distance`. In a name that starts -- with a preposition or a question, the last word isn't -- the thing named (`from_fraction`, `after_two_steps`, -- `is_fraction`), so it is not judged. `none` means no -- name may end in the word, whatever its type or start, -- and `any` means the word holds no promise at all. -- bare_beside_unit A field that is a bare number in one record and a unit -- in another, a unit being a nominal type built on a -- number and declared in the files read. It means a -- retyping stopped halfway. Each bare field is a finding. -- A field named by a preposition (`from`, `to`, `at`) or -- by a word the table gives `any` (`id`, where a host's -- number and a user's id are two things) is not judged, -- because that word fits any two things. -- no_value A constant whose first word is `no`, `none` or `unset` -- and whose type is not a `Bool` or a tag union. An -- ordinary value kept to mean "none" should be a tag. -- A `List` has its own empty case, and a type's own member -- of that type (`Attention.none : Attention`) is its -- scale's bottom, so neither is judged, and neither is a -- constant with no annotation. A string with something in -- it is words about the case, not a stand-in for it -- (`no_match_words`), so only `""` is judged. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if -- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const TABLE_FILE = arg("table", "") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") const CHECKS = {"name_type", "bare_beside_unit", "no_value"} const BARE_NUMBERS = {U8 = true, U16 = true, U32 = true, U64 = true, U128 = true, I8 = true, I16 = true, I32 = true, I64 = true, I128 = true, F32 = true, F64 = true, Dec = true} const NONE_WORDS = {no = true, none = true, unset = true} const QUESTION_WORDS = {is = true, has = true, can = true, should = true} const PREPOSITIONS = word_set("cookbook:words/prepositions.txt") -- The table as a map from each word to the list of types allowed for it, -- which is empty for `none` and `{"any"}` for `any`. function name_type_table(path) local table_of_words = {} if path == "" then return table_of_words end if not exists(path) then fail("check_name_types: no table " .. path) end local number = 0 for raw in lines(read(path)) do number = number + 1 local l = trim(raw) if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then local m = re_find(l, "^([a-z0-9]+): *(none|any|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:, *[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*)$") if m == nil then fail("check_name_types: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": expected `word: Type, Type`, `word: none` or `word: any`") end if has_key(table_of_words, m.groups[1]) then fail("check_name_types: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": `" .. m.groups[1] .. "` is listed twice") end local allowed = {} if m.groups[2] ~= "none" then for t in split(m.groups[2], ",") do push(allowed, trim(t)) end end table_of_words[m.groups[1]] = allowed end end return table_of_words end function promises_nothing(table_of_words, word) return has_key(table_of_words, word) and has_item(table_of_words[word], "any") end function judge_name_type(d, table_of_words, report) local ws = name_words(sub(d.name, 1, ends_with(d.name, "!") and #d.name - 1 or #d.name)) if #ws == 0 or not has_key(table_of_words, ws[#ws]) then return nil end local allowed = table_of_words[ws[#ws]] if promises_nothing(table_of_words, ws[#ws]) then return nil end local type_name = d.kind == "field" and d.type or d.result if type_name == "" or type_name == "_" then return nil end local names_something_else = has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[1]) or has_key(QUESTION_WORDS, ws[1]) if #allowed == 0 then push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "name_type", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` ends in `" .. ws[#ws] .. "`, which no name here may: its type is `" .. type_name .. "`"}) elseif not names_something_else and not has_item(allowed, last_part(type_name)) then push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "name_type", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` is `" .. type_name .. "`, and a name ending `" .. ws[#ws] .. "` is `" .. join(allowed, "` or `") .. "` here"}) end return nil end -- The nominal types built on a number, by name. function unit_types(all) local units = {} for d in all do if d.kind == "type" and d.is_nominal and has_key(BARE_NUMBERS, d.underlying) then units[d.name] = true end end return units end function judge_bare_fields(all, table_of_words, report) local units = unit_types(all) local unit_of_field = {} for d in all do if d.kind == "field" and has_key(units, last_part(d.type)) then unit_of_field[d.name] = d end end for d in all do if d.kind == "field" and has_key(BARE_NUMBERS, d.type) and has_key(unit_of_field, d.name) and not has_key(PREPOSITIONS, d.name) and not promises_nothing(table_of_words, d.name) then local typed = unit_of_field[d.name] push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "bare_beside_unit", what = "the field `" .. d.name .. "` is a bare `" .. d.type .. "` here and a `" .. typed.type .. "` at " .. typed.path .. ":" .. typed.line}) end end return nil end function judge_no_values(all, report) local tag_types = {} for d in all do if d.kind == "type" and d.is_tags then tag_types[d.name] = true end end for d in all do if d.kind == "value" and d.annotated and not d.fn then local ws = split(d.name, "_") local is_none_word = has_key(NONE_WORDS, ws[1]) local is_plain = d.type ~= "Bool" and not d.has_text and not starts_with(d.type, "[") and not starts_with(d.type, "List(") and d.owner ~= last_part(d.type) and not has_key(tag_types, last_part(d.type)) if is_none_word and is_plain then push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "no_value", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` means none and is a `" .. d.type .. "`: keep the case as a tag"}) end end end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_name_types/" local table_arg = "table=" .. at .. "table.txt" check_plants("check_name_types", "cookbook:roc/check_name_types.shale", CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "name_type.roc", args = {table_arg}, counts = {name_type = 6}, says = {"name_type.roc:3: name_type: `bull_dist` is `Geom.Along`, and a name ending `dist` is `Distance` here", "`in_2_frames` ends in `frames`"}}, {glob = at .. "name_type.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_name_type.roc", args = {table_arg}}, {glob = at .. "bare_beside_unit/*.roc", counts = {bare_beside_unit = 2}, says = {"Rider.roc:4: bare_beside_unit: the field `forward` is a bare `F64` here and a `Distance` at"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_bare/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "bare_any/*.roc", counts = {bare_beside_unit = 1}, says = {"the field `id` is a bare `U64` here"}}, {glob = at .. "bare_any/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_any.txt"}}, {glob = at .. "name_type.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_any.txt"}}, {glob = at .. "no_value.roc", counts = {no_value = 3}, says = {"no_value.roc:3: no_value: `no_frames` means none and is a `Steps`"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_no_value.roc"}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_name_type.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no table"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_name_type.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_malformed.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"table_malformed.txt:2: expected"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_name_type.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_twice.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`dist` is listed twice"}}, }) return nil end function run_check() local table_of_words = name_type_table(TABLE_FILE) local paths = glob(GLOB) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local all = {} for f in parsed.files do for d in declarations_of(f) do push(all, d) end end local report = {} for d in all do if d.kind == "field" or d.kind == "value" then judge_name_type(d, table_of_words, report) end end judge_bare_fields(all, table_of_words, report) judge_no_values(all, report) local verdict = verdict_of("check_name_types", CHECKS, report, #paths) print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("check_name_types", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale
html: -- This recipe finds groups in .roc files laid out against the stacking rule, -- and with `write=1` lays them out by it. A group is a list, record, tuple, -- call's arguments, tag payload or lambda's arguments. A group of three or -- more items and six or more tokens stacks, one item a line. Any other group -- sits on one line while that line fits `width`. The rule and what counts as -- a token are in cookbook/roc/groups.shale. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc write=1 -- shale cookbook:roc/check_stacking.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- skip files the glob finds to leave out, by path, comma-separated, for -- tables of data that read better side by side; -- width the widest a line may be, 100 by default, a tab counting four; -- tokens the tokens from which a group stacks, 6 by default; -- dictated a table of functions whose arguments something outside the file -- dictates, one `path name -- reason` a line, judged as a header's -- names are (below); -- house with `house=0`, leave out every finding here, as the stacking rule -- is our house style (cookbook/roc/house.shale); -- write with `write=1`, rewrite the files (see below). -- -- A group on one line that should stack is a finding, `path:line: stack: ...`, -- left to right. A stacked group that should sit on one line is a finding, -- `path:line: unstack: ...`, at the line it opens on. A line wider than `width` -- with nothing to stack by the rule is a finding too, of one of two kinds. It -- is `wide string` when -- it would fit `width` if the text of each string literal on it counted as -- empty, because Roc has no short way to split a string. Otherwise it is -- `long`. Roc's own parser says which columns are a string's text, so the -- code in an interpolation (`"${...}"`) counts, a comment counts, and so does -- a string in an `import` or the file's header, which has no such node. The -- output is the counts, the findings, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). A file with a line wider than `width` that -- roc-ast refuses keeps that line as `long`, and the run fails, naming it, as -- it does for an app's or platform's file that roc-ast refuses. -- -- A stacked group stays stacked, with no finding, when its joined line would -- be wider than `width`, or when it holds a comment, a `\\` string, a blank -- line, a block's statements, or a group that stays stacked. -- -- Some groups are not findings, or get special advice: -- - A list or tuple whose items are all literals (numbers, plain strings, -- characters, bare tags) is a table's row, like `[0, 0, 0]` or -- `(0.0, 0.0, 1.5)`, and is read at a glance. It is no finding while -- its line fits `width`. A call's arguments are never a row. -- - A group of three or more `Bool`s or Bool literals is told that a flag -- a caller passes should be a tag, as roc-style.md says, whatever its -- tokens. -- - A function's annotation (`name : A, B, C -> R`), or a type alias of a -- function (`Pick(a) : a, a, a -> a`), is read to its first arrow, over -- the lines `roc fmt` wraps it onto, from a type that starts on the line -- after the colon, past a comment on a line of its own, to a blank line. -- When it is a finding for its arguments, at its first line, the -- function's lambda arguments on the line after it are not reported -- again. -- - A field of a record type on one line whose type is a function -- (`{ on_pick : U8, U8, U8 -> U8 }`) is read the same way, its arguments -- counted up to its arrow, unless its file's header dictates it (a -- platform's `requires { step : U8, U8, U8 -> U8 }`). -- - The annotation of a name its file's header dictates is no finding for -- its arguments, as the platform chose them: what an app's header -- provides, and what a platform's header requires and provides -- (cookbook/roc/headers.shale). Nor are that name's lambda arguments. -- - The items of a `where` clause are its method constraints, so -- `k.is_eq : k, k -> Bool` is one item, and a record or list pattern's -- rest (`..`) is no item. -- - The groups of a platform header's `targets:` section are no findings, and -- the rewrite leaves them alone, as `roc fmt` lays that section out by -- itself. A line there wider than `width` is still `long`. -- Strings, characters, `\\` multiline strings and `#` comments are skipped, -- so a comma or bracket inside one is no item. -- -- With `write=1`, the recipe gives each group that should stack a trailing -- comma after its last item, outermost first, takes the trailing comma from -- each group that should unstack, and runs `roc fmt` on the files it changed, -- which stacks a group with a trailing comma and joins a group without one. On -- a long line with no group to stack by the rule, the widest group of two or -- more items gets the comma, as wrap_long_lines.shale does. This repeats until a -- pass changes nothing, so a second run changes nothing either. The recipe then -- prints the findings left, which the rewrite can't reach: long lines, and -- the arguments of a function type, bare (`three : U8, U8, U8 -> U8`) or in -- parentheses (`(U8, U8, U8 -> U8)`), because Roc refuses a trailing comma -- there. -- -- `roc fmt`'s layout changes between Roc nightlies, so `write=1` runs the -- Roc the tree is built with: `tools:roc-<pin>/roc`, the pin read from the -- `roc-version` file in the directory the run starts in, normally the -- repository's root. Without that file it stops before changing anything -- (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale). -- -- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/check_stacking/`. Each -- plant must give a finding of the kind its name starts with (`long`, -- `wide`, `unstack`, or else `stack`), a `long` plant no `wide string` and a -- `wide` plant no `long`, and a `clean*.roc` plant none. A plant line ending -- `# findings N` must give exactly N findings, and with `advice W` after -- it each of them must contain the word W. Then the test copies the plants -- to `scratch:stack/` and rewrites them there with the self-test's Roc: -- the rewrite must end, a second rewrite must change nothing, every file must -- still parse, and a plant with a `.want` file must come out as it. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_stacking" const SCRATCH = "scratch:stack" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const SKIP = arg("skip", "") const DICTATED = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/dictated.txt") or arg("dictated", "") const WIDTH = arg("width", 100) const WRITE = arg("write", "") == "1" -- The files the glob finds, less the ones `skip` names. A name in `skip` that -- the glob doesn't find stops the run, so a renamed file can't go unchecked. function chosen_files() local found = glob(GLOB) if SKIP == "" then return found end local skipped = {} for name in split(SKIP, ",") do skipped[name] = false end local kept = {} for f in found do if has_key(skipped, f) then skipped[f] = true else push(kept, f) end end for name in keys(skipped) do if not skipped[name] then fail("check_stacking: skip names " .. name .. ", which the glob doesn't find") end end return kept end use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/groups.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/headers.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") const TOKENS = arg("tokens", STACK_TOKENS) const MAX_PASSES = 12 const STRING_TEXT = {["e-string-part"] = true, ["p-string-text"] = true} -- Text cut to 60 characters for a finding line. function shortened(s) if #s > 60 then return sub(s, 1, 57) .. "..." end return s end -- The start of a function's annotation (`name :`) or of a type alias -- (`Handler :`, `Pick(a) :`), the type's text after it, which may be empty -- when the type starts on the next line. const ANNOTATION_START = "^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? :(?: (.*))?$" const ALIAS_START = "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\\([^()]*\\))? :(?: (.*))?$" -- The start of an annotation or alias on the line `l`, read with type_line, -- or nil. function annotation_start(l) local m = re_find(l, ANNOTATION_START) if m ~= nil then return m end return re_find(l, ALIAS_START) end -- The type text an annotation's start gives on its own line. function start_text(m) local text = get(m.groups, 1, "") if text == nil then return "" end return text end -- Line `l` without a `#` comment, trimmed. A type has no string, so the -- first `#` starts the comment. function type_line(l) local at = find(l, "#") if at == nil then return trim(l) end return trim(sub(l, 1, at - 1)) end -- If line `i` of `ls` starts a function's annotation (`name : A, B, C -> R`), -- its arguments before the first arrow, counted by the commas outside any -- brackets: `{items, shown, text, name, last}`, where `shown` is `text` -- shortened and `last` the annotation's last line read. A type alias of a -- function (`Handler : U8, U8, U8 -> U8`) counts the same way. `roc fmt` wraps -- a long signature, so the annotation goes on to the next line while its text -- so far is empty (the type starts after the colon's line), a bracket is open -- or its text ends in a comma outside any bracket, until the first arrow -- outside any bracket. A comment on a line of its own is passed over; a blank -- line, or a next line that starts another annotation or field, ends it. nil -- when line `i` annotates no function. function annotation_arguments(ls, i) local m = annotation_start(type_line(ls[i])) if m == nil then return nil end local name = trim(split(trim(ls[i]), " :")[1]) local type_text = "" local depth = 0 local commas = 0 local n = i local piece = start_text(m) while true do local start = #type_text type_text = type_text .. ((start == 0 or piece == "") and "" or " ") .. piece for at = start + 1, #type_text do local c = sub(type_text, at, at) if has_key(OPENERS, c) then depth = depth + 1 end if has_key(CLOSERS, c) then depth = depth - 1 end if depth < 0 then return nil end if depth == 0 and c == "," then commas = commas + 1 end if depth == 0 and (sub(type_text, at, at + 1) == "->" or sub(type_text, at, at + 1) == "=>") then local text = trim(sub(type_text, 1, at - 1)) return {items = commas + 1, shown = shortened(text), text = text, name = name, last = n} end end local goes_on = type_text == "" or depth > 0 or ends_with(type_text, ",") if not goes_on then return nil end -- The next line of code, past any comment on a line of its own. n = n + 1 while n <= #ls and trim(ls[n]) ~= "" and type_line(ls[n]) == "" do n = n + 1 end if n > #ls or trim(ls[n]) == "" then return nil end local next_line = type_line(ls[n]) if depth == 0 and annotation_start(next_line) ~= nil then return nil end piece = next_line end end -- Whether every comma-separated item of `text` is `Bool` or a Bool -- literal, like `Bool, Bool, Bool` or `Bool.true, Bool.false, Bool.true`. const FLAGS = {Bool = true, ["Bool.true"] = true, ["Bool.false"] = true, ["Bool.True"] = true, ["Bool.False"] = true} function are_all_flags(text) for item in split(text, ",") do if not has_key(FLAGS, trim(item)) then return false end end return true end const FLAG_ADVICE = ": a flag a caller passes is a tag, not a Bool (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)" -- The finding for a function type's arguments, which can't take a -- trailing comma. The advice is a record for values that travel together, -- or a tag for a run of flags. function function_type_finding(path, line, items, shown, text) local advice = are_all_flags(text) and FLAG_ADVICE or ": take a record (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md, Name what travels together)" return {path = path, line = line, kind = "stack", what = items .. " bare arguments in " .. shown .. ", which no comma stacks" .. advice} end -- The start of a record type's field, `name : `. const FIELD_START = "^ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* : " -- The function types among the fields of a record type whose inside, between -- its braces, is `inner`, each `{name, items, text}`: a field whose type has an -- arrow outside any bracket, its arguments counted by the commas before it. A -- comma starts the next field only when `name : ` follows it, so the commas -- of a field's function type stay its own. function record_field_functions(inner) local out = {} if re_find(inner, FIELD_START) == nil then return out end local depth = 0 local commas = 0 local type_start = 0 local field_start = 1 local name = "" local done = false local at = 1 while at <= #inner do local c = sub(inner, at, at) if has_key(OPENERS, c) then depth = depth + 1 end if has_key(CLOSERS, c) then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 0 then if type_start == 0 and sub(inner, at, at + 2) == " : " then type_start = at + 3 name = trim(sub(inner, field_start, at - 1)) at = at + 2 elseif c == "," and re_find(sub(inner, at + 1), FIELD_START) ~= nil then commas = 0 type_start = 0 field_start = at + 1 done = false elseif c == "," then commas = commas + 1 elseif not done and type_start > 0 and sub(inner, at - 1, at - 1) == " " and (sub(inner, at, at + 1) == "->" or sub(inner, at, at + 1) == "=>") then push(out, {name = name, items = commas + 1, text = trim(sub(inner, type_start, at - 1))}) done = true end end at = at + 1 end return out end -- Whether any line of the file at `p` is wider than WIDTH. function has_wide_line(p) for l in lines(read(p)) do if line_width(l) > WIDTH then return true end end return false end -- The columns that strings' text takes up in `files`, by Roc's parser, as -- `{columns, refused}`. `columns[path]` maps a line's number, as text, to -- those columns. Only a file with a wide line is parsed, so a tree of short -- lines never needs roc-ast. `refused` is parse_roc_files' list. function string_columns_in(files) local wide_files = {} for p in files do if has_wide_line(p) then push(wide_files, p) end end local columns = {} if #wide_files == 0 then return {columns = columns, refused = {}} end local parsed = parse_roc_files(wide_files) for f in parsed.files do local ls = split(read(f.path), "\n") local by_line = {} for n in f.nodes do if has_key(STRING_TEXT, n.kind) then if n.line ~= n.end_line then fail("check_stacking: " .. f.path .. ":" .. n.line .. ": a run of string text crosses a line") end incr(by_line, "" .. n.line, line_width(sub(ls[n.line], n.col, n.end_col - 1))) end end columns[f.path] = by_line end return {columns = columns, refused = parsed.refused} end -- The finding for line `i` of `p`, wider than WIDTH with nothing else found -- on it. `string_columns` is the columns of strings' text on that file's -- lines, by line number. function wide_line_finding(p, i, l, reachable_line, string_columns) local width = line_width(l) local without_strings = width - get(string_columns, "" .. i, 0) if without_strings <= WIDTH then return {path = p, line = i, kind = "wide string", what = width .. " columns, " .. without_strings .. " without its strings"} end local why = starts_with(trim(l), "#") and "a comment" or (group_to_stack(reachable_line, TOKENS, WIDTH) ~= nil and "a group to stack" or "nothing to stack") return {path = p, line = i, kind = "long", what = width .. " columns, " .. why} end function concat_lists(a, b) local out = {} for x in a do push(out, x) end for x in b do push(out, x) end return out end -- The names the headers of `files` dictate, by path, as `{names, refused}`. -- Only an app's or a platform's file is parsed, so a tree of modules needs no -- roc-ast for this. function dictated_names_in(files) local headed = {} for p in files do local word = header_word(read(p)) if word == "app" or word == "platform" then push(headed, p) end end local names = {} if #headed == 0 then return {names = names, refused = {}} end local parsed = parse_roc_files(headed) for f in parsed.files do names[f.path] = header_names(f.nodes).dictated end return {names = names, refused = parsed.refused} end -- The names the `dictated` table adds to `names`, the result of -- dictated_names_in. Each line of the table is a file's path, a function's -- name, and after ` -- ` who dictates its arguments, such as an API the file -- copies or an edge with no records. The path names the file the glob finds -- with that path or ending `/` and that path, so the self-test's copies in -- scratch are found too. A line whose file the glob doesn't find, whose -- function has no annotation there, or that gives no reason stops the run, so -- the table can't go stale. function with_dictated_table(names, files) if DICTATED == "" then return names end for l in lines(read(DICTATED)) do if trim(l) ~= "" and not starts_with(trim(l), "#") then local m = re_find(l, "^(\\S+) ([a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?) -- \\S") if m == nil then fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " has a line that is not `path name -- reason`: " .. l) end local name = m.groups[2] local path = nil for p in files do if p == m.groups[1] or ends_with(p, "/" .. m.groups[1]) then path = p end end if path == nil then fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " names " .. m.groups[1] .. ", which the glob doesn't find") end local annotated = false for line in lines(read(path)) do if starts_with(trim(line), name .. " :") then annotated = true end end if not annotated then fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " names " .. name .. ", which has no annotation in " .. path) end local here = get(names, path, {}) here[name] = true names[path] = here end end return names end -- Every finding in `files`, as `{found, refused}`: `found` holds each as -- `{path, line, kind, what}`, and `refused` the files roc-ast refused. function findings_in(files) local out = {} local strings = string_columns_in(files) local dictated = dictated_names_in(files) dictated.names = with_dictated_table(dictated.names, files) for p in files do local ls = split(read(p), "\n") local reachable = without_targets_section(ls) local string_columns = get(strings.columns, p, {}) local dictated_here = get(dictated.names, p, {}) -- The function whose annotation ended on the line before and was a -- finding for its arguments, or "". Its lambda's arguments are not -- reported again. local annotated_fn = "" local annotation_end = 0 for i = 1, #ls do local found_on_line = 0 local skip_lambda = annotated_fn ~= "" and i == annotation_end + 1 and starts_with(trim(ls[i]), annotated_fn .. " = |") if i > annotation_end then annotated_fn = "" end local data_line = is_data_line(reachable[i], WIDTH) for g in sort(groups_on_line(reachable[i]), "open") do local inner = sub(ls[i], g.open + 1, g.close - 1) if sub(ls[i], g.open, g.open) == "{" then for field in record_field_functions(inner) do if field.items >= 3 and not has_key(dictated_here, field.name) then push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, field.items, shortened(field.text), field.text)) found_on_line = found_on_line + 1 end end end if g.items >= 3 and g.fn_type then local arguments = split(split(inner, "->")[1], "=>")[1] push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, g.items, shortened(sub(ls[i], g.open, g.close)), arguments)) found_on_line = found_on_line + 1 elseif skip_lambda and sub(ls[i], g.open, g.open) == "|" then skip_lambda = false elseif not data_line then local are_flags = g.items >= 3 and not g.trailing and are_all_flags(inner) if are_flags or should_stack(ls[i], g, TOKENS, WIDTH) then local advice = are_flags and FLAG_ADVICE or "" push(out, {path = p, line = i, kind = "stack", what = g.tokens .. " tokens in " .. shortened(sub(ls[i], g.open, g.close)) .. advice}) found_on_line = found_on_line + 1 end end end -- A line inside a wrapped annotation starts none. local annotation = i > annotation_end and annotation_arguments(ls, i) or nil if annotation ~= nil then annotation_end = annotation.last end if annotation ~= nil and annotation.items >= 3 then annotated_fn = annotation.name if not has_key(dictated_here, annotation.name) then push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, annotation.items, annotation.shown, annotation.text)) found_on_line = found_on_line + 1 end end if found_on_line == 0 and line_width(ls[i]) > WIDTH then push(out, wide_line_finding(p, i, ls[i], reachable[i], string_columns)) end end for g in groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH) do push(out, {path = p, line = g.line, kind = "unstack", what = g.tokens .. " tokens in " .. shortened(trim(group_on_one_line(ls, g)))}) end end return {found = out, refused = unique(concat_lists(strings.refused, dictated.refused))} end -- Runs `roc fmt` on `files`. The result's code is not 0 when a file does -- not parse. function roc_fmt(files) local argv = {roc_bin("check_stacking", SELF_TEST), "fmt"} for p in files do push(argv, real(p)) end return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20}) end -- Rewrites `files` pass after pass until a pass changes nothing, and -- returns how many groups the first pass changed. A pass takes the trailing -- comma from each group that should unstack and gives one to each line's group -- that should stack, and `roc fmt` lays out the result. function rewrite_trailing_commas(files) local first_pass_count = 0 local pass = 1 local changed = 1 local touched = {} while changed > 0 and pass <= MAX_PASSES do changed = 0 touched = {} for p in files do local ls = split(read(p), "\n") local unstacked = groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH) ls = without_trailing_commas(ls, unstacked) local reachable = without_targets_section(ls) local n = #unstacked for i = 1, #ls do if not starts_with(trim(ls[i]), "#") then local g = group_to_stack(reachable[i], TOKENS, WIDTH) if g ~= nil then ls[i] = with_trailing_comma(ls[i], g) n = n + 1 end end end if n > 0 then replace(p, join(ls, "\n")) push(touched, p) changed = changed + n end end print("pass " .. pass .. ": " .. changed .. " groups rewritten, in " .. #touched .. " files") if pass == 1 then first_pass_count = changed end if #touched > 0 then local r = roc_fmt(touched) if r.code ~= 0 then print(r.out) fail("roc fmt failed") end end pass = pass + 1 end if changed > 0 then fail("check_stacking: still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes: " .. join(touched, ", ")) end return first_pass_count end function self_test() local files = chosen_files() local kinds_by_plant = {} local count_by_line = {} local whats_by_line = {} local judged = findings_in(files) fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused) for f in judged.found do local name = sub(f.path, #PLANTS + 2) kinds_by_plant[name] = get(kinds_by_plant, name, " ") .. f.kind .. " " incr(count_by_line, f.path .. ":" .. f.line) push_at(whats_by_line, f.path .. ":" .. f.line, f.what) end local bad = 0 for p in files do local n = 0 for l in lines(read(p)) do n = n + 1 local mark = re_find(l, "# findings ([0-9]+)(?: advice ([a-z]+))?$") if mark ~= nil then local got = get(count_by_line, p .. ":" .. n, 0) local ok = got == tonumber(mark.groups[1]) local word = get(mark.groups, 2, "") if word ~= nil and word ~= "" then for what in get(whats_by_line, p .. ":" .. n, {}) do if not contains(what, word) then ok = false end end end print((ok and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. sub(p, #PLANTS + 2) .. ":" .. n .. ": " .. got .. " findings, want " .. mark.groups[1]) if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end end end end for p in files do local name = sub(p, #PLANTS + 2) local is_long = starts_with(name, "long") local is_wide = starts_with(name, "wide") local want = is_long and "long" or (is_wide and "wide string" or (starts_with(name, "unstack") and "unstack" or "stack")) local got = get(kinds_by_plant, name, "") local clean = starts_with(name, "clean") local ok = (clean and got == "") or (not clean and contains(got, " " .. want .. " ")) if is_long and contains(got, "wide string") then ok = false end if is_wide and contains(got, "long") then ok = false end print((ok and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": " .. (got == "" and "no finding" or got)) if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end end if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " plants wrong") end if is_dir(SCRATCH) then remove_tree(SCRATCH) end mkdir(SCRATCH) local copies = {} for p in files do local to = SCRATCH .. "/" .. sub(p, #PLANTS + 2) replace(to, read(p)) push(copies, to) end rewrite_trailing_commas(copies) local again = rewrite_trailing_commas(copies) if again > 0 then fail("check_stacking: a second rewrite changed " .. again .. " more groups") end local r = roc_fmt(copies) if r.code ~= 0 then print(r.out) fail("check_stacking: a rewritten plant no longer parses") end for want in glob(PLANTS .. "/*.want") do local name = sub(basename(want), 1, #basename(want) - 5) local ok = read(SCRATCH .. "/" .. name .. ".roc") == read(want) print((ok and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ".roc: comes out as its .want") if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end end if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " plants came out wrong") end print("PASS: every plant gives its finding, the clean ones none; the rewrite ends, a second changes nothing, every plant parses and comes out as its .want") end function finding_line(f) return f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.kind .. ": " .. f.what end if SELF_TEST then self_test() elseif WRITE then refuse_house_rewrite("check_stacking") -- Stop before any change if the tree's Roc is missing. roc_bin("check_stacking", SELF_TEST) local files = chosen_files() rewrite_trailing_commas(files) local left = {} local judged = findings_in(files) for f in judged.found do push(left, finding_line(f)) end print_findings(#left .. " left, each a line the rewrite can't reach", left) fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused) else local files = chosen_files() local all = {} local count_by_kind = {} local judged = findings_in(files) for f in judged.found do if not house_leaves_out("check_stacking", f.kind) then push(all, finding_line(f)) incr(count_by_kind, f.kind) end end local counts = get(count_by_kind, "stack", 0) .. " to stack, " .. get(count_by_kind, "unstack", 0) .. " to unstack, " .. get(count_by_kind, "long", 0) .. " long, " .. get(count_by_kind, "wide string", 0) .. " wide string" .. house_note("check_stacking") print_findings(#all .. " findings in " .. #files .. " files: " .. counts, all) fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused) end

name: cookbook/roc/check_vocabulary.shale
html: -- This recipe holds a project to the words it has decided on. The project -- keeps a file of them, and the recipe reports each identifier and comment -- in its .roc files that uses a word the file retires. The word lists belong -- to the project, so none is built in here. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_vocabulary.shale words=vocabulary.txt -- shale cookbook:roc/check_vocabulary.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- words the project's file of decided words, which must be given; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/check_vocabulary/`. -- -- Each line of the words file is `kept: retired, retired`, in lower case, -- such as `lean: tilt`. A blank line or one starting with `#` is skipped. -- The file is matched by whole words, so a plural that should go needs its -- own entry, and a word with a good second meaning can't be listed at all. -- A malformed line stops the run, as does a word retired twice or a word -- both kept and retired. -- -- Identifiers are read from the tree of Roc's own parser and split into words -- at underscores and capitals, so `TiltStep` and `tilt_step` both hold -- `tilt`. They include the names a header or an import exposes, a `where` -- clause's methods and an `as` pattern's name. Comments are read as words too, and the text of a string doesn't -- count. There are two checks, one for each place a word can be: -- -- retired_name an identifier that holds a retired word; -- retired_comment a comment that holds one. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, -- `path:line: retired_name: tilt_step: tilt is lean here`, and the counts -- again (cookbook/findings.shale). Each word is reported once a line for -- each name that holds it. The run fails if there are findings, or if any -- file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const WORDS_FILE = arg("words", "") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") const CHECKS = {"retired_name", "retired_comment"} -- Which attribute holds the identifier in each kind of node that has one. A -- `field` node may hold a field's name under either attribute. A `method` is a -- `where` clause's constraint, and a `p-as` the name an `as` pattern gives. const IDENTIFIER_ATTRIBUTES = { ty = {"name"}, ["ty-var"] = {"raw"}, ["e-ident"] = {"raw"}, ["p-ident"] = {"raw"}, ["e-tag"] = {"raw"}, ["p-tag"] = {"raw"}, ["s-type-anno"] = {"name"}, ["s-import"] = {"raw"}, ["s-var"] = {"name"}, ["anno-record-field"] = {"name"}, ["record-field"] = {"name"}, header = {"name"}, field = {"field", "name"}, segment = {"field"}, ["e-method-call"] = {"method"}, ["p-list-rest"] = {"name"}, method = {"name"}, ["p-as"] = {"name"}, ["exposed-upper-ident"] = {"text"}, } -- The kinds of node whose identifier is the `value` of a `text` node among its -- kids: a lower-case name a header or an import exposes. const TEXT_KID_IDENTIFIERS = {["exposed-lower-ident"] = true} -- The identifiers node `i` of `tree` holds. function identifiers_at(tree, i) local out = {} local node = tree[i] for name_attribute in get(IDENTIFIER_ATTRIBUTES, node.kind, {}) do local name = attribute(tree, i, name_attribute) if name ~= "" then push(out, name) end end if has_key(TEXT_KID_IDENTIFIERS, node.kind) then for k in node.kids do if tree[k].kind == "text" and get(tree[k], "value", "") ~= "" then push(out, tree[k].value) end end end return out end -- The words file as a map from each retired word to the word kept for it. function retired_words(path) if not exists(path) then fail("check_vocabulary: no words file " .. path) end local kept_by_retired = {} local kept_words = {} local number = 0 for raw in lines(read(path)) do number = number + 1 local l = trim(raw) if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then local m = re_find(l, "^([a-z0-9]+): *([a-z0-9]+(?:, *[a-z0-9]+)*)$") if m == nil then fail("check_vocabulary: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": expected `kept: retired, retired`, in lower case") end kept_words[m.groups[1]] = true for retired in split(m.groups[2], ",") do local word = trim(retired) if has_key(kept_by_retired, word) then fail("check_vocabulary: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": `" .. word .. "` is retired twice") end kept_by_retired[word] = m.groups[1] end end end for word in keys(kept_by_retired) do if has_key(kept_words, word) then fail("check_vocabulary: " .. path .. ": `" .. word .. "` is both kept and retired") end end return kept_by_retired end -- The line of node `at`, or of the nearest node around it that has one. function node_line(tree, at) local k = at while k ~= 0 and tree[k].line == 0 do k = tree[k].parent end return k == 0 and 0 or tree[k].line end -- Each retired word in `text`, once, as the words of the names in it. function retired_in(text, kept_by_retired) local found = {} for m in re_find_all(text, "[A-Za-z0-9_]+") do for w in name_words(m.text) do if has_key(kept_by_retired, w) then found[w] = true end end end return sort(keys(found)) end function judge_names(f, kept_by_retired, report) local tree = f.nodes local seen = {} for i = 1, #tree do for name in identifiers_at(tree, i) do for w in retired_in(name, kept_by_retired) do local line = node_line(tree, i) local key = line .. "|" .. name .. "|" .. w if not has_key(seen, key) then seen[key] = true push(report, {path = f.path, line = line, check = "retired_name", what = name .. ": " .. w .. " is " .. kept_by_retired[w] .. " here"}) end end end end return nil end function judge_comments(f, kept_by_retired, report) local number = 0 for l in lines(read(f.path)) do number = number + 1 local comment = comment_on_line(l) if comment ~= nil then for w in retired_in(comment, kept_by_retired) do push(report, {path = f.path, line = number, check = "retired_comment", what = w .. " is " .. kept_by_retired[w] .. " here"}) end end end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_vocabulary/" local words = "words=" .. at .. "words.txt" check_plants("check_vocabulary", "cookbook:roc/check_vocabulary.shale", CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "names.roc", args = {words}, counts = {retired_name = 9}, says = {"names.roc:6: retired_name: tilt_step: tilt is lean here", "RideTour: tour is ride here", "names.roc:12: retired_name: tour_stops", "names.roc:16: retired_name: .tilt"}}, {glob = at .. "names_unseen.roc", args = {words}, counts = {retired_name = 3}, says = {"names_unseen.roc:3: retired_name: tilt_now", "names_unseen.roc:7: retired_name: tilt_of", "names_unseen.roc:12: retired_name: tilt_pair"}}, {glob = at .. "comments.roc", args = {words}, counts = {retired_comment = 3}, says = {"comments.roc:2: retired_comment: tilt is lean here"}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", args = {words}}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", args = {words}, stops = true, counts = {retired_name = 1}, says = {"refused: "}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", stops = true, says = {"give words="}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", args = {"words=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no words file"}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", args = {"words=" .. at .. "words_malformed.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"words_malformed.txt:2: expected"}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", args = {"words=" .. at .. "words_twice.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`tilt` is retired twice"}}, {glob = at .. "clean.roc", args = {"words=" .. at .. "words_both.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`tilt` is both kept and retired"}}, }) return nil end function run_check() if WORDS_FILE == "" then fail("check_vocabulary: give words=<the project's file of decided words>") end local kept_by_retired = retired_words(WORDS_FILE) local paths = glob(GLOB) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local report = {} for f in parsed.files do judge_names(f, kept_by_retired, report) judge_comments(f, kept_by_retired, report) end local verdict = verdict_of("check_vocabulary", CHECKS, report, #paths) print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("check_vocabulary", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/compare_machine_code.shale
html: -- Compare two builds of a Roc archive (or of any object file objdump can -- disassemble) and say whether they hold the same machine code, and if not, -- where they first differ. Roc names each procedure `roc__p` or `roc__proc_` -- followed by hex digits that change whenever the source's layout does, so a pure -- reformat (roc fmt, a new comment, a renamed local) changes the archive's -- bytes without changing its code. This script masks those names before -- comparing the two disassemblies line by line. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/compare_machine_code.shale old=<a.a> new=<b.a> -- -- To get the old archive, build the old commit in a git worktree. The run -- fails on an archive objdump can't disassemble (binutils' objdump doesn't -- read wasm32), because two empty listings would compare as the same. -- -- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 const OLD = arg("old", "") const NEW = arg("new", "") -- The line with each `roc__p<hex>` and `roc__proc_<hex>` written as `roc__pX`. function with_roc_names_masked(line) if not contains(line, "roc__p") then return line end return re_replace(line, "roc__p(roc_)?[0-9a-f]+", "roc__pX") end -- The file's disassembly with Roc's names masked. The lines naming the file -- itself are left out, and the addresses are kept, since the same code is -- laid out at the same addresses. function disassembly(path) local r = run({"objdump", "-dr", "--no-show-raw-insn", path}, {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 64000000}) if r.code ~= 0 then fail("objdump failed on " .. path .. " (code " .. r.code .. "), so it can't be compared: " .. trim(sub(r.out, 1, 200))) end local out = {} local instructions = 0 for l in lines(r.out) do if not contains(l, "file format") and not starts_with(l, "In archive") then local masked = with_roc_names_masked(l) push(out, masked) if like(masked, "*:\t*") then instructions = instructions + 1 end end end if instructions == 0 then fail("objdump read no instructions from " .. path ..
