" (wasm32? binutils can't), so it can't be compared") end return out end if OLD == "" or NEW == "" then fail("compare_machine_code needs old=<archive> new=<archive>") end local old_lines = disassembly(OLD) local new_lines = disassembly(NEW) for i = 1, min(#old_lines, #new_lines) do if old_lines[i] ~= new_lines[i] then print("DIFFERENT at line " .. i .. " of " .. #old_lines .. " and " .. #new_lines .. ":") print(" old: " .. old_lines[i]) print(" new: " .. new_lines[i]) fail("not the same code") end end if #old_lines ~= #new_lines then fail("DIFFERENT: " .. #old_lines .. " lines against " .. #new_lines) end print("SAME: " .. #old_lines .. " lines of disassembly, Roc's hashed names masked")

name: cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale
html: -- This recipe counts a Roc project: for each folder of `in`, its modules and -- lines of Roc, the same for its tests, and its `expect`s, the numbers a -- landing page or a review quotes. A module is a test's when its path holds -- one of `tests`' literals (by default `/gates/`, `/tests/`, `Tests.roc`, -- `Expects.roc` and `_test.roc`); `skip` names more literals whose modules -- are left out (a book's builder inside an app's folder, say). Build output -- (zig-out, .zig-cache and every hidden folder) is never counted. -- -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale in=roc-apps/basic,roc-markdown/package -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale in=roc-apps/canvas_apps/safari skip=/tutorial/ -- -- budget: steps=400000000 reads=50000 arena_bytes=1000000000 const IN = arg("in", ".") const TESTS = arg("tests", "/gates/,/tests/,Tests.roc,Expects.roc,_test.roc") const SKIP = arg("skip", "") function literals(s) local out = {} for x in split(s, ",") do if trim(x) ~= "" then push(out, trim(x)) end end return out end function holds_any(path, lits) for l in lits do if contains(path, l) then return true end end return false end const TEST_LITS = literals(TESTS) const SKIP_LITS = literals(SKIP) local rows = {} for place in literals(IN) do local row = {place = place, modules = 0, lines = 0, test_modules = 0, test_lines = 0, expects = 0} for e in walk_all(place, {kind = "file", skip = ".*", like = "*.roc"}) do if not contains(e.path, "/zig-out/") and not holds_any(e.path, SKIP_LITS) then local text = read(e.path) local n = count_lines(e.path) row.expects = row.expects + #re_lines(text, "^\\s*expect\\b") if holds_any(e.path, TEST_LITS) then row.test_modules = row.test_modules + 1 row.test_lines = row.test_lines + n else row.modules = row.modules + 1 row.lines = row.lines + n end end end push(rows, row) end print(table(rows, {"place", "modules", "lines", "test_modules", "test_lines", "expects"}))

name: cookbook/roc/declared.shale
html: -- A Roc file's parse tree (from `roc_tree`) is a list of nodes, each -- `{kind, parent, kids, line, col, end_line, end_col, depth}` plus attributes -- such as `name` and `raw`, and a node's index is its place in the list. This -- library reads the things the naming recipes share out of that tree: a -- type written as Roc writes it, a name's words, and the list of what a file -- declares. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") -- declarations_of(file) each type, value and record field declared -- render_type(tree, at) the type at node `at`, as text -- name_words(name) a name's words, lowercased -- comment_on_line(l) the text of the comment on line `l` -- last_part(type_name) a dotted type's last part -- module_name(path), is_app(f) a file's module, and whether it is an app -- opening_comment(src) the comment lines that open a file -- word_set(path) a word list, such as one in cookbook/words -- namespace_instructions(file), taken_word_kinds(file), list_name_kinds(file) -- the word lists that hold more than words -- span_text(src, tree, at) a node's source text -- union_shape, argument_shape, mentioned_type_names -- what a type in the tree holds -- previous_sibling, calls_itself -- where a node sits, and what a definition calls -- camel_case(ws), tag_first_word(tag) -- words into a type's name, and a tag's first word -- first_argument, success_type, list_element, element_word -- the parts of a type written as text -- The kinds of node a definition may sit in and still be top-level or a -- module type's member, which `associated` holds. Inside any other kind, -- such as a lambda's block, a definition is local. const OUTER_KINDS = {file = true, statements = true, ["s-type-decl"] = true, associated = true} function children(tree, at) return tree[at].kids end function attribute(tree, at, name) return get(tree[at], name, "") end -- A dotted type's last part. function last_part(type_name) local parts = split(type_name, ".") return parts[#parts] end -- The type at `at`, as Roc writes it: `List(U8)`, `{ id : U8 }`, `[A, B]`, -- `(U8 -> Bool)`. The tree does not say which arrow a function type has, -- so both come out as `->`. With `as_shape`, each name is cut to its last part -- and fields and tags are sorted, so two copies of a type read alike. function render_type(tree, at, as_shape?) local kind = tree[at].kind local kids = children(tree, at) local name = attribute(tree, at, "name") if kind == "ty-apply" then local args = {} for c in drop(kids, 1) do push(args, render_type(tree, c, as_shape)) end return render_type(tree, kids[1], as_shape) .. "(" .. join(args, ", ") .. ")" end if kind == "ty-fn" then local args = {} for c in take(kids, #kids - 1) do push(args, render_type(tree, c, as_shape)) end return "(" .. join(args, ", ") .. " -> " .. render_type(tree, kids[#kids], as_shape) .. ")" end if kind == "ty-record" or kind == "ty-tuple" or kind == "tags" then local parts = {} for c in kids do push(parts, render_type(tree, c, as_shape)) end if as_shape and kind ~= "ty-tuple" then sort(parts) end if kind == "ty-record" then return "{ " .. join(parts, ", ") .. " }" end if kind == "ty-tuple" then return "(" .. join(parts, ", ") .. ")" end return join(parts, ", ") end if kind == "ty-tag-union" then return "[" .. render_type(tree, kids[1], as_shape) .. "]" end if kind == "anno-record-field" then return name .. " : " .. render_type(tree, kids[1], as_shape) end if name ~= "" then return as_shape and last_part(name) or name end -- An inferred type, as in `name : _`. if kind == "_" then return "_" end local raw = attribute(tree, at, "raw") if raw ~= "" then return raw end return "(" .. kind .. ")" end -- A name's words, lowercased: a type's split at its capitals (`NodeInfo` -- gives `node`, `info`), a field's at its underscores. function name_words(name) local out = {} local current = "" for i = 1, #name do local c = sub(name, i, i) if c == "_" then if current ~= "" then push(out, lower(current)) end current = "" elseif c ~= lower(c) and current ~= "" then push(out, lower(current)) current = c else current = current .. c end end if current ~= "" then push(out, lower(current)) end return out end -- The comment lines directly above line `line` of `src`, lowercased and -- joined: a declaration's doc. function doc_above(src, line) local parts = {} local k = line - 1 while k >= 1 and starts_with(trim(src[k]), "#") do push(parts, lower(trim(src[k]))) k = k - 1 end return join(parts, " ") end -- The line of the declaration that the record field at `at` belongs to: -- the nearest top-level or member annotation or type declaration above it, -- as `declaration_line` records it. It is "" when an expression, pattern -- or definition lies between them, since the field is then a local's. function field_declaration_line(tree, declaration_line, at) local k = tree[at].parent while k ~= 0 do local kind = tree[k].kind if starts_with(kind, "e-") or starts_with(kind, "p-") or kind == "s-decl" then return "" end if kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl" then return declaration_line[k] end k = tree[k].parent end return "" end -- The text after the `#` that starts line `l`'s comment, or nil when it has -- none. A `#` inside a string or a character is not a comment, and a line -- of a `\\` multiline string has no comment at all. function comment_on_line(l) if starts_with(trim(l), "\\\\") then return nil end local i = 1 local n = #l while i <= n do local c = sub(l, i, i) if c == "\"" or c == "'" then i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(l, i, i) ~= c do if sub(l, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end elseif c == "#" then return sub(l, i + 1) end i = i + 1 end return nil end -- The module a .roc file holds, by its file name. function module_name(path) local base = basename(path) return sub(base, 1, #base - 4) end -- Whether the parsed file `f` is an app, with an `app` header. function is_app(f) for n in f.nodes do if n.kind == "app" then return true end end return false end -- The comment lines that open a file, from its lines `src`, trimmed. function opening_comment(src) local out = {} local k = 1 while k <= #src and starts_with(trim(src[k]), "#") do push(out, trim(src[k])) k = k + 1 end return out end -- The lines of a word list, with any note after `--` cut off. function word_list_lines(path) local out = {} for l in lines(read(path)) do push(out, trim(split(l, "--")[1])) end return out end -- A list of one word per line, as a set. A word listed twice, or a line of -- two words, fails the run. function word_set(path) if not exists(path) then fail("no word list " .. path) end local set = {} for word in word_list_lines(path) do if contains(word, " ") or has_key(set, word) then fail(path .. ": `" .. word .. "` is no single new word") end if word ~= "" then set[word] = true end end return set end -- cookbook/words/namespaces.txt has a prefix per line followed by the -- namespace's own instructions (`port in out`). The result maps each prefix -- to the set of its instructions: `{port = {["in"] = true, out = true}}`. function namespace_instructions(file) local by_prefix = {} for l in word_list_lines("cookbook:words/" .. file) do local ws = words(l) if #ws > 0 then if has_key(by_prefix, ws[1]) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. ws[1] .. "` twice") end by_prefix[ws[1]] = set_of(drop(ws, 1)) end end return by_prefix end -- cookbook/words/taken.txt has a word per line followed by its kind, `roc` -- or `cardinal`. The result maps each word to its kind: -- `{record = "roc", two = "cardinal"}`. function taken_word_kinds(file) local kinds = {} for l in word_list_lines("cookbook:words/" .. file) do local ws = words(l) if #ws > 0 then if #ws ~= 2 or (ws[2] ~= "roc" and ws[2] ~= "cardinal") or has_key(kinds, ws[1]) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. join(ws, " ") .. "` is no new word with its kind, `roc` or `cardinal`") end kinds[ws[1]] = ws[2] end end return kinds end -- cookbook/words/list_names.txt has a word per line followed by its kind, -- `many`, `one`, `after` or `accumulator`. The result maps each word to its -- kind. function list_name_kinds(file) local kinds = {} for l in word_list_lines("cookbook:words/" .. file) do local ws = words(l) if #ws > 0 then if #ws ~= 2 or (ws[2] ~= "many" and ws[2] ~= "one" and ws[2] ~= "after" and ws[2] ~= "accumulator") or has_key(kinds, ws[1]) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. join(ws, " ") .. "` is no new word with its kind, `many`, `one`, `after` or `accumulator`") end kinds[ws[1]] = ws[2] end end return kinds end -- The name of the type declaration around node `at`, or "" at the top level. function owner_of(tree, at) local k = tree[at].parent while k ~= 0 do if tree[k].kind == "s-type-decl" then return attribute(tree, children(tree, k)[1], "name") end k = tree[k].parent end return "" end -- Whether the node is a string with something in it: `""` spans two columns. function is_text(node) return node.kind == "e-string" and (node.end_line > node.line or node.end_col - node.col > 2) end -- The record for the annotation at `i`, or nil when it is only a `where` -- clause. `type` is its whole type. `has_text` says its definition is a string -- with something in it. A function also has `result`, what it returns, and -- `first`, its first argument's type. function annotated_value(path, tree, i) local kids = children(tree, i) if #kids == 0 or tree[kids[1]].kind == "where" then return nil end local record = {path = path, line = tree[i].line, kind = "value", name = attribute(tree, i, "name"), owner = owner_of(tree, i), annotated = true, fn = false, has_text = false, type = render_type(tree, kids[1])} record.result = record.type if tree[kids[1]].kind == "ty-fn" then local parts = children(tree, kids[1]) record.fn = true record.result = render_type(tree, parts[#parts]) record.first = #parts > 1 and render_type(tree, parts[1]) or "" end return record end -- The record for the type declared at `i`. `underlying` is the type it is -- built on, `shape` the same as `render_type` gives a shape, and `is_nominal` -- says it is declared with `:=` or `::`, not as an alias with `:`. function declared_type(path, src, tree, i) local kids = children(tree, i) local name = attribute(tree, kids[1], "name") if name == "" then return nil end local record = {path = path, line = tree[i].line, kind = "type", name = name, owner = owner_of(tree, i), underlying = "", shape = "", is_nominal = false, is_tags = false} if #kids > 1 and tree[kids[2]].kind ~= "associated" then local between = sub(src[tree[kids[1]].end_line], tree[kids[1]].end_col, tree[kids[1]].end_col + 3) record.is_nominal = contains(between, ":=") or contains(between, "::") record.underlying = render_type(tree, kids[2]) record.shape = render_type(tree, kids[2], true) record.is_tags = tree[kids[2]].kind == "ty-tag-union" end return record end -- Everything the parsed file `f` declares at its top level or as a module -- type's member, in file order. Each record is `{path, line, kind, name, -- owner}`, where `owner` is the type it is a member of, or "" at the top -- level, and `kind` is one of these: -- value an annotation, or a definition with no annotation just above it -- (`annotated` false, and `fn` true when its value is a lambda); -- field a record field in a type or an annotation, with its `type`; -- type a type declaration (see `declared_type`). function declarations_of(f) local tree = f.nodes local src = split(read(f.path), "\n") local out = {} -- Each node is outer when it and every ancestor sit in OUTER_KINDS, and -- its `declaration_line` is its line when it is an outer annotation or -- type declaration, else "". A parent comes before its children. local outer = {} local declaration_line = {} local annotated_names = {} for i = 1, #tree do local node = tree[i] local parent = node.parent push(outer, parent == 0 or (outer[parent] and has_key(OUTER_KINDS, tree[parent].kind))) local kind = node.kind push(declaration_line, (outer[i] and (kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl")) and tostring(node.line) or "") if outer[i] and kind == "s-type-decl" then local record = declared_type(f.path, src, tree, i) if record ~= nil then push(out, record) end end if kind == "anno-record-field" and field_declaration_line(tree, declaration_line, i) ~= "" then push(out, {path = f.path, line = node.line, kind = "field", name = attribute(tree, i, "name"), owner = owner_of(tree, i), type = render_type(tree, children(tree, i)[1])}) end if outer[i] and kind == "s-type-anno" then local record = annotated_value(f.path, tree, i) if record ~= nil then push(out, record) annotated_names[record.owner .. "." .. record.name] = record end end if outer[i] and kind == "s-decl" then local kids = children(tree, i) if #kids > 0 and tree[kids[1]].kind == "p-ident" then local name = attribute(tree, kids[1], "raw") local owner = owner_of(tree, i) if has_key(annotated_names, owner .. "." .. name) then annotated_names[owner .. "." .. name].has_text = #kids > 1 and is_text(tree[kids[2]]) else push(out, {path = f.path, line = node.line, kind = "value", name = name, owner = owner, annotated = false, fn = #kids > 1 and tree[kids[2]].kind == "e-lambda", type = "", result = ""}) end end end end return out end -- The source text of the node at `at`, from the file's lines `src`. A -- node's end column is one past its last character. function span_text(src, tree, at) local node = tree[at] if node.line == 0 then return "" end if node.line == node.end_line then return sub(src[node.line], node.col, node.end_col - 1) end local parts = {sub(src[node.line], node.col)} for l = node.line + 1, node.end_line - 1 do push(parts, src[l]) end push(parts, sub(src[node.end_line], 1, node.end_col - 1)) return join(parts, "\n") end -- The tags of the tag union at `at`, as `{names, payload}`: `names` lists -- the tag names (`Unpinned` for `Unpinned(Str)` too), and `payload` says -- whether any tag carries one. function union_shape(tree, at) local shape = {names = {}, payload = false} for t in children(tree, at) do if tree[t].kind == "tags" then for tag in children(tree, t) do local name = attribute(tree, tag, "name") if tree[tag].kind == "ty-apply" then shape.payload = true name = attribute(tree, children(tree, tag)[1], "name") end if name ~= "" then push(shape.names, name) end end end end return shape end -- An argument's type, as `command_tense` and `mixed_tense` need it: -- `{union}` for a tag union written in place, `{ref}` for a named type -- (its last part: `ChatState.PinEdit` gives `PinEdit`), or `{}`. A -- `List(T)` gives the shape of `T`, with `list` set. function argument_shape(tree, at) local kind = tree[at].kind if kind == "ty-tag-union" then return {union = union_shape(tree, at)} end if kind == "ty-apply" then local kids = children(tree, at) if #kids == 2 and attribute(tree, kids[1], "name") == "List" then local element = argument_shape(tree, kids[2]) element.list = true return element end return {} end local name = attribute(tree, at, "name") if name == "" then return {} end local parts = split(name, ".") return {ref = parts[#parts]} end -- The names of the types the type at `at` mentions, added to the set -- `into`, each by its last part (`Draw.RoundedRectangle` gives -- `RoundedRectangle`). function mentioned_type_names(tree, at, into) local name = attribute(tree, at, "name") if starts_with(tree[at].kind, "ty") and name ~= "" then local parts = split(name, ".") into[parts[#parts]] = true end for c in children(tree, at) do mentioned_type_names(tree, c, into) end return into end -- Whether the definition at `at` mentions `name` in its body, as an -- identifier (`name`, `Tree.name`) or a method call (`x.name(...)`). A -- node's descendants follow it in the tree, each deeper than it. function calls_itself(tree, at, name) local j = at + 1 while j <= #tree and tree[j].depth > tree[at].depth do local node = tree[j] if node.kind == "e-ident" then local raw = attribute(tree, j, "raw") if raw == name or ends_with(raw, "." .. name) then return true end end if node.kind == "e-method-call" and attribute(tree, j, "method") == name then return true end j = j + 1 end return false end -- The sibling just before the node at `at`, or 0. function previous_sibling(tree, at) local parent = tree[at].parent if parent == 0 then return 0 end local previous = 0 for k in tree[parent].kids do if k == at then return previous end previous = k end return 0 end -- Words joined as one type name: `rounded`, `rectangle` gives -- `RoundedRectangle`. function camel_case(ws) local out = "" for w in ws do out = out .. upper(sub(w, 1, 1)) .. sub(w, 2) end return out end -- A tag's first word, lowercased: `Unpinned` gives `unpinned`, `AddedTo` -- gives `added`. function tag_first_word(tag) local word = lower(sub(tag, 1, 1)) local k = 2 while k <= #tag and sub(tag, k, k) == lower(sub(tag, k, k)) do word = word .. sub(tag, k, k) k = k + 1 end return word end -- The first argument in a function type's argument text, `a, b`. function first_argument(args) local depth = 0 for i = 1, #args do local ch = sub(args, i, i) if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then depth = depth + 1 end if ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 0 and ch == "," then return trim(sub(args, 1, i - 1)) end end return trim(args) end -- `Try(Fraction, [OutOfRange])` gives `Fraction`, and any other type itself. function success_type(type_text) local text = trim(type_text) if starts_with(text, "Try(") and ends_with(text, ")") then return first_argument(sub(text, 5, #text - 1)) end return text end -- The element type's text of a `List(...)` or a `Try` of one, else nil. function list_element(type_text) local text = success_type(type_text) if starts_with(text, "List(") and ends_with(text, ")") then return sub(text, 6, #text - 1) end return nil end -- The last word of `element`, a type's text, or "" for one with no name: -- `Shapes.RoundShape(a)` gives `shape`. function element_word(element) local head = re_find(element, "^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+") if head == nil then return "" end local type_words = name_words(last_part(head.text)) return #type_words > 0 and type_words[#type_words] or "" end

name: cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats.shale
html: -- This recipe finds every bare `F64` in a project's declarations, for a project -- that keeps its floats inside unit types. What must stay a float is named in -- the project's table, with a reason. -- -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale table=bare_floats.txt -- shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- table the project's exceptions, without which every `F64` is a finding; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/find_bare_floats/`. -- -- Each line of the table is `Name: reason`. A name is a module, or what is in -- it: `Pixels`, `Scene.fade`, `Animation.Spot.lift`. A type's own module isn't -- repeated, so `to_metres` in `Distance.roc` is `Distance.to_metres`, whether -- or not it is a member of the type `Distance`. A record field's name follows -- what declares it. A line covers its name and whatever is inside it, and only -- the longest line that fits a finding answers for it. A blank line or one -- starting with `#` is skipped, and a line with no reason or a name listed -- twice stops the run. -- -- The checks: -- -- bare_float An `F64` in a top-level or member annotation or in a type -- declaration, however deep in the type: a field, a list's -- element, a tag's payload. Each `F64` is a finding, so a -- signature with two gives two. A local's annotation is the -- body's business and isn't judged. A constant with no -- annotation has no signature, so it can't be judged. -- unused_exception A line of the table that no finding needs, or that names -- a module no file below the table's folder holds. A line -- for a module the run didn't read isn't judged, so a run -- over part of a tree still fails only for what it read. -- -- A helper only tests use is test code and isn't judged, and a line tells it -- so at the top of the output. It is a definition at the top level of a type -- module, outside the type's block, which the compiler lets no other module -- reach, so a file's own text shows everything that uses it. Every use must be -- in an `expect` or in another such helper, and there must be one. The file has -- to be a type module for this: an app's or a `module [...]` file's top-level -- names can be reached from outside, so its helpers are always judged. A local -- that shares a helper's name counts as a use, which can only report more. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if -- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const TABLE_FILE = arg("table", "") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") const CHECKS = {"bare_float", "unused_exception"} -- The table as `{lines, by_name, used}`: its lines in order, each `{name, -- module, line}`, the same by name, and an empty set `judge_float` fills. function exception_table(path) local lines_of_table = {} local by_name = {} if path == "" then return {lines = lines_of_table, by_name = by_name, used = {}} end if not exists(path) then fail("find_bare_floats: no table " .. path) end local number = 0 for raw in lines(read(path)) do number = number + 1 local l = trim(raw) if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then local m = re_find(l, "^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?)*): +[^ ]") if m == nil then fail("find_bare_floats: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": expected `Name: reason`") end if has_key(by_name, m.group) then fail("find_bare_floats: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": `" .. m.group .. "` is listed twice") end local entry = {name = m.group, module = split(m.group, ".")[1], line = number} push(lines_of_table, entry) by_name[m.group] = entry end end return {lines = lines_of_table, by_name = by_name, used = {}} end -- The longest name of the table that covers `key`, or nil. function exception_for(exceptions, key) local parts = split(key, ".") local n = #parts while n >= 1 do local name = join(take(parts, n), ".") if has_key(exceptions.by_name, name) then return name end n = n - 1 end return nil end function is_type_module(tree) for at in children(tree, 1) do if tree[at].kind == "type-mod" then return true end end return false end -- Where the `F64` at `at` is declared, or nil when it belongs to a local. `key` -- is its dotted name, `declaration` the annotation or type declaration holding -- it, `name` that declaration's own name, and `in_type` whether a type's block -- holds it. function declaration_of(tree, at, module) local names = {} local declaration = 0 local in_type = false local k = tree[at].parent while k ~= 0 do local kind = tree[k].kind if starts_with(kind, "e-") or starts_with(kind, "p-") or kind == "s-decl" then return nil end if kind == "anno-record-field" or kind == "s-type-anno" then push(names, attribute(tree, k, "name")) end if kind == "s-type-decl" then local type_name = attribute(tree, children(tree, k)[1], "name") if type_name ~= module then push(names, type_name) end in_type = true end if (kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl") and declaration == 0 then declaration = k end k = tree[k].parent end local parts = {module} local i = #names while i >= 1 do push(parts, names[i]) i = i - 1 end return {key = join(parts, "."), declaration = declaration, in_type = in_type, name = attribute(tree, declaration, "name")} end -- The node's type as text, for a finding: what a reader will find at the line. function declared_type_text(tree, at) local kids = children(tree, at) if tree[at].kind == "s-type-anno" then return render_type(tree, kids[1]) end return render_type(tree, kids[2]) end -- The name a node uses, or "": an identifier, or a field in a record's short -- form, `{ a, b }`, which uses `a` and `b`. function name_used(tree, at) local node = tree[at] if node.kind == "e-ident" then return node.raw end if node.kind == "field" and #node.kids == 0 then return get(node, "field", "") end return "" end -- The definitions at the top level of the file, outside any type's block, as a -- map from each name to its `s-decl`. function top_level_definitions(tree) local found = {} for at in children(tree, 1) do if tree[at].kind == "statements" then for s in children(tree, at) do if tree[s].kind == "s-decl" then local kids = children(tree, s) if #kids > 0 and tree[kids[1]].kind == "p-ident" then found[attribute(tree, kids[1], "raw")] = s end end end end end return found end -- The helpers only tests use, by the rule the header gives: a map from each -- top-level definition to whether it is one. -- Each node's `place` is the helper it sits in, `expect` in a test, and "" for -- anything else. A parent comes before its children, so one pass fills it. function test_only_helpers(tree) local helpers = {} if not is_type_module(tree) then return helpers end local definitions = top_level_definitions(tree) local definition_at = {} for name in keys(definitions) do definition_at[tostring(definitions[name])] = name end local place = {} local places_of = {} for name in keys(definitions) do places_of[name] = {} end for i = 1, #tree do local node = tree[i] local here = node.parent == 0 and "" or place[node.parent] if node.kind == "s-expect" then here = "expect" end if here == "" and has_key(definition_at, tostring(i)) then here = definition_at[tostring(i)] end push(place, here) local used = name_used(tree, i) if used ~= "" and has_key(places_of, used) and here ~= used then places_of[used][here] = true end end for name in keys(definitions) do helpers[name] = #keys(places_of[name]) > 0 end -- A helper falls when anything outside tests uses it, which can bring down -- the helpers only it used. local changed = true while changed do changed = false for name in keys(helpers) do for used_at in keys(places_of[name]) do if helpers[name] and used_at ~= "expect" and not get(helpers, used_at, false) then helpers[name] = false changed = true end end end end return helpers end -- Judges the one `F64` at `at`, and gives 1 when a test's helper holds it. function judge_float(f, at, module, helpers, exceptions, report) local tree = f.nodes local where = declaration_of(tree, at, module) if where == nil then return 0 end if not where.in_type and get(helpers, where.name, false) then return 1 end local covered_by = exception_for(exceptions, where.key) if covered_by ~= nil then exceptions.used[covered_by] = true return 0 end push(report, {path = f.path, line = tree[at].line, check = "bare_float", what = "`" .. where.key .. "` has a bare `F64`: " .. declared_type_text(tree, where.declaration)}) return 0 end -- Judges one file, and gives how many of its floats belong to tests' helpers. function judge_file(f, exceptions, report) local tree = f.nodes local module = module_name(f.path) local helpers = test_only_helpers(tree) local in_helpers = 0 for i = 1, #tree do if tree[i].kind == "ty" and last_part(attribute(tree, i, "name")) == "F64" then in_helpers = in_helpers + judge_float(f, i, module, helpers, exceptions, report) end end return in_helpers end function judge_exceptions(exceptions, read_modules, report) if #exceptions.lines == 0 then return nil end local known = {} for p in glob(path_under(dirname(TABLE_FILE), "**/*.roc")) do known[module_name(p)] = true end for e in exceptions.lines do if not has_key(known, e.module) then push(report, {path = TABLE_FILE, line = e.line, check = "unused_exception", what = "`" .. e.name .. "` names a module no file here holds"}) elseif has_key(read_modules, e.module) and not has_key(exceptions.used, e.name) then push(report, {path = TABLE_FILE, line = e.line, check = "unused_exception", what = "`" .. e.name .. "` excuses nothing: no finding needs it"}) end end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_bare_floats/" local recipe = "cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale" local table_arg = "table=" .. at .. "whole/table.txt" check_plants("find_bare_floats", recipe, CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "Signatures.roc", counts = {bare_float = 12}, says = {"Signatures.roc:5: bare_float: `Signatures.Reading` has a bare `F64`: F64", "`Signatures.scaled` has a bare `F64`: (Reading, F64 -> Reading)", "`Signatures.Trip.length` has a bare `F64`: { length : F64, name : Str }", "`Signatures.pair` has a bare `F64`: (F64, F64)"}}, {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc"}, {glob = at .. "Helpers.roc", counts = {bare_float = 7}, says = {"`Helpers.used_by_a_member` has", "`Helpers.used_by_a_definition` has", "`Helpers.reached_from_production` has", "`Helpers.in_a_short_record` has", "`Helpers.used_by_nothing` has", "`Helpers.only_itself` has", "`Helpers.member_tests_use` has"}}, {glob = at .. "QuietHelpers.roc", says = {"3 bare `F64`s are in helpers only tests use"}}, {glob = at .. "helpers_app.roc", counts = {bare_float = 1}, says = {"`helpers_app.only_tests` has"}}, {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", counts = {bare_float = 7}}, {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {table_arg}}, {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/narrow.txt"}, counts = {bare_float = 2}, says = {"`Held.Spot.left_out` has a bare", "`Held.other` has a bare"}}, {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/shadowed.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 1}, says = {"`Held` excuses nothing"}}, {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/unused.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 4}, says = {"unused.txt:4: unused_exception: `Held.gone` excuses nothing", "`Unit.plus` excuses nothing", "`Held.Spot.gone` excuses nothing", "`Vanished` names a module no file here holds"}}, {glob = at .. "whole/Held.roc", args = {table_arg}}, {glob = at .. "whole/Unit.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/unused.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 2}, says = {"`Unit.plus` excuses nothing", "`Vanished` names a module"}}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}}, {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no table"}}, {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_no_reason.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"table_no_reason.txt:2: expected"}}, {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_twice.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`Quiet.name` is listed twice"}}, }) return nil end function run_check() local exceptions = exception_table(TABLE_FILE) local paths = glob(GLOB) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local report = {} local read_modules = {} local in_helpers = 0 for f in parsed.files do read_modules[module_name(f.path)] = true in_helpers = in_helpers + judge_file(f, exceptions, report) end judge_exceptions(exceptions, read_modules, report) if in_helpers > 0 then print(in_helpers .. " bare `F64`s are in helpers only tests use, and aren't judged") end local verdict = verdict_of("find_bare_floats", CHECKS, report, #paths) print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("find_bare_floats", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls.shale
html: -- This recipe finds calls nested three or more deep, like `f(g(h(x)))`, in -- every .roc file of a tree. Such a call has to be read from the inside -- out. The Roc style guide (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md) asks for code that -- reads left to right instead: a method chain, a pipe, or a named middle -- step. The recipe reads each file's syntax tree from Roc's own parser -- (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale). -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc min=4 -- shale cookbook:roc/find_deep_calls.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- min the least depth to report, 3 by default; -- house with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style -- (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code; -- loose with `loose=1`, a record, list or tuple argument does not reset -- the depth. -- -- A call's depth is one more than the deepest call among its arguments. -- Some things pass their parts' depth through without adding a level: -- whatever reads left to right (a method's receiver in `a.f().g()`, the -- left side of `x |> f` and `x->f()`), a tag or nominal wrapper -- (`Ok(...)`, `ChatPath.(...)`), `?`, parentheses, operators, field or -- tuple access, and a string's interpolation. So `f(g(h(x) + 1))`, -- `f(!g(h(x)))`, `f(g(h(x).a))` and `f("${g(h(x))}")` are each three deep. A lambda argument starts again at zero, since its body -- is read on its own, and so does a record, list or tuple argument, whose -- parts have names or places, unless `loose=1`. -- -- Each finding is the outermost call of one nest: -- path:line:column: nested: depth N, <outermost> to <deepest>: <source line> -- The column tells apart two nests on one line. The outermost and deepest -- calls are named (`List.concat to Str.to_utf8`, or `.concat` for a method) -- so that a nest spread over several lines says more than its first line. -- The output is the count by depth, the findings, and the count again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). Files that don't parse are listed after -- the findings, and then the run fails. -- -- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/find_deep_calls/` at -- `min=3`. A plant line ending `# depth N` must give one finding of depth -- N, and one ending `# depth N, M` a finding for each, left to right; an -- added `from A to B` means the finding must say `A to B`. No unmarked line -- may give a finding, no two findings may print the same line, and a -- `quiet_*.roc` plant may hold no mark. -- budget: steps=100000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_deep_calls/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const LOOSE = arg("loose", "") == "1" const MIN = SELF_TEST and 3 or arg("min", 3) use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") -- The node kinds that pass their parts' depth through. `unary` is `!x` or -- `-x`, `receiver` holds the value whose method is called, and an `e-string` -- holds its interpolations' code. const PASS_THROUGH = {["e-arrow-call"] = true, ["e-question-suffix"] = true, ["e-nominal-apply"] = true, mapper = true, ["e-binop"] = true, unary = true, ["e-field-access"] = true, ["e-tuple-access"] = true, receiver = true, ["e-string"] = true} const LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH = {["e-record"] = true, ["e-list"] = true, ["e-tuple"] = true, field = true} function passes_depth_through(kind, loose) return has_key(PASS_THROUGH, kind) or (loose and has_key(LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH, kind)) end function is_call(node) return node.kind == "e-apply" or node.kind == "e-method-call" end -- Whether a call nested under a node of this kind still belongs to the -- same nest as the call above it. function continues_nest(node, loose) local kind = node.kind return is_call(node) or kind == "args" or kind == "receiver" or kind == "e-tuple" or passes_depth_through(kind, loose) end -- The call depth of node `i`, cached in `memo`, where -1 means not yet -- computed. function call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose) if memo[i] >= 0 then return memo[i] end local node = nodes[i] local kind = node.kind local depth = 0 if kind == "e-apply" then -- The first kid is the function called, the rest its arguments. local deepest_argument = 0 for argument in drop(node.kids, 1) do deepest_argument = max(deepest_argument, call_depth(nodes, memo, argument, loose)) end -- A tag's payload, as in `Ok(...)`, is no call. if nodes[node.kids[1]].kind == "e-tag" then depth = deepest_argument else depth = 1 + deepest_argument end elseif kind == "e-method-call" then local receiver_depth = 0 local deepest_argument = 0 for kid in node.kids do if nodes[kid].kind == "receiver" then receiver_depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, nodes[kid].kids[1], loose) end if nodes[kid].kind == "args" then for argument in nodes[kid].kids do deepest_argument = max(deepest_argument, call_depth(nodes, memo, argument, loose)) end end end depth = max(1 + deepest_argument, receiver_depth) elseif passes_depth_through(kind, loose) or (kind == "e-tuple" and #node.kids == 1) then -- A one-item tuple is a pair of parentheses. for kid in node.kids do depth = max(depth, call_depth(nodes, memo, kid, loose)) end end memo[i] = depth return depth end -- Whether the call at `i` is the outermost of its nest: the first call -- above it, through nodes that continue the nest, is not as deep. function is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, loose) local p = nodes[i].parent while p > 0 do if is_call(nodes[p]) then return call_depth(nodes, memo, p, loose) < call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose) end if not continues_nest(nodes[p], loose) then return true end p = nodes[p].parent end return true end -- A call's name: an apply's function (`List.concat`), or a method call's -- method (`.concat`). function call_name(nodes, i) local node = nodes[i] if node.kind == "e-method-call" then return get(node, "method", "?") end local head = nodes[node.kids[1]] return get(head, "raw", get(head, "name", head.kind)) end -- Whether the call at `j` is inside the nest of the call at `top`: every -- node between them continues the nest. function is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose) local p = nodes[j].parent while p > 0 and p ~= top do if not continues_nest(nodes[p], loose) then return false end p = nodes[p].parent end return p == top end -- The deepest call of the nest under the call at `top`: the first call of -- depth 1 inside it, in source order. function deepest_call(nodes, memo, top, loose) local j = top + 1 while j <= #nodes and nodes[j].depth > nodes[top].depth do if is_call(nodes[j]) and call_depth(nodes, memo, j, loose) == 1 and is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose) then return j end j = j + 1 end return top end const paths = glob(GLOB) local finding_count = 0 local count_by_depth = {} local finding_lines = {} -- For the self-test: each line's findings, `path:line` to a list of -- `{col, depth, text}`, and how many times each finding line printed. const findings_at_line = {} const times_printed = {} local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) for f in parsed.files do local nodes = f.nodes local memo = {} for n in nodes do push(memo, -1) end local source_lines = {} for i = 1, #nodes do if is_call(nodes[i]) and call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) >= MIN and is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) then if #source_lines == 0 then source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") end local line = nodes[i].line local depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) local span = call_name(nodes, i) .. " to " .. call_name(nodes, deepest_call(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE)) local head = f.path .. ":" .. line .. ":" .. nodes[i].col .. ": nested: depth " .. depth .. ", " .. span local finding = head .. ": " .. trim(source_lines[line]) if not house_leaves_out("find_deep_calls", "nested") then push(finding_lines, finding) incr(times_printed, finding) count_by_depth[tostring(depth)] = get(count_by_depth, tostring(depth), 0) + 1 push_at(findings_at_line, f.path .. ":" .. line, {col = nodes[i].col, depth = depth, text = head}) finding_count = finding_count + 1 end end end end local counts = {} for depth in sort(keys(count_by_depth)) do push(counts, "depth " .. depth .. " " .. count_by_depth[depth]) end print_findings("find_deep_calls (Roc): " .. #paths .. " files; nested " .. finding_count .. " (min " .. MIN .. ", " .. (LOOSE and "loose" or "strict") .. ")" .. (#counts > 0 and ("; " .. join(counts, ", ")) or "") .. house_note("find_deep_calls"), finding_lines) fail_if_refused("find_deep_calls", parsed.refused) if SELF_TEST then local wrong = {} local marks = 0 for p in paths do local n = 0 for l in lines(read(p)) do n = n + 1 local mark = re_find(l, "# depth ([0-9]+(?:, [0-9]+)*)(?: from ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+) to ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+))?$") local key = p .. ":" .. n local got = {} local texts = {} if has_key(findings_at_line, key) then for g in sort(findings_at_line[key], "col") do push(got, tostring(g.depth)) push(texts, g.text) end end if mark ~= nil then marks = marks + 1 if starts_with(sub(p, #PLANTS + 1), "quiet_") then push(wrong, key .. ": a quiet plant holds a `# depth` mark") end local want = mark.groups[1] local outermost_name = get(mark.groups, 2, "") if outermost_name ~= nil and outermost_name ~= "" then local says = outermost_name .. " to " .. mark.groups[3] if #texts == 0 or not contains(texts[1], says) then push(wrong, key .. ": the finding does not say `" .. says .. "`") end end if #got == 0 then push(wrong, key .. ": no finding, want depth " .. want) elseif join(got, ", ") ~= want then push(wrong, key .. ": depth " .. join(got, ", ") .. ", want " .. want) end elseif #got > 0 then push(wrong, key .. ": a finding (depth " .. join(got, ", ") .. ") on a line not marked for one") end end end for l in keys(times_printed) do if times_printed[l] > 1 then push(wrong, "two findings print the same line, " .. l) end end if marks == 0 then push(wrong, "no plant holds a `# depth` mark") end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("find_deep_calls self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end print("find_deep_calls (Roc) self_test: PASS (each marked line gives its depths left to right, the outermost only, no other line a finding, and no two findings print alike)") end

name: cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens.shale
html: -- This recipe finds the parentheses and braceless `if`s that a code emitter -- leaves in Roc, and with `write=1` rewrites them. Roc's own formatter keeps -- both, and adds the condition's parentheses itself to an `if` with no braces, -- so neither `roc check` nor `roc fmt` sees them. The recipe reads each file's -- syntax tree from Roc's own parser (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale). -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc write=1 -- shale cookbook:roc/find_extra_parens.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- house with `house=0`, leave out `paren_if` and `lambda_if`, which are -- only our house style (cookbook/roc/house.shale): Luke Boswell's -- roc-style.md asks for `if (x) a else b`; -- write with `write=1`, rewrite the files (see below). -- -- Each finding is one line, `path:line: check: source line`: -- paren_if an `if` written `if (x) a else b`, or with a condition wholly -- in parentheses, or a branch with no braces; -- wrapped_body parentheses around the whole of a lambda's body, a match -- branch's body, a statement or a declaration's multi-line -- value (`|x| (...)`, `Some => (...)`, `y = (\n...\n)`); -- else_block `else { if ... }`, which is `else if ...`; -- lambda_if an `if` that is a lambda's whole body and hangs off its `|` -- (`|x| if x > 1 {`). It starts its own line. An `if` that -- paren_if also finds gets this finding once that one is fixed. -- -- Parentheses around one operand or one argument are left alone: they group, -- and a float's order of operations can rest on them. So is a one-line -- declaration such as `width = (half * 2.0)`, which holds no structure to hide. -- -- The output is the counts, the findings, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). Files that don't parse are listed after the -- findings, and then the run fails. -- -- With `write=1`, the recipe makes each of these edits by the parser's spans, -- runs `roc fmt` on the files it changed, and repeats until a pass changes -- nothing, because taking off one pair can show the next. A comment inside a -- bracket stays, so it can leave a line a reader tidies. It runs the Roc the -- tree is built with (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale), from the repository's root. -- -- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/find_extra_parens/`. A plant -- line ending `# paren_if`, `# wrapped_body`, `# else_block` or `# lambda_if` -- must give that finding, and no unmarked line may give one. Then the test copies the plants -- to `scratch:parens/` and rewrites them there: every file must still parse, no -- finding may be left, a second rewrite must change nothing, and a plant with a -- `.want` file must come out as it. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_extra_parens" const SCRATCH = "scratch:parens" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const WRITE = arg("write", "") == "1" const CHECKS = {"paren_if", "wrapped_body", "else_block", "lambda_if"} use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") -- A one-item tuple is a pair of parentheses. function is_parens(node) return node.kind == "e-tuple" and #node.kids == 1 end function is_last_kid(nodes, i) local kids = nodes[nodes[i].parent].kids return kids[#kids] == i end -- Whether parentheses at `i` wrap a whole body. The value of a declaration -- counts only over several lines; a statement counts wherever it stands, and -- `if`'s branches are paren_if's and the block's own. function wraps_body(nodes, i) local node = nodes[i] if not is_parens(node) or node.parent == 0 then return false end local kind = nodes[node.parent].kind if kind == "statements" then return true end if kind == "e-lambda" or kind == "branch" then return is_last_kid(nodes, i) end if kind == "s-decl" then return is_last_kid(nodes, i) and node.end_line > node.line end return false end function has_braces(node) return node.kind == "e-block" end function is_paren_if(nodes, i) local node = nodes[i] if node.kind ~= "e-if-then-else" then return false end local kids = node.kids local otherwise = nodes[kids[3]] return is_parens(nodes[kids[1]]) or not has_braces(nodes[kids[2]]) or not (has_braces(otherwise) or otherwise.kind == "e-if-then-else") end -- The `if` that is the whole of a block, or 0: the block's one statement. function only_if_in(nodes, block) local statements = nodes[nodes[block].kids[1]] if #statements.kids ~= 1 then return 0 end local only = statements.kids[1] if nodes[only].kind == "e-if-then-else" then return only end return 0 end function is_else_block(nodes, i) local node = nodes[i] if node.kind ~= "e-if-then-else" then return false end local otherwise = node.kids[3] return has_braces(nodes[otherwise]) and only_if_in(nodes, otherwise) ~= 0 end -- Whether the node at `i` is an `if` that is a lambda's whole body and shares -- its line with what comes before it, which can only be the lambda's `|`. function is_lambda_if(nodes, i, source) local node = nodes[i] if node.kind ~= "e-if-then-else" or node.parent == 0 then return false end if nodes[node.parent].kind ~= "e-lambda" or not is_last_kid(nodes, i) then return false end if is_paren_if(nodes, i) then return false end return trim(sub(source[node.line], 1, node.col - 1)) ~= "" end -- Each file's findings: `{check, line}`, with the node they stand on. function findings_in(file) local found = {} local source = split(read(file.path), "\n") local i = 1 while i <= #file.nodes do local node = file.nodes[i] if wraps_body(file.nodes, i) then push(found, {check = "wrapped_body", line = node.line, at = i}) end if is_paren_if(file.nodes, i) then push(found, {check = "paren_if", line = node.line, at = i}) end if is_else_block(file.nodes, i) then push(found, {check = "else_block", line = node.line, at = i}) end if is_lambda_if(file.nodes, i, source) then push(found, {check = "lambda_if", line = node.line, at = i}) end i = i + 1 end return found end -- Where each line starts in `text`, as an index into it. function line_starts(text) local starts = {1} for at in find_all(text, "\n") do push(starts, at + 1) end return starts end function offset_of(starts, line, col) return starts[line] + col - 1 end function is_space(text, at) local c = sub(text, at, at) return c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\n" end -- The first index past `at` that isn't white space. function past_space(text, at) local i = at while is_space(text, i) do i = i + 1 end return i end -- The last index before `at` that isn't white space, plus one. function before_space(text, at) local i = at while is_space(text, i - 1) do i = i - 1 end return i end -- Where the line holding the index just before `at` starts. function last_line_start(text, at) local i = at - 1 while i > 1 and sub(text, i - 1, i - 1) ~= "\n" do i = i - 1 end return i end -- The edits that take off the brackets at the ends of `node`: the space inside -- them goes too, so nothing is left of a line that held a bracket alone. With -- `keep_break`, the line break after the opening bracket stays, as a body on -- its own line wants. A comment beside a bracket keeps its line. function push_bracket_removal(edits, text, starts, node, keep_break) local opening = offset_of(starts, node.line, node.col) local closing = offset_of(starts, node.end_line, node.end_col) - 1 local cut_to = past_space(text, opening + 1) if keep_break or sub(text, cut_to, cut_to) == "#" then cut_to = opening + 1 end push(edits, {at = opening, cut = cut_to - opening, put = ""}) local cut_from = before_space(text, closing) local last_line_from = last_line_start(text, cut_from) if contains(sub(text, last_line_from, cut_from - 1), "#") then cut_from = closing end push(edits, {at = cut_from, cut = closing + 1 - cut_from, put = ""}) end -- The first index at or past `at` outside white space and comments. function past_comments(text, at) local i = past_space(text, at) while sub(text, i, i) == "#" do while i <= #text and sub(text, i, i) ~= "\n" do i = i + 1 end i = past_space(text, i) end return i end function fail_no_span(src, node) fail("find_extra_parens: " .. src.path .. ": can't find the ends of a " .. node.kind .. ", which the tree gives no span") end -- Roc's tree gives a `match` and a unary operator no span of their own, so an -- edit finds their ends from the nodes they hold. Any other kind with no span -- stops the run: a guess here would write braces into the wrong place. function start_of(src, i) local node = src.nodes[i] if node.line ~= 0 then return offset_of(src.starts, node.line, node.col) end if node.kind ~= "unary" and node.kind ~= "e-match" then fail_no_span(src, node) end local before = before_space(src.text, start_of(src, node.kids[1])) if node.kind == "unary" then return before - 1 end if sub(src.text, before - 5, before - 1) ~= "match" then fail_no_span(src, node) end return before - 5 end -- The index just past the node at `i`. function end_of(src, i) local node = src.nodes[i] if node.line ~= 0 then return offset_of(src.starts, node.end_line, node.end_col) end if node.kind == "unary" then return end_of(src, node.kids[1]) end if node.kind ~= "e-match" then fail_no_span(src, node) end local branches = src.nodes[node.kids[2]].kids local closing = past_comments(src.text, end_of(src, branches[#branches])) if sub(src.text, closing, closing) ~= "}" then fail_no_span(src, node) end return closing + 1 end -- The opening brace of the branch at `i`, on the line of what stands before it, -- which ends at `after`, since `roc fmt` keeps a line break before a brace. A -- comment there keeps its place after the brace. function push_opening_brace(edits, src, i, after) local from = start_of(src, i) if contains(sub(src.text, after, from - 1), "#") then push(edits, {at = after, cut = 0, put = " {"}) else push(edits, {at = after, cut = from - after, put = " { "}) end end -- The index just past the `else` that follows `then_end`. function past_else(src, then_end) local at = past_comments(src.text, then_end) if sub(src.text, at, at + 3) ~= "else" then fail("find_extra_parens: " .. src.path .. ": no `else` where a branch ended") end return at + 4 end -- The closing brace of a `then` branch, with `else` brought up to it. function push_brace_before_else(edits, src, i) local to = end_of(src, i) local next_word = past_space(src.text, to) if sub(src.text, next_word, next_word + 3) == "else" then push(edits, {at = to, cut = next_word - to, put = " } "}) else push(edits, {at = to, cut = 0, put = " }"}) end end -- A body keeps its own line after `|x|`, `=>` or `=`, unless it is a block, -- whose brace sits there. A statement has nothing before it to keep. function keeps_break(nodes, node, inner) return nodes[node.parent].kind ~= "statements" and inner.kind ~= "e-block" end function push_edits(edits, src, finding) local nodes = src.nodes local text = src.text local starts = src.starts local node = nodes[finding.at] if finding.check == "wrapped_body" then push_bracket_removal(edits, text, starts, node, keeps_break(nodes, node, nodes[node.kids[1]])) elseif finding.check == "else_block" then push_bracket_removal(edits, text, starts, nodes[node.kids[3]], false) elseif finding.check == "lambda_if" then local from = start_of(src, finding.at) local after = before_space(text, from) push(edits, {at = after, cut = from - after, put = "\n"}) else local condition = nodes[node.kids[1]] local then_branch = nodes[node.kids[2]] local otherwise = nodes[node.kids[3]] if is_parens(condition) then push_bracket_removal(edits, text, starts, condition, false) end if not has_braces(then_branch) then push_opening_brace(edits, src, node.kids[2], end_of(src, node.kids[1])) push_brace_before_else(edits, src, node.kids[2]) end if not (has_braces(otherwise) or otherwise.kind == "e-if-then-else") then push_opening_brace(edits, src, node.kids[3], past_else(src, end_of(src, node.kids[2]))) push(edits, {at = end_of(src, node.kids[3]), cut = 0, put = " }"}) end end end -- At one index, an edit that only inserts goes first, so that a closing brace -- nested in a branch's end stands before the one that cuts the space after it. function with_edits(text, edits) sort(edits, {"at", "cut"}) local pieces = {} local from = 1 for e in edits do if e.at < from then fail("find_extra_parens: two edits overlap at index " .. e.at) end if e.at > from then push(pieces, sub(text, from, e.at - 1)) end push(pieces, e.put) from = e.at + e.cut end if from <= #text then push(pieces, sub(text, from, #text)) end return join(pieces, "") end -- One kind of edit a pass, so no two edits of a pass touch one place. A finding -- inside another's span of the same kind is safe: its brackets are its own. function rewrite_pass(file, check) local edits = {} local text = read(file.path) local src = {path = file.path, text = text, starts = line_starts(text), nodes = file.nodes} for finding in findings_in(file) do if finding.check == check then push_edits(edits, src, finding) end end if #edits == 0 then return 0 end replace(file.path, with_edits(text, edits)) return #edits end -- Makes one kind of edit across `paths`, and answers how many it made. function rewrite_check(paths, check, roc) local made = 0 local touched = {} for file in parse_roc_files(paths).files do local n = rewrite_pass(file, check) if n > 0 then made = made + n push(touched, file.path) end end if #touched > 0 then local argv = {roc, "fmt"} for p in touched do push(argv, real(p)) end must(run(argv, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20, want = "roc-pin: the tree's own formatter"})) end return made end -- Rewrites `paths` until a pass changes nothing, and answers how many edits it -- made. Each kind runs in its own call, so a tree's parse is gone by the `yield`. function rewrite(paths, roc) local made = 0 local changed = true while changed do changed = false for check in CHECKS do local n = rewrite_check(paths, check, roc) if n > 0 then made = made + n changed = true end yield() end end return made end -- The findings across `paths`, as lines, with the counts. function report(paths) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local lines_found = {} local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do counts[c] = 0 end local at_line = {} for file in parsed.files do local source = split(read(file.path), "\n") for f in findings_in(file) do if not house_leaves_out("find_extra_parens", f.check) then counts[f.check] = counts[f.check] + 1 push(lines_found, file.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.check .. ": " .. trim(source[f.line])) push_at(at_line, file.path .. ":" .. f.line, f.check) end end end local said = {} for c in CHECKS do push(said, c .. " " .. counts[c]) end return {summary = "find_extra_parens (Roc): " .. #paths .. " files; " .. join(said, ", ") .. house_note("find_extra_parens"), lines = lines_found, at_line = at_line, refused = parsed.refused, total = #lines_found} end function self_test(paths, found) local wrong = {} local marks = 0 for p in paths do local n = 0 for l in lines(read(p)) do n = n + 1 local key = p .. ":" .. n local got = {} if has_key(found.at_line, key) then got = found.at_line[key] end local mark = re_find(l, "# (paren_if|wrapped_body|else_block|lambda_if)$") if mark ~= nil then marks = marks + 1 if not has_item(got, mark.group) then push(wrong, key .. ": no " .. mark.group .. " finding") end if #got > 1 then push(wrong, key .. ": more than the one finding marked") end elseif #got > 0 then push(wrong, key .. ": a finding (" .. join(got, ", ") .. ") on a line not marked for one") end end end if marks == 0 then push(wrong, "no plant holds a mark") end if exists(SCRATCH) then remove_tree(SCRATCH) end mkdir(SCRATCH) local copies = {} for p in paths do local copy = SCRATCH .. "/" .. basename(p) replace(copy, read(p)) push(copies, copy) end local roc = roc_bin("find_extra_parens", true) rewrite(copies, roc) local left = report(copies) for l in left.lines do push(wrong, "left after the rewrite: " .. l) end for r in left.refused do push(wrong, "the rewrite broke a file: " .. r) end for p in paths do local want = sub(p, 1, #p - 4) .. ".want" local copy = SCRATCH .. "/" .. basename(p) if exists(want) and read(copy) ~= read(want) then push(wrong, copy .. ": not as " .. want) end end if rewrite(copies, roc) ~= 0 then push(wrong, "a second rewrite changed something") end remove_tree(SCRATCH) for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("find_extra_parens self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end print("find_extra_parens (Roc) self_test: PASS (each marked line gives its finding, no other line one; the rewrite leaves none, and a second changes nothing)") end const paths = glob(GLOB) if WRITE then refuse_house_rewrite("find_extra_parens") print("find_extra_parens: " .. rewrite(paths, roc_bin("find_extra_parens", false)) .. " edits") end local found = report(paths) print_findings(found.summary, found.lines) fail_if_refused("find_extra_parens", found.refused) if SELF_TEST then self_test(paths, found) end

name: cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names.shale
html: -- This recipe finds names and top comments that say less than they should: a -- pure function named like a mutation, an abbreviation in a name, and a -- module with no doc or with history where its doc belongs. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names.shale -- shale cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- abbreviations the file of abbreviations, one a line, by default -- cookbook/words/abbreviations.txt, for a project with -- words of its own to add; -- terms a project's file of fixed terms that open a name and only -- look like a verb, one a line, such as `set_cookie` for -- HTTP's header, which `pure_mutator` leaves alone; -- house with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style -- (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/find_unclear_names/`. -- -- The checks read top-level names, module members and the record fields of -- types and annotations, never locals: -- -- pure_mutator An annotated pure function whose first word says it changes -- something (`push`, `fill`, `set`, `append`, `add`), though -- nothing is being added to. Something is when the result is -- the first argument's type, on its own, as a `Try`'s value, -- or as a field of a record or of an alias in the same file -- (`Try({ users : Users, user : User }, [Full])`), or when the -- first argument is a record with a field of the result's -- type (`{ so_far : List(U8), count : U64 }`). A first word -- `get` always counts, because a Roc function's plain name -- is already what it gets. -- abbreviation A name, member, field or type with a word from the -- abbreviations file, since Roc's style guide prefers the -- plain word. A name is reported once a file. -- module_doc A module with no `##` doc at the top of its file or above -- its type, or a top comment or a doc above its type that -- tells history (`originally`, `used to`, `emitted`, -- `ported`, even wrapped across two lines) instead of what -- the module does. A -- module its package or platform keeps to itself has no public -- doc to write, so any comment there will do. App files are -- left out, as they have no module type. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if -- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const ABBREVIATIONS_FILE = arg("abbreviations", "cookbook:words/abbreviations.txt") const TERMS_FILE = arg("terms", "") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") use("cookbook:roc/headers.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") const CHECKS = {"pure_mutator", "abbreviation", "module_doc"} const MUTATION_WORDS = {push = true, fill = true, set = true, append = true, add = true} const HISTORY_RE = "\\b(originally|used to|emitted|ported)\\b" -- The value of a `Try(value, errors)`, or `result` when it is no `Try`. function value_of_try(result) if not starts_with(result, "Try(") then return result end local depth = 0 for i = 5, #result do local c = sub(result, i, i) if c == "(" or c == "{" or c == "[" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == ")" or c == "}" or c == "]" then depth = depth - 1 elseif c == "," and depth == 0 then return trim(sub(result, 5, i - 1)) end end return result end function record_holds(record, type_name) return starts_with(record, "{") and (contains(record, " : " .. type_name .. ",") or contains(record, " : " .. type_name .. " }")) end -- Whether a function's result is what its first argument was added to. function gives_first_back(d, aliases) local value = value_of_try(d.result) if value == d.first or record_holds(d.first, value) then return true end return record_holds(get(aliases, last_part(value), value), d.first) end function opens_with_term(name, terms) for term in keys(terms) do if name == term or starts_with(name, term .. "_") then return true end end return false end function judge_mutator(d, aliases, terms, report) if not d.fn or not d.annotated or ends_with(d.name, "!") or opens_with_term(d.name, terms) then return nil end local first_word = split(d.name, "_")[1] local is_mutation = has_key(MUTATION_WORDS, first_word) and not gives_first_back(d, aliases) if first_word == "get" or is_mutation then push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "pure_mutator", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` is pure and gives a new `" .. d.result .. "`: name it for what it gives"}) end return nil end function judge_abbreviations(declared, abbreviations, report) local seen = {} for d in declared do if not has_key(seen, d.name) then seen[d.name] = true local found = {} for w in name_words(d.name) do if has_key(abbreviations, w) then push(found, w) end end if #found > 0 then push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "abbreviation", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` abbreviates: " .. join(found, ", ")}) end end end return nil end -- The history word in the comment lines `comment`, or nil. Each line's -- leading `#`s go before the lines are joined, so a phrase wrapped across -- two lines reads as one. function history_word(comment) local words = {} for l in comment do push(words, trim(re_replace(l, "^#+", ""))) end local found = re_find(lower(join(words, " ")), HISTORY_RE) if found == nil then return nil end return found.group end -- The comment lines just above line `at` of `src`, trimmed, as `{lines, -- first}`, where `first` is the line the comment starts on, or `at` when -- there is none. function comment_above(src, at) local first = at while first > 1 and starts_with(trim(src[first - 1]), "#") do first = first - 1 end local out = {} for k = first, at - 1 do push(out, trim(src[k])) end return {lines = out, first = first} end function judge_module_doc(f, declared, report) if is_app(f) then return nil end local name = module_name(f.path) local type_line = 0 for d in declared do if d.kind == "type" and d.name == name and d.owner == "" then type_line = d.line end end if type_line == 0 then return nil end local src = split(read(f.path), "\n") local top = opening_comment(src) local has_doc = (#top > 0 and starts_with(top[1], "##")) or (type_line > 1 and starts_with(trim(src[type_line - 1]), "##")) if is_private_module(f.path) and (#top > 0 or starts_with(trim(src[max(type_line - 1, 1)]), "#")) then has_doc = true end if not has_doc then push(report, {path = f.path, line = 1, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "` has no `##` doc saying what it is for"}) end local history = history_word(top) if history ~= nil then push(report, {path = f.path, line = 1, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "`'s top comment says `" .. history .. "`: say what the module does, and leave history to git"}) end local doc = comment_above(src, type_line) local doc_history = history_word(doc.lines) if doc.first > 1 and doc_history ~= nil then push(report, {path = f.path, line = doc.first, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "`'s doc says `" .. doc_history .. "`: say what the module does, and leave history to git"}) end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unclear_names/" check_plants("find_unclear_names", "cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale", CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "pure_mutator.roc", counts = {pure_mutator = 7}, says = {"pure_mutator.roc:3: pure_mutator: `push_cat` is pure and gives a new `List(U64)`", "`get_speed`"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_pure_mutator.roc"}, {glob = at .. "terms.roc", counts = {pure_mutator = 2}, says = {"`set_cookie_header`", "`set_cookies`"}}, {glob = at .. "terms.roc", args = {"terms=" .. at .. "terms.txt"}, counts = {pure_mutator = 1}, says = {"`set_cookies`"}}, {glob = at .. "terms.roc", args = {"terms=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}}, {glob = at .. "abbreviation.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 4}, says = {"abbreviation.roc:3: abbreviation: `max_vis_cats` abbreviates: vis", "`SunPos` abbreviates: pos", "`dist` abbreviates: dist"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_abbreviation.roc"}, {glob = at .. "abbreviation.roc", args = {"abbreviations=" .. at .. "project_words.txt"}, counts = {abbreviation = 1}, says = {"`max_vis_cats` abbreviates: cats"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_abbreviation.roc", args = {"abbreviations=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}}, {glob = at .. "module_doc/*.roc", counts = {module_doc = 5}, says = {"`NoDoc` has no `##` doc", "`Hashless` has no `##` doc", "`Old`'s top comment says `originally`", "`Sky`'s top comment says `used to`", "Sun.roc:3: module_doc: `Sun`'s doc says `originally`"}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_module_doc/*.roc"}, {glob = at .. "module_doc_private/*.roc", counts = {module_doc = 2}, says = {"`Shown` has no `##` doc", "`Silent` has no `##` doc"}}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}}, }) return nil end function run_check() local abbreviations = word_set(ABBREVIATIONS_FILE) local terms = TERMS_FILE == "" and {} or word_set(TERMS_FILE) local paths = glob(GLOB) local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local report = {} for f in parsed.files do local declared = declarations_of(f) local aliases = {} for d in declared do if d.kind == "type" and not d.is_nominal then aliases[d.name] = d.underlying end end for d in declared do if d.kind == "value" then judge_mutator(d, aliases, terms, report) end end if not house_leaves_out("find_unclear_names", "abbreviation") then judge_abbreviations(declared, abbreviations, report) end judge_module_doc(f, declared, report) end local verdict = verdict_of("find_unclear_names", CHECKS, report, #paths) verdict.summary = verdict.summary .. house_note("find_unclear_names") print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("find_unclear_names", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale
html: -- This recipe finds import lines that the file never uses, since Roc doesn't -- warn of one. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale -- shale cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; several globs may -- be given, separated by commas; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/find_unused_imports/`. -- -- The check: -- -- unused_import An `import` line whose name the file never refers to. The -- name is the alias of `import pkg.Mod as M`, else the last part -- of the module's path: `Mod` of `import pkg.Mod` and of -- `import Mod`. A use is a value, tag or type whose first part -- is that name: `Mod.name`, `Mod.Type`, `Mod.Tag(x)`, the -- module's own type `Mod`, in an annotation, a pattern, an -- expect or an interpolation alike. A name the line exposes -- (`exposing [line!]`) and the file uses is a use of the line. -- A file import, `import "page.html" as page : Str`, is used -- when the file refers to `page`. A name in a comment or a -- string is no use. -- -- A method call never names its module, so a module whose only use is a -- method on a value of its type is unused here, and Roc agrees: the method -- resolves through the value's type without the import. A bare tag that -- shares a module's name (`Other`, in an expression, a pattern or a tag union -- type) is no use of the module, but a nominal type's name before its record -- (`Point.{ x: 0 }`) is. -- -- roc-ast drops the qualifier of a tag in a pattern (`Color.Red =>` comes as -- `.Red`), so that name is read from the source at the pattern's column. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if -- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") const CHECKS = {"unused_import"} -- The first part of a dotted name: `Mod` of `Mod.Type.name`. function head_of(name) return split(name, ".")[1] end -- The name a pattern's tag is written with, read from the source line `text` -- at byte `col`, since the tree keeps only `.Red` of `Color.Red`. function written_tag(text, col) local m = re_find(sub(text, col), "^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)") if m == nil then return "" end return m.group end -- Each import of the file, as `{line, label, names}`: `names` are the names a -- use of the line may start with. function imports_of(tree) local out = {} for i = 1, #tree do local node = tree[i] if node.kind == "s-import" then local parts = split(node.raw, ".") local name = get(node, "alias", "") if name == "" then name = parts[#parts] end local names = {name} for k in node.kids do if tree[k].kind == "exposing" then for e in tree[k].kids do if tree[e].kind == "exposed-upper-ident" then push(names, tree[e].text) end if tree[e].kind == "exposed-lower-ident" then for t in tree[e].kids do push(names, tree[t].value) end end end end end push(out, {line = node.line, label = "`" .. node.raw .. "`" .. (get(node, "alias", "") == "" and "" or " as `" .. node.alias .. "`"), names = names}) elseif node.kind == "s-file-import" then for k in node.kids do if tree[k].kind == "name" then push(out, {line = node.line, label = "the file import `" .. tree[k].value .. "`", names = {tree[k].value}}) end end end end return out end -- The indexes, as text, of the nodes of `tree` that are kids of a node of -- kind `kind`. function kids_of_kind(tree, kind) local out = {} for node in tree do if node.kind == kind then for k in node.kids do out["" .. k] = true end end end return out end -- The set of first parts of every value, tag and type name the file uses. A -- bare tag (`Other`, in an expression, a pattern or a tag union type) names -- no module, so only a qualified one counts, or one that is a nominal type's -- name (`Point.{ x: 0 }`). function heads_used(tree, src) local used = {} local union_tags = kids_of_kind(tree, "tags") local nominal_names = kids_of_kind(tree, "mapper") for i = 1, #tree do local node = tree[i] local name = "" if node.kind == "e-ident" then name = node.raw end if node.kind == "e-tag" and (contains(node.raw, ".") or has_key(nominal_names, "" .. i)) then name = node.raw end if node.kind == "ty" and not has_key(union_tags, "" .. i) then name = node.name end if node.kind == "p-tag" then local written = starts_with(node.raw, ".") and written_tag(src[node.line], node.col) or node.raw if contains(written, ".") then name = written end end if name ~= "" then used[head_of(name)] = true end end return used end function judge_file(f, report) local tree = f.nodes local used = heads_used(tree, split(read(f.path), "\n")) for imp in imports_of(tree) do local is_used = false for name in imp.names do if has_key(used, name) then is_used = true end end if not is_used then push(report, {path = f.path, line = imp.line, check = "unused_import", what = imp.label .. " is imported and never used: delete the line"}) end end return nil end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unused_imports/" check_plants("find_unused_imports", "cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale", CHECKS, { {glob = at .. "unused.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"unused.roc:3: unused_import: `game.Polygon` is imported and never used"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_alias.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Distance` as `D` is imported and never used"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_exposing.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`pf.Stdout` is imported"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_file_import.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"the file import `page` is imported"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_in_prose.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Polygon` is imported"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_method_only.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Distance` is imported"}}, {glob = at .. "unused_tag_namesake.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Other` is imported"}}, {glob = at .. "unused.roc," .. at .. "unused_alias.roc", counts = {unused_import = 2}}, {glob = at .. "quiet_qualified.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_annotation.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_expect.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_pattern_tag.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_tag.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_exposing.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_alias.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_interpolation.roc"}, {glob = at .. "quiet_file_import.roc"}, {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}}, }) return nil end function run_check() local paths = {} for g in split(GLOB, ",") do for p in glob(trim(g)) do push(paths, p) end end local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) local report = {} for f in parsed.files do judge_file(f, report) end local verdict = verdict_of("find_unused_imports", CHECKS, report, #paths) print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) fail_if_refused("find_unused_imports", parsed.refused) return verdict end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local verdict = run_check() if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end end

name: cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale
