html: -- This library is what the recipes that can gate a build share: a nonzero -- exit when there are findings, and a self-test that proves it. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/gate_recipe.shale") -- local verdict = verdict_of("check_vocabulary", CHECKS, report, #paths) -- print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found) -- fail_if_refused("check_vocabulary", parsed.refused) -- return verdict, and `fail(verdict.summary)` at the script's top level -- check_plants("check_vocabulary", "cookbook:roc/check_vocabulary.shale", CHECKS, rows) -- -- The self-test runs the recipe itself as a child program, once for each row -- of a table, so each row judges the exit code and the printed findings -- together. A row is `{glob, args, counts, says, stops}`. `glob` is what the -- recipe reads and `args` its other arguments. `counts` maps each check to -- the findings it must print, and a check the row leaves out must print -- none. `says` is a list of literals the output must hold. A row with no -- counts is a clean case: the recipe must exit 0 and print no finding. A row -- with counts must exit nonzero. `stops` marks a row that must exit nonzero -- without any finding, such as one with a bad data file. Every other row's -- last line, leaving out the `──` lines Shale adds, must be the summary, -- because a gate that holds counts reads them there. -- The summary and the finding lines of `report`, a list of `{path, line, -- check, what}`, sorted. The summary gives each check's count as `check N`. function verdict_of(who, checks, report, file_count) sort(report, {"path", "line", "what"}) local count_by_check = {} local found = {} for r in report do incr(count_by_check, r.check) push(found, r.path .. ":" .. r.line .. ": " .. r.check .. ": " .. r.what) end local counts = {} for c in checks do push(counts, c .. " " .. get(count_by_check, c, 0)) end return {summary = who .. " (Roc): " .. file_count .. " files; " .. join(counts, ", "), found = found} end function findings_of(out, check) local found = 0 for l in lines(out) do if re_find(l, "^[^ ]+:[0-9]+: " .. check .. ": ") ~= nil then found = found + 1 end end return found end -- The last line of `out` that isn't one of Shale's `──` lines. function last_said(out) local last = "" for l in lines(trim(out)) do if not starts_with(l, "──") and trim(l) ~= "" then last = l end end return last end -- What is wrong with one row's run, as a list of sentences. function row_faults(checks, row, r) local faults = {} local counts = get(row, "counts", {}) local stops = get(row, "stops", false) local must_fail = stops or #keys(counts) > 0 if must_fail and r.code == 0 then push(faults, "it exited 0") end if not must_fail and r.code ~= 0 then push(faults, "it exited " .. r.code) end for check in checks do local found = findings_of(r.out, check) local wanted = get(counts, check, 0) if found ~= wanted then push(faults, check .. " printed " .. found .. ", not " .. wanted) end end if not stops and not contains(last_said(r.out), " files; ") then push(faults, "its last line is no summary: " .. last_said(r.out)) end for literal in get(row, "says", {}) do if not contains(r.out, literal) then push(faults, "its output lacks `" .. literal .. "`") end end return faults end -- Runs every row and fails if any is wrong, or if a check has no row that -- makes it fire, since a check no plant fires could be blind. function check_plants(who, recipe, checks, rows) local wrong = 0 local fired = {} for row in rows do local argv = {"shale", real(recipe), "glob=" .. row.glob} for a in get(row, "args", {}) do push(argv, a) end local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = 120000, whole = 4000000}) local faults = row_faults(checks, row, r) for check in keys(get(row, "counts", {})) do fired[check] = true end print((#faults == 0 and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. row.glob .. (#faults == 0 and "" or ": " .. join(faults, "; "))) if #faults > 0 then wrong = wrong + 1 print(r.out) end end for check in checks do if not has_key(fired, check) then print("FAIL `" .. check .. "` has no plant") wrong = wrong + 1 end end if wrong > 0 then fail(who .. " self_test: " .. wrong .. " wrong") end print(who .. " self_test: PASS (" .. #rows .. " rows: each plant gives its findings and a nonzero exit, each clean case none and exit 0)") return nil end

name: cookbook/roc/groups.shale
html: -- This library reads the bracket groups of Roc, their items and their -- tokens, as check_stacking.shale finds them and wrap_long_lines.shale -- rewrites them. Both use this one reading, so a group one rewrites is a -- group the other no longer reports. -- -- The stacking rule's home is here: a group of three or more items and -- STACK_TOKENS or more tokens stacks, and any other group sits on one line -- while that line fits. A token is a name (a dotted path like `Angle.Bearing` -- is one), a number, a string or a character; punctuation and operators are -- none. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/groups.shale") -- groups_on_line(l) each group that opens and closes on l -- without_targets_section(ls) ls with the lines no rewrite can reach blank -- is_data_line(l, width) a wide line of numeric data, left packed -- group_to_stack(l, tokens, width) the group a rewrite gives a comma -- with_trailing_comma(l, g) l with that comma added -- groups_to_unstack(ls, tokens, width) the stacked groups that shouldn't be -- without_trailing_commas(ls, gs) ls with each of those commas taken out const STACK_ITEMS = 3 const STACK_TOKENS = 6 const OPENERS = {["("] = ")", ["{"] = "}", ["["] = "]"} const CLOSERS = {[")"] = true, ["}"] = true, ["]"] = true} -- A line's width, with a tab counting four columns. function line_width(l) return #l + 3 * (#split(l, "\t") - 1) end -- The last character before position `i` that is not a space, or "". function char_before(l, i) local j = i - 1 while j > 0 and sub(l, j, j) == " " do j = j - 1 end if j == 0 then return "" end return sub(l, j, j) end const NO_PARENT = {closer = "", line = 0, trailing = false} -- The innermost of `open_groups`, closed at column `close` of the line numbered -- `close_line`, with its items counted from the commas at its own depth. A -- last item that is a rest pattern (`{ a, b, .. }`, `[x, .. as more]`) does -- not count. A parenthesized group with an arrow at its own depth, like -- `(A, B => C)`, is a function type, whose arguments can't take a trailing -- comma. `tokens` is how many tokens lie between the brackets. `fixed` says -- that a comment or a `\\` string lies between them, so no rewrite can bring -- them onto one line. `parent` is the group around it, as the scan holds it. function closed_group(ls, open_groups, close_line, close, last_code, tokens, fixed) local l = ls[close_line] local g = open_groups[#open_groups] local trailing = last_code == "," g.trailing = trailing local items = g.commas + 1 if trailing then items = g.commas end if g.line == close_line then if trim(sub(l, g.at + 1, close - 1)) == "" then items = 0 end local last = trim(sub(l, g.last + 1, close - 1)) if not trailing and g.commas > 0 and (last == ".." or starts_with(last, ".. as ")) then items = items - 1 end end return { line = g.line, open = g.at, close_line = close_line, close = close, items = items, tokens = tokens - g.tokens_before, fixed = fixed > g.fixed_before, trailing = trailing, depth = #open_groups - 1, parent = #open_groups > 1 and open_groups[#open_groups - 1] or NO_PARENT, fn_type = g.has_arrow and sub(ls[g.line], g.at, g.at) == "(", } end const WORD_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_" -- Searched for with `from` at a word character, so it matches there. A data -- line can run to 80,000 bytes, and copying the rest of the line at each word -- would cost the square of that. const WORD = "[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:\\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*" -- Whether the code before column `i` of `l` ends in the keyword `where`, so -- that a `[` there opens a `where` clause. It looks back from `i` only, for -- the same reason. function follows_where(l, i) local j = i - 1 while j > 0 and (sub(l, j, j) == " " or sub(l, j, j) == "\t") do j = j - 1 end if j < 5 or sub(l, j - 4, j) ~= "where" then return false end if j == 5 then return true end local b = sub(l, j - 5, j - 5) return b == " " or (b == "\t" and trim(sub(l, 1, j - 5)) == "") end -- The start of a method constraint (`k.is_eq :`). In a `where` clause's -- brackets, only a comma followed by one of these, or ending its line, -- separates items. const CONSTRAINT = "^ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? *:" -- A group just opened at column `i` of the line numbered `line`. function opened_group(line, i, closer, is_where, tokens, fixed) return {line = line, at = i, closer = closer, commas = 0, last = i, has_arrow = false, is_where = is_where, trailing = false, tokens_before = tokens, fixed_before = fixed} end -- The groups of the lines `ls`, each `{line, open, close_line, close, items, -- tokens, fixed, trailing, depth, parent, fn_type}`, by where they close. A group is a -- pair of brackets or a lambda's `|...|`. A group that never closes in `ls` is -- left out. function groups_in_lines(ls) local out = {} -- The groups still open, innermost last. Each holds where it opened, -- the character that closes it, its commas so far and the place of the -- last one, whether it is a `where` clause's brackets, whether a -- ` ->` or ` =>` appears at its own depth, and the running counts when it -- opened. An arrow call (`x->f()`) has no space before its arrow, so it -- doesn't count. local open_groups = {} -- The running counts of tokens and of comments and `\\` strings, and the -- last character of code seen. local tokens = 0 local fixed = 0 local last_code = "" for line = 1, #ls do local l = ls[line] local i = 1 local n = #l if starts_with(trim(l), "\\\\") then fixed = fixed + 1 tokens = tokens + 1 last_code = "\\" n = 0 end while i <= n do local c = sub(l, i, i) local code = c if c == " " then -- A space only separates, and spaces are the most common character. elseif find(WORD_CHARS, c) ~= nil then -- A name right after a dot continues a path, as in `f(x).name`. if sub(l, i - 1, i - 1) ~= "." or sub(l, i - 2, i - 2) == "." then tokens = tokens + 1 end i = i + #(re_find(l, WORD, {from = i}).text) - 1 elseif c == "\"" or c == "'" then tokens = tokens + 1 i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(l, i, i) ~= c do if sub(l, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end elseif c == "#" then fixed = fixed + 1 break elseif has_key(OPENERS, c) then local is_where = c == "[" and follows_where(l, i) push(open_groups, opened_group(line, i, OPENERS[c], is_where, tokens, fixed)) elseif (c == "-" or c == "=") and sub(l, i + 1, i + 1) == ">" and sub(l, i - 1, i - 1) == " " and #open_groups > 0 then open_groups[#open_groups].has_arrow = true i = i + 1 elseif c == "|" and sub(l, i + 1, i + 1) ~= ">" and sub(l, i + 1, i + 1) ~= "|" and sub(l, i - 1, i - 1) ~= "|" then if #open_groups > 0 and open_groups[#open_groups].closer == "|" then push(out, closed_group(ls, open_groups, line, i, last_code, tokens, fixed)) open_groups = take(open_groups, #open_groups - 1) else -- A `|` opens a lambda only where an expression can start. local b = char_before(l, i) if b == "" or b == "=" or b == "(" or b == "," or b == "[" or b == "{" or b == ":" then push(open_groups, opened_group(line, i, "|", false, tokens, fixed)) end end elseif has_key(CLOSERS, c) then -- Pop down to the group this character closes. A `|` that turned out -- to be no lambda is dropped on the way. while #open_groups > 0 and open_groups[#open_groups].closer ~= c do open_groups = take(open_groups, #open_groups - 1) end if #open_groups > 0 then push(out, closed_group(ls, open_groups, line, i, last_code, tokens, fixed)) open_groups = take(open_groups, #open_groups - 1) end elseif c == "," and #open_groups > 0 then local g = open_groups[#open_groups] if not g.is_where or trim(sub(l, i + 1)) == "" or re_find(sub(l, i + 1), CONSTRAINT) ~= nil then g.commas = g.commas + 1 g.last = i end end if code ~= " " and code ~= "\t" then last_code = code end i = i + 1 end end return out end -- The groups that open and close on line `l`, as groups_in_lines gives them. function groups_on_line(l) return groups_in_lines({l}) end -- The lines `ls` with a platform header's `targets:` section blanked, for -- reading groups. `roc fmt` lays that section out by itself and puts back or -- takes out any comma a rewrite changes there, so a rewrite that tried would -- never end. `targets` is a keyword, so nothing else can be this group. function without_targets_section(ls) if not contains(join(ls, "\n"), "targets:") then return ls end for g in groups_in_lines(ls) do if re_find(sub(ls[g.line], 1, g.open - 1), "\\btargets: *$") ~= nil then local out = {} for i = 1, #ls do push(out, (i >= g.line and i <= g.close_line) and "" or ls[i]) end return out end end return ls end -- Whether group `g` on line `l` is a row of literals, read at a glance: -- a list, or a tuple (a `(` not right after a name, `)` or `!`, so not a -- call's arguments), whose items are all numbers, strings with nothing -- interpolated, characters or bare tags, on a line within `width`. A string -- holding a comma would be split wrongly, so it never makes a row. const LITERAL_ITEM = [=[^(-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*|"[^"\\$]*"|'[^']+'|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)$]=] function is_literal_row(l, g, width) -- A line's width is at least its length, which costs nothing to read. if #l > width or line_width(l) > width then return false end local c = sub(l, g.open, g.open) if c == "(" then local b = char_before(l, g.open) if g.open > 1 and sub(l, g.open - 1, g.open - 1) ~= " " and re_find(b, "[A-Za-z0-9_)!]") ~= nil then return false end elseif c ~= "[" then return false end for item in split(trim(sub(l, g.open + 1, g.close - 1)), ",") do if trim(item) ~= "" and re_find(trim(item), LITERAL_ITEM) == nil then return false end end return true end -- Numeric data, such as a polygon's points, stays packed at any width. A -- number is a literal or a negative written `(0.0 - 0.5)`; a flat number -- record is a record of numbers, `{ x: 0.5, y: (0.0 - 0.25) }`; and a number -- list is a list of two or more numbers or flat number records. const NEGATIVE_NUMBER = "\\(-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]* - [0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*\\)" const NUMBER_RECORD = "\\{ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*: *-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*(?: *, *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*: *-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*)* *,? *\\}" const NUMBER_LIST = "\\[ *-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*(?: *, *-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*)+ *,? *\\]" -- `text` with each negative number and each flat number record read as the -- number 0, so that a list of them reads as a list of numbers. function numbers_as_zero(text) return re_replace(re_replace(text, NEGATIVE_NUMBER, "0"), NUMBER_RECORD, "0") end -- Whether text holds a number list. function holds_number_list(text) return re_find(numbers_as_zero(text), NUMBER_LIST) ~= nil end -- Whether group `g` on line `l` is numeric data: a number list, or a flat -- number record on a line that holds a number list, as a point among a -- polygon's points is. A flat number record on a line of its own is an -- ordinary record. function is_number_data(l, g) local text = numbers_as_zero(sub(l, g.open, g.close)) if re_find(text, "^" .. NUMBER_LIST .. "$") ~= nil then return true end return text == "0" and holds_number_list(l) end -- Whether line `l` is a line of data: wider than `width`, with a number list -- on it. No group on it stacks, since stacking any group around the data, or -- beside it, makes `roc fmt` open every group around that one, and the data -- spreads one item a line in later passes. A line that fits stacks as any -- other, but its number lists stay packed. function is_data_line(l, width) return line_width(l) > width and holds_number_list(l) end -- Whether group `g` holds enough to read better stacked. function is_big(g, min_tokens) return g.items >= STACK_ITEMS and g.tokens >= min_tokens end -- Whether group `g` on line `l` should stack. A function type's arguments -- can't take a trailing comma, a row of literals stays side by side, and so -- does numeric data. The caller asks is_data_line first, once a line. function should_stack(l, g, min_tokens, width) return is_big(g, min_tokens) and not g.trailing and not g.fn_type and not is_literal_row(l, g, width) and not is_number_data(l, g) end -- The group on line `l` the rewrite gives a trailing comma: the outermost, -- then widest, group that should stack; or else, on a line wider than -- `width`, the widest group of two or more items. nil when no group -- qualifies or the line is a line of data. function group_to_stack(l, min_tokens, width) if is_data_line(l, width) then return nil end local best = nil local groups = groups_on_line(l) for g in groups do if should_stack(l, g, min_tokens, width) then if best == nil or g.depth < best.depth or (g.depth == best.depth and g.close - g.open > best.close - best.open) then best = g end end end if best ~= nil or line_width(l) <= width then return best end for g in groups do if g.items >= 2 and not g.trailing and not g.fn_type then if best == nil or g.close - g.open > best.close - best.open then best = g end end end return best end -- Line `l` with a comma after the last item of group `g`, before any -- spaces that come ahead of its closing bracket. function with_trailing_comma(l, g) local j = g.close - 1 while j > g.open and sub(l, j, j) == " " do j = j - 1 end return sub(l, 1, j) .. "," .. sub(l, j + 1) end -- The start of a function's annotation, whose bare arguments can't stack. const ANNOTATION = "^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? : .*,$" -- The start of a function's annotation, on the line a group opens on. const ANNOTATION_OPENS = "^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? : " -- The text before group `g` once it sits on one line. A stacked group among -- an annotation's arguments moves its line down from the annotation's, and -- `roc fmt` brings it back up with the group on one line. function text_up_to_group(ls, g) local l = sub(ls[g.line], 1, g.open) if g.line > 1 and re_find(trim(ls[g.line - 1]), ANNOTATION) ~= nil then return ls[g.line - 1] .. " " .. trim(l) end return l end -- `joined`, the line group `g` would be on, with the rest of its annotation -- when `g` is among an annotation's arguments. Stacking such a group puts the -- arguments after it on lines of their own, and `roc fmt` brings them back up -- with it, so they are on the line `roc fmt` would make. The rest runs to the -- line with the annotation's arrow. Without an arrow, as in a record type's -- fields, `joined` is the whole line. function with_annotation_rest(ls, g, joined) local opens = re_find(trim(ls[g.line]), ANNOTATION_OPENS) ~= nil local follows = g.line > 1 and re_find(trim(ls[g.line - 1]), ANNOTATION) ~= nil if not opens and not follows then return joined end local rest = joined local i = g.close_line + 1 while sub(rest, #rest, #rest) == "," and i <= #ls do local piece = trim(ls[i]) if piece == "" then return joined end rest = rest .. " " .. piece if re_find(piece, "->|=>") ~= nil then return rest end i = i + 1 end return joined end -- The line stacked group `g` of `ls` would be on one line, spaced as `roc fmt` -- spaces it, or nil when a line break inside it does more than separate -- items: a blank line, or a block's statements. function group_on_one_line(ls, g) local joined = text_up_to_group(ls, g) for i = g.line + 1, g.close_line do local piece = trim(ls[i]) local before = sub(joined, #joined, #joined) local closes = has_key(CLOSERS, sub(piece, 1, 1)) or (i == g.close_line and sub(piece, 1, 1) == "|") if piece == "" then return nil end if before ~= "," and not has_key(OPENERS, before) and not (before == "|" and i == g.line + 1) then return nil end if closes and before == "," then joined = sub(joined, 1, #joined - 1) end if before == "{" or sub(piece, 1, 1) == "}" or (before == "," and not closes) then joined = joined .. " " end joined = joined .. piece end return with_annotation_rest(ls, g, joined) end -- Whether group `g` is what keeps the parentheses around it on several lines. -- They would join its line, past what group_on_one_line measures. function holds_parentheses_open(g) return g.parent.closer == ")" and g.parent.line < g.line and not g.parent.trailing end -- Whether stacked group `g` of `ls` should sit on one line: not big, nothing -- a rewrite can't join, and a joined line within `width`. function should_unstack(ls, g, min_tokens, width) if not g.trailing or is_big(g, min_tokens) or g.fixed or holds_parentheses_open(g) then return false end local joined = group_on_one_line(ls, g) return joined ~= nil and line_width(joined) <= width end -- Whether group `inner`, which closes before `outer`, lies inside it. function is_inside(inner, outer) return inner.line > outer.line or (inner.line == outer.line and inner.open > outer.open) end -- The stacked groups of `ls` that should sit on one line, by where they -- close, each with the column and line of its trailing comma as `comma` and -- `comma_line`. A group around one that stays on several lines can't be one -- line itself: `roc fmt` would give it its comma back. function groups_to_unstack(ls, min_tokens, width) local out = {} local last_kept = nil for g in groups_in_lines(without_targets_section(ls)) do if g.line ~= g.close_line then local holds_kept = last_kept ~= nil and is_inside(last_kept, g) if holds_kept or not should_unstack(ls, g, min_tokens, width) then last_kept = g else local at = g.close_line if trim(sub(ls[at], 1, g.close - 1)) == "" then at = at - 1 end g.comma_line = at g.comma = #(trim_end(ls[at])) if sub(ls[at], g.comma, g.comma) ~= "," then fail("groups: line " .. at .. " does not end in its group's trailing comma") end push(out, g) end end end return out end -- The lines `ls` with the trailing comma of each of `groups` taken out, which -- `roc fmt` reads as asking for one line. Each comma ends its own line. function without_trailing_commas(ls, groups) local out = ls for g in groups do out[g.comma_line] = sub(out[g.comma_line], 1, g.comma - 1) end return out end

name: cookbook/roc/headers.shale
html: -- What a Roc file's header says about who chooses its names. A name an app's -- platform asks for, a hook a platform hands its host, and a method Roc calls -- by name were all chosen somewhere else, so the recipes judge them differently -- from the names a program picks for itself. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/headers.shale") -- LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES the methods Roc calls by name -- header_names(nodes) a parse tree's `dictated` and `exposed` names -- exposed_by_folder(dir) the modules a folder's main.roc exposes -- is_exposed_module(path) whether a package or platform exposes a file -- is_private_module(path) whether a file is a package's own, unexposed -- header_word(text) a file's first word of code -- The methods Roc calls by name, from Roc's docs/langref/static-dispatch.md and -- operators.md, with the encoders' `encode` and `decode`. const LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES = {to_inspect = true, is_eq = true, to_hash = true, plus = true, minus = true, times = true, div_by = true, div_trunc_by = true, rem_by = true, is_lt = true, is_lte = true, is_gt = true, is_gte = true, range_exclusive_to = true, range_inclusive_to = true, range_exclusive_from = true, range_inclusive_from = true, range_iter = true, range_len_if_known = true, negate = true, ["not"] = true, from_numeral = true, from_quote = true, from_interpolation = true, iter = true, next = true, parser_for = true, encoder_for = true, map = true, ["map!"] = true, subscript = true, encode = true, decode = true} const EXPOSED_BY_DIR = {} -- A file's text with its comment lines left out. function code_of(text) local code = {} for l in lines(text) do if not starts_with(trim(l), "#") then push(code, l) end end return join(code, "\n") end -- The first word of a file's code: `app`, `package`, `platform`, `module`, -- `hosted`, or for a type module the type's name. function header_word(text) local found = re_find(code_of(text), "[A-Za-z_]+") return found == nil and "" or found.text end -- The names in the list between `[` and `]` of `text`. function bracketed_names(text) local out = {} for m in split(between(text, "[", "]") or "", ",") do if trim(m) ~= "" then push(out, trim(m)) end end return out end -- What a folder's `main.roc` exposes, as `{is_package, modules}`. `is_package` -- says the header is `package` or `platform`, and `modules` lists what it -- exposes. The header is read from the file, so it counts whether or not the -- run's glob holds it. function exposed_by_folder(dir) if has_key(EXPOSED_BY_DIR, dir) then return EXPOSED_BY_DIR[dir] end local main = (dir == "" or dir == ".") and "main.roc" or (dir .. "/main.roc") local out = {is_package = false, modules = {}} if exists(main) then local text = code_of(read(main)) local word = header_word(text) if word == "package" then out = {is_package = true, modules = bracketed_names(text)} end if word == "platform" then out = {is_package = true, modules = bracketed_names((between(text, "exposes", "]") or "") .. "]")} end end EXPOSED_BY_DIR[dir] = out return out end function module_of_path(path) local base = basename(path) return sub(base, 1, #base - 4) end function is_exposed_module(path) return has_item(exposed_by_folder(dirname(path)).modules, module_of_path(path)) end -- Whether a file is a module its package keeps to itself: it sits beside a -- package's or platform's main.roc, which doesn't expose it. function is_private_module(path) return exposed_by_folder(dirname(path)).is_package and not is_exposed_module(path) and basename(path) ~= "main.roc" end -- The value names a parse tree's header speaks for, as two sets. `dictated` -- holds what an app provides, what a platform requires of its app and what it -- provides to its host. `exposed` holds what a `module` or `hosted` header -- exposes. function header_names(nodes) local names = {dictated = {}, exposed = {}} local i = 2 while i <= #nodes and nodes[i].kind ~= "statements" do local n = nodes[i] if n.kind == "entrypoint" then names.dictated[n.value] = true end if n.kind == "symbol-map-entry" then names.dictated[n.func] = true end if n.kind == "text" and has_key(n, "value") and nodes[n.parent].kind == "exposed-lower-ident" then local list = nodes[nodes[n.parent].parent].kind if list == "provides" then names.dictated[n.value] = true else names.exposed[n.value] = true end end i = i + 1 end return names end

name: cookbook/roc/house.shale
html: -- This library names the Roc recipes' checks that are our own house style, not -- a fault in anyone else's code. Our guides hold our trees to them, and they -- stay on by default. Another project's guide may say otherwise: Luke Boswell's -- roc-style.md asks for `if (x) a else b` where ours has braces. `house=0` on a -- recipe leaves its house checks out, and cookbook/roc/check_foreign_code.shale runs every -- recipe that way. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") -- house_leaves_out("check_stacking", kind) whether `house=0` leaves this check out -- house_note("check_stacking") what the summary says when it does -- -- A check belongs here when a careful project could fairly do the opposite, so -- a finding says more about our habits than about their code. A check that -- points at a fault, or at something a project's own guide would also ask, -- does not. const HOUSE_CHECKS = { check_boundaries = {"single"}, hunt_names = {"bare_participle", "container", "phrase_name", "singular_list", "where_name", "world_verb"}, find_deep_calls = {"nested"}, find_extra_parens = {"paren_if", "lambda_if"}, find_unclear_names = {"abbreviation"}, check_stacking = {"stack", "unstack", "long", "wide string"}, } function house_is_off() local house = arg("house", 1) if house ~= 0 and house ~= 1 then fail("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not " .. house) end return house == 0 end function house_leaves_out(recipe, check) return house_is_off() and has_item(HOUSE_CHECKS[recipe], check) end -- The end of a summary line, saying what `house=0` left out. function house_note(recipe) if not house_is_off() then return "" end return "; left out as house style: " .. join(HOUSE_CHECKS[recipe], ", ") end -- Stops a rewrite under `house=0`, which would apply the rules it leaves out. function refuse_house_rewrite(recipe) if house_is_off() then fail(recipe .. ": write=1 applies our house style, so it refuses house=0") end return nil end

name: cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale
html: -- This recipe looks for awkward names in every .roc file of a tree: an -- effect named like a state, a question that returns no `Bool`, a name made -- only of vague words, and the other checks below. A finding is a question -- for the reader, not a verdict. The recipe reads the top-level definitions -- and the members of module types (`Html := [].{ ... }`), never local ones, -- from the syntax tree of Roc's own parser (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale), so -- an annotation broken across lines and a `where` clause read as Roc reads -- them. Files that don't parse are listed after the findings, and then the -- run fails. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc -- shale cookbook:roc/hunt_names.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; -- words with `words=1`, print the census of effects' first words -- (below) instead of the findings; -- house with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style -- (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code; -- types with `types=1`, also ask Roc's type checker (below); -- root the app the type checker starts from, or several -- (`root=a.roc,b.roc`); -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants (below). -- -- An effect is a function whose name ends in `!`. The checks: -- -- state_effect An effect whose first word is a past participle -- (`held_raw!`, `done!`) is named like a state; a verb would -- say what it does. The participle is fine when it starts -- the name of a type in the effect's annotation -- (`rounded_rectangle! : Frame, RoundedRectangle => {}`), -- because there it describes the thing the effect draws. -- question A function named as a question (`is_*`, `has_*`, `can_*`, -- `should_*`) that returns something other than a `Bool`, -- or an effect so named that returns no `Bool` -- (`is_open! : Str => Str`); and a function that returns a -- `Bool` but is named like a state (`marked : Str -> Bool`). -- A name with `_is_` or `_has_` inside (`unsigned_is_even`) -- is a question too. An effect that returns a `Bool` -- (`is_playing! : Sound => Bool`) is fine, because asking -- the host about live state has to be an effect. Only -- functions are checked: a value (`has_got : List(Bool)`) -- and an inferred type (`is_eq : _`) are not. With -- `types=1` a definition's type comes from the checker, so -- an unannotated `is_ready = |n| n + 1` is checked, and a -- result that is an alias of `Bool` (`Answer : Bool`) -- counts as a `Bool`. -- vague A name made only of vague words (cookbook/words/vague.txt): -- `handle_data`, `process!`, `do_it`. The entry points -- `handle`, `run` and `main` are fine. -- name_type A value named `*_count` whose type is not an integer, or -- `*_path` whose type is neither `Str` nor one naming `Path`. -- noun_effect An effect whose first word is not a known verb -- (cookbook/words/verbs.txt), such as a plain noun (`links!`, -- `page!`), reads as a value rather than an act. When the -- first word is a namespace prefix such as `block_` or -- `port_` (cookbook/words/namespaces.txt), the word after it -- is checked instead, here and by `state_effect`, and the -- namespace's own instructions listed in that file count as -- verbs (`port_out_32!`). An effect whose first argument is -- a surface, a `Frame` or a `Canvas`, is named for what it -- draws there (`circle! : Frame, Circle => {}`, called as -- `frame.circle!(...)`), so it is not checked. An effect with -- no annotation shows no surface, so it is checked. -- negative A `Bool` value named `no_*` or `not_*`, or an annotated -- name starting `is_not_`: its negation reads twice. -- preposition_split One stem given different trailing prepositions in -- one file (`blocks_of`, `blocks_in`, `blocks_from`). One -- relation should keep one preposition, or the names should -- say how they differ. It is reported once, at the first -- name. These prepositions are left out before counting: -- - one of a pair of opposites (`insert_before` beside -- `insert_after`; also `from` and `to`, `with` and -- `without`, `over` and `under`); -- - a `_from` name that takes more arguments than its -- siblings, a recursive worker resuming at an index -- (`blocks_from` beside `blocks_in`); -- - a module's suffix convention: a preposition on three -- or more stems in the same file, whose annotations -- share their first argument's type and their result -- (roc-markdown's `*_onto` writers each take a `List(U8)` -- and return it), so `run_onto` beside `run_at` is no -- split. Only the pair's own file counts, so a pair's -- verdict never moves when another file gains or loses -- a name; -- - a word the file declares as a keyword of the language -- it interprets, in a comment line such as -- `# keywords: for, on` (BASIC's `do_for`, `do_on`). -- command_tense An effect that takes a tag union whose tags all start -- with a past participle and carry no payload -- (`pin! : ..., [Pinned, Unpinned]`) names an instruction -- like an event. A command is a verb (`[Pin, Unpin]`). A -- union with a payload (`[Known(accounts), Unasked]`) -- carries state rather than an order. The union may be -- written in place or be a type declared in any file -- checked, and a `List(T)` argument is checked as `T`. -- mixed_tense An effect that takes a tag union (read as for -- `command_tense`, payloads included) with a tag starting -- with a verb beside one starting with a past participle -- (`apply! : [Pin, Unpinned]`): one of them is in the wrong -- mood. Only what an effect is handed is checked. A union an -- effect returns, a record field and a pure function's -- argument hold the domain's words for states (`Redirect` -- beside `Found`). -- container A type's name (`Entry`, `NodeInfo`) or a record field's -- (`items : List(Str)`) made only of container words -- (cookbook/words/containers.txt) and vague words. It says -- where a value sits, not what it holds. When the container -- word is the domain's own, the doc comment above the -- declaration says whose it is: `## A folder's entry` keeps -- `Entry`, and `## A listing's entries` keeps a field -- `entries`. A type's words are split at its capitals, a -- field's at its underscores. Fields in a local's annotation -- are not read. -- short_name A top-level or member name of one letter (`w : F64`). It -- is read far from where it is defined, and a local of the -- same letter shadows it. Locals and lambda parameters are -- not checked. -- worker_name A name whose last word says only that it is a helper: -- `_acc`, `_loop`, `_inner`, `_helper` or `_rec` -- (`count_acc`). Name a recursive worker for the parameter -- it adds, so that a call reads as a sentence: -- `count_from(xs, at)` for a start point, -- `html_onto(out, node)` for an output being built, -- `walk_with(tree, seen)` for other carried state. The entry -- function takes the plain name, `count`. `_step`, `_walk` -- and `_go` are ordinary words too, so they are reported -- only on a definition that calls itself. -- stacked_preposition A name whose last two words are both prepositions -- (cookbook/words/prepositions.txt), like `rest_from_onto`: -- a worker's suffix added to an entry name that already ends -- in one. Let each read once: the entry says what it returns -- (`tail_after`), the worker what it adds (`rest_onto`). A -- name made only of prepositions (`at_of`) is not reported, -- since its first word serves as a noun. -- taken_word A name that is a whole word from cookbook/words/taken.txt: -- a function named by one of Roc's own words (`record`, -- `tag`, `alias`, `module`), which reads as Roc's rather -- than the domain's, or a value named by a number from -- `one` to `twelve` (`three : List(Fields)`), which says -- how many rather than what it holds. A function that -- returns the very thing, its result's last part being the -- word capitalized (`record : ApiKey.Key -> ApiKey.Record`), -- is fine. -- bare_participle A pure function whose whole name is one past participle -- (`added`, `joined`, `named`, `chosen`), which reads too -- easily as a `Bool`. Name it by a noun for what it gives -- (`user_by_name`) or a verb for what it does (`add_user`). -- A name of two parts or more (`escaped_text`, `is_added`) -- and a value are not reported. An effect named this way is -- left to `state_effect`, and a function that gives a `Bool` -- to `question`. -- phrase_name A pure function, not a constant, whose first word is a -- preposition (cookbook/words/prepositions.txt) and which gives -- something other than a `Bool`: `in_view`, `on_next_segment`, -- `over_gap`. Bare like that it reads as a yes or no and hides -- what it gives, and a reader of a definition has often lost -- the module's context. Name the thing (`trees_in_view`, -- `rider_on_next_segment`), even if that repeats the module. -- The type decides what reads as a constructor or conversion, -- and these pass: -- - a constructor: a first word in CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS and a -- result, or a `Try` of one, that is its own module's type, -- a type declared in that module, or the type it is a -- member of (`Clock.at_step : U32 -> Clock`, -- `Color.of_hex : U32 -> Color.Rgb`). The word matters as -- well as the type: `Scene.in_view : View -> Scene` gives -- its own type and still reads as a question; -- - a conversion: `to_*` and `into_*`, which name what they -- give; -- - a `from_*` that takes or gives its own module's type, as -- above, even inside a record, a union or a list -- (`Along.from_start : Along -> Distance`, -- `Key.from_path : Str -> Try({ key : Key }, [NoKey])`). A -- `Try` gives its success only: an error that carries the -- type is no conversion to it; -- - a `from_<noun>` in a module that has no type of its own, -- one whose file declares only `Hex :: [].{ ... }` -- (`Hex.from_hex : Str -> Try(List(U8), [NotHex])`). Such a -- module has no type to take or give. A module with a type -- is held to the rule above, so -- `DateTime.from_clock : I64 -> Try(Str, [OutOfRange])`, -- which neither takes nor gives a `DateTime`, is reported. -- The next word has to be no preposition, so `from_behind` -- stays a phrase, and the type has to be known; -- - a changed copy: `with_*` or `without_*` that gives its -- first argument's type (`with_lean : Bike, Angle -> Bike`). -- A definition with no annotation shows none of this, so it -- is reported unless `types=1` supplies its type. -- singular_list A name that holds or gives a `List(...)`, or a `Try` of -- one, but reads as one thing: `triangle : List(Shape)`. The -- name ends in a plural of what the list holds (`triangles`, -- `herd_cows`) or is explicit (`triangle_list`). A collective -- noun is no plural: `herd`, `crowd` and `route` are reported. -- Read are top-level and member definitions, record fields, -- and the plain parameters of a top-level or member lambda. -- The word that counts is the one before a preposition or an -- `after` word of cookbook/words/list_names.txt, else the -- last (`trees_in_view`, `corners_ahead`). These pass: -- - a `List(U8)`, whose bytes are plumbing: the name says what -- they mean (`boundary`). A `List(F64)` is checked, since a -- flat run of coordinates can't be told from many readings; -- - a word list_names.txt calls `many`, one that can't be -- counted, and a word read as a participle (`clipped`); -- - a function whose whole name is a verb (`draw`), and a -- changed copy: one starting with a verb, `with` or -- `without` that gives its first argument's type -- (`trim_hull`); -- - one letter, and a value named by a number, which are -- `short_name`'s and `taken_word`'s to judge; -- - an accumulator's short idiom, as a whole name (`out`); -- - a name `phrase_name` reports, to be named again anyway. -- The word list, a participle and a verb don't pass a word -- that is the element's own (`route : List(Route)`). A word -- verbs.txt holds that list_names.txt calls `one` is no verb -- here (`route`). An `s` makes no plural after `s` (`class`), -- after letters that are no word (`pts`), or in a `one` word -- (`axis`). An alias of a list isn't seen, and with `types=1` -- an unannotated definition or parameter is read by its -- inferred type. -- world_verb A pure function whose first word is a verb of -- cookbook/words/world_verbs.txt, one that claims to act on -- something outside (`draw`, `paint_shape`). Nothing is drawn -- by a function that only makes a value, so name it for that -- value (`tree_shapes`). A verb that says what happens to its -- argument is fine (`plus`, `clamp`, `trim_hull`). An effect, -- which does act, and a value are not reported. -- where_name A method in a `where` clause named by one word -- (`[a.height : a -> U64]`). A clause matches by name alone, -- so the name is the whole contract: two words say what it is -- for (`scenery_height`). The methods Roc calls by name -- (`is_eq`, `plus`, `map`) are fine. A local's clause is read. -- -- Each name is judged once: from its annotation when it has one, else from -- its definition. An effect that takes an effectful function (`map2!`, -- `on_err!`: an argument's type holds a `=>`, or a lambda argument's name -- ends in `!`) has its `!` from that callback, so it is judged as the name -- without the `!`. Names chosen elsewhere are skipped: the methods Roc calls -- by name (cookbook/roc/headers.shale), and the top-level names a platform -- dictates, which are what an app's header provides (`app [loaded, step]`) -- and what a platform's header requires and provides. -- -- The output is the counts, one line per finding, -- `path:line: <check>: <why>`, and the counts again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). -- -- The word lists are in cookbook/words/, shared with the Zig name hunt. -- participles.txt lists the irregular past participles; any other word -- ending in `ed` counts as one unless ed_verbs.txt lists it. With `words=1` -- the recipe prints a census instead of the findings: each first word the -- effects start with, how many start with it, and its verdict: `verb`, -- `participle`, `vague`, `asks` (`is`, `has`) or `refused` (what -- `noun_effect` reports). A verb missing from verbs.txt shows up there as -- `refused`. -- -- With `types=1` the recipe asks Roc's type checker for each definition's -- type (cookbook/roc/types.shale). It needs `root=` and the tree's -- `roc-version` file. A root the checker refuses, or a roc-types built for -- another Roc version, stops the run. A file that no root imports is -- checked without types, listed after the findings, and fails the run. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc types=1 -- -- `self_test=1` runs the recipe over `cookbook/roc/plants/hunt_names/`. Each -- plant is named for the check it holds (`question.roc`, -- `question_where.roc`) and must make that check report, and no other. A -- `quiet_*.roc` plant must make no check report. Every check needs a plant, -- and a plant named for no check fails the test. The census must also give -- the right verdict for one known word of the plants per verdict. The -- plants in `typed/` are checked with the types, from their app -- `typed/QuietApp.roc`, and their CamelCase module names read as snake case -- (`QuestionInferred` as `question_inferred`); the rest are checked -- without. The self-test fails without roc-types. -- -- The recipe reads each file's source as well as its tree, to tell `->` -- from `=>`, which the tree writes alike. On a large tree that needs more -- than the default arena. -- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/parsed.shale") use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") use("cookbook:roc/types.shale") use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:roc/headers.shale") use("cookbook:roc/house.shale") const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/hunt_names/" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const TYPES_ARG = arg("types", "0") if TYPES_ARG ~= "0" and TYPES_ARG ~= "1" then fail("hunt_names: types=" .. TYPES_ARG .. ": 0 (the default) or 1") end -- The self-test checks its typed plants with the types, and the rest -- without. const USE_TYPES = SELF_TEST or TYPES_ARG == "1" const ROOT = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "typed/QuietApp.roc") or arg("root", "") -- The type checker's answers, filled in once the files are known; empty -- unless USE_TYPES. const CHECKER_TYPES = {real = {}, pats = {}, exprs = {}, unreached = {}} const CENSUS_ONLY = arg("words", "") == "1" const CHECKS = {"state_effect", "question", "vague", "name_type", "negative", "noun_effect", "command_tense", "mixed_tense", "container", "preposition_split", "short_name", "worker_name", "stacked_preposition", "taken_word", "bare_participle", "phrase_name", "singular_list", "world_verb", "where_name"} -- `worker_name` reports a helper suffix always, and a suffix that is also an -- ordinary word (a fold's `step`, `List.walk`, `can_go`) only on a -- definition that calls itself. const HELPER_SUFFIXES = {acc = true, loop = true, inner = true, helper = true, rec = true} const RECURSION_SUFFIXES = {step = true, walk = true, go = true} const VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/verbs.txt") const PARTICIPLES = word_set("cookbook:words/participles.txt") const ED_VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/ed_verbs.txt") const VAGUE = word_set("cookbook:words/vague.txt") const CONTAINERS = word_set("cookbook:words/containers.txt") const PREPOSITIONS = word_set("cookbook:words/prepositions.txt") const NAMESPACES = namespace_instructions("namespaces.txt") const TAKEN_WORDS = taken_word_kinds("taken.txt") const LIST_NAMES = list_name_kinds("list_names.txt") const WORLD_VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/world_verbs.txt") const PLAIN_ELEMENTS = set_of({"U16", "U32", "U64", "I16", "I32", "I64", "F32", "F64", "Dec", "Str", "Bool"}) const SURFACES = {Frame = true, Canvas = true} -- The first words `phrase_name` lets a constructor start with. They are the -- ones constructors use in safari, roc-chat and roc-markdown: `Clock.at_step`, -- `Dm.between`, `SignedIn.by_session`, `MdText.for_input`, `Name.of_strict`, -- `Directory.with_founder`. `from` has a wider rule of its own, -- `is_from_conversion`. const CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS = set_of({"at", "between", "by", "for", "of", "with"}) const CONVERSION_WORDS = set_of({"into", "to"}) const CHANGED_COPY_WORDS = set_of({"with", "without"}) -- The names in each file that end in a preposition, grouped by the stem -- before it. Each key is `path|stem`, each value `{path, line, stem, -- prepositions}`, and `prepositions` maps each preposition to the first -- name using it and that name's arity. const PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM = {} -- The stems each trailing preposition is put on in each file, grouped by the -- preposition and the shape of the annotation: its first argument's type and -- its result. Each key is `path|preposition|first|result`, each value a set -- of stems. A preposition reaching CONVENTION_STEMS stems of one shape in a -- file goes into SUFFIX_CONVENTIONS as `path|preposition`. Counting stems by -- preposition alone, or by result alone, would make a common preposition -- (`_of`) a convention in any large module. Counting them across files made -- a pair's verdict move when an unrelated file lost a name. const STEMS_BY_SHAPE = {} const CONVENTION_STEMS = 3 const SUFFIX_CONVENTIONS = {} -- The keywords each file declares (`# keywords: for, on`), by path. const DECLARED_KEYWORDS = {} const ENTRY_POINT_NAMES = {handle = true, run = true, main = true} const INTEGER_TYPES = {U8 = true, U16 = true, U32 = true, U64 = true, U128 = true, I8 = true, I16 = true, I32 = true, I64 = true, I128 = true} -- The tag union each type declaration names, by the type's name: `Edit` of -- `Edit : [Opened, Closed]` maps to its `union_shape`. const TAG_UNION_TYPES = {} -- The aliases of `Bool` declared in the files read, by each name the type -- checker may write for them (`Answer`, `Owner.Answer`). const BOOL_ALIASES = {} -- Each type a file declares, by path, as whether it is `[].{ ... }`: an empty -- union with members. const TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE = {} -- Every type name and record field name that `container` checks, each -- `{path, line, name, words, is_field, doc}`, where `doc` is the comment -- lines above its declaration, lowercased. const TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES = {} const count_by_check = {} for c in CHECKS do count_by_check[c] = 0 end -- The set of `path|check` pairs where the check reported, for the self-test. const fired_in_file = {} -- Each first word an effect starts with, mapped to `{word, count, verdict}`. const first_word_census = {} const finding_lines = {} function report(path, line, check, why) if house_leaves_out("hunt_names", check) then return nil end if not CENSUS_ONLY then push(finding_lines, path .. ":" .. line .. ": " .. check .. ": " .. why) end count_by_check[check] = count_by_check[check] + 1 fired_in_file[path .. "|" .. check] = true return nil end function is_participle(word) if has_key(PARTICIPLES, word) then return true end return #word > 3 and ends_with(word, "ed") and not has_key(ED_VERBS, word) end for word in keys(VERBS) do if is_participle(word) then fail("hunt_names: `" .. word .. "` is in cookbook/words/verbs.txt and reads as a participle, which would make its effects states") end end -- What an effect's first word says: `participle`, `verb`, `vague`, `asks` -- (`is`, `has`) or `refused`. function first_word_verdict(word) if is_participle(word) then return "participle" end if has_key(VERBS, word) then return "verb" end if has_key(VAGUE, word) then return "vague" end if word == "is" or word == "has" then return "asks" end return "refused" end -- ── the syntax tree ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The keywords a file declares in a comment line `# keywords: for, on`, -- added to DECLARED_KEYWORDS. function note_declared_keywords(path, src) for l in src do local found = re_find(trim(l), "^# keywords: (.*)$") if found ~= nil then for w in split(found.groups[1], ",") do if trim(w) ~= "" then push_at(DECLARED_KEYWORDS, path, lower(trim(w))) end end end end return nil end -- Notes what the type declaration at `i` declares: its tag union in -- TAG_UNION_TYPES, its kind in TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE, its name in -- TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES, and in BOOL_ALIASES -- when it is an alias of `Bool`, under its bare name and, for a module -- type's member, `Owner.Name` as the checker writes it. function note_type_declaration(path, src, tree, i) local kids = children(tree, i) local declared = #kids > 0 and attribute(tree, kids[1], "name") or "" if declared == "" then return nil end local line = tostring(tree[i].line) local is_union = #kids > 1 and tree[kids[2]].kind == "ty-tag-union" if is_union then TAG_UNION_TYPES[declared] = union_shape(tree, kids[2]) end push_at(TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE, path, is_union and #TAG_UNION_TYPES[declared].names == 0 and tree[kids[#kids]].kind == "associated") push(TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES, {path = path, line = line, name = declared, words = name_words(declared), is_field = false, doc = doc_above(src, tree[i].line)}) if #kids > 1 and tree[kids[2]].kind == "ty" and attribute(tree, kids[2], "name") == "Bool" then BOOL_ALIASES[declared] = true local parent = tree[i].parent if parent > 0 and tree[parent].kind == "associated" and tree[parent].parent > 0 then local owner_kids = children(tree, tree[parent].parent) local owner = #owner_kids > 0 and attribute(tree, owner_kids[1], "name") or "" if owner ~= "" then BOOL_ALIASES[owner .. "." .. declared] = true end end end return nil end -- The top-level annotation at `i`, as a definition record, or nil when it -- is only a `where` clause. `whole` is its type rendered, and `result` the -- type it returns. A function's record also has `arity` and `first` (its -- first argument's type), and an effect's has `types`, the type names its -- annotation mentions, and `args`, each argument's `argument_shape`. -- `callback` says it takes an effectful function, an argument whose source -- holds `=>`. function annotation_definition(path, src, tree, i) local def = {path = path, line = tostring(tree[i].line), name = attribute(tree, i, "name"), owner = owner_of(tree, i), annotation = true, fn = false, callback = false, paired = false} local kids = children(tree, i) if #kids == 0 or tree[kids[1]].kind == "where" then return nil end def.whole = render_type(tree, kids[1]) def.result = def.whole if tree[kids[1]].kind == "ty-fn" then local parts = children(tree, kids[1]) local is_effect = ends_with(def.name, "!") def.fn = true def.arity = #parts - 1 def.result = render_type(tree, parts[#parts]) def.first = #parts > 1 and render_type(tree, parts[1]) or "" def.argument_types = {} if is_effect then def.types = mentioned_type_names(tree, kids[1], {}) def.args = {} end for a in take(parts, #parts - 1) do push(def.argument_types, render_type(tree, a)) if contains(span_text(src, tree, a), "=>") then def.callback = true end if is_effect then push(def.args, argument_shape(tree, a)) end end end return def end -- The top-level definition `name = ...` at `i`, as a definition record, or -- nil when its pattern is not a plain name. `lambda` says its value is a -- lambda, `callback` that a lambda argument's name ends in `!`, `recurses` -- (for a name ending in a RECURSION_SUFFIXES word) that it calls itself, -- `typed` is the checker's type when there is one, and `parameters` holds -- `{at, name, line, typed}` for each lambda argument, `name` "" for one that -- is a pattern rather than a plain name. function value_definition(path, tree, i) local kids = children(tree, i) if #kids == 0 or tree[kids[1]].kind ~= "p-ident" then return nil end local def = {path = path, line = tostring(tree[i].line), name = attribute(tree, kids[1], "raw"), owner = owner_of(tree, i), annotation = false, fn = false, callback = false, paired = false} if #kids > 1 and tree[kids[2]].kind == "e-lambda" then def.lambda = true def.parameters = {} for part in children(tree, kids[2]) do if tree[part].kind == "args" then for a in children(tree, part) do if ends_with(attribute(tree, a, "raw"), "!") then def.callback = true end local parameter = {name = tree[a].kind == "p-ident" and attribute(tree, a, "raw") or "", line = tostring(tree[a].line)} if parameter.name ~= "" and USE_TYPES and has_key(CHECKER_TYPES.real, path) then local checker_type = roc_type_at(CHECKER_TYPES, "pat", path, tree[a]) if checker_type ~= nil then parameter.typed = checker_type end end push(def.parameters, parameter) end end end end local ws = split(ends_with(def.name, "!") and sub(def.name, 1, #def.name - 1) or def.name, "_") if #ws > 1 and has_key(RECURSION_SUFFIXES, ws[#ws]) then def.recurses = calls_itself(tree, i, def.name) end if USE_TYPES and has_key(CHECKER_TYPES.real, path) then local checker_type = roc_type_at(CHECKER_TYPES, "pat", path, tree[kids[1]]) if checker_type ~= nil then def.typed = checker_type end end return def end -- Whether the definition at `i` is a top-level name its file's header dictates. function is_dictated(tree, i, def, dictated) return has_key(dictated, def.name) and owner_of(tree, i) == "" end -- Every top-level and module-member annotation and definition in the parsed -- files, as definition records `{path, line, name, annotation, fn, -- callback, paired, ...}`. A definition whose annotation is just above it -- is `paired`, and the annotation then gets `has_def`, the definition's -- `typed` and its `callback`. Along the way this fills DECLARED_KEYWORDS, -- TAG_UNION_TYPES, BOOL_ALIASES and TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES. function read_definitions(parsed_files) local definitions = {} for f in parsed_files do local path = f.path local tree = f.nodes local src = split(read(path), "\n") note_declared_keywords(path, src) local dictated = header_names(tree).dictated -- Each node is outer when it and every ancestor sit in OUTER_KINDS, and -- its `declaration_line` is its line when it is an outer annotation or -- type declaration, else "". A parent comes before its children. local outer = {} local declaration_line = {} -- The definition record of each annotation, by the node's index. local annotation_records = {} for i = 1, #tree do local node = tree[i] local parent = node.parent push(outer, parent == 0 or (outer[parent] and has_key(OUTER_KINDS, tree[parent].kind))) local kind = node.kind push(declaration_line, (outer[i] and (kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl")) and tostring(node.line) or "") if outer[i] and kind == "s-type-decl" then note_type_declaration(path, src, tree, i) end if kind == "anno-record-field" then local at = field_declaration_line(tree, declaration_line, i) local field = attribute(tree, i, "name") if at ~= "" and field ~= "" then local named = {path = path, line = tostring(node.line), name = field, words = name_words(field), is_field = true, doc = doc_above(src, tonumber(at))} local field_type = children(tree, i)[1] named.gives = render_type(tree, field_type) named.is_function = tree[field_type].kind == "ty-fn" named.first = "" if named.is_function then local parts = children(tree, field_type) named.gives = render_type(tree, parts[#parts]) named.first = #parts > 1 and render_type(tree, parts[1]) or "" end push(TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES, named) end end if outer[i] and kind == "s-type-anno" then local def = annotation_definition(path, src, tree, i) if def ~= nil and not is_dictated(tree, i, def, dictated) then push(definitions, def) annotation_records[tostring(i)] = def end end if outer[i] and kind == "s-decl" then local def = value_definition(path, tree, i) if def ~= nil and not is_dictated(tree, i, def, dictated) then local above = get(annotation_records, tostring(previous_sibling(tree, i))) if above ~= nil and above.name == def.name then def.paired = true above.has_def = true if has_key(def, "typed") then above.typed = def.typed end if def.callback then above.callback = true end above.parameters = get(def, "parameters", {}) end push(definitions, def) end end end end return definitions end -- ── the checks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function all_tags_past(tags) for t in tags do if not is_participle(tag_first_word(t)) then return false end end return true end -- What a definition's type says, for `question`, `taken_word` and -- `phrase_name`: `{is_function, first, result, known, source_note}`. The type -- is the checker's when it gave one, else the annotation's. `known` is false -- for a definition with no annotation and no checker's type. function definition_signature(def) local signature = {is_function = def.annotation and def.fn, first = get(def, "first", ""), result = get(def, "result", ""), known = def.annotation, source_note = ""} if has_key(def, "typed") then local checker = roc_type_parts(def.typed) signature = {is_function = checker.fn, first = first_argument(checker.args), result = checker.result, known = true, source_note = " (the checker's type)"} if has_key(BOOL_ALIASES, checker.result) then signature.result = "Bool" end end return signature end -- Whether `type_text` names the module `def` is in, a type declared in it, or -- the type `def` is a member of. Type arguments don't count: -- `Bike.Motion(others)` is `Bike.Motion`. function is_own_type(def, type_text) local head = re_find(type_text, "^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+") if head == nil then return false end local parts = split(head.text, ".") local module = module_name(def.path) return parts[1] == module or parts[1] == def.owner or parts[#parts] == def.owner end -- Whether `type_text` names its module's own type anywhere in it. Only a -- capital starts a type, so a field that shares a file's name is no mention. function mentions_own_type(def, type_text) for found in re_find_all(type_text, "\\b[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*") do if is_own_type(def, found.text) then return true end end return false end -- Whether the file at `path` declares one type, `[].{ ... }`, which holds the -- module's functions and has no values of its own. function has_no_type_of_its_own(path) local declared = get(TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE, path, {}) return #declared == 1 and declared[1] end -- Whether a function named `ws`, whose first word is `from`, reads as a -- conversion: `phrase_name` in the header. function is_from_conversion(def, ws, signature) if mentions_own_type(def, signature.first) or mentions_own_type(def, success_type(signature.result)) then return true end return signature.known and has_no_type_of_its_own(def.path) and #ws > 1 and not has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[2]) end -- Whether a function named `ws`, whose first word is a preposition, reads as a -- constructor, a conversion or a changed copy: `phrase_name` in the header. function reads_as_maker(def, ws, signature) local word = ws[1] if has_key(CONVERSION_WORDS, word) then return true end if has_key(CHANGED_COPY_WORDS, word) and signature.result == signature.first then return true end if word == "from" then return is_from_conversion(def, ws, signature) end return has_key(CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS, word) and is_own_type(def, success_type(signature.result)) end -- The word of a name that says what it is, by index in `ws`: the one before -- the first preposition or word list_names.txt calls `after`, past the name's -- first word (`trees_in_view` and `corners_ahead` give `trees` and `corners`), -- else the last. Digits alone are no word (`corner_2`). function head_word_at(ws) for k = 2, #ws do if has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[k]) or get(LIST_NAMES, ws[k], "") == "after" then return k - 1 end end local at = #ws while at > 1 and re_find(ws[at], "^[0-9]+$") ~= nil do at = at - 1 end return at end -- Whether a word reads as a plural. An `s` doesn't make one in `class`, in a -- word list_names.txt calls `one` (`axis`), or after letters that are no word -- (`pts`); after one letter it does (`xs`). function reads_as_plural(word) if get(LIST_NAMES, word, "") == "one" then return false end if not ends_with(word, "s") or ends_with(word, "ss") then return false end local stem = sub(word, 1, #word - 1) return #stem == 1 or re_find(stem, "[aeiouy]") ~= nil end function plural_of(word) if ends_with(word, "y") and re_find(word, "[aeiou]y$") == nil then return sub(word, 1, #word - 1) .. "ies" end if re_find(word, "(s|x|z|ch|sh)$") ~= nil then return word .. "es" end return word .. "s" end -- The names `singular_list` offers for `bare`, whose head word is at `at` in -- `ws`: the plural of what the list holds put after the head, as in -- `herd_cows`, or the head's own plural when the element is that word, a -- number or text; else the name with `_list`. function honest_list_names(bare, ws, at, element) local held = element_word(element) local says_what_it_holds = held ~= "" and held ~= ws[at] and re_find(element, "^[A-Z]") ~= nil and not has_key(PLAIN_ELEMENTS, element) local plural_words = {} for k = 1, #ws do if k ~= at then push(plural_words, ws[k]) elseif says_what_it_holds then push(plural_words, ws[k]) push(plural_words, plural_of(held)) else push(plural_words, plural_of(ws[k])) end end return "`" .. join(plural_words, "_") .. "`, or `" .. bare .. "_list`" end -- Reports a name whose type says many and whose head word says one: -- `singular_list` in the header. `subject` is `{path, line, name, kind, -- is_function, first, gives}`, `kind` being what the report calls it. function judge_list_name(subject) local element = list_element(subject.gives) if element == nil or element == "U8" then return nil end local bare = ends_with(subject.name, "!") and sub(subject.name, 1, #subject.name - 1) or subject.name if #bare < 2 or get(TAKEN_WORDS, bare, "") == "cardinal" or get(LIST_NAMES, bare, "") == "accumulator" then return nil end local ws = split(bare, "_") local at = head_word_at(ws) local head = ws[at] if head == "list" or reads_as_plural(head) then return nil end if element_word(element) ~= head then if get(LIST_NAMES, head, "") == "many" or is_participle(head) then return nil end local starts_with_act = subject.is_function and has_key(VERBS, ws[1]) and get(LIST_NAMES, ws[1], "") ~= "one" local is_changed_copy = subject.is_function and subject.first == subject.gives and (starts_with_act or has_key(CHANGED_COPY_WORDS, ws[1])) if is_changed_copy or (starts_with_act and #ws == 1) then return nil end end report(subject.path, subject.line, "singular_list", "the " .. subject.kind .. " `" .. subject.name .. "` " .. (subject.is_function and "gives" or "holds") .. " `" .. subject.gives .. "` but reads as one thing, `" .. head .. "`: " .. honest_list_names(bare, ws, at, element)) return nil end -- Notes a name that ends in a preposition, for `preposition_split`, in -- PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM and, when it is an annotated function, in -- STEMS_BY_SHAPE and SUFFIX_CONVENTIONS. function note_trailing_preposition(def, ws) local preposition = ws[#ws] local stem = join(take(ws, #ws - 1), "_") local key = def.path .. "|" .. stem if not has_key(PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM, key) then PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM[key] = {path = def.path, line = def.line, stem = stem, prepositions = {}} end local group = PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM[key] if def.annotation and def.fn then local shape_key = def.path .. "|" .. preposition .. "|" .. def.first .. "|" .. def.result if not has_key(STEMS_BY_SHAPE, shape_key) then STEMS_BY_SHAPE[shape_key] = {} end STEMS_BY_SHAPE[shape_key][stem] = true if #keys(STEMS_BY_SHAPE[shape_key]) >= CONVENTION_STEMS then SUFFIX_CONVENTIONS[def.path .. "|" .. preposition] = true end end if not has_key(group.prepositions, preposition) then group.prepositions[preposition] = {name = def.name, arity = get(def, "arity", -1)} end return nil end -- Reports what each check finds in one definition record, except -- `container` and `preposition_split`, which are judged over all the files -- afterwards. function judge_definition(def) local path = def.path local line = def.line local full_name = def.name if has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, full_name) then return nil end local has_bang = ends_with(full_name, "!") local name = has_bang and sub(full_name, 1, #full_name - 1) or full_name local is_effect = has_bang and not def.callback local ws = split(name, "_") local last_word = ws[#ws] local is_annotation = def.annotation -- A definition paired with an annotation was judged at the annotation. local judged_here = not def.paired local asks_inside = contains(name, "_is_") or contains(name, "_has_") local has_namespace = is_effect and #ws > 1 and has_key(NAMESPACES, ws[1]) local act_word = has_namespace and ws[2] or ws[1] local act_verdict = first_word_verdict(act_word) if has_namespace and act_verdict == "refused" and has_key(NAMESPACES[ws[1]], act_word) then act_verdict = "verb" end local act_place = has_namespace and ("the word after its namespace `" .. ws[1] .. "_`") or "its first word" local named_as_state = is_participle(act_word) and not asks_inside if is_effect and judged_here then if not has_key(first_word_census, act_word) then first_word_census[act_word] = {word = act_word, count = 0, verdict = act_verdict} end first_word_census[act_word].count = first_word_census[act_word].count + 1 end local arguments = get(def, "args") or {} local draws_on_surface = #arguments > 0 and has_key(SURFACES, get(arguments[1], "ref", "")) if is_effect and judged_here and act_verdict == "refused" and not draws_on_surface then if has_key(PREPOSITIONS, act_word) then report(path, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but " .. act_place .. " is a preposition, `" .. act_word .. "`: an effect is named for its act") else report(path, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but " .. act_place .. ", `" .. act_word .. "`, is no verb: it reads as a value, not an act") end end if judged_here and #ws > 1 and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, last_word) then note_trailing_preposition(def, ws) end local names_drawn_type = #ws > 1 and has_key(get(def, "types") or {}, camel_case(ws)) if is_effect and judged_here and named_as_state and not names_drawn_type then report(path, line, "state_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but is named as a state, `" .. act_word .. "`: a verb says what it does") end local named_as_question = #ws > 1 and (ws[1] == "is" or ws[1] == "has" or ws[1] == "can" or ws[1] == "should") local signature = definition_signature(def) local returns_bool = signature.is_function and signature.result == "Bool" if named_as_question and judged_here and is_effect and not returns_bool then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a question but has an effect" .. (signature.is_function and (" and gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) or "")) end if returns_bool and named_as_state and judged_here then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` gives a `Bool`" .. signature.source_note .. " but is named as a state, `" .. ws[1] .. "`: ask it (`is_*`, `has_*`)") end if named_as_question and judged_here and signature.known and signature.is_function and not is_effect and signature.result ~= "Bool" and signature.result ~= "_" then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a question but gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) end if judged_here then local all_vague = true for w in ws do if not has_key(VAGUE, w) then all_vague = false end end if #ws == 1 and has_key(ENTRY_POINT_NAMES, ws[1]) then all_vague = false end if all_vague then report(path, line, "vague", "`" .. full_name .. "` is only vague words: what does it handle, and how?") end if #name == 1 then report(path, line, "short_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` is one letter, read far from where it is defined: name what it holds") end local has_leading_noun = false for w in take(ws, max(#ws - 2, 0)) do if not has_key(PREPOSITIONS, w) then has_leading_noun = true end end if has_leading_noun and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, last_word) and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[#ws - 1]) then report(path, line, "stacked_preposition", "`" .. full_name .. "` stacks two prepositions, `_" .. ws[#ws - 1] .. "_" .. last_word .. "`: let each read once, the entry named for what it gives (`rest`, `tail_after`) and the worker for what it adds (`rest_onto`)") end -- A function is known by its type, else by a lambda definition; a value -- by a type that is no function, else by a definition that is no -- lambda. An inferred annotation (`two : _`) with no checker's type is -- neither. local has_type = signature.known and not (is_annotation and get(def, "whole", "") == "_" and not has_key(def, "typed")) local is_lambda = get(def, "lambda", false) local is_function = signature.is_function or (not signature.known and is_lambda) local is_value = (has_type and not signature.is_function) or (not signature.known and not is_lambda) local taken_kind = get(TAKEN_WORDS, name, "") if taken_kind == "roc" and is_function then local result_parts = split(signature.result, ".") local returns_the_word = signature.is_function and result_parts[#result_parts] == camel_case({name}) if not returns_the_word then report(path, line, "taken_word", "`" .. full_name .. "` is Roc's own word, `" .. name .. "`, for a function that gives no `" .. camel_case({name}) .. "`: name it for the domain's thing (`element`, `append`), and keep Roc's words for Roc") end end if taken_kind == "cardinal" and is_value then report(path, line, "taken_word", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a number's name for a value: it says how many, not what it holds") end -- An effect so named is `state_effect`'s, and a function so named that -- gives a `Bool` is `question`'s, so this check takes the rest. if not has_bang and #ws == 1 and is_participle(name) and is_function and not returns_bool then report(path, line, "bare_participle", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a function named by a bare past participle, which reads as a `Bool`: name it by a noun for what it gives (`user_by_name`) or a verb for what it does (`add_user`)") end -- An effect is `noun_effect`'s, and a result of `_` says nothing. if not has_bang and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[1]) and is_function and not returns_bool and signature.result ~= "_" and not reads_as_maker(def, ws, signature) then local gives = signature.known and ("gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) or "has no annotation to show it makes its own type" report(path, line, "phrase_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` starts with a preposition, `" .. ws[1] .. "`, and " .. gives .. ": bare, it reads as a yes or no and hides what it gives; name the thing (`trees_in_view`, not `in_view`)") elseif signature.known then judge_list_name({path = path, line = line, name = full_name, kind = signature.is_function and "function" or "value", is_function = signature.is_function, first = signature.first, gives = signature.result}) end if not has_bang and is_function and has_key(WORLD_VERBS, ws[1]) then report(path, line, "world_verb", "`" .. full_name .. "` is pure, and `" .. ws[1] .. "` claims to act on something outside: name it for the value it gives (`tree_shapes`, not `draw_tree`)") end local argument_types = get(def, "argument_types", {}) local parameters = get(def, "parameters", {}) for k = 1, #parameters do local parameter = parameters[k] local parameter_type = k <= #argument_types and argument_types[k] or get(parameter, "typed", "") if parameter.name ~= "" then judge_list_name({path = path, line = parameter.line, name = parameter.name, kind = "parameter", is_function = false, first = "", gives = parameter_type}) end end end -- `worker_name` is judged at the definition, which knows whether it calls -- itself, and at an annotation only when no definition follows it, as -- with a hosted effect. local annotation_alone = is_annotation and not get(def, "has_def", false) local helper_suffix = has_key(HELPER_SUFFIXES, last_word) and (annotation_alone or not is_annotation) local recursion_suffix = has_key(RECURSION_SUFFIXES, last_word) and get(def, "recurses", false) if #ws > 1 and (helper_suffix or recursion_suffix) then report(path, line, "worker_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` is named only as a helper, `_" .. last_word .. "`: name the worker for the parameter it adds (`_from` a start point, `_onto` an output built, `_with` other carried state) and give the entry function the plain name") end if is_annotation and not def.fn and def.whole ~= "_" then local annotated_type = def.whole if last_word == "count" and not has_key(INTEGER_TYPES, annotated_type) then report(path, line, "name_type", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a count of type `" .. annotated_type .. "`") end if last_word == "path" and annotated_type ~= "Str" and not contains(annotated_type, "Path") then report(path, line, "name_type", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a path of type `" .. annotated_type .. "`") end if annotated_type == "Bool" and (ws[1] == "no" or ws[1] == "not") and #ws > 1 then report(path, line, "negative", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a negative flag: `" .. full_name .. " = Bool.false` reads twice") end end if is_annotation and is_effect and def.fn then for argument in arguments do local union = get(argument, "union") local ref = get(argument, "ref") if union == nil and ref ~= nil then union = get(TAG_UNION_TYPES, ref) end if union ~= nil then local shown = (get(argument, "list") and "a list of " or "") .. "`[" .. join(union.names, ", ") .. "]`" if not union.payload and #union.names >= 2 and all_tags_past(union.names) then report(path, line, "command_tense", "`" .. full_name .. "` takes " .. shown .. ", an instruction named like an event: name its tags as commands (`Pinned` is `Pin`)") end local command_tags = {} local event_tags = {} for t in union.names do local w = tag_first_word(t) if is_participle(w) then push(event_tags, t) elseif has_key(VERBS, w) then push(command_tags, t) end end if #command_tags > 0 and #event_tags > 0 then report(path, line, "mixed_tense", "`" .. full_name .. "` takes " .. shown .. ": commands (" .. join(command_tags, ", ") .. ") beside events (" .. join(event_tags, ", ") .. "): name what it is told to do in one mood") end end end end if is_annotation and #ws > 2 and ws[1] == "is" and ws[2] == "not" then report(path, line, "negative", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a negative: `!" .. full_name .. "(...)` reads twice") end return nil end local paths = glob(GLOB) if SELF_TEST then for q in glob(PLANTS .. "typed/*.roc") do push(paths, q) end end local file_count = #paths -- The self-test's untyped plants are imported by no root. const UNTYPED_PLANTS = SELF_TEST and set_of(glob(PLANTS .. "*.roc")) or {} if USE_TYPES then local got = roc_types_for_files("hunt_names", ROOT, roc_bin("hunt_names", SELF_TEST), paths, UNTYPED_PLANTS) CHECKER_TYPES.real = got.real CHECKER_TYPES.pats = got.pats CHECKER_TYPES.exprs = got.exprs CHECKER_TYPES.unreached = got.unreached end local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths) -- This loop does not `yield`, because a yield may keep only 1 MiB, and a -- large tree's definitions pass that. The arena in the header holds them. for def in read_definitions(parsed.files) do judge_definition(def) end -- `where_name` in the header. function judge_where_names(file) for n in file.nodes do if n.kind == "method" and file.nodes[n.parent].kind == "where" then local bare = ends_with(n.name, "!") and sub(n.name, 1, #n.name - 1) or n.name if #split(bare, "_") < 2 and not has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, n.name) then report(file.path, n.line, "where_name", "the `where` method `" .. n.name .. "` is one word, and a `where` clause matches by name alone: say what it is for (`scenery_height`, not `height`)") end end end return nil end for file in parsed.files do judge_where_names(file) end -- Whether a doc says whose a container word is (`a folder's entry`, `a -- listing's entries`), in the word's singular or plural. function doc_says_whose(doc, word) local forms = {word, word .. "s"} if ends_with(word, "ies") then push(forms, sub(word, 1, #word - 3) .. "y") end if ends_with(word, "y") then push(forms, sub(word, 1, #word - 1) .. "ies") end if ends_with(word, "s") then push(forms, sub(word, 1, #word - 1)) end for form in forms do if contains(doc, "'s " .. form) then return true end end return false end for named in TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES do local only_container_words = #named.words > 0 local doc_owns_it = false for w in named.words do if not has_key(VAGUE, w) and not has_key(CONTAINERS, w) then only_container_words = false end if doc_says_whose(named.doc, w) then doc_owns_it = true end end if only_container_words and not doc_owns_it then report(named.path, named.line, "container", (named.is_field and "the field `" or "the type `") .. named.name .. "` is only container words: name it for what it holds, or say whose it is in its doc (`## A folder's entry`)") end if named.is_field then judge_list_name({path = named.path, line = named.line, name = named.name, kind = "field", is_function = named.is_function, first = named.first, gives = named.gives}) end end const OPPOSITE_PAIRS = {["after|before"] = true, ["from|to"] = true, ["with|without"] = true, ["over|under"] = true} for key in sort(keys(PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM)) do local group = PREPOSITIONS_BY_STEM[key] local fewest_arguments = -1 for preposition in keys(group.prepositions) do local arity = group.prepositions[preposition].arity if arity >= 0 and (fewest_arguments < 0 or arity < fewest_arguments) then fewest_arguments = arity end end local split_names = {} local split_prepositions = {} for preposition in sort(keys(group.prepositions)) do local first_use = group.prepositions[preposition] local is_from_worker = preposition == "from" and fewest_arguments >= 0 and first_use.arity > fewest_arguments local is_convention = has_key(SUFFIX_CONVENTIONS, group.path ..
