"|" .. preposition) local is_keyword = has_item(get(DECLARED_KEYWORDS, group.path, {}), preposition) if not is_from_worker and not is_convention and not is_keyword then push(split_names, first_use.name) push(split_prepositions, preposition) end end local is_opposite_pair = #split_names == 2 and get(OPPOSITE_PAIRS, join(split_prepositions, "|"), false) if #split_names > 1 and not is_opposite_pair then report(group.path, group.line, "preposition_split", "`" .. group.stem .. "` takes " .. #split_names .. " prepositions here (" .. join(split_names, ", ") .. "): one relation keeps one preposition, or the names say how they differ") end end if CENSUS_ONLY then local rows = {} local effects_by_verdict = {} local total = 0 for w in keys(first_word_census) do local row = first_word_census[w] push(rows, row) effects_by_verdict[row.verdict] = get(effects_by_verdict, row.verdict, 0) + row.count total = total + row.count end sort(rows, {{key = "count", desc = true}, "word"}) local census_lines = {} for r in rows do push(census_lines, pad(r.count, -4) .. " " .. pad(r.word, 12) .. " " .. r.verdict) end local verdict_counts = {} for v in {"verb", "participle", "vague", "asks", "refused"} do push(verdict_counts, v .. " " .. get(effects_by_verdict, v, 0)) end print_findings("hunt_names (Roc) census: " .. file_count .. " files; " .. total .. " effects, " .. #rows .. " first words; effects by verdict: " .. join(verdict_counts, ", "), census_lines) else local check_counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(check_counts, c .. " " .. count_by_check[c]) end print_findings("hunt_names (Roc): " .. file_count .. " files; " .. join(check_counts, ", ") .. house_note("hunt_names"), finding_lines) end fail_if_refused("hunt_names", parsed.refused, CHECKER_TYPES.unreached) -- A plant's name relative to PLANTS. A typed plant is a CamelCase module -- (`typed/QuestionInferred.roc`), and its name is given in snake case -- (`question_inferred.roc`). function plant_name(path) local name = sub(path, #PLANTS + 1) if starts_with(name, "typed/") then return snake_case_plant_name(sub(name, 7)) end return name end function plant_is_for(plant, check) return plant == check .. ".roc" or starts_with(plant, check .. "_") end if SELF_TEST then -- Every plant is judged before the test fails, so one run shows each -- plant that is wrong. local wrong = {} for c in CHECKS do local planted = 0 for path in paths do local is_its_plant = plant_is_for(plant_name(path), c) if is_its_plant then planted = planted + 1 end local fired = has_key(fired_in_file, path .. "|" .. c) if is_its_plant and not fired then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. path) end if fired and not is_its_plant then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on " .. path .. ", another check's plant") end end if planted == 0 then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` has no plant") end end -- A plant named for no check could never fail. for path in paths do local plant = plant_name(path) local is_named = starts_with(plant, "quiet_") for c in CHECKS do if plant_is_for(plant, c) then is_named = true end end if not is_named then push(wrong, path .. ": a plant the table does not judge") end end for expected in {{word = "read", verdict = "verb"}, {word = "held", verdict = "participle"}, {word = "process", verdict = "vague"}, {word = "links", verdict = "refused"}} do local got = get(first_word_census, expected.word) if got == nil then push(wrong, "the census has no `" .. expected.word .. "`") elseif got.verdict ~= expected.verdict then push(wrong, "the census calls `" .. expected.word .. "` " .. got.verdict .. ", not " .. expected.verdict) end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("hunt_names self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end print("hunt_names (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none, and the census gives each verdict its known word)") end

name: cookbook/roc/member_uses.shale
html: -- How `cookbook/roc/print_module_types.shale` resolves a type's name and finds a -- type's members, and how many files use each member of the asked module's -- types. Resolving reads only files the walk has read already (`st.files`). -- -- use("cookbook:roc/member_uses.shale") -- load_files(st, paths), load_imports(st) -- parse files into `st.files` and `st.types` -- package_folders(root, given, trees), own_packages(st, tree, path) -- where a file's `import pkg.Module` reads from -- client_files(text, skip), then clients_line(st, paths, start, root_files) -- the files `clients=` names, and their apps -- clients_missing_apps(st, root, client_paths) -- the apps beside a package that `clients=` leaves out -- resolve(st, info, name) what a type name written in a file refers to -- members_of(tree, at) the annotations in a type's block -- source_text(src, ...), doc_lines_above(src, line) -- a declaration's text, and its doc -- private_signatures(st, start), public_names(st, start) -- a family member's private functions, and its -- public names with the error tags each answers -- test_context(info) where each node sits, and the values only expects use -- in_tests(fc, c) whether a node there is in tests -- test_only_imports(st, info) -- a file's imports that only its tests use -- asked_members(st, start), then count_uses(st, info, start) for each other -- file, then uses_note(rec, app_of), unused_members(st) and precision_note(st). -- Several modules may be asked at once: asked_members for each, their files -- in the set `st.asked_files`, and count_uses once a file. Each member's -- record keeps `sites`, `{path, at}` for each node that names it or calls -- it on a receiver of its type, in production or tests. -- refused_line(st), with_refused_line(lines, line) -- the files roc-ast refused, named before the counts -- -- A use is in tests when it sits in an `expect`, in a top-level value that -- only expects use (directly or through other such values), or anywhere in a -- file under a `gates/` folder, a gates-only app. -- -- A file uses a member by naming it through its import of the asked module, -- or by calling it as a method or through an operator. Roc's checker sends -- `a + b` to `a.plus(b)`, and so on for the operators in -- WALK_OPERATOR_METHODS, and a unary `-` to `negate` (src/check/Check.zig); -- `!` is always Bool's `not`. A call counts for a member of the receiver's -- type when the file makes that type plain (`expr_type`), and for no member -- of another type of the same name. A receiver it can't type counts for -- every member of the method's name, pooled, and keeps that member off the -- list of those used only in their own file. -- The source between two places, a end column being one past the last -- character, with each line after the first losing the first line's -- indentation. function source_text(src, line, col, end_line, end_col) local first = src[line] local indent = #first - #re_find(first, "^[ \t]*(.*)$").group if line == end_line then return {sub(first, col, end_col - 1)} end local out = {sub(first, col)} for l = line + 1, end_line do local text = l == end_line and sub(src[l], 1, end_col - 1) or src[l] local k = 1 while k <= indent and k <= #text and (sub(text, k, k) == "\t" or sub(text, k, k) == " ") do k = k + 1 end push(out, sub(text, k)) end return out end -- The comment lines directly above line `line`, trimmed, in order. function doc_lines_above(src, line) local out = {} local k = line - 1 while k >= 1 and starts_with(trim(src[k]), "#") do push(out, trim(src[k])) k = k - 1 end local ordered = {} for i = #out, 1, -1 do push(ordered, out[i]) end return ordered end -- The builtin types, leaves of the walk. const WALK_BUILTINS = {Str = true, List = true, Bool = true, Try = true, Box = true, Dict = true, Set = true, Iter = true, Num = true, Int = true, Frac = true, Dec = true, F32 = true, F64 = true, U8 = true, U16 = true, U32 = true, U64 = true, U128 = true, I8 = true, I16 = true, I32 = true, I64 = true, I128 = true, Utf8Problem = true} -- The kinds of node a type declaration may sit in and still be one this -- recipe reads: the top level, or a type's block. const WALK_OUTER_KINDS = {file = true, statements = true, ["s-type-decl"] = true, associated = true} -- Whether every ancestor of node `at` is a kind in WALK_OUTER_KINDS. function is_outer(tree, at) local k = tree[at].parent while k ~= 0 do if not has_key(WALK_OUTER_KINDS, tree[k].kind) then return false end k = tree[k].parent end return true end function path_join(dir, name) if dir == "" or dir == "." then return name end return dir .. "/" .. name end -- Roc's trees of the files `paths`, in order, as `roc_tree` gives them, -- parsing only those not already in `trees` and keeping them there, so walks -- that share `trees` parse a file once. function parsed_files(trees, paths) local fresh = {} for p in paths do if not has_key(trees, p) then push(fresh, p) end end if #fresh > 0 then for f in roc_tree(fresh) do trees[f.path] = f end end local out = {} for p in paths do push(out, trees[p]) end return out end -- The type declaration's name with the names of the declarations it is -- nested in: `Pigs.PigInterest`. function qualified_name(tree, at) local parts = {get(tree[tree[at].kids[1]], "name", "")} local k = tree[at].parent while k ~= 0 do if tree[k].kind == "s-type-decl" then local name = get(tree[tree[k].kids[1]], "name", "") local grown = {name} for p in parts do push(grown, p) end parts = grown end k = tree[k].parent end return join(parts, ".") end -- The packages an app's or a package's header names, from its tree, as -- `{name, raw}`, `raw` being the path written for its main file. function header_packages(tree) local out = {} for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "record-field" and n.parent ~= 0 and tree[n.parent].kind == "packages" then local raw = "" for j = i + 1, #tree do if tree[j].kind == "e-string-part" and tree[tree[j].parent].parent == i then raw = tree[j].raw end end push(out, {name = n.name, raw = raw}) end end return out end -- Whether the line `l` opens an app's or a package's header. function is_header_line(l) return starts_with(l, "app [") or starts_with(l, "app[") or l == "package" or starts_with(l, "package [") or starts_with(l, "package[") end -- Each package's folder, from the `packages=` argument `given` and the -- headers of the apps and packages directly in the folder `root`, as `{dir}` -- or `{err}`, a given one with `given` set. function package_folders(root, given, trees) local out = {} local apps = {} for p in glob(path_join(root, "*.roc")) do local header = false for l in lines(read(p)) do if is_header_line(l) then header = true end end if header then push(apps, p) end end if #apps > 0 then for f in parsed_files(trees, apps) do if f.err == "" then for pkg in header_packages(f.nodes) do local dir = path_normal(path_join(root, dirname(pkg.raw))) local found = dir == nil and {err = "`" .. pkg.name .. "` is at `" .. dirname(pkg.raw) .. "` from the root, outside it: pass packages=" .. pkg.name .. "=<folder>, such as a repos: path"} or {dir = dir} if has_key(out, pkg.name) and get(out[pkg.name], "dir", "") ~= get(found, "dir", "") then found = {err = "the apps in the root give `" .. pkg.name .. "` two folders: pass packages=" .. pkg.name .. "=<folder>"} end out[pkg.name] = found end end end end if given ~= "" then for pair in split(given, ",") do local at = find(pair, "=") if at == nil then fail("print_module_types: packages=: `" .. pair .. "` is no name=folder") end out[trim(sub(pair, 1, at - 1))] = {dir = trim(sub(pair, at + 1)), given = true} end end return out end -- The folder of each package the file at `path` reads, unless `packages=` -- names that package: from its own header, a gates app's -- `game: "../game.roc"`, else from the headers of the apps and packages in -- its folder, as a client app's module reads `import lib.Brush` through its -- folder's `main.roc`. A folder outside the root and its mounts is left out. function own_packages(st, tree, path) local dir = dirname(path) if not has_key(st.dir_packages, dir) then st.dir_packages[dir] = package_folders(dir, "", st.trees) end local found = st.dir_packages[dir] local own = {} for name in keys(found) do if has_key(found[name], "dir") then own[name] = found[name] end end for pkg in header_packages(tree) do local at = path_normal(path_join(dir, dirname(pkg.raw))) if at ~= nil then own[pkg.name] = {dir = at} end end local out = {} for name in keys(own) do if not get(get(st.packages, name, {}), "given", false) then out[name] = own[name] end end return out end -- Parses the files in `paths` not read before and records what each -- declares and imports, in `st.files` and `st.types`; a file roc-ast refuses -- goes in `st.refused` and `st.refusals`. function load_files(st, paths) local fresh = {} for p in paths do if not has_key(st.files, p) then push(fresh, p) end end if #fresh == 0 then return nil end for f in parsed_files(st.trees, fresh) do if f.err ~= "" then st.files[f.path] = {path = f.path, err = f.err} if f.err ~= "no such file" then -- roc_tree's `err` names the file first when roc-ast did. local why = starts_with(f.err, f.path .. ": ") and sub(f.err, #f.path + 3) or f.err push(st.refused, f.path .. ": " .. why) push(st.refusals, {path = f.path, why = why}) end else -- A library uses no other, so this is declared.shale's module_name, -- the file's name less `.roc`. local base = basename(f.path) local info = {path = f.path, err = "", module = sub(base, 1, #base - 4), nodes = f.nodes, src = split(read(f.path), "\n"), types = {}, imports = {}} local tree = f.nodes local own = own_packages(st, tree, f.path) for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "s-type-decl" and is_outer(tree, i) and get(tree[n.kids[1]], "name", "") ~= "" then local q = qualified_name(tree, i) local q_parts = split(q, ".") local t = {id = f.path .. "#" .. q, path = f.path, module = info.module, qualified = q, name = q_parts[#q_parts], at = i, line = n.line} push(info.types, t) st.types[t.id] = t end if n.kind == "s-import" and is_outer(tree, i) then local raw = get(n, "raw", "") local parts = split(raw, ".") local target = {} if #parts == 1 then target = {path = path_normal(path_join(dirname(f.path), raw .. ".roc"))} else local pkg = has_key(own, parts[1]) and own[parts[1]] or get(st.packages, parts[1], {err = "no app in the root names the package `" .. parts[1] .. "`: pass packages=" .. parts[1] .. "=<folder>"}) if has_key(pkg, "err") then target = {err = pkg.err} else target = {path = path_join(pkg.dir, join(drop(parts, 1), "/") .. ".roc")} end end info.imports[parts[#parts]] = target end end st.files[f.path] = info end end return nil end -- Reads every file the files read import, and theirs, so a receiver's type -- resolves when the uses are counted. function load_imports(st) local more = true while more do local found = {} for p in keys(st.files) do local imports = get(st.files[p], "imports", {}) for name in keys(imports) do local q = get(imports[name], "path", "") if q ~= "" and not has_key(st.files, q) then found[q] = true end end end load_files(st, sort(keys(found))) more = #keys(found) > 0 end return nil end -- Stops a walk whose `root=`, `module=` or `clients=` climbs with `..`, -- which no path may, naming the forms that reach a package from outside it. function refuse_climbing(root, module, clients) for pair in {{"root", root}, {"module", module}, {"clients", clients}} do if contains(pair[2], "..") then fail("print_module_types: " .. pair[1] .. "=" .. pair[2] .. " climbs with `..`, which no path may. Walk a package from outside it with root= as a mount path, root=repos:roc-apps/canvas_apps/lib module=Brush, or from its parent folder, root=lib, and name the apps that use it with clients=, such as clients=repos:roc-apps/canvas_apps/*") end end return nil end -- The client files `clients=`'s text names, comma separated, as `{paths, -- app_of}`: an entry ending in `.roc` is a glob of files, and any other is a -- folder or a glob of folders, `repos:roc-apps/canvas_apps/*`, whose `.roc` -- files at any depth are read. A file's app is the folder its entry names, -- or for a `.roc` glob the file's own folder. The files in the set `skip`, -- the root's, are left out. An entry that names no file stops the walk. function client_files(text, skip) local paths = {} local app_of = {} for part in split(text, ",") do local entry = trim(part) while ends_with(entry, "/") do entry = sub(entry, 1, #entry - 1) end if entry ~= "" then local is_file = ends_with(entry, ".roc") local found = glob(is_file and entry or entry .. "/**/*.roc") if #found == 0 then fail("print_module_types: clients=: `" .. entry .. "` names no .roc file") end local depth = #split(entry, "/") for p in found do local q = path_normal(p) if not has_key(skip, q) and not has_key(app_of, q) then push(paths, q) app_of[q] = is_file and dirname(q) or join(take(split(q, "/"), depth), "/") end end end end return {paths = sort(paths), app_of = app_of} end -- The app folders beside the folder `root` that name it as a package in a -- header directly in them, sorted: `safari` beside `lib`, whose `main.roc` -- says `lib: "../lib/main.roc"`. None when `root` is `.`, whose parent no -- path may reach. function apps_beside(root, trees) local here = path_normal(root) if here == nil or here == "." or here == "" then return {} end local headers = {} for p in glob(path_join(dirname(here), "*/*.roc")) do local q = path_normal(p) if dirname(q) ~= here then local header = false for l in lines(read(q)) do if is_header_line(l) then header = true end end if header then push(headers, q) end end end local apps = {} if #headers > 0 then for f in parsed_files(trees, headers) do if f.err == "" then for pkg in header_packages(f.nodes) do if path_normal(path_join(dirname(f.path), dirname(pkg.raw))) == here then apps[dirname(f.path)] = true end end end end end return sort(keys(apps)) end -- The lost entry when an app beside the package folder `root` that uses it -- holds none of the client files `client_paths`, else nil. Its uses would go -- uncounted, and a member only it uses would read as unused, as when -- `clients=*_widget` leaves out every app that is no widget. function clients_missing_apps(st, root, client_paths) local missed = {} for app in apps_beside(root, st.trees) do local covered = false for p in client_paths do if starts_with(p, app .. "/") then covered = true end end if not covered then push(missed, app) end end if #missed == 0 then return nil end return "clients=: the apps beside " .. path_normal(root) .. " that use it as a package and hold no client file, whose uses are not counted: " .. join(missed, ", ") .. "; name every app that uses it, as clients=" .. path_join(dirname(path_normal(root)), "*") end function plural(n, word) return n .. " " .. word .. (n == 1 and "" or "s") end -- The clients' header line, after their files are read: how many files in -- how many apps, and how many of them import the asked file `start`, which -- may be none. When no client imports any of the root's files, the set -- `root_files`, a lost entry says so, since paths are compared as written and -- then the root and the clients are named by paths of two kinds. function clients_line(st, paths, start, root_files) local apps = {} local importing = 0 local into_root = false for p in paths do apps[st.app_of[p]] = true local imports = get(st.files[p], "imports", {}) local hit = false for name in keys(imports) do local q = get(imports[name], "path", "") if q == start then hit = true end if has_key(root_files, q) then into_root = true end end if hit then importing = importing + 1 end end if not into_root then push(st.lost, "clients=: none of the " .. #paths .. " client files imports any of the root's files, such as " .. start .. "; name root= and clients= alike, both as mount paths or both from one folder") end return "# Clients: " .. plural(#paths, "file") .. " in " .. plural(#keys(apps), "app") .. ", " .. importing .. " importing " .. start end -- The type in `info` whose name is `q` exactly, else nil. function type_named(info, q) for t in info.types do if t.qualified == q then return t end end return nil end -- What `name` is in the imported module `target`, whose own type `rest` may -- be when `name` is qualified by the module's name. function resolve_in_module(st, target, name, rest) if has_key(target, "err") then return {kind = "lost", why = target.err} end if not has_key(st.files, target.path) then return {kind = "need", path = target.path} end local file = st.files[target.path] if file.err == "no such file" then return {kind = "lost", why = "no file " .. target.path} end if file.err ~= "" then return {kind = "lost", why = target.path .. " doesn't parse"} end local t = type_named(file, name) or type_named(file, rest) if t ~= nil then return {kind = "type", id = t.id} end return {kind = "lost", why = "no type `" .. name .. "` in " .. target.path} end -- What the type name `name`, written in the file `info`, refers to: -- `{kind = "type", id}`, `{kind = "leaf"}`, `{kind = "need", path}` when the -- file that says is not read yet, or `{kind = "lost", why}`. function resolve(st, info, name) local parts = split(name, ".") if #parts == 1 then local here = {} for t in info.types do if t.name == name then push(here, t) end end if #here == 1 then return {kind = "type", id = here[1].id} end if #here > 1 then local top = type_named(info, name) or type_named(info, info.module .. "." .. name) if top ~= nil then return {kind = "type", id = top.id} end return {kind = "lost", why = #here .. " types of this name in the file"} end if has_key(info.imports, name) then return resolve_in_module(st, info.imports[name], name, name) end if has_key(WALK_BUILTINS, name) then return {kind = "leaf"} end return {kind = "lost", why = "no type of this name in the file, no import of it, and no builtin"} end local head = parts[1] local rest = join(drop(parts, 1), ".") if head == info.module then local t = type_named(info, name) or type_named(info, rest) if t ~= nil then return {kind = "type", id = t.id} end return {kind = "lost", why = "no type `" .. name .. "` in its own module"} end if has_key(info.imports, head) then return resolve_in_module(st, info.imports[head], name, rest) end if has_key(WALK_BUILTINS, head) then return {kind = "leaf"} end return {kind = "lost", why = "`" .. head .. "` is no imported module"} end -- The annotations in the type's own block, in source order, as `{at, -- constant}`: `at` is the annotation's node, and `constant` is true when its -- type is not written as a function. An annotation whose whole type is `_` -- says nothing about the type's surface, so it is left out. function members_of(tree, at) local out = {} for k in tree[at].kids do if tree[k].kind == "associated" then for m in tree[k].kids do if tree[m].kind == "s-type-anno" and #tree[m].kids > 0 then local kind = tree[tree[m].kids[1]].kind if kind ~= "_" then push(out, {at = m, constant = kind ~= "ty-fn"}) end end end end end return out end -- The member each binary operator calls on its left operand. const WALK_OPERATOR_METHODS = {["+"] = "plus", ["-"] = "minus", ["*"] = "times", ["/"] = "div_by", ["//"] = "div_trunc_by", ["%"] = "rem_by", ["<"] = "is_lt", ["<="] = "is_lte", [">"] = "is_gt", [">="] = "is_gte", ["=="] = "is_eq", ["!="] = "is_eq"} -- The operators' members whose two operands have one type, so the right -- operand's type is the left's. const WALK_SAME_SIDES = {is_lt = true, is_lte = true, is_gt = true, is_gte = true, is_eq = true} -- Whether the file at `path` is a gates-only app, under a `gates/` folder. function is_gates(path) return contains("/" .. path, "/gates/") end -- The value the node `i` names: an identifier's name, or a punned record -- field's, as `still_shapes` in `{ still_shapes }`, which roc-ast keeps as a -- `field` with no identifier under it (check_boundaries.shale reads it so too). -- Any other node names none, "". function value_named(tree, i) local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "e-ident" then return get(n, "raw", "") end if n.kind == "field" and #n.kids == 0 and n.parent ~= 0 and tree[n.parent].kind == "e-record" then return get(n, "field", "") end return "" end -- Where each node of the file `info` (`{path, nodes}`) sits, as `{ctx, -- test_values, gates}`: `ctx[i]` is `expect` inside an `expect`, -- `value:<name>` inside the definition of a top-level value, `block` inside a -- type's block, and `none` elsewhere. `test_values` is the set of top-level -- values that only expects use, directly or through other such values; a -- value nothing uses is not one. A parent comes before its children in the -- tree. function test_context(info) local tree = info.nodes local ctx = {} local tops = {} for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] local up = n.parent == 0 and "none" or ctx[n.parent] local c = up if n.kind == "s-expect" then c = "expect" elseif n.kind == "associated" then c = "block" elseif n.kind == "s-decl" and up == "none" and #n.kids > 0 and tree[n.kids[1]].kind == "p-ident" then local name = get(tree[n.kids[1]], "raw", "") c = "value:" .. name tops[name] = true end push(ctx, c) end local refs = {} for i = 1, #tree do local raw = value_named(tree, i) if has_key(tops, raw) and ctx[i] ~= "value:" .. raw then push_at(refs, raw, ctx[i]) end end local test_values = {} local changed = true while changed do changed = false for name in sort(keys(refs)) do if not has_key(test_values, name) then local all = true for c in refs[name] do if not (c == "expect" or (starts_with(c, "value:") and has_key(test_values, sub(c, 7)))) then all = false end end if all then test_values[name] = true changed = true end end end end return {ctx = ctx, test_values = test_values, gates = is_gates(info.path)} end -- Whether a node whose context is `c`, in a file whose `test_context` is -- `fc`, is in tests: in a gates app, an `expect`, or a value only expects -- use. function in_tests(fc, c) return fc.gates or c == "expect" or (starts_with(c, "value:") and has_key(fc.test_values, sub(c, 7))) end -- The file `info`'s `test_context`, worked out once a walk. function file_context(st, info) if not has_key(st.contexts, info.path) then st.contexts[info.path] = test_context(info) end return st.contexts[info.path] end -- The imports of the file `info` that only its tests use, sorted, by the name -- the file uses each by (its alias, else its last part). A use is a name -- (a punned field's among them), tag or type whose first part is that name -- or one the import exposes; it is -- a test's by `in_tests`, or inside the annotation of a top-level value only -- expects use. A type's block is production, as other files may call its -- members. A gates app's are all tests, so it has none. function test_only_imports(st, info) local tree = info.nodes local fc = file_context(st, info) if fc.gates then return {} end local owner = {} for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "s-import" and is_outer(tree, i) then local parts = split(get(n, "raw", ""), ".") local name = get(n, "alias", parts[#parts]) owner[name] = name for k in n.kids do if tree[k].kind == "exposing" then for e in tree[k].kids do if tree[e].kind == "exposed-upper-ident" then owner[get(tree[e], "text", "")] = name end if tree[e].kind == "exposed-lower-ident" then for t in tree[e].kids do owner[get(tree[t], "value", "")] = name end end end end end end end local test_anno = {} local used = {} for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] local c = fc.ctx[i] if (n.parent ~= 0 and has_key(test_anno, tostring(n.parent))) or (n.kind == "s-type-anno" and c == "none" and has_key(fc.test_values, get(n, "name", ""))) then test_anno[tostring(i)] = true end local name = value_named(tree, i) if n.kind == "e-tag" then name = get(n, "raw", "") end if n.kind == "ty" then name = get(n, "name", "") end -- roc-ast keeps only `.Red` of a pattern's `Color.Red`, so the source says. if n.kind == "p-tag" then name = get(n, "raw", "") local m = starts_with(name, ".") and re_find(sub(info.src[n.line], n.col), "^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)") or nil if m ~= nil then name = m.group end end local head = split(name, ".")[1] if name ~= "" and has_key(owner, head) then local side = (has_key(test_anno, tostring(i)) or in_tests(fc, c)) and "test" or "production" if get(used, owner[head], "") ~= "production" then used[owner[head]] = side end end end local out = {} for name in sort(keys(used)) do if used[name] == "test" then push(out, name) end end return out end -- What the file `info` binds where, worked out once a walk, for `expr_type`: -- `scope[i]`, the top-level definition or `expect` node `i` sits in (0 -- outside any); `binds`, the names each of those binds, by `<scope>\t<name>`, -- not counting the definition's own name; `annos`, the annotations at the top -- level or in a type's block by name, and `beside` the same by the node they -- sit in and name, `<parent>\t<name>`; and `decls`, how many definitions -- there bind each name. function typing_context(st, info) if has_key(st.typing, info.path) then return st.typing[info.path] end local tree = info.nodes local scope = {} local cx = {scope = scope, binds = {}, annos = {}, beside = {}, decls = {}} for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] local p = n.parent local s = p == 0 and 0 or scope[p] local k = n.kind if s == 0 and (k == "s-decl" or k == "s-expect") and is_outer(tree, i) then s = i end push(scope, s) if k == "p-ident" and s ~= 0 then if p == s and tree[s].kids[1] == i then if tree[s].kind == "s-decl" then incr(cx.decls, get(n, "raw", "")) end else push_at(cx.binds, s .. "\t" .. get(n, "raw", ""), i) end end if k == "s-type-anno" and s == 0 and is_outer(tree, i) then push_at(cx.annos, get(n, "name", ""), i) push_at(cx.beside, p .. "\t" .. get(n, "name", ""), i) end end st.typing[info.path] = cx return cx end -- `resolve_type`'s work, which that function keeps by file and name. function resolve_alias(st, info, name) local here = info local want = name for step = 1, 8 do local r = resolve(st, here, want) if r.kind == "leaf" then return "leaf" end if r.kind ~= "type" then return nil end local t = st.types[r.id] local file = st.files[t.path] local kids = file.nodes[t.at].kids if #kids < 2 or file.nodes[kids[2]].kind ~= "ty" then return r.id end local head = file.nodes[kids[1]] if contains(sub(file.src[head.end_line], head.end_col, head.end_col + 3), "::") then return r.id end here = file want = get(file.nodes[kids[2]], "name", "") end return nil end -- What the type name `name`, written in the file `info`, is, an alias -- (`Across : Width`) followed to the type it names: a type's id, `leaf` for a -- builtin, or nil when it can't be told, as when its file isn't read. function resolve_type(st, info, name) local key = info.path .. "\t" .. name if not has_key(st.resolved, key) then st.resolved[key] = resolve_alias(st, info, name) or false end return st.resolved[key] or nil end -- The type a type annotation's node `at` in the file `info` names, as -- `resolve_type` gives it: a name, or an applied name by its head. Any other -- form (a record, a function, a type variable) is nil. function anno_type(st, info, at) local n = info.nodes[at] local name = "" if n.kind == "ty" then name = get(n, "name", "") end if n.kind == "ty-apply" then name = get(info.nodes[n.kids[1]], "name", "") end if name == "" then return nil end return resolve_type(st, info, name) end -- The type of a value the annotation `anno` in the file `info` declares: what -- a call of it gives when `applied`, else the constant's own type. function anno_value_type(st, info, anno, applied) local at = info.nodes[anno].kids[1] local ty = info.nodes[at] if applied then if ty.kind ~= "ty-fn" then return nil end return anno_type(st, info, ty.kids[#ty.kids]) end if ty.kind == "ty-fn" then return nil end return anno_type(st, info, at) end -- The member `name` of the type `id`, as `{info, at}`, its file and its -- annotation, else nil. function member_anno(st, id, name) local t = st.types[id] local info = st.files[t.path] for member in members_of(info.nodes, t.at) do if get(info.nodes[member.at], "name", "") == name then return {info = info, at = member.at} end end return nil end -- The type of the qualified value `raw`, `Pixels.zero` or `Distance.metres` -- when `applied`, written in the file `info`: from its member's annotation. function qualified_type(st, info, raw, applied) local parts = split(raw, ".") local id = resolve_type(st, info, join(take(parts, #parts - 1), ".")) if id == nil or id == "leaf" then return nil end local m = member_anno(st, id, parts[#parts]) if m == nil then return nil end return anno_value_type(st, m.info, m.at, applied) end -- The type of the bare value `raw` that no definition binds locally, from -- the file's one annotation and definition of that name, else nil. function top_value_type(st, info, cx, raw, applied) local annos = get(cx.annos, raw, {}) if #annos ~= 1 or get(cx.decls, raw, 0) > 1 then return nil end return anno_value_type(st, info, annos[1], applied) end -- The type of the field `field` of the record type `id`, else nil. function field_type(st, id, field) local t = st.types[id] local info = st.files[t.path] local kids = info.nodes[t.at].kids if #kids < 2 or info.nodes[kids[2]].kind ~= "ty-record" then return nil end for k in info.nodes[kids[2]].kids do if get(info.nodes[k], "name", "") == field then return anno_type(st, info, info.nodes[k].kids[1]) end end return nil end -- The type the nominal pattern `Pixels.(p)`, its node `at`, gives `p`: the -- type the nominal type is over, else nil. A tag's pattern, `Ok(p)`, is nil. function backing_type(st, info, at) local n = info.nodes[at] local raw = get(n, "raw", "") if #n.kids ~= 1 or sub(info.src[n.line], n.col + #raw, n.col + #raw + 1) ~= ".(" then return nil end local id = resolve_type(st, info, raw) if id == nil or id == "leaf" then return nil end local t = st.types[id] local file = st.files[t.path] local kids = file.nodes[t.at].kids local head = file.nodes[kids[1]] if #kids < 2 or not contains(sub(file.src[head.end_line], head.end_col, head.end_col + 3), "::") then return nil end return anno_type(st, file, kids[2]) end -- The type of the parameter `p`, in the lambda's `args` node `args`, of the -- definition `s`, from the definition's annotation beside it, else nil. function param_type(st, info, cx, s, args, p) local tree = info.nodes local found = get(cx.beside, tree[s].parent .. "\t" .. get(tree[tree[s].kids[1]], "raw", ""), {}) if #found ~= 1 then return nil end local ty = tree[tree[found[1]].kids[1]] local params = tree[args].kids if ty.kind ~= "ty-fn" or #ty.kids - 1 ~= #params then return nil end for k = 1, #params do if params[k] == p then return anno_type(st, info, ty.kids[k]) end end return nil end -- The type of the expression at node `at` in the file `info` (whose -- `typing_context` is `cx`), where the file makes it plain, as a type's id, -- `leaf` for a builtin, or nil. It is plain for a parameter of a definition -- whose annotation gives its type, a local or top-level value bound once in -- reach, a qualified constant or call (`Pixels.zero`, `Distance.metres(2)`), -- a call of a top-level annotated function, a field of a value of a record -- type, a method call on a value of a known type, by the method's -- annotation, and the value a nominal pattern `Pixels.(p)` unwraps. A name -- bound twice in a definition, or a `$` variable, is nil. function expr_type(st, info, cx, at, depth) if depth > 12 then return nil end local tree = info.nodes local n = tree[at] if n.kind == "e-tuple" and #n.kids == 1 then return expr_type(st, info, cx, n.kids[1], depth + 1) end if n.kind == "e-apply" or n.kind == "e-ident" then local applied = n.kind == "e-apply" local f = applied and tree[n.kids[1]] or n if f.kind ~= "e-ident" then return nil end local raw = get(f, "raw", "") if contains(raw, ".") then return qualified_type(st, info, raw, applied) end if starts_with(raw, "$") then return nil end local binds = get(cx.binds, cx.scope[at] .. "\t" .. raw, {}) if #binds == 0 then return top_value_type(st, info, cx, raw, applied) end if #binds > 1 or applied then return nil end local p = binds[1] local up = tree[tree[p].parent] if up.kind == "s-decl" and up.kids[1] == p then return expr_type(st, info, cx, up.kids[2], depth + 1) end if up.kind == "p-tag" then return backing_type(st, info, tree[p].parent) end local s = cx.scope[at] if up.kind == "args" and tree[s].kind == "s-decl" and tree[s].kids[2] == up.parent then return param_type(st, info, cx, s, tree[p].parent, p) end return nil end if n.kind == "e-method-call" then local recv = expr_type(st, info, cx, tree[n.kids[1]].kids[1], depth + 1) if recv == nil or recv == "leaf" then return nil end local name = get(n, "method", "") if starts_with(name, ".") then name = sub(name, 2) end local m = member_anno(st, recv, name) if m == nil then return nil end return anno_value_type(st, m.info, m.at, true) end if n.kind == "e-field-access" then local ty = expr_type(st, info, cx, tree[n.kids[1]].kids[1], depth + 1) for k in drop(n.kids, 1) do if ty == nil or ty == "leaf" then return nil end ty = field_type(st, ty, get(tree[k], "field", "")) end return ty end return nil end -- Records each member of the asked module's types, to count its outside -- uses: `st.member_rec` by type id and name, and `st.members_by_name`. function asked_members(st, start) local info = st.files[start] for t in info.types do for member in members_of(info.nodes, t.at) do local name = get(info.nodes[member.at], "name", "") local label = name if starts_with(t.qualified, t.module .. ".") then label = sub(t.qualified, #t.module + 2) .. "." .. name end if t.qualified ~= t.module and not starts_with(t.qualified, t.module .. ".") then label = t.qualified .. "." .. name end local rec = {label = label, line = info.nodes[member.at].line, prod = {}, test = {}, method_prod = {}, method_test = {}, op_prod = {}, op_test = {}, sites = {}} st.member_rec[t.id .. "\t" .. name] = rec push(st.member_list, rec) push_at(st.members_by_name, name, rec) end end return nil end -- The member a dotted name such as `Geom.AheadPoint.at_height`, split into -- `parts`, names in the asked file `start`, or nil: the type is the parts -- before the last, with the module's name or without it. function member_named(st, start, parts) local n = #parts if n < 2 then return nil end local type_parts = take(parts, n - 1) local candidates = {join(type_parts, ".")} if n > 2 then push(candidates, join(drop(type_parts, 1), ".")) end for q in candidates do local t = type_named(st.files[start], q) if t ~= nil and has_key(st.member_rec, t.id .. "\t" .. parts[n]) then return st.member_rec[t.id .. "\t" .. parts[n]] end end return nil end -- Counts one call of the member `name`, by a method or (`kind` `op`) an -- operator, in the file `path`, on a receiver of the type `ty`: for that -- type's member when it is one of the asked module's, for every member of -- the name, pooled, when `ty` is nil, and for none otherwise. function count_call(st, path, test, name, ty, kind, at) if ty == nil then incr(st.precision, kind .. "_pooled") for rec in st.members_by_name[name] do local into = test and rec[kind .. "_test"] or rec[kind .. "_prod"] into[path] = true end return nil end incr(st.precision, kind .. "_typed") local key = ty .. "\t" .. name if has_key(st.asked, ty) and has_key(st.member_rec, key) then local rec = st.member_rec[key] if test then rec.test[path] = true else rec.prod[path] = true end push(rec.sites, {path = path, at = at}) end return nil end -- Counts the file `info`'s uses of the asked modules' members: names through -- its import of the asked file `start` or of a file in `st.asked_files`, -- method calls, and operators. function count_uses(st, info, start) local fc = file_context(st, info) local cx = typing_context(st, info) local tree = info.nodes local asked_files = get(st, "asked_files", {}) for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "e-ident" then local parts = split(get(n, "raw", ""), ".") local target = #parts > 1 and get(get(info.imports, parts[1], {}), "path", "") or "" if target ~= "" and (target == start or has_key(asked_files, target)) then local rec = member_named(st, target, parts) if rec ~= nil then if in_tests(fc, fc.ctx[i]) then rec.test[info.path] = true else rec.prod[info.path] = true end push(rec.sites, {path = info.path, at = i}) end end elseif n.kind == "e-method-call" then local name = get(n, "method", "") if starts_with(name, ".") then name = sub(name, 2) end if has_key(st.members_by_name, name) then count_call(st, info.path, in_tests(fc, fc.ctx[i]), name, expr_type(st, info, cx, tree[n.kids[1]].kids[1], 0), "method", i) end elseif n.kind == "e-binop" or (n.kind == "unary" and get(n, "value", "") == "-") then local name = n.kind == "unary" and "negate" or get(WALK_OPERATOR_METHODS, get(n, "op", ""), "") if has_key(st.members_by_name, name) then local ty = expr_type(st, info, cx, n.kids[1], 0) if ty == nil and has_key(WALK_SAME_SIDES, name) then ty = expr_type(st, info, cx, n.kids[2], 0) end count_call(st, info.path, in_tests(fc, fc.ctx[i]), name, ty, "op", i) end end end return nil end -- How many files of `set`, a set of paths, are not in `seen`, and how many of -- those are not in `prod` either, so only tests use the member there; each -- is then added to `seen`. function fresh_files(seen, set, prod) local files = 0 local in_tests = 0 for p in sort(keys(set)) do if not has_key(seen, p) then files = files + 1 if not has_key(prod, p) then in_tests = in_tests + 1 end end end for p in keys(set) do seen[p] = true end return {files = files, in_tests = in_tests} end -- A member's outside uses as `{named, method, op}`, each `{files, -- in_tests}`, from its record's sets of files: those that name it or call it -- on a receiver of its type, then those of the rest that call a method of -- its name on a receiver of no known type, then those of the rest that apply -- its operator so. function uses_of(rec) local seen = {} local named = {} for p in keys(rec.prod) do named[p] = true end for p in keys(rec.test) do named[p] = true end local out = {named = fresh_files(seen, named, rec.prod)} local called = {} for p in keys(rec.method_prod) do called[p] = true end for p in keys(rec.method_test) do called[p] = true end out.method = fresh_files(seen, called, rec.method_prod) local applied = {} for p in keys(rec.op_prod) do applied[p] = true end for p in keys(rec.op_test) do applied[p] = true end out.op = fresh_files(seen, applied, rec.op_prod) return out end -- Whether no other file uses the member, by name, by a typed call, or by a -- call its name or operator might be. function is_unused(rec) local u = uses_of(rec) return u.named.files == 0 and u.method.files == 0 and u.op.files == 0 end -- How many client apps, by `app_of`, hold a file that names the member of -- the record `rec` or calls it on a receiver of its type. function apps_using(rec, app_of) local apps = {} for p in keys(rec.prod) do if has_key(app_of, p) then apps[app_of[p]] = true end end for p in keys(rec.test) do if has_key(app_of, p) then apps[app_of[p]] = true end end return #keys(apps) end -- What a claim of no use adds when a file was refused, whose uses the walk -- can't see. const AS_FAR_AS_PARSED = "as far as the parsed files show" -- The note after a member's annotation: `used by 3 files, 1 in tests only; -- by method name in 2 more; by operator, untyped, in 1 more`. When the files -- that name it or call it typed lie in several client apps, by `app_of`, the -- first part says how many: `used by 9 files in 5 apps`. With `partial`, -- some file was refused and its uses are unknown, so a member with none says -- `no outside use, as far as the parsed files show`. function uses_note(rec, app_of, partial?) local u = uses_of(rec) local apps = apps_using(rec, app_of) if apps > 1 then u.named.apps = apps end local parts = {} local kinds = {{u.named, "used by ", ""}, {u.method, "by method name in ", "used by method name only, in "}, {u.op, "by operator, untyped, in ", "used by operator only, untyped, in "}} for k in kinds do local c = k[1] if c.files > 0 then local text = k[2] .. plural(c.files, "file") if #parts > 0 then text = k[2] .. c.files .. " more" elseif k[3] ~= "" then text = k[3] .. plural(c.files, "file") end if has_key(c, "apps") then text = text .. " in " .. c.apps .. " apps" end if c.in_tests > 0 then text = text .. ", " .. c.in_tests .. " in tests only" end push(parts, text) end end if #parts == 0 then return partial == true and "no outside use, " .. AS_FAR_AS_PARSED or "no outside use" end return join(parts, "; ") end -- The labels of the asked module's members no other file uses, in file -- order. function unused_members(st) local out = {} for rec in st.member_list do if is_unused(rec) then push(out, rec.label) end end return out end -- The walk's second line when roc-ast refused files, each named with its -- reason's first clause, `# Refused by roc-ast, so their uses and mentions -- are not counted: Scene.roc (52 parse problem(s))`. A refused file's uses -- are unread, so the counts line ends by naming it too, and a member with -- none says `no outside use, as far as the parsed files show`, as does the -- line of members used only in this file. function refused_line(st) local named = {} for r in st.refusals do local cut = find(r.why, ": ") push(named, r.path .. " (" .. (cut == nil and r.why or sub(r.why, 1, cut - 1)) .. ")") end return "# Refused by roc-ast, so their uses and mentions are not counted: " .. join(sort(named), "; ") end -- The walk's lines `lines` with `line` second, under the title, where a -- reader meets it before any count it qualifies. function with_refused_line(lines, line) local out = {lines[1], line} for l in drop(lines, 1) do push(out, l) end return out end -- The counts line's note of how many method calls and operators of the -- asked members' names had a receiver typed, and how many were pooled. function precision_note(st) local p = st.precision return ", method calls " .. get(p, "method_typed", 0) .. " typed and " .. get(p, "method_pooled", 0) .. " pooled, operators " .. get(p, "op_typed", 0) .. " typed and " .. get(p, "op_pooled", 0) .. " pooled" end -- The private top-level functions of the asked file `start`, in source -- order, each its doc and its annotation, marked `# private`, or `# private; -- tests only` when only expects use it; with their count. function private_signatures(st, start) local info = st.files[start] local tree = info.nodes local fc = file_context(st, info) local out = {} local count = 0 for i = 1, #tree do local n = tree[i] if n.kind == "s-type-anno" and #n.kids > 0 and tree[n.kids[1]].kind == "ty-fn" and is_outer(tree, i) and tree[n.parent].kind ~= "associated" then count = count + 1 push(out, "") for l in doc_lines_above(info.src, n.line) do push(out, l) end local anno = source_text(info.src, n.line, n.col, n.end_line, n.end_col) local test = fc.gates or has_key(fc.test_values, get(n, "name", "")) anno[#anno] = anno[#anno] .. (test and " # private; tests only" or " # private") for l in anno do push(out, l) end end end return {lines = out, count = count} end -- The error tags the annotation `anno` answers, sorted, as `[A, B]`: those of -- the `Try` its function returns, or its constant's type is. A `Try` whose -- error is not written as tags gives that type's text; no `Try` gives "". function error_tags(info, anno) local tree = info.nodes local top = tree[anno].kids[1] local result = tree[top].kind == "ty-fn" and tree[top].kids[#tree[top].kids] or top local r = tree[result] if r.kind ~= "ty-apply" or #r.kids < 3 or get(tree[r.kids[1]], "name", "") ~= "Try" then return "" end local u = tree[r.kids[3]] if u.kind ~= "ty-tag-union" then return join(source_text(info.src, u.line, u.col, u.end_line, u.end_col), " ") end local names = {} for k in u.kids do if tree[k].kind == "tags" then for g in tree[k].kids do local tag = tree[g].kind == "ty-apply" and tree[tree[g].kids[1]] or tree[g] push(names, get(tag, "name", "?")) end end end return "[" .. join(sort(names), ", ") .. "]" end -- The public names of the asked file `start`, its types' members in source -- order, as `{name, label, errors}`, a nested type's member labelled with its -- type. function public_names(st, start) local info = st.files[start] local out = {} for t in info.types do for member in members_of(info.nodes, t.at) do local name = get(info.nodes[member.at], "name", "") local label = name if t.qualified ~= t.module then label = (starts_with(t.qualified, t.module .. ".") and sub(t.qualified, #t.module + 2) or t.qualified) .. "." .. name end push(out, {name = name, label = label, errors = error_tags(info, member.at)}) end end return out end

name: cookbook/roc/module_family.shale
html: -- How `cookbook/roc/print_module_types.shale` walks several sibling modules as one -- family, `modules=TreeSighting,RailSighting,...`, for a review that reads -- them together. -- -- use("cookbook:roc/module_family.shale") -- parse_modules(text) the family's modules from `modules=` -- printing_order(st) a walk's types, the most primitive first -- family_order(runs, ids, asked), family_table(names, entries) -- the pieces of print_module_types.shale's `family_walk` -- check, has_line, has_text, headers_of, and family_checks(failures, r, at) -- the self-test's, the last on the plant family -- `cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/family/` -- refused_checks(failures, rf, clean, at) -- the self-test's on the plant -- `cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/refused/` -- -- Each member is walked as `module=` walks it, with the same settings, and the -- output is pooled: -- -- 1. One header: the builtin leaves, stopped, beyond-depth and brief types -- and type variables of every member's walk together. -- 2. The shared types: those two or more members' closures reach, at the -- usual depth rules, printed once, the most primitive first, each with a -- `# shared by` line. A member's own types are never shared; they print -- in its block. -- 3. Each member's block, in the order `modules=` gives: its walk's -- import lines, unused-members and clients lines, the types only -- its closure reaches, its own types with their public members' -- signatures and outside uses, then its private top-level functions' -- signatures in source order, each marked `# private` (`# private; -- tests only` for one only expects use), then its "named by" section, -- and its walk's counts line. The uses and named-by sections are per -- member: they are about one module's surface, and pooled they would -- repeat an annotation that names two siblings. -- 4. The family table: the members' public names grouped by shape, a row -- per shape and a line per member in each row, `-` where a member has no -- name of that shape, and after each name the error tags its `Try` -- result answers, sorted. A name whose error set differs from the row's -- most common one is marked `<- errors differ`. -- -- The shape rule: a name's words are split at `_`. Its suffix shape is the -- name with its first word, the noun, made `*` (`trees_in_view` is -- `*_in_view`), and its prefix shape is the first word and `*` -- (`segment_sightings` is `segment_*`); a one-word name is its own shape. A -- suffix shape that names of two or more members have is a row; then a -- prefix shape, among the names left; the names left after both are listed -- per member as unmatched. -- A walk's type `id`'s key for ordering: the asked module's types last, -- then by module, name and path. function sort_key(st, id) local t = st.types[id] return (has_key(st.asked, id) and "1" or "0") .. t.module .. "\t" .. t.qualified .. "\t" .. t.path end -- Tarjan's strongly connected components over `st.deps`. function strong_connect(st, g, v) g.index[v] = g.counter g.low[v] = g.counter g.counter = g.counter + 1 push(g.stack, v) g.on[v] = true for w in get(st.deps, v, {}) do if not has_key(g.index, w) then strong_connect(st, g, w) if g.low[w] < g.low[v] then g.low[v] = g.low[w] end elseif get(g.on, w, false) then if g.index[w] < g.low[v] then g.low[v] = g.index[w] end end end if g.low[v] == g.index[v] then local members = {} local done = false while not done do local w = g.stack[#g.stack] g.stack = take(g.stack, #g.stack - 1) g.on[w] = false push(members, w) done = w == v end push(g.components, members) end return nil end -- The id with the smallest sort key among `ids` that `is_ready` allows. function smallest_ready(st, ids, is_ready) local best = nil local best_key = "" for id in ids do if is_ready[id] then local key = sort_key(st, id) if best == nil or key < best_key then best = id best_key = key end end end return best end -- A cycle's members, each after the members its definition mentions where -- that orders them, else by sort key. function order_in_cycle(st, members) local inside = set_of(members) local placed = {} local out = {} while #out < #members do local ready = {} local any = false for id in members do local ok = not has_key(placed, id) if ok then for w in get(st.def_deps, id, {}) do if has_key(inside, w) and not has_key(placed, w) then ok = false end end end ready[id] = ok if ok then any = true end end if not any then for id in members do ready[id] = not has_key(placed, id) end end local pick = smallest_ready(st, members, ready) placed[pick] = true push(out, pick) end return out end -- Every type read, in printing order, as `{id, cycle}` items, where an item -- with `cycle` set is a cycle's report line, with its members. function printing_order(st) local ids = sort(keys(st.visited)) local g = {index = {}, low = {}, counter = 1, stack = {}, on = {}, components = {}} for id in ids do if not has_key(g.index, id) then strong_connect(st, g, id) end end local component_of = {} local key_of = {} for c = 1, #g.components do local best = "" for id in g.components[c] do component_of[id] = c local key = sort_key(st, id) if best == "" or key < best then best = key end end key_of[c] = best end local printed = {} for c = 1, #g.components do push(printed, false) end local out = {} local left = #g.components while left > 0 do local pick = 0 for c = 1, #g.components do if not printed[c] and (pick == 0 or key_of[c] < key_of[pick]) then local ready = true for id in g.components[c] do for w in get(st.deps, id, {}) do if component_of[w] ~= c and not printed[component_of[w]] then ready = false end end end if ready then pick = c end end end printed[pick] = true left = left - 1 local members = g.components[pick] if #members == 1 then push(out, {id = members[1]}) else push(out, {cycle = members}) for id in order_in_cycle(st, members) do push(out, {id = id}) end end end return out end function check(failures, ok, what) if not ok then push(failures, what) end return nil end function has_line(ls, line) for l in ls do if l == line then return true end end return false end function has_text(ls, text) for l in ls do if contains(l, text) then return true end end return false end -- The type names of the header lines, in order. function headers_of(ls) local out = {} for l in ls do if starts_with(l, "#### ") then push(out, split(sub(l, 6), " (")[1]) end end return out end -- The family's modules from `modules=`'s comma-separated text: two or more, -- each once. function parse_modules(text) local out = {} for part in split(text, ",") do local s = trim(part) if s ~= "" then if has_item(out, s) then fail("print_module_types: modules=: `" .. s .. "` is named twice") end push(out, s) end end if #out < 2 then fail("print_module_types: modules=" .. text .. " names " .. #out .. " module; a family is two or more, as modules=TreeSighting,RailSighting") end return out end -- The ids in `ids`, ordered as `printing_order` orders a walk's types, with -- the edges of every member's walk among them. `asked` marks the types that -- sort last. function family_order(runs, ids, asked) local inside = set_of(ids) local ps = {types = {}, deps = {}, def_deps = {}, visited = inside, asked = asked} local seen = {} for run in runs do local st = run.st for id in ids do if has_key(st.types, id) then ps.types[id] = st.types[id] end for pair in {{st.deps, ps.deps, ">"}, {st.def_deps, ps.def_deps, "="}} do for w in get(pair[1], id, {}) do if has_key(inside, w) and not has_key(seen, id .. pair[3] .. w) then seen[id .. pair[3] .. w] = true push_at(pair[2], id, w) end end end end end return printing_order(ps) end -- The name's shape in the pass `pass`, `suffix` or `prefix`, by the rule in -- the header. function name_shape(name, pass) local words = split(name, "_") if #words == 1 then return name end if pass == "suffix" then return "*_" .. join(drop(words, 1), "_") end return words[1] .. "_*" end function padded(text, width) local out = text while #out < width do out = out .. " " end return out end -- The family table's lines and counts, from `entries`, each `{member, name, -- label, errors}`, `member` an index into `names`. function family_table(names, entries) local width = 0 for m in names do if #m + 2 > width then width = #m + 2 end end local assigned = {} local rows = {} for pass in {"suffix", "prefix"} do local members_by_shape = {} local order = {} for i = 1, #entries do if not has_key(assigned, "" .. i) then local shape = name_shape(entries[i].name, pass) if not has_key(members_by_shape, shape) then members_by_shape[shape] = {} push(order, shape) end members_by_shape[shape]["" .. entries[i].member] = true end end for shape in order do if #keys(members_by_shape[shape]) >= 2 then local row = {shape = shape, entries = {}} for i = 1, #entries do if not has_key(assigned, "" .. i) and name_shape(entries[i].name, pass) == shape then assigned["" .. i] = true push(row.entries, entries[i]) end end push(rows, row) end end end local out = {"", "## The family table: the public names by shape (module_family.shale's rule), and the error tags each answers."} for row in rows do local count = {} for e in row.entries do incr(count, e.errors) end local most = "" local best = 0 for e in row.entries do if count[e.errors] > best then best = count[e.errors] most = e.errors end end local present = {} for e in row.entries do present["" .. e.member] = true end push(out, "") push(out, "### " .. row.shape .. " (" .. #keys(present) .. " of " .. #names .. ")") for m = 1, #names do local shown = {} local differs = false for e in row.entries do if e.member == m then push(shown, e.errors == "" and e.label or e.label .. " ! " .. e.errors) if #keys(count) > 1 and e.errors ~= most then differs = true end end end local text = #shown == 0 and "-" or join(shown, ", ") push(out, padded(" " .. names[m], width + 2) .. text .. (differs and " <- errors differ" or "")) end end local unmatched = 0 local left = {} for i = 1, #entries do if not has_key(assigned, "" .. i) then unmatched = unmatched + 1 push_at(left, "" .. entries[i].member, entries[i].errors == "" and entries[i].label or entries[i].label .. " ! " .. entries[i].errors) end end if unmatched > 0 then push(out, "") push(out, "### unmatched: names of a shape no sibling has") for m = 1, #names do if has_key(left, "" .. m) then push(out, padded(" " .. names[m], width + 2) .. join(left["" .. m], ", ")) end end end return {lines = out, rows = #rows, unmatched = unmatched} end -- How many lines of `ls` are `line`. function count_line(ls, line) local n = 0 for l in ls do if l == line then n = n + 1 end end return n end -- The family plant: Spot and View are reached by all three siblings, Bark by -- OakSighting alone; ElmSighting names its list `visible_elms`, not -- `elms_in_view`, and its segment's sighting answers fewer errors. -- `r` is `family_walk`'s result for the plant family at `at`. function family_checks(failures, r, at) local ls = r.lines check(failures, #r.lost == 0 and #r.refused == 0, "family: lost or refused: " .. join(r.lost, "; ") .. join(r.refused, "; ")) check(failures, count_line(ls, "#### Spot (" .. at .. "/Spot.roc:3)") == 1 and count_line(ls, "#### View (" .. at .. "/View.roc:2)") == 1, "family: a shared type printed other than once") check(failures, has_line(ls, "## Shared: the 2 types two or more members reach, the most primitive first.") and has_line(ls, "# shared by all 3"), "family: the shared heading and note") check(failures, join(headers_of(ls), " | ") == "Spot | View | Bark | OakSighting | PineSighting | ElmSighting", "family: order: got " .. join(headers_of(ls), " | ")) check(failures, has_line(ls, "oak_at : View -> Spot # private") and has_line(ls, "## An oak at the view's middle."), "family: a private signature, marked, with its doc") check(failures, has_line(ls, "view_of : F64 -> View # private; tests only"), "family: a private function only expects use") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "sample : View") and not has_text(ls, "{ x: view.width"), "family: a private constant or a body printed") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# No private top-level functions in ElmSighting."), "family: a member with no private functions") check(failures, has_line(ls, "### *_in_view (2 of 3)") and has_line(ls, " ElmSighting -"), "family: the table's row missing a member") check(failures, has_line(ls, " OakSighting segment_oaks ! [Behind, TooSmall]") and has_line(ls, " ElmSighting segment_elms ! [Behind] <- errors differ"), "family: the error sets, sorted, and the one that differs") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "segment_pines ! [Behind, TooSmall] <-"), "family: an error set marked that matches") check(failures, has_line(ls, "### unmatched: names of a shape no sibling has") and has_line(ls, " ElmSighting visible_elms"), "family: the name that breaks the pattern, unmatched") check(failures, ls[#ls] == "# The family: 3 modules, 2 shared types, 1 types only one member reaches, 6 public names in 2 table rows and 1 unmatched, 3 private functions", "family: counts line: " .. ls[#ls]) return nil end -- The self-test's checks of a walk `rf` of the plant -- `cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/refused/`, whose -- Broken.roc holds `spin`'s only outside use but which roc-ast refuses, -- and of `clean`, a walk with no file refused. function refused_checks(failures, rf, clean, at) local ls = rf.lines local broken = at .. "refused/Broken.roc" check(failures, #rf.refused == 1 and rf.refused[1] == broken .. ": 4 parse problem(s): a file that does not parse has no tree to hunt", "refused: got " .. join(rf.refused, "; ")) check(failures, ls[2] == "# Refused by roc-ast, so their uses and mentions are not counted: " .. broken .. " (4 parse problem(s))", "the refused line: got " .. ls[2]) check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tspin : Coin -> Coin # no outside use, as far as the parsed files show"), "a member with no outside use, beside a refused file") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tflip : Coin -> Coin # used by 1 file"), "a member used by a file read, beside a refused file") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Public, but used only in this file, as far as the parsed files show: spin"), "the unused-members line, beside a refused file") check(failures, ends_with(ls[#ls], ", 1 files refused and not counted: " .. broken), "counts line with a refused file: " .. ls[#ls]) check(failures, not has_text(clean, "as far as") and not has_text(clean, "# Refused"), "a refused note with no file refused") return nil end

name: cookbook/roc/parsed.shale
html: -- The Roc recipes (hunt_names, find_deep_calls and the rest) check every .roc -- file in a tree, and some files may not parse. This library lets a recipe -- check the files that do parse, print what it found, and then fail with a -- list of the files it couldn't parse and why. -- The files that parse, and a `path: reason` line for each that doesn't. function parse_roc_files(paths) local files = {} local refused = {} for f in roc_tree(paths) do if f.err == "" then push(files, f) elseif starts_with(f.err, f.path) then push(refused, f.err) else push(refused, f.path .. ": " .. f.err) end end return {files = files, refused = refused} end -- A recipe calls this after printing what it found. It lists the files -- that didn't parse, and the files no root imports (which were checked -- without their types), then fails. function fail_if_refused(who, refused, unreached?) local missed = unreached or {} if #refused == 0 and #missed == 0 then return nil end for r in refused do print("refused: " .. r) end for m in missed do print(m) end local why = {} if #refused > 0 then push(why, "roc-ast refused " .. #refused .. " files (named above), which have no tree to judge") end if #missed > 0 then push(why, #missed .. " files (named above) are reached by no root of the types, so were judged without them") end fail(who .. ": " .. join(why, "; ") .. "; every other file was judged") end

name: cookbook/roc/pinned.shale
html: -- Each repository names its Roc version in a `roc-version` file. This -- library finds that version's `roc` for the Roc recipes that run the -- compiler. The version matters because `roc fmt`'s layout and the -- compiler's method lookup change from one nightly to the next. -- Every recipe's self-test runs this Roc. CI installs it from roc-apps's release. const SELF_TEST_PIN = "nightly-2026-10-30-0602c5f" -- The pin comes from the `roc-version` file where the run starts, or is -- `SELF_TEST_PIN` in a self-test. `who` names the recipe when it stops. function roc_bin(who, self_test) local pin = SELF_TEST_PIN if not self_test then if not exists("roc-version") then fail(who .. ": no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc") end pin = trim(read("roc-version")) end local roc = "tools:roc-" .. pin .. "/roc" if not exists(roc) then fail(who .. ": no " .. roc .. ": install Roc " .. pin .. " into ~/tools/roc-" .. pin .. "/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)") end return real(roc) end

name: cookbook/roc/print_module_types.shale
html: -- This recipe prints a Roc module's types and every type they depend on, -- the most primitive first, with no function bodies, so the types can be -- reviewed on their own. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/print_module_types.shale module=Pigs -- shale cookbook:roc/print_module_types.shale self_test=1 -- -- A package that apps use is walked from outside it, its folder named as a -- mount path and its apps as clients, since no path may climb with `..`: -- -- shale cookbook:roc/print_module_types.shale root=repos:roc-apps/canvas_apps/lib \ -- module=Brush clients=repos:roc-apps/canvas_apps/* -- -- (or from canvas_apps, `root=lib clients=*`). Run from inside the package, -- the walk sees only the package's own files. -- -- The arguments: -- module the module to start from, read from `<root>/<module>.roc`; -- root the folder that holds it, `.` by default; -- clients the code that uses the package, comma separated: a folder or -- a glob of folders, each an app whose `.roc` files at any depth -- are read, or a glob ending in `.roc`, whose files' folders are -- the apps. Named as the root is, both mount paths or both from -- one folder, as the walk compares paths as written. Their files -- join the other files below, each reading its imports from its -- own app header or its folder's (`import lib.Brush`, or -- `import game.Geom` in a gates app); -- packages where a package's modules are, as `lib=repos:roc-apps/lib`, -- several separated by commas. Without it a package's folder is -- read from the headers of the apps in the root folder, which -- works only when that folder is under the root, so a package at -- `../lib` needs this argument; -- max_depth how many steps from the module's own types to follow, 2 by -- default (WALK_MAX_DEPTH). The module's types are at depth 0 and -- the types they mention at depth 1. A type at the last depth is -- printed, and the types it mentions that aren't printed anyway -- are named in one line, not followed. A clear type reads from -- its immediate children alone, which is depth 1; -- full_depth the deepest depth printed in full, 1 by default -- (WALK_FULL_DEPTH). A deeper type prints its header, doc and -- definition, and its block's members as one line of names, -- `.{ metres, to_metres, zero }`. It still counts and is followed -- as before; only its printing is shorter; -- stop the hub types that are named but never expanded, comma -- separated, WALK_STOP by default; `stop=` empty stops none. An -- entry is a type's printed name, `Shapes.Shape`, or a module's -- name and `.*`, `Brush.*`, for every type of that module. A -- stopped type is named once, in the `# Stopped` line, is not -- printed, and nothing it mentions is followed through it. The -- asked module's own types are never stopped; -- brief the types printed by name and members alone at every depth, -- even depth 1, comma separated, WALK_BRIEF by default; `brief=` -- empty makes none brief. An entry is a type's printed name or -- `Module.*`, as for `stop`, or `units`: every nominal type over -- one builtin number with no type nested in its block, such as -- `Distance :: F64.{ ... }` or `Steps :: U32.{ ... }`, found from -- its declaration. The asked module's own types are never brief; -- uses with `uses=0`, leave out the outside uses of the asked module's -- members (below); -- named_by with `named_by=0`, leave out the "named by" section (below); -- with `named_by=production`, list only its untagged entries, -- leaving out those tagged `(test)` or `(private)`; -- modules in place of `module=`, two or more sibling modules, comma -- separated, walked as one family with the settings above: the -- types two or more reach once, each member's own types and -- signatures with its private functions', its uses and named-by -- sections per member, and a table of their public names by -- shape (module_family.shale says how); -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/`. -- -- The types read are the type declarations at a file's top level and those -- nested in a type's `.{ ... }` block. A type's members are the annotations -- in its own block, in source order: its functions, whose type is written as -- a function, and its constants, whose type is not, such as `count : I64`. -- Each is printed as its doc and its annotation, with its body or value left -- out, not written as `...`, and a constant's annotation ends in -- `# constant`, so it reads as one even when its type is an alias. An -- annotation whose whole type is `_` is left out, since it says nothing of -- the type's surface. Values outside any block (a module's private helpers) -- are left out, and so are the types only they mention. -- -- Every type name in a printed definition or annotation is followed: a bare -- name declared in the same file, a bare name that is an imported module's own -- type (`Distance` after `import Distance`), and `Module.Type`. A tag's name is -- not a type, but its payload is. Builtins (`Str`, `List`, `U32` and the rest) -- are leaves, named in one line and not expanded. Type variables are not -- followed; each is named with the types it appears in. -- -- The types come out in topological order: a type before every type that -- mentions it, its definition or its functions. Ties go by module, then by -- name, and the asked-for module's types come last. Types that mention each -- other form a cycle, which is reported in one line before its members; the -- members then follow, by their definitions where those order them, else by -- name. Each type has a header line with its name, file and line, then its -- doc comment and its definition as written, and then its functions inside a -- `.{ ... }`. The source's text is kept, re-indented. -- -- A header line names the asked module's imports that hold no printed, -- stopped or beyond-depth type, `# Imported but not in any printed type: -- Camera, Screen`: modules its functions use only in their bodies (or in -- annotations outside its types' blocks), which a reviewer should read too. -- The imports only its tests use are left out of it and named on their own, -- `# Imported for tests only: Polygon`: every use of the import sits in an -- `expect`, or in a top-level value (its annotation included) that only -- expects use, directly or through other such values. A member of a type's -- block is production, as other files may call it. No import may be a -- test's alone: its test moves to a CrossModuleExpects file. In a family, -- each member's block has its own line. -- -- The other files are the root folder's other `.roc` files, those under its -- `gates/` folder, and the clients'. A file's `import game.Geom` reads the -- package's folder from its own header, else from the headers of the apps and -- packages in its folder, unless `packages=` names it. A header line counts -- the clients' files and apps and those importing the asked module, which -- may be none, and a member used by files in several client apps says how -- many, `# used by 9 files in 5 apps`. When no client imports any of the -- root's files, the root and the clients are taken to be named unlike, and -- the walk fails. It fails too when an app beside the root, one whose header -- directly in its folder names the root as a package (`safari/main.roc`'s -- `lib: "../lib/main.roc"`), holds no client file, with or without -- `clients=`: a member only that app uses would read as unused. From the -- root's parent folder, `clients=*` names them all. -- -- Each member of the asked module's types ends with its outside uses, `# -- used by 3 files, 1 in tests only`, or `# no outside use` (after `# -- constant;` on a constant). A file uses a member by naming it through its -- import of the asked module, `Geom.ahead_point` or -- `Geom.AheadPoint.at_height`, or by calling it, `point.at_height(h)`, or -- through its operator, `a < b` for `is_lt`, on a receiver the file plainly -- types as its type (member_uses.shale says when). A call on a receiver of no -- known type counts for every member of its name, and only in a file with no -- use above: `; by method name in 2 more`, `; by operator, untyped, in 1 -- more`. A use is in tests when it sits in an `expect`, in a top-level value -- that only expects use (directly or through other such values), or anywhere -- in a file under a `gates/` folder; a file is "in tests only" when all its -- uses of the member are. A header line lists the members no other file uses -- or may use, `# Public, but used only in this file: near_plane_crossing, -- AheadPoint.at_right`, a nested type's members named with their type. -- -- After the types, the "named by" section lists every annotation, a -- function's or a constant's, in a type's block or at the top level, and -- every type definition, in the other files that mentions one of the asked -- module's types, grouped by module, each as `file:line: ` and its text, a -- member or nested type qualified by the type it sits in. An entry in tests, -- by the rule above, is tagged `(test)` after its place, and a top-level -- annotation that is not is tagged `(private)`, being a helper outside any -- block. A mention counts when it resolves to the asked module's type as the -- walk resolves names, through the file's import of the asked module, -- qualified or bare, so another type of the same bare name does not. The last -- line counts the types, functions, constants, modules, leaves, type -- variables, types beyond the depth, stopped types, the members with no -- outside use, the method calls and operators of their names typed and -- pooled, and the annotations and types the "named by" section found, -- all of them whatever `named_by=production` lists, split into production -- (untagged or private) and test. -- -- A name that resolves to no file or no type, or a file that doesn't parse, -- is listed after the output, and the run then fails. A refused file's uses -- are unread, so member_uses.shale's refused_line says how it is named. -- budget: steps=2000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=8000000 reads=100000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" -- How many steps from the module's own types the walk follows when -- `max_depth=` doesn't say. const WALK_MAX_DEPTH = 2 -- The deepest depth printed in full when `full_depth=` doesn't say. const WALK_FULL_DEPTH = 1 -- The hub types named but never expanded when `stop=` doesn't say: types so -- widely used that following them buries the module's own story. const WALK_STOP = {"Shapes.Shape", "Brush.*", "World.Segment"} -- The types printed by name and members alone at every depth when `brief=` -- doesn't say: the plain unit wrappers, whose members are arithmetic a -- reviewer reads past. const WALK_BRIEF = {"units"} -- The builtin numbers a unit wrapper may be a nominal type over. const WALK_NUMBERS = {"F32", "F64", "Dec", "U8", "U16", "U32", "U64", "U128", "I8", "I16", "I32", "I64", "I128"} use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:roc/member_uses.shale") use("cookbook:roc/module_family.shale") -- The type names and type variables the type at node `at` mentions, pushed -- onto `into` as `{name, line}` and `{var, line}`. A tag's name is skipped and -- its payload read. function mentions_in(tree, at, into) local n = tree[at] local parent_kind = n.parent ~= 0 and tree[n.parent].kind or "" if n.kind == "ty-var" then push(into, {var = get(n, "raw", ""), line = n.line}) return into end if n.kind == "ty" then if parent_kind ~= "tags" and get(n, "name", "") ~= "" then push(into, {name = n.name, line = n.line}) end return into end local kids = n.kids local from = 1 if n.kind == "ty-apply" and parent_kind == "tags" then from = 2 end for k = from, #kids do mentions_in(tree, kids[k], into) end return into end -- A type's name as printed: qualified by its module, or with the module -- named after it when the type sits outside the module's own type. function display_name(t) if t.qualified == t.module or starts_with(t.qualified, t.module .. ".") then return t.qualified end return t.qualified .. ", in module " .. t.module end function add_edge(st, from, to, in_definition) if from == to then return nil end local seen = st.dep_seen if not has_key(seen, from .. ">" .. to) then seen[from .. ">" .. to] = true push_at(st.deps, from, to) end if in_definition and not has_key(seen, from .. "=" .. to) then seen[from .. "=" .. to] = true push_at(st.def_deps, from, to) end return nil end -- Adds the type `id`, at `depth` steps from the module, to the next depth's -- types, unless it is already read. function enqueue(st, id, depth) if has_key(st.visited, id) then return nil end st.visited[id] = true st.depth_of[id] = depth push(st.next, id) return nil end -- Whether the list of type names `names` (a stop list or a brief list) holds -- the type `t`: its printed name, or its module's name and `.*`. function listed(names, t) local name = display_name(t) for s in names do if s == name or s == t.module .. ".*" then return true end end return false end -- A list of type names from `who=`'s comma-separated text: none for "". function parse_type_list(text, who) local out = {} for part in split(text, ",") do local s = trim(part) if s ~= "" then if contains(s, "*") and not (ends_with(s, ".*") and #s > 2 and not contains(sub(s, 1, #s - 1), "*")) then fail("print_module_types: " .. who .. "=: `" .. s ..
