"` is no type's name and no `Module.*`") end push(out, s) end end return out end -- The stop list from `stop=`'s text. function parse_stops(text) return parse_type_list(text, "stop") end -- The brief list from `brief=`'s text, which may also hold `units`. function parse_brief(text) return parse_type_list(text, "brief") end -- Whether the type `t` is a unit wrapper: a nominal type (`::`) over one -- builtin number, with no type declared in its block. function is_unit(st, t) local info = st.files[t.path] local tree = info.nodes local kids = tree[t.at].kids if #kids < 2 or tree[kids[2]].kind ~= "ty" or not has_item(WALK_NUMBERS, get(tree[kids[2]], "name", "")) then return false end local name_node = tree[kids[1]] local between = sub(info.src[name_node.end_line], name_node.end_col, name_node.end_col + 3) if not contains(between, "::") then return false end for k in kids do if tree[k].kind == "associated" then for m in tree[k].kids do if tree[m].kind == "s-type-decl" then return false end end end end return true end -- Whether the type `id` prints by name and members alone at every depth: it -- is on the brief list, or a unit wrapper while the list holds `units`. The -- asked module's own types never are. function is_brief(st, id) if has_key(st.asked, id) then return false end local t = st.types[id] if listed(st.brief, t) then return true end return has_item(st.brief, "units") and is_unit(st, t) end -- Settles one mention of the type `m.from`: an edge, a leaf, a lost name, or -- a wait for its file. ")) check(failures, #r.refused == 0, "refused: " .. join(r.refused, "; ")) -- U32 appears only in the constant `count : U32`, so it is a leaf because -- constants are printed and followed. check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Builtin leaves, not expanded: F64, List, Str, U32"), "leaves line") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Type variables, not followed: a (Tagged, in module Leg)"), "type variable line") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Cycle: these types mention each other: Note, Note.Mark"), "cycle line") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# 9 types, 4 functions, 4 constants, 5 modules, 4 leaves, 1 type variables, 0 beyond depth 3, 0 stopped, 1 members with no outside use, method calls 0 typed and 1 pooled, operators 0 typed and 0 pooled, named by 4 annotations and 1 types: 3 production, 2 test"), "counts line: " .. ls[#ls]) check(failures, not has_text(ls, "# Beyond depth"), "a beyond line when the walk reached every type") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\t## How many rides a day allows."), "a constant's doc") -- main.roc reads `Ride.count` in production, and Trip.roc in a value that -- only another value reads, which only an expect reads. check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tcount : U32 # constant; used by 2 files, 1 in tests only"), "a constant's annotation, marked, used in production and in a test-only value") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tcruising : Speed # constant; no outside use"), "a constant of a type from another module, which nothing outside uses") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "CONSTANT_MARKER") and not has_text(ls, "= 3"), "a constant's value is printed") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "legs_of : Ride -> List(Leg) # constant"), "a function is marked as a constant") -- `is_eq : _` leaves its whole type to inference, so its annotation says -- nothing of Ride's surface and is left out. check(failures, not has_text(ls, "is_eq"), "an annotation of type `_` is printed") check(failures, has_line(ls, "Ride :: { legs : List(Leg), name : Str }.{"), "a module type's definition opens its block") -- Only gates/Check.roc, through its own header's `game` package, uses -- `legs_of`. check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tlegs_of : Ride -> List(Leg) # used by 1 file, 1 in tests only"), "a function's annotation, used by a gates app alone") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\t## The legs of a ride, in order."), "a function's doc") -- Trip.roc names `noted` in an expect, and Log.roc calls `.noted()` on a -- value of no known type. check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tnoted : Ride, Note -> Str # used by 1 file, 1 in tests only; by method name in 1 more"), "a type only an annotation mentions, its member used in an expect and by method name") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Public, but used only in this file: cruising"), "the members no other file uses") local unused = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, uses = false}).lines check(failures, has_line(unused, "\tcount : U32 # constant") and has_line(unused, "\tlegs_of : Ride -> List(Leg)"), "uses=0 keeps the uses") check(failures, not has_text(unused, "Public, but") and not has_text(unused, "outside use") and not has_text(unused, "used by"), "uses=0 keeps the summary") check(failures, unused[#unused] == "# 9 types, 4 functions, 4 constants, 5 modules, 4 leaves, 1 type variables, 0 beyond depth 3, 0 stopped, named by 4 annotations and 1 types: 3 production, 2 test", "uses=0 counts line: " .. unused[#unused]) check(failures, has_line(ls, "Plan : [Short, Long(Leg.Stretch)]"), "a nested type, re-indented") check(failures, has_line(ls, "## How long a ride's plan is."), "a nested type's doc") check(failures, has_line(ls, "## A ride is a list of legs, with a name."), "a module type's doc from the file's opening comment") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tlabel : Tagged(Str),"), "a multiline definition, re-indented") check(failures, has_line(ls, "#### Unit.Metres (" .. at .. "chain/shared/Unit.roc:6)"), "a type from a package") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "BODY_MARKER") and not has_text(ls, "ride.legs") and not has_text(ls, "|ride|"), "a body is printed") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "helper") and not has_text(ls, "#### Hidden"), "a helper outside the block, or its type, is printed") -- Unit.Metres is two steps from Ride, past the default full depth of 1, so -- its members are one line of names; Leg, one step away, is whole. check(failures, has_line(ls, "Metres :: F64.{ zero, plus }"), "a type past the full depth, its members by name") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "plus : Metres, Metres -> Metres"), "a type past the full depth printed whole") check(failures, has_line(ls, "\tlength_of : Leg -> Unit.Metres"), "a type at the full depth printed whole") -- Metres is a unit, brief by default, so this full depth is shown with no -- brief types. local full = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, full_depth = 3, brief = {}}).lines check(failures, has_line(full, "Metres :: F64.{") and has_line(full, "\tplus : Metres, Metres -> Metres") and has_line(full, "\tzero : Metres # constant"), "full_depth=3 prints a depth-2 type whole") check(failures, not has_text(full, "Metres :: F64.{ zero"), "full_depth=3 still names a depth-2 type's members") check(failures, full[#full] == ls[#ls], "the full depth changes the counts: " .. full[#full]) -- Speed and Unit.Metres are nominal types over F64 with no nested type, so -- units: brief at every depth, Speed at depth 1 among them. check(failures, has_line(ls, "Speed :: F64.{ still }"), "a unit at depth 1 printed whole") check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Brief, members by name at every depth: Speed; Unit.Metres"), "the brief line") check(failures, has_line(full, "Speed :: F64.{") and has_line(full, "\tstill : Speed # constant") and not has_text(full, "# Brief"), "brief= empty prints a unit brief") local deep = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, full_depth = 3}).lines check(failures, has_line(deep, "Metres :: F64.{ zero, plus }"), "a unit within the full depth printed whole") local named_brief = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, brief = parse_brief("Leg")}).lines check(failures, has_line(named_brief, "}.{ length_of }") and has_line(named_brief, "# Brief, members by name at every depth: Leg"), "a type on the brief list by name printed whole") check(failures, has_line(named_brief, "Speed :: F64.{") and has_line(named_brief, "\tstill : Speed # constant"), "a unit printed brief without `units` on the list") local asked_unit = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Speed", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, has_line(asked_unit, "Speed :: F64.{") and not has_text(asked_unit, "# Brief"), "the asked module's unit printed brief") -- Tally is imported for a body alone, and Hidden for a helper outside the -- block; Leg, Note and Speed hold printed types. check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Imported but not in any printed type: Hidden, Tally"), "the imports in no printed type") -- Sample is used only by an expect and a value only it reads, annotation -- and body; Tally by an expect and by `legs_of`; Hidden by a helper nothing -- reads, which is no test's. check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Imported for tests only: Sample"), "the imports only tests use") -- A punned field, `{ shades }`, names a top-level value: `shades` reaches -- production that way, so Shade is no test's, and `probed` reaches only an -- expect that way, so Probe is. local punned = walk(at .. "punned", "Pun", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, has_line(punned, "# Imported for tests only: Probe"), "a punned field's uses: Shade's production value counted a test's, or Probe's test value production's") -- Trip names Ride in its definition, in a member's annotation and in a -- top-level helper's; its own `own_plan` mentions Trip's `Plan`, not Ride's. check(failures, has_line(ls, "# Named by: the annotations and types in the other modules of " .. at .. "chain/app that mention Ride's types."), "the named-by heading") check(failures, has_line(ls, "### Trip"), "the named-by module") check(failures, has_line(ls, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:6: Trip :: { ride : Ride, legs : List(Leg) }"), "named by a type's definition") check(failures, has_line(ls, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:9: Trip.plan_of : Trip -> Ride.Plan"), "named by a member's annotation") check(failures, has_line(ls, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:20: (private) start : Ride -> Trip"), "named by a top-level helper, tagged private") check(failures, has_line(ls, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:32: (test) sample_plan : Ride.Plan"), "named by a value only an expect reads, tagged test") check(failures, has_line(ls, at .. "chain/app/gates/Check.roc:10: (test) check : Ride -> U64"), "named by a gates app, tagged test") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "own_plan"), "named by another type of the same bare name") local production = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, named_by_production = true}).lines check(failures, has_line(production, "# Named by: the annotations and types in the other modules of " .. at .. "chain/app that mention Ride's types. Production only: 2 test and 1 private entries left out."), "the production-only heading") check(failures, has_line(production, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:6: Trip :: { ride : Ride, legs : List(Leg) }") and has_line(production, at .. "chain/app/Trip.roc:9: Trip.plan_of : Trip -> Ride.Plan"), "named_by=production leaves out an untagged entry") check(failures, not has_text(production, "start : Ride") and not has_text(production, "sample_plan") and not has_text(production, "### Check"), "named_by=production lists a tagged entry") check(failures, production[#production] == ls[#ls], "named_by=production changes the counts: " .. production[#production]) -- Ride's own `helper : Ride -> Hidden` would be listed were Ride read. local own = false for l in ls do if starts_with(l, at .. "chain/app/Ride.roc:") then own = true end end check(failures, not own, "named by the asked module itself") local unnamed = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, named_by = false}).lines check(failures, not has_text(unnamed, "Named by") and not has_text(unnamed, "Trip.roc"), "named_by=0 keeps the section") check(failures, unnamed[#unnamed] == "# 9 types, 4 functions, 4 constants, 5 modules, 4 leaves, 1 type variables, 0 beyond depth 3, 0 stopped, 1 members with no outside use, method calls 0 typed and 1 pooled, operators 0 typed and 0 pooled", "named_by=0 counts line: " .. unnamed[#unnamed]) -- Lost names a module no other file names, and its type has no members. local alone = walk(at .. "unresolved", "Lost", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, has_line(alone, "# Named by: no annotation or type in the other modules of " .. at .. "unresolved mentions Lost's types."), "the named-by line with none") check(failures, not has_text(alone, "Public, but"), "the unused-members line with no members") check(failures, not has_text(alone, "# Imported for tests only"), "a tests-only line with no import only tests use") -- Note stopped: named once, not printed, and Note.Mark, reached only -- through it, never read. Ride's own Ride.Plan is never stopped. local stopped = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, stops = {"Note", "Ride.Plan"}}).lines check(failures, has_line(stopped, "# Stopped, not expanded: Note"), "the stopped line") check(failures, not has_text(stopped, "#### Note") and not has_text(stopped, "Mark"), "a stopped type expanded") check(failures, has_text(stopped, "#### Ride.Plan"), "an asked type stopped") check(failures, has_line(stopped, "# Imported but not in any printed type: Hidden, Tally"), "a stopped import named as unprinted") check(failures, stopped[#stopped] == "# 7 types, 4 functions, 4 constants, 4 modules, 4 leaves, 1 type variables, 0 beyond depth 3, 1 stopped, 1 members with no outside use, method calls 0 typed and 1 pooled, operators 0 typed and 0 pooled, named by 4 annotations and 1 types: 3 production, 2 test", "stopped counts line: " .. stopped[#stopped]) local by_module = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, stops = parse_stops(" Leg.* , ")}).lines check(failures, has_line(by_module, "# Stopped, not expanded: Leg; Leg.Stretch"), "a module's types stopped by `.*`: got " .. join(headers_of(by_module), " | ")) check(failures, not has_text(by_module, "Unit.Metres") and not has_text(by_module, "Tagged"), "a type followed through a stopped one") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "# Stopped"), "a stopped line with nothing stopped") check(failures, #parse_stops("") == 0, "stop= empty stops something") local unstopped = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 3, {trees = trees, stops = parse_stops("")}).lines check(failures, has_text(unstopped, "#### Note (") and not has_text(unstopped, "# Stopped"), "with no stops, Note is expanded") check(failures, not has_text(ls, "#### Unit "), "a module type nobody mentions is printed") check(failures, not has_line(ls, "#### Short") and not has_text(ls, "Long,"), "a tag is read as a type") -- Ride's deepest types, Note.Mark, Tagged and Unit.Metres, are two steps -- from it, so depth 1 names them and prints the rest, and Note's cycle -- through Note.Mark is gone with it. local one = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 1, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, join(headers_of(one), " | ") == "Leg | Leg.Stretch | Note | Speed | Ride | Ride.Plan", "depth 1 order: got " .. join(headers_of(one), " | ")) check(failures, has_line(one, "# Beyond depth 1, not followed: Note.Mark; Tagged, in module Leg; Unit.Metres"), "depth 1 beyond line") check(failures, has_line(one, "# 6 types, 3 functions, 3 constants, 4 modules, 4 leaves, 0 type variables, 3 beyond depth 1, 0 stopped, 1 members with no outside use, method calls 0 typed and 1 pooled, operators 0 typed and 0 pooled, named by 4 annotations and 1 types: 3 production, 2 test"),"depth 1 counts line: " .. one[#one]) check(failures, not has_text(one, "# Cycle"), "a cycle through a type beyond the depth") check(failures, has_line(one, "\tlabel : Tagged(Str),"), "a type at the last depth printed whole") -- Depth 0 is the module's own types, and Speed's F64 is no longer read. local zero = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "", 0, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, join(headers_of(zero), " | ") == "Ride | Ride.Plan", "depth 0 order: got " .. join(headers_of(zero), " | ")) check(failures, has_line(zero, "# Beyond depth 0, not followed: Leg; Leg.Stretch; Note; Speed"), "depth 0 beyond line") check(failures, has_line(zero, "# Builtin leaves, not expanded: List, Str, U32"), "depth 0 leaves line") -- Width has members named as Span's. Typed.roc calls each Span member -- below on a Span through one typing rule; OtherType.roc calls `plus`, -- `minus` and `>` on Widths alone, and Width.roc's own `+`, `-` and `>` -- are on the F64s its patterns unwrap; Pooled.roc calls `plus` and applies -- `<=` on values of no known type. local m = walk(at .. "methods", "Span", "", 3, {trees = trees, named_by = false}).lines check(failures, has_line(m, "\tplus : Span, Span -> Span # used by 1 file; by method name in 1 more"), "a field's receiver typed, and an untyped one pooled") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tscaled : Span, F64 -> Span # used by 1 file"), "a local from a qualified call typed") check(failures, has_line(m, "\thalved : Span -> Span # used by 1 file"), "a qualified constant typed") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tdoubled : Span -> Span # used by 1 file"), "a method's result typed") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tflipped : Span -> Span # used by 1 file"), "a constant of the file typed") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tminus : Span, Span -> Span # no outside use") and has_line(m, "\tis_gt : Span, Span -> Bool # no outside use"), "a call on another type counted, through a parameter, an alias, a field, an operator or a nominal pattern") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tis_lt : Span, Span -> Bool # used by 1 file"), "an operator on an alias of the type") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tis_gte : Span, Span -> Bool # used by 1 file"), "a comparison typed by its right side") check(failures, has_line(m, "\tis_lte : Span, Span -> Bool # used by operator only, untyped, in 1 file"), "an untyped operator pooled") check(failures, has_line(m, "# Public, but used only in this file: minus, is_gt"), "the members used only here, beside calls typed elsewhere and untyped operators") check(failures, m[#m] == "# 1 types, 11 functions, 1 constants, 1 modules, 2 leaves, 0 type variables, 0 beyond depth 3, 0 stopped, 2 members with no outside use, method calls 9 typed and 1 pooled, operators 6 typed and 1 pooled", "methods counts line: " .. m[#m]) -- The package pkg's Dot: app one names it `kit` and uses shift and scale; -- app two names it `geo`, and its Helper, with no header, uses scale -- through the folder's app; pkg's own Grid uses origin. local cl_at = at .. "clients/" local c = walk(cl_at .. "pkg", "Dot", "", 3, {trees = trees, clients = cl_at .. "apps/*"}) local cls = c.lines check(failures, #c.lost == 0 and #c.refused == 0, "clients: lost or refused: " .. join(c.lost, "; ") .. join(c.refused, "; ")) check(failures, has_line(cls, "# Clients: 3 files in 2 apps, 2 importing " .. cl_at .. "pkg/Dot.roc"), "the clients line") check(failures, has_line(cls, "\tshift : Dot -> Dot # used by 1 file"), "a member only one client app uses, through its alias") check(failures, has_line(cls, "\tscale : Dot -> Dot # used by 2 files in 2 apps"), "a member two client apps use, one through its folder's header, with its apps") check(failures, has_line(cls, "\torigin : Dot # constant; used by 1 file"), "a member the package's own file uses, with clients") check(failures, has_line(cls, "# Public, but used only in this file: hidden"), "the members used only here, with clients") check(failures, has_line(cls, cl_at .. "apps/one/main.roc:7: (private) moved : Dot -> Dot") and has_line(cls, cl_at .. "apps/two/Helper.roc:8: Helper.far : Dot -> Dot"), "named by the clients' signatures") check(failures, has_line(cls, "# Named by: the annotations and types in the other modules of " .. cl_at .. "pkg and the clients that mention Dot's types."), "the named-by heading with clients") local alone_pkg = walk(cl_at .. "pkg", "Dot", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lines check(failures, has_line(alone_pkg, "# Public, but used only in this file: shift, scale, hidden"), "without clients, the members only clients use") check(failures, has_line(alone_pkg, "\tscale : Dot -> Dot # no outside use") and not has_text(alone_pkg, "apps/") and not has_text(alone_pkg, "# Clients"), "without clients, a client counted") -- A root written from the data root, beside clients through a mount, gives -- the asked file two names, and no client imports the one the walk has. local unlike = walk("cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/clients/pkg", "Dot", "", 3, {trees = trees, clients = cl_at .. "apps/*"}).lost check(failures, #unlike == 1 and has_text(unlike, "clients=: none of the 3 client files imports any of the root's files, such as cookbook/roc/plants/print_module_types/clients/pkg/Dot.roc"), "clients named unlike the root, got " .. join(unlike, "; ")) -- The app grid_only imports the package's Grid and not Dot, which is no -- mismatch: it walks cleanly, with no client importing Dot. local others = walk(cl_at .. "pkg", "Dot", "", 3, {trees = trees, clients = cl_at .. "others/*"}) check(failures, #others.lost == 0 and #others.refused == 0, "a client importing other root modules: lost or refused: " .. join(others.lost, "; ") .. join(others.refused, "; ")) check(failures, has_line(others.lines, "# Clients: 1 file in 1 app, 0 importing " .. cl_at .. "pkg/Dot.roc"), "the clients line with none importing the asked module") -- Beside the package beside/lib are two apps that use it, walker and -- dot_widget. Clients that leave walker out, or no clients, would read -- `step`, which only walker uses, as unused, so the walk fails naming the -- apps left out; with both, each member is used once. local bs = at .. "beside/" local widgets_only = walk(bs .. "lib", "Spot", "", 3, {trees = trees, clients = bs .. "*_widget"}).lost check(failures, #widgets_only == 1 and has_text(widgets_only, "clients=: the apps beside " .. bs .. "lib that use it as a package and hold no client file, whose uses are not counted: " .. bs .. "walker; name every app that uses it, as clients=" .. bs .. "*"), "an app beside the package left out of the clients, got " .. join(widgets_only, "; ")) local no_clients = walk(bs .. "lib", "Spot", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lost check(failures, #no_clients == 1 and has_text(no_clients, "not counted: " .. bs .. "dot_widget, " .. bs .. "walker;"), "the apps beside the package with no clients, got " .. join(no_clients, "; ")) local every = walk(bs .. "lib", "Spot", "", 3, {trees = trees, clients = bs .. "*"}) check(failures, #every.lost == 0 and #every.refused == 0, "every app beside the package a client: lost or refused: " .. join(every.lost, "; ") .. join(every.refused, "; ")) check(failures, has_line(every.lines, "\tstep : Spot -> Spot # used by 1 file") and has_line(every.lines, "\thome : Spot # constant; used by 1 file"), "every app beside the package a client, a member each app alone uses") local unread = walk(bs .. "lib", "Spot", "", 3, {trees = trees, uses = false, named_by = false}).lost check(failures, #unread == 0, "uses=0 named_by=0 with apps beside the package, which reads no other file, got " .. join(unread, "; ")) refused_checks(failures, walk(at .. "refused", "Coin", "", 3, {trees = trees}), ls, at) local lost = walk(at .. "unresolved", "Lost", "", 3, {trees = trees}).lost check(failures, #lost == 2, "two lost names, got " .. #lost .. ": " .. join(lost, "; ")) check(failures, has_text(lost, "`Nowhere.Thing`: `Nowhere` is no imported module"), "a name of no import is lost") check(failures, has_text(lost, "`Gone`: no file " .. at .. "unresolved/Gone.roc"), "a missing module is lost") local moved = walk(at .. "chain/app", "Ride", "shared=" .. at .. "chain/nowhere", 3, {trees = trees}).lost check(failures, #moved == 2 and has_text(moved, "Leg.roc:5: `Unit.Metres`: no file " .. at .. "chain/nowhere/Unit.roc"), "packages= overrides the app's folder, got " .. join(moved, "; ")) local family_at = "cookbook:roc/plants/print_module_types/family" family_checks(failures, family_walk(family_at, parse_modules("OakSighting, PineSighting,ElmSighting"), "", 3, {trees = trees}), family_at) for f in failures do print("FAIL: " .. f) end if #failures > 0 then fail("print_module_types: " .. #failures .. " self-test checks failed") end print("print_module_types: self test passed") return nil end if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local depth_arg = arg("max_depth", tostring(WALK_MAX_DEPTH)) local max_depth = parse_int(depth_arg) if max_depth == nil or max_depth < 0 then fail("print_module_types: max_depth=" .. depth_arg .. " is no count of steps, such as 3") end local full_arg = arg("full_depth", tostring(WALK_FULL_DEPTH)) local full_depth = parse_int(full_arg) if full_depth == nil or full_depth < 0 then fail("print_module_types: full_depth=" .. full_arg .. " is no count of steps, such as 1") end local named_by_arg = arg("named_by", "1") if named_by_arg ~= "0" and named_by_arg ~= "1" and named_by_arg ~= "production" then fail("print_module_types: named_by=" .. named_by_arg .. " is none of 0, 1 and production") end local uses_arg = arg("uses", "1") if uses_arg ~= "0" and uses_arg ~= "1" then fail("print_module_types: uses=" .. uses_arg .. " is neither 0 nor 1") end local settings = {stops = parse_stops(arg("stop", join(WALK_STOP, ","))), brief = parse_brief(arg("brief", join(WALK_BRIEF, ","))), full_depth = full_depth, uses = uses_arg == "1", named_by = named_by_arg ~= "0", named_by_production = named_by_arg == "production", clients = arg("clients", "")} local modules_arg = arg("modules", "") if modules_arg ~= "" and arg("module", "") ~= "" then fail("print_module_types: module= and modules= both given; name one module, or a family") end local r = modules_arg == "" and walk(arg("root", "."), arg("module", ""), arg("packages", ""), max_depth, settings) or family_walk(arg("root", "."), parse_modules(modules_arg), arg("packages", ""), max_depth, settings) print(join(r.lines, "\n")) for l in r.lost do print("lost: " .. l) end for l in r.refused do print("refused: " .. l) end if #r.lost > 0 or #r.refused > 0 then fail("print_module_types: " .. #r.lost .. " names resolve to no type and " .. #r.refused .. " files don't parse (named above); every other type is printed") end end

name: cookbook/roc/rank_boundary_hints.shale
html: -- This recipe ranks cheap hints that one Roc module does another's work: a -- module whose public names carry another module's noun, and a public member -- that only one other module uses, most of all one that module draws with. -- They are candidates for a review, not findings to fix on sight. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/rank_boundary_hints.shale root=safari \ -- clients=*_widget,widget_kit -- shale cookbook:roc/rank_boundary_hints.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- root the folder of the modules, `.` by default; -- glob which of its files are the modules, relative to the root, -- `*.roc` by default; several globs may be given, separated by -- commas. A file that declares no type (an app, a package -- header) is read as a user only; -- clients the code that uses the modules from outside the root, read as -- users only, as print_module_types.shale reads `clients=`: a folder or a -- glob of folders, or a glob ending in `.roc`, named as the root -- is; -- packages where a package's modules are, as print_module_types.shale takes it; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, check the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/rank_boundary_hints/`. -- -- The hints: -- -- fed_to_one A member of a module M's types whose production uses -- outside M all sit in one other module N. A use is counted as -- print_module_types.shale counts one (member_uses.shale): a name through -- N's import of M, or a call on a receiver N plainly types as -- M's type. Uses in tests are no use: an `expect`, a value only -- expects read, or any file under the root's `gates/` folder, -- which is read for that. A member some other file may call by -- method name on a receiver of no known type is left out, and -- counted in the summary, since its one user is not sure. When -- the function in N around a use builds a shape (a tag in -- SHAPE_TAGS, or a `Shapes.` call) or is annotated to give one -- (its result names a type `Shape`), N draws with the member: the -- strongest form, with those functions named. When N only -- imports Shapes, that is said too. -- borrowed_noun A member of M's types whose snake_case name starts with -- another module's name, in snake_case, and an underscore: -- `sky_top_stop` in Backdrop when there is a Sky module, but not -- `skyline` and not a bare `sky`. The longest such module is -- named. -- -- The lines come strongest first: fed_to_one with drawing in a function, -- then with Shapes imported, then the rest of fed_to_one, each by uses, most -- first; then borrowed_noun. They sit between two copies of the summary -- (cookbook/findings.shale). Hints don't gate: the run fails only when a -- file doesn't parse or an import names no file. -- budget: steps=4000000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 reads=100000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" use("cookbook:roc/declared.shale") use("cookbook:roc/member_uses.shale") use("cookbook:roc/module_family.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") -- The tags that build a shape or its paint: lib's Shapes.Shape and -- Brush.Fill. const SHAPE_TAGS = {Poly = true, Disc = true, Rect = true, Image = true, Flat = true, Span = true, Radial = true, Linear = true, Ellipse = true, Glow = true} -- A module's name in snake_case: `TruckBody` gives `truck_body`. function snake_name(module) return join(name_words(module), "_") end -- The paths the comma-separated globs `globs` give under `root`, normalized -- and sorted, each once. function module_paths(root, globs) local seen = {} for g in split(globs, ",") do local pattern = trim(g) if pattern ~= "" then for p in glob(path_join(root, pattern)) do seen[path_normal(p)] = true end end end return sort(keys(seen)) end -- The functions around the uses `sites` in the file `info` that build a -- shape, each as `name (Tag, Shapes.call, gives a Shape)` with what showed -- it. function drawing_functions(st, info, sites) local tree = info.nodes local cx = typing_context(st, info) local done = {} local out = {} for site in sites do local s = cx.scope[site.at] if s ~= 0 and not has_key(done, tostring(s)) and tree[s].kind == "s-decl" then done[tostring(s)] = true local built = {} local j = s + 1 while j <= #tree and tree[j].depth > tree[s].depth do local n = tree[j] if n.kind == "e-tag" then local parts = split(get(n, "raw", ""), ".") if has_key(SHAPE_TAGS, parts[#parts]) then built[parts[#parts]] = true end end if n.kind == "e-ident" and starts_with(get(n, "raw", ""), "Shapes.") then built[get(n, "raw", "")] = true end j = j + 1 end -- A function annotated to give a Shape draws, though a helper of its -- own builds the shape. local name = get(tree[tree[s].kids[1]], "raw", "") for anno in get(cx.beside, tree[s].parent .. "\t" .. name, {}) do local ty = tree[anno].kids[1] local result = tree[ty].kind == "ty-fn" and tree[ty].kids[#tree[ty].kids] or ty if has_key(mentioned_type_names(tree, result, {}), "Shape") then built["gives a Shape"] = true end end if #keys(built) > 0 then push(out, get(tree[tree[s].kids[1]], "raw", "?") .. " (" .. join(sort(keys(built)), ", ") .. ")") end end end return out end -- The production uses among `rec.sites` in the file `path`. function production_sites(st, rec, path) local info = st.files[path] local fc = file_context(st, info) local out = {} for site in rec.sites do if site.path == path and not in_tests(fc, fc.ctx[site.at]) then push(out, site) end end return out end -- The hints for the modules in `root` that `globs` names, with `clients=` and -- `packages=` as `clients` and `packages_arg`, as `{summary, lines, refused, -- lost}`. function hints(root, globs, clients, packages_arg, trees) refuse_climbing(root, "", clients) local st = {files = {}, types = {}, trees = trees, packages = package_folders(root, packages_arg, trees), dir_packages = {}, app_of = {}, refused = {}, refusals = {}, lost = {}, contexts = {}, typing = {}, resolved = {}, precision = {}, member_rec = {}, member_list = {}, members_by_name = {}, asked = {}, asked_files = {}} local paths = module_paths(root, globs) if #paths == 0 then fail("rank_boundary_hints: glob=" .. globs .. " names no file under " .. root) end load_files(st, paths) local users = {} for p in paths do push(users, p) end local gates = {} for p in glob(path_join(root, "gates/**/*.roc")) do push(gates, path_normal(p)) end load_files(st, gates) for p in sort(gates) do push(users, p) end if clients ~= "" then local skip = set_of(users) local cl = client_files(clients, skip) load_files(st, cl.paths) st.app_of = cl.app_of for p in cl.paths do push(users, p) end end load_imports(st) -- The modules: the files the glob names that declare a type. local modules = {} local snake_of = {} for p in paths do local info = st.files[p] if info.err == "" and #info.types > 0 then push(modules, p) snake_of[p] = snake_name(info.module) st.asked_files[p] = true for t in info.types do st.asked[t.id] = true end end end local owned = {} for p in modules do local from = #st.member_list + 1 asked_members(st, p) for k = from, #st.member_list do push(owned, {path = p, rec = st.member_list[k]}) end end for p in users do if st.files[p].err == "" then count_uses(st, st.files[p], "") end end local fed = {} local pooled_out = 0 local drawing = 0 for o in owned do local rec = o.rec local others = {} for q in keys(rec.prod) do if q ~= o.path then push(others, q) end end if #others == 1 then local n_path = others[1] local unsure = 0 for set in {rec.method_prod, rec.op_prod} do for q in keys(set) do if q ~= o.path and q ~= n_path then unsure = unsure + 1 end end end if unsure > 0 then pooled_out = pooled_out + 1 else local n_info = st.files[n_path] local sites = production_sites(st, rec, n_path) local draws = drawing_functions(st, n_info, sites) local rank = 3 local note = "" if #draws > 0 then rank = 1 drawing = drawing + 1 note = "; " .. n_info.module .. " draws with it in " .. join(draws, ", ") elseif has_key(n_info.imports, "Shapes") then rank = 2 note = "; " .. n_info.module .. " imports Shapes" end local m = st.files[o.path].module local text = o.path .. ":" .. rec.line .. ": fed_to_one: " .. m .. "." .. rec.label .. " is used only by " .. n_info.module .. ", " .. plural(#sites, "use") .. note push(fed, {key = rank .. "/" .. (100000 - #sites) .. "/" .. m .. "." .. rec.label, text = text}) end end end local borrowed = {} for o in owned do local name = split(o.rec.label, ".") name = name[#name] local best = "" local best_module = "" for q in modules do local s = snake_of[q] if q ~= o.path and starts_with(name, s .. "_") and #s > #best then best = s best_module = st.files[q].module end end if best ~= "" then push(borrowed, o.path .. ":" .. o.rec.line .. ": borrowed_noun: " .. st.files[o.path].module .. "." .. o.rec.label .. " names the module " .. best_module) end end sort(fed, {"key"}) local lines_out = {} for f in fed do push(lines_out, f.text) end for b in borrowed do push(lines_out, b) end local summary = "rank_boundary_hints (Roc): " .. plural(#users, "file") .. ", " .. plural(#modules, "module") .. ", " .. plural(#owned, "public member") .. "; fed_to_one " .. #fed .. " (" .. drawing .. " drawn with), borrowed_noun " .. #borrowed .. "; " .. pooled_out .. " more used by one module but maybe called by method name elsewhere, left out" return {summary = summary, lines = lines_out, refused = st.refused, lost = st.lost} end function self_test() local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/rank_boundary_hints/" local failures = {} local trees = {} local loud = hints(at .. "loud_pair", "*.roc", "", "", trees) local ls = loud.lines check(failures, #loud.refused == 0 and #loud.lost == 0, "loud: refused or lost: " .. join(loud.refused, "; ") .. join(loud.lost, "; ")) -- Sun.glow is called as a method on a parameter typed as a Sun, and the -- two drawn-with members tie on uses, so they go by name. Backdrop's -- sun_shapes borrows Sun's noun as sky_top_stop borrows Sky's. -- Sun.ring_size's user halo builds its shape through a helper, and is -- annotated to give one. local want = { at .. "loud_pair/Sun.roc:10: fed_to_one: Sun.glow is used only by Backdrop, 1 use; Backdrop draws with it in sun_shapes (Disc, gives a Shape)", at .. "loud_pair/Sun.roc:6: fed_to_one: Sun.look is used only by Backdrop, 1 use; Backdrop draws with it in sun_shapes (Disc, gives a Shape)", at .. "loud_pair/Sun.roc:26: fed_to_one: Sun.ring_size is used only by Backdrop, 1 use; Backdrop draws with it in halo (gives a Shape)", at .. "loud_pair/Sun.roc:14: fed_to_one: Sun.tint is used only by Backdrop, 1 use", at .. "loud_pair/Backdrop.roc:8: borrowed_noun: Backdrop.sky_top_stop names the module Sky", at .. "loud_pair/Backdrop.roc:16: borrowed_noun: Backdrop.sun_shapes names the module Sun", } check(failures, join(ls, "\n") == join(want, "\n"), "loud lines, got:\n" .. join(ls, "\n")) check(failures, loud.summary == "rank_boundary_hints (Roc): 4 files, 4 modules, 13 public members; fed_to_one 4 (3 drawn with), borrowed_noun 2; 0 more used by one module but maybe called by method name elsewhere, left out", "loud summary: " .. loud.summary) local quiet = hints(at .. "quiet_pair", "*.roc", "", "", trees) check(failures, #quiet.refused == 0 and #quiet.lost == 0, "quiet: refused or lost: " .. join(quiet.refused, "; ") .. join(quiet.lost, "; ")) check(failures, #quiet.lines == 0, "quiet lines, got:\n" .. join(quiet.lines, "\n")) check(failures, quiet.summary == "rank_boundary_hints (Roc): 3 files, 2 modules, 9 public members; fed_to_one 0 (0 drawn with), borrowed_noun 0; 0 more used by one module but maybe called by method name elsewhere, left out", "quiet summary: " .. quiet.summary) for f in failures do print("FAIL: " .. f) end if #failures > 0 then fail("rank_boundary_hints: " .. #failures .. " self-test checks failed") end print("rank_boundary_hints: self test passed") return nil end if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local r = hints(arg("root", "."), arg("glob", "*.roc"), arg("clients", ""), arg("packages", ""), {}) print_findings(r.summary, r.lines) for l in r.lost do print("lost: " .. l) end for l in r.refused do print("refused: " .. l) end if #r.lost > 0 or #r.refused > 0 then fail("rank_boundary_hints: " .. #r.lost .. " imports name no file and " .. #r.refused .. " files don't parse (named above); the hints count the rest") end end

name: cookbook/roc/rename.shale
html: -- This recipe renames one identifier across a tree of Roc code, by whole -- words, so renaming `portion` leaves `proportion` and `portion_size` alone, -- and `Rider` leaves `RiderState`. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/rename.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- glob=app/**/*.roc -- from=portion -- to=share -- ARGS -- shale cookbook:roc/rename.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to rename in, `**/*.roc` by default; several globs -- may be given, separated by commas; -- from, to the name and its new name, each a whole identifier; -- module with `module=Ride`, only Ride's own `from` is renamed: the -- qualified form `Ride.from` in every file, and `from` bare -- inside `Ride.roc`, its declaration among them. Without it, -- every bare `from` and every `Mod.from` is renamed, whatever -- `Mod` is; -- skip globs to leave out, separated by commas (a huge data file); -- fields with `fields=1`, a record field named `from` is renamed too: -- `.from` after a value (`slice.from`, which is also how a -- method call reads), and `from:` in a record or a record type. -- Without it they are left; -- book a markdown file whose `{{code Mod.from ...}}` includes are -- renamed too, `Mod` held to `module=` when it is given. Any -- other mention of `from` in the book (prose, an include's -- `from "..."` text) is left and counted as in a string; -- to_module with `to_module=RiderView` (and `module=Geom`), Geom's `from` -- moves to RiderView: each `Geom.from` becomes `RiderView.to` -- (`to` is `from` unless given), or bare `to` inside -- `RiderView.roc`. A file that changed gains `import RiderView` -- beside its `import Geom` (`import game.Geom` gives -- `import game.RiderView`) unless it imports RiderView already, -- and loses `import Geom` when no `Geom.` is left in its code. -- A changed file whose `import Geom` exposes or aliases, or -- which has none, is refused, and a refusal writes no file. -- Bare uses are left: the declarations move by hand; -- dry with `dry=1`, the counts are reported and nothing is written; -- self_test with `self_test=1`, run the plants in -- `cookbook/roc/plants/rename/` on copies under `scratch:`. -- -- What counts as a use: `from` with no letter, digit, `_` or `$` either -- side, in code. A `from` in a comment or inside a string is left and -- counted (`left in comments`, `left in strings`), since those are often -- prose; a `${...}` interpolation is code. A `from` followed by `:` is a -- record field when it comes after `{` or `,`, or its line ends in `,`; -- otherwise it is a declaration. -- -- What it can't see: the text is read line by line, not parsed, so a -- multi-line string's lines read as code. A record field written as a pun -- (`{ from }`, `{ from, other }`) is renamed with the variable, which changes -- the field's name. An import's alias (`import pkg.Ride as R`) and a name -- an import exposes (`exposing [from]`) are not followed under `module=`. -- `roc check` judges the result. -- -- The output is one line per file that changed or holds a left mention, then -- the total. The run fails when nothing was renamed: a rename that renames -- nothing is a mistake. No file is written until every file has been read, -- so a refusal leaves the tree as it was. -- -- shale cookbook:roc/rename.shale from=RiderPoint module=Geom to_module=RiderView -- budget: steps=400000000 reads=100000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=2000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const FROM = arg("from", "") const TO = arg("to", FROM) const MODULE = arg("module", "") const TO_MODULE = arg("to_module", "") const MOVE = TO_MODULE ~= "" const SKIP = arg("skip", "") const FIELDS = arg("fields", "") == "1" const BOOK = arg("book", "") const DRY = arg("dry", "") == "1" const IDENT = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_$" const UPPER = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" function is_ident(c) return c ~= "" and contains(IDENT, c) end function is_name(s) if s == "" then return false end for i = 1, #s do if not is_ident(sub(s, i, i)) then return false end end return true end -- Whether byte `at` of `line` is in code, a string or a comment. function context_at(line, at) local state = "code" local interp = false local depth = 0 local i = 1 while i < at do local c = sub(line, i, i) if state == "code" then if c == "#" then return "comment" end if c == "\"" then state = "string" elseif interp and c == "{" then depth = depth + 1 elseif interp and c == "}" then if depth == 0 then state = "string" interp = false else depth = depth - 1 end end else if c == "\\" then i = i + 1 elseif c == "\"" then state = "code" elseif c == "$" and sub(line, i + 1, i + 1) == "{" then state = "code" interp = true depth = 0 i = i + 1 end end i = i + 1 end return state end -- The identifier that ends just before the `.` at byte `dot`. function qualifier_of(line, dot) local s = dot while s > 1 and is_ident(sub(line, s - 1, s - 1)) do s = s - 1 end return sub(line, s, dot - 1) end -- Whether the name at `at`, ending before `stop`, is a record field's -- declaration: `name:` after `{` or `,`, or on a line that ends in `,`. function is_field_def(line, at, stop) local rest = trim(sub(line, stop)) if not starts_with(rest, ":") or starts_with(rest, ":=") or starts_with(rest, "::") then return false end local before = trim(sub(line, 1, at - 1)) if ends_with(before, "{") or ends_with(before, ",") then return true end return ends_with(trim(line), ",") end function is_wanted(line, at, stop, in_module) if at > 1 and sub(line, at - 1, at - 1) == "." then local q = qualifier_of(line, at - 1) if q ~= "" and contains(UPPER, sub(q, 1, 1)) then return MODULE == "" or q == MODULE end return FIELDS end if MOVE then return false end if MODULE ~= "" and not in_module then return false end if is_field_def(line, at, stop) then return FIELDS end return true end function rename_line(line, in_module, counts) local out = "" local copied = 1 local pos = 1 while true do local at = find(line, FROM, pos) if at == nil then break end local stop = at + #FROM pos = at + 1 local before = "" if at > 1 then before = sub(line, at - 1, at - 1) end if not is_ident(before) and not is_ident(sub(line, stop, stop)) then local where = context_at(line, at) if where == "comment" then counts.comments = counts.comments + 1 elseif where == "string" then counts.strings = counts.strings + 1 elseif MOVE and is_wanted(line, at, stop, in_module) then -- A move rewrites the qualifier too; `in_module` is whether this -- is the new module's own file, where the name stands bare. local start = at - 1 - #qualifier_of(line, at - 1) local name = TO_MODULE .. "." .. TO if in_module then name = TO end out = out .. sub(line, copied, start - 1) .. name copied = stop pos = stop counts.renamed = counts.renamed + 1 elseif is_wanted(line, at, stop, in_module) then out = out .. sub(line, copied, at - 1) .. TO copied = stop pos = stop counts.renamed = counts.renamed + 1 end end end return out .. sub(line, copied) end -- Every whole-word `from` the line held but its renamed includes is left. -- They are counted first, since a move can keep the name. function rename_book_line(line, counts) local pos = 1 while true do local at = find(line, FROM, pos) if at == nil then break end local stop = at + #FROM if (at == 1 or not is_ident(sub(line, at - 1, at - 1))) and not is_ident(sub(line, stop, stop)) then counts.strings = counts.strings + 1 end pos = at + 1 end pos = 1 while true do local at = find(line, "{{code ", pos) if at == nil then break end local s = at + 7 local e = s while e <= #line and (is_ident(sub(line, e, e)) or sub(line, e, e) == ".") do e = e + 1 end local parts = split(sub(line, s, e - 1), ".") if #parts == 2 and parts[2] == FROM and (MODULE == "" or parts[1] == MODULE) then local qualifier = parts[1] if MOVE then qualifier = TO_MODULE end line = sub(line, 1, s - 1) .. qualifier .. "." .. TO .. sub(line, e) counts.renamed = counts.renamed + 1 counts.strings = counts.strings - 1 end pos = s end return line end -- The module an `import` line names: `import game.Geom` gives name `Geom`, -- prefix `game.`, and `tail`, what follows (an `exposing [...]` or `as G`). function import_of(line) local t = trim(line) if not starts_with(t, "import ") then return nil end local rest = trim(sub(t, 8)) local e = 1 while e <= #rest and (is_ident(sub(rest, e, e)) or sub(rest, e, e) == ".") do e = e + 1 end local token = sub(rest, 1, e - 1) local parts = split(token, ".") local name = parts[#parts] return {name = name, prefix = sub(token, 1, #token - #name), tail = trim(sub(rest, e)), indent = sub(line, 1, find(line, "import") - 1)} end -- Whether a line other than an import still says `MODULE.name` in code. function uses_module(lines) local q = MODULE .. "." for line in lines do if import_of(line) == nil then local pos = 1 while true do local at = find(line, q, pos) if at == nil then break end pos = at + 1 local before = "" if at > 1 then before = sub(line, at - 1, at - 1) end if not is_ident(before) and before ~= "." and is_ident(sub(line, at + #q, at + #q)) and context_at(line, at) == "code" then return true end end end end return false end -- A moved file's import block: `import TO_MODULE` added beside the old -- import unless present (or this is TO_MODULE's own file), and the old one -- dropped when no `MODULE.` is left. Gives the lines, or a refusal. function move_imports(lines, own_file, counts) local old_at = 0 local has_new = false for i = 1, #lines do local imp = import_of(lines[i]) if imp ~= nil and imp.name == MODULE and old_at == 0 then old_at = i end if imp ~= nil and imp.name == TO_MODULE then has_new = true end end if old_at == 0 then return {refusal = "it says `" .. MODULE .. "." .. FROM .. "` but has no `import " .. MODULE .. "` line"} end local old = import_of(lines[old_at]) if old.tail ~= "" and not starts_with(old.tail, "#") then return {refusal = "its `import " .. MODULE .. "` has `" .. old.tail .. "`, which a move doesn't follow: edit that import by hand first"} end local keep_old = uses_module(lines) local out = {} for i = 1, #lines do if i ~= old_at then push(out, lines[i]) else if keep_old then push(out, lines[i]) else counts.dropped = true end if not has_new and not own_file then push(out, old.indent .. "import " .. old.prefix .. TO_MODULE) counts.added = true end end end return {lines = out, refusal = ""} end -- Renames in one file and gives its counts, its new text, and a refusal -- (`""` when there is none). Nothing is written here. function rename_file(p, is_book) local counts = {renamed = 0, comments = 0, strings = 0, added = false, dropped = false} local result = {counts = counts, text = "", refusal = ""} local was = read(p) local needle = FROM if is_book then needle = "{{code " end if not contains(was, FROM) or not contains(was, needle) then return result end local in_module = MODULE ~= "" and basename(p) == MODULE .. ".roc" if MOVE then in_module = basename(p) == TO_MODULE .. ".roc" end if MODULE ~= "" and (MOVE or not in_module) and not is_book and not contains(was, MODULE .. "." .. FROM) then return result end local out = {} for line in split(was, "\n") do if not contains(line, FROM) then push(out, line) elseif is_book then push(out, rename_book_line(line, counts)) else push(out, rename_line(line, in_module, counts)) end end if MOVE and not is_book and counts.renamed > 0 then local m = move_imports(out, in_module, counts) if m.refusal ~= "" then result.refusal = m.refusal return result end out = m.lines end result.text = join(out, "\n") return result end function report_line(p, c) local parts = {} if c.renamed > 0 then push(parts, c.renamed .. " renamed") end if c.comments > 0 then push(parts, c.comments .. " left in comments") end if c.strings > 0 then push(parts, c.strings .. " left in strings") end if c.added then push(parts, "import " .. TO_MODULE .. " added") end if c.dropped then push(parts, "import " .. MODULE .. " dropped") end return p .. ": " .. join(parts, ", ") end -- A copy of the plant folder `name` under `scratch`, its .roc and .md files. function copy_plants(name, scratch) local dir = scratch .. "/" .. name mkdir(dir) for p in glob("cookbook:roc/plants/rename/" .. name .. "/*") do if ends_with(p, ".roc") or ends_with(p, ".md") then replace(dir .. "/" .. basename(p), read(p)) end end return dir end function child(args) local argv = {"shale", real("cookbook:roc/rename.shale")} for a in args do push(argv, a) end return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 40}) end function expect_ok(what, r, says, wrong) if r.code ~= 0 then push(wrong, what .. ": exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. r.out) end for s in says do if not contains(r.out, s) then push(wrong, what .. ": the output doesn't say `" .. s .. "`: " .. r.out) end end return nil end function expect_same(what, got, want, wrong) if read(got) ~= read(want) then push(wrong, what .. ": " .. got .. " is not as " .. want .. ":\n" .. read(got)) end return nil end -- A move of `Geom.RiderPoint` to RiderView, with `more` arguments. function move_args(more) local a = {"from=RiderPoint", "module=Geom", "to_module=RiderView"} for x in more do push(a, x) end return a end function self_test() local plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/rename/" local scratch = fresh_dir("scratch:", "rename") local wrong = {} local d = copy_plants("portion", scratch) local r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=portion", "to=share", "skip=" .. d .. "/data.roc"}) expect_ok("portion", r, {"shapes.roc: 8 renamed, 2 left in comments, 2 left in strings", "8 renamed in 1 file of 1"}, wrong) expect_same("portion", d .. "/shapes.roc", plants .. "portion/shapes.want", wrong) expect_same("portion's skip", d .. "/data.roc", plants .. "portion/data.roc", wrong) d = copy_plants("portion", scratch .. "/fields") r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/shapes.roc", "from=portion", "to=share", "fields=1"}) expect_ok("portion fields=1", r, {"shapes.roc: 11 renamed, 2 left in comments, 2 left in strings"}, wrong) expect_same("portion fields=1", d .. "/shapes.roc", plants .. "portion/shapes.fields.want", wrong) d = copy_plants("rider", scratch) r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=Rider", "to=Cyclist", "module=Ride", "book=" .. d .. "/book.md"}) expect_ok("Rider module=Ride", r, {"Ride.roc: 5 renamed", "Uses.roc: 1 renamed", "book.md: 2 renamed, 2 left in strings", "8 renamed in 3 files of 3"}, wrong) expect_same("Rider module=Ride", d .. "/Ride.roc", plants .. "rider/Ride.want", wrong) expect_same("Rider module=Ride", d .. "/Uses.roc", plants .. "rider/Uses.want", wrong) expect_same("Rider module=Ride", d .. "/book.md", plants .. "rider/book.want", wrong) d = copy_plants("portion", scratch .. "/dry") r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=portion", "to=share", "dry=1"}) expect_ok("dry=1", r, {"shapes.roc: 8 renamed", "data.roc: 2 renamed", "dry run, nothing written"}, wrong) expect_same("dry=1", d .. "/shapes.roc", plants .. "portion/shapes.roc", wrong) expect_same("dry=1", d .. "/data.roc", plants .. "portion/data.roc", wrong) r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=portio", "to=share"}) if r.code == 0 or not contains(r.out, "nothing matched") then push(wrong, "a rename of nothing (`portio`) should fail saying so: exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. r.out) end r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=portion", "to=share", "module=Ride"}) if r.code == 0 or not contains(r.out, "nothing matched") then push(wrong, "a rename of `Ride.portion`, which no file has, should fail: exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. r.out) end d = copy_plants("move", scratch) r = child(move_args({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "skip=" .. d .. "/Exposes.roc", "book=" .. d .. "/book.md"})) expect_ok("move", r, {"Drops.roc: 1 renamed, 1 left in comments, 1 left in strings, import RiderView added, import Geom dropped", "Keeps.roc: 2 renamed, import RiderView added", "Already.roc: 1 renamed, import Geom dropped", "RiderView.roc: 1 renamed, import Geom dropped", "book.md: 1 renamed", "move `Geom.RiderPoint` to `RiderView.RiderPoint`: 6 renamed in 5 files of 6"}, wrong) if contains(r.out, "Keeps.roc: 2 renamed, import RiderView added, import Geom dropped") then push(wrong, "move: Keeps.roc still says `Geom.near` and must keep its import: " .. r.out) end if contains(r.out, "Geom.roc:") then push(wrong, "move: Geom.roc has no `Geom.RiderPoint` and should be left: " .. r.out) end for name in {"Drops", "Keeps", "Already", "RiderView"} do expect_same("move", d .. "/" .. name .. ".roc", plants .. "move/" .. name .. ".want", wrong) end expect_same("move", d .. "/book.md", plants .. "move/book.want", wrong) expect_same("move", d .. "/Geom.roc", plants .. "move/Geom.roc", wrong) d = copy_plants("move", scratch .. "/move_dry") r = child(move_args({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "skip=" .. d .. "/Exposes.roc", "dry=1"})) expect_ok("move dry=1", r, {"Drops.roc: 1 renamed", "import Geom dropped", "5 renamed in 4 files of 5 (dry run, nothing written)"}, wrong) expect_same("move dry=1", d .. "/Drops.roc", plants .. "move/Drops.roc", wrong) r = child(move_args({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc"})) if r.code == 0 or not contains(r.out, "Exposes.roc: its `import Geom` has `exposing [near]`") then push(wrong, "a move into a file whose `import Geom` exposes should be refused: exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. r.out) end expect_same("a refused move", d .. "/Drops.roc", plants .. "move/Drops.roc", wrong) expect_same("a refused move", d .. "/Exposes.roc", plants .. "move/Exposes.roc", wrong) r = child({"glob=" .. d .. "/*.roc", "from=RiderPont", "module=Geom", "to_module=RiderView"}) if r.code == 0 or not contains(r.out, "nothing matched") then push(wrong, "a move of nothing (`RiderPont`) should fail saying so: exited " .. r.code .. ": " .. r.out) end remove_tree(scratch) for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("rename self_test: " .. #wrong .. " wrong") end print("rename (Roc) self_test: PASS (portion, fields=1, module=Ride with a book, skip=, dry=1, two renames of nothing that fail, and to_module= moves: imports added, kept, dropped, already there, refused, dry, and of nothing)") return nil end function rename_tree() if not is_name(FROM) or not is_name(TO) then fail("rename: from= and to= must each be an identifier, e.g. from=portion to=share") end if not MOVE and arg("to", "") == "" then fail("rename: to= is missing, e.g. from=portion to=share") end if FROM == TO and not MOVE then fail("rename: from= and to= are the same") end if MODULE ~= "" and not is_name(MODULE) then fail("rename: module= must be a module's name, e.g. module=Ride") end if MOVE then if MODULE == "" or not is_name(TO_MODULE) then fail("rename: to_module= moves a name from module= to another module, e.g. module=Geom to_module=RiderView") end if MODULE == TO_MODULE then fail("rename: module= and to_module= are the same") end if FIELDS then fail("rename: fields=1 and to_module= don't go together: a move takes `Mod.name` alone") end end local skipped = {} if SKIP ~= "" then for g in split(SKIP, ",") do for p in glob(trim(g)) do skipped[p] = true end end end local paths = {} for g in split(GLOB, ",") do for p in glob(trim(g)) do if not has_key(skipped, p) then push(paths, p) end end end if BOOK ~= "" then push(paths, BOOK) end local total = 0 local files = 0 local changed = {} local refusals = {} for p in paths do local f = rename_file(p, p == BOOK) local c = f.counts if f.refusal ~= "" then push(refusals, p .. ": " .. f.refusal) else if c.renamed + c.comments + c.strings > 0 then print(report_line(p, c)) end if c.renamed > 0 then total = total + c.renamed files = files + 1 push(changed, {path = p, text = f.text}) end end yield() end -- Every file is written only once all of them have been read, so a -- refusal anywhere writes none. if #refusals == 0 and not DRY then for f in changed do replace(f.path, f.text) end end local verb = "rename " local scope = "`" .. FROM .. "`" if MODULE ~= "" then scope = "`" .. MODULE .. "." .. FROM .. "`" end local target = "`" .. TO .. "`" if MOVE then verb = "move " target = "`" .. TO_MODULE .. "." .. TO .. "`" end local plural = "s" if files == 1 then plural = "" end local dry = "" if DRY then dry = " (dry run, nothing written)" end return {total = total, refusals = refusals, line = verb .. scope .. " to " .. target .. ": " .. total .. " renamed in " .. files .. " file" .. plural .. " of " .. #paths .. dry} end -- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a -- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it. if SELF_TEST then self_test() else local r = rename_tree() for w in r.refusals do print("refused " .. w) end print(r.line) if #r.refusals > 0 then fail("rename: " .. #r.refusals .. " file(s) refused, nothing written") end if r.total == 0 then fail("rename: nothing matched " .. r.line) end end

name: cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale
html: -- This recipe rewrites old-style Roc calls as method calls. A call -- `Module.fn(first, rest...)` becomes `first.fn(rest...)` wherever that is -- the same call, that is, wherever the first argument's type is the -- module's own: `List.map(xs, f)` becomes `xs.map(f)`, and -- `Str.concat(a, b)` becomes `a.concat(b)`. Nested calls turn from the -- inside out, so `List.len(List.keep_if(xs, p))` becomes -- `xs.keep_if(p).len()`. -- -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc apply=1 -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc,app/specs.roc -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=src/*.roc root=src/Lib.roc types=0 -- shale cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale self_test=1 -- -- The arguments: -- glob the files to rewrite, `**/*.roc` by default. -- root the app that `roc check` and `roc test` run on. Several apps, -- comma-separated, serve a tree that no one app imports whole, -- such as test-only modules with an app of their own; each file is -- then judged on the first root that imports it. With `types=0` -- only one root is allowed, and it defaults to each file itself. -- apply with `apply=1`, the rewrites that pass are kept. Without it the -- run is a dry run: each trial is written in place and put back -- byte for byte, so the tree ends as it began. -- types with `types=0`, the type checker's types (below) are not read. -- from the glob's file to start at, 1 by default (see the program limit -- below). -- Run it with `--undo-on-stop`, so that a run stopped in the middle of a -- trial (by a budget, or Ctrl-C) puts the trial's file back too. -- -- A syntax tree can't tell a value's type, so the compiler judges each -- rewrite. The candidates come from `roc_tree` (Roc's own parser), and the -- types sort them first (below). A file's remaining candidates are written -- in, and the file passes when `roc check` on its root passes and the -- summary of `roc test` (its count of expects and their results) is what it -- was before. When `roc check` reports an error on a rewritten call's -- lines, that call stays as it was, with the error's title as its reason, -- and the file is tried again without it. A `missing method` error on a -- definition `name = <value>` means the value's type never resolved, and it -- counts against the rewritten calls whose first argument is that `name`. -- Any other error, a warning included, is a stray. A refused call can cause -- errors where its value is used (an `unconditional condition` on an `if` -- it decides), so strays are judged only in a round that refused no call. -- A stray in such a round, a changed `roc test` summary, or a file still -- failing after the last round puts the whole file back, and every -- candidate in it stays, with that reason. Under `apply=1`, a file that -- `roc fmt` found clean before is formatted again after its rewrite. -- -- Some calls are not candidates at all: -- - a function used as a value, like `Str.trim` in `List.map(xs, Str.trim)`; -- - a call of the file's own module, like `Store.load!(id)` in Store.roc. -- Inside its module a function is called by the name it is declared -- with, and listing every such call would bury the ones that need a -- hand. -- These calls are candidates that stay, each listed with its reason: -- - a call on the right of a `|>`, where the pipe gives the first -- argument: `x |> List.concat(y)` is `List.concat(x, y)`, not -- `y.concat()`; -- - a call with an argument that has no span in the tree (the compiler's -- `match`), since its text can't be moved; -- - a call whose first argument is a constant numeric expression, that is, -- number literals (`5`, `-3`, `1.5`, `'a'`) joined only by operators and -- parentheses (`2 + 3`, `-(1 + 2)`). The module call fixes the number's -- type, but a receiver's type defaults: `U64.to_str(5)` is "5", while -- `(5).to_str()` is a `Dec`'s "5.0". Both pass `roc check`, so only an -- `expect` would notice. The same holds for a plain name bound to such an -- expression without an annotation, at its nearest definition (`n = 5` -- earlier in a block, or a top-level `top = 7`). A typed literal -- (`5.U64`), a name, a call or a field anywhere in the expression fixes -- its type, so `n + 1` is a candidate, and so are an annotated name -- (`m : U64`) and a parameter. A name bound to anything else whose type -- only literals give (`start = if c 1 else 0`) is a candidate too, and -- its type defaults the same way; the compiler catches that only where -- the default clashes (the ProvenFails plant), and otherwise only an -- `expect` would. -- Without the types, a call whose first argument has another type -- (`Str.from_utf8(bytes)`, a list) is tried, and stays because the -- compiler reports a `missing method`. -- -- By default the recipe first reads every expression's type from Roc's own -- type checker, `roc-types` (`tools:roc-types/bin/roc-types`, built from -- Shale's `tools/roc_types` and read through cookbook/roc/types.shale). It -- runs once on each root, before any file is tried. The type of each -- candidate's first argument decides what happens to it: -- - a concrete type of another kind (`List(U8)` for a `Str` call, a -- record, a tag union, a function) leaves the call untried, with a -- reason like `the first argument is a List, not a Str`; -- - a type whose head names the module (`Str`, `List(...)`, `MessageRef` -- or `X.MessageRef`) proves the call; -- - a type variable, or no type at that spot, leaves the call to the trial. -- The summary counts each kind. The files whose open calls are all proven -- are written at once, and one `roc check` and one `roc test` on their root -- confirm them together. When that check fails, the files its errors name -- are set aside and the rest are confirmed again; an error in any other -- file, or a changed test summary, sets them all aside. A file set aside, -- and any file with a call the types couldn't settle, goes through the -- trial alone. A proof is not a pass: in `U8.to(0, 3)` the checker types -- `0` as a U8 only because the call makes it one, which is why a constant -- numeric expression is not a candidate. -- When the types can't be read, the run stops rather than going on without -- them. That happens with no `root=` (roc-types reads an app, and reads a -- type module only through an app), a root that is not an app or that the -- checker refuses, a file of the glob that no root imports, and a -- roc-types built for a different Roc than the tree's `roc-version`. With -- `types=0` every candidate is tried. -- -- A Shale run starts at most its `programs` budget of programs, and a very -- large tree needs more. The run then stops before a file it might not finish, prints `go on with -- from=N`, and the next run, given `from=N`, starts at the glob's Nth file. -- A file with nothing to try uses no programs. Under `apply=1`, a stopped -- run has already written the files the confirm kept, and the next run -- finds their calls already turned. Each trial also adds an entry to Roc's -- cache (`~/.cache/roc`), so a tree of a few dozen files can fill several -- gigabytes there. -- -- The output is the summary line (`candidates N, rewritten N, left N`, and -- the programs used), a line `path:line: Module.fn: why` for each call that -- stays, the count of each kind the types found, and the summary again -- (cookbook/findings.shale). -- -- The compiler is the one the tree pins: `tools:roc-<pin>/roc`, with the pin -- read from the `roc-version` file in the directory the run starts in, and -- a run without that file stops. Method lookup has changed between Roc -- nightlies, so a rewrite is judged only by the Roc the tree is built with. -- The self-test uses `SELF_TEST_PIN`. Both come from `roc_bin` in -- cookbook/roc/pinned.shale. -- -- `self_test=1` judges each plant in `cookbook/roc/plants/rewrite_method_calls/` in a -- child run of its own (`plant=<Name>`, run by the `shale` on PATH), so each -- plant gets a run's programs of its own. The child copies the plants to a fresh -- folder under `scratch:` and runs with `apply=1` there. The table `EXPECT` -- below says how many calls each plant must leave, a reason one of them must -- give, and how many confirms and rounds it takes; a plant with a -- `<Name>.want` file must come out as that text. A plant marked `types` runs -- with the types, its root one of the app plants in `ROOT_PLANTS`; the -- others run with `types=0`. A plant with a `stop` must stop its child run -- with that text. The self-test fails at once when roc-types is not -- installed. -- budget: steps=900000000 output_bytes=4000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 changes=100000 change_bytes=2000000000 call_depth=1000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const APPLY = SELF_TEST or arg("apply", "") == "1" const TYPES_ARG = arg("types", "1") if TYPES_ARG ~= "0" and TYPES_ARG ~= "1" then fail("rewrite_method_calls: types=" .. TYPES_ARG .. ": types must be 1 (the default) or 0") end const USE_TYPES = TYPES_ARG == "1" const PLANT = arg("plant", "") const PLANTS_DIR = "cookbook:roc/plants/rewrite_method_calls" const THIS_SCRIPT = "cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale" const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc") const ROOT = arg("root", "") const FROM = tonumber(arg("from", "1")) use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/types.shale") -- Each round leaves out the calls the compiler refused, and the next round -- may find more that their errors hid. const MAX_ROUNDS = 6 -- A file may take `MAX_ROUNDS` checks, a test and, under `apply=1`, two -- `roc fmt`s; the first file on a root also takes the baseline's check and -- test. A file is begun only while that many programs are left. const MAX_PROGRAMS = budget().programs const PROGRAMS_PER_FILE = MAX_ROUNDS + 5 -- The node kinds a receiver can be without parentheses, as in `f(x).len()` -- or `"a".to_utf8()`. Any other (a number, a sum, a lambda, an `if`) is -- wrapped in them: `(a + b).to_str()`. const BARE_RECEIVER_KINDS = {["e-ident"] = true, ["e-apply"] = true, ["e-method-call"] = true, ["e-field-access"] = true, ["e-string"] = true, ["e-list"] = true, ["e-record"] = true, ["e-tuple"] = true, ["e-tag"] = true} -- The number literals whose type only their use fixes (`5`, `-3`, `0x1F`, -- `1.5`, `1e3`, `'a'`). Typed literals like `5.U64` (`e-typed-int`, -- `e-typed-frac`) are not among them. const UNTYPED_NUMBER_LITERALS = {["e-int"] = true, ["e-frac"] = true, ["e-single-quote"] = true} -- Whether node `i` is a constant numeric expression: untyped number literals -- joined only by operators (`e-binop`, `unary`) and parentheses (a -- one-element `e-tuple`), as in `5`, `(5)`, `2 + 3` or `-(1 + 2)`. function is_constant_numeric(t, i) local n = t.nodes[i] if has_key(UNTYPED_NUMBER_LITERALS, n.kind) then return true end local joins = n.kind == "e-binop" or n.kind == "unary" or (n.kind == "e-tuple" and #n.kids == 1) if not joins or #n.kids == 0 then return false end for k in n.kids do if not is_constant_numeric(t, k) then return false end end return true end function is_plain_name(n) return n.kind == "e-ident" and find(n.raw, ".") == nil end -- The name a definition `name = <value>` binds, or "" for any other node. function defined_name(t, n) if n.kind == "s-decl" and #n.kids == 2 and t.nodes[n.kids[1]].kind == "p-ident" then return t.nodes[n.kids[1]].raw end return "" end function has_parameter_named(t, lambda, name) for k in lambda.kids do if t.nodes[k].kind == "args" then for a in t.nodes[k].kids do if t.nodes[a].kind == "p-ident" and t.nodes[a].raw == name then return true end end end end return false end -- Whether the plain name `name`, used at node `at`, is bound without an -- annotation to a constant numeric expression, or to another name that is. -- The binding that counts is the nearest one up the tree: in a block, the -- last definition before the statement holding the use; at the top level, -- any definition, since order doesn't matter there. A lambda parameter of -- that name, or an annotation `name : Type` beside the definition, fixes -- the type, and the answer is false. function is_bound_to_constant_numeric(t, at, name, depth) if depth > 8 then return false end local child = at local up = t.nodes[at].parent while up > 0 do local scope = t.nodes[up] if scope.kind == "e-lambda" and has_parameter_named(t, scope, name) then return false end local in_block = scope.kind == "statements" and scope.parent > 0 and t.nodes[scope.parent].kind == "e-block" local definition = 0 local annotated = false for k in scope.kids do if in_block and k == child then break end local s = t.nodes[k] if defined_name(t, s) == name then definition = k end if s.kind == "s-type-anno" and s.name == name then annotated = true end end if definition > 0 then if annotated then return false end local value = t.nodes[definition].kids[2] if is_constant_numeric(t, value) then return true end local vn = t.nodes[value] return is_plain_name(vn) and is_bound_to_constant_numeric(t, value, vn.raw, depth + 1) end child = up up = scope.parent end return false end -- ── the tree ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- A node's span as byte offsets into the file's text: `from` is its first -- byte (1-based) and `to` one past its last. nil for a node with no position. function span_of(n, starts) if n.line == 0 then return nil end return {from = starts[n.line] + n.col - 1, to = starts[n.end_line] + n.end_col - 1} end -- The byte offset at which each line starts. function line_starts(text) local out = {1} local at = 1 for l in split(text, "\n") do at = at + #l + 1 push(out, at) end return out end -- Every file's syntax tree from `roc_tree`, by path: `{nodes, text, starts}`, -- each node `{kind, raw, name, span, has_span, kids, parent, region}`, where -- `kids` are its children's indexes in order, `parent` is 0 at the top, and -- `region` is the compiler's `line:col:end_line:end_col`, by which the types -- are looked up. function parse_trees(paths) local out = {} for f in roc_tree(paths) do if f.err ~= "" then fail("rewrite_method_calls: roc-ast: " .. f.path .. ": " .. f.err) end local text = read(f.path) local t = {nodes = {}, text = text, starts = line_starts(text)} for n in f.nodes do local span = span_of(n, t.starts) push(t.nodes, {kind = n.kind, raw = get(n, "raw", ""), name = get(n, "name", ""), span = span or {from = 0, to = 0}, has_span = span ~= nil, kids = n.kids, parent = n.parent, region = n.line .. ":" .. n.col .. ":" .. n.end_line .. ":" .. n.end_col}) end out[f.path] = t end return out end -- The nodes that carry node `i`'s text: `i` itself when it has a span, else -- its nearest descendants that do (`args` and `receiver` have none). function spanned_nodes(t, i) local n = t.nodes[i] if n.has_span then return {i} end local out = {} for k in n.kids do for j in spanned_nodes(t, k) do push(out, j) end end return out end function line_at(t, offset) local l = 1 while l < #t.starts and t.starts[l + 1] <= offset do l = l + 1 end return l end -- The reason the call `module.fn(...)` at node `i` must stay, whatever the -- types say, or "" when it may be tried. function reason_call_stays(t, i, module, fn) local n = t.nodes[i] local parent = n.parent > 0 and t.nodes[n.parent] or nil if parent ~= nil and parent.kind == "e-arrow-call" and parent.kids[2] == i then return "the right of a `|>`, whose first argument the pipe gives" end -- An argument with no span (the compiler's `e-match`) begins before any -- node it holds, at `match`, so its text can't be found, and writing it -- from no span would copy the whole file. for a in drop(n.kids, 1) do if not t.nodes[a].has_span then return "an argument with no span in the tree (" .. t.nodes[a].kind .. "), whose text cannot be moved" end end local first = n.kids[2] local first_node = t.nodes[first] if is_constant_numeric(t, first) then local text = sub(t.text, first_node.span.from, first_node.span.to - 1) if first_node.kind ~= "e-tuple" then text = "(" .. text .. ")" end return "a number literal's type would default as a receiver (`" .. text .. "." .. fn .. "()` is no longer a " .. module .. ")" end if is_plain_name(first_node) and is_bound_to_constant_numeric(t, first, first_node.raw, 0) then return "a number literal's type would default as a receiver (`" .. first_node.raw .. "` is bound to a number literal, unannotated, and `" .. first_node.raw .. "." .. fn .. "()` is no longer a " .. module .. ")" end return "" end -- The calls `Module.fn(first, ...)` in tree `t`, except calls of the file's -- own module, each `{node, module, fn, line, why_left, proven, from_line, -- to_line}`. `why_left` is "" while the call is open to rewriting, else the -- reason it stays. `from_line` and `to_line` are its lines in a trial's text. function candidates_in(t, own_module) local out = {} for i = 1, #t.nodes do local n = t.nodes[i] if n.kind == "e-apply" and #n.kids >= 2 then local callee = t.nodes[n.kids[1]] local m = re_find(callee.raw, "^([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\\.([a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?)$") if callee.kind == "e-ident" and m ~= nil and m.groups[1] ~= own_module then local module = m.groups[1] local fn = m.groups[2] push(out, {node = i, module = module, fn = fn, line = line_at(t, n.span.from), why_left = reason_call_stays(t, i, module, fn), proven = false, from_line = 0, to_line = 0}) end end end return out end -- ── the rewrite ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function emit(writer, s) push(writer.out, s) writer.line = writer.line + #split(s, "\n") - 1 end -- Writes node `i`'s text, from byte `start` on. A call being turned is -- written as a method call. Any other node is written as it is, with each -- child that has a span written in its place by the same rule, so nested -- calls turn too. "(") for k = 2, #args do if k > 2 then emit(writer, ", ") end emit_node(writer, args[k], 0) end emit(writer, ")") c.to_line = writer.line return nil end local at = n.span.from if start > at then at = start end for k in n.kids do for j in spanned_nodes(t, k) do local s = t.nodes[j].span if s.to > at then if s.from > at then emit(writer, sub(t.text, at, s.from - 1)) end emit_node(writer, j, at) at = s.to end end end emit(writer, sub(t.text, at, n.span.to - 1)) return nil end -- The file's text with every candidate in `turning` (keyed by node) turned -- into a method call. Each turned call records its lines in the new text -- (`from_line`, `to_line`), and `t.trial_line_of_node` records each node's -- first line there. function rewritten_text(t, turning) local writer = {out = {}, line = line_at(t, t.nodes[1].span.from), t = t, turning = turning, line_of_node = {}} emit_node(writer, 1, 0) t.trial_line_of_node = writer.line_of_node -- The file node spans what roc-ast parsed; the bytes outside it, such as a -- final newline, are kept. return sub(t.text, 1, t.nodes[1].span.from - 1) .. join(writer.out, "") .. sub(t.text, t.nodes[1].span.to) end function is_below(t, i, top) local at = t.nodes[i].parent while at > 0 do if at == top then return true end at = t.nodes[at].parent end return false end -- A `missing method` error that `roc check` reports on the value of a -- definition `name = <value>`, rather than on a call, means that value's -- type never resolved because its only use was a turned `name.fn()`.
