" (on `" .. name .. "`'s definition)" end blamed = true end end end end return blamed end -- The open candidates by node, as `rewritten_text` takes them, and their count. function open_calls(cands) local turning = {} local count = 0 for c in cands do if c.why_left == "" then turning["" .. c.node] = c count = count + 1 end end return {turning = turning, count = count} end function leave_open_calls(cands, why) for c in cands do if c.why_left == "" then c.why_left = why end end return nil end -- ── the compiler ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Runs `roc check` on `root`: `{ok, errors, out}`, each error `{title, file, -- line}`. A warning counts as an error, since a warning fails the build. function roc_check(ctx, root) ctx.programs_used = ctx.programs_used + 1 local r = run({roc_bin("rewrite_method_calls", SELF_TEST), "check", real(root)}, {timeout_ms = 900000, whole = 64000000}) local errors = {} for l in lines(r.out) do -- An error's heading is `── ✗ <title> ───── <path>:<line>:<col>`, and a -- warning's has `●` in place of `✗`. local is_heading = starts_with(l, "── ✗ ") or starts_with(l, "── ● ") local at = is_heading and re_find(l, " ([^ ]+):([0-9]+):([0-9]+)$") or nil if at ~= nil then local title = trim(split(sub(l, #"── ✗ " + 1), " ─")[1]) push(errors, {title = title, file = basename(at.groups[1]), line = tonumber(at.groups[2])}) end end return {ok = r.ended == "exit" and r.code == 0, errors = errors, out = r.out} end -- The first non-blank line of `out`, for a failure that names no error -- (a crash). function first_line_said(out) for l in lines(out) do if trim(l) ~= "" then return trim(l) end end return "nothing said" end -- The last line of `roc test` on `root`, without its time, and the exit -- code: what a rewrite may not change. function roc_test_summary(ctx, root) ctx.programs_used = ctx.programs_used + 1 local r = run({roc_bin("rewrite_method_calls", SELF_TEST), "test", real(root)}, {timeout_ms = 900000, whole = 64000000}) local said = lines(trim(r.out)) local last = said[#said] or "" local m = re_find(last, "^(.*) in [0-9.]+ ms\\.") return (m ~= nil and m.groups[1] or last) .. " (exit " .. r.code .. ")" end function is_fmt_clean(ctx, p) ctx.programs_used = ctx.programs_used + 1 return run({roc_bin("rewrite_method_calls", SELF_TEST), "fmt", "--check", real(p)}, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20}).code == 0 end function roc_fmt(ctx, p) ctx.programs_used = ctx.programs_used + 1 run({roc_bin("rewrite_method_calls", SELF_TEST), "fmt", real(p)}, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20}) return nil end -- The `roc test` summary of `root` before any rewrite, which every trial on -- that root must match. "` fails before any rewrite: fix it first") end baselines[root] = roc_test_summary(ctx, root) end return baselines[root] end -- ── the types (read unless `types=0`) ──────────────────────────────────── -- Every expression's type in the app `root`, from `roc_types` (one program; -- the library stops the run on a root the checker refuses, whose types -- would be guesses). Returns `{by_region, modules}`: each type keyed by -- `<real path>|line:col:end_line:end_col`, and the set of the modules' real -- paths. Where several expressions share a region, the first that roc-types -- gives, the outermost, is kept as the value written there. "|" .. rec.line .. ":" .. rec.col .. ":" .. rec.end_line .. ":" .. rec.end_col if not has_key(by_region, key) then by_region[key] = rec.type end end end end for l in got.warnings do print("rewrite_method_calls: roc-types " .. root .. ": " .. l) end return {by_region = by_region, modules = set_of(got.paths)} end -- A type's head, as `{head}`, or `{var = true}` for a type variable (`a`, -- `_a`, `a where [...]`). `List(U8)`'s head is `List` and -- `Access.Viewer(Topic.At)`'s is `Access.Viewer`. A function's (an arrow -- outside every bracket) is `function`, `{...}`'s is `record`, `[...]`'s -- is `tag union`, and `(a, b)`'s is `tuple`. function type_head(ty) if find(ty, "->") ~= nil or find(ty, "=>") ~= nil then local depth = 0 for i = 1, #ty - 1 do local ch = sub(ty, i, i) if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then depth = depth + 1 end if ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then depth = depth - 1 end local two = sub(ty, i, i + 1) if depth == 0 and (two == "->" or two == "=>") then return {head = "function"} end end end local first = sub(ty, 1, 1) if first == "{" then return {head = "record"} end if first == "[" then return {head = "tag union"} end if first == "(" then return {head = "tuple"} end if re_find(first, "^[A-Z]$") == nil then return {var = true} end local m = re_find(ty, "^([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)") return {head = m.groups[1]} end -- `word` after its indefinite article: "an" before a vowel letter, "a" -- otherwise (`an Admin`, `a List`). -- "an" before a vowel sound. Each kind -- is counted in `kind_counts`. function judge_by_types(kind_counts, t, cands, p, types) local real_path = real(p) for c in cands do if c.why_left == "" then local key = real_path .. "|" .. t.nodes[t.nodes[c.node].kids[2]].region if not has_key(types.by_region, key) then incr(kind_counts, "no type") else local h = type_head(types.by_region[key]) if has_key(h, "var") then incr(kind_counts, "a type variable") else local segments = split(h.head, ".") if h.head == c.module or segments[#segments] == c.module then incr(kind_counts, "the module's type") c.proven = true else incr(kind_counts, "another type") c.why_left = "the first argument is " .. with_article(h.head) .. ", not " .. with_article(c.module) end end end end end return nil end -- ── the trial and the confirm ──────────────────────────────────────────── -- Tries one file's open candidates, round by round, until `roc check` -- passes or nothing is left to try, then runs the test. ", was " .. baseline_test .. "; the file is put back") replace(p, original) return 0 end if not APPLY then replace(p, original) end return open.count end -- Each error on a turned call's lines leaves that call. "; the file is put back") replace(p, original) return 0 end for c in cands do c.from_line = 0 end end leave_open_calls(cands, "still failing after " .. MAX_ROUNDS .. " rounds; the file is put back") replace(p, original) return 0 end -- Confirms the files whose open calls are all proven: `files` (`{p, t, -- cands}`) are written with all their calls turned, at once, and one -- `roc check` on `root` and one `roc test` judge them together. ":" .. c.line .. ": " .. c.module .. "." .. c.fn .. ": " .. c.why_left) end end end end return total end -- ── the self-test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function report_check(failures, passed, what) if passed then print("ok " .. what) else print("FAIL " .. what) failures.count = failures.count + 1 end return nil end -- For each plant: how many calls it must leave (`left`), a reason one of -- them must give (`why`), the root it is judged on (`root`, the plant -- itself by default), whether it runs with the types (`types`), and how -- many confirms and trial rounds it takes. ": left because " .. want.why) end local want_path = PLANTS_DIR .. "/" .. name .. ".want" if exists(want_path) then report_check(failures, read(p) == read(want_path), name .. ": comes out as " .. name .. ".want") end -- In Typed, the types turn one call and leave the other, so the trial -- decides neither. local kinds = got.ctx.type_kind_counts if name == "Typed" then report_check(failures, #keys(kinds) == 2 and get(kinds, "another type", 0) == 1 and get(kinds, "the module's type", 0) == 1, name .. ": by type, " .. json_write(kinds)) end local confirms = got.ctx.confirms local rounds = got.ctx.rounds local want_confirms = get(want, "confirms", 0) report_check(failures, confirms == want_confirms, name .. ": " .. confirms .. " confirm(s), want " .. want_confirms) if has_key(want, "rounds") then report_check(failures, rounds == want.rounds, name .. ": " .. rounds .. " round(s), want " .. want.rounds) end if not with_types then report_check(failures, #keys(kinds) == 0 and #keys(got.ctx.types_by_root) == 0, name .. ": under types=0, no roc-types run") end -- With the types, roc-types runs once per root when a candidate is open, -- and not at all on a file with none (`no_types_run`). if with_types then local runs = #keys(got.ctx.types_by_root) local want_runs = has_key(want, "no_types_run") and 0 or #roots report_check(failures, runs == want_runs, name .. ": " .. runs .. " roc-types run(s), want " .. want_runs) end if want.left > 0 and not exists(want_path) then report_check(failures, read(p) == read(PLANTS_DIR .. "/" .. name .. ".roc"), name .. ": put back as it was") end if failures.count > 0 then fail("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: " .. name .. ": " .. failures.count .. " failed") end remove_tree(scratch) return nil end -- Runs every plant in a child run of its own; a failed plant is named, and -- the rest still run. function self_test() if not exists(ROC_TYPES_EXE) then fail("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: no " .. ROC_TYPES_EXE .. ", which the plants marked `types` are judged by: Shale's `shale tools/roc_types/install.shale` installs it") end local failed = {} for file in ls(PLANTS_DIR) do local name = strip_suffix(file, ".roc") if ends_with(file, ".roc") and not has_key(EXPECT, name) and not has_key(ROOT_PLANTS, name) then print("FAIL " .. file .. ": a plant the table does not judge") push(failed, file) end end for name in sort(keys(EXPECT)) do local r = run({"shale", "--root", ".", THIS_SCRIPT, "self_test=1", "plant=" .. name}, {timeout_ms = 3600000, tail = 200}) local stop = get(EXPECT[name], "stop", "") if stop ~= "" then local held = r.ended == "exit" and r.code ~= 0 and contains(r.out, stop) print((held and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": stops, saying " .. stop .. (held and "" or (": " .. trim(r.out)))) if not held then push(failed, name) end else for l in lines(r.out) do if not starts_with(l, "── budgets") then print(l) end end if r.ended ~= "exit" or r.code ~= 0 then push(failed, name) end end end if #failed > 0 then fail("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: " .. #failed .. " plant(s) failed: " .. join(failed, ", ")) end print("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: every plant as it says") end if PLANT ~= "" and not SELF_TEST then fail("rewrite_method_calls: plant= is for the self-test's child runs, and needs self_test=1") elseif SELF_TEST and PLANT ~= "" then self_test_plant(PLANT) elseif SELF_TEST then self_test() else local paths = glob(GLOB) local total = run_all(paths, ROOT, FROM, nil, USE_TYPES, roc_bin("rewrite_method_calls", SELF_TEST)) local summary = (APPLY and "" or "dry run: ") .. "candidates " .. total.candidates .. ", rewritten " .. total.rewritten .. ", left " .. total.left .. ", programs " .. total.ctx.programs_used .. " (checks: " .. total.ctx.confirms .. " confirming proven calls, " .. total.ctx.rounds .. " in trial rounds)" if total.next > 0 then summary = summary .. ", in files " .. FROM .. " to " .. (total.next - 1) .. " of " .. #paths .. ": a run holds " .. MAX_PROGRAMS .. " programs; go on with from=" .. total.next end local finding_lines = total.lines if USE_TYPES then local kinds = {} for kind in sort(keys(total.ctx.type_kind_counts)) do push(kinds, kind .. " " .. total.ctx.type_kind_counts[kind]) end push(finding_lines, "types: the first arguments of the candidates the types judged: " .. join(kinds, ", ")) end print_findings(summary, finding_lines) end

name: cookbook/roc/types.shale
html: -- A library for the Roc recipes that check types, loaded with -- `use("cookbook:roc/types.shale")`. It runs roc-types, Shale's tool that -- asks Roc's own type checker for the type of every expression and pattern -- in an app, and reads what the tool prints. The tool's source is -- tools/roc_types, and `shale tools/roc_types/install.shale` installs it -- under the `tools` mount. Its output format is described at the top of -- tools/roc_types/main.zig; this file reads version 1 of that format. const ROC_TYPES_EXE = "tools:roc-types/bin/roc-types" const ROC_TYPES_FORMAT = "1" -- A type's text with roc-types' escapes of `\`, tab, newline and carriage -- return undone. -- The checker for the compiler `roc`: the one installed for that compiler's -- pin, `tools:roc-types-<pin>/bin/roc-types`, as compilers sit side by side, -- or else the default. A checker built for another pin is refused by name -- when its first line is read. function roc_types_exe(roc) local m = re_find(roc, "/roc-([^/]+)/roc$") if m ~= nil then local own = "tools:roc-types-" .. m.groups[1] .. "/bin/roc-types" if exists(own) then return own end end return ROC_TYPES_EXE end function unescape_roc_type(s) local out = {} local i = 1 while i <= #s do local ch = sub(s, i, i) if ch == "\\" and i < #s then local esc = sub(s, i + 1, i + 1) if esc == "t" then push(out, "\t") elseif esc == "n" then push(out, "\n") elseif esc == "r" then push(out, "\r") elseif esc == "\\" then push(out, "\\") else fail("`roc_types`: a type with a bad escape, `\\" .. esc .. "`: " .. s) end i = i + 2 else if ch == "\\" then fail("`roc_types`: a type ending in a lone `\\`: " .. s) end push(out, ch) i = i + 1 end end return join(out, "") end -- Reads `r`, the result of running roc-types on `root`, into the record -- `roc_types` returns. `roc` is the OS path of the Roc compiler the tree is -- built with. The pin in roc-types' first line is checked against it before -- anything else, because the errors (or the silence) of a checker from -- another Roc version say nothing about this tree. function parse_roc_types_output(r, root, roc) local all = lines(r.out) local head = "" if #all > 0 then head = all[1] end if not starts_with(head, "roc-types ") then fail("`roc_types`: no `roc-types " .. ROC_TYPES_FORMAT .. "` header (" .. root .. ", the first line `" .. head .. "`): an older roc-types, or not roc-types; Shale's `shale tools/roc_types/install.shale` installs the one this reads") end local said = words(head) if #said < 2 or said[2] ~= ROC_TYPES_FORMAT then fail("`roc_types`: roc-types' header is `" .. head .. "`, not format " .. ROC_TYPES_FORMAT .. "'s, the one this reads: Shale's `shale tools/roc_types/install.shale` installs the matching roc-types") end if #said ~= 3 then fail("`roc_types`: a header that is not `roc-types <N> <pin>`: " .. head) end local own = "tools:roc-" .. said[3] .. "/roc" if not exists(own) or real(own) ~= roc then fail("`roc_types`: roc-types reads Roc " .. said[3] .. ", and " .. root .. "'s tree is built with " .. roc .. ": its types would be another compiler's. Install the roc-types of the tree's pin (Shale's tools/roc_types), or move the tree to " .. said[3]) end if r.ended ~= "exit" or r.code ~= 0 then local why = slice(all, 2, 61) if #all > 61 then push(why, "(" .. (#all - 61) .. " lines more)") end fail("`roc_types`: roc-types " .. root .. " " .. (r.ended == "exit" and ("exited " .. r.code) or r.ended) .. ", what it said:\n" .. join(why, "\n")) end local out = {pin = said[3], paths = {}, modules = {}, warnings = {}} local path = "" for k = 2, #all do local l = all[k] if starts_with(l, "== ") then path = sub(l, 4) if not starts_with(path, "/") then fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. ", a module path that is not absolute: " .. path) end if has_key(out.modules, path) then fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. ", module " .. path .. " twice") end out.modules[path] = {} push(out.paths, path) elseif path == "" then push(out.warnings, l) elseif starts_with(l, "t\t") then local f = split(l, "\t") if #f ~= 8 then fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. ", a record of " .. #f .. " fields, not 8: " .. l) end if f[2] ~= "expr" and f[2] ~= "pat" then fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. ", a record of kind `" .. f[2] .. "`") end local ty = f[8] if find(ty, "\\") ~= nil then ty = unescape_roc_type(ty) end local span = {} for x in slice(f, 4, 7) do local n = parse_int(x) if n == nil then fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. ", a span's number `" .. x .. "`") end push(span, n) end push(out.modules[path], {kind = f[2], tag = f[3], line = span[1], col = span[2], end_line = span[3], end_col = span[4], type = ty}) else fail("`roc_types`: line " .. k .. " is no record of roc-types' format: " .. l) end end return out end -- The types of every module reachable from the app `root`, as roc-types -- reports them. `roc` is the OS path of the tree's Roc compiler, as -- `roc_bin` in cookbook/roc/pinned.shale gives it. The result is a record: -- paths: each module's real, absolute path, in roc-types' order; -- modules: for each path, a list of `{kind, tag, line, col, end_line, -- end_col, type}`, where `kind` is "expr" or "pat". The list is in the -- checker's pre-order, so when several nodes share a region, the -- outermost comes first; -- warnings: the lines roc-types printed before the first module; -- pin: the Roc version roc-types was built from. -- The run fails, showing what roc-types said, when the checker rejects the -- app (a type error, a module left unchecked, a file that isn't an app), -- because the types would then be guesses. It also fails when roc-types is -- missing, prints a format this file doesn't read, or was built for a Roc -- version other than `roc`'s. function roc_types(root, roc) local exe = roc_types_exe(roc) if not exists(exe) then fail("`roc_types`: no " .. exe .. ": Shale's `shale tools/roc_types/install.shale` installs it") end return parse_roc_types_output(run({real(exe), real(root)}, {timeout_ms = 300000, whole = 64000000}), root, roc) end -- The app paths in a recipe's `root=` argument, which may list several, -- `root=a.roc,b.roc`, when no one app imports every file the recipe checks. -- `who` names the recipe in the failure when `root=` is empty. function roc_types_root_apps(who, root) local out = {} for r in split(root, ",") do if trim(r) ~= "" then push(out, trim(r)) end end if #out == 0 then fail(who .. ": types=1 needs root=, an app (or several, `root=a.roc,b.roc`) importing the files of the glob: roc-types reads an app, and a type module only through one") end return out end -- The key under which `roc_types_for_files` stores the type at a region of a -- file, given the file's real path and anything with the region's -- `line, col, end_line, end_col`. function roc_types_region_key(real_path, region) return real_path .. "|" .. region.line .. ":" .. region.col .. ":" .. region.end_line .. ":" .. region.end_col end -- The types a recipe needs for the files `paths`, gathered by running -- `roc_types` on each app named in `root` (see `roc_types_root_apps`). `who` -- names the recipe in failures. The result is a record: -- pats, exprs: the type of each pattern and expression, by -- `roc_types_region_key`. When several nodes share a region, the -- outermost one's type is kept, and when two apps reach one module, -- the first app's types are kept; -- real: for each file of `paths` that some app reaches, its real path; -- unreached: a line `not reached by <root>: <path>` for each file of -- `paths` that no app reaches, except those in the set `exempt`. -- A recipe checks an unreached file without types and passes `unreached` -- to `fail_if_refused` (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale), which lists those -- files after the findings and fails the run. function roc_types_for_files(who, root, roc, paths, exempt) local roots = roc_types_root_apps(who, root) local pats = {} local exprs = {} local reached = {} for one in roots do local got = roc_types(one, roc) for path in got.paths do if not has_key(reached, path) then reached[path] = true for rec in got.modules[path] do local key = roc_types_region_key(path, rec) if rec.kind == "pat" then if not has_key(pats, key) then pats[key] = rec.type end elseif not has_key(exprs, key) then exprs[key] = rec.type end end end end for l in got.warnings do print(who .. ": roc-types " .. one .. ": " .. l) end end local reals = {} local unreached = {} for p in paths do local r = real(p) if has_key(reached, r) then reals[p] = r elseif not has_key(exempt, p) then push(unreached, "not reached by " .. join(roots, ",") .. ": " .. p) end end return {pats = pats, exprs = exprs, real = reals, unreached = unreached} end -- The type of the roc_tree node `n` in the file `path`, from the result of -- `roc_types_for_files`, or nil where the checker gave none. `kind` is "pat" -- or "expr". function roc_type_at(types, kind, path, n) return get(kind == "pat" and types.pats or types.exprs, roc_types_region_key(types.real[path], n)) end -- The parts of a type's text, `{fn, effect, result, args}`. A type is a -- function when an arrow appears outside every bracket, after any `where` -- clause is dropped. For a function, `fn` is true, `effect` says whether -- the arrow is `=>`, `args` is the text before the arrow and `result` the -- text after it. For any other type, `result` is the whole type and `args` -- is empty. function roc_type_parts(ty) local depth = 0 local body = ty for i = 1, #ty do local ch = sub(ty, i, i) if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then depth = depth + 1 end if ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 0 and sub(ty, i, i + 6) == " where " then body = sub(ty, 1, i - 1) break end end depth = 0 for i = 1, #body - 1 do local ch = sub(body, i, i) if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then depth = depth + 1 end if ch == ")" or ch == "]" or ch == "}" then depth = depth - 1 end local two = sub(body, i, i + 1) if depth == 0 and (two == "->" or two == "=>") then return {fn = true, effect = two == "=>", result = trim(sub(body, i + 2)), args = trim(sub(body, 1, i - 1))} end end return {fn = false, effect = false, result = trim(body), args = ""} end -- A typed plant's file name converted to the snake_case of an ordinary -- plant, `QuestionInferred.roc` to `question_inferred.roc`. A typed plant -- is a type module, which Roc names in CamelCase, and a self-test chooses -- the check that judges a plant by the start of its snake_case name. function snake_case_plant_name(base) local out = "" for i = 1, #base do local ch = sub(base, i, i) if re_find(ch, "^[A-Z]$") ~= nil then if i > 1 then out = out .. "_" end out = out .. lower(ch) else out = out .. ch end end return out end

name: cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale
html: -- Shorten long Roc lines by letting `roc fmt` lay them out. roc fmt never -- wraps a line, but it puts the items of a record, list, call or lambda's -- arguments one to a line when the last item has a trailing comma. For each -- code line wider than `width`, this script adds that comma to the widest -- group of two or more items that opens and closes on the line, runs roc -- fmt, and repeats until no line changes; a folder still changing after 8 -- passes stops the run, naming its files. The passes work on a copy of the -- folder's .roc files under `scratch:roc_commas_work/`, and the changed -- files are written back only once the rewrite has finished, so a run that -- stops, on a pass too many or on a budget, leaves the folder as it was. -- Then it lists the lines still too wide: comment lines, and code lines with -- no such group (a function type's arguments, which have no brackets). The -- list is printed between its counts, as cookbook/findings.shale -- describes. It runs the Roc that the repository's roc-version file names. -- -- With `tokens=N`, the script holds the folder to roc-style.md's stacking -- rule, whose six tokens are `tokens=6`, whatever a line's width: a group of -- three or more items and N or more tokens gets the trailing comma, and a -- stacked group that should sit on one line loses it, which is how `roc fmt` -- is asked to join it. A group and its tokens are read as check_stacking.shale reads -- them (cookbook/roc/groups.shale), so after `tokens=6` check_stacking.shale finds no -- group left to stack or to unstack. A line's outermost group goes first, and -- the next pass reaches the groups inside it. A function type's arguments and -- a row of literals are left alone, as check_stacking.shale leaves them, and so is a -- platform header's `targets:` section, which `roc fmt` lays out by itself. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=roc width=100 -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=roc tokens=6 -- shale cookbook:roc/wrap_long_lines.shale self_test=1 -- -- `self_test=1` copies the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/wrap_long_lines/` to -- `scratch:wrap_long_lines/`, rewrites them there with `tokens=6` and the -- self-test's Roc, and checks that the rewrite ends, that each plant comes -- out as its `.want` file, and that no group is left to stack or to unstack. -- `at_the_cap.roc` nests as deep as 8 passes reach, and `too_deep/` one group -- deeper, which has to stop the rewrite, name its file and leave it as it was. -- -- Numeric data stays packed, as groups.shale's is_data_line and -- is_number_data say: a number list never stacks, and nothing on a line wider -- than `width` that holds one does. `numbers.roc` in the plants checks both -- and that a list of names beside them still stacks. -- -- roc-apps' canvas_apps/safari, with its 70,000-byte lines of polygon data, -- takes about 160,000,000 steps with `tokens=6`. -- -- budget: steps=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 changes=5000 use("cookbook:findings.shale") use("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale") use("cookbook:roc/groups.shale") const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/wrap_long_lines" const DIR = SELF_TEST and "scratch:wrap_long_lines" or arg("dir", "roc") not_option("wrap_long_lines", "dir", DIR) const WIDTH = arg("width", 100) const TOKENS = SELF_TEST and STACK_TOKENS or arg("tokens", 0) const MAX_PASSES = 8 const ROC = roc_bin("wrap_long_lines", SELF_TEST) -- The position of the closing bracket that should get a trailing comma, or -- 0 if there is none. Of the groups that open and close on the line, it is -- the widest one with a comma directly inside it. A lambda's arguments, -- `|a, b|`, count as a group; the pipe `|>` does not. function closer_for_trailing_comma(line) local openers = {} local commas_inside = {} local best = 0 local best_width = 0 local in_string = false local i = 1 while i <= #line do local c = sub(line, i, i) local closes_group = false if in_string then if c == "\\" then i = i + 1 elseif c == "\"" then in_string = false end elseif c == "\"" then in_string = true elseif c == "#" then break elseif c == "(" or c == "{" or c == "[" then push(openers, i) push(commas_inside, 0) elseif c == "|" and sub(line, i + 1, i + 1) ~= ">" and sub(line, i - 1, i - 1) ~= "|" and sub(line, i + 1, i + 1) ~= "|" then if #openers > 0 and sub(line, openers[#openers], openers[#openers]) == "|" then closes_group = true else push(openers, i) push(commas_inside, 0) end elseif c == ")" or c == "}" or c == "]" then closes_group = #openers > 0 elseif c == "," and #commas_inside > 0 then commas_inside[#commas_inside] = commas_inside[#commas_inside] + 1 end if closes_group then local open = openers[#openers] if commas_inside[#commas_inside] > 0 and i - open > best_width then best = i best_width = i - open end openers = take(openers, #openers - 1) commas_inside = take(commas_inside, #commas_inside - 1) end i = i + 1 end return best end -- The line with a trailing comma added, or nil when it has no group to take -- one or its widest group already ends in a comma. function line_with_trailing_comma(line) local at = closer_for_trailing_comma(line) if at == 0 then return nil end if ends_with(trim(sub(line, 1, at - 1)), ",") then return nil end -- The comma goes right after the last item, before any spaces fmt left there. local j = at - 1 while j > 0 and sub(line, j, j) == " " do j = j - 1 end return sub(line, 1, j) .. "," .. sub(line, j + 1) end function is_comment(line) return starts_with(trim(line), "#") end function roc_files() local out = {} for e in walk_all(DIR) do if e.kind == "file" and ends_with(e.path, ".roc") then push(out, e.path) end end return out end -- The .roc files of DIR, each as its path inside DIR. function roc_paths_in_dir() local out = {} for path in roc_files() do push(out, sub(path, #DIR + 2)) end return out end -- The rewrite works on a copy of the folder's .roc files, so a run that -- stops, on a budget or a pass too many, leaves the folder as it was. const WORK = SELF_TEST and "scratch:roc_commas_work/self_test" or "scratch:roc_commas_work/" .. re_replace(real(DIR), "[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_") function fresh_work_copy(paths) if is_dir(WORK) then remove_tree(WORK) end mkdir(WORK) for p in paths do replace(WORK .. "/" .. p, read(DIR .. "/" .. p)) end end -- Writes each file the rewrite changed back to the folder. It reads them all -- first and checks that what is left of the budgets covers every write, so -- the folder gets all of the rewrite or none of it. function write_back(paths) local changed = {} local bytes = 0 for p in paths do local text = read(WORK .. "/" .. p) if text ~= read(DIR .. "/" .. p) then push(changed, {path = DIR .. "/" .. p, text = text}) bytes = bytes + #text end end local left = budget() if left.changes < #changed + 1 or left.change_bytes < bytes or left.steps < 2 * bytes + 1000 * #changed + 100000 then fail("wrap_long_lines: too little budget left to write the " .. #changed .. " changed files, so none was written") end for c in changed do replace(c.path, c.text) end print(#changed .. " files rewritten") end function run_roc_fmt() local r = run({ROC, "fmt", real(WORK)}, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 20}) if r.code ~= 0 then print(r.out) fail("roc fmt failed") end end -- How many commas line `l` holds, not counting one that ends it. A group of -- STACK_ITEMS items that opens and closes on the line holds STACK_ITEMS - 1 of -- them at least, and a comma that ends the line is inside no such group, so a -- line that fits with fewer has no group to stack. Counting is far cheaper -- than reading the line's groups, and most of a data file's lines are like -- `{ x: 0.5, y: 0.25 },`. function commas_before_the_last(l) local commas = #split(l, ",") - 1 if ends_with(trim_end(l), ",") then commas = commas - 1 end return commas end -- Line `l` with a trailing comma for its outermost group that should stack, -- or else, when it is wider than WIDTH, for its widest group. nil when it -- gets none. A line of data, by groups.shale's is_data_line, gets none. function line_with_comma(l) local fits = line_width(l) <= WIDTH if fits and (TOKENS == 0 or commas_before_the_last(l) < STACK_ITEMS - 1) then return nil end if TOKENS > 0 then local g = group_to_stack(l, TOKENS, WIDTH) if g ~= nil then return with_trailing_comma(l, g) end end if not fits and not is_data_line(l, WIDTH) then return line_with_trailing_comma(l) end return nil end -- Takes the trailing comma from each group of the file at `path`, whose text -- is `text`, that should unstack, adds one to each code line that should get -- one, and returns how many groups and lines it changed. function rewrite_trailing_commas(path, text) local ls = split(text, "\n") local unstacked = {} if TOKENS > 0 then unstacked = groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH) end ls = without_trailing_commas(ls, unstacked) local reachable = without_targets_section(ls) local changed = #unstacked for i = 1, #ls do if not is_comment(ls[i]) then local with_comma = line_with_comma(reachable[i]) if with_comma ~= nil then ls[i] = with_comma changed = changed + 1 end end end if changed > 0 then replace(path, join(ls, "\n")) end return changed end -- Rewrites commas and runs roc fmt, in the work copy, until a pass changes -- nothing, and then writes the changed files back. Files still changing after -- MAX_PASSES stop the run, since the list of long lines would otherwise judge -- a rewrite that never finished. function rewrite() local paths = roc_paths_in_dir() fresh_work_copy(paths) run_roc_fmt() local pass = 1 local changed = 1 local touched = {} -- A file's text when a pass last left it alone. A later pass would leave -- the same text alone again, so it is not read for groups a second time. local settled = {} while changed > 0 and pass <= MAX_PASSES do changed = 0 touched = {} for p in paths do local text = read(WORK .. "/" .. p) if not has_key(settled, p) or settled[p] ~= text then local n = rewrite_trailing_commas(WORK .. "/" .. p, text) if n > 0 then changed = changed + n push(touched, DIR .. "/" .. p) else settled[p] = text end end end print("pass " .. pass .. ": " .. changed .. " trailing commas added or taken out") run_roc_fmt() pass = pass + 1 end if changed > 0 then fail("wrap_long_lines: still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes, so no file was written: " .. join(touched, ", ")) end write_back(paths) remove_tree(WORK) return nil end function fresh_copies(plants) if is_dir(DIR) then remove_tree(DIR) end mkdir(DIR) for p in glob(plants .. "/*.roc") do replace(DIR .. "/" .. basename(p), read(p)) end end function self_test() fresh_copies(PLANTS) rewrite() local bad = 0 for p in glob(PLANTS .. "/*.roc") do local name = basename(p) local want = PLANTS .. "/" .. sub(name, 1, #name - 4) .. ".want" local got = read(DIR .. "/" .. name) local ok = got == read(want) print((ok and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": comes out as its .want") if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end local reachable = without_targets_section(split(got, "\n")) for n = 1, #reachable do local l = reachable[n] if not is_comment(l) and group_to_stack(l, TOKENS, WIDTH) ~= nil then print("FAIL " .. name .. ":" .. n .. ": a group left to stack: " .. trim(l)) bad = bad + 1 end end for g in groups_to_unstack(split(got, "\n"), TOKENS, WIDTH) do print("FAIL " .. name .. ":" .. g.line .. ": a group left to unstack") bad = bad + 1 end end if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " checks failed") end if is_dir(WORK) then fail("wrap_long_lines: a finished rewrite should remove its work copy, " .. WORK) end fresh_copies(PLANTS .. "/too_deep") local stopped = attempt(rewrite) local named = "still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes, so no file was written: " .. DIR .. "/too_deep.roc" if stopped.ok or not contains(stopped.error, named) then fail("wrap_long_lines: too_deep.roc should stop with `" .. named .. "`") end if read(DIR .. "/too_deep.roc") ~= read(PLANTS .. "/too_deep/too_deep.roc") then fail("wrap_long_lines: a rewrite that stops should leave too_deep.roc as it was") end print("ok too_deep.roc: stops naming its file, and is left as it was") remove_tree(WORK) print("PASS: the rewrite ends, every plant comes out as its .want, no group is left to stack or to unstack, and a rewrite past its passes stops naming its file and changes none") end if SELF_TEST then self_test() else rewrite() local long_comments = 0 local long_code = {} for path in roc_files() do local ls = split(read(path), "\n") for i = 1, #ls do local w = line_width(ls[i]) if w > WIDTH then if is_comment(ls[i]) then long_comments = long_comments + 1 else push(long_code, path .. ":" .. i .. " (" .. w .. "): " .. trim(sub(ls[i], 1, 140))) end end end end print_findings("still over " .. WIDTH .. ": " .. #long_code .. " code lines, " .. long_comments .. " comment lines", long_code) end

name: cookbook/run.shale
html: -- This recipe runs a program and prints what it said that matters. It takes -- one command line, or several joined by `&&` and run in order until one -- fails, and prints for each how it ended, how long it took, the lines -- holding `grep`'s literals and its last lines. The whole output is kept in -- `log`. The default log is .zig-cache/run.log under `dir`, and only where -- that folder is already (a Zig checkout, which ignores it); elsewhere (an -- essay repo, a memory folder) nothing is written, and the last line says -- so. It is `run` from a launch line, for `roc check`, a `zig build` with a -- log and a timing, a bench binary, `gh run` or `node`. Inside a heredoc, -- call the prelude's `report_run(argv, opts)`, which this recipe is a -- launch line for: the same verdict, with no child run. -- -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:run.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- cmd=roc check roc/Game.roc && roc test roc/Game.roc && roc fmt --check roc/ -- grep=error,warning -- ARGS -- -- `cmd` is split on `&&`, each part on spaces (no quoting: a word with a -- space needs a script of its own); a program named through a mount -- (`zig:zig`) runs by its OS path. `dir` is where each runs, `minutes` -- the time each gets, `tail` the last lines printed of each (more for a -- failure), `grep` comma-separated literals, `most` the most grep lines -- printed of each. `want=tag: why` runs a program `run` refuses (a shell, -- an interpreter such as `node`, a text tool), logged as `run` logs it. -- The launch fails when a command does, naming it, so a chain in a -- shell's `&&` stops as this one does. -- -- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 const CMD = arg("cmd", "") const DIR = arg("dir", ".") const MINUTES = arg("minutes", 10) const TAIL = arg("tail", 10) const GREP = arg("grep", "") const MOST = arg("most", 60) const LOG = arg("log", "") const WANT = arg("want", "") if trim(CMD) == "" then fail("run: say `cmd=`, the command line (with spaces: on stdin, `--args-stdin`)") end -- Where the whole output goes, `report_run`'s rule: `log=`, else -- .zig-cache/run.log where that folder is, else nowhere (""). local log_path = "auto" if LOG ~= "" then log_path = path_under(DIR, LOG) end local wanted = {} for w in split(GREP, ",") do if w ~= "" then push(wanted, w) end end -- Each command in order through the prelude's `report_run`, which prints -- its verdict and stops the launch on the first that fails. local k = 0 local r = nil for part in split(CMD, "&&") do k = k + 1 local argv = {} for w in words(part) do push(argv, w) end if #argv == 0 then fail("run: an empty command in `" .. CMD .. "`") end local opts = {cwd = DIR, timeout_ms = MINUTES * 60000, shown = trim(part), grep = wanted, tail = TAIL, most = MOST, log = log_path, append_log = k > 1} if WANT ~= "" then opts.want = WANT end r = report_run(argv, opts) end print(report_run_kept(r.log))

name: cookbook/run_zig_build.shale
html: -- This recipe runs `zig build STEP` and prints its verdict without the -- noise, in place of `zig build ... | grep error | sort | uniq -c`. It prints -- the Build Summary, each distinct error line with how often it came (a -- failing step's error repeats once per binary), the failed tests' names and -- their first lines, a failed run's last lines, and the exit code. Every line -- of the output is kept in `log` (default .zig-cache/run_zig_build.log under -- `dir`) for the rest. -- -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:run_zig_build.shale step=test -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:run_zig_build.shale step=metal zig=zig016:zig -- cd <repo> && shale cookbook:run_zig_build.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- args=test -Dtest-file=src/floor_sim.zig --summary all -- ARGS -- -- `zig` is the compiler: by default the one `dir`'s `zig-version` pins, -- installed side by side at `tools:zig-<version>/zig` as Roc's pins are (it -- stops, naming the install, when that is not there), and with no -- `zig-version`, `zig` on the PATH. Another goes through a ` tools` mount, -- such as `zig016:zig`. `step` a step's name, `args` more words after -- it (split on spaces), `dir` where to run, `minutes` the time it gets. -- -- With `grep=`, in place of `zig build fuzz 2>&1 | grep FAIL`, it also -- prints every line of the output holding one of `grep`'s literals (comma-separated), in -- order, after the summary, at most `most` of them (said when more): -- -- shale cookbook:run_zig_build.shale step=fuzz --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- grep=FAIL,hunts ran -- ARGS -- -- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 const STEP = arg("step", "") not_option("run_zig_build", "step", STEP) const ARGS = arg("args", "") const DIR = arg("dir", ".") -- The compiler `zig=` names, else the one `dir`'s zig-version pins, else -- `zig` on the PATH. function compiler() local given = arg("zig", "") if given ~= "" then return given end local pin_file = "zig-version" if DIR ~= "." then pin_file = DIR .. "/zig-version" end if not exists(pin_file) then return "zig" end local pin = trim(read(pin_file)) local at = "tools:zig-" .. pin .. "/zig" if not exists(at) then local from = "https://ziglang.org/download/" .. pin .. "/" if contains(pin, "+") then from = "https://github.com/showell/patched-zig-compiler/releases/tag/" .. split(pin, "+")[2] end fail("run_zig_build: " .. pin_file .. " pins Zig " .. pin .. ", and " .. at .. " is not there. Install it from " .. from .. ": check zig-x86_64-linux-" .. pin .. ".tar.xz against its .sha256 and unpack it as ~/tools/zig-" .. pin) end return at end const ZIG = compiler() const MINUTES = arg("minutes", 10) const LOG = arg("log", ".zig-cache/run_zig_build.log") const GREP = arg("grep", "") const MOST = arg("most", 60) local argv = {ZIG, "build"} if contains(ZIG, ":") then argv = {real(ZIG), "build"} end print("zig: " .. ZIG) if STEP ~= "" then push(argv, STEP) end -- `--summary all` goes to the build itself, before any `--` (after it, the -- words are the step's own). local passed = {} local to_step = false for w in words(ARGS) do if w == "--" then to_step = true end if to_step then push(passed, w) else push(argv, w) end end if not contains(ARGS, "--summary") then push(argv, "--summary") push(argv, "all") end for w in passed do push(argv, w) end -- A compiler named through a mount runs if that mount is marked ` tools` -- (SHALE-AGENTS.md: the user's word, once, for a new toolchain). local r = run(argv, {cwd = DIR, timeout_ms = MINUTES * 60000, whole = 16777216}) -- A run ended by its time or a signal has no exit code: say how it ended. local how = "" if has_key(r, "code") then how = "exit " .. r.code else how = "ended: " .. tostring(r.ended) .. " (no exit code)" end local failed_run = not has_key(r, "code") or r.code ~= 0 local log_path = LOG if DIR ~= "." then log_path = DIR .. "/" .. LOG end replace(log_path, r.out) local counts = {} local order = {} local failed = {} local summary = "" local lines_of = lines(r.out) for i = 1, #lines_of do local t = trim(lines_of[i]) if starts_with(t, "Build Summary:") then summary = t end if contains(t, "error:") and not contains(t, "compilation errors") and not starts_with(t, "failed command:") then if not has_key(counts, t) then push(order, t) counts[t] = 0 end counts[t] = counts[t] + 1 end if starts_with(t, "error: '") and contains(t, "' failed:") then local why = "" if i < #lines_of then why = trim(lines_of[i + 1]) end push(failed, sub(t, 9, #t - 9) .. ": " .. why) end end print(summary ~= "" and summary or "(no Build Summary: the build runner did not get that far)") -- A test run taken from the cache reports no counts, so the summary's -- total is only of the runs that ran: said, so it is not compared as whole. local cached_runs = 0 for l in lines_of do if contains(l, "+- run test cached") or contains(l, "+- run test") and ends_with(trim(l), "cached") then cached_runs = cached_runs + 1 end end if cached_runs > 0 then print("(" .. cached_runs .. " test runs came from the cache and are not in the counts: `args=--cache-dir .zig-cache/fresh` for a whole count)") end for t in order do if not starts_with(t, "error: '") then print(counts[t] .. "x " .. sub(t, 1, 240)) end end for f in failed do print("FAILED " .. sub(f, 1, 240)) end if GREP ~= "" then local wanted = split(GREP, ",") local held = 0 for l in lines_of do for w in wanted do if w ~= "" and contains(l, w) then held = held + 1 if held <= MOST then print("grep: " .. sub(l, 1, 240)) end break end end end if held > MOST then print("grep: ... " .. (held - MOST) .. " more (most=" .. MOST .. ")") end if held == 0 then print("grep: no line holds " .. GREP) end end -- A failed run whose own words are not `error:` lines (a checker's -- findings, a script's stop): its last lines, so nothing is hidden. if failed_run then print("-- the last lines:") local from = #lines_of - 14 if from < 1 then from = 1 end for i = from, #lines_of do print(" " .. sub(lines_of[i], 1, 200)) end end print(how .. " in " .. (r.ms // 1000) .. " s; the whole output in " .. log_path) if failed_run then fail("run_zig_build: " .. how) end

name: cookbook/survey_repos.shale
html: -- This recipe surveys a folder of checkouts for a map of how they relate: -- what each folder is, how old each repo is, what its README says first, -- and which READMEs name which folders. It prints what a person draws the -- map from and draws nothing itself, since choosing what a diagram shows is -- that person's job. `map_repos.shale` is its sibling for the state of each -- checkout today (dirty files, upstream, recent commits). For an essay on -- the repos, start with `plan_repo_essay.shale`, the playbook that runs this. -- -- It prints four sections, plain lines and a pipe table that paste straight -- into a note: -- -- * `== folders`: a pipe table, one row a folder, oldest first commit first. -- A row has the folder's kind (`clone`, `worktree of <main>` for a linked -- worktree, with the main checkout's folder name, or `not git`), its -- branch, its remote (a GitHub URL is shown as `owner/name`), its first -- and last commit dates, its age in days (from its first commit to -- `today`), its commit count (`git rev-list --count HEAD`) and its -- README's title. A worktree's history is its main checkout's plus its -- branch, so its age is its main's. -- * `== openings`: each README's first 320 characters after its title, on -- one line. -- * `== mentions`: for each README, the other folders it names and how many -- times, `from -> to: count, ...`. With `contexts=1`, each pair's first -- mention follows on its own line, with the sentence around it. -- * `== dot edges`: the same pairs as a Graphviz edge list, one -- `"from" -> "to";` a line, ready to trim by hand and wrap in a -- `digraph { }`. -- -- A README names a folder where the folder's name stands alone: the name -- is a whole run of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, so `dog-park` is not -- counted inside `dog-park-page` or `dog-park_x`, and the case must match, -- so `Shale` never counts as `shale`. That rule's one home is -- `folder_names.shale`, which `map_repos.shale` and `retire_checkout.shale` -- use too. -- -- Some matches that stand alone are file names, not folders, and are left -- out (`folder_names.shale`'s `in_file_name`): a name followed by a dot and -- a letter (`docs/observatory.adoc` links a file of its own repo, not the -- observatory repo), except `.git` (`showell/shale.git` names the repo), -- and a name right after a dot that follows a letter or digit (`Main.roc`, -- a file's extension). Each one left out is listed under `== left out as file names`, with the word it was -- in, so a wrong guess is visible. What this cannot tell is a folder's name -- used as a plain word (the `roc` command, say): `skip=` such a folder. -- -- `skip=a,b` leaves folders out of the mention scan both ways: their -- READMEs are not read for mentions, and nothing counts as naming them. -- Skip the worktrees and the upstream clones, whose READMEs are another -- repo's. They still get a row in the table. -- -- `today=YYYY-MM-DD` sets the day the ages are counted to; the default is -- the clock's today, in UTC. `json=1` prints the whole survey as one JSON -- value instead (rows, mentions, the matches left out, the folders that are -- symbolic links), for a page to draw from. -- -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:survey_repos.shale -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:survey_repos.shale contexts=1 skip=roc,lanes -- shale cookbook:survey_repos.shale root=repos: today=2026-11-15 -- shale cookbook:survey_repos.shale self_test=1 -- -- Each git folder costs five programs (its branch, remote, first and last -- commit dates, and its count), so a folder of more than about 190 repos -- wants `--budget programs=N`. A symbolic link is listed, not followed. -- -- budget: steps=100000000 arena_bytes=400000000 use("cookbook:folder_names.shale") const ROOT = arg("root", ".") const CONTEXTS = arg("contexts", 0) const SKIP = arg("skip", "") const TODAY = arg("today", "") const JSON = arg("json", 0) const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", 0) const OPENING_CHARS = 320 const CONTEXT_REACH = 240 function flat(s) return join(words(s), " ") end function cell(s) return join(split("" .. s, "|"), "\\|") end -- One git command's output, trimmed, or "" when it exits nonzero (no -- remote, no commits). `keep` is "head" for a command whose first line is -- all that is wanted, as `log --reverse` is: git has no way to give the -- oldest commit alone, since `--reverse` applies after `-1` limits. function git_out(path, args, keep) local argv = {"git", "-C", real(path)} for a in args do push(argv, a) end local opts = {timeout_ms = 60000} if keep == "head" then opts.head = 1 else opts.whole = 20000 end local r = run(argv, opts) if r.code ~= 0 then return "" end return trim(r.out) end function short_remote(url) local s = url for prefix in {"https://github.com/", "git@github.com:"} do if starts_with(s, prefix) then s = sub(s, #prefix + 1, #s) end end if ends_with(s, ".git") then s = sub(s, 1, #s - 4) end return s end -- What a folder is: a clone (its own .git folder), a linked worktree (a -- .git file naming `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`), or not git at all. function kind_of(path) if exists(path .. "/.git/HEAD") then return {kind = "clone", main = ""} end if not exists(path .. "/.git") then return {kind = "not git", main = ""} end local gitdir = trim(read(path .. "/.git")) local at = find(gitdir, "/.git/worktrees/") if at == nil then return {kind = "git file", main = ""} end local main = basename(sub(gitdir, 1, at - 1)) return {kind = "worktree of " .. main, main = main} end function readme_of(path) for name in {"README.md", "README", "readme.md"} do if exists(path .. "/" .. name) then return {name = name, text = read(path .. "/" .. name)} end end return {name = "", text = ""} end -- A README's title (its first `# ` line outside a code fence, since a shell -- comment in a fence is no title; else its first line) and the line number -- it is on. function title_of(text) local all = lines(text) local fenced = false local i = 1 while i <= #all do if starts_with(trim(all[i]), "```") then fenced = not fenced end if not fenced and starts_with(all[i], "# ") then return {text = trim(sub(all[i], 3, #all[i])), line = i} end i = i + 1 end if #all > 0 then return {text = trim(all[1]), line = 1} end return {text = "", line = 0} end function opening_of(text, title_line) local all = lines(text) local out = "" local i = title_line + 1 while i <= #all and #out < OPENING_CHARS do out = out .. " " .. all[i] i = i + 1 end return sub(flat(out), 1, OPENING_CHARS) end function survey_folder(root, name, today_day) local path = path_under(root, name) local k = kind_of(path) local row = {folder = name, kind = k.kind, main = k.main, branch = "", remote = "", first = "", last = "", days = "", commits = "", title = "", readme = ""} if k.kind ~= "not git" then row.branch = git_out(path, {"branch", "--show-current"}, "whole") if row.branch == "" then row.branch = "(detached)" end row.remote = short_remote(git_out(path, {"remote", "get-url", "origin"}, "whole")) -- A head keep ends with a `… N lines left out …` line: the date is the first. row.first = get(lines(git_out(path, {"log", "--reverse", "--format=%as"}, "head")), 1, "") row.last = git_out(path, {"log", "-1", "--format=%as"}, "whole") row.commits = git_out(path, {"rev-list", "--count", "HEAD"}, "whole") if row.first ~= "" then row.days = today_day - seconds(row.first) // 86400 end end local readme = readme_of(path) if readme.name ~= "" then local t = title_of(readme.text) row.title = t.text row.readme = readme.name row.opening = opening_of(readme.text, t.line) end return row end -- The path-like word around `at`, to show what a match left out was in. function word_around(src, at, len) local pathy = "^[A-Za-z0-9_./~-]$" local from = at while from > 1 and at - from < 60 and re_find(sub(src, from - 1, from - 1), pathy) ~= nil do from = from - 1 end local to = at + len - 1 while to < #src and to - at < 60 and re_find(sub(src, to + 1, to + 1), pathy) ~= nil do to = to + 1 end return sub(src, from, to) end -- The sentence around `at`: back to the last sentence end, blank line or -- line that starts a block (a table row, a list item, a heading, a quote, -- a fence) before it, on to the first after it, at most CONTEXT_REACH -- characters each way, with `…` where the reach cut it. So a mention in a -- table is its row, and one in a list its item. function sentence_at(src, at, len) local ends = "[.!?](?:[ \\t\\n]|$)|\\n[ \\t]*\\n|\\n[ \\t]*(?:[|#>*-]|```)" local from = at - CONTEXT_REACH local cut_front = true if from <= 1 then from = 1 cut_front = false end local start = from for m in re_find_all(sub(src, from, at - 1), ends) do -- A line that starts a block begins the sentence; any other end is -- passed over whole. if starts_with(m.text, "\n") and not ends_with(m.text, "\n") then start = from + m.at else start = from + m.at - 1 + #m.text end cut_front = false end local tail_from = at + len local stop = tail_from + CONTEXT_REACH local cut_back = stop < #src local m = re_find(sub(src, tail_from, stop), ends) if m ~= nil then stop = tail_from + m.at - 1 if sub(src, stop, stop) == "\n" then stop = stop - 1 end cut_back = false end local text = flat(sub(src, start, stop)) if cut_front then text = "…" .. text end if cut_back then text = text .. "…" end return text end -- One README's mentions of the target folders: {counts, contexts, left_out}, -- counts and contexts by target, left_out a list of {to, word}. function scan_readme(src, self, targets) local counts = {} local contexts = {} local left_out = {} for t in re_find_all(src, NAME_RUN) do if t.text ~= self and has_key(targets, t.text) then if in_file_name(src, t.at, #t.text) then push(left_out, {to = t.text, word = word_around(src, t.at, #t.text)}) else if not has_key(counts, t.text) then contexts[t.text] = sentence_at(src, t.at, #t.text) end incr(counts, t.text) end end end return {counts = counts, contexts = contexts, left_out = left_out} end -- The folders and the symbolic links directly in `root`, by name, hidden -- ones (`.claude`) left out. function entries_of(root) local dirs = {} local links = {} for e in walk_all(root, {depth = 1}) do local name = basename(e.path) if not starts_with(name, ".") then if e.kind == "directory" then push(dirs, name) elseif e.kind == "other" then push(links, name) end end end sort(dirs) sort(links) return {dirs = dirs, links = links} end function survey(root, skip_text, today_text) local today_day = now() // 86400 local today = sub(date(now()), 1, 10) if today_text ~= "" then today_day = seconds(today_text) // 86400 today = today_text end local skip = {} for s in split(skip_text, ",") do if trim(s) ~= "" then skip[trim(s)] = true end end local listed = entries_of(root) for s in keys(skip) do if not has_item(listed.dirs, s) then fail("survey_repos: skip names `" .. s .. "`, which is no folder in " .. root) end end local rows = {} for name in listed.dirs do local row = survey_folder(root, name, today_day) row.order = row.first .. " " .. name if row.first == "" then row.order = "~ " .. name end push(rows, row) yield() end sort(rows, "order") local targets = {} for name in listed.dirs do if not has_key(skip, name) then targets[name] = true end end local mentions = {} local left_out = {} for row in rows do if row.readme ~= "" and not has_key(skip, row.folder) then local src = read(path_under(root, row.folder) .. "/" .. row.readme) local found = scan_readme(src, row.folder, targets) local tos = keys(found.counts) sort(tos) for to in tos do push(mentions, {from = row.folder, to = to, count = found.counts[to], context = found.contexts[to]}) end for l in found.left_out do push(left_out, {from = row.folder, to = l.to, word = l.word}) end yield() end end return {root = root, today = today, rows = rows, mentions = mentions, left_out = left_out, links = listed.links, skipped = keys(skip)} end function print_survey(s, contexts) local git_rows = 0 print("== folders: " .. #s.rows .. " in " .. s.root .. ", ages as of " .. s.today) print("| folder | kind | branch | remote | first | last | days | commits | title |") print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|") for r in s.rows do if r.kind ~= "not git" then git_rows = git_rows + 1 end print("| " .. join({cell(r.folder), cell(r.kind), cell(r.branch), cell(r.remote), r.first, r.last, "" .. r.days, r.commits, cell(r.title)}, " | ") .. " |") end if #s.links > 0 then print("symbolic links, not followed: " .. join(s.links, ", ")) end print("") print("== openings") for r in s.rows do if r.readme ~= "" then print(r.folder .. ": " .. r.opening) end end print("") print("== mentions (from -> to: count), where the name stands alone") local from = "" local parts = {} local sources = 0 for m in s.mentions do if m.from ~= from then if from ~= "" then print(from .. " -> " .. join(parts, ", ")) end from = m.from parts = {} sources = sources + 1 end push(parts, m.to .. ": " .. m.count) end if from ~= "" then print(from .. " -> " .. join(parts, ", ")) end if contexts == 1 then print("") print("== first mentions, in context") for m in s.mentions do print(m.from .. " -> " .. m.to .. ": " .. m.context) end end if #s.left_out > 0 then print("") print("== left out as file names (from -> to: count, each word once)") local pairs = {} local by_pair = {} for l in s.left_out do local pair = l.from .. " -> " .. l.to if not has_key(by_pair, pair) then push(pairs, pair) end push_at(by_pair, pair, l.word) end for pair in pairs do print(pair .. ": " .. #by_pair[pair] .. ", " .. join(unique(by_pair[pair]), " ")) end end print("") print("== dot edges") for m in s.mentions do print(" \"" .. m.from .. "\" -> \"" .. m.to .. "\";") end print("") local skipped = "none skipped" if #s.skipped > 0 then local names = s.skipped sort(names) skipped = "skipped " .. join(names, ", ") end print("survey_repos: " .. #s.rows .. " folders, " .. git_rows .. " git; " .. #s.mentions .. " mentions from " .. sources .. " READMEs, " .. #s.left_out .. " left out as file names; " .. skipped) end -- The self-test's plants, in a fresh folder under `scratch:`: alpha (a -- clone, two commits, a README naming beta twice (once as `x/beta.git`), -- beta-tools twice, and beta in two file names), beta (one commit, a GitHub remote, a README naming -- alpha twice, the worktree once and beta-tools in a table row, its title -- after a fenced `#` line), -- beta-tools (three commits, no -- README), alpha-wt (a worktree of alpha on `side`, one commit more, with -- alpha's README) and notes (not git). const ALPHA_README = [=[# Alpha Alpha draws with beta. The beta-tools repo builds it; see beta-tools/README. A file named beta.md is not a repo, and beta_x is no name. Clone x/beta.git; its Main.beta is a file. ]=] const BETA_README = [=[```sh # a comment in a fence, not the title ``` # Beta Beta is used by alpha, and by alpha-wt, which is alpha on a branch. | tool | where | | the builder | beta-tools, beside it | | the docs | here | ]=] function plant_commit(dir, day, msg) local stamp = day .. "T12:00:00+00:00" must(run({"git", "-C", dir, "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", msg}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000, env = {GIT_AUTHOR_DATE = stamp, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE = stamp}})) end function plant_repo(T, name) must(run({"git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main", real(T) .. "/" .. name}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000})) return real(T) .. "/" .. name end function expect(what, got, want) if got ~= want then fail("survey_repos self_test: " .. what .. " is " .. tostring(got) .. ", should be " .. tostring(want)) end end function mention_map(s) local m = {} for e in s.mentions do m[e.from .. "->" .. e.to] = e end return m end function row_map(s) local m = {} for r in s.rows do m[r.folder] = r end return m end function self_test() local T = fresh_dir("scratch:", "survey_repos_self_test") local alpha = plant_repo(T, "alpha") create(T .. "/alpha/README.md", ALPHA_README) must(run({"git", "-C", alpha, "add", "README.md"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000})) plant_commit(alpha, "2026-01-01", "first") plant_commit(alpha, "2026-01-11", "second") local beta = plant_repo(T, "beta") must(run({"git", "-C", beta, "remote", "add", "origin", "https://github.com/x/beta.git"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000})) create(T .. "/beta/README.md", BETA_README) plant_commit(beta, "2026-01-21", "only") local tools = plant_repo(T, "beta-tools") plant_commit(tools, "2025-12-01", "a") plant_commit(tools, "2025-12-02", "b") plant_commit(tools, "2025-12-03", "c") must(run({"git", "-C", alpha, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "side", real(T) .. "/alpha-wt"}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 10000})) plant_commit(real(T) .. "/alpha-wt", "2026-01-15", "on side") mkdir(T .. "/notes") -- Unskipped: the worktree reads as a source, and is named. local s = survey(T, "", "2026-02-01") local rows = row_map(s) expect("the folder count", #s.rows, 5) expect("alpha's kind", rows["alpha"].kind, "clone") expect("alpha's first", rows["alpha"].first, "2026-01-01") expect("alpha's last", rows["alpha"].last, "2026-01-11") expect("alpha's age", rows["alpha"].days, 31) expect("alpha's commits", rows["alpha"].commits, "2") expect("alpha's remote", rows["alpha"].remote, "") expect("alpha's title", rows["alpha"].title, "Alpha") expect("beta's title, past a fence", rows["beta"].title, "Beta") expect("beta's age", rows["beta"].days, 11) expect("beta's remote", rows["beta"].remote, "x/beta") expect("beta-tools' age", rows["beta-tools"].days, 62) expect("beta-tools' commits", rows["beta-tools"].commits, "3") expect("beta-tools' readme", rows["beta-tools"].readme, "") expect("alpha-wt's kind", rows["alpha-wt"].kind, "worktree of alpha") expect("alpha-wt's branch", rows["alpha-wt"].branch, "side") expect("alpha-wt's first", rows["alpha-wt"].first, "2026-01-01") expect("alpha-wt's last", rows["alpha-wt"].last, "2026-01-15") expect("alpha-wt's commits", rows["alpha-wt"].commits, "3") expect("notes' kind", rows["notes"].kind, "not git") expect("notes' age", rows["notes"].days, "") local order = {} for r in s.rows do push(order, r.folder) end expect("the order", join(order, ","), "beta-tools,alpha,alpha-wt,beta,notes") local m = mention_map(s) expect("alpha -> beta", m["alpha->beta"].count, 2) expect("alpha -> beta-tools", m["alpha->beta-tools"].count, 2) expect("beta -> alpha", m["beta->alpha"].count, 2) expect("beta -> alpha-wt", m["beta->alpha-wt"].count, 1) expect("alpha-wt -> beta", m["alpha-wt->beta"].count, 2) expect("alpha-wt -> beta-tools", m["alpha-wt->beta-tools"].count, 2) expect("alpha-wt -> alpha", has_key(m, "alpha-wt->alpha"), false) expect("the mentions", #s.mentions, 7) expect("beta -> beta-tools's context, a table row", m["beta->beta-tools"].context, "| the builder | beta-tools, beside it |") expect("alpha -> beta's context", m["alpha->beta"].context, "Alpha draws with beta.") expect("beta -> alpha-wt's context", m["beta->alpha-wt"].context, "Beta is used by alpha, and by alpha-wt, which is alpha on a branch.") expect("the left out", #s.left_out, 4) expect("a name before an extension, left out", s.left_out[1].word, "beta.md") expect("an extension, left out", s.left_out[2].word, "Main.beta") -- Skipped: the worktree is neither read nor named, and keeps its row. local k = survey(T, "alpha-wt", "2026-02-01") local km = mention_map(k) expect("the folder count, skipping", #k.rows, 5) expect("alpha-wt -> beta, skipped", has_key(km, "alpha-wt->beta"), false) expect("beta -> alpha-wt, skipped", has_key(km, "beta->alpha-wt"), false) expect("beta -> alpha, skipping", km["beta->alpha"].count, 2) expect("the mentions, skipping", #k.mentions, 4) expect("the left out, skipping", #k.left_out, 2) expect("a skip of no folder refused", attempt(survey, T, "nope", "2026-02-01").ok, false) print_survey(k, 1) remove_tree(T) print("survey_repos self_test: PASS (kinds, ages and counts exact; a prefix name and a file name not counted; skip both ways)") end if SELF_TEST == 1 then self_test() else local s = survey(ROOT, SKIP, TODAY) if JSON == 1 then print(json_write(s)) else print_survey(s, CONTEXTS) end end

name: cookbook/test_times.shale
html: -- Tests the time-history library on canned `run` results: -- -- shale cookbook:test_times.shale self_test=1 -- -- `timed_run` itself, over a real program and a real `build:` mount, is -- src/shale_cli_test.zig's. use("cookbook:times.shale") function ran(cpu_ms) return {ended = "exit", code = 0, cpu_ms = cpu_ms, ms = cpu_ms + 7} end function expect(what, got, want) if got ~= want then fail("times: " .. what .. ": got `" .. got .. "`, wanted `" .. want .. "`") end end function stage_count(path, stage) local n = 0 for row in times_rows(path) do if row.stage == stage then n = n + 1 end end return n end function reads_broken(path) return times_rows(path) end if not arg("self_test", false) then fail("test_times: only `self_test=1`, there is nothing else to check") end -- What is said, at and around each edge: half as much again, and a second. expect("the example", times_change("build.sh safari", 35000, 192000), "build.sh safari: 192 s, was 35 s (5.5x)") expect("1.5x slower", times_change("s", 2000, 3000), "s: 3.0 s, was 2.0 s (1.5x)") expect("under 1.5x slower", times_change("s", 2000, 2999), "") expect("1.5x faster", times_change("s", 3000, 2000), "s: 2.0 s, was 3.0 s (1.5x faster)") expect("under 1.5x faster", times_change("s", 3000, 2001), "") expect("a second more", times_change("s", 1000, 2000), "s: 2.0 s, was 1.0 s (2.0x)") expect("under a second more", times_change("s", 1000, 1999), "") expect("a large ratio under a second", times_change("s", 10, 900), "") expect("no change", times_change("s", 5000, 5000), "") expect("from nothing", times_change("s", 0, 2000), "s: 2.0 s, was 0.0 s") expect("to nothing", times_change("s", 2000, 0), "s: 0.0 s, was 2.0 s") expect("the seconds' edge", times_seconds(9949) .. " " .. times_seconds(9950) .. " " .. times_seconds(10000), "9.9 s 10.0 s 10 s") expect("a cold run's line", times_cold_line("s", ran(192000)), "s: cold, 192 s, not judged") -- The middle: a lone slow run is not the usual time, three in five are. expect("the middle of two", tostring(times_middle({35000, 192000})), "35000") expect("the middle of three", tostring(times_middle({192000, 35000, 40000})), "40000") local dir = fresh_dir("scratch:", "times") local p = dir .. "/check.tsv" -- The first run has nothing to be compared with, and is kept. expect("the first run", times_note(p, "build", ran(35000)), "") expect("what it kept", tostring(stage_count(p, "build")), "1") expect("the second run", times_note(p, "build", ran(192000)), "build: 192 s, was 35 s (5.5x)") -- One slow run left the usual time alone. expect("after one slow run", times_note(p, "build", ran(35000)), "") -- A run that failed counts for nothing, either side of a compare. expect("a failed run", times_note(p, "build", {ended = "exit", code = 1, cpu_ms = 500000, ms = 500000}), "") expect("a run timed out", times_note(p, "build", {ended = "timeout", cpu_ms = 500000, ms = 500000}), "") expect("they were not kept", tostring(stage_count(p, "build")), "3") -- Stages are held apart, and each keeps its last five. expect("another stage's first run", times_note(p, "test", ran(90000)), "") for i = 1, 7 do times_note(p, "build", ran(35000 + i)) end expect("five kept", tostring(stage_count(p, "build")), "5") expect("the other stage kept", tostring(stage_count(p, "test")), "1") local oldest = 0 for row in times_rows(p) do if row.stage == "build" and oldest == 0 then oldest = row.cpu_ms end end expect("the oldest went", tostring(oldest), "35003") -- The file reads as a table: a header, then a line a time. local text = lines(read(p)) expect("the header", text[1], "when\tstage\tcpu_ms\tms") expect("its fields", tostring(#split(text[2], "\t")), "4") -- A file that is not this shape stops the run, and is left as it was. local broken = dir .. "/broken.tsv" replace(broken, "when\tstage\tcpu_ms\tms\nnot a row\n") expect("a broken row", attempt(reads_broken, broken).error, "times: " .. broken .. ":2 is not four fields: not a row") replace(broken, "someone else's file\n") expect("a foreign file", attempt(reads_broken, broken).error, "times: " .. broken .. " does not start with its header") -- The book and the stage are names. expect("a plain book", times_path("safari"), "build:times/safari.tsv") expect("a book with a path", attempt(times_path, "a/b").class, "fail") expect("a book with a mount", attempt(times_path, "m:b").class, "fail") remove_tree(dir) print("times self_test: PASS (each edge of a change, the middle, failed runs, stages apart, five kept, a broken file stops)")

name: cookbook/times.shale
html: -- A library for a stage's time history: `use("cookbook:times.shale")`. It -- keeps a script's recent times, one small file a script, and prints the -- change when a stage's time has moved far enough to mean something: -- -- local r = timed_run("safari", "build.sh safari", {"./build.sh", "safari"}, -- {timeout_ms = 300000, tail = 20, cpu_budget_ms = 60000}) -- -- build.sh safari: 192 s, was 35 s (5.5x) -- -- The first word names the file, `build:times/safari.tsv`, whose lines are -- `when`, `stage`, `cpu_ms` and `ms`, the last five of each stage. -- -- It compares CPU time, for the reason `run`'s budget does: wall time doubles -- on a busy box. "Was" is the middle of the stage's recent times, so one cold -- run neither sets off a line of its own nor becomes what the next run is -- held to. Only a run that exited 0 counts, since a build that stopped at its -- first error says nothing of its speed, and a stage over its `cpu_budget_ms` -- stops inside `run`, so it leaves the history as it was. -- -- `cold = true` says this run compiles from nothing, as a fresh worktree's -- first does: it isn't held to `cpu_budget_ms` or compared, and leaves the -- history as it was, so a budget and "was" are judged on warm runs alone. The -- caller says so because the history can't: a book outlives a deleted cache, -- and two worktrees share one. A tier reads its own sign once, before its -- first stage, as stages fill the cache one by one: -- -- local cold = not exists(cache .. "/green.txt") -- -- build.sh safari: cold, 192 s, not judged const TIMES_KEPT = 5 const TIMES_HEADER = "when\tstage\tcpu_ms\tms" -- Below this much CPU a change is noise, however large the ratio. const TIMES_LEAST_CHANGE_MS = 1000 -- The file of the script named `book`. function times_path(book) if book == "" or contains(book, "/") or contains(book, ":") then fail("times: the book is a plain name, a file's, not \"" .. book .. "\"") end return "build:times/" .. book .. ".tsv" end -- The file's rows, oldest first; none for a file not there yet. A file that -- is not this shape stops the run rather than losing the history in it. function times_rows(path) local rows = {} if not exists(path) then return rows end local all = lines(read(path)) if #all == 0 or all[1] ~= TIMES_HEADER then fail("times: " .. path .. " does not start with its header") end for i = 2, #all do local f = split(all[i], "\t") if #f ~= 4 then fail("times: " .. path .. ":" .. i .. " is not four fields: " .. all[i]) end push(rows, {when = f[1], stage = f[2], cpu_ms = tonumber(f[3]), ms = tonumber(f[4])}) end return rows end -- The middle of a list that is not empty, the lower of the two for an even -- count, so a single slow run among two never counts as the usual time. function times_middle(list) local sorted = sort(list) return sorted[(#sorted + 1) // 2] end -- `192 s` from ten seconds up, `1.4 s` below. function times_seconds(ms) if ms >= 10000 then return ((ms + 500) // 1000) .. " s" end local tenths = (ms + 50) // 100 return (tenths // 10) .. "." .. (tenths % 10) .. " s" end -- `5.5x`, rounded; "" when the smaller time is zero, which has no ratio. function times_ratio(big, small) if small == 0 then return "" end local tenths = (big * 20 // small + 1) // 2 return (tenths // 10) .. "." .. (tenths % 10) .. "x" end -- The line for a stage's change, or "" for one too small to mean anything: -- less than half as much again, or less than a second. function times_change(stage, was_ms, now_ms) local big = now_ms local small = was_ms if was_ms > now_ms then big = was_ms small = now_ms end if big * 2 < small * 3 or big - small < TIMES_LEAST_CHANGE_MS then return "" end local ratio = times_ratio(big, small) local said = stage .. ": " .. times_seconds(now_ms) .. ", was " .. times_seconds(was_ms) if ratio == "" then return said end if now_ms < was_ms then return said .. " (" .. ratio .. " faster)" end return said .. " (" .. ratio .. ")" end -- Adds `run`'s result `r` to the file and gives the line for its change. function times_note(path, stage, r) if r.ended ~= "exit" or r.code ~= 0 then return "" end local rows = times_rows(path) local recent = {} for row in rows do if row.stage == stage then push(recent, row.cpu_ms) end end local said = "" if #recent > 0 then said = times_change(stage, times_middle(recent), r.cpu_ms) end local left = #recent local text = TIMES_HEADER .. "\n" for row in rows do local keep = true if row.stage == stage then keep = left < TIMES_KEPT left = left - 1 end if keep then text = text .. row.when .. "\t" .. row.stage .. "\t" .. row.cpu_ms .. "\t" .. row.ms .. "\n" end end replace(path, text .. date(now()) .. "\t" .. stage .. "\t" .. r.cpu_ms .. "\t" .. r.ms .. "\n") return said end -- The line for a cold run, which says why a budget went unheld. function times_cold_line(stage, r) return stage .. ": cold, " .. times_seconds(r.cpu_ms) .. ", not judged" end -- `run`, its time kept under `stage` in the book's file, and the change -- printed; a `cold` run's only said. Its answer is `run`'s; `cpu_budget_ms`'s -- stop names the stage. The file is written first, so a `build:` that cannot -- be written stops the run before the program spends its time. function timed_run(book, stage, argv, opts) if stage == "" or contains(stage, "\t") or contains(stage, "\n") then fail("times: a stage's name is one line with no tab, not \"" .. stage .. "\"") end local path = times_path(book) if not exists("build:times") then mkdir("build:times") end local kept = TIMES_HEADER .. "\n" if exists(path) then kept = read(path) end replace(path, kept) local cold = get(opts, "cold", false) local o = {} for k in keys(opts) do if k ~= "cold" and not (cold and k == "cpu_budget_ms") then o[k] = opts[k] end end if has_key(o, "cpu_budget_ms") then o.stage = stage end local r = run(argv, o) if cold then print(times_cold_line(stage, r)) return r end local said = times_note(path, stage, r) if said ~= "" then print(said) end return r end

name: cookbook/write_tree_patch.shale
html: -- This script turns a changed copy of a folder into a patch. Copy the -- folder aside, change the copy, then run this from the repository's root. -- It writes one unified patch that `patch -p1` applies from that root. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/write_tree_patch.shale old=roc new=<copy>/roc under=roc out=test/new_kind/sheep.patch -- -- Give `old` and `new` relative to where the run starts; `under` is the -- folder's path in the repository. The patch compares the files that match -- `like` (`*.roc` unless you give one). A file that is only in the copy is -- added. A file deleted from the copy stays out of the patch. -- -- budget: steps=100000000 const OLD = arg("old", "") const NEW = arg("new", "") const UNDER = arg("under", "") const OUT = arg("out", "") const LIKE = arg("like", "*.roc") if OLD == "" or NEW == "" or UNDER == "" or OUT == "" then fail("write_tree_patch: old=<folder> new=<changed copy> under=<folder's path in the repo> out=<patch file>") end local patch = "" local files = 0 local changed = 0 for e in walk_all(NEW, {kind = "file", like = LIKE}) do local rel = sub(e.path, #NEW + 2) local was = path(OLD, rel) local from = was if not exists(was) then from = "/dev/null" end local r = run({"diff", "-u", "--label", "a/" .. path(UNDER, rel), "--label", "b/" .. path(UNDER, rel), from, e.path}, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 4000000}) -- diff exits 0 when the files match, 1 when they differ, and 2 on trouble. if r.code > 1 then fail("diff " .. rel .. ": code " .. r.code) end if r.code == 1 then patch = patch .. r.out if not ends_with(r.out, "\n") then patch = patch .. "\n" end changed = changed + 1 end files = files + 1 end if changed == 0 then fail("no file under " .. NEW .. " differs from " .. OLD .. ": no patch") end replace(OUT, patch) print(OUT .. ": " .. changed .. " of " .. files .. " files changed")

name: cookbook/zig/add_missing_pubs.shale
html: -- This script finishes a move of Zig declarations by adding the `pub`s that -- only the compiler can name. `zig_move` reports what a move broke, but it -- cannot see a method called through a value (`machine.step()`). The script -- builds, and for each "is not marked 'pub'" error it puts `pub` on the line -- the error's "declared here" note points at. It builds again until the build -- passes, or until only errors of another kind are left, which it prints. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/add_missing_pubs.shale [build=<step>] const MAX_ROUNDS = 20 const MAX_ERRORS_SHOWN = 20 const DECLARED_HERE = "([A-Za-z0-9_/]+\\.zig:[0-9]+):[0-9]+: note: declared here" -- Gives the file and line of the first "declared here" note at or after -- `start`, or nil when there is none. function declaration_site(output, start) local i = start while i <= #output and not contains(output[i], "declared here") do i = i + 1 end if i > #output then return nil end local note = re_find(output[i], DECLARED_HERE) if note == nil then return nil end local parts = split(note.group, ":") return {path = parts[1], line = parse_int(parts[2])} end -- Gives whether the line needed `pub`. function make_pub(site) local line = lines(read(site.path))[site.line] local indent = re_find(line, "^( *)").group local declaration = sub(line, #indent + 1) if starts_with(declaration, "pub ") then return false end edit(site.path, line .. "\n", indent .. "pub " .. declaration .. "\n") return true end -- Acts on one failed build's output, and gives how many lines it made `pub` -- and the errors that are not about `pub`. function fix_reported_declarations(output) local made_pub = 0 local other_errors = {} for i = 1, #output do if contains(output[i], "is not marked 'pub'") then local site = declaration_site(output, i + 1) if site ~= nil and make_pub(site) then made_pub = made_pub + 1 end elseif contains(output[i], "error:") then push(other_errors, output[i]) end end return {made_pub = made_pub, other_errors = other_errors} end local build = {"zig", "build"} if arg("build", "") ~= "" then push(build, arg("build", "")) end local made_pub = 0 local round = 0 local built = false while round < MAX_ROUNDS and not built do round = round + 1 local result = run(build, {timeout_ms = 400000, whole = 2000000}) if result.code == 0 then print("builds after " .. round .. " rounds, " .. made_pub .. " made pub") built = true else local fixes = fix_reported_declarations(lines(result.out)) made_pub = made_pub + fixes.made_pub if fixes.made_pub == 0 then for error_line in take(fixes.other_errors, MAX_ERRORS_SHOWN) do print(error_line) end fail("add_missing_pubs: round " .. round .. ": no pub to make, and it does not build") end end end if not built then fail("add_missing_pubs: still not building after " .. round .. " rounds") end

name: cookbook/zig/check_comments_only.shale
html: -- This recipe checks that a change touches comments only. It reads each Zig -- file as it is and as `rev` holds it, by Zig's tokenizer (`zig_tokens`), -- drops the doc-comment tokens (a plain `//` comment is no token), and holds -- the two lists of tags and texts to be the same. It says "comment-only" for -- each file that passes, and for one that does not, the first token that -- differs, with its line on each side.
