A commit that fails it is split. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_comments_only.shale -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_comments_only.shale rev=origin/master -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_comments_only.shale rev=HEAD~1 files=src/script/vm.zig -- -- `rev` defaults to `HEAD` (the working tree's uncommitted change); -- `files` (comma-separated) defaults to every `.zig` file `git diff -- --name-only rev` names. A file new or gone since `rev` is not -- comment-only. Each version at `rev` is written under -- `.zig-cache/check_comments_only/` for the tokenizer to read. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=400000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 const REV = arg("rev", "HEAD") const FILES = arg("files", "") -- The tokens that are not comments, `{tag, text, line}`. function code_tokens(p) local got = {} for t in zig_tokens(p) do if t.tag ~= "doc_comment" and t.tag ~= "container_doc_comment" then push(got, t) end end return got end local files = {} if FILES ~= "" then for f in split(FILES, ",") do push(files, trim(f)) end else for f in lines(git_call(".", {"diff", "--name-only", REV, "--", "*.zig"}, nil, true, nil).out) do if f ~= "" then push(files, f) end end end if #files == 0 then print("check_comments_only: no .zig file differs from " .. REV) else -- Every file at `rev` from one `git cat-file --batch` (a `git show` a -- file would spend a program on each file): a header line, -- `<object> blob <size>` or `<name> missing`, then that many bytes and a -- newline. local asked = {} for f in files do push(asked, REV .. ":" .. f) end local out = git_call(".", {"cat-file", "--batch"}, nil, true, join(asked, "\n") .. "\n").out local at_rev = {} local pos = 1 for f in files do local nl = find(out, "\n", pos) local header = sub(out, pos, nl - 1) pos = nl + 1 if not ends_with(header, " missing") then local size = parse_int(words(header)[3]) at_rev[f] = sub(out, pos, pos + size - 1) pos = pos + size + 1 end end local failed = 0 for f in files do if not exists(f) or not has_key(at_rev, f) then failed = failed + 1 print(f .. ": not comment-only: the file is new or gone since " .. REV) else local old_path = ".zig-cache/check_comments_only/" .. substitute(f, "/", "__", {missing_ok = true}) replace(old_path, at_rev[f]) local was = code_tokens(old_path) local now = code_tokens(f) local differ = nil local n = #was if #now < n then n = #now end for i = 1, n do if was[i].tag ~= now[i].tag or was[i].text ~= now[i].text then differ = i break end end if differ == nil and #was ~= #now then differ = n + 1 end if differ == nil then print(f .. ": comment-only (" .. #now .. " tokens)") else failed = failed + 1 local w = "the end" if differ <= #was then w = "`" .. was[differ].text .. "` (" .. was[differ].tag .. ", line " .. was[differ].line .. ")" end local h = "the end" if differ <= #now then h = "`" .. now[differ].text .. "` (" .. now[differ].tag .. ", line " .. now[differ].line .. ")" end print(f .. ": NOT comment-only: token " .. differ .. " was " .. w .. ", is " .. h) end end end if failed > 0 then fail("check_comments_only: " .. failed .. " of " .. #files .. " files change more than comments since " .. REV) end print("check_comments_only: all " .. #files .. " files comment-only since " .. REV) end

name: cookbook/zig/check_const_unchanged.shale
html: -- This script checks that a top-level Zig constant holds the same bytes after -- a refactor. It compiles the constant as `rev` had it and as the file has it -- now into a throwaway test beside the file, and Zig compares the two byte for -- byte. That judges what the constant is, not how it is written, which suits a -- page's text spliced from shared parts (`a ++ shared.js ++ b`) or a rewritten -- table. -- -- The test takes its imports from the file as it is now, so a part the new text -- names is found. A constant of the same file that the old text names is not -- found: copy it in, or judge that one too. A constant is found as `const x =` -- or `pub const x =`, so a refactor may add or drop the `pub`. -- -- cd <repo>/<dir> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_const_unchanged.shale path=src/x.zig name=page [rev=HEAD] -- shale cookbook:zig/check_const_unchanged.shale self_test=1 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const PATH = arg("path", "") const NAME = arg("name", "") const REV = arg("rev", "HEAD") not_option("check_const_unchanged", "rev", REV) if not SELF_TEST and (PATH == "" or NAME == "") then fail("check_const_unchanged: path= name= [rev=]") end -- Where `text` starts a line of `source`, or nil. function line_start(source, text) if starts_with(source, text) then return 1 end local newline = find(source, "\n" .. text) if newline == nil then return nil end return newline + 1 end -- Gives the lines of `name`'s declaration in `source`, declared `pub` under the -- name `new_name`. The constant ends at the `;` of a one-line declaration, or -- else at a `;` alone on its line. `where` says what `source` is, for a stop. function constant_as(source, name, new_name, where) local declaration = "const " .. name .. " =" local start = line_start(source, declaration) if start == nil then local after_pub = line_start(source, "pub " .. declaration) if after_pub == nil then fail("check_const_unchanged: no `" .. declaration .. "` or `pub " .. declaration .. "` in " .. where) end start = after_pub + 4 end local text = sub(source, start) local closing_line = find(text, "\n;\n") local semicolon = find(text, ";\n") local last = nil if closing_line ~= nil then last = closing_line + 2 end if semicolon ~= nil and not contains(sub(text, 1, semicolon), "\n") then last = semicolon + 1 end if last == nil then fail("check_const_unchanged: `" .. declaration .. "` has no end in " .. where) end return substitute(sub(text, 1, last), declaration, "pub const " .. new_name .. " =") end function import_lines(source) local imports = {} for line in lines(source) do if (starts_with(line, "const ") or starts_with(line, "pub const ")) and contains(line, "@import(") then push(imports, line) end end return join(imports, "\n") end -- Judges `name` in the file `path` of the checkout `dir`, against `rev`. function judge(dir, path, name, rev) local at = path_under(dir, path) local prefix_from_repo_top = trim(must(run({"git", "rev-parse", "--show-prefix"}, {cwd = dir, timeout_ms = 10000, whole = 4096})).out) local old_source = must(run({"git", "show", rev .. ":" .. prefix_from_repo_top .. path}, {cwd = dir, timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 16777216})).out local new_source = read(at) local test_path = path_under(dirname(at), "zz_const_judge_test.zig") if exists(test_path) then fail("check_const_unchanged: " .. test_path .. " is there already: a judge left behind? remove it") end create(test_path, import_lines(new_source) .. "\nconst zz_testing = @import(\"std\").testing;\n" .. constant_as(old_source, name, "zz_was", path .. " at " .. rev) .. constant_as(new_source, name, "zz_is", path) .. "test \"" .. name .. " is the same bytes as at " .. rev .. "\" { try zz_testing.expectEqualStrings(zz_was, zz_is); }\n") local result = run({"zig", "test", real(test_path)}, {timeout_ms = 300000, tail = 8000}) remove(test_path) if result.code ~= 0 then print(result.out) fail("check_const_unchanged: `" .. name .. "` in " .. path .. " is not the bytes it was at " .. rev) end print("check_const_unchanged: `" .. name .. "` in " .. path .. " is the same bytes as at " .. rev) return nil end function expect(what, got, want) if got ~= want then fail("check_const_unchanged: " .. what .. ": got `" .. got .. "`, wanted `" .. want .. "`") end end function expect_stop(what, stopped, says) if stopped.ok or not contains(stopped.error, says) then fail("check_const_unchanged: " .. what .. " should stop saying `" .. says .. "`") end end function git_in(dir, words_of_git) local argv = {"git", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t"} for w in words_of_git do push(argv, w) end must(run(argv, {cwd = dir, timeout_ms = 30000, tail = 5})) end function self_test() -- Finding it: either form, first in the file or below, on one line or more. local want = "pub const zz = \"x\";\n" expect("a const that opens the file", constant_as("const page = \"x\";\n", "page", "zz", "f"), want) expect("a pub const that opens the file", constant_as("pub const page = \"x\";\n", "page", "zz", "f"), want) expect("a const below", constant_as("const a = 1;\nconst page = \"x\";\nconst b = 2;\n", "page", "zz", "f"), want) expect("a pub const below", constant_as("const a = 1;\npub const page = \"x\";\nconst b = 2;\n", "page", "zz", "f"), want) expect("a pub const on several lines", constant_as("pub const page = \"x\" ++\n \"y\"\n;\n", "page", "zz", "f"), "pub const zz = \"x\" ++\n \"y\"\n;\n") local neither = "no `const page =` or `pub const page =` in f" expect_stop("no such constant", attempt(constant_as, "const a = 1;\n", "page", "zz", "f"), neither) expect_stop("a longer name", attempt(constant_as, "pub const pages = 1;\n", "page", "zz", "f"), neither) expect_stop("a constant with no end", attempt(constant_as, "pub const page = 1", "page", "zz", "f"), "`const page =` has no end in f") -- Judged by Zig: dropping the `pub` and moving the text behind a `pub` import -- keeps the bytes; the same declarations with one byte changed do not. local dir = fresh_dir("scratch:", "check_const_unchanged") git_in(dir, {"init", "-q"}) replace(dir .. "/x.zig", "pub const page = \"ab\";\n") git_in(dir, {"add", "x.zig"}) git_in(dir, {"commit", "-q", "-m", "base"}) replace(dir .. "/parts.zig", "pub const a = \"ab\";\npub const c = \"ac\";\n") replace(dir .. "/x.zig", "pub const parts = @import(\"parts.zig\");\nconst page = parts.a;\n") judge(dir, "x.zig", "page", "HEAD") replace(dir .. "/x.zig", "pub const parts = @import(\"parts.zig\");\npub const page = parts.c;\n") expect_stop("a changed constant", attempt(judge, dir, "x.zig", "page", "HEAD"), "`page` in x.zig is not the bytes it was at HEAD") expect("the throwaway test", tostring(exists(dir .. "/zz_const_judge_test.zig")), "false") remove_tree(dir) print("check_const_unchanged self_test: PASS (const and pub const found and judged, same bytes pass, changed bytes and a missing constant stop)") return nil end if SELF_TEST then self_test() else judge("", PATH, NAME, REV) end

name: cookbook/zig/check_same_tests.shale
html: -- This script checks that a refactor kept a checkout's test suite: every test -- passes, and the same tests run, whichever file holds them. It compares test -- names against a saved baseline, leaving out the module part of each name -- (before ".test."), since a moved test's module changes. -- -- Run it from the checkout whose suite it is (zig-webbox's or shale's), once -- before the refactor and once after: -- shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_same_tests.shale mode=baseline -- shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_same_tests.shale mode=check -- The baseline holds one test's full name a line. const MODE = arg("mode", "") const BASELINE = "zig-out/refactor-baseline.txt" function without_module(test_name) local match = re_find(test_name, "\\.test\\.(.*)$") if match == nil then return test_name end return match.group end function test_names_in(build_output) local names = {} for line in lines(build_output) do local timing = re_find(line, "^ *[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+ s (.*)$") if timing ~= nil and re_find(timing.group, "^total, ") == nil then push(names, timing.group) end end sort(names) return names end function save_baseline(names) replace(BASELINE, join(names, "\n") .. "\n") print("same tests: baseline of " .. #names .. " tests in " .. BASELINE) end function check_against_baseline(names) local current = {} for name in names do push(current, without_module(name)) end local expected = {} for name in lines(read(BASELINE)) do if name ~= "" then push(expected, without_module(name)) end end sort(expected) -- A test name can occur more than once, so each one is counted. local unmatched = {} for name in current do incr(unmatched, name) end local missing = 0 for name in expected do if get(unmatched, name, 0) == 0 then print("missing: " .. name) missing = missing + 1 else unmatched[name] = unmatched[name] - 1 end end local added = 0 for name in keys(unmatched) do if unmatched[name] > 0 then print("new: " .. name) added = added + unmatched[name] end end if missing > 0 or added > 0 then fail(missing .. " missing, " .. added .. " new, of " .. #expected) end print("same tests: " .. #current .. " of " .. #expected .. ", all passing") end if MODE ~= "baseline" and MODE ~= "check" then fail("check_same_tests: give mode=baseline (before the refactor) or mode=check (after)") end local build = run({"zig", "build", "test", "-Dtest-timing"}, {timeout_ms = 110000, whole = 4000000}) if build.code ~= 0 then for line in last(lines(build.out), 40) do print(line) end fail("zig build test exited " .. build.code) end if MODE == "baseline" then save_baseline(test_names_in(build.out)) else check_against_baseline(test_names_in(build.out)) end

name: cookbook/zig/check_stacking.shale
html: -- This recipe finds Zig groups of three or more items on one line. Any -- struct, tuple or array literal, call's or function's argument list, -- container or error set holding three or more items on one line is a -- finding, `path:line: stack: ...`, and so is a line wider than `width` -- (100), `long: ...`. It is the Roc recipe's twin -- (`cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale`). -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_stacking.shale glob=src/**/*.zig -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/check_stacking.shale glob=src/**/*.zig write=1 -- shale cookbook:zig/check_stacking.shale self_test=1 -- -- The rewrite (`write=1`) gives each such group a trailing comma after -- its last item, outermost first, and runs `zig fmt` on the files it -- changed, which lays a group with a trailing comma out one item a line; -- then again, until a pass changes nothing. A long line with no group of -- three gets its widest group of two, as the Roc recipe does. A second -- run changes nothing. Strings and comments are left as they are: the -- scan steps over `"..."` (escapes and all), `'x'`, a `\\` line and a `//` -- comment, so a comma or bracket in one is no item. A capture `|a, b, c|` -- and a `for`'s or `while`'s operands are no group (`zig fmt` takes no -- trailing comma there). What it can't reach is listed: a long line with no -- group (a long string, a long condition). -- -- `self_test=1` reads `cookbook/zig/plants/check_stacking/`: each plant named for -- what it holds must give a finding of its kind, and `clean.zig` none. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 const SELF = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = SELF and "cookbook:zig/plants/check_stacking/*.zig" or arg("glob", "**/*.zig") const WIDTH = arg("width", 100) const WRITE = arg("write", "") == "1" const PASSES = 12 const OPENERS = {["("] = ")", ["{"] = "}", ["["] = "]"} const CLOSERS = {[")"] = true, ["}"] = true, ["]"] = true} -- A line's width, a tab four columns. function width(l) return #l + 3 * (#split(l, "\t") - 1) end -- The last character before `i` that is not a space, or "". function before(l, i) local j = i - 1 while j > 0 and sub(l, j, j) == " " do j = j - 1 end if j == 0 then return "" end return sub(l, j, j) end -- One group closed: its items, by the commas at its depth. function close_group(l, open, close, commas, depth) local inner = trim(sub(l, open + 1, close - 1)) local trailing = ends_with(inner, ",") local items = commas + 1 if trailing then items = commas end if inner == "" then items = 0 end return {open = open, close = close, items = items, trailing = trailing, depth = depth} end -- The groups that open and close on `l`, each `{open, close, items, -- trailing, depth}`: brackets, items counted by the -- commas at the group's own depth. Strings, characters and the comment -- are stepped over. A group that runs onto another line is no group here. function groups(l) local out = {} if starts_with(trim(l), "\\\\") then return out end local opens = {} local kinds = {} local commas = {} local i = 1 local n = #l while i <= n do local c = sub(l, i, i) if c == "\"" then i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(l, i, i) ~= "\"" do if sub(l, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end elseif c == "'" then i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(l, i, i) ~= "'" do if sub(l, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end elseif c == "/" and sub(l, i + 1, i + 1) == "/" then break elseif has_key(OPENERS, c) then push(opens, i) -- A `for`'s or `while`'s operands are no group: kept apart as `x`. local kw = trim(sub(l, 1, i - 1)) if c == "(" and (ends_with(kw, "for") or ends_with(kw, "while")) then push(kinds, "x") else push(kinds, OPENERS[c]) end push(commas, 0) elseif has_key(CLOSERS, c) then -- Pop to the opener this closes; one left open by a `|` that was -- no lambda is dropped with it. while #kinds > 0 and kinds[#kinds] ~= c and not (c == ")" and kinds[#kinds] == "x") do opens = take(opens, #opens - 1) kinds = take(kinds, #kinds - 1) commas = take(commas, #commas - 1) end if #kinds > 0 then if kinds[#kinds] ~= "x" then push(out, close_group(l, opens[#opens], i, commas[#commas], #opens - 1)) end opens = take(opens, #opens - 1) kinds = take(kinds, #kinds - 1) commas = take(commas, #commas - 1) end elseif c == "," and #commas > 0 then commas[#commas] = commas[#commas] + 1 end i = i + 1 end return out end -- The group to stack on `l`: the outermost (then widest) of three or more -- items with no trailing comma; else, on a line over WIDTH, the widest of -- two or more. nil when there is none. function pick(l) local best = nil for g in groups(l) do if g.items >= 3 and not g.trailing then if best == nil or g.depth < best.depth or (g.depth == best.depth and g.close - g.open > best.close - best.open) then best = g end end end if best ~= nil or width(l) <= WIDTH then return best end for g in groups(l) do if g.items >= 2 and not g.trailing then if best == nil or g.close - g.open > best.close - best.open then best = g end end end return best end -- `l` with a comma after the last item of `g`, before the spaces that -- `zig fmt` puts there. function with_comma(l, g) local j = g.close - 1 while j > g.open and sub(l, j, j) == " " do j = j - 1 end return sub(l, 1, j) .. "," .. sub(l, j + 1) end function snip(l, g) local s = sub(l, g.open, g.close) if #s > 60 then s = sub(s, 1, 57) .. "..." end return s end -- Every finding in the files, `{path, line, kind, what}`. function findings(files) local out = {} for p in files do local ls = split(read(p), "\n") for i = 1, #ls do local g = nil for h in groups(ls[i]) do if h.items >= 3 and not h.trailing and (g == nil or h.depth < g.depth) then g = h end end if g ~= nil then push(out, {path = p, line = i, kind = "stack", what = g.items .. " items in " .. snip(ls[i], g)}) elseif width(ls[i]) > WIDTH then local why = starts_with(trim(ls[i]), "//") and "a comment" or (pick(ls[i]) ~= nil and "a group of two to stack" or "nothing to stack") push(out, {path = p, line = i, kind = "long", what = width(ls[i]) .. " columns, " .. why}) end end end return out end function fmt(files) local argv = {"zig", "fmt"} for p in files do push(argv, real(p)) end local r = run(argv, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20}) if r.code ~= 0 then print(r.out) fail("zig fmt failed") end end local files = glob(GLOB) if SELF then local seen = {} for f in findings(files) do local name = sub(f.path, #"cookbook:zig/plants/check_stacking/" + 1) seen[name] = (has_key(seen, name) and seen[name] or "") .. f.kind .. " " end local bad = 0 for p in files do local name = sub(p, #"cookbook:zig/plants/check_stacking/" + 1) local want = starts_with(name, "long") and "long" or "stack" local got = has_key(seen, name) and seen[name] or "" local ok = (name == "clean.zig" and got == "") or (name ~= "clean.zig" and contains(got, want)) print((ok and "ok " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": " .. (got == "" and "no finding" or got)) if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end end if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " plants wrong") end print("PASS: every plant gives its finding, clean.zig none") elseif WRITE then local pass = 1 local changed = 1 while changed > 0 and pass <= PASSES do changed = 0 local touched = {} for p in files do local ls = split(read(p), "\n") local n = 0 for i = 1, #ls do if not starts_with(trim(ls[i]), "//") then local g = pick(ls[i]) if g ~= nil then ls[i] = with_comma(ls[i], g) n = n + 1 end end end if n > 0 then replace(p, join(ls, "\n")) push(touched, p) changed = changed + n end end print("pass " .. pass .. ": " .. changed .. " groups given a trailing comma, in " .. #touched .. " files") if #touched > 0 then fmt(touched) end pass = pass + 1 end if changed > 0 then fail("still changing after " .. PASSES .. " passes") end local left = findings(files) for f in left do print(f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.kind .. ": " .. f.what) end print(#left .. " left, each a line the rewrite can't reach") else local all = findings(files) local stack = 0 for f in all do print(f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.kind .. ": " .. f.what) if f.kind == "stack" then stack = stack + 1 end end print(#all .. " findings in " .. #files .. " files: " .. stack .. " to stack, " .. (#all - stack) .. " long") end

name: cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale
html: -- This recipe counts how much a Zig tree's comments say, and how loudly. For -- each file it gives its code lines, its doc lines (`///`, `//!`), its plain -- `//` lines, comment lines per 100 lines of code, words a comment line, and -- the loud and dated comment lines. Run before and after a commit that -- rewrites comments, it shows what the commit changed. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale -- shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale dir=zig:lib/std/zig files=AstGen.zig,Parse.zig,Zir.zig -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale top=10 -- -- `files` is comma-separated globs under `dir` (default `.`, the root; -- a mount works): default `src/**/*.zig,tools/*.zig,build.zig`. A glob's -- `*` on the command line is the shell's unless quoted. -- -- A line is code when it holds anything but a comment, a comment line -- when it is only one (a comment after code counts as code). A loud line -- holds `**`, a heading of two upper-case words or more (`THE HUNT`), or a -- `──` banner. A dated line names a QUEUE or -- FEEDBACK item, a date (`2026-10-20`), or a person (`Steve`, `the box`, -- `CC`). The table is the loudest first, `top` rows of it (default all), -- then the whole's totals. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=400000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 const DIR = arg("dir", ".") const FILES = arg("files", "src/**/*.zig,tools/*.zig,build.zig") const TOP = arg("top", 0) function is_loud(c) return contains(c, "**") or contains(c, "──") or re_match(c, "\\b[A-Z][A-Z]+ [A-Z][A-Z]+") end function is_dated(c) return re_match(c, "QUEUE|FEEDBACK|\\b20\\d\\d-\\d\\d-\\d\\d\\b|\\bSteve\\b|\\bthe box\\b|\\bCC\\b") end -- The files `FILES` names under `DIR`, each once, in the order named. local paths = {} local seen = {} for pattern in split(FILES, ",") do local p = trim(pattern) local full = p if DIR ~= "." then full = DIR .. "/" .. p end local got = {} if contains(p, "*") then got = glob(full) elseif exists(full) then got = {full} end for g in got do if not get(seen, g, false) then seen[g] = true push(paths, g) end end end if #paths == 0 then fail("count_comments: no file matches " .. FILES .. " under " .. DIR) end local rows = {} local all = {code = 0, doc = 0, plain = 0, words = 0, loud = 0, dated = 0} for p in paths do local r = {code = 0, doc = 0, plain = 0, words = 0, loud = 0, dated = 0} for l in lines(read(p)) do local t = trim(l) if t ~= "" then if starts_with(t, "//") then if starts_with(t, "///") or starts_with(t, "//!") then r.doc = r.doc + 1 else r.plain = r.plain + 1 end r.words = r.words + #words(sub(t, 4)) if is_loud(t) then r.loud = r.loud + 1 end if is_dated(t) then r.dated = r.dated + 1 end else r.code = r.code + 1 end end end for k in keys(all) do all[k] = all[k] + r[k] end local shown = p if DIR ~= "." and starts_with(p, DIR .. "/") then shown = sub(p, #DIR + 2) end push(rows, {file = shown, code = r.code, doc = r.doc, plain = r.plain, loud = r.loud, dated = r.dated, r = r}) end -- A share as `n.d`, of `part` per 100 of `whole`. function per100(part, whole) if whole == 0 then return "-" end local tenths = (part * 1000 + whole // 2) // whole return (tenths // 10) .. "." .. (tenths % 10) end for row in rows do local comments = row.r.doc + row.r.plain row.per100 = per100(comments, row.r.code) row.words = per100(row.r.words, comments * 100) end local sorted = sort(rows, "loud", "desc") if TOP > 0 then sorted = take(sorted, TOP) end print(table(sorted, {"file", "code", "doc", "plain", "per100", "words", "loud", "dated"})) local comments = all.doc + all.plain print(#paths .. " files: " .. all.code .. " code lines, " .. comments .. " comment lines (" .. all.doc .. " doc, " .. all.plain .. " plain), " .. per100(comments, all.code) .. " per 100, " .. per100(all.words, comments * 100) .. " words a line, " .. all.loud .. " loud, " .. all.dated .. " dated")

name: cookbook/zig/find_bool_flags.shale
html: -- This recipe finds `bool` parameters used as flags. It lists each function -- with one, and the calls that pass it a bare `true` or `false`, which says -- nothing at the call (`begin(c, n, true, false)`), where a named enum would -- say what it means (`.chunked`, `.upload`). A computed condition -- (`settle(n == want)`) reads; a literal does not. It reads Zig's tokens -- across the tree: a call is the name, `(`, and its arguments split at the -- commas of its own depth. A method's call (`x.name(`) counts its receiver as -- the first argument. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_bool_flags.shale -- -- `glob=` (default src/**/*.zig) and `glob2=` (a second glob, -- probe/**/*.zig) hold a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin` (see the README). -- -- Each file's tokens are held for the run, so a real tree needs room: -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const GLOB2 = arg("glob2", "") const files = {} for p in glob(GLOB) do push(files, p) end if GLOB2 ~= "" then for p in glob(GLOB2) do push(files, p) end end -- Every function with a bool parameter: name -> {at, params, bools = {i = name}}. const flagged = {} -- How many functions each name declares, anywhere: a name declared twice -- has calls this cannot tell apart, said beside its counts. const declared = {} for p in files do local toks = zig_tokens(p) local n = #toks for k = 1, n - 2 do if toks[k].tag == "keyword_fn" and toks[k + 1].tag == "identifier" and toks[k + 2].tag == "l_paren" then local name = toks[k + 1].text declared[name] = get(declared, name, 0) + 1 local j = k + 3 local depth = 1 local index = 0 local seen_any = false local bools = {} local self_first = false while j <= n and depth > 0 do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "l_paren" or u.tag == "l_brace" or u.tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if u.tag == "r_paren" or u.tag == "r_brace" or u.tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 1 and u.tag == "colon" then index = index + 1 if j < n and toks[j + 1].text == "bool" and toks[j - 1].tag == "identifier" then bools[tostring(index)] = toks[j - 1].text end end j = j + 1 end if count(bools) > 0 then local key = name if has_key(flagged, key) then key = name .. "@" .. p .. ":" .. toks[k].line end flagged[key] = {name = name, at = p .. ":" .. toks[k].line, bools = bools, calls = 0, literal = 0, sites = {}, values = {}} end end end end -- Every call of each, and what it passes where the bool goes. for p in files do local toks = zig_tokens(p) local n = #toks for k = 1, n - 1 do local t = toks[k] if t.tag == "identifier" and toks[k + 1].tag == "l_paren" and has_key(flagged, t.text) and (k == 1 or toks[k - 1].tag ~= "keyword_fn") then local f = flagged[t.text] -- `x.name(`: the receiver is the first parameter (`self`). local index = (k > 1 and toks[k - 1].tag == "period") and 2 or 1 local j = k + 2 local depth = 1 local arg_toks = {} local args = {} while j <= n and depth > 0 do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "l_paren" or u.tag == "l_brace" or u.tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if u.tag == "r_paren" or u.tag == "r_brace" or u.tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 1 and u.tag == "comma" then push(args, arg_toks) arg_toks = {} elseif depth >= 1 then push(arg_toks, u) end j = j + 1 end if #arg_toks > 0 then push(args, arg_toks) end f.calls = f.calls + 1 local bare = false for i = 1, #args do local at = tostring(index + i - 1) local a = args[i] if has_key(f.bools, at) then -- What the call passes there: a literal, or `computed`. local v = (#a == 1 and (a[1].text == "true" or a[1].text == "false")) and a[1].text or "computed" local seen = get(f.values, at, {}) seen[v] = true f.values[at] = seen if v ~= "computed" then bare = true push(f.sites, p .. ":" .. t.line .. " " .. f.bools[at] .. "=" .. v) end end end if bare then f.literal = f.literal + 1 end end end end const rows = {} for key in keys(flagged) do push(rows, flagged[key]) end sort(rows, {{key = "literal", desc = true}, "at"}) print("functions with a bool parameter: " .. #rows .. "; those a call passes a bare true or false:") for f in rows do if f.literal > 0 then local names = {} for i in sort(keys(f.bools)) do push(names, f.bools[i]) end -- **ONE VALUE EVER**: a bool every call passes the same literal is no -- parameter at all. local always = {} for i in sort(keys(f.bools)) do local seen = get(f.values, i, {}) if count(seen) == 1 and not has_key(seen, "computed") then push(always, f.bools[i] .. " is always " .. keys(seen)[1]) end end local note = "" if #always > 0 then note = " ONE VALUE: " .. join(always, ", ") end if declared[f.name] > 1 then note = note .. " (" .. declared[f.name] .. " functions are named " .. f.name .. ": calls of any are counted)" end print(" " .. f.literal .. " of " .. f.calls .. " calls " .. f.name .. "(" .. join(names, ", ") .. ") " .. f.at .. note) for s in take(f.sites, 3) do print(" " .. s) end end end

name: cookbook/zig/find_clones.shale
html: -- This recipe finds the same code in two places: runs of `window=` (6) or -- more lines, alike once each is trimmed, in one file or two. Such a run is -- what a shared function, a table or a loop would say once. Blank lines, -- comments and a line of only brackets (`}`, `};`, `) {`) are passed by, so a -- run is of lines that do something; so are imports and one-name aliases. It -- matches exactly, line by line, so a copy with its names changed is not -- found. -- -- A find is a question, not a fix. Code may be alike on purpose: two -- simulators kept apart to judge each other, or two algorithms whose shared -- setup, an `errdefer` among it, stays each function's own. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_clones.shale [tests=yes] [window=6] [top=20] -- (`glob=`, default src/**/*.zig, holds a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin`; -- see the README.) -- A tree of 75 files passes the default 5,000,000 steps: -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const TESTS = arg("tests", "no") == "yes" const W = parse_int(arg("window", "6")) const TOP = parse_int(arg("top", "20")) -- A line that does something: not blank, no comment, not brackets alone. function significant(t) if t == "" or starts_with(t, "//") then return false end -- An import or a one-name alias (`const X = y.X;`) names, it does nothing. if contains(t, "@import(") then return false end if re_find(t, "^(pub )?const [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* = [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*;$") ~= nil then return false end return re_find(t, "^[{}()\\[\\];,. ]+$") == nil end const files = {} const sig = {} for p in glob(GLOB) do if TESTS or not contains(p, "_test") then local kept = {} local ls = lines(read(p)) -- A `test` block's lines are its own setup, said again in each test; -- passed by unless tests=yes (zig_decls gives each test's lines). local in_test = {} if not TESTS then for d in zig_decls(p) do if d.kind == "test" then for i = d.first, d.last do in_test[tostring(i)] = true end end end end for i = 1, #ls do local t = trim(ls[i]) if significant(t) and not has_key(in_test, tostring(i)) then push(kept, {text = t, line = i}) end end push(files, p) push(sig, kept) end end -- Every window, by its text: file index, its first line's index. const at = {} for f = 1, #files do local kept = sig[f] for i = 1, #kept - W + 1 do local parts = {} for j = i, i + W - 1 do push(parts, kept[j].text) end local key = join(parts, "\n") local places = get(at, key, {}) push(places, {f = f, i = i}) at[key] = places end end -- Each pair of places a window has, by the two files and the offset -- between them, so a run of windows that slide together is one clone. const pairs = {} for key in keys(at) do local places = at[key] if #places >= 2 and #places <= 8 then for a = 1, #places - 1 do for b = a + 1, #places do local x = places[a] local y = places[b] -- A window against itself shifted (a repeated line in one run) is -- no clone of anything. if not (x.f == y.f and y.i - x.i < W) then local id = x.f .. ":" .. y.f .. ":" .. (y.i - x.i) local starts = get(pairs, id, {}) push(starts, x.i) pairs[id] = starts end end end end end const runs = {} for id in keys(pairs) do local parts = split(id, ":") local fa = parse_int(parts[1]) local fb = parse_int(parts[2]) local off = parse_int(parts[3]) local starts = sort(pairs[id]) local first = starts[1] local last = starts[1] for k = 2, #starts + 1 do if k <= #starts and starts[k] == last + 1 then last = starts[k] else local n = last - first + W local a0 = sig[fa][first].line local a1 = sig[fa][last + W - 1].line local b0 = sig[fb][first + off].line local b1 = sig[fb][last + W - 1 + off].line push(runs, {n = n, a = files[fa] .. ":" .. a0 .. "-" .. a1, b = files[fb] .. ":" .. b0 .. "-" .. b1, first = sig[fa][first].text}) if k <= #starts then first = starts[k] last = starts[k] end end end end sort(runs, {{key = "n", desc = true}, "a"}) local lines_in = 0 for r in runs do lines_in = lines_in + r.n end print(#files .. " files (" .. GLOB .. (TESTS and ", tests included" or ", tests left out") .. "): " .. #runs .. " runs of " .. W .. "+ alike lines, " .. lines_in .. " lines in all") for r in take(runs, TOP) do print("") print(r.n .. " lines " .. r.a) print(" and " .. r.b) print(" " .. sub(r.first, 1, 100)) end if #runs > TOP then print("") print("... " .. (#runs - TOP) .. " more (top=)") end

name: cookbook/zig/find_dead_code.shale
html: -- This recipe finds Zig declarations nothing uses. Zig never reports them, -- because its analysis is lazy, so a function nobody calls sits in its file. -- It reads Zig's tokens and reports two kinds: -- -- - dead: a top-level declaration that is not `pub` and whose name no -- other identifier in its file is (not after a `.` either: a private -- name is only reached bare). This is certain, as nothing outside can -- see it. -- - unreached, pub: a `pub` one no identifier in the tree names, bare or -- after a `.`. This is a question, not a verdict: another repo, a build -- script, or `@field(x, "name")` may reach it. -- -- Tests, `comptime` blocks, `export`ed and `extern` declarations, and -- `_` are never counted dead. `main`, `panic` and the root's `std_options` -- are a program's, by name. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_dead_code.shale [drop=yes] -- -- `glob=` (default src/**/*.zig) and `also=` (a second glob, -- probe/**/*.zig) hold a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin` (see the README). -- -- `drop=yes` removes the dead ones (never a pub one), each by its own -- bytes (`zig_decls`' start and stop, its doc comment with it), the last -- in a file first; a run with `--undo-on-stop` puts them back on a stop. -- The compiler and the tests judge after. -- -- Each file's tokens are held for the run, so a real tree needs room: -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const DROP = arg("drop", "no") == "yes" const ALSO = arg("also", "") const files = {} for p in glob(GLOB) do push(files, p) end if ALSO ~= "" then for p in glob(ALSO) do push(files, p) end end -- Every identifier in the tree, by name: how many times, and per file. const tree = {} const per_file = {} for p in files do local mine = {} for t in zig_tokens(p, {tag = "identifier"}) do tree[t.text] = get(tree, t.text, 0) + 1 mine[t.text] = get(mine, t.text, 0) + 1 end per_file[p] = mine end const by_name = {main = true, panic = true, std_options = true, _ = true} const dead = {} const unreached = {} for p in files do for d in zig_decls(p) do local skip = d.kind == "test" or d.kind == "comptime" or d.kind == "field" or d.linkage ~= "none" or d.name_form ~= "identifier" or has_key(by_name, d.name) if not skip then -- Its own name is one identifier; any more is a use. if d.visibility ~= "pub" then if get(per_file[p], d.name, 0) <= 1 then push(dead, {at = p .. ":" .. d.first, p = p, name = d.name, kind = d.kind, lines = d.last - d.first + 1, start = d.start, stop = d.stop}) end elseif get(tree, d.name, 0) <= 1 then push(unreached, {at = p .. ":" .. d.first, name = d.name, kind = d.kind, lines = d.last - d.first + 1}) end end end end sort(dead, {{key = "lines", desc = true}, "at"}) sort(unreached, {{key = "lines", desc = true}, "at"}) local dead_lines = 0 for d in dead do dead_lines = dead_lines + d.lines end print(#files .. " files: " .. #dead .. " dead (" .. dead_lines .. " lines), " .. #unreached .. " pub ones the tree never names") print("") print("dead (not pub, unnamed in its file):") for d in dead do print(" " .. d.lines .. " lines " .. d.kind .. " " .. d.name .. " " .. d.at) end print("") print("pub, unnamed anywhere in the tree (another repo, a build, @field?):") for d in unreached do print(" " .. d.lines .. " lines " .. d.kind .. " " .. d.name .. " " .. d.at) end if DROP and #dead > 0 then local in_file = {} for d in dead do local l = get(in_file, d.p, {}) push(l, d) in_file[d.p] = l end for p in sort(keys(in_file)) do -- The last first, so each one's bytes are where zig_decls said. local ds = sort(in_file[p], {{key = "start", desc = true}}) local t = read(p) for d in ds do local after = sub(t, d.stop + 1) -- Its line's own newline goes with it. if starts_with(after, "\n") then after = sub(after, 2) end local before = sub(t, 1, d.start) -- Blank lines on both sides become one, as zig fmt keeps them. while ends_with(before, "\n\n") and starts_with(after, "\n") do after = sub(after, 2) end t = before .. after end replace(p, t) print("dropped " .. #ds .. " from " .. p) end end

name: cookbook/zig/find_repeated_params.shale
html: -- This recipe finds the same parameters in a row in function after function: -- a run of parameter names (`conv_dir, conv_key, sid`) that several -- functions declare, in that order. A long list is a question; a run that -- recurs is a struct with more than one user already, which is when one -- earns its keep. It reads Zig's tokens: each `fn`'s names before a `:` at -- its parentheses' own depth. -- -- The plumbing every handler takes (`skip=`, by default io, alloc, a, -- req, bus, self, gpa, arena, and a comparator's `_`) is passed by, so runs are of the parameters -- that say what a function is about. A run is reported once, at its -- longest: a shorter run inside it, in no more functions, is left out. -- Functions are counted by name: an interface's implementations (a -- writer's `drain` in five files, a vtable's `read`) declare one shape -- because they must, so a run needs `min` distinct names. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_repeated_params.shale [min=3] [longest=4] [skip=io,alloc] [top=15] -- (`glob=`, default src/**/*.zig, holds a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin`; -- see the README.) -- -- Each file's tokens are held for the run, so a real tree needs room: -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const MIN = parse_int(arg("min", "3")) const LONGEST = parse_int(arg("longest", "4")) const TOP = parse_int(arg("top", "15")) const SKIP = {} for w in split(arg("skip", "io,alloc,a,req,bus,self,gpa,arena,_"), ",") do SKIP[trim(w)] = true end -- Each function's parameter names, plumbing passed by. const fns = {} function params_of(p) local toks = zig_tokens(p) local n = #toks local k = 1 while k <= n do local t = toks[k] if t.tag == "keyword_fn" and k < n and toks[k + 1].tag == "identifier" and k + 2 <= n and toks[k + 2].tag == "l_paren" then local names = {} local depth = 1 local j = k + 3 while j <= n and depth > 0 do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "l_paren" or u.tag == "l_brace" or u.tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if u.tag == "r_paren" or u.tag == "r_brace" or u.tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 1 and u.tag == "colon" and toks[j - 1].tag == "identifier" and not has_key(SKIP, toks[j - 1].text) then push(names, toks[j - 1].text) end j = j + 1 end push(fns, {name = toks[k + 1].text, at = p .. ":" .. t.line, names = names}) k = j else k = k + 1 end end end for p in glob(GLOB) do params_of(p) end -- Every run of 2 to LONGEST names, and the functions declaring it. const runs = {} for f in fns do local seen = {} local m = #f.names for i = 1, m do local len = 2 local key = f.names[i] while len <= LONGEST and i + len - 1 <= m do key = key .. ", " .. f.names[i + len - 1] if not has_key(seen, key) then seen[key] = true local r = get(runs, key, {key = key, len = len, at = {}, names = {}}) push(r.at, f.name .. " " .. f.at) r.names[f.name] = true runs[key] = r end len = len + 1 end end end -- Kept: in MIN functions or more, and not inside a longer kept run that -- as many functions declare. const kept = {} for key in keys(runs) do local r = runs[key] if count(r.names) >= MIN then push(kept, {key = key, len = r.len, n = count(r.names), at = r.at}) end end const shown = {} for r in kept do local inside = false for o in kept do if o.len > r.len and o.n >= r.n and contains(", " .. o.key .. ", ", ", " .. r.key .. ", ") then inside = true end end if not inside then push(shown, r) end end sort(shown, {{key = "n", desc = true}, {key = "len", desc = true}, "key"}) print(#fns .. " functions; " .. #shown .. " runs of parameters in " .. MIN .. " or more names") local i = 0 for r in shown do i = i + 1 if i > TOP then print(" ... " .. (#shown - TOP) .. " more (top=)") break end print("") print(" " .. r.n .. " names, " .. #r.at .. " functions (" .. r.key .. ")") for a in sort(r.at) do print(" " .. a) end end

name: cookbook/zig/find_seams.shale
html: -- This recipe finds where a Zig file divides. It reads the file's top-level -- declarations as a graph (zig_decls' `uses`), sets the hubs aside (what much -- of the file uses, and what uses much of it), and looks at what is left. It -- prints a count line (declarations, production and tests, the edges left), -- the largest declarations (150 lines or more), the hubs with their edges in -- and out, the cut profile in file order (the gaps the fewest edges cross, -- each with the edges that cross it), and each declaration grouped by the -- hubs that reach it: the structure by caller. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_seams.shale path=src/x.zig [container=Name] [hub=N] [out=N] [min=N] [show=N] [names=N] -- -- `container=Name`: that container's members, not the file's, with what -- each reaches through a `.` (`self.slots`) counted as a use. -- `hub=N`: a declaration that N or more use is a hub (default: an eighth -- of the production declarations, at least 4). -- `out=N`: a declaration that uses N or more is a hub (default: a sixth of -- them, at least 6). -- `min=N`: a gap is listed only with N lines or more on each side (120). -- `show=N`: how many gaps the cut profile lists (10). -- `names=N`: how many declarations each group lists (12). const P = arg("path", "") const SHOW = parse_int(arg("show", "10")) const C = arg("container", "") const NAMES_SHOWN = parse_int(arg("names", "12")) function lines_of(d) return d.last - d.first + 1 end function root_of(parent, x) local r = x while parent[r] ~= r do r = parent[r] end return r end function union(parent, a, b) local ra = root_of(parent, a) local rb = root_of(parent, b) if ra ~= rb then parent[ra] = rb end return nil end function member(l, x) for y in l do if y == x then return true end end return false end if P == "" then fail("seams: give path=src/x.zig") end local decls = nil if C == "" then decls = zig_decls(P) else decls = zig_decls(P, {container = C}) -- A member's edges: the names it uses and the members it reaches. for d in decls do for r in d.reaches do if not member(d.uses, r) then push(d.uses, r) end end end end local imported = {} for i in zig_imports(P) do if i.name ~= "" then imported[i.name] = true end end -- A const that only renames another (`const Io = std.Io;`) is an import too. local prod = {} local tests = {} local by_name = {} local total = 0 for d in decls do total = total + lines_of(d) if d.kind == "test" then push(tests, d) elseif d.name ~= "" and not has_key(imported, d.name) then local text = read(P, d.start, d.stop - d.start) local alias = re_find(text, "^(pub )?const [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* = [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*;$") ~= nil if alias and lines_of(d) == 1 and #d.uses <= 1 then imported[d.name] = true else push(prod, d) by_name[d.name] = d end end end -- How many production declarations use each name (its fan-in), and how -- many it uses (its fan-out). local used_by = {} local uses_n = {} for d in prod do local n = 0 for u in d.uses do if has_key(by_name, u) then used_by[u] = get(used_by, u, 0) + 1 n = n + 1 end end uses_n[d.name] = n end -- A hub is one of two kinds: what much of the file uses (a shared type or -- helper), and what uses much of the file (an orchestrator: `main`, -- `serve`). Either glues everything to everything; set aside, what is left -- shows its parts. local in_at = parse_int(arg("hub", tostring(max(4, #prod // 8)))) local out_at = parse_int(arg("out", tostring(max(6, #prod // 6)))) local hubs = {} local hub_names = {} for d in prod do local fin = get(used_by, d.name, 0) if fin >= in_at or uses_n[d.name] >= out_at then hubs[d.name] = true push(hub_names, d.name .. " (in " .. fin .. ", out " .. uses_n[d.name] .. ")") end end -- The rest, in file order, with the edges among them. local rest = {} local at = {} for d in prod do if not has_key(hubs, d.name) then push(rest, d) at[d.name] = #rest end end local edges = {} for d in rest do for u in d.uses do if has_key(at, u) then push(edges, {a = at[d.name], b = at[u], text = d.name .. "->" .. u}) end end end local before = {} local sum = 0 for i = 1, #rest do sum = sum + lines_of(rest[i]) before[i] = sum end print(P .. ": " .. #decls .. " declarations; " .. #prod .. " production, " .. #tests .. " tests; " .. #rest .. " left once " .. #hub_names .. " hubs are set aside, " .. #edges .. " edges among them") local big = {} for d in decls do if lines_of(d) >= 150 then push(big, d.name .. ":" .. d.first .. "(" .. lines_of(d) .. ")") end end if #big > 0 then print("largest (150+ lines; a seam inside one is below the top level): " .. join(big, ", ")) end print("hubs: " .. join(hub_names, ", ")) -- The cut profile: for each gap after the i-th, the edges that cross -- it; a gap few cross, with code on both sides, is a seam in the file's -- own order. local min_lines = parse_int(arg("min", "120")) local gaps = {} for i = 1, #rest - 1 do local left = before[i] local right = sum - left if left >= min_lines and right >= min_lines then local crossing = {} for e in edges do local lo = min(e.a, e.b) local hi = max(e.a, e.b) if lo <= i and hi > i then push(crossing, e.text) end end push(gaps, {i = i, n = #crossing, crossing = crossing, left = left, right = right}) end end print("") print("the gaps fewest edges cross (each side at least " .. min_lines .. " lines):") local shown = 0 local taken = {} while shown < SHOW and count(taken) < #gaps do local best = 0 for k = 1, #gaps do if not has_key(taken, tostring(k)) then if best == 0 or gaps[k].n < gaps[best].n then best = k end end end taken[tostring(best)] = true local g = gaps[best] -- Neighbours of a gap already shown say the same seam: shown once. local near = false for k in keys(taken) do local o = gaps[parse_int(k)] if o.i ~= g.i and o.i >= g.i - 2 and o.i <= g.i + 2 and get(o, "shown", false) then near = true end end if not near then g.shown = true shown = shown + 1 local a = rest[g.i] local b = rest[g.i + 1] print(" after " .. a.name .. ":" .. a.last .. ", before " .. b.name .. ":" .. b.first .. ": " .. g.n .. " cross (" .. g.left .. " lines above, " .. g.right .. " below)" .. (g.n > 0 and (": " .. join(take(g.crossing, 6), ", ")) or "")) end end -- Each declaration that is not a hub, grouped by the -- hubs whose uses reach it (through other declarations, not through -- hubs). A helper only `serve` reaches goes with `serve`; one `main` and -- `serve` both reach is shared; one no hub reaches is the tests' or dead. -- This is the file's structure by caller, whatever its order. local reached = {} for d in rest do reached[d.name] = {} end for h in prod do if has_key(hubs, h.name) then local todo = {} for u in h.uses do if has_key(at, u) then push(todo, u) end end local seen = {} while #todo > 0 do local x = todo[#todo] todo = take(todo, #todo - 1) if not has_key(seen, x) then seen[x] = true push(reached[x], h.name) for u in rest[at[x]].uses do if has_key(at, u) and not has_key(seen, u) then push(todo, u) end end end end end end local by_sig = {} local sigs = {} for d in rest do local hs = reached[d.name] sort(hs) local sig = join(hs, " + ") if sig == "" then sig = "(no hub: tests' or unused)" end if not has_key(by_sig, sig) then by_sig[sig] = {lines = 0, names = {}} push(sigs, sig) end by_sig[sig].lines = by_sig[sig].lines + lines_of(d) push(by_sig[sig].names, d.name .. ":" .. d.first .. "(" .. lines_of(d) .. ")") end print("") print("by the hubs that reach them:") for s in sigs do local g = by_sig[s] print(" " .. s .. ": " .. #g.names .. " declarations, " .. g.lines .. " lines: " .. join(take(g.names, NAMES_SHOWN), ", ") .. (#g.names > NAMES_SHOWN and (", ... " .. (#g.names - NAMES_SHOWN) .. " more") or "")) end

name: cookbook/zig/find_smells.shale
html: -- This recipe lists the places in a Zig tree that may want a second look, -- each smell a list, read from Zig's tokens (so never a comment's or a -- string's). A list is a question, not a verdict: -- -- - a long function (`long=` lines, 80), a struct's members and nested -- functions included; -- - a long parameter list (`params=`, 6): a struct waiting to be named; -- - a flag-like `bool` parameter or field: a named enum says what true -- means at each call (`f(x, true)` says nothing); -- - an error swallowed, `catch {}`, and `catch unreachable` (a crash -- where a reason was due), each counted by file; -- - a protocol in comments: three or more numbered steps (`// 1.`) in a -- file, where a call order wants to be a function or a type. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/find_smells.shale [tests=yes] [long=80] [params=6] [top=15] -- (`glob=`, default src/**/*.zig, holds a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin`; -- see the README.) -- -- Each file's tokens are held for the run, so a real tree needs room -- past the defaults (zig-webbox's 70 files ran out of arena): -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const TESTS = arg("tests", "no") == "yes" const LONG = parse_int(arg("long", "80")) const PARAMS = parse_int(arg("params", "6")) const TOP = parse_int(arg("top", "15")) -- The lists every file adds to (a function sees the script's `const`s). const fns = {} const bool_params = {} const bool_fields = {} const swallowed = {} const crashes = {} const protocols = {} local files = 0 function smells_of(p) local toks = zig_tokens(p) local n = #toks local paren = 0 local k = 1 while k <= n do local t = toks[k] if t.tag == "l_paren" then paren = paren + 1 end if t.tag == "r_paren" then paren = paren - 1 end -- A function: its name, its parameters, its body's lines. if t.tag == "keyword_fn" and k < n and toks[k + 1].tag == "identifier" then local name = toks[k + 1].text local j = k + 2 local params = 0 local any = false local depth = 0 if j <= n and toks[j].tag == "l_paren" then depth = 1 j = j + 1 while j <= n and depth > 0 do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "l_paren" or u.tag == "l_brace" or u.tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if u.tag == "r_paren" or u.tag == "r_brace" or u.tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 1 and u.tag == "colon" then params = params + 1 if j < n and toks[j + 1].text == "bool" and toks[j - 1].tag == "identifier" then push(bool_params, p .. ":" .. u.line .. " " .. name .. "(" .. toks[j - 1].text .. ": bool)") end end j = j + 1 end end if params >= PARAMS then push(fns, {kind = "params", n = params, at = p .. ":" .. t.line, name = name}) end -- `fn X(...) type`: a type made of its arguments (a generic -- container), long as its struct is, not a function to cut. local makes_type = j <= n and toks[j].text == "type" -- The body: the first `{` at no depth that no `error` names, unless -- a `;` comes first (an extern, a function type). local body = nil while j <= n and body == nil do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "semicolon" then break end if u.tag == "l_brace" and toks[j - 1].tag ~= "keyword_error" then body = j end if u.tag == "l_brace" and toks[j - 1].tag == "keyword_error" then local d = 1 j = j + 1 while j <= n and d > 0 do if toks[j].tag == "l_brace" then d = d + 1 end if toks[j].tag == "r_brace" then d = d - 1 end if d > 0 then j = j + 1 end end end j = j + 1 end if body ~= nil then local d = 1 local e = body + 1 while e <= n and d > 0 do if toks[e].tag == "l_brace" then d = d + 1 end if toks[e].tag == "r_brace" then d = d - 1 end if d > 0 then e = e + 1 end end if e <= n then local len = toks[e].line - t.line + 1 if len >= LONG then push(fns, {kind = "long", n = len, at = p .. ":" .. t.line, name = makes_type and (name .. " (a type)") or name}) end end end end -- A field `name: bool` (after a `,` or a container's `{`), at no -- parenthesis: not a parameter, not a local (`const x: bool`). if t.tag == "colon" and paren == 0 and k > 2 and k < n and toks[k + 1].text == "bool" and toks[k - 1].tag == "identifier" then local before = toks[k - 2].tag if before == "comma" or before == "l_brace" or before == "doc_comment" then push(bool_fields, p .. ":" .. t.line .. " " .. toks[k - 1].text .. ": bool") end end if t.tag == "keyword_catch" and k + 2 <= n and toks[k + 1].tag == "l_brace" and toks[k + 2].tag == "r_brace" then -- Inside another error's handler (`catch |e| { ... }`), a cleanup -- whose own failure the error already returned outranks: apart. local in_handler = false local back = k - 1 local d = 0 while back > 1 and back > k - 60 and not in_handler do if toks[back].tag == "r_brace" then d = d + 1 end if toks[back].tag == "l_brace" then if d == 0 and toks[back - 1].tag == "pipe" and back > 4 and toks[back - 4].tag == "keyword_catch" then in_handler = true end d = d - 1 end back = back - 1 end local key = in_handler and (p .. " (a cleanup in an error's handler)") or p swallowed[key] = get(swallowed, key, 0) + 1 end if t.tag == "keyword_catch" and k < n and toks[k + 1].tag == "keyword_unreachable" then crashes[p] = get(crashes, p, 0) + 1 end k = k + 1 end -- Numbered steps in comments: the comments are no tokens, so lines. local steps = 0 for l in lines(read(p)) do if re_find(l, "^ *//+ +[0-9]+[.)] ") ~= nil then steps = steps + 1 end end if steps >= 3 then push(protocols, {at = p, n = steps}) end end for p in glob(GLOB) do -- A test's file is named *_test.zig, or a test helper's *_test_*.zig. if TESTS or not contains(p, "_test") then files = files + 1 smells_of(p) end end function section(title, rows) print("") print(title .. " (" .. #rows .. ")") for r in take(rows, TOP) do print(" " .. r) end if #rows > TOP then print(" ... " .. (#rows - TOP) .. " more (top=)") end end local long = {} local many = {} for f in fns do if f.kind == "long" then push(long, f) else push(many, f) end end sort(long, {{key = "n", desc = true}, "at"}) sort(many, {{key = "n", desc = true}, "at"}) local long_rows = {} for f in long do push(long_rows, f.n .. " lines " .. f.name .. " " .. f.at) end local many_rows = {} for f in many do push(many_rows, f.n .. " params " .. f.name .. " " .. f.at) end function counted(m) local rows = {} for p in keys(m) do push(rows, {p = p, n = m[p]}) end sort(rows, {{key = "n", desc = true}, "p"}) local out = {} for r in rows do push(out, r.n .. " " .. r.p) end return out end sort(protocols, {{key = "n", desc = true}, "at"}) local proto_rows = {} for r in protocols do push(proto_rows, r.n .. " numbered steps " .. r.at) end print(files .. " files (" .. GLOB .. (TESTS and ", tests included" or ", tests left out") .. ")") section("functions of " .. LONG .. "+ lines", long_rows) section("functions of " .. PARAMS .. "+ parameters", many_rows) section("bool parameters", sort(bool_params)) section("bool fields", sort(bool_fields)) section("catch {} (an error swallowed), by file", counted(swallowed)) section("catch unreachable, by file", counted(crashes)) section("numbered steps in comments (a function's own order is fine; a caller's is a protocol to make code)", proto_rows)

name: cookbook/zig/flip_bools.shale
html: -- This recipe flips each bare `true` or `false` a call passes and runs the -- tests. A flip the tests let through is a decision nothing checks. It is -- mutation testing kept to the one mutation that names a choice at a call: a -- bool argument (`f(x, true)`), outside tests, comments and strings' lines. -- Each flip is planted alone, the build's tests run, and the file is put back -- before the next; under `--undo-on-stop` a stop puts it back too. -- -- It is a hunt, never a gate: each flip is a whole test run (half a minute in -- angry-gopher), so it runs alone, detached, and what survives becomes a -- test, or an enum and a test. -- -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/zig/flip_bools.shale [build=test] [most=40] [timeout_ms=600000] -- (`glob=`, default src/**/*.zig, holds a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin`; -- see the README.) -- -- `most` caps the flips a run plants; the rest are listed, not run. -- -- Read each survivor before believing it. One in code the build step never -- runs (a bench's own binary) survives for that alone, and one a separate -- step judges (angry-gopher's `markdown-regression`) wants `build=` that -- step. Some survivors change nothing that matters. const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const BUILD = arg("build", "test") not_option("flip_bools", "build", BUILD) const MOST = parse_int(arg("most", "40")) const TIMEOUT = parse_int(arg("timeout_ms", "600000")) -- Whether `c` may be part of a name. function ident(c) return c ~= "" and re_find(c, "[A-Za-z0-9_]") ~= nil end -- The candidates: a whole `true` or `false` right after `(` or `, ` and -- right before `)` or `,`, on a line that is no comment, outside any -- top-level `test "..." {` block, in a file that is no test file. const sites = {} for p in glob(GLOB) do if not ends_with(p, "_test.zig") then local ls = lines(read(p)) local in_test = false for i = 1, #ls do local l = ls[i] if starts_with(l, "test \"") or starts_with(l, "test {") then in_test = true end if in_test and l == "}" then in_test = false elseif not in_test and not starts_with(trim(l), "//") and find(l, "\"") == nil then for word in {"true", "false"} do local from = 1 while true do local at = find(l, word, from) if at == nil then break end local before = sub(l, at - 2, at - 1) local after = sub(l, at + #word, at + #word) local opens = ends_with(before, "(") or before == ", " if opens and (after == ")" or after == ",") and not ident(sub(l, at - 1, at - 1)) then push(sites, {p = p, line = i, at = at, word = word}) end from = at + #word end end end end end end print(#sites .. " bare bool arguments outside tests") const survived = {} local planted = 0 for s in sites do if planted >= MOST then break end planted = planted + 1 local good = read(s.p) local ls = lines(good) local l = ls[s.line] local flip = s.word == "true" and "false" or "true" ls[s.line] = sub(l, 1, s.at - 1) .. flip .. sub(l, s.at + #s.word) replace(s.p, join(ls, "\n") .. "\n") local r = run({"zig", "build", BUILD}, {timeout_ms = TIMEOUT, tail = 3}) replace(s.p, good) local where = s.p .. ":" .. s.line .. " " .. trim(l) if r.code == 0 then push(survived, where) print("SURVIVED " .. where) else print("caught " .. s.p .. ":" .. s.line) end end print("") print(planted .. " flipped, " .. #survived .. " survived" .. (#sites > planted and ("; " .. (#sites - planted) .. " not run (most=)") or "")) for w in survived do print(" " .. w) end

name: cookbook/zig/hunt_alignment_math.shale
html: -- This recipe hunts a Zig compiler for code that copies alignment arithmetic -- instead of asking for it. The alignment is known in one place (a layout -- store, `@alignOf(T)`, a string blob's `strings.alignment(id)`), and code -- that copies the arithmetic uses a stand-in or forgets to ask. The -- archetype is roc-lang/roc#12641: `addAllocation(.u8, len, self.word_size, -- ...)` where the blob needed `@max(word, strings.alignment(id))`. It is -- written for the Roc compiler; each check is a few lines, to copy and -- change for another tree. -- -- cd <roc> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/hunt_alignment_math.shale -- cd <shale> && shale cookbook/zig/hunt_alignment_math.shale self_test=1 -- -- The checks, each by name: -- stand_in_alignment an allocation's alignment argument is the word -- (`word_size`, `@alignOf(usize)`, `@sizeOf(usize)`) -- or a literal 8 or 16 -- backing_without_alignment a function reads a string backing -- (`getString(`, `getStringLiteralBacking(`), -- copies, allocates or emits it, and never -- asks `strings.alignment(` -- duplicated_header_formula `alignForward` of a word, a header or extra -- bytes: the refcount and blob header rule, copied; -- all of them, to read side by side -- duplicated_arg_layout a comparator ordering by alignment, and each -- `entrypointParamSlotSize` / `computeArgOffsets`: -- copies of one layout rule -- dealloc_ignores_alignment a dealloc callback (`roc*Dealloc`, an -- allocator's `free`) whose alignment is `_` -- unchecked_aligncast `@alignCast` of a base plus an offset, in a -- function with no `% @alignOf` or `isAligned` -- host_size_in_target_code `@sizeOf(usize)` / `@alignOf(usize)` in -- `layout/`, or in a function with a `Target` or -- `target_usize` parameter -- -- A finding is a question for a reader, not a verdict. Everything is read -- from Zig's tokenizer, so a comment or a string never counts. Output: -- `path:line: <check>: <why>`, then a count per check. -- -- `glob=` (default src/**/*.zig) holds a `*`: on stdin, `--args-stdin`. -- `self_test=1` runs on the plants in cookbook/zig/plants/hunt_alignment_math/ -- (from the shale checkout): each `<check>.zig` must fire its check, and -- `clean.zig` nothing; then PASS or FAIL. -- -- Each file's tokens are walked whole, so a compiler-sized tree needs room: -- -- budget: steps=4000000000 read_bytes=500000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 output_bytes=1000000 const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "0") == "1" const PLANTS = "cookbook/zig/plants/hunt_alignment_math" const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/*.zig") or arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const CHECKS = {"stand_in_alignment", "backing_without_alignment", "duplicated_header_formula", "duplicated_arg_layout", "dealloc_ignores_alignment", "unchecked_aligncast", "host_size_in_target_code"} -- Which argument of each call is its alignment, counted as written -- (`self.addAllocation(.u8, len, align, ...)`: the third). const ALIGN_ARG = {addAllocation = 3, reserveAllocation = 3, allocateWithRefcount = 2, unsafeReallocate = 2, allocStackMemory = 2, setAlignment = 1, alignedAlloc = 2} -- An alignment argument that is a stand-in, not an answer: the whole -- argument, its spaces gone. const STAND_INS = {"^([\\w.()]+\\.)?word_size$", "^@intCast\\(([\\w.()]+\\.)?word_size\\)$", "^@alignOf\\(usize\\)$", "^@sizeOf\\(usize\\)$", "^(8|16)$", "^@as\\(u\\d+,(8|16)\\)$", "^\\.@\"(8|16)\"$", "fromByteUnits\\((8|16)\\)$"} -- What a function calls to turn a string backing into data. const DATA_SINKS = {"@memcpy(", "addAllocation(", "appendSlice(", "dupe(", "alignedAlloc(", "allocStackMemory(", "setAlignment(", "setInitializer("} -- Every finding: {check, at, line, why}. const FOUND = {} function report(check, p, line, why) push(FOUND, {check = check, at = p, line = line, why = why}) end -- Tokens a..b as text, a space only where two words would run together: -- `lhs.alignment > rhs.alignment` reads `lhs.alignment>rhs.alignment`. function text_of(toks, a, b) local parts = {} local prev = "" for k = a, b do local t = toks[k].text if prev ~= "" and re_match(sub(prev, -1) .. sub(t, 1, 1), "^\\w\\w$") then push(parts, " ") end push(parts, t) prev = t end return join(parts, "") end -- The token closing the bracket opened at k. function close_of(toks, k) local depth = 0 for j = k, #toks do local tag = toks[j].tag if tag == "l_paren" or tag == "l_brace" or tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if tag == "r_paren" or tag == "r_brace" or tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 if depth == 0 then return j end end end return #toks end -- The arguments of the call whose `(` is at k, each as text. function args_of(toks, k) local last = close_of(toks, k) local args = {} local from = k + 1 local depth = 0 for j = k + 1, last - 1 do local tag = toks[j].tag if tag == "l_paren" or tag == "l_brace" or tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if tag == "r_paren" or tag == "r_brace" or tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 0 and tag == "comma" then push(args, text_of(toks, from, j - 1)) from = j + 1 end end if from <= last - 1 then push(args, text_of(toks, from, last - 1)) end return args end -- Each `fn name(...) ... { ... }` with a body: {name, first, last (tokens), -- line, params, sig}. The body is the first `{` after the parameters that -- does not open a return type's `struct`, `union`, `enum` or error set. function functions_of(toks) local fns = {} for k = 1, #toks - 2 do if toks[k].tag == "keyword_fn" and toks[k + 1].tag == "identifier" and toks[k + 2].tag == "l_paren" then local params_end = close_of(toks, k + 2) local j = params_end + 1 local body = 0 while j <= #toks and body == 0 do local tag = toks[j].tag if tag == "semicolon" then break end if tag == "l_brace" then local before = toks[j - 1].tag if before == "keyword_struct" or before == "keyword_union" or before == "keyword_enum" or before == "keyword_opaque" or before == "keyword_error" or before == "r_paren" and j - params_end > 1 then j = close_of(toks, j) else body = j end elseif tag == "l_paren" or tag == "l_bracket" then j = close_of(toks, j) end j = j + 1 end if body > 0 then push(fns, {name = toks[k + 1].text, first = k, last = close_of(toks, body), line = toks[k].line, params = args_of(toks, k + 2), sig = text_of(toks, k, body - 1)}) end end end return fns end -- The innermost function holding token k, or nil. function fn_at(fns, k) local found = nil for f in fns do if f.first <= k and k <= f.last then found = f end end return found end function stand_in(a) for pat in STAND_INS do if re_match(a, pat) then return true end end return false end -- Whether a parameter is a target: its type a `Target` (`std.Target`, -- `RocTarget`), or its name the target's word (`target_usize`, -- `target_word_size`). Parameters read `name:type`. function takes_target(f) for q in f.params do local named = substitute(q, "comptime ", "", {missing_ok = true}) if re_match(q, ":[\\w.*]*\\b(std\\.Target|RocTarget|Target|TargetUsize)$") or starts_with(named, "target_usize") or starts_with(named, "target_word") then return true end end return false end -- Whether a function body turns bytes into data: copies, allocates or -- emits them. A backing only read (an identifier's text) is no blob. function makes_data(body) for s in DATA_SINKS do if contains(body, s) then return true end end return false end -- One file's findings into FOUND. function scan(p) local toks = zig_tokens(p) local fns = functions_of(toks) -- A function's body text, made once and only when a check asks. local bodies = {} -- stand_in_alignment, duplicated_header_formula, duplicated_arg_layout's -- sorts, unchecked_aligncast, host_size_in_target_code: by call. for k = 1, #toks - 1 do local t = toks[k] local name = t.text local calls = toks[k + 1].tag == "l_paren" and (k == 1 or toks[k - 1].tag ~= "keyword_fn") if calls and has_key(ALIGN_ARG, name) then local a = get(args_of(toks, k + 1), ALIGN_ARG[name]) if a ~= nil and stand_in(a) then report("stand_in_alignment", p, t.line, name .. "(...) aligned at `" .. a .. "`, not the value's own alignment") end end if calls and name == "alignForward" then local args = args_of(toks, k + 1) -- `std.mem.alignForward(usize, x, a)`: the value is after the type. local v = get(args, 1, "") if #args == 3 then v = args[2] end if re_match(v, "word|header|required_space|extra_bytes", {nocase = true}) then local f = fn_at(fns, k) report("duplicated_header_formula", p, t.line, "alignForward(" .. join(args, ", ") .. ") in " .. (f and f.name or "a top-level declaration")) end end if t.tag == "angle_bracket_right" or t.tag == "angle_bracket_left" then local lhs = toks[k - 1].text local rhs = toks[k + 1].text if k + 3 <= #toks and toks[k + 2].tag == "period" then rhs = toks[k + 3].text end local f = fn_at(fns, k) -- A comparator (a function giving `bool`) that orders by alignment. if f ~= nil and re_match(f.sig, "\\)bool$") and re_match(lhs, "^(alignment|\\w+_alignment|\\w+_align)$") and re_match(rhs, "^(alignment|\\w+_alignment|\\w+_align)$") then report("duplicated_arg_layout", p, t.line, "a sort by alignment (`" .. text_of(toks, k - 3, k + 3) .. "`) in " .. f.name) end end if calls and name == "@alignCast" then local a = text_of(toks, k + 2, close_of(toks, k + 1) - 1) if contains(a, "+") or re_match(a, "\\[[^0\\]][^\\]]*\\.\\.") then local f = fn_at(fns, k) if f ~= nil then if not has_key(bodies, f.name .. f.first) then bodies[f.name .. f.first] = text_of(toks, f.first, f.last) end local body = bodies[f.name .. f.first] if not contains(body, "%@alignOf") and not contains(body, "isAligned") then report("unchecked_aligncast", p, t.line, "@alignCast(" .. a .. ") in " .. f.name .. ", which never checks the offset's alignment") end end end end if calls and (name == "@sizeOf" or name == "@alignOf") and k + 3 <= #toks and toks[k + 2].text == "usize" and toks[k + 3].tag == "r_paren" then local f = fn_at(fns, k) if re_match(p, "(^|/)layout/") then report("host_size_in_target_code", p, t.line, name .. "(usize) in layout/: the host's word, not the target's") elseif f ~= nil and takes_target(f) then report("host_size_in_target_code", p, t.line, name .. "(usize) in " .. f.name .. ", which takes a target") end end end -- backing_without_alignment, duplicated_arg_layout's copies, -- dealloc_ignores_alignment: by function. for f in fns do if f.name == "entrypointParamSlotSize" or f.name == "computeArgOffsets" then report("duplicated_arg_layout", p, f.line, "fn " .. f.name .. ": one copy of the argument layout rule") end if re_match(f.name, "^roc\\w*Dealloc") and #f.params >= 3 and starts_with(f.params[3], "_:") then report("dealloc_ignores_alignment", p, f.line, "fn " .. f.name .. " takes its alignment as `" .. f.params[3] .. "`") end if f.name == "free" then for q in f.params do if starts_with(q, "_:") and contains(q, "Alignment") then report("dealloc_ignores_alignment", p, f.line, "fn free takes its alignment as `" .. q .. "`") end end end -- Only the function's own tokens: a nested function is judged alone. for k = f.first, f.last - 1 do local name = toks[k].text if (name == "getString" or name == "getStringLiteralBacking") and toks[k + 1].tag == "l_paren" and fn_at(fns, k).first == f.first then if not has_key(bodies, f.name .. f.first) then bodies[f.name .. f.first] = text_of(toks, f.first, f.last) end local body = bodies[f.name .. f.first] if makes_data(body) and not contains(body, "strings.alignment(") then report("backing_without_alignment", p, toks[k].line, name .. "(...) in " .. f.name .. ", which never asks strings.alignment(") end break end end end end -- A file's tokens are done with once it is scanned: yield lets them go, -- so a tree of any size fits. const files = {} for p in glob(GLOB) do push(files, p) end for p in files do scan(p) yield() end -- The findings, check by check, then the counts. const counts = {} for c in CHECKS do counts[c] = 0 end for c in CHECKS do for x in FOUND do if x.check == c then counts[c] = counts[c] + 1 print(x.at .. ":" .. x.line .. ": " .. c .. ": " .. x.why) end end end print("") print("hunt_alignment_math: " .. #files .. " files") for c in CHECKS do print(pad(tostring(counts[c]), 6) .. " " .. c) end if SELF_TEST then -- Each plant fires its own check; clean.zig fires none. local bad = {} for c in CHECKS do local fired = false for x in FOUND do if x.check == c and x.at == PLANTS .. "/" .. c .. ".zig" then fired = true end end if not fired then push(bad, c .. " did not fire on its plant") end end for x in FOUND do if x.at == PLANTS .. "/clean.zig" then push(bad, "clean.zig:" .. x.line .. " fired " .. x.check) end end for b in bad do print(" " .. b) end if #bad == 0 then print("PASS: each check fired on its plant, none on clean.zig") else fail("FAIL: " .. #bad .. " self-test failures") end end

name: cookbook/zig/hunt_names.shale
html: -- This recipe hunts a Zig tree for awkward names: names that say something -- other than what the code does, read from Zig's tokens by heuristics. A -- finding is a question for a reader, never a verdict: -- -- state_effect a function with effects (it takes `io`, an `Io` or a -- store) named as a state, not a verb: `held*`, a past -- participle first (`loaded`, `kept`), `done`, `ready` -- question `is*`, `has*`, `can*`, `should*` that returns no bool, -- or a bool named as a state (`marked`): ask it, `isSigned` -- vague a name of nothing but vague words: `handle`, -- `process`, `doIt`, `handleData`, `manageStuff` -- name_type a `*count` parameter that is no integer, a `*path` one -- that is no string or path type -- negative a bool parameter named `no*`/`not*`, a fn `isNot*` -- noun_effect a function with effects whose first word is no verb this -- knows: a plain noun (`links`, `session`), which reads as -- a value, not an act -- -- One line a finding, `path:line: <check>: <why>`, then the counts. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/hunt_names.shale glob=src/**/*.zig -- shale cookbook:zig/hunt_names.shale self_test=1 -- -- The words it judges by are cookbook/words/'s tables, the Roc hunt's -- too: participles.txt (English's irregular ones; the rule takes `-ed`), -- ed_verbs.txt (the rule's exceptions), vague.txt and verbs.txt. `words=1` -- gives the census instead of the findings: every first word a function -- with effects (as `state_effect` decides) starts with, its count and its -- verdict, `verb`, `participle`, `vague`, `asks` (`is*`, `has*`) or -- `refused` (no word of the tables: what `noun_effect` fires on), then the -- totals. A missing verb shows there as `refused` before it is taken for a -- noun. -- -- `self_test=1` runs it over `cookbook/zig/plants/hunt_names/`, each plant -- named for the check it holds (`question.zig`, `question_irregular.zig`): -- every check must fire on its own plants and on no other, a `quiet_*.zig` -- plant on none, and the census must give a known word of the plants each -- verdict but `asks`. `glob2=` is a second glob. -- -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const SELF = arg("self_test", "") == "1" const GLOB = SELF and "cookbook:zig/plants/hunt_names/*.zig" or arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const GLOB2 = arg("glob2", "") const CHECKS = {"state_effect", "question", "vague", "name_type", "negative", "noun_effect", "preposition_split"} const WORDS = arg("words", "") == "1" -- A word table of cookbook/words/, the name hunts' one home for them: a -- word a line, `--` starting a note. A word twice, or a line of two, is a -- mistake in the table: it fails. function word_table(file) local t = {} for l in lines(read("cookbook:words/" .. file)) do local w = trim(split(l, "--")[1]) if contains(w, " ") or has_key(t, w) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. w .. "` is no single new word") end if w ~= "" then t[w] = true end end return t end const VERBS = word_table("verbs.txt") const PARTICIPLES = word_table("participles.txt") const ED_VERBS = word_table("ed_verbs.txt") const VAGUE = word_table("vague.txt") const PREPS = word_table("prepositions.txt") -- Each file's names that end in a preposition, by the words before it: -- `path|base` -> {line, preps (prep -> {name, arity})}. const SPLITS = {} const ENTRY = {handle = true, run = true} const INTS = {usize = true, isize = true, comptime_int = true} -- A Zig name's words, lower case: `handleData` and `handle_data` both -- `{handle, data}`. function words_of(name) local s = re_replace(name, "([A-Z])", "_\\1") local got = {} for w in split(lower(s), "_") do if w ~= "" then push(got, w) end end return got end function is_participle(w) if has_key(PARTICIPLES, w) then return true end return #w > 3 and ends_with(w, "ed") and not has_key(ED_VERBS, w) end -- A verb that reads as a participle would make its functions states. for w in keys(VERBS) do if is_participle(w) then fail("hunt_names: `" .. w .. "` is in cookbook/words/verbs.txt and reads as a participle") end end -- What an effect's first word says, as the Roc hunt judges it: -- `participle` (a state: `state_effect` fires), `verb`, `vague`, `asks` -- (`is`, `has`: `question` judges it), or `refused`, which `noun_effect` -- fires on. function verdict(w) if is_participle(w) then return "participle" end if has_key(VERBS, w) then return "verb" end if has_key(VAGUE, w) then return "vague" end if w == "is" or w == "has" then return "asks" end return "refused" end function is_int(t) if has_key(INTS, t) then return true end return re_match(t, "^[ui][0-9]+$") end -- The text of `toks[a..b]`, joined. function text_of(toks, a, b) local got = {} for k = a, b do push(got, toks[k].text) if starts_with(toks[k].tag, "keyword_") then push(got, " ") end end return join(got, "") end const found = {} for c in CHECKS do found[c] = 0 end const per_file = {} -- Each first word an effect starts with, by word: `{word, count, -- verdict}`, for the census (`words=1`). const census = {} function say(p, line, check, why) if not WORDS then print(p .. ":" .. line .. ": " .. check .. ": " .. why) end found[check] = found[check] + 1 per_file[p ..
