"|" .. check] = true return nil end -- One file's findings. function hunt(p) local toks = zig_tokens(p) local n = #toks for k = 1, n - 2 do if toks[k].tag == "keyword_fn" and toks[k + 1].tag == "identifier" and toks[k + 2].tag == "l_paren" then local name = toks[k + 1].text local line = toks[k].line -- The parameters, `{name, type}`, split at their own depth's commas. local params = {} local j = k + 3 local depth = 1 local pname = nil local tfrom = 0 while j <= n and depth > 0 do local u = toks[j] if u.tag == "l_paren" or u.tag == "l_brace" or u.tag == "l_bracket" then depth = depth + 1 end if u.tag == "r_paren" or u.tag == "r_brace" or u.tag == "r_bracket" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 1 and u.tag == "colon" and toks[j - 1].tag == "identifier" then pname = toks[j - 1].text tfrom = j + 1 end if (depth == 1 and u.tag == "comma") or depth == 0 then if pname ~= nil then push(params, {name = pname, type = text_of(toks, tfrom, j - 1)}) end pname = nil end j = j + 1 end -- The return type: from `)` to the body's `{` or the `;`. local rfrom = j while j <= n and toks[j].tag ~= "l_brace" and toks[j].tag ~= "semicolon" do j = j + 1 end local ret = text_of(toks, rfrom, j - 1) local ws = words_of(name) local effect = false for q in params do if q.name == "io" or contains(q.type, "Io") or contains(lower(q.type), "store") then effect = true end end if effect and #ws > 0 then if not has_key(census, ws[1]) then census[ws[1]] = {word = ws[1], count = 0, verdict = verdict(ws[1])} end census[ws[1]].count = census[ws[1]].count + 1 if census[ws[1]].verdict == "refused" then if has_key(PREPS, ws[1]) then say(p, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. name .. "` has effects (takes io or a store) but starts with a preposition, `" .. ws[1] .. "`: an effect is named for its act") else say(p, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. name .. "` has effects (takes io or a store) but its first word, `" .. ws[1] .. "`, is no verb: it reads as a value, not an act") end end end local gives_bool = ret == "bool" or ret == "!bool" if gives_bool and #ws > 0 and is_participle(ws[1]) then say(p, line, "question", "`" .. name .. "` gives a bool but is named as a state, `" .. ws[1] .. "`: ask it (`is*`, `has*`)") end if effect and not gives_bool and #ws > 0 and is_participle(ws[1]) then say(p, line, "state_effect", "`" .. name .. "` has effects (takes io or a store) but is named as a state, `" .. ws[1] .. "`: a verb says what it does") end if #ws > 1 and (ws[1] == "is" or ws[1] == "has" or ws[1] == "can" or ws[1] == "should") and not contains(ret, "bool") and ret ~= "" then say(p, line, "question", "`" .. name .. "` asks a question but returns `" .. ret .. "`") end local all_vague = #ws > 0 for w in ws do if not has_key(VAGUE, w) then all_vague = false end end -- A lone `handle` or `run` is an entry point's convention, not vague. if #ws == 1 and has_key(ENTRY, ws[1]) then all_vague = false end if all_vague then say(p, line, "vague", "`" .. name .. "` is only vague words: what does it handle, and how?") end for q in params do local qw = words_of(q.name) local last = "" if #qw > 0 then last = qw[#qw] end local t = q.type if last == "count" and not is_int(t) then say(p, line, "name_type", "`" .. name .. "`'s `" .. q.name .. "` is a count of type `" .. t .. "`") end if last == "path" and not contains(t, "u8") and not contains(t, "Path") and not contains(t, "anytype") then say(p, line, "name_type", "`" .. name .. "`'s `" .. q.name .. "` is a path of type `" .. t .. "`") end if t == "bool" and (qw[1] == "no" or qw[1] == "not") and #qw > 1 then say(p, line, "negative", "`" .. name .. "`'s `" .. q.name .. "` is a negative flag: `" .. q.name .. " = false` reads twice") end end if #ws > 1 and has_key(PREPS, ws[#ws]) then local key = p .. "|" .. join(take(ws, #ws - 1), "_") if not has_key(SPLITS, key) then SPLITS[key] = {path = p, line = line, base = name, preps = {}} end if not has_key(SPLITS[key].preps, ws[#ws]) then SPLITS[key].preps[ws[#ws]] = {name = name, arity = #params} end end if #ws > 2 and ws[1] == "is" and ws[2] == "not" then say(p, line, "negative", "`" .. name .. "` asks a negative: `!" .. name .. "(...)` reads twice") end end end return nil end -- Two opposite prepositions on one noun name a matched pair on purpose -- (`insert_before` and `insert_after`): no split. const OPPOSITES = {["after|before"] = true, ["from|to"] = true, ["with|without"] = true, ["over|under"] = true, ["into|onto"] = false} -- One noun given different trailing prepositions in one file, less the -- house's recursion worker (a `*From` taking more parameters than its -- siblings: its `from` names the index it resumes at). function report_splits() for key in sort(keys(SPLITS)) do local s = SPLITS[key] local least = -1 for prep in keys(s.preps) do local a = s.preps[prep].arity if least < 0 or a < least then least = a end end local kept = {} local kept_preps = {} for prep in sort(keys(s.preps)) do local e = s.preps[prep] if not (prep == "from" and e.arity > least) then push(kept, e.name) push(kept_preps, prep) end end if #kept > 1 and not (#kept == 2 and get(OPPOSITES, join(kept_preps, "|"), false)) then say(s.path, s.line, "preposition_split", "`" .. join(kept, "`, `") .. "`: one noun, " .. #kept .. " prepositions in one file: one relation keeps one preposition, or the names say how they differ") end end return nil end local files = 0 for p in glob(GLOB) do files = files + 1 hunt(p) yield() end if GLOB2 ~= "" then for p in glob(GLOB2) do files = files + 1 hunt(p) yield() end end report_splits() local counts = {} for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. found[c]) end if WORDS then local rows = {} local by = {} local total = 0 for w in keys(census) do push(rows, census[w]) by[census[w].verdict] = get(by, census[w].verdict, 0) + census[w].count total = total + census[w].count end sort(rows, {{key = "count", desc = true}, "word"}) for r in rows do print(pad(r.count, -4) .. " " .. pad(r.word, 12) .. " " .. r.verdict) end local verdicts = {} for v in {"verb", "participle", "vague", "asks", "refused"} do push(verdicts, v .. " " .. get(by, v, 0)) end print("hunt_names census: " .. files .. " files; " .. total .. " effects, " .. #rows .. " first words; effects by verdict: " .. join(verdicts, ", ")) else print("hunt_names: " .. files .. " files; " .. join(counts, ", ")) end if SELF then -- Every plant is judged before a failure stops the run, so one run shows -- each plant that is wrong. local wrong = {} for c in CHECKS do for p in glob(GLOB) do local base = sub(p, #"cookbook:zig/plants/hunt_names/" + 1) local mine = base == c .. ".zig" or starts_with(base, c .. "_") local fired = has_key(per_file, p .. "|" .. c) if mine and not fired then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. p) end if fired and not mine then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on " .. p .. ", another check's plant") end end end -- The census: a known word of the plants in each verdict. for want in {{word = "read", verdict = "verb"}, {word = "held", verdict = "participle"}, {word = "process", verdict = "vague"}, {word = "links", verdict = "refused"}} do local got = get(census, want.word) if got == nil then push(wrong, "the census has no `" .. want.word .. "`") elseif got.verdict ~= want.verdict then push(wrong, "the census calls `" .. want.word .. "` " .. got.verdict .. ", not " .. want.verdict) end end for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end if #wrong > 0 then fail("hunt_names self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end print("hunt_names self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none, and the census gives each verdict its known word)") end

name: cookbook/zig/judge_move.shale
html: -- This recipe judges a refactor that only moves declarations between files, -- in a Zig repo with `zig build` and `zig build test`: such a move should -- change nothing. It takes three things before the move (`mode=baseline`) -- and holds them equal after (`mode=check`): -- -- - the tests, by name, read from the source with zig_decls (a moved -- test keeps its name; its file is left out), and the runner's count; -- - the release binary's symbols, each by name and size, the name's -- first part (its file) left out: Zig compiles one unit, so where a -- function lives does not change its code; -- - every test passing. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/judge_move.shale mode=baseline bin=zig-out/bin/metal-vmm -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/judge_move.shale mode=check bin=zig-out/bin/metal-vmm -- -- The baseline is zig-out/move-judge.txt. -- -- A large file's symbols and tests need room: -- -- budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const MODE = arg("mode", "check") -- `bin=a,b`: each binary's symbols, by name and size, under its own name. const BINS = split(arg("bin", ""), ",") -- `build=<step>`: `zig build <step>` (default: `zig build`); `test=none` -- for a tree whose moved file has no tests of its own (a kernel's root). const BUILD = arg("build", "") const TEST = arg("test", "test") -- `clean=yes`: refuse a tree with changes. A build that stamps its commit -- (zig-metal-unikernel's) says `+dirty` on one, a string 6 bytes longer: -- commit first (locally), then judge. const CLEAN = arg("clean", "no") == "yes" -- `flags=-Dstamp=off,...`: options for the build (zig-metal-unikernel's -- and dog-park's `-Dstamp=off` unstamp their commits, so no commit or -- `+dirty` moves a byte, and `clean=yes` is not needed). const FLAGS = arg("flags", "") -- `same=gopher,volumes`: module names a move makes one, wherever they -- appear in a symbol (a generic over a moved type: `Checker(*gopher.X)` -- becomes `Checker(*volumes.X)`). A coverage site's file name -- (`siteOf...S.file_`) is the file's name: its size is not compared. const SAME = split(arg("same", ""), ",") -- `new_files=src/a.zig,...`: the files the move made. Each that holds a -- coverage site (`@src()`) has a file-name string of its own, where its -- sites shared the old file's: exactly one more `S.file_` symbol each, -- in each binary, and nothing else is excused. const NEW_FILES = split(arg("new_files", ""), ",") const SAVED = "zig-out/move-judge.txt" function test_names() local got = {} for p in glob("src/**/*.zig") do for d in zig_decls(p) do if d.kind == "test" then push(got, "test " .. d.name) end end end sort(got) return got end -- `main.Machine.step` and `machine.Machine.step` are one function. function symbols(bin) local nm = must(run({"nm", "-S", "-t", "d", bin}, {timeout_ms = 60000, whole = 64000000})) local got = {} for l in lines(nm.out) do local parts = split(l, " ") if #parts >= 4 then local kind = lower(parts[3]) if kind == "t" or kind == "r" or kind == "d" or kind == "b" then local name = parts[4] local dot = find(name, ".") if dot ~= nil then name = sub(name, dot + 1) end -- Zig numbers its anonymous types and instances (`__enum_2457`, -- `__anon_31`): the numbers move with any change, so they go. local f = re_find(name, "__[a-z]+_[0-9]+") while f ~= nil do local kind = sub(f.text, 1, find(sub(f.text, 3), "_") + 1) name = sub(name, 1, f.at - 1) .. kind .. sub(name, f.at + #f.text) f = re_find(name, "__[a-z]+_[0-9]+") end -- The coverage SDK names a site by a hash of where it is: a move -- changes the name, not the code under it. local cov = re_find(name, "^zig_coverage_site_[0-9a-f]+$") if cov ~= nil then name = "zig_coverage_site_" end push(got, "sym " .. bin .. " " .. name .. " " .. parse_int(parts[2])) end end end sort(got) return got end -- A line as the comparison takes it (`same`, and a file name's size left -- out), on both sides: the baseline is written as it was found. function same_as(l) if not starts_with(l, "sym ") then return l end local out = l if SAME[1] ~= "" then for m in SAME do out = substitute(out, m .. ".", SAME[1] .. ".", {missing_ok = true}) end end local f = re_find(out, "\\.S\\.file_ [0-9]+$") if f ~= nil then out = sub(out, 1, f.at - 1) .. ".S.file_ (a file's name)" end return out end function passed() -- The summary line alone: after `--summary all`'s step tree it was -- past what a short tail keeps (the kernel's tree is long). local r = run({"zig", "build", "test", "--summary", "line"}, {timeout_ms = 580000, tail = 4000}) if r.code ~= 0 then print(r.out) fail("zig build test exited " .. r.code) end local m = re_find(r.out, "([0-9]+/[0-9]+) tests passed") if m == nil then fail("no `N/M tests passed` in the test step's summary") end return "passed " .. m.group end if BINS[1] == "" then fail("judge_move: give bin=<the release binary>[,<another>]") end if CLEAN then local st = must(run({"git", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"}, {timeout_ms = 10000, whole = 100000})) if trim(st.out) ~= "" then fail("judge_move: clean=yes, and the tree has changes: commit them first (a stamped build says +dirty)") end end local build = {"zig", "build"} if BUILD ~= "" then push(build, BUILD) end if FLAGS ~= "" then for f in split(FLAGS, ",") do push(build, f) end end must(run(build, {timeout_ms = 580000, tail = 20})) local now = test_names() for b in BINS do for s in symbols(b) do push(now, s) end end if TEST ~= "none" then push(now, passed()) end if MODE == "baseline" then replace(SAVED, join(now, "\n") .. "\n") print("move judge: baseline of " .. #now .. " lines in " .. SAVED) else local was = {} for l in lines(read(SAVED)) do if l ~= "" then push(was, same_as(l)) end end local now_n = {} for l in now do push(now_n, same_as(l)) end now = now_n local count = {} for l in was do count[l] = get(count, l, 0) + 1 end local extra = {} for l in now do if get(count, l, 0) > 0 then count[l] = count[l] - 1 else push(extra, l) end end local missing = {} for l in keys(count) do if count[l] > 0 then push(missing, l) end end sort(missing) -- A new file's own file-name string, as many as `new_files` excuses. local with_sites = 0 for f in NEW_FILES do if f ~= "" and count_in(f, "@src()") > 0 then with_sites = with_sites + 1 end end local excused = {} for b in BINS do excused[b] = 0 end local kept = {} for l in extra do local excuse = false for b in BINS do if not excuse and l == "sym " .. b .. " siteOf__anon.S.file_ (a file's name)" and excused[b] < with_sites then excused[b] = excused[b] + 1 excuse = true end end if not excuse then push(kept, l) end end for b in BINS do if excused[b] > 0 then print("excused: " .. excused[b] .. " new file-name string(s) in " .. b .. " (new_files with a coverage site: " .. with_sites .. ")") end end extra = kept for l in take(missing, 30) do print("before only: " .. l) end for l in take(extra, 30) do print("after only: " .. l) end if #missing > 0 or #extra > 0 then fail("move judge: " .. #missing .. " before only, " .. #extra .. " after only") end print("move judge: the same " .. #now .. " lines (tests, symbols by name and size, the count passing)") end

name: cookbook/zig/list_long_files.shale
html: -- This script lists the .zig files over a thousand lines in the repos we work -- in, longest first. `over=N` sets another limit. Run it from the folder that -- holds the repos: -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/list_long_files.shale [over=N] const OVER = arg("over", 1000) local repos = {"zig-metal-unikernel", "zig-webbox", "shale", "metal-vmm", "dog-park", "observatory", "angry-gopher", "zig-coverage-sdk"} local long_files = {} local file_count = 0 for repo in repos do for path in glob(repo .. "/**/*.zig") do file_count = file_count + 1 local line_count = count_lines(path) if line_count > OVER then push(long_files, {lines = line_count, path = path}) end end end sort(long_files, "lines", "desc") print(table(long_files, {"lines", "path"})) print(#long_files .. " of " .. file_count .. " .zig files are over " .. OVER .. " lines")

name: cookbook/zig/map_file.shale
html: -- This script prints a map of a Zig file: each top-level function, type and -- test, with its first line and its length up to the next one, and then how -- many of the file's lines are tests. A constant that is not a type is left out. -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/map_file.shale path=src/x.zig const LONGEST_SHOWN = 90 function is_test(text) return re_find(text, "^test ") ~= nil end function is_mapped(line) if is_test(line) then return true end if re_find(line, "^(pub fn|fn|pub const|const|pub var|var) ") == nil then return false end return re_find(line, "fn |= struct|= enum|= union") ~= nil end local source = lines(read(arg("path", ""))) local mapped = {} for number = 1, #source do if is_mapped(source[number]) then push(mapped, {line = number, text = sub(source[number], 1, LONGEST_SHOWN)}) end end local rows = {} local test_lines = 0 local first_test = 0 for k = 1, #mapped do local next_line = #source + 1 if k < #mapped then next_line = mapped[k + 1].line end local length = next_line - mapped[k].line if is_test(mapped[k].text) then test_lines = test_lines + length if first_test == 0 then first_test = mapped[k].line end end push(rows, {line = mapped[k].line, lines = length, decl = mapped[k].text}) end print(table(rows, {"line", "lines", "decl"})) print(#source .. " lines; tests " .. test_lines .. "; the first test at line " .. first_test)

name: cookbook/zig/plan_function_cut.shale
html: -- This script says what a piece of a long Zig function would need if it were -- cut out into a function of its own. For lines `first` to `last` of function -- `fn` in `path`, it prints three lists: -- -- - takes: the locals and parameters declared before the range that it reads, -- which become the new function's parameters or a context's fields; -- - writes: those it assigns (`x = ...`, `x +=`), which become pointers or fields; -- - gives: the locals it declares that the function uses after it, which the -- new function hands back. -- -- It reads Zig's tokens: a name is an identifier not after a `.`, and a -- declaration is `const x`, `var x`, a `|x|` capture or a parameter. A name -- declared again inside the range counts as the range's own. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/plan_function_cut.shale path=src/x.zig fn=main first=120 last=180 const PATH = arg("path", "") const FN = arg("fn", "") const FIRST = parse_int(arg("first", "0")) const LAST = parse_int(arg("last", "0")) const ASSIGNMENT_TAGS = {"equal", "plus_equal", "minus_equal", "plus_percent_equal"} if PATH == "" or FN == "" or FIRST == 0 or LAST == 0 then fail("plan_function_cut: path= fn= first= last=") end -- Gives whether the identifier at `tokens[k]` declares its name, in a function -- whose signature starts at `signature_line`. function is_declaration(tokens, k, signature_line) local tag_before = tokens[k - 1].tag local tag_after = tokens[k + 1].tag return tag_before == "keyword_const" or tag_before == "keyword_var" or (tag_before == "pipe" and (tag_after == "pipe" or tag_after == "comma")) or (tag_before == "asterisk" and k > 2 and tokens[k - 2].tag == "pipe") or (tag_before == "comma" and tag_after == "pipe") or (tokens[k].line == signature_line and tag_after == "colon") end local target = nil for declaration in zig_decls(PATH) do if declaration.name == FN then target = declaration end end if target == nil then fail("plan_function_cut: no top-level `" .. FN .. "` in " .. PATH) end if FIRST < target.first or LAST > target.last then fail("plan_function_cut: " .. FIRST .. ".." .. LAST .. " is not inside " .. FN .. " (" .. target.first .. ".." .. target.last .. ")") end local tokens = zig_tokens(PATH) local line_declared_before = {} local names_declared_before = {} local declared_inside = {} local used_inside = {} local assigned_inside = {} local used_after = {} for k = 1, #tokens do local token = tokens[k] local name = token.text if token.line >= target.first and token.line <= target.last and token.tag == "identifier" and (k == 1 or tokens[k - 1].tag ~= "period") then if is_declaration(tokens, k, target.first) then if token.line < FIRST then if not has_key(line_declared_before, name) then line_declared_before[name] = token.line push(names_declared_before, name) end elseif token.line <= LAST then declared_inside[name] = true end elseif token.line >= FIRST and token.line <= LAST then used_inside[name] = true if has_item(ASSIGNMENT_TAGS, tokens[k + 1].tag) then assigned_inside[name] = true end elseif token.line > LAST then used_after[name] = true end end end local takes = {} local writes = {} for name in names_declared_before do if has_key(used_inside, name) and not has_key(declared_inside, name) then local entry = name .. ":" .. line_declared_before[name] if has_key(assigned_inside, name) then push(writes, entry) else push(takes, entry) end end end local gives = {} for name in keys(declared_inside) do if has_key(used_after, name) then push(gives, name) end end sort(gives) print(FN .. " " .. FIRST .. ".." .. LAST .. " of " .. target.first .. ".." .. target.last) print("takes (" .. #takes .. ", read only): " .. join(takes, " ")) print("writes (" .. #writes .. ", assigned in the range): " .. join(writes, " ")) print("gives (" .. #gives .. ", used after it): " .. join(gives, " "))

name: cookbook/zig/rename_member.shale
html: -- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=4000000000 -- This recipe renames a Zig declaration with its callers across a tree. It -- renames `from` in `file` (a top-level declaration, or with `container=` a -- container's member), and in every other file of the tree that imports -- `file`, each `alias.from` (or `alias.Container.from`) through the name it -- imports it by. What a file reaches some other way (a value of the type, -- `@import("root")`) is never guessed at: its lines are printed, for a -- reader. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/rename_member.shale file=src/search_index.zig from=ready to=indexOrBuild -- shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/rename_member.shale file=src/router_harness.zig container=UidSite from=marked to=isSigned glob=src/**/*.zig -- -- `glob=` is the tree (default src/**/*.zig). In `file`, a container's -- member is renamed by `zig_rename`'s `container` (its uses inside, and -- `C.`, `self.`, `@This().` ones); a `.from` there it cannot attribute -- stops the run before any file is written. const FILE = arg("file", "") const FROM = arg("from", "") const TO = arg("to", "") const CONTAINER = arg("container", "") const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") if FILE == "" or FROM == "" or TO == "" then fail("rename_member: say `file=`, `from=` and `to=`") end -- `p` with its `.` and `..` parts resolved: `src/a/../b.zig` is `src/b.zig`. function clean(p) local out = {} for part in split(p, "/") do if part == ".." and #out > 0 and out[#out] ~= ".." then out = take(out, #out - 1) elseif part ~= "." and part ~= "" then push(out, part) end end return join(out, "/") end -- The folder `p` is in, or "". function folder(p) local at = 0 local i = 1 while true do local k = find(p, "/", i) if k == nil then break end at = k i = k + 1 end if at == 0 then return "" end return sub(p, 1, at - 1) end const TARGET = clean(FILE) -- First the declaring file: a refusal here stops the run with nothing written. local own = nil if CONTAINER ~= "" then own = zig_rename(TARGET, FROM, TO, {container = CONTAINER}) else own = zig_rename(TARGET, FROM, TO) end print(TARGET .. ": " .. own.renamed .. " renamed, " .. own.left_in_comments .. " left in comments") local total = own.renamed local files = 0 for p in glob(GLOB) do if clean(p) ~= TARGET and #grep(p, FROM) > 0 then local via = {} for imp in zig_imports(p) do if imp.kind == "import" and imp.file == "found" and imp.name ~= nil and imp.name ~= "" then local dir = folder(p) local path = imp.target if dir ~= "" then path = dir .. "/" .. imp.target end if clean(path) == TARGET then if CONTAINER ~= "" then push(via, imp.name .. "." .. CONTAINER) else push(via, imp.name) end end end end if #via > 0 then local r = zig_rename(p, FROM, TO, {via = via}) if r.renamed > 0 or #r.left > 0 then files = files + 1 total = total + r.renamed local line = p .. ": " .. r.renamed .. " through " .. join(via, ", ") if #r.left > 0 then line = line .. "; `." .. FROM .. "` left at lines " .. join(r.left, ", ") .. " (not through the import: a reader's)" end print(line) end end end yield() end print("rename_member: " .. FROM .. " -> " .. TO .. ": " .. total .. " in " .. (files + 1) .. " files")

name: cookbook/zig/rewrite_call_args.shale
html: -- This recipe regroups the arguments of every call of a function: the call -- sites' half of changing a signature, as when seven strings in a row become -- two structs and two strings. Each call `name(a1, a2, ...)` (bare, or after -- a `.`, so `store.name(` too) is rewritten by `template`, where `$N` is the -- Nth argument's text as written: -- -- template=$1, $2, $3, $4, .{ .dir = $5, .key = $6, .sid = $7 }, .{ .name = $8, .id = $9 }, $10, $11 -- -- The arguments are split at the commas of the call's own depth, past -- brackets of every kind, `"..."` strings with their escapes and `'x'` -- characters. A call it cannot take whole is refused by name, before -- anything is written: one that runs past its line (`\\` strings, an -- argument list wrapped), or one whose arguments number other than the -- template's highest `$N` (`count=` says how many every call must have). -- The declaration (`fn name(`) is left: its signature is yours to write. -- Run it under `--undo-on-stop`; the compiler judges after. -- -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/zig/rewrite_call_args.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- name=appendMessage -- glob=src/**/*.zig -- template=... -- ARGS -- -- Every file is read and every line scanned. -- -- budget: steps=100000000 const NAME = arg("name", "") const GLOB = arg("glob", "src/**/*.zig") const TEMPLATE = arg("template", "") if NAME == "" or TEMPLATE == "" then fail("rewrite_call_args: name= template= [glob=] [count=]") end -- The highest `$N` the template names: what every call must have. function highest(t) local most = 0 local rest = t while true do local m = re_find(rest, "\\$([0-9]+)") if m == nil then return most end local n = parse_int(m.group) if n > most then most = n end rest = sub(rest, m.at + #m.text) end end const WANT = parse_int(arg("count", tostring(highest(TEMPLATE)))) -- The arguments of the call whose `(` is at `open` in `s`: {args, close}, -- each argument's text trimmed; nil when the line ends first. function args_at(s, open) local args = {} local depth = 0 local start = open + 1 local i = open + 1 local n = #s while i <= n do local c = sub(s, i, i) if c == "\"" then i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(s, i, i) ~= "\"" do if sub(s, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end if i > n then return nil end elseif c == "'" then i = i + 1 while i <= n and sub(s, i, i) ~= "'" do if sub(s, i, i) == "\\" then i = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end if i > n then return nil end elseif c == "(" or c == "[" or c == "{" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == ")" or c == "]" or c == "}" then if depth == 0 then local last = trim(sub(s, start, i - 1)) if last ~= "" or #args > 0 then push(args, last) end return {args = args, close = i} end depth = depth - 1 elseif c == "," and depth == 0 then push(args, trim(sub(s, start, i - 1))) start = i + 1 end i = i + 1 end return nil end function filled(args) local out = TEMPLATE -- The highest first, so `$1` never eats the start of `$11`. local k = #args while k >= 1 do out = substitute(out, "$" .. k, args[k], {missing_ok = true}) k = k - 1 end return out end -- Every call, planned first; nothing is written unless all can be taken. const rewritten = {} const refused = {} local calls = 0 for p in glob(GLOB) do local ls = lines(read(p)) local touched = false for i = 1, #ls do local line = ls[i] local from = 1 local out = "" local any = false while true do local at = find(line, NAME .. "(", from) if at == nil then break end local before = at > 1 and sub(line, at - 1, at - 1) or " " local is_call = re_find(before, "[A-Za-z0-9_]") == nil and not ends_with(trim(sub(line, 1, at - 1)), "fn") local open = at + #NAME if not is_call then out = out .. sub(line, from, open) from = open + 1 else local got = args_at(line, open) if got == nil then push(refused, p .. ":" .. i .. " runs past its line") break elseif #got.args ~= WANT then push(refused, p .. ":" .. i .. " has " .. #got.args .. " arguments, not " .. WANT) break end -- An argument holding `$N` would be filled again by a later `$N`. local dollar = false for x in got.args do if re_find(x, "\\$[0-9]") ~= nil then dollar = true end end if dollar then push(refused, p .. ":" .. i .. " has an argument holding `$` and a digit") break end out = out .. sub(line, from, open) .. filled(got.args) .. ")" from = got.close + 1 any = true calls = calls + 1 end end if any then ls[i] = out .. sub(line, from) touched = true end end if touched then rewritten[p] = ls end end if #refused > 0 then for r in refused do print("refused: " .. r) end fail("rewrite_call_args: " .. #refused .. " calls of " .. NAME .. " it cannot take whole: none changed") end for p in sort(keys(rewritten)) do replace(p, join(rewritten[p], "\n") .. "\n") end print("rewrite_call_args: " .. calls .. " calls of " .. NAME .. " rewritten in " .. count(rewritten) .. " files")

name: cookbook/zig/split_file.shale
html: -- This recipe moves Zig declarations to a new file and makes the old file -- use them: zig_move and what a split needs around it, as one script. -- -- cd <repo> && shale --undo-on-stop <shale>/cookbook/zig/split_file.shale --args-stdin <<'ARGS' -- from=src/main.zig -- to=src/boot.zig -- as=boot -- names=a|b|the boot's test, which has a comma -- doc=The guest's boot: ...\nits second line -- ARGS -- -- The values on stdin, raw, so the doc and a test's name need no quoting; -- `--undo-on-stop`, so a stop leaves both files as they were. Optional: -- uses=alias, into=yes, from_as=X, reexport=yes, after=<import>. `names` -- are separated by `|` (a test's name may hold a comma); `doc`'s lines by -- `\n`. -- -- 1. zig_move the names, each with its doc and the plain comment above; -- 2. `pub` on each the old file still uses (needs_pub); -- 3. the new file's `//!` (doc) and the imports the moved code uses; -- 4. each use left in the old file qualified, `as.name` (zig_rename); -- or, with `uses=alias`, left as it is under `const name = as.name;` -- beside the import (the old file's own idiom, where it has one); -- 4b. with `reexport=yes`, each moved `pub` declaration re-exported: -- `pub const name = as.name;` (uses of it left as they are); -- 5. `const as = @import("to's name");` in the old file, after the -- import named `after` (or after its last top-level import); -- 6. what the moved code uses of the old file (needs_from_from) printed: -- the script's caller decides, import or copy; -- 6b. with `from_as=X`, what the moved code uses of the old file is -- reached through it (zig_move's own `from_as`: the uses qualified, -- the import, `pub` in the old file); -- 7. the new file named in the old file's `test {}` block of -- `_ = @import(...)` lines, where it has one: a test build never -- analyses `main`, so a file only `main` reaches never runs its tests -- (metal-vmm's serve.zig: the same names, two tests fewer run). -- The compiler judges after (`zig build`), and a move judge. const FROM = arg("from", "") const TO = arg("to", "") const AS = arg("as", "") const NAMES = split(arg("names", ""), "|") const DOC = arg("doc", "") const AFTER = arg("after", "") const USES = arg("uses", "qualify") -- `into=yes`: TO is a file already there (the declarations join it): no -- `//!` of its own, only the imports it lacks, and no test block to add it to. const INTO = arg("into", "no") == "yes" const FROM_AS = arg("from_as", "") -- `reexport=yes`: each moved `pub` declaration stays the old file's too, -- `pub const x = as.x;` beside the import, for a module whose surface is -- the file itself (the kernel's io.zig is `Io`: callers say `Io.mount`). -- A `pub var` cannot be one (a var is no comptime value): refused. const REEXPORT = arg("reexport", "no") == "yes" if USES ~= "qualify" and USES ~= "alias" then fail("split_file: uses=qualify or uses=alias, not " .. USES) end if FROM == "" or TO == "" or AS == "" or #NAMES == 0 or (DOC == "" and not INTO) then fail("split_file: from, to, as, names and doc (or into=yes)") end if INTO and not exists(TO) then fail("split_file: into=yes, and " .. TO .. " is not there") end if not INTO and exists(TO) then fail("split_file: " .. TO .. " is there already: this makes a new file (into=yes joins one)") end -- The import's name must be free, because Zig lets nothing shadow a top-level -- name, so a parameter or a local already called `as` would stop the -- build in every function that has one. Exact, by Zig's tokenizer: an -- identifier `as` not right after a `.` (`x.as` is a field, not a name). local toks = zig_tokens(FROM) local taken = 0 for k = 1, #toks do if toks[k].tag == "identifier" and toks[k].text == AS and (k == 1 or toks[k - 1].tag ~= "period") then taken = taken + 1 end end -- Joining a file the old one imports already, under `as`, is the point. local imported_as = false for i in zig_imports(FROM) do local tb = split(TO, "/") if i.name == AS and i.target == tb[#tb] then imported_as = true end end if taken > 0 and not imported_as then fail("split_file: `" .. AS .. "` is a name in " .. FROM .. " already (" .. taken .. " times, a parameter, a local or a declaration): choose another `as`") end -- What is pub before the move, for reexport=yes: step 2 makes more pub. -- A pub var refused here, before anything moves. local was_pub = {} if REEXPORT then local wanted = {} for n in NAMES do wanted[n] = true end for d in zig_decls(FROM) do if has_key(wanted, d.name) and d.visibility == "pub" and d.kind ~= "test" then if d.kind == "var" then fail("split_file: reexport=yes, and `" .. d.name .. "` is a pub var: a var cannot be re-exported") end was_pub[d.name] = true end end end local move_opts = {comment = "doc_and_plain"} if FROM_AS ~= "" then move_opts.from_as = FROM_AS end local r = zig_move(FROM, TO, NAMES, move_opts) print("moved " .. r.moved) if FROM_AS ~= "" then print("reached through " .. FROM_AS .. ": " .. r.qualified .. " uses; made pub in " .. FROM .. ": " .. join(r.made_pub, ", ")) end -- 2. pub, where the old file still uses one. local made_pub = {} for n in r.needs_pub do if not has_key(made_pub, n.name) then made_pub[n.name] = true local done = false -- The name whole: what follows it is what follows a declaration's name -- (`var site:` is not `var site_cache:`). for prefix in {"const ", "fn ", "var "} do for after in {" ", ":", "("} do local key = prefix .. n.name .. after if not done and count_in(TO, "\n" .. key) + (starts_with(read(TO), key) and 1 or 0) > 0 then local text = read(TO) if starts_with(text, key) then replace(TO, "pub " .. text) else edit(TO, "\n" .. key, "\npub " .. key) end done = true end end end -- A member (`Scenario.choose`): found in its container by Zig's parser, -- and its declaration's line made pub where it is, so two containers' -- `fn choose(` are never confused. local dot = find(n.name, ".") if not done and dot ~= nil then local container = sub(n.name, 1, dot - 1) local member = sub(n.name, dot + 1) for d in zig_decls(TO, {container = container}) do if not done and d.name == member then local ls = lines(read(TO)) for i = d.first, d.last do local body = trim(ls[i]) local decl = starts_with(body, "fn " .. member) or starts_with(body, "const " .. member) or starts_with(body, "var " .. member) if not done and decl then local ind = re_find(ls[i], "^( *)") ls[i] = ind.group .. "pub " .. sub(ls[i], #ind.group + 1) replace(TO, join(ls, "\n") .. "\n") print("pub: " .. n.name .. " (" .. TO .. ":" .. i .. ")") done = true end end end end end if not done then print("needs pub, not made: " .. n.name .. " (by hand)") end end end -- 3. The new file's head: its doc and its imports; or, joining a file, -- the imports it lacks, after its last. if INTO then local have = {} for d in zig_decls(TO) do have[d.name] = true end local add = {} local seen = {} for i in r.needs_import do if not has_key(seen, i.name) and not has_key(have, i.name) then seen[i.name] = true push(add, "const " .. i.name .. " = " .. i.target .. ";") end end if #add > 0 then local to_lines = lines(read(TO)) local its = {} for i in zig_imports(TO) do if i.name ~= "" and (starts_with(to_lines[i.line], "const ") or starts_with(to_lines[i.line], "pub const ")) then push(its, i) end end local at_text = to_lines[its[#its].line] edit(TO, at_text .. "\n", at_text .. "\n" .. join(add, "\n") .. "\n") end print("imports added to " .. TO .. ": " .. #add) else local head = {} for l in split(DOC, "\\n") do push(head, "//! " .. l) end push(head, "") local seen = {} for i in r.needs_import do if not has_key(seen, i.name) then seen[i.name] = true push(head, "const " .. i.name .. " = " .. i.target .. ";") end end -- One blank line under the head, whatever it holds. while #head > 0 and head[#head] == "" do head = take(head, #head - 1) end local body = read(TO) while starts_with(body, "\n") do body = sub(body, 2) end replace(TO, join(head, "\n") .. "\n\n" .. body) end -- 4. The old file's uses, qualified, or aliased. local moved = {} for n in NAMES do moved[n] = true end local renamed = 0 local qualified = {} local aliases = {} -- The re-exports first: a name the old file uses and re-exports is the -- re-export, used unqualified. local reexported = {} if REEXPORT then for d in zig_decls(TO) do if has_key(was_pub, d.name) then push(aliases, "pub const " .. d.name .. " = " .. AS .. "." .. d.name .. ";") reexported[d.name] = true qualified[d.name] = true end end end for u in r.uses_left do if has_key(moved, u.name) and not has_key(qualified, u.name) then qualified[u.name] = true -- A `var` cannot be aliased (`const x = m.x;` copies it, at comptime, -- which a var is not): its uses are qualified, in either mode. local is_var = false for d in zig_decls(TO) do if d.name == u.name and d.kind == "var" then is_var = true end end if USES == "alias" and not is_var then push(aliases, "const " .. u.name .. " = " .. AS .. "." .. u.name .. ";") else local z = zig_rename(FROM, u.name, AS .. "." .. u.name) renamed = renamed + z.renamed end end end if REEXPORT then print("re-exported " .. count(reexported) .. " pub names") end if USES == "alias" then print("aliased " .. #aliases .. " names") else print("qualified " .. renamed .. " uses of " .. count(qualified) .. " names") end -- 5. The import, in the old file. -- Top-level imports only: a function's own `const x = @import(...)` is -- no place for the file's (tcp_sim.zig has one at its end). local lines_of = lines(read(FROM)) local imports = {} for i in zig_imports(FROM) do local at = lines_of[i.line] if i.name ~= "" and (starts_with(at, "const ") or starts_with(at, "pub const ")) then push(imports, i) end end local anchor = nil for i in imports do if AFTER ~= "" and i.name == AFTER then anchor = i end end if anchor == nil then anchor = imports[#imports] end local anchor_text = lines_of[anchor.line] local base = split(TO, "/") local added = "const " .. AS .. " = @import(\"" .. base[#base] .. "\");" if imported_as then added = nil end if #aliases > 0 then if added == nil then added = join(aliases, "\n") else added = added .. "\n" .. join(aliases, "\n") end end if added ~= nil then edit(FROM, anchor_text .. "\n", anchor_text .. "\n" .. added .. "\n") end -- 7. The new file in the old file's test block, if it has one. local text = read(FROM) -- A plain find first: the pattern over a whole large file is costly. local block = nil local tb_at = find(text, "\ntest {\n") if tb_at ~= nil then block = re_find(sub(text, tb_at, tb_at + 8000), "^\ntest \\{\n( _ = @import\\(\"[^\"]+\"\\);\n)+\\}") end if INTO then print(TO .. " was there: enrolled as it was") block = nil end if block ~= nil and contains(block.text, "@import(\"" .. base[#base] .. "\")") then print(base[#base] .. " is enrolled in " .. FROM .. "'s test block already") elseif block ~= nil then local closing = sub(block.text, 1, #block.text - 1) edit(FROM, block.text, closing .. " _ = @import(\"" .. base[#base] .. "\");\n}") print("enrolled " .. base[#base] .. " in " .. FROM .. "'s test block") elseif not INTO then print("no `test {}` block of imports in " .. FROM .. ": name " .. TO .. " where its tests are enrolled") end -- 6. What the moved code uses of the old file. if FROM_AS == "" then for n in r.needs_from_from do print("needs from " .. FROM .. ": " .. n.name .. " (" .. FROM .. ":" .. n.line .. "): import or copy it, or give from_as") end end for n in r.needs_pub do print("pub: " .. n.name) end

name: cookbook/zig/tidy_file.shale
html: -- This recipe tidies a Zig file after a move. It orders the first block of -- top-level `const` lines, `@import`s first (each in the order it had), then -- the aliases, and it removes a section banner (`// ──`) with nothing under -- it, only blank lines before the next banner or the end. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/tidy_file.shale path=src/x.zig const P = arg("path", "") if P == "" then fail("tidy_file: give path=src/x.zig") end local l = lines(read(P)) -- The first block of `const ` lines: an alias (`const x = y.z;`) that -- comes before the import it names (`const y = @import(...)`) moves to just -- after it; every other line keeps its place, so an alias already beside -- what it aliases (`const linux = std.os.linux;` under `std`) stays. local first = 1 while first <= #l and not starts_with(l[first], "const ") and not starts_with(l[first], "pub const ") do first = first + 1 end if first <= #l then local i = first local block = {} while i <= #l and (starts_with(l[i], "const ") or starts_with(l[i], "pub const ")) do push(block, l[i]) i = i + 1 end -- Where each name is declared in the block. local at = {} for k = 1, #block do local m = re_find(block[k], "const ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) ") if m ~= nil then at[m.group] = k end end local waiting = {} local ordered = {} local moved = 0 for k = 1, #block do local m = re_find(block[k], "= ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\.") local root = nil if m ~= nil and not contains(block[k], "@import(") then root = m.group end if root ~= nil and has_key(at, root) and at[root] > k then if not has_key(waiting, root) then waiting[root] = {} end push(waiting[root], block[k]) moved = moved + 1 else push(ordered, block[k]) local d = re_find(block[k], "const ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) ") if d ~= nil and has_key(waiting, d.group) then for w in waiting[d.group] do push(ordered, w) end waiting[d.group] = {} end end end if moved > 0 then edit(P, join(block, "\n") .. "\n", join(ordered, "\n") .. "\n") print(P .. ": " .. moved .. " aliases moved after the imports they name") end end -- Banners with nothing under them. l = lines(read(P)) local keep = {} local dropped = 0 for i = 1, #l do local drop = false if starts_with(l[i], "// ──") then local j = i + 1 while j <= #l and trim(l[j]) == "" do j = j + 1 end if j > #l or starts_with(l[j], "// ──") then drop = true end end if drop then dropped = dropped + 1 else push(keep, l[i]) end end if dropped > 0 then -- A dropped banner's blank line after it goes too: no two blank lines left. local out = {} for x in keep do if not (x == "" and #out > 0 and out[#out] == "") then push(out, x) end end local text = join(out, "\n") if not ends_with(text, "\n") then text = text .. "\n" end replace(P, text) print(P .. ": " .. dropped .. " banners with nothing under them removed") end

name: cookbook/zig17/count_upgrade_changes.shale
html: -- This recipe counts what each repo uses that Zig 0.17 changed, for the -- 0.16 to 0.17 upgrade. For each repo it counts each change the 0.17 release -- notes list, by a literal text pattern in its .zig files (.zig-cache, -- zig-out and zig-pkg skipped): a census to choose the scripted fixes by, -- and to show a repo done (every count 0, or every remaining hit one the -- compiler accepts). It counts text, not tokens: a comment counts too, so a -- count is an upper bound. -- -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/zig17/count_upgrade_changes.shale -- cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/zig17/count_upgrade_changes.shale only=zig-webbox -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const ONLY = arg("only", "") const REPOS = {"zig-coverage-sdk", "zig-webbox", "metal-vmm", "shale", "zig-metal-unikernel", "angry-gopher", "dog-park", "observatory"} -- {name, pattern}: each a change in the 0.17 release notes. const CHANGES = { {"typeInfo .fields", ".@\"struct\".fields"}, {"optimize ReleaseSafe", ".ReleaseSafe"}, {"optimize ReleaseFast", ".ReleaseFast"}, {"optimize ReleaseSmall", ".ReleaseSmall"}, {"OptimizeMode", "OptimizeMode"}, {"b.build_root", "build_root"}, {"run addArgs(b.args)", "addArgs(args)"}, {"addFileArg", "addFileArg("}, {"addPrefixedFileArg", "addPrefixedFileArg("}, {"addOutputFileArg", "addOutputFileArg("}, {"addPrefixedOutputFileArg", "addPrefixedOutputFileArg("}, {"addArtifactArg", "addArtifactArg("}, {"addDirectoryArg", "addDirectoryArg("}, {"findProgram", "findProgram("}, {"Ast.parse", "Ast.parse("}, {"StaticBitSet", "StaticBitSet"}, {"ArrayBitSet", "ArrayBitSet"}, {"IntegerBitSet", "IntegerBitSet"}, {"DynamicBitSet", "DynamicBitSet"}, {"initEmpty", "initEmpty"}, {"initFull", "initFull"}, {"getLast(", "getLast("}, {"getLastOrNull(", "getLastOrNull("}, {"void{}", "void{}"}, {"errdefer |", "errdefer |"}, {"stackFallback", "stackFallback"}, {"StackFallbackAllocator", "StackFallbackAllocator"}, {"zon fromSlice", "zon.parse.fromSlice"}, {"indexOfIgnoreCase", "indexOfIgnoreCase"}, {"readPackedInt", "readPackedInt"}, {"writePackedInt", "writePackedInt"}, {"containsAtLeastScalar", "containsAtLeastScalar"}, {"meta.fieldNames", "meta.fieldNames"}, {"meta.fieldInfo", "meta.fieldInfo"}, {"Uri.getHost", "getHost("}, {"GlobalLinkage internal", ".internal"}, {"link_once", "link_once"}, {"@bitCast (audit)", "@bitCast("}, {"std.builtin (deprecated)", "std.builtin"}, {"@intFromEnum (deprecated)", "@intFromEnum("}, {"@enumFromInt (deprecated)", "@enumFromInt("}, {"builtin.cpu/os (deprecated)", "builtin.cpu"}, {"allocPrint (arena.print)", "allocPrint("}, } function zig_files(repo) local out = {} for e in walk_all(repo, {kind = "file", like = "*.zig", skip = ".zig-cache"}) do if not contains(e.path, "/zig-out/") and not contains(e.path, "/zig-pkg/") and not contains(e.path, "/.zig-cache/") then push(out, e.path) end end return out end local rows = {} for repo in REPOS do if ONLY == "" or ONLY == repo then local files = zig_files(repo) local counts = {} for f in files do local text = read_or(f, "") for c in CHANGES do local n = #split(text, c[2]) - 1 if n > 0 then counts[c[1]] = get(counts, c[1], 0) + n end end end for c in CHANGES do if get(counts, c[1], 0) > 0 then push(rows, {repo = repo, change = c[1], hits = counts[c[1]]}) end end print(repo .. ": " .. #files .. " .zig files") end end print("") print(table(rows, {"repo", "change", "hits"}))

name: cookbook/zig17/find_hidden_decls.shale
html: -- This script finds declarations that Zig 0.17's `@hasDecl` no longer sees. -- Under 0.16 `@hasDecl(T, "name")` also found a declaration that was not `pub`, -- in the same file at least; under 0.17 it finds only a `pub` one. Where the -- check is optional (a site's `between`, `family` or `uploader`, a host's -- feature flag), a declaration without `pub` turns its feature off with no -- compile error, and at most a test notices. -- -- The script prints every declaration of a checked name that is not `pub` in a -- repo's .zig files, and `fix=yes` makes each one `pub`. The checked names are -- those our repos ask `@hasDecl` about by a literal; `names=a,b` gives others. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig17/find_hidden_decls.shale dir=. -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig17/find_hidden_decls.shale dir=. fix=yes -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const DIR = arg("dir", ".") const FIX = arg("fix", "no") == "yes" const CHECKED_NAMES = split(arg("names", "between,family,uploader,shale_change_check,shale_preludes,shale_diff_summary,coverage_checks,burst,name"), ",") -- Gives the checked name a line declares without `pub`, or nil. A `fn` counts -- at any depth, since a function always belongs to a container. A `const` or -- `var` counts only at the top level: indented, it may be a function's local, -- where `pub` would not compile. function checked_name_lacking_pub(line) local code = trim(line) if starts_with(code, "pub ") or starts_with(code, "//") then return nil end local keywords = {"fn "} if #code == #line then keywords = {"fn ", "const ", "var "} end for keyword in keywords do if starts_with(code, keyword) then local rest = sub(code, #keyword + 1) for name in CHECKED_NAMES do if starts_with(rest, name .. "(") or starts_with(rest, name .. " ") or starts_with(rest, name .. ":") then return name end end end end return nil end function with_pub(line) local code = trim(line) return sub(line, 1, #line - #code) .. "pub " .. code end -- Prints the file's findings, rewrites it under `fix=yes`, and gives their count. function check_file(path) local found = 0 local fixed_lines = {} local number = 0 for line in lines(read(path)) do number = number + 1 if checked_name_lacking_pub(line) == nil then push(fixed_lines, line) else found = found + 1 print(path .. ":" .. number .. ": " .. trim(line)) push(fixed_lines, with_pub(line)) end end if FIX and found > 0 then replace(path, join(fixed_lines, "\n") .. "\n") end return found end local found = 0 for entry in walk_all(DIR, {kind = "file", like = "*.zig"}) do if not contains(entry.path, ".zig-cache") and not contains(entry.path, "zig-out") then found = found + check_file(entry.path) end end print("declarations of a checked name, not pub: " .. found .. (FIX and " (made pub)" or " (fix=yes makes them pub)"))

name: cookbook/zig17/rewrite_array_mult.shale
html: -- This recipe rewrites array multiplication as `@splat`, for the Zig 0.16 to -- 0.17 upgrade. 0.17 removed `a ** n` for arrays; a repeated one-element -- array, `[_]T{v} ** N`, is `@splat(v)` with the array's type known. Each -- one is rewritten by where it stands: -- - an untyped declaration, `var x = [_]T{v} ** N;` (and `const`, `pub`, -- `export`, with `align(...)` or `linksection(...)` kept after the -- type): `var x: [N]T = @splat(v);` -- - after an `=` whose target has a type (a typed declaration, a field's -- default, an assignment, a struct literal's `.field =`): `@splat(v)` -- - anywhere else (an operand of `&`, an argument): `@as([N]T, @splat(v))` -- A repeated one-character string, `"x" ** N`, is `&@as([N]u8, @splat('x'))` -- (a pointer to an array: it is a slice where one is wanted, and `++` -- takes it). A longer string repeated, `"ab" ** N`, is `repeated("ab", N)`, -- and the file gets that function appended (built at comptime: a pointer -- to an array as well). -- An anonymous `.{v} ** N`, with no element type, is listed, not changed: -- give it its type by hand. Every changed file is rewritten whole; run -- `zig fmt` after, and let the compiler judge. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig17/rewrite_array_mult.shale dir=src -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig17/rewrite_array_mult.shale dir=src dry=yes -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const DIR = arg("dir", ".") const DRY = arg("dry", "no") == "yes" -- What a file that repeats a longer string gets at its end. const REPEATED = join({ "", "/// `s` repeated `n` times, built at comptime (Zig 0.17 removed `s ** n`).", "fn repeated(comptime s: []const u8, comptime n: usize) *const [s.len * n]u8 {", " const out = comptime blk: {", " var a: [s.len * n]u8 = undefined;", " @setEvalBranchQuota(1000 + n);", " for (0..n) |i| @memcpy(a[i * s.len ..][0..s.len], s);", " break :blk a;", " };", " return &out;", "}", }, "\n") .. "\n" -- The end of the count expression that starts at `at` in `l`: one operand, -- since `**` binds tighter than any other operator (`"b" ** max ++ "x"` is -- `("b" ** max) ++ "x"`), so up to a space, `;`, `,` or a closing bracket -- at depth zero. function count_end(l, at) local depth = 0 local i = at while i <= #l do local c = sub(l, i, i) if c == "(" or c == "[" or c == "{" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == ")" or c == "]" or c == "}" then if depth == 0 then return i - 1 end depth = depth - 1 elseif (c == ";" or c == "," or c == " ") and depth == 0 then return i - 1 end i = i + 1 end return #l end -- `(n)` without its outer parentheses, when they wrap it whole. function bare(n) local t = trim(n) if starts_with(t, "(") and ends_with(t, ")") then local depth = 0 for i = 1, #t do local c = sub(t, i, i) if c == "(" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == ")" then depth = depth - 1 end if depth == 0 and i < #t then return t end end return trim(sub(t, 2, #t - 1)) end return t end -- The value inside `{...}` from `open` (the `{`), and the index of its `}`. function braced(l, open) local depth = 0 for i = open, #l do local c = sub(l, i, i) if c == "{" or c == "(" or c == "[" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == "}" or c == ")" or c == "]" then depth = depth - 1 if depth == 0 then return {value = sub(l, open + 1, i - 1), close = i} end end end return nil end -- When `before` (the line up to the array) is an untyped declaration's -- head, `[pub ][export ](var|const) NAME[ align(..)][ linksection(..)] = `: -- {head = "...var NAME", attrs = "align(..) ..."}; else nil. function untyped_decl(before) if not ends_with(before, " = ") then return nil end local s = sub(before, 1, #before - 3) local indent = #s - #trim(s) local w = trim(s) local head = sub(s, 1, indent) for kw in {"pub ", "export "} do if starts_with(w, kw) then head = head .. kw w = sub(w, #kw + 1) end end local kind = "" if starts_with(w, "var ") then kind = "var " elseif starts_with(w, "const ") then kind = "const " else return nil end head = head .. kind w = sub(w, #kind + 1) local name = re_find(w, "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*") if name == nil then return nil end head = head .. name.text local attrs = trim(sub(w, #name.text + 1)) if attrs ~= "" and not starts_with(attrs, "align(") and not starts_with(attrs, "linksection(") then return nil end return {head = head, attrs = attrs} end -- One line with its array multiplications rewritten, and what was left. function fix_line(l) local changed = 0 local left = 0 local strings = 0 local from = 1 while true do local m = re_find(sub(l, from), "\\[_\\]") if m == nil then break end local at = from + m.at - 1 local open = find(l, "{", at) if open == nil then break end local elem = trim(sub(l, at + 3, open - 1)) local b = braced(l, open) if b == nil then break end local rest = sub(l, b.close + 1) local star = re_find(rest, "^\\s*\\*\\*\\s*") if star == nil or contains(elem, " ") and not contains(elem, "(") then from = b.close + 1 else local nstart = b.close + 1 + #star.text local nend = count_end(l, nstart) local n = bare(sub(l, nstart, nend)) local before = sub(l, 1, at - 1) local after = sub(l, nend + 1) local value = trim(b.value) local decl = untyped_decl(before) if decl ~= nil then local typed = decl.head .. ": [" .. n .. "]" .. elem if decl.attrs ~= "" then typed = typed .. " " .. decl.attrs end l = typed .. " = @splat(" .. value .. ")" .. after from = 1 elseif ends_with(before, "= ") then l = before .. "@splat(" .. value .. ")" .. after from = #before + 1 else l = before .. "@as([" .. n .. "]" .. elem .. ", @splat(" .. value .. "))" .. after from = #before + 1 end changed = changed + 1 end end -- A repeated one-character string: `"x" ** N`. local sseek = 1 while true do local star = find(l, "\" **", sseek) if star == nil then break end -- The string's opening quote, back from its closing one. local open = star - 1 while open > 0 do if sub(l, open, open) == "\"" and (open == 1 or sub(l, open - 1, open - 1) ~= "\\") then break end open = open - 1 end local inner = sub(l, open + 1, star - 1) local one = #inner == 1 or (#inner == 2 and starts_with(inner, "\\")) if open > 0 and not one then local nstart = star + 4 while sub(l, nstart, nstart) == " " do nstart = nstart + 1 end local nend = count_end(l, nstart) local before = sub(l, 1, open - 1) l = before .. "repeated(\"" .. inner .. "\", " .. bare(sub(l, nstart, nend)) .. ")" .. sub(l, nend + 1) changed = changed + 1 strings = strings + 1 sseek = #before + 1 elseif open > 0 and one then local nstart = star + 4 while sub(l, nstart, nstart) == " " do nstart = nstart + 1 end local nend = count_end(l, nstart) local ch = inner if ch == "'" then ch = "\\'" end local n = bare(sub(l, nstart, nend)) local before = sub(l, 1, open - 1) l = before .. "&@as([" .. n .. "]u8, @splat('" .. ch .. "'))" .. sub(l, nend + 1) changed = changed + 1 sseek = #before + 1 else sseek = star + 4 end end -- An anonymous `.{v} ** N` whose target has its type (`x: [6]u8 = -- .{0} ** 6`, a typed field's default): `@splat(v)`. Untyped, or nested, -- it is left for a hand. local seek = 1 while true do local open = find(l, ".{", seek) if open == nil then break end local b = braced(l, open + 1) if b == nil then break end local star = re_find(sub(l, b.close + 1), "^\\s*\\*\\*\\s*") local before = sub(l, 1, open - 1) if star ~= nil and ends_with(before, "= ") and untyped_decl(before) == nil and not contains(b.value, "**") then local nstart = b.close + 1 + #star.text local nend = count_end(l, nstart) l = before .. "@splat(" .. trim(b.value) .. ")" .. sub(l, nend + 1) changed = changed + 1 seek = #before + 1 else seek = open + 2 end end if re_find(l, "\\}\\s*\\*\\*") ~= nil or contains(l, "\" **") then left = left + 1 end return {line = l, changed = changed, left = left, strings = strings} end local total = 0 local files = 0 local leftover = {} for e in walk_all(DIR, {kind = "file", like = "*.zig"}) do if not contains(e.path, ".zig-cache") and not contains(e.path, "zig-out") then local text = read(e.path) if contains(text, " ** ") then local out = {} local n = 0 local strings = 0 local i = 0 for l in lines(text) do i = i + 1 local r = fix_line(l) push(out, r.line) n = n + r.changed strings = strings + r.strings if r.left > 0 then push(leftover, e.path .. ":" .. i .. ": " .. trim(r.line)) end end if n > 0 then files = files + 1 total = total + n print(e.path .. ": " .. n) local whole = join(out, "\n") .. "\n" if strings > 0 and not contains(text, "fn repeated(") then whole = whole .. REPEATED end if not DRY then replace(e.path, whole) end end end end end print("array multiplications rewritten: " .. total .. " in " .. files .. " files" .. (DRY and " (dry run: nothing written)" or "")) if #leftover > 0 then print("left for a hand (no element type, or a form this does not read):") for l in leftover do print(" " .. sub(l, 1, 160)) end end

name: cookbook/zig17/rewrite_renamed_calls.shale
html: -- This recipe rewrites the calls Zig 0.17 renamed or reshaped, for the 0.16 -- to 0.17 upgrade: each one 0.17 removed (not merely deprecated), rewritten -- in place: -- - `x.dupeZ(T, s)`: `x.dupeSentinel(T, s, 0)` (the call's closing -- parenthesis found by depth, so nested arguments are safe) -- - type info reshaped: a pointer's `.pointer.is_const` (and -- `is_volatile`, `is_allowzero`, `alignment`, `address_space`): -- `.pointer.attrs.@"const"` (`@"volatile"`, `@"allowzero"`, `@"align"`, -- `@"addrspace"`); a function's `.params[i].type`: `.param_types[i]` -- - `std.fmt.bufPrintZ(b, f, a)`: `std.mem.printSentinel(b, f, a, 0)` -- - a fixed-size bitset's `.initEmpty()` / `.initFull()`: `.empty` / -- `.full` (the dynamic sets' take an allocator, and are left) -- - `std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase...`: `std.ascii.findIgnoreCase...` -- (and its Pos, PosLinear) -- - `Ast.parse(gpa, src, .zig)` (or `.zon`): `Ast.parse(gpa, src, -- .{ .mode = .zig })` -- - a container's field count, `@typeInfo(T).@"enum".fields.len` (and -- `@"struct"`, `@"union"`): `.field_names.len` (0.17's type info is -- struct-of-arrays; a loop over the fields is a hand's) -- - the optimize modes' old tags, deprecated and refused after `orelse`, -- `==` and in a switch: `.ReleaseSafe` / `.ReleaseFast` / `.ReleaseSmall` -- to `.safe` / `.fast` / `.small` everywhere (whole tokens), and -- `.Debug` to `.debug` on a line that says `ptimize` (other enums have -- a `Debug`). The command line's `-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` still reads. -- - `if (b.args) |a| run.addArgs(a);`: `run.addPassthruArgs();` (0.17's -- build script no longer sees the arguments after `--`) -- - `X.pathFromRoot(p)` (removed): `pathFromRoot(X, p)`, the file given -- that function and `rootOf`, which make the path absolute (0.17's -- `b.root` may hold a relative one); `b.build_root.handle`: -- `b.root.root_dir.handle` -- Every changed file is rewritten whole; run `zig fmt` after, and let the -- compiler judge. -- -- cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig17/rewrite_renamed_calls.shale dir=src -- -- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 arena_bytes=4000000000 const DIR = arg("dir", ".") -- What a build.zig that called `b.pathFromRoot` gets at its end. const FROM_ROOT = join({ "", "/// `builder`'s build root as an absolute path: 0.17's `b.root` may hold a", "/// relative one, and these paths are handed to other processes and builds.", "fn rootOf(builder: *std.Build) []const u8 {", " return builder.root.root_dir.handle.realPathFileAlloc(builder.graph.io, builder.root.subPathOrDot(), builder.allocator) catch |e|", " std.debug.panic(\"the build root {f}: {t}\", .{ builder.root, e });", "}", "", "/// `sub` under this build's root, absolute (0.17 removed `b.pathFromRoot`).", "fn pathFromRoot(b: *std.Build, sub: []const u8) []const u8 {", " return b.pathJoin(&.{ rootOf(b), sub });", "}", }, "\n") .. "\n" -- The index of the `)` closing the call whose `(` is at `open`. function close_of(l, open) local depth = 0 for i = open, #l do local c = sub(l, i, i) if c == "(" or c == "[" or c == "{" then depth = depth + 1 elseif c == ")" or c == "]" or c == "}" then depth = depth - 1 if depth == 0 then return i end end end return nil end function fix(text) local n = 0 -- dupeZ(T, s) -> dupeSentinel(T, s, 0) local from = 1 while true do local at = find(text, ".dupeZ(", from) if at == nil then break end local open = at + 6 local close = close_of(text, open) if close == nil then break end text = sub(text, 1, at) .. "dupeSentinel(" .. sub(text, open + 1, close - 1) .. ", 0)" .. sub(text, close + 1) n = n + 1 from = at + 1 end -- fmt.bufPrintZ(b, f, a) -> mem.printSentinel(b, f, a, 0) from = 1 while true do local at = find(text, "fmt.bufPrintZ(", from) if at == nil then break end local open = at + 13 local close = close_of(text, open) if close == nil then break end text = sub(text, 1, at - 1) .. "mem.printSentinel(" .. sub(text, open + 1, close - 1) .. ", 0)" .. sub(text, close + 1) n = n + 1 from = at + 1 end -- A pointer's attributes moved under `attrs`. for pair in {{".pointer.is_const", ".pointer.attrs.@\"const\""}, {".pointer.is_volatile", ".pointer.attrs.@\"volatile\""}, {".pointer.is_allowzero", ".pointer.attrs.@\"allowzero\""}, {".pointer.alignment", ".pointer.attrs.@\"align\""}, {".pointer.address_space", ".pointer.attrs.@\"addrspace\""}} do local k = #split(text, pair[1]) - 1 if k > 0 then text = substitute(text, pair[1], pair[2]) n = n + k end end -- A function's .params[i].type -> .param_types[i] from = 1 while true do local at = find(text, ".params[", from) if at == nil then break end local close = find(text, "]", at) if close ~= nil and sub(text, close + 1, close + 5) == ".type" then text = sub(text, 1, at) .. "param_types[" .. sub(text, at + 8, close) .. sub(text, close + 6) n = n + 1 end from = at + 1 end -- .initEmpty() / .initFull(), no arguments -> .empty / .full for pair in {{".initEmpty()", ".empty"}, {".initFull()", ".full"}} do local k = #split(text, pair[1]) - 1 if k > 0 then text = substitute(text, pair[1], pair[2]) n = n + k end end -- std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase... -> findIgnoreCase... local k = #split(text, "ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase") - 1 if k > 0 then text = substitute(text, "ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase", "ascii.findIgnoreCase") n = n + k end -- Ast.parse(a, s, .zig) -> Ast.parse(a, s, .{ .mode = .zig }) for mode in {"zig", "zon"} do from = 1 while true do local at = find(text, "Ast.parse(", from) if at == nil then break end local close = close_of(text, at + 9) if close == nil then break end local call = sub(text, at, close) if ends_with(call, ", ." .. mode .. ")") then local fixed = sub(call, 1, #call - #mode - 3) .. ".{ .mode = ." .. mode .. " })" text = sub(text, 1, at - 1) .. fixed .. sub(text, close + 1) n = n + 1 end from = at + 1 end end -- The optimize modes' tags, whole tokens: the next byte no identifier's. local out = {} for line in split(text, "\n") do for pair in {{".ReleaseSafe", ".safe"}, {".ReleaseFast", ".fast"}, {".ReleaseSmall", ".small"}, {".Debug", ".debug"}} do if pair[1] ~= ".Debug" or contains(line, "ptimize") then local seek = 1 while true do local at = find(line, pair[1], seek) if at == nil then break end local next = sub(line, at + #pair[1], at + #pair[1]) if next ~= "" and contains("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_0123456789", next) then seek = at + 1 else line = sub(line, 1, at - 1) .. pair[2] .. sub(line, at + #pair[1]) n = n + 1 seek = at + #pair[2] end end end end -- if (b.args) |a| run.addArgs(a); -> run.addPassthruArgs(); local t = trim(line) if starts_with(t, "if (b.args) |") then local bar = find(t, "|", 14) local cap = sub(t, 14, bar - 1) local rest = trim(sub(t, bar + 1)) local call = find(rest, ".addArgs(" .. cap .. ");") if call ~= nil and call + #(".addArgs(" .. cap .. ");") - 1 == #rest then line = sub(line, 1, #line - #t) .. sub(rest, 1, call - 1) .. ".addPassthruArgs();" n = n + 1 end end push(out, line) end text = join(out, "\n") -- X.pathFromRoot(p) -> pathFromRoot(X, p) for any builder X (`b`, -- `dep.builder`), with the helpers appended once. local roots = 0 local seek = 1 while true do local at = find(text, ".pathFromRoot(", seek) if at == nil then break end local start = at while start > 1 and contains("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_0123456789.", sub(text, start - 1, start - 1)) do start = start - 1 end local receiver = sub(text, start, at - 1) text = sub(text, 1, start - 1) .. "pathFromRoot(" .. receiver .. ", " .. sub(text, at + 14) roots = roots + 1 seek = start + 1 end if roots > 0 then if not contains(text, "fn pathFromRoot(") then text = text .. FROM_ROOT end n = n + roots end roots = #split(text, "b.build_root.handle") - 1 if roots > 0 then text = substitute(text, "b.build_root.handle", "b.root.root_dir.handle") n = n + roots end for kind in {"enum", "struct", "union"} do local old = ".@\"" .. kind .. "\".fields.len" local k = #split(text, old) - 1 if k > 0 then text = substitute(text, old, ".@\"" .. kind .. "\".field_names.len") n = n + k end end return {text = text, n = n} end local total = 0 for e in walk_all(DIR, {kind = "file", like = "*.zig"}) do if not contains(e.path, ".zig-cache") and not contains(e.path, "zig-out") then local was = read(e.path) if contains(was, "dupeZ(") or contains(was, "indexOfIgnoreCase") or contains(was, "Ast.parse(") or contains(was, ".fields.len") or contains(was, ".Release") or contains(was, ".Debug") or contains(was, "b.args") or contains(was, "bufPrintZ(") or contains(was, ".initEmpty()") or contains(was, ".initFull()") or contains(was, ".pointer.") or contains(was, ".params[") or contains(was, "pathFromRoot(") or contains(was, "build_root.handle") then local r = fix(was) if r.n > 0 then print(e.path .. ": " .. r.n) replace(e.path, r.text) total = total + r.n end end end end print("calls rewritten: " .. total)

name: books-book/build.shale
html: -- budget: steps=200000000 output_bytes=200000 arena_bytes=200000000 -- This builds the books book into a stage of the dev channel: a contents page, -- one page a chapter, and an index. -- -- cd <shale checkout> && shale books-book/build.shale -- -- books-book/book.md is the whole book. Its `#` line is the title, the text -- under it is the contents page's, and each `##` heading starts a chapter, -- whose `###` headings are its sections. -- -- A line that is exactly an include becomes a code block, so the book quotes -- each file as it stands at build time: -- {{file PATH}} the whole file; -- {{function PATH NAME}} one top-level Shale function, with the -- comment lines right above it; -- {{lines PATH from "A" to "B"}} the lines from the one holding A -- through the one holding B, each text -- in the file exactly once; -- {{runs PATH}} a Shale script and what it printed, -- which must end well; -- {{stops PATH}} a Shale script and its stop, which -- must stop. -- A path through the `repos` mount (`repos:roc-apps/...`) reaches a checkout -- beside this one. -- -- The build is the book's first gate. It stops on an include that names no -- file, an anchor found twice or never, any other `{{` in the prose, a -- chapter over MAX_PROSE_WORDS words of prose, and any negative sentence the -- cookbook's lint finds that negatives.txt leaves unlisted. Then it fetches -- every page from the channel and stops on one that fails to answer. -- -- The settings below are everything a copy of this builder changes for its -- own book. The two taste gates are the last two: a higher MAX_PROSE_WORDS -- allows longer pages, and CHECK_NEGATIVES = false drops the lint. -- Where the book's files are, from the checkout's root. const SOURCE = "books-book/book.md" const CSS = "books-book/book.css" const NEGATIVES_TABLE = "books-book/negatives.txt" const TERMS = "books-book/index_terms.txt" -- Where the pages go: the folder of the dev channel named STAGE. const STAGE = "books-book" const DEST = "build:roc-apps/next/" .. STAGE -- The web server over that folder, which the build asks for each page; "" -- skips the check, for a machine with no server running. const CHANNEL = "http://127.0.0.1:9210/" -- The taste gates. const MAX_PROSE_WORDS = 900 const CHECK_NEGATIVES = true const NEGATIVES = "cookbook:prose/find_negatives.shale" const TERM_INDEX = "cookbook:prose/build_term_index.shale" const DOT_WANT = "graphviz: the book's diagrams, drawn at build time" const FENCE = "```" -- The lines of a text, without the empty one after its last newline. function text_lines(text) local ls = lines(text) if #ls > 0 and ls[#ls] == "" then return take(ls, #ls - 1) end return ls end -- A path as the reader sees it, without the mount that reaches it. function shown_path(path) if starts_with(path, "repos:") then return sub(path, 7) end return path end -- A fence's language, from the file's extension; Shale's unless named here. const FENCE_TAGS = {roc = "roc", go = "go", zig = "zig", js = "javascript", mjs = "javascript", css = "css", md = "markdown", json = "json", txt = "text"} function fenced(path, ls, label) for l in ls do if starts_with(trim(l), FENCE) then fail("book: " .. path .. " holds a fence of its own, and a quote can't") end end local tag = "shale" local m = re_find(path, "\\.(\\w+)$") if m ~= nil and has_key(FENCE_TAGS, m.group) then tag = FENCE_TAGS[m.group] end return FENCE .. tag .. " " .. label .. "\n" .. join(ls, "\n") .. "\n" .. FENCE end function whole_file(path) if not exists(path) then fail("book: {{file " .. path .. "}} names no file") end return fenced(path, text_lines(read(path)), shown_path(path) .. ", the whole file") end -- One top-level function, with the comment lines right above it, through the -- first `end` at the start of a line. function function_of(path, name) if not exists(path) then fail("book: {{function " .. path .. " " .. name .. "}} names no file") end local ls = text_lines(read(path)) local start = 0 local i = 0 for l in ls do i = i + 1 if start == 0 and starts_with(l, "function " .. name .. "(") then start = i end end if start == 0 then fail("book: " .. path .. " has no top-level function " .. name) end local first = start while first > 1 and starts_with(ls[first - 1], "--") do first = first - 1 end local last = start while last <= #ls and ls[last] ~= "end" do last = last + 1 end if last > #ls then fail("book: " .. name .. " in " .. path .. " has no `end` at the start of a line") end return fenced(path, slice(ls, first, last), shown_path(path) .. ", the function " .. name) end -- The number of the one line of `ls` that holds `anchor`. The anchor must be -- there exactly once, so an edit that removes or repeats it stops the build. function anchored_line(ls, anchor, path) local at = 0 local seen = 0 local i = 0 for l in ls do i = i + 1 if contains(l, anchor) then seen = seen + 1 at = i end end if seen ~= 1 then fail("book: `" .. anchor .. "` is in " .. path .. " " .. seen .. " times, and an anchor must be there once") end return at end function between_anchors(path, from, to) if not exists(path) then fail("book: {{lines " .. path .. " ...}} names no file") end local ls = text_lines(read(path)) local first = anchored_line(ls, from, path) local last = anchored_line(ls, to, path) if last < first then fail("book: in " .. path .. ", `" .. to .. "` comes before `" .. from .. "`") end return fenced(path, slice(ls, first, last), shown_path(path) .. ", an excerpt") end -- A script and what it printed, run here and now. `stops` says how the book -- claims the run ends, and a run that ends the other way stops the build. function script_run(path, stops) if not exists(path) then fail("book: the include names no file " .. path) end local r = run({"shale", path}, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 30}) local ended_well = r.ended == "exit" and get(r, "code", -1) == 0 if stops and ended_well then fail("book: " .. path .. " ran to its end, and the book says it stops") end if not stops and not ended_well then print(trim(r.out)) fail("book: " .. path .. " stopped, and the book says it runs") end local said = "what it printed" if stops then said = "how it stopped" end return fenced(path, text_lines(read(path)), shown_path(path) .. ", the whole file") .. "\n\n" .. FENCE .. "text " .. said .. "\n" .. trim(r.out) .. "\n" .. FENCE end function expanded(text) local out = {} for l in text_lines(text) do local file = re_find(l, "^\\{\\{file (\\S+)\\}\\}$") local func = re_find(l, "^\\{\\{function (\\S+) (\\w+)\\}\\}$") local span = re_find(l, "^\\{\\{lines (\\S+) from \"([^\"]+)\" to \"([^\"]+)\"\\}\\}$") local runs = re_find(l, "^\\{\\{runs (\\S+)\\}\\}$") local stops = re_find(l, "^\\{\\{stops (\\S+)\\}\\}$") local block = nil if file ~= nil then block = whole_file(file.group) elseif func ~= nil then block = function_of(func.groups[1], func.groups[2]) elseif span ~= nil then block = between_anchors(span.groups[1], span.groups[2], span.groups[3]) elseif runs ~= nil then block = script_run(runs.group, false) elseif stops ~= nil then block = script_run(stops.group, true) elseif contains(re_replace(l, "`[^`]*`", ""), "{{") then fail("book: a `{{` the build doesn't know: " .. l) end if block == nil then push(out, l) else for q in lines(block) do push(out, q) end end end return out end -- The book's parts: its title, the contents page's lines, and each chapter -- as {title, lines}. function parts_of(ls) local title = "" local front = {} local chapters = {} local current = nil local in_code = false for l in ls do if starts_with(l, FENCE) then in_code = not in_code end if in_code or starts_with(l, FENCE) then if current == nil then push(front, l) else push(current.lines, l) end elseif title == "" and starts_with(l, "# ") then title = sub(l, 3) elseif starts_with(l, "## ") then current = {title = sub(l, 4), lines = {}} push(chapters, current) elseif current == nil then push(front, l) else push(current.lines, l) end end if title == "" then fail("book: book.md has no `#` title") end return {title = title, front = front, chapters = chapters} end -- The words of prose in some lines of markdown: every word outside a fence. function prose_words(ls) local n = 0 local in_code = false for l in ls do if starts_with(l, FENCE) then in_code = not in_code elseif not in_code then n = n + #words(l) end end return n end function html_escaped(text) local s = join(split(text, "&"), "&") s = join(split(s, "<"), "<") s = join(split(s, ">"), ">") s = join(split(s, "\""), """) return join(split(s, "'"), "'") end -- Shale's code blocks are colored with Shale's own lexer, `shale_tokens`: a -- keyword, a string, a comment, a number, a function's name where `function` -- declares it, and a name called, the one before a `(`. const SYN_OF_TAG = {comment = "syn-comment", string = "syn-string", int = "syn-number"} function syn_classes(tokens) local classes = {} local before = "" local i = 0 for t in tokens do i = i + 1 local class = get(SYN_OF_TAG, t.tag, "") if starts_with(t.tag, "kw_") then class = "syn-keyword" end if t.tag == "name" then local j = i + 1 while j <= #tokens and tokens[j].tag == "comment" do j = j + 1 end if before == "kw_function" then class = "syn-name" elseif j <= #tokens and tokens[j].tag == "lparen" then class = "syn-call" end end push(classes, class) if t.tag ~= "comment" then before = t.tag end end return classes end -- `attempt` calls the script's own functions. function tokens_of(path) return shale_tokens(path) end -- A Shale block's text as HTML, its tokens in spans. `where` names the block -- in a stop. function colored_code(text, dir, where) local path = dir .. "/block.shale" replace(path, text) local got = attempt(tokens_of, path) if not got.ok then fail("book: the Shale block " .. where .. " doesn't lex as Shale: " .. got.error) end local tokens = got.value local classes = syn_classes(tokens) local pieces = {} local at = 1 local i = 0 for t in tokens do i = i + 1 if classes[i] ~= "" then push(pieces, html_escaped(sub(text, at, t.start))) push(pieces, "<span class=\"" .. classes[i] .. "\">" .. html_escaped(sub(text, t.start + 1, t.stop)) .. "</span>") at = t.stop + 1 end end push(pieces, html_escaped(sub(text, at, #text))) return join(pieces, "") end -- A ```dot fence's source drawn as SVG by Graphviz, ready to sit in a page, -- its comments and titles dropped (a title shows as a tooltip on hover). function drawn(source) local dir = fresh_dir("scratch:", "book-dot") replace(dir .. "/d.dot", source) local r = run({"dot", "-Tsvg", "-Gfontsize=12", "-Nfontsize=12", "-Efontsize=11", real(dir .. "/d.dot")}, {timeout_ms = 30000, whole = 2000000, want = DOT_WANT}) remove_tree(dir) if r.code ~= 0 then print(trim(r.out)) fail("book: dot could not draw a diagram") end local at = find(r.out, "<svg ") if at == nil then fail("book: dot drew no <svg>") end local kept = {} for l in lines(sub(r.out, at)) do if not starts_with(l, "<!--") and not starts_with(l, "<title>") then push(kept, l) end end return join(kept, "\n") end -- The renderer, for the markdown this book uses: headings, paragraphs, flat -- lists, quotes, pipe tables and fences, with code spans, bold, italics and -- links inside a line. function emphasized(s) s = re_replace(s, "\\*\\*([^*]+)\\*\\*", "<strong>\\1</strong>") s = re_replace(s, "\\*([^*]+)\\*", "<em>\\1</em>") return re_replace(s, "\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\(([^) ]+)\\)", "<a href=\"\\2\">\\1</a>") end function inline_html(s) local out = {} local in_code = false for piece in split(s, "`") do if in_code then push(out, "<code>" .. html_escaped(piece) .. "</code>") else push(out, emphasized(html_escaped(piece))) end in_code = not in_code end if not in_code then fail("book: a line with an unclosed backtick: " .. s) end return join(out, "") end function slug_of(title) local s = re_replace(lower(title), "[^a-z0-9]+", "-") s = re_replace(s, "^-+", "") return re_replace(s, "-+$", "") end function caption_of(label) if label == "" then return "" end return "<figcaption>" .. html_escaped(label) .. "</figcaption>" end function fence_html(head, body, dir) local lang = get(words(head), 1, "") local label = trim(sub(head, #lang + 1)) local text = join(body, "\n") if lang == "raw" then return text end if lang == "dot" then return "<figure class=\"diagram\">" .. caption_of(label) .. drawn(text) .. "</figure>" end local code = html_escaped(text) if lang == "shale" then code = colored_code(text, dir, label) end local pre = "<pre><code class=\"language-" .. lang .. "\">" .. code ..
